Then you are these ones who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes verse. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then you are these ones who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes verse. He said: God informed them of that from their actions, and He forbade them in the Torah to shed their blood. And he imposed on them the ransom of their prisoners, so they were two groups: a group of them were Banu Qaynuqa, who were allies of Khazraj and Nadir, and Qurayza, who were allies of Aws. So when there was war between Aws and Khazraj, Banu Qaynuqa would go out with Khazraj, and Nadir and Qurayza would go out with Aws. Each of the two groups would support its allies against its brothers until their blood was shed among them, and they had the Torah in their hands, knowing in it what was against them and what was for them. The Aws and Khazraj were polytheists who worshipped idols and did not know Paradise or Hell, nor resurrection or Day of Judgment, nor a book, nor lawful or unlawful. So when the war laid down its burdens, they ransomed their prisoners in confirmation of what was in the Torah and took it from one another. Banu Qaynuqa would ransom those of their prisoners who were in the hands of Aws, and Nadir and Qurayza would ransom those of them who were in the hands of Khazraj, and they would seek what they had taken of their blood, and they would kill those of them who were killed among themselves in support of the polytheists against them. God says: God the Almighty mentioned Him when He informed them of that, Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? That is, do you ransom them according to the ruling of the Torah and kill them, while according to the ruling of the Torah, one should not be killed, nor should one leave his home, nor should one support against him who associates partners with God and worships idols other than Him, seeking worldly gain? This story was revealed about what they did with the Aws and Khazraj, as far as I have been informed. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi: Qurayzah were allies of the Aws, and Nadir were allies of Khazraj, so they used to fight in a war among themselves. Banu Qurayzah fought with their allies, Nadir, and their allies, and Nadir used to fight Qurayzah and their allies and defeat them, so they would destroy their homes and expel them from them. So if a man from both sides was taken prisoner, they would gather around him until they ransom him, and the Arabs would taunt them about that, saying: How do you fight them and ransom them? They said: We were commanded to ransom them, and it was forbidden for us to fight them. They said: Then why do you kill them? They said: We are ashamed that our allies should be humiliated. That is when God, the Blessed and Exalted, reproached them and said: Then you are these people who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes (al-Anbiya’ 4:10). Asbat said on the authority of al-Suddi on the authority of al-Sha’bi that this verse was revealed about Qays ibn al-Khatim: Then you are these people who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes (al-Anbiya’ 4:10). Asbat said on the authority of al-Suddi on the authority of Abd al-Khair, who said: We raided with Sulayman ibn Rabi’ah al-Bahili in Balanjar and besieged its people. We conquered the city and captured captives. Abdullah ibn Salam bought a Jewish woman for seven hundred. When he passed by the head of the diaspora, he went down to him. Abdullah said to him: O head of the diaspora, would you like an old woman here from your religion to buy from me? He said: Yes. He said: I took it for seven hundred dirhams. He said: Then I will give you another seven hundred. He said: I swore that I would not reduce it from four thousand. He said: I have no need of it. He said: By God, you must buy it from me or you will renounce the religion that you are following. He said: Come closer to me. So he came closer to him, and he recited in his ear from what is in the Torah: “You will not find a slave from the Children of Israel except that you will buy him, and he will set him free. And if they come to you as captives, you may ransom them, although it is forbidden to you to expel them.” He said: Are you Abdullah ibn Salam? He said: Yes. So he came with four thousand, and Abdullah took two thousand and returned two thousand to him. Adam bin Abi Iyas said in his interpretation: Abu Jaafar, meaning Al-Razi, told us, Al-Rabi bin Anas told us, Abu Al-Aaliyah told us: Abdullah bin Salam passed by the head of the exodus in Kufa, and he was ransoming women who the Arabs had not had intercourse with, and he was not ransoming those who the Arabs had had intercourse with, so Abdullah said: As for it being written in your book that you ransom them all, and that is what the noble verse has guided you to, and this context is a condemnation of the Jews for their implementation of the matter of the Torah, which they believe to be correct and contradict its law, despite their knowledge of that and their testimony to its correctness, so for this reason they are not to be trusted with what is in it or with its transmission, and they are not to be believed in what they concealed of the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description, his mission, his exit, his migration, and other matters of his that the prophets before him, may God bless them and grant them peace, informed us about, and the Jews, may God’s curses be upon them, concealed it among themselves, and for this reason God Almighty said: So what is the reward of those who do that among you except disgrace in the life of this world meaning because of their disobedience to God’s law and command, And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe… The punishment is a recompense for their disobedience to the Book of God which is in their hands. And God is not unaware of what you do. Those are the ones who have purchased the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter. So the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided.
2:86: God the Almighty says, denouncing the Jews who were in Medina at the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what they were suffering from fighting with the Aws and Khazraj, that the Aws and Khazraj, who were the Ansar, were idol worshippers during the pre-Islamic period, and there were many wars between them, and the Jews of Medina were three tribes: Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir: allies of the Khazraj, and Banu Qurayza: allies of the Aws, so when war broke out between them, each group would fight with its allies, and the Jew would kill his enemy, and another Jew might kill another from the other group, and that is forbidden to them in their religion and the text of their book, and they would expel them from their homes and plunder what was in them of furniture, goods and money, then when the war ended, they would free the prisoners from the defeated group in accordance with the ruling of the Torah, and for this reason God the Almighty said: Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part? And for this reason God the Almighty said: "And when We took a covenant from you, that you would not shed your blood And do not expel yourselves from your homes” meaning do not kill one another, nor expel one another from his home, nor support one another against him, as God Almighty said: “Then repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is better for you with your Creator.” This is because the people of one religion are like one soul, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The example of the believers in their love, mercy, and communication with one another is like that of a single body. If one part of it is ill, the rest of the body responds to it with fever and sleeplessness.” And God Almighty said: Then you acknowledged, while you were witnessing meaning then you acknowledged knowing this covenant and its validity, while you were witnessing it. 2:87: The Blessed and Exalted describes the Children of Israel as being stubborn, obstinate, disobedient and arrogant towards the prophets, and that they only follow their own desires. So the Almighty mentioned that He gave Moses the Book, which is the Torah, but they distorted it, changed it, and disobeyed its commands and interpretations. And He sent messengers and prophets after him who rule by His law, as the Almighty said: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and scholars [associated themselves with God] by what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, and they were witnesses thereto.” The verse: And for this reason the Almighty said: And We followed him up with messengers. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Malik: We followed, and others said: We followed behind, and all are close, as the Almighty said: Then We sent Our messengers one after the other, until the prophets of the Children of Israel were sealed with Jesus, son of Mary, who came with a disobedience to the Torah in some rulings. And for this reason God gave him clear proofs, which are miracles. Ibn Abbas said: From the revival of the dead. And He created him from clay in the form of a bird, and He breathed into it and it became a bird by the permission of God, and He healed diseases, and He informed them of the unseen, and He supported them with the Holy Spirit, who is Gabriel, peace be upon him - what indicates to them his truthfulness in what he brought to them, so the Children of Israel’s denial of him intensified, and their envy and stubbornness for contradicting the Torah in some of it, as God the Almighty said, informing about Jesus: And that I may make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you, and I have come to you with a sign from your Lord verse. So the Children of Israel treated the prophets in the worst way, so a group of them denied them, and a group of them killed them, and that was only because they came to them with matters that contradicted their desires and opinions, and with the obligation of the rulings of the Torah that they had acted to contradict, so that was difficult for them so they denied them, and perhaps killed some of them, and that is why God the Almighty said: So is it that whenever there came to you a messenger with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? So a group you denied and a group you killed verse. The evidence that the Holy Spirit is Gabriel, as Ibn Masoud stated in his interpretation of this verse, and Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Kaab, Ismail ibn Khalid, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Atiyah Al-Awfi and Qatadah followed him in this, with the Almighty’s saying: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart that you may be among the warners, is what Al-Bukhari said. Ibn Abi Al-Zinad said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed a pulpit for Hassan ibn Thabit in the mosque, and he would defend the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, support Hassan with the Holy Spirit as he defended your Prophet. This is from Al-Bukhari as a suspended hadith, and Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Sirin and Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ali ibn Hajar and Ismail ibn Musa Al-Fazari, all three of them, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Al-Zinad, on the authority of his father and Hisham ibn Urwah, both of them on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic, and it is the hadith of Abu Al-Zinad. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: That Umar ibn al-Khattab passed by Hassan while he was reciting poetry in the mosque, so he looked at him and said: I used to recite poetry in it and there was someone better than you in it. Then he turned to Abu Hurayrah and said: I ask you by God, did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Answer on my behalf, O God, support him with the Holy Spirit. He said: O God, yes. And in some narrations: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Hassan, Satirize them - or incite them - and Gabriel is with you. And in Hassan’s poetry, he said: Gabriel is the Messenger of God among us, and there is no concealment in the Holy Spirit. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Hussein Al-Makki told me, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab Al-Ash'ari: "A group of Jews asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Tell us about the spirit. He said: I ask you by God and by His days with the Children of Israel, do you know that it is Gabriel who comes to me? They said: Yes." And in Sahih Ibn Hibban, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Holy Spirit inspired in my heart that no soul will die until it has completed its provision and its appointed time, so fear God and be fair in your request." Other sayings - Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah told us, Munjab bin Al-Harith told us, Bishr told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We supported him with the Holy Spirit. He said: It is the greatest name by which Jesus revived the dead. Ibn Jarir said: I was told by Al-Munjab and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair. Al-Qurtubi also narrated it from Ubaid bin Umair who said: It is the greatest name. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: The spirit is the guardians over the angels. Abu Jaafar Al-Razi said from Al-Rabi bin Anas: Al-Quds is the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and this is the saying of Ka’b. Al-Qurtubi narrated from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri that they said: Al-Quds is God, the Most High, and His spirit is Gabriel, and this is the saying of Ka’b. Al-Qurtubi narrated from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri that they said: Al-Quds is God, the Most High, and His spirit is Gabriel. So based on this is the first saying. Al-Suddi said: Al-Quds is the blessing. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Al-Quds: Purity. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus bin Abdul-Ala told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of God Almighty: And We supported him with the Holy Spirit, he said: God supported Jesus with the Gospel as a spirit just as He made the Qur’an a spirit. Both are spirits from God, as God Almighty said: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. Then Ibn Jarir said: The most correct interpretation of that is the saying of the one who said: The spirit in this place is Gabriel, for God Almighty informed that He supported Jesus with it as He informed in His words, “When God said, O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Holy Spirit so that you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel,” the verse, so He mentioned that He supported him with it. So if the spirit with which He supported him was the Gospel, then His words: When I supported you with the Holy Spirit so that you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel, would be a repetition of a meaningless statement, and God Almighty It is more honorable and sublime that He addresses His servants with what does not benefit them with it. I said And among the evidence that it is Gabriel is what was presented at the beginning of the context, and praise be to God. Al-Zamakhshari said, with the Holy Spirit, with the Holy Spirit, as you say: Hatim al-Joud and a man of truth, and he described it as holy as he said: and a spirit from Him, so he described it with specialization and proximity as an honor. And it was said: because the loins and the wombs did not contain it, and it was said: with Gabriel. It was said: with the Gospel as he said in the Qur’an: a spirit from Our command. And it was said: in the name of the Greatest God who used to revive the dead with His remembrance, so his words included another statement, which is that what is meant is the spirit of Jesus himself, the holy and purified. Al-Zamakhshari said in the words of God Almighty: So a party you denied and a party you killed, He did not say and a party you killed, because he intended by that to describe them in the future also because they tried to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with poison and magic, and he, peace be upon him, said during his death illness: The food of Khaybar has not ceased to come back to me, so this is the time for my aorta to be severed. I said And this hadith is in Sahih al-Bukhari and others.
2:88: Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ meaning in coverings. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ meaning they do not understand. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ meaning they do not understand. Mujahid said: And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ meaning they have a covering over them. Ikrimah said: They have a seal over them. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They do not understand. Al-Suddi said: They say, ‘Its cover,’ meaning it is a covering. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So you do not comprehend or understand. Mujahid and Qatada said: Ibn Abbas read Ghalaf, with a damma on the lam, and it is the plural of ghalaf, meaning our hearts are the vessels of all knowledge, so we do not need your knowledge. Ibn Abbas and Ata’ said this. Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief, meaning God has expelled them and distanced them from all good. So little do they believe. Qatada said: Its meaning is: No. Only a few of them believe. And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered’ is like His saying, And they said, ‘Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us’. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His saying, covered, he said: You say, My heart is covered, so nothing of what you say reaches it. He recited, And they said, ‘Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us’ This is what Ibn Jarir preferred, and he cited as evidence what was narrated from the hadith of Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali from Abu al-Bukhtari from Hudhayfah who said: Hearts are of four types, and among them he mentioned a covered heart that has incurred wrath, and that is the heart of the disbeliever. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Arzami told us, my father told us, from my grandfather, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan regarding His saying, Our hearts are covered, he said: They are not circumcised. The meaning of this statement goes back to what was mentioned previously about the impurity of their hearts and that they are far from goodness. Another statement - Ad-Dahhak said from Ibn Abbas, And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ he said: They say, our hearts are covered and filled, and they do not need the knowledge of Muhammad or anyone else. Atiyah Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ meaning, vessels for action. This is the meaning of the reading of some of the Ansar in it, as narrated by Ibn Jarir. They said: Our hearts are covered, with a damma on the lam, as Al-Zamakhshari transmitted, meaning the plural of ghalf, meaning vessels, meaning that they claimed that their hearts were filled with knowledge that they did not need any other knowledge, just as they used to boast of the knowledge of the Torah. For this reason, the Almighty said: Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief, so little do they believe, meaning that the matter is not as they claimed, rather their hearts are cursed and sealed, as He said in Surat al-Nisa 4:And their saying, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief, so they believe not except a little. They differed regarding the meaning of His statement: So little do they believe, and His statement: So little do they believe, so some of them said: So few of them believe, and little: their little faith means that they believe in what Moses brought them regarding the matter of the afterlife, reward, and punishment, but it is a faith that does not benefit them because it is overwhelmed by what they disbelieved in that which came to them. By Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: They were not believers in anything. Rather, he said: They rarely believe and they are disbelievers in everything, just as the Arabs say: I have rarely seen anything like this, meaning I have never seen anything like this. Al-Kisa’i said: The Arabs say: Whoever commits adultery in a land that rarely grows, meaning it does not grow anything. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. And God knows best.
2:89: God Almighty says: And when there came to them, meaning the Jews, a Book from God, which is the Qur’an that was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, confirming what was with them, meaning of the Torah. And His statement, And before that they used to pray for victory over those who disbelieved, meaning that before the coming of this Messenger with this Book, they used to pray for victory over their enemies from the polytheists when they fought them, saying: A prophet will be sent at the end of time, with whom we will kill you as ‘Aad and Iram were killed, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Asim ibn ‘Amr, on the authority of Qatadah al-Ansari, on the authority of some of their elders, he said: By God, this story was revealed about us and them, meaning the Ansar and the Jews who were their neighbors, meaning: “And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them, and before that they used to pray for victory over those who disbelieved. But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it,” they said: “We had prevailed over them by force for a long time in the Age of Ignorance, and we are people of polytheism, and they are people of the Book, and they say: A prophet will be sent now.” We will follow him, his time has come, so we will kill you with him as the people of Aad and Iram were killed. When God sent His Messenger from Quraysh and we followed him, they disbelieved in him. God the Most High says: “But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.” Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And before that they used to pray for victory over those who disbelieved, he said: They used to pray for victory, saying: We will help Muhammad against them, but they are not like that, rather they lie. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me, Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That the Jews used to pray for victory over the Aws and Khazraj through the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before his mission. When God sent him from the Arabs, they disbelieved in him and denied what they used to say about him. So Muadh bin Jabal, Bishr bin Al-Bara’ bin Ma’rur, and Dawud bin Salamah said to them: O group of Jews, fear God and submit, for you used to pray for victory over us through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while we were polytheists, and you used to tell us that he was sent and describe him according to his description. So Salam bin Mishkam, brother of Banu Nadir: He did not bring us anything that we know of. What is it that we used to mention to you? So God revealed regarding that from their saying: And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them the verse. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved meaning: They used to pray for victory through the uprising of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the polytheists of the Arabs, meaning by that the People of the Book. So when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent and they saw him from among others, they disbelieved in him and envied him. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The Jews used to pray for victory through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the polytheists of the Arabs, saying: O God, send this Prophet whose name we find written with us so that we may torment the polytheists and kill them. When God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they saw that he was not from them, they disbelieved in him out of envy of the Arabs, even though they knew that he was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God the Most High said: “But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.” Qatada said: And before that, they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved. He said: And they used to say: A prophet will come. But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. Mujahid said: “But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.” He said: They are the Jews.
2:90: Mujahid said, How evil is that for which they have sold their souls. The Jews bought the truth with falsehood and concealed what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought by making it clear. Al-Suddi said, How evil is that for which they have sold their souls. He said, They sold their souls. He said, "How evil is that for which they were satisfied and turned to it from disbelief in what God revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, instead of believing in him, supporting him, and aiding him. What drove them to do that was transgression, envy, and hatred for "that God should send down from His grace upon whomever He wills of His servants." There is no greater envy than this. Ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Sa`id, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, "How evil is that for which they have sold their souls, that they should disbelieve in what God has revealed, envying that God should send down from His grace upon whomever He wills of His servants." That is, that God made it from other than them. "So they incurred wrath upon wrath." Ibn `Abbas said, in wrath upon wrath, so He became angry with them for what they had neglected of the Torah, which is With them, and He became angry with their disbelief in this Prophet whom God sent to them I said and the meaning of they deserved is they deserved and deserved and settled with anger upon anger, and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: God became angry with them for their disbelief in the Gospel and Jesus, then God became angry with them for their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the Qur’an, and from Ikrimah and Qatadah something similar, Al-Suddi said: As for the first anger, it was when He became angry with them regarding the calf, and as for the second anger, He became angry with them when they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from Ibn Abbas something similar. And the Almighty said: And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment. Since their disbelief was caused by oppression and envy, and the origin of that was arrogance, they were met with humiliation and degradation in this world and the hereafter, as the Almighty said: Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell in humiliation. That is, humiliated, contemptible, abject, and resentful. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us, Ibn Ajlan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection like ants in the form of people, and everything of smallness will rise above them until they enter a prison in Hell called Bolus, and the fire of the fire will rise above them, and they will be given to drink from the mud of corruption, the juice of the people of Hell.”
2:91: God Almighty says: And when it is said to them meaning the Jews and their likes from the People of the Book Believe in what God has revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe him and follow him they say, ‘We believe in what was revealed to us’ meaning believing in what was revealed to us of the Torah and the Gospel is sufficient for us and we do not accept anything but that and they disbelieve in what is after it meaning what comes after it and it is the truth confirming what is with them meaning and they know that what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the truth confirming what is with them is in the accusative case as a state, meaning in the state of his believing what is with them of the Torah and the Gospel, so the argument is established against them with that, as God Almighty said: Those to whom We gave the Scripture know it as they know their own sons then God Almighty said: Then why did you kill the prophets of God before, if you were believers meaning if you were truthful in your claim to believe in what was revealed to you, then why did you kill the prophets who came to you with confirmation of the Torah that is in your hands and ruling by it and not abrogating it, and you know Did you believe them? You killed them out of oppression, stubbornness and arrogance towards the Messengers of God. You follow nothing but whims, opinions and desires, as God the Almighty said: So, whenever there came to you a Messenger with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? So a party you denied and a party you killed. Al-Suddi said: In this verse, God the Almighty reproaches them: “Say: Why then did you kill the Prophets of God before, if you were believers?” Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews of the Children of Israel, when you say to them, Believe in what God has revealed, they say, We believe in what has been revealed to us. Why did you kill, O group of Jews, if you were believers in what God has revealed? God has forbidden in the Book that He revealed to you, killing them. Rather, He has commanded you to follow them, obey them and believe in them. This is from God as a denial of their saying, We believe in what has been revealed to us, and as a reproach to them. And indeed, Moses came to you with clear proofs, meaning with clear signs and conclusive evidence that he is the Messenger of God and that there is no god but God. The clear signs are: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff, the hand, the parting of the sea and their shade with clouds, the manna, the quails, the stone, and other signs that they witnessed. Then you took the calf, i.e., as a deity other than God, in the time of Moses and his days. And His saying: after him, i.e. after he left you to the mountain to commune with God Almighty, as God Almighty said: And the people of Moses took after him from their ornaments a calf, a body that lowed, “and you are wrongdoers,” i.e., you are wrongdoers in this action that you did by worshipping the calf, and you know that there is no god but God, as God Almighty said: And when their hands fell and they saw that they had gone astray, they said, ‘If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.’

2:93: God Almighty enumerates their mistakes, their violation of the covenant, their insolence and their turning away from it, until He lifted the mountain upon them until they accepted it and then violated it. For this reason, They said, ‘We hear and disobey.’ The explanation of that has already been presented. And they made the calf drink into their hearts because of their disbelief. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah. And they made the calf drink into their hearts because of their disbelief. He said, they made its love drink until it reached their hearts. Abu al-Aaliyah and al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said the same. Imam Ahmad said: Issam ibn Khalid told us, Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Maryam al-Ghasani told me, on the authority of Khalid ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Bilal ibn Abi al-Darda’, on the authority of Abi al-Darda’, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, Loving something blinds and deafens. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Haywah ibn Shuraih, on the authority of Baqiyah, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Maryam, on his authority. Al-Suddi said: Moses, peace be upon him, took the calf and slaughtered it with a file, then scattered it in The sea, then there was no sea that flowed on that day except that something fell into it, then Moses said to them, drink from it, so they drank, and whoever loved it came out with gold on his drinkers, and that is when God Almighty says: And they drank the calf into their hearts. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ammarah bin Umair and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Moses went to the calf, and put the files on it and cooled it with them, and he was on the bank of a river, and no one who worshipped the calf drank from that water except that his face turned yellow like gold, and Saeed bin Jubair said: And they drank the calf into their hearts, he said: When the calf was burned, it cooled and then blew up, so they sipped the water until their faces returned to saffron, and al-Qurtubi narrated from the book of al-Qushayri: that no one who worshipped the calf drank from it except that he went crazy, then al-Qurtubi said: This is something other than what is here, because the intended meaning of this context is that it appeared on their lips and faces, and what is mentioned here is: They had drunk the calf into their hearts, meaning while they were worshipping it. Then he recited the words of Al-Nabigha about his wife, Uthma: Othma's love has penetrated my heart, so his desert walks with the hidden He penetrated where no drink, no sorrow, and no joy reached. When I remember the covenant, I almost fly, if only a human could fly. And His saying, Say, ‘How evil is that which your faith enjoins upon you, if you are believers.’ That is, how evil is what you have relied upon in ancient and modern times, from your disbelief in the signs of God, and your opposition to the prophets, then your reliance in your disbelief on Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the greatest of your sins and the most severe matter for you, since you disbelieved in the Seal of the Messengers and Master of the Prophets and Messengers, who was sent to all of mankind. So how can you call for yourselves to believe, when you have committed these ugly deeds: from your breaking of covenants, your disbelief in the signs of God, and your worship of the calf instead of God?
2:94: Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively yours and not the people's, then wish for death, if you should be truthful." That is, claim death on the authority of which of the two groups is more lying, so they refused that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. "And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers." That is, with their knowledge of what they have of knowledge, and even disbelief in that, and if they had wished for it on the day He said that to them, there would not have remained a Jew on the earth who did not die. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So wish for death, so ask for death. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari on the authority of Ikrimah, his statement: So wish for death, if you should be truthful. He said: Ibn Abbas said: If the Jews wished for death, they would have died. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Uthman told us: I heard al-A’mash say: I do not think it was except on the authority of al-Munhal, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If they wished for death, one of them would choke on his saliva. These are authentic chains of transmission back to Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir said in his interpretation: It has reached us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If the Jews wished for death, they would die and see their places in Hell. And if those who challenged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were to go out, they would return without finding family or wealth.” Abu Kurayb told us that, Zakariya bin Adi told us, Ubaydullah bin Amr told us on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Yazid al-Ruqi, Furat told us on the authority of Abdul Karim with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Ahmad told us, Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Bashar told us, Surur bin al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Mansur, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The saying of God: They would not have wished for it because of what their hands have put forth. I said: Have you seen if they loved death when it was said to them, Wish for death, would you think they would have died? He said: No, by God, they would not have died even if they wished for death, and they would not have wished for it, and God said what you heard: “And they will never wish for it because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.” This is strange from Al-Hasan. Then this is what Ibn Abbas interpreted the verse with, which is the specific one, and it is a supplication against which of the two groups is more lying, them or the Muslims, in the manner of a mutual cursing. Ibn Jarir transmitted it from Qatadah, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, may God have mercy on them. Similar to this verse is the statement of God in Surat Al-Jumu’ah: “Say, ‘O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of mankind, then wish for death, if you should be truthful.’ But they will never wish for it because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. Say, ‘Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.’” So the curses of God are upon them, because they claimed that they are the sons of God. And his beloved ones, they said: None will enter Paradise except those who were Jews or Christians, they were called to the Mubahala and to pray against the most lying of the two groups among them or among the Muslims, when they refrained from that, everyone knew that they were wrongdoers, because if they were certain of what they were doing, they would have gone ahead with that, but when they delayed, their lie was known. This is like the Messenger of God called the delegation of Najran from the Christians after the proof was established against them in the debate and their arrogance and stubbornness to the Mubahala, so he said: “So whoever argues with you about him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us pray together and invoke the curse of God upon the liars.” So when they saw that, some of the people said to each other: By God, if you pray together with this Prophet, not a single eye will remain among you that blinks, so at that time they inclined towards peace, and paid the Jizya willingly while they were humiliated, so he imposed it on them, and sent with them Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah as a trustee, and something similar to this meaning or something close to it is the saying of God Almighty For his Prophet to say to the polytheists, Say, ‘Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend to him a term.’ That is, whoever is in error among us and you, then God has increased what he is in, extended to him, and led him astray, as will be explained in its place, God willing. As for those who interpreted the verse to mean if you are truthful, that is, in your claim, then wish for death now, and these people did not resort to the Mubahala, as was decided by a group of theologians and others, and Ibn Jarir leaned towards it after he approached the first statement, for he said: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you, apart from the people,” the verse, this verse is among what God, the Most High, used as evidence for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the Jews who were among his immigrants, and He exposed their rabbis and scholars with it, and that is because God, the Most High, commanded His Prophet to a just case in what was between him and them of disagreement, just as He commanded him to call the other group of Christians when they disagreed with him about Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and argued with him about him to a decisive Mubahala between him and them, so He said to the group of Jews: If you are right, then wish for death, for that will not harm you if you are right in what you claim of faith and the closeness of status from God to you so that He may grant you your wish of death if you wish, for it is only You will find rest from the fatigue, toil, and hardship of this world and will attain the proximity of God in His gardens if the matter is as you claim, that the Hereafter is exclusively yours and not ours. If you are not given it, people will know that you are the liars and we are the ones who are right in our claim, and our affair and your affair will be revealed to them. So the Jews refused to answer that because they knew that if they wished for death, they would perish and their world would be lost and they would be in eternal disgrace in the Hereafter, just as the group of Christians who argued with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Jesus refused to answer the Mubahala when they were called to the Mubahala. This statement is good in the beginning, but its end is questionable, because the proof against them does not appear on this interpretation, as it is said: It does not necessarily follow from their belief that they are truthful in their claim that they wish for death, because there is no necessary connection between the existence of righteousness and wishing for death, and how many righteous people do not wish for death, but rather wish to live long in order to increase in goodness and raise their status in Paradise, as came in the hadith: The best of you is he whose life is long and whose deeds are good. And they have the right to say on this: So here you are, O Muslims, believing that you are the people of Paradise, and you do not wish for death when you are healthy, so how do you hold us accountable for what is not required of you? All of this arose from the interpretation of the verse in this sense. As for the interpretation of Ibn Abbas: None of that is required of him. Rather, it was said to them, “Half-words, if you believe that you are the friends of God without the people, and that you are the sons of God and His beloved, and that you are from the people of Paradise and those other than you are from the people of Hell, then engage in a mutual cursing on that and supplicate against the liars among you or others, and know that the mutual cursing will inevitably eradicate the liar.” So when they were certain of that and recognized his truthfulness, they refrained from engaging in a mutual cursing because they knew of their lies, their fabrications, and their concealment of the truth about the description and attributes of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they knew him as they knew their sons and were certain of it. So everyone knew their falsehood, their shame, their misguidance, and their stubbornness. Upon them are the curses of God that continue until the Day of Resurrection. This mutual cursing was called a wish, because every person who is right wishes that God would destroy the one who is wronging him, especially if that was an argument for him in clarifying his truth and making him appear. The mutual cursing was by death because life, according to them, is life. They are very dear to them because they know of their bad end after death, and for this reason God the Almighty said: “And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life” meaning for a long life because they know of their bad end and their losing end with God, because this world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. They wish they could delay the Hereafter for as much as they can, and what they fear will inevitably happen to them, even though they are more greedy than the polytheists who have no book. This is from the category of linking the specific to the general. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And who are those who associate others with God? He said: The non-Arabs. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of al-Thawri, and he said: It is authentic according to their criteria, but they did not include it. He said: They agreed on the chain of transmission of the interpretation of the Companion, and al-Hasan al-Basri said: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life. He said: The hypocrite is the most greedy of people, and more greedy than the polytheist for life. One of them would like, that is, one of the Jews would like, as the order of the context indicates. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: One of them would like, that is, one of the Magians, and he goes back to the first, if he could live a thousand years. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: One of them would like to live a thousand years. He said: It is like the saying of the Persian Dah Hazarsal, who says: Ten thousand years. And it was also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair himself, and Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us: I heard my father say: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, One of them would like to live a thousand years, he said: It is the saying of the Persians, the Hazarsal of Nowruz and the Mahrajan. And Mujahid said, One of them would like to live a thousand years, he said: Sin made them love a long life. And Mujahid bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Saeed or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live a long life, meaning it will not save him from the punishment, because the polytheist does not hope for resurrection after death, so he loves a long life, and the Jew has known what shame he will have in the Hereafter, because he wasted what he had of knowledge. And Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live a long life, he said: They are those who opposed Gabriel. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Ibn Omar said: That will not save him from the punishment, nor will it save him from it. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said about this verse: The Jews are more eager for life than these people, and these people would like one of them to live a thousand years, but it will not save him from the punishment even if he lives a thousand years, just as the life of Iblis did not benefit him since he was a disbeliever. And God is Seeing of what they do, meaning He is All-Knowing of what His servants do of good and evil, and He will reward every worker according to his work.

This is like the Messenger of God called the delegation of Najran from the Christians after the proof was established against them in the debate and their arrogance and stubbornness to the Mubahala, so he said: “So whoever argues with you about him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us pray together and invoke the curse of God upon the liars.” So when they saw that, some of the people said to each other: By God, if you pray together with this Prophet, not a single eye will remain among you that blinks, so at that time they inclined towards peace, and paid the Jizya willingly while they were humiliated, so he imposed it on them, and sent with them Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah as a trustee, and something similar to this meaning or something close to it is the saying of God Almighty For his Prophet to say to the polytheists, Say, ‘Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend to him a term.’ That is, whoever is in error among us and you, then God has increased what he is in, extended to him, and led him astray, as will be explained in its place, God willing. As for those who interpreted the verse to mean if you are truthful, that is, in your claim, then wish for death now, and these people did not resort to the Mubahala, as was decided by a group of theologians and others, and Ibn Jarir leaned towards it after he approached the first statement, for he said: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you, apart from the people,” the verse, this verse is among what God, the Most High, used as evidence for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the Jews who were among his immigrants, and He exposed their rabbis and scholars with it, and that is because God, the Most High, commanded His Prophet to a just case in what was between him and them of disagreement, just as He commanded him to call the other group of Christians when they disagreed with him about Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and argued with him about him to a decisive Mubahala between him and them, so He said to the group of Jews: If you are right, then wish for death, for that will not harm you if you are right in what you claim of faith and the closeness of status from God to you so that He may grant you your wish of death if you wish, for it is only You will find rest from the fatigue, toil, and hardship of this world and will attain the proximity of God in His gardens if the matter is as you claim, that the Hereafter is exclusively yours and not ours. If you are not given it, people will know that you are the liars and we are the ones who are right in our claim, and our affair and your affair will be revealed to them. This statement is good in the beginning, but its end is questionable, because the proof against them does not appear on this interpretation, as it is said: It does not necessarily follow from their belief that they are truthful in their claim that they wish for death, because there is no necessary connection between the existence of righteousness and wishing for death, and how many righteous people do not wish for death, but rather wish to live long in order to increase in goodness and raise their status in Paradise, as came in the hadith: The best of you is he whose life is long and whose deeds are good. And they have the right to say on this: So here you are, O Muslims, believing that you are the people of Paradise, and you do not wish for death when you are healthy, so how do you hold us accountable for what is not required of you? All of this arose from the interpretation of the verse in this sense. As for the interpretation of Ibn Abbas: None of that is required of him. Rather, it was said to them, “Half-words, if you believe that you are the friends of God without the people, and that you are the sons of God and His beloved, and that you are from the people of Paradise and those other than you are from the people of Hell, then engage in a mutual cursing on that and supplicate against the liars among you or others, and know that the mutual cursing will inevitably eradicate the liar.” So when they were certain of that and recognized his truthfulness, they refrained from engaging in a mutual cursing because they knew of their lies, their fabrications, and their concealment of the truth about the description and attributes of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they knew him as they knew their sons and were certain of it. So everyone knew their falsehood, their shame, their misguidance, and their stubbornness. Upon them are the curses of God that continue until the Day of Resurrection. This mutual cursing was called a wish, because every person who is right wishes that God would destroy the one who is wronging him, especially if that was an argument for him in clarifying his truth and making him appear. The mutual cursing was by death because life, according to them, is life. They are very dear to them because they know of their bad end after death, and for this reason God the Almighty said: “And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life” meaning for a long life because they know of their bad end and their losing end with God, because this world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. They wish they could delay the Hereafter for as much as they can, and what they fear will inevitably happen to them, even though they are more greedy than the polytheists who have no book. This is from the category of linking the specific to the general. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And who are those who associate others with God? He said: The non-Arabs. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of al-Thawri, and he said: It is authentic according to their criteria, but they did not include it. He said: They agreed on the chain of transmission of the interpretation of the Companion, and al-Hasan al-Basri said: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life. He said: The hypocrite is the most greedy of people, and more greedy than the polytheist for life. One of them would like, that is, one of the Jews would like, as the order of the context indicates. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: One of them would like, that is, one of the Magians, and he goes back to the first, if he could live a thousand years. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: One of them would like to live a thousand years. He said: It is like the saying of the Persian Dah Hazarsal, who says: Ten thousand years. And it was also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair himself, and Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us: I heard my father say: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, One of them would like to live a thousand years, he said: It is the saying of the Persians, the Hazarsal of Nowruz and the Mahrajan. And Mujahid said, One of them would like to live a thousand years, he said: Sin made them love a long life. And Mujahid bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Saeed or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live a long life, meaning it will not save him from the punishment, because the polytheist does not hope for resurrection after death, so he loves a long life, and the Jew has known what shame he will have in the Hereafter, because he wasted what he had of knowledge. And Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live a long life, he said: They are those who opposed Gabriel. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Ibn Omar said: That will not save him from the punishment, nor will it save him from it. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said about this verse: The Jews are more eager for life than these people, and these people would like one of them to live a thousand years, but it will not save him from the punishment even if he lives a thousand years, just as the life of Iblis did not benefit him since he was a disbeliever. And God is Seeing of what they do, meaning He is All-Knowing of what His servants do of good and evil, and He will reward every worker according to his work.

2:97: Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir al-Tabari, may God have mercy on him, said: All scholars of interpretation agreed that this verse was revealed in response to the Jews of the Children of Israel, when they claimed that Gabriel was their enemy and that Michael was their guardian. Then they differed about the reason for which they said that. Some of them said: The reason for their saying that was because of a debate that took place between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the matter of his prophethood mentioning who said that. Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus ibn Bakir told us, on the authority of `Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: A group of Jews attended the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, tell us about characteristics that we ask you about that only a prophet would know. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ask about whatever you wish, but give me God’s protection and what Jacob took from his sons, that if I tell you about something and you recognize it, you will follow me in Islam. They said: That is for you. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ask about whatever you wish. They said: Tell us about four things that we will ask you about. Tell us which food Israel prohibited for himself before the Torah was revealed? And tell us about the woman’s water and the man’s water, and how the male and female are formed from it? And tell us about this unlettered prophet in the Torah, and who is his guardian from the angels? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have a covenant from God that if I inform you, you will all follow me. So they gave him whatever covenant and pact God willed. He said: I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that Israel Jacob fell seriously ill and his illness lasted a long time? He made a vow to God that if God cured him of his illness, he would forbid him the food and drink he loved the most. The food he loved the most was camel meat, and the drink he loved the most was camel milk. They said: O God, yes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, bear witness against them. I ask you by God, there is no god but Him, who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that the man’s semen is thick and white, and the woman’s semen is thin and yellow, so whichever of them rises above will have a child and will resemble him, by God’s permission? If the man’s semen rises above the woman’s semen, the child will be a boy, by God’s permission. If the woman’s semen rises above the man’s semen, the child will be a girl, by God’s permission. They said: O God, yes. He said: O God, bear witness. I ask you by God, who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that the eyes of this illiterate prophet sleep but his heart does not? They said: Yes, by God. He said: O God, bear witness. They said: You now, so tell us who is your guardian from the angels, then we will have intercourse with you or leave you. He said: My guardian is Gabriel, and God never sent a prophet except that he is his guardian. They said: Then we will leave you, and if your guardian were other than him from the angels, we would follow you and believe you. He said: What prevents you from believing him? They said: He is our enemy. So God the Almighty revealed: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by God’s permission, confirming what was before it” to His saying: If they only knew. Then they incurred wrath upon wrath.” Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim and Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamid in his Tafsir on the authority of Ahmad ibn Yunus, both of them on the authority of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, and Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi on the authority of Abd al-Hamid in a similar manner. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated it, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, and he mentioned it as a mursal and added to it: “They said: Then tell us about the spirit.” He said: I ask you by God and by His days with the Children of Israel, do you know that he is Gabriel and he is the one who comes to me? They said: O God, yes, but he is an enemy to us, and he is an angel who only comes with hardship and bloodshed. If it were not for that, we would have followed you. So God the Almighty revealed about them: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel” to His saying: They do not know. And he said: Imam Ahmad: Abu Ahmad told us, Abdullah bin Al-Waleed Al-Ajli told us, on the authority of Bakir bin Shihab, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu Al-Qasim, tell us about five things, for if you inform us of them, we will know that you are a prophet and we will follow you. So he took from them what Israel took from his sons, when he said: God is the witness over what we say. He said: Bring them. They said: So tell us about the sign of a prophet? He said: His eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep. They said: Tell us how a woman is made feminine? And how a man is made masculine? He said: The two waters meet, so if the man’s water rises above the woman’s water, she becomes masculine, and if the woman’s water rises above the man’s water, she becomes feminine. They said: Tell us what Israel forbade himself? He said: He used to suffer from sciatica, and he did not find anything that suited him except the milk of such-and-such. Ahmad said: Some of them said: He meant camels, so he forbade their meat. They said: You have spoken the truth. They said: Tell us, what is this thunder? He said: An angel from the angels of God Almighty, who is assigned to the clouds, with his hands or in his hands is a whip of fire with which he drives the clouds where God Almighty commands him. They said: What is this voice that we hear? He said: His voice. They said: You have spoken the truth. They said: There is only one thing left, and it is the one that we will follow if you tell us about it, that there is no prophet but that he has an angel who brings him report, so tell us who your companion is? He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him. They said: Gabriel is the one who descends with war, fighting and torment. He is our enemy. If you had said Michael, who descends with mercy, rain and plants, he would have been. So God Almighty revealed: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - for he has brought it down upon your heart by permission of God” to the end of the verse. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah bin Al-Waleed with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Sunayd said in his interpretation on the authority of Hajjaj bin Muhammad on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza informed me that the Jews asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his companion who descends with revelation. He said: Gabriel. They said: He is our enemy and does not come except with war, hardship and fighting. So the verse was revealed: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel” 2:10. Ibn Jarir said: Mujahid said: The Jews said: O Muhammad, Gabriel only descends with hardship, war and fighting. He is our enemy. So the verse was revealed: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel” 2:10. Al-Bukhari said: God Almighty’s statement: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel 2:10. Ikrimah said: Gabriel, Mika and Israf are slaves. Il: God, Abdullah bin Munir told us, Abdullah bin Bakr heard, Humaid told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: Abdullah bin Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in a land collecting dung, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I am going to ask you about three things that only a prophet knows: What is the first sign of the Hour, what is the first food of the people of Paradise, and what will draw a father to his father or to his mother? He said: Gabriel told me this just now. He said: Gabriel? He said: Yes. He said: That is the enemy of the Jews from the angels, so he recited this verse: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart. “As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather people from the east to the west. As for the first food that the people of Paradise will eat, it is the extra liver of a fish. If a man’s semen precedes a woman’s semen, the child will be conceived, and if a woman’s semen precedes a woman, she will be conceived.” He said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God. O Messenger of God, the Jews are a people of slanderers, and if they know that I have become Muslim before you ask them, they will slander me. So the Jews came and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What kind of man is Abdullah bin Salam among you? They said: The best of us and the son of the best of us, our master and the son of our master. He said: What if he becomes Muslim? They said: May God protect him from that. So Abdullah came out and said: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. They said: He is our evil and the son of our evil, and they attacked him. He said: This is what I feared, O Messenger of God. Al-Bukhari alone narrated it from this source, and they narrated it from another source from Anas in a similar manner. In Sahih Muslim, from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is close to this context, as will come in its place, God willing. Al-Bukhari’s narration, as mentioned above, from Ikrimah is the well-known one that El is God. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it from Khasif, from Ikrimah, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated it from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Ikrimah, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahan, from Ishaq ibn Mansur, from Qays ibn Asim, from Ikrimah, that he said: Gabriel’s name is Abdullah, and Michael’s name is Abdullah. El is God. Yazid al-Nahwi narrated it from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, in the same manner. More than one of the Salaf said the same, as will come soon. Some people say: El is an expression for Abd, and the other word is the name of God, because the word El does not change in all of them. Fawzan is Abdullah Abd al-Rahman Abd al-Malik. Abdul Quddus Abdul Salam Abdul Kafi Abdul Jalil, so Abdul is present in all of this, and the names added to it differ, as well as Gabriel, Michael, Azrael, Israfil, and the like, and in the speech of non-Arabs they put the added to it before the added, and God knows best. Then Ibn Jarir said, and others said: Rather, the reason for their saying that was because of a debate that took place between them and Umar ibn al-Khattab regarding the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace mention those who said that. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Rib’i ibn Ulayyah told me, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: Umar went down to al-Rawha’ and saw men rushing to stones to pray to them, so he said: What is wrong with these people? They said: They claim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed here. He said: He disliked that and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was overtaken by prayer in a valley and prayed there, then he departed and left it, then he began to tell them, and he said: I used to witness the Jews during their schools and I was amazed at how the Torah confirmed the Qur’an and how the Qur’an confirmed the Torah. While I was with them one day, they said: O Ibn al-Khattab, none of your companions are more beloved to us than you. I said: Why is that? They said: Because you visit us and come to us. I said: I come to you and I am amazed at the Qur’an and how it confirms the Torah, and at the Torah and how it confirms the Qur’an. They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by and they said: O Ibn Al-Khattab, that is your companion, so join him. I said to them: At that time, I ask you by God, there is no god but Him, and by what He has entrusted to you of His right, and by what He has entrusted to you of His Book, do you know that he is the Messenger of God? They said: So they were silent. Then their scholar and elder said to him: He has been harsh with you, so answer him. They said: Then you are our scholar and elder, so answer him. He said: If you ask us what you ask us, then we know that he is the Messenger of God. I said: Woe to you, then you are doomed. They said: We are not doomed. I said: How is that when you know that he is the Messenger of God and you do not follow him or believe him? They said: We have an enemy from the angels and a peace from the angels, and he has linked his prophethood to our enemy from the angels. I said: Who is your enemy and your peace? They said: Our enemy is Gabriel, and our peace is Michael. They said: Gabriel is the angel of harshness, roughness, poverty, severity, torment, and the like, and Michael is the angel of mercy, compassion, leniency, and the like. He said: I said: What is their status with their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic? They said: One of them is on his right and the other is on his left. He said: I said: By Him besides Whom there is no god, they and the one between them are enemies to those who are enemies to them, and peace to those who are peaceable to them. It is not appropriate for Gabriel to be peaceable to the enemy of Michael, and it is not appropriate for Michael to be peaceable to the enemy of Gabriel. He said: Then I got up and followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I caught up with him as he was coming out of a window of the Banu so-and-so. He said: O Ibn al-Khattab, shall I not recite to you verses that were revealed before? So he recited to me: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down to your heart by permission of God - until he recited the verses. He said: I said: My father and mother are your ransom, O Messenger of God, by Him who sent you with the truth, I have come wanting to inform you and I hear the Gracious, the All-Knowing, who has preceded me to you with the report. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed al-Ashja told us, Abu Usama told us on the authority of Mujalid, Aamer told us, he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab went to the Jews and said: I ask you by Him who revealed the Torah to Moses, do you find Muhammad in your books? They said: Yes. He said: What prevents you from following him? He said: God did not send a messenger except that He made for him a guardian from the angels. Gabriel is the guardian of Muhammad and he is the one who comes to him, and he is our enemy from the angels. And Michael, we have submitted. If Michael was the one who came to him, we would have submitted. He said: Then I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what is their status with God Almighty? They said: Gabriel is on his right, and Michael is on his left. Omar said: I bear witness that they do not descend except by the permission of God. Michael would not make peace with the enemy of Gabriel, and Gabriel would not make peace with the enemy of Michael. While he was with them, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by. They said: This is your companion, O Ibn Al-Khattab. Omar went to him and God, the Almighty, had revealed: Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, God is an enemy to the disbelievers. These two chains of transmission indicate that Al-Sha’bi narrated it from Omar, but there is a break between him and Omar, as he did not live in his time. And God knows best. Ibn Jubayr said: Bashir told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that Omar bin Al-Khattab went to the Jews one day. When he returned and they welcomed him, Omar said to them: By God, I did not come to you out of love for you or desire for you, but I came to hear from you. So he asked them and they asked him, and they said: Who is the companion of your companion? He said to them: Gabriel. They said: That is our enemy from the people of heaven who reveals our secret to Muhammad, and when he comes he brings war and strife, but the companion of our companion is Michael, and when he comes he brings fertility and peace. So Omar said to them: Do you recognize Gabriel, and you deny Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? Then Omar left them and went towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to tell him their story, and he found that this verse had been revealed to him: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - for he has brought the Qur’an down upon your heart by God’s permission” (al-An’am 2:10). Then he said: Al-Muthanna told me, Adam told us, Abu Ja`far told us, Qatada told us, he said: It reached us that `Umar came to the Jews one day and mentioned something similar, and this is in the interpretation of Adam and it is also disconnected, and likewise Asbat narrated it from Al-Suddi from `Umar something similar or similar, and it is also disconnected. And Ibn Ibn Hatim said: Muhammad Ibn `Ammar told us, `Abd Al-Rahman told us, meaning Al-Dashtaki told us, Abu Ja`far told us from Hisayn Ibn `Abd Al-Rahman, from `Abd Al-Rahman, who is `Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Abi Laila: That a Jew met `Umar Ibn Al-Khattab and said: Gabriel, whom your companion mentions, is an enemy to us, so `Umar said: Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael, then indeed God is an enemy to the disbelievers. He said: So it was revealed on the tongue of `Umar, may God be pleased with him, and `Abd Ibn Hamid narrated it from Abu Al-Nadr Hashim Ibn Al-Qasim, from Abu Ja`far, who is Al-Razi, and Ibn Jarir said: Ya`qub Ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told me, Husayn Ibn `Abd Al-Rahman told us, from Ibn Abi Laila regarding his statement: God the Almighty said: Who is an enemy to Gabriel? He said: The Jews said to the Muslims: If Michael was the one who descends upon you, we would follow you, for he descends with mercy and rain, but Gabriel descends with torment and vengeance, so he is an enemy to us. He said: So this verse was revealed. Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Abdul Malik told us on the authority of Ata’ something similar. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: “Say: Who is an enemy to Gabriel?” He said: The Jews said: Gabriel is an enemy to us, because he descends with hardship and famine, and Michael descends with ease, health and fertility, so Gabriel is an enemy to us. So God the Almighty said: Who is an enemy to Gabriel? As for the interpretation of the verse, the Almighty said: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel,” then he brought it down to your heart by the permission of God, meaning whoever is hostile to Gabriel, let him know that he is the trustworthy spirit who brought down the wise remembrance to your heart from God by His permission for him to do so. He is a messenger from the messengers of God, an angel. Whoever is hostile to a messenger has been hostile to all the messengers, just as whoever believes in a messenger is obligated to believe in all the messengers, and just as whoever disbelieves in a messenger is obligated to disbelieve in all the messengers, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His messengers and wish to differentiate between God and His messengers and say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ 2:100. So He ruled that they are true disbelievers if they believe in some of the messengers and disbelieve in others. Likewise, whoever is hostile to Gabriel is an enemy of God, because Gabriel does not bring down the command of his own accord, but rather he comes down by the command of his Lord, as He said: And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord, 2:100. And God the Almighty said: “And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. * The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down * Upon your heart that you may be among the warners.” Al-Bukhari narrated in It is authentically reported on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine has declared war on Me. For this reason, God became angry with Gabriel for whoever showed enmity to him, and God the Almighty said: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by God’s permission, confirming what was before it meaning of the previous books: And guidance and good tidings for the believers meaning guidance for their hearts and good tidings for them of Paradise, and that is only for the believers, as God the Almighty said: Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guide and a cure’ 3:17. And God the Almighty said: And We send down from the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers 3:17.
