Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: On the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim that he used to read it and what was sent down to the two angels and he said: They are two giants from the people of Babylon. The proponents of this opinion explained that sending down means creation, not inspiration, as in the words of God Almighty: and what was sent down to the two angels as God Almighty said: And He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock “and We sent down iron, wherein is great strength” and He sends down for you provision from the sky and in the hadith: God has not sent down a disease except that He has sent down a cure for it and as it is said: God sent down good and evil. Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abza and Al-Hasan Al-Basri that they read and what was sent down to the two angels with a kasra on the lam. Ibn Abza said: They are David and Solomon. Al-Qurtubi said: According to this, what is also a negative. Others stopped at his words they teach people magic and what is a negative. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Al-Layth told us on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad and a man asked him about the words of God Almighty: they teach people magic and what was sent down to the two angels In Babylon, Harut and Marut.” He said: The two men teach people what was revealed to them and teach people what was not revealed to them. Al-Qasim said: I do not care which of them it was. Then he narrated on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Anas bin Ayyad on the authority of some of his companions that Al-Qasim said in this story: I do not care which of them it was, I believed in it. Many of the predecessors believed that they were two angels from heaven, and that they were sent down to earth, and what happened to them happened. A hadith was narrated on this subject by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, may God have mercy on him, as we will mention, God willing. Based on this, the combination between this and what was reported of the evidence for the infallibility of the angels is that God had previously known about these two, so it is a specification for them, so there is no contradiction then, as was previously mentioned in His knowledge of the matter of Iblis, and in His statement that he was one of the angels, based on the Almighty’s statement: And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ and they prostrated, except for Iblis, he refused. And other verses indicating this, even though the matter of Harut and Marut is as mentioned. Less severe than what happened from Satan, may God curse him. Al-Qurtubi narrated it on the authority of Ali, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, Kaab al-Ahbar, al-Suddi, and al-Kalbi.
2:101: And the Almighty said: "And they do not teach anyone until they say, 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.'" Abu Ja`far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, on the authority of Qays ibn `Ibad, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: So when the one who came to them wanted to practice magic, they forbade him with the strongest prohibition and said to him: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. This is because they knew good and evil, disbelief and faith, so they knew that magic is from disbelief. He said: So if he refused them, they ordered him to go to such and such a place, and when he came to him, he saw Satan and taught him, and when he learned him, a light came out of him, and he looked at him shining in the sky and said: Oh, what a pity! Oh, what did he do? And on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, he said in the interpretation of this verse: Yes, the two angels sent down magic to teach people the affliction with which God wanted to test people, so He took a covenant from them that they would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Qatada said: He took a covenant from them that they would not They would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, meaning a trial with which we have been afflicted, so do not disbelieve. As-Suddi said: If a person came to them wanting to practice magic, they would admonish him and say to him: Do not disbelieve, we are only a trial. If he refused, they would say to him: Go to these ashes and urinate on them. When he urinates on them, a light comes out of it and shines until it enters the sky, and that is faith. Something black like smoke comes and enters his ears, and everything, and that is the wrath of God. If he tells them about that, they would teach him magic. This is the statement of God the Most High: And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ (al-Baqarah 2:170) Sunayd said on the authority of Hajjaj on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding this verse: None would dare to practice magic except a disbeliever. As for the trial, it is the test and choice, and from it is the saying of the poet: He tempted people in their religion and left Ibn Affan in a state of evil for a long time. And also the saying of the Almighty, informing about Moses, peace be upon him, where he said: It is only your trial, meaning your trial, your test, and your examination, with which You misguide whom You will and guide whom You will. Some of them have used this verse as evidence for the disbelief of those who learn magic, and they have cited as evidence for it the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar, who told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “Whoever goes to a soothsayer or magician and believes what he says, has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.” This is a sound chain of transmission and it has other corroborating evidence. And the saying of the Almighty: And they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, meaning that people learn from Harut and Marut the science of magic and what they do with it in what they do of reprehensible actions, by which they cause separation between spouses, despite the mixing and harmony between them, and this is from the doing of the devils, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Talhah bin Nafi’, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The devil places his throne on the water and then sends out his armies among the people. The one closest to him in status is the one who causes the greatest temptation. One of them comes and says: ‘I kept on with so-and-so until I left him saying such-and-such.’ Iblis says: ‘No, by God, I did nothing!’ And one of them comes and says: ‘I did not leave him until I separated him from his family.’ He acknowledges it, brings him close, embraces him and says: ‘Yes, you are.’” The reason for separation between spouses through magic is what a man or woman imagines of the other in terms of bad appearance, character, or something similar, or a contract, or hatred, or something similar to the reasons that necessitate separation. ‘Man’ refers to a man and its feminine form is ‘woman.’ Both of them are dual, but they are not plural, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Except by the decree of God. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Except by God’s leaving him alone with what He willed. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. He said: Yes, whoever God wills, He gives them power over him, and whoever God does not will, He does not give them power over him, and they cannot do anything to anyone except by permission of God, as God the Almighty said. And in a narration from Al-Hasan, he said: This magic does not harm anyone except the one who engages in it. And the Almighty’s saying: And they learn that which harms them and does not benefit them means that it harms them in their religion and has no benefit that matches its harm. And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter means that the Jews who exchanged magic for following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that whoever did what they did, that he will have no share in the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: No share. And Abd Al-Razzaq said from Muammar from Qatadah: He will have no share in the Hereafter with God. And Abd Al-Razzaq said, and Al-Hasan said: He has no religion. And Saad said from Qatadah: He will have no share in the Hereafter He said: And the People of the Book knew in what God entrusted them with that the magician will have no share in the Hereafter. And the Almighty’s saying: “And evil is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew. And if they had believed and feared God, the reward from God would have been better, if they only knew.” The Almighty says: And evil is the substitute that they exchanged for magic in place of faith. And following the Messenger, if they had knowledge of what they were admonished with, And if they had believed and feared God, the reward from God would have been better for them. That is, if they had believed in God and His Messengers and feared the forbidden things, God’s reward for that would have been better for them than what they sought for themselves and were satisfied with, as God the Almighty said, “And those who were given knowledge said, ‘Woe to you! The reward from God is better for him who believes and does righteousness. And none is granted it except the patient.’” And the saying of And if they had believed and feared God was used as evidence by those who considered the magician to be an infidel, as is narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and a group of the Salaf. It was said: Rather, he is not an infidel, but his punishment is to behead him, as narrated by Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. They said: Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, told us on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar that he heard Bajalah ibn Abdah say: Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, wrote: Kill every male and female magician. He said: So we killed three female magicians. Al-Bukhari also included it in his Sahih. And thus it was authenticated that Hafsah, the Mother of the Believers, was bewitched by a slave girl of hers, so she ordered that she be killed. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: It was authenticated on the authority of three of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding killing the magician. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Ismail bin Muslim from Al-Hasan from Jundub Al-Azdi that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The punishment for a magician is to strike him with a sword. Then he said: We do not know it as being attributed to the Prophet except from this source, and Ismail bin Muslim is considered weak in hadith, and the correct version is from Al-Hasan from Jundub as a mursal. I said: Al-Tabarani narrated it from another source from Al-Hasan from Jundub as a mursal. And God knows best. It has been narrated from multiple chains of transmission that Al-Walid bin Uqbah had a magician playing in front of him. He would strike a man’s head and then shout at him, and his head would be returned to him. The people said: Glory be to God, He brings the dead back to life. A righteous man from the Muhajireen saw him, so the next day he came with his sword wrapped around him and went to play that game. The man drew his sword and struck the magician’s neck, and said: If he is telling the truth, then let him revive himself. Then he recited the verse of God, Do you then practice magic while you are seeing? Al-Walid became angry because he did not ask his permission to do so, so he imprisoned him and then released him. And God knows best. Imam Abu Bakr Al-Khalal said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Abu Ishaq told me on the authority of Haritha, who said: There was a man playing with one of the princes, then a soldier came with his sword drawn and killed him. He said: I think he was a magician. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, attributed the story of Umar and Hafsa to magic that constitutes polytheism, and God knows best. Chapter Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated in his interpretation of the Mu’tazila that they denied the existence of magic. He said: And perhaps they disbelieved whoever believed in its existence. He said: As for the Sunnis, they allowed that the magician could fly in the air and turn a human into a donkey, and a donkey into a human, except that they said: God creates things when the magician says those incantations and specific words. As for the one who has an effect on that being the heavens and the stars, then no, contrary to the philosophers, astrologers, and Sabians. Then he provided evidence for the occurrence of magic and that it is by the creation of God Almighty by His Almighty saying: And they do not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. And from the report that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bewitched, and that magic worked on him and the story of that woman with Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and what that woman mentioned about her coming to Babylon and learning magic. He said: And from what is mentioned in this chapter of many stories, then he said after this. The fifth issue is that knowledge of magic is not ugly or forbidden - the scholars agreed on this because knowledge in itself is noble, and also because of the generality of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” And because if magic were not known, it would not be possible to differentiate between it and a miracle, and knowledge that a miracle is a miracle is obligatory, and whatever the obligation depends on is obligatory. This requires that acquiring knowledge of magic be obligatory, and whatever is obligatory, how can it be forbidden and ugly? This is his wording on this issue, and this statement is questionable from several aspects, one of which is his saying: Knowledge of magic is not ugly rationally, so his opponents from the Mu’tazila forbid this, even if he meant that it is not ugly religiously, so in this noble verse there is an ugliness to learning magic, and in the Sahih: Whoever goes to a fortune teller or a soothsayer has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad, and in the Sunan: Whoever ties a knot and blows into it has practiced magic, and his saying: and there is no prohibition, the scholars have agreed on that, how could it not be prohibited with what we have mentioned from the verse and the hadith and the agreement of the scholars requires that the imams of the scholars or most of them have stated this issue, and where are their texts on that? Then, its inclusion in the science of magic in the generality of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” There is a consideration in this, because this verse only indicates the praise of those who know Islamic knowledge. And why did I say that this is from it? Then, it is an advancement to the obligation of learning it, because knowledge of the miracle cannot be obtained except through it. It is weak, rather corrupt, because the greatest miracle of our Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the Great Qur’an, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy. Then, the knowledge that it is a miracle does not depend on the knowledge of magic at all. Then, it is known by necessity that the Companions, the Followers, the Imams of the Muslims and their common folk knew the miracle and differentiated between it and other things, and they did not know magic, nor did they know it, nor did they teach it. And God knows best. Then Abu Abdullah al-Razi mentioned that there are eight types of magic: The first is the magic of the liars and the Kasdaniyyin, who used to worship the seven wandering planets, which are the moving ones, and they believed that they governed the world and that they bring good and evil. They are the ones to whom God sent Abraham, peace be upon him, to invalidate their statement and reject their doctrine. He investigated it thoroughly in The Book of the Hidden Secret, in Addressing the Sun and the Stars attributed to him, as mentioned by Judge Ibn Khallikan and others. It is said that he repented from it, and it is said that he wrote it in order to show virtue, not as a matter of belief. This is what is thought of him, except that he mentioned in it their method in addressing each of these seven planets and the manner in which they do, what they wear, and what they adhere to. He said: And the second type is the magic of those with delusions and strong souls. Then he provided evidence that delusion has an effect in that a person can walk on a bridge placed on the ground, but he cannot walk on it if it is extended over a river or something similar. He said: And just as the doctors agreed to forbid the frightened from looking at red things, and the possessed from looking at things that are very shiny or rotating, and that is only because souls were created obedient to delusions. He said: The wise have agreed that the evil eye is true - and he can prove that with what is proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye is true, and if there were anything that could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye. He said: So if you know this, then we say that the soul that does these actions may be very strong, so it does not need to resort to tools and instruments in these actions, and it may be weak, so it needs to resort to these tools. The truth of this is that if the soul is elevated above the body and strongly attracted to the world of the heavens, it becomes as if it is a spirit from the heavenly spirits, so it is strong in influencing the materials of this world. If it is weak and strongly attached to this physical self, then at that time it has no influence at all except in this body. Then he advised to treat this disease by reducing food, cutting off from people and showing off. I said: What he is referring to is dealing with the state, and it is of two types: sometimes it is a correct, legitimate state, in which one deals with what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, have commanded, and one leaves what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, have forbidden. These states are gifts from God the Almighty and miracles for the righteous of this nation, and this is not called magic in the Sharia. Sometimes the situation is corrupt and its owner does not comply with what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded, and does not act in that way. This is the situation of the wretched who oppose the Sharia, and God giving them these situations does not indicate His love for them. Likewise, the Antichrist has supernatural powers that are indicated by many hadiths, even though he is condemned in the Sharia, may God curse him, and likewise those who resemble him from those who oppose the Muhammadan Sharia, upon its owner the best prayers and peace. Explaining this would take a long time and this is not the place for it. He said: The third type of magic is seeking help from earthly spirits, who are the jinn, contrary to the philosophers and the Mu'tazila, who are divided into two groups: believers and infidels, who are the devils. He said: The communication of the speaking souls with them is easier than their communication with the heavenly spirits, because of the relevance and closeness between them. Then the masters of the craft and the masters of experience have witnessed that communication with these earthly spirits results in a few easy works of incantation, smoke, and abstraction. This type is called incantations and the work of subjugation. He said: The fourth type of magic is imagination, taking the eyes, and magic. It is based on the fact that sight may err and be occupied with a specific thing and not with something else. Do you not see the skilled magician showing off the work of something that astounds the minds of those who look at it and takes their eyes to it until, when they are exhausted by the preoccupation with that thing by talking and the like, he does something else very quickly. Then something else appears to them other than what they expected, and they are very amazed by it. If he were silent and did not speak in a way that would divert the thoughts to the opposite of what he wants to teach, and the souls and imaginations were not moved to other than what he wants to bring out, the observers would be aware of everything he does. He said And whenever the conditions are beneficial to good sight, some type of defect is more severe, the work is better, such as if the magician sits in a very bright or dark place, so the seeing power does not stop at its conditions in this case. I said Some commentators said: The magic of the magicians before Pharaoh was only a form of sorcery, and for this reason the Almighty said: So when they cast, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them and produced a great magic. And the Almighty said: It appeared to him from their magic that it was moving. They said: And it was not moving in reality, and God knows best. The fifth type of magic: The amazing works that appear from the assembly of machines based on geometric proportions, such as a knight on a horse with a trumpet in his hand, every hour of the day he strikes the trumpet without anyone touching him - and from them are the images that the Romans and Indians depicted so that the observer cannot distinguish between them and a human being until they depict them laughing and crying, until he said: These faces are from the subtle matters of imagination. He said: And the magic of Pharaoh’s magicians was of this type I said meaning what some of the commentators said: They took those ropes and sticks and filled them with mercury so that they began to twist because of what was in them of that mercury, so it seemed to the observer that they were moving of their own free will. Al-Razi said: And from this category is the assembly of a watch box, and the science of dragging weights with light machines falls under this category. He said: And this in reality should not be considered magic because it has known and certain causes that whoever looks at them can do. I said And of this kind are the tricks of the Christians upon their common people with what they show them of lights, such as the case of the garbage of the church that they have in the city of Jerusalem, and the trick they use of secretly bringing fire into the church and lighting that lamp with a clever craft that is popular with the common people among them. As for the elite, they acknowledge that, but they interpret that they are uniting their companions in their religion, so they see that as permissible for them. And there is a doubt about them for the ignorant fools among the worshippers of the Karamiyyah who see the permissibility of fabricating hadiths in encouragement and intimidation, so they are included in the number of those about whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire. And his saying: Talk about me and do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me will enter the Fire. Then he mentioned here a story about some monks, which is that he heard the voice of a bird with a sad voice and weak movement, so when the birds heard it, they took pity on it and went and threw olive fruits into its nest to eat them. So this monk proceeded to make a bird in his shape and reached the point of making it hollow, so when the wind entered it, a sound like the sound of a bird was heard from it, and he secluded himself in a monastery that he built and claimed that it was on the grave of one of their righteous people, and he hung that bird in a place in it, so when it was the time of the olives, he opened a door on its side so that the wind would enter inside this image, and every bird in its shape would also hear its sound, so the birds would come and carry a lot of olives, and you would not see it among the Christians. Except for that olive in this monastery, and they do not know what caused it, so he tempted them with that and made them think that this was one of the miracles of the owner of this grave, upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection. (Al-Razi said: The sixth type of magic) is seeking help from the properties of medicines, meaning in this case foods and ointments. He said: Know that there is no way to deny the properties, because the effect of magnets is observable. I said Many of those who claim poverty and trick ignorant people with these properties fall into this category, claiming that they are conditions for him, such as mixing with fire and holding snakes, and other such impossibilities. He said: The seventh type of magic is the attachment of the heart, which is that the magician claims that he knows the Greatest Name and that the jinn obey him and submit to him in most matters. If it happens that the listener is weak-minded and has little discernment, he believes that it is true and his heart is attached to it and a kind of terror and fear occurs in his soul. If fear occurs, the sensitive powers weaken, and then the magician is able to do whatever he wants. I said This type is called al-tanbalah and it is only popular among the weak-minded among the sons of Adam. In the science of physiognomy there is guidance in knowing the mind from its deficiency. If the one who is being al-tanbalah is skilled in the science of physiognomy, he knows who among the people will submit to him and who will not. He said: The eighth type of magic is seeking to gossip and bring people closer together in light and pleasant ways, and this is common among people. I said Gossip is of two types: sometimes it is for the purpose of causing discord among people and dividing the hearts of the believers, then this is forbidden and agreed upon. But if it is for the purpose of reforming among people and uniting the Muslims’ word, as stated in the hadith, He is not a liar who divulges good, or it is for the purpose of discouraging and dividing the masses of the infidels, then this is a required matter, as stated in the hadith, War is deception, and as Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud did in dividing the word of the Confederates and Banu Qurayzah: he came to these people and spread to them some words about these people, and he conveyed from these people to those people something else, then he made a distinction between that and the souls became estranged and separated. Only the one with penetrating insight can do such a thing, and God is the One sought for help. Then Al-Razi said: This is the summary of the discussion on the types of magic and the explanation of its types and kinds. I said Many of these mentioned types were included in the art of magic because of the subtlety of their perceptions, because magic in the language is an expression for what is subtle and hidden because of it, and for this reason it came in the hadith: Indeed, some eloquence is magic. And it was called suhoor because it occurs hidden at the end of the night, and magic is the lung, which is the place of food and it was called that because of its concealment and the subtlety of its passages to the parts of the body and its wrinkles, as Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr to Utbah: His magic swelled, meaning his lung swelled from fear. And Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died between my throat and my chest, and God Almighty said: They bewitched the eyes of the people, meaning they concealed their knowledge from them, and God knows best. Abu Abdullah Al-Qurtubi said: We believe that magic is true and has a reality, and God creates with it what He wills, contrary to the Mu’tazila and Abu Ishaq Al-Isfarayni of the Shafi’is, who said: It is deception and imagination. He said: And from magic is that which is done by sleight of hand, like sorcery, and the sorcerer is the mailman due to his lightness of movement. Ibn Faris said: This word is not from the speech of the Bedouins. Al-Qurtubi said: And from it is that which is spoken by memorizing incantations of the names of God Almighty, and it may be from the covenants of the devils and it may be medicines and smokes and other than that. He said: And his saying, peace be upon him: Indeed, some eloquence is magic may be praise as a group says, and it may be a censure of eloquence. He said: This is more correct. He said: Because it corrects falsehood until the listener thinks that it is true, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Perhaps some of you will be more eloquent in his argument than others, so I will rule in his favor. The hadith. Chapter The minister Abu al-Muzaffar Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Hubayrah, may God have mercy on him, mentioned in his book Al-Ishraf ala Madhahib al-Ashraf a chapter on magic and said: They agreed that magic has a reality except for Abu Hanifa, who said: It has no reality according to him. They differed about the one who learns magic and uses it. Abu Hanifa, Malik and Ahmad said that he is a disbeliever because of that. Among the companions of Abu Hanifa, there are those who said that if he learns it to guard against it or avoid it, then he is not a disbeliever, and the one who learns it believing that it is permissible or that it benefits him is a disbeliever. Likewise, the one who believes that the devils do whatever he wants for him is a disbeliever. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: If he learns magic, we say to him, Describe your magic to us. If he describes what necessitates disbelief, such as what the people of Babylon believed about drawing closer to the seven planets and that they do what is sought from them, then he is a disbeliever. If it does not necessitate disbelief, then if he believes that it is permissible, then he is a disbeliever. Ibn Hubayrah said: Is he killed simply because of his doing and using it? Malik and Ahmad said: Yes. Ash-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifa said: No. If someone kills a person with his magic, then he is to be killed according to Malik, Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abu Hanifa said: He is to be killed unless he repeats it or admits to it with regard to a specific person. If he kills, then he is to be killed as a prescribed punishment according to them, except Ash-Shafi'i who said: He is to be killed in this case as retaliation. He said: If the magician repents, is his repentance accepted? Malik, Abu Hanifa and Ahmad said in the well-known opinion from them: It is not to be accepted. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad said in the other narration: It is to be accepted. As for the magician of the People of the Book, according to Abu Hanifa, he is to be killed just as a Muslim magician is to be killed. Malik, Ahmad and Ash-Shafi'i said: He is not to be killed, meaning because of the story of Labid ibn Al-A'sam. They differed concerning the Muslim female magician. According to Abu Hanifa, she is not to be killed, but she is to be imprisoned. The three said that her ruling is the same as that of a man, and God knows best. Abu Bakr Al-Khalal said: Abu Bakr Al-Marwazi told us: Umar ibn Harun read to Abu Abdullah - meaning Ahmad ibn Hanbal - that Yunus told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri: He said: The Muslim sorcerer is killed, but the polytheist sorcerer is not killed, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bewitched by a Jewish woman, but he did not kill her. Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Malik, may God have mercy on him, that he said about the dhimmi, he is killed if he kills his sorcery. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad narrated two narrations on the authority of Malik about the dhimmi who is bewitched: One of them is that he is asked to repent, and if he converts to Islam, otherwise he is killed. The second is that he is killed even if he converts to Islam. As for the Muslim sorcerer, if his sorcery includes disbelief, he is considered a disbeliever according to the four imams and others, based on the words of God the Almighty: And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ But Malik said: If he is found out, his repentance is not accepted, because he is like a heretic. If he repents before he is found out and comes to us repentant, we accept him. If he kills, his sorcery is killed. Al-Shafi’i said: If he says, I did not intend to kill, then he is mistaken and blood money is due on him. Question And does the magician ask for a solution for his magic? Saeed bin Al-Musayyab permitted it, as narrated by Al-Bukhari, and Amer Al-Shaabi said: There is nothing wrong with spreading it, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri disliked it. And in the Sahih, on the authority of Aisha, she said: O Messenger of God, why didn’t you spread it? He said: As for God, He has healed me, and I feared that I would open evil upon the people. And Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Wahb: He said: Seven leaves of Sidr are taken and crushed between two stones, then they are mixed with water and the Throne Verse is recited over them and the bewitched person drinks three sips of it, then he washes with the rest of it, for what is with him will go away. And it is good for the man who takes it from his wife. I said The most beneficial thing to use to remove magic is what God revealed to His Messenger to remove it, and they are the two Mu’awwidhat, and in the hadith: The one seeking refuge has not sought refuge with anything like them. And likewise the recitation of the Throne Verse, for it repels the devils.
2:102: And the Almighty said: And they do not teach anyone until they say, 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.' Abu Ja`far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, on the authority of Qays ibn `Ibad, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: So when the one who came to them wanted to practice magic, they forbade him with the strongest prohibition and said to him: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. This is because they knew good and evil, disbelief and faith, so they knew that magic is from disbelief. He said: So if he refused them, they ordered him to go to such and such a place, and when he came to him, he saw Satan and taught him, and when he learned him, a light came out of him, and he looked at him shining in the sky and said: Oh, what a pity! Oh, what did he do? And on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, he said in the interpretation of this verse: Yes, the two angels sent down magic to teach people the affliction with which God wanted to test people, so He took a covenant from them that they would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Qatada said: He took a covenant from them that they would not They would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, meaning a trial with which we have been afflicted, so do not disbelieve. As-Suddi said: If a person came to them wanting to practice magic, they would admonish him and say to him: Do not disbelieve, we are only a trial. If he refused, they would say to him: Go to these ashes and urinate on them. When he urinates on them, a light comes out of it and shines until it enters the sky, and that is faith. Something black like smoke comes and enters his ears, and everything, and that is the wrath of God. If he tells them about that, they would teach him magic. This is the statement of God the Most High: And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ (al-Baqarah 2:170) Sunayd said on the authority of Hajjaj on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding this verse: None would dare to practice magic except a disbeliever. As for the trial, it is the test and choice, and from it is the saying of the poet: He tempted people in their religion and left Ibn Affan in a state of evil for a long time. And also the saying of the Almighty, informing about Moses, peace be upon him, where he said: It is only your trial, meaning your trial, your test, and your examination, with which You misguide whom You will and guide whom You will. Some of them have used this verse as evidence for the disbelief of those who learn magic, and they have cited as evidence for it the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar, who told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “Whoever goes to a soothsayer or magician and believes what he says, has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.” This is a sound chain of transmission and it has other corroborating evidence. And the saying of the Almighty: And they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, meaning that people learn from Harut and Marut the science of magic and what they do with it in what they do of reprehensible actions, by which they cause separation between spouses, despite the mixing and harmony between them, and this is from the doing of the devils, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Talhah bin Nafi’, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The devil places his throne on the water and then sends out his armies among the people. The one closest to him in status is the one who causes the greatest temptation. One of them comes and says: ‘I kept on with so-and-so until I left him saying such-and-such.’ Iblis says: ‘No, by God, I did nothing!’ And one of them comes and says: ‘I did not leave him until I separated him from his family.’ He acknowledges it, brings him close, embraces him and says: ‘Yes, you are.’” The reason for separation between spouses through magic is what a man or woman imagines of the other in terms of bad appearance, character, or something similar, or a contract, or hatred, or something similar to the reasons that necessitate separation. ‘Man’ refers to a man and its feminine form is ‘woman.’ Both of them are dual, but they are not plural, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Except by the decree of God. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Except by God’s leaving him alone with what He willed. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. He said: Yes, whoever God wills, He gives them power over him, and whoever God does not will, He does not give them power over him, and they cannot do anything to anyone except by permission of God, as God the Almighty said. And in a narration from Al-Hasan, he said: This magic does not harm anyone except the one who engages in it. And the Almighty’s saying: And they learn that which harms them and does not benefit them means that it harms them in their religion and has no benefit that matches its harm. And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter means that the Jews who exchanged magic for following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that whoever did what they did, that he will have no share in the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: No share. And Abd Al-Razzaq said from Muammar from Qatadah: He will have no share in the Hereafter with God. And Abd Al-Razzaq said, and Al-Hasan said: He has no religion. And Saad said from Qatadah: He will have no share in the Hereafter He said: And the People of the Book knew in what God entrusted them with that the magician will have no share in the Hereafter. And the Almighty’s saying: “And evil is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew. And if they had believed and feared God, the reward from God would have been better, if they only knew.” The Almighty says: And evil is the substitute that they exchanged for magic in place of faith. And following the Messenger, if they had knowledge of what they were admonished with, And if they had believed and feared God, the reward from God would have been better for them. That is, if they had believed in God and His Messengers and feared the forbidden things, God’s reward for that would have been better for them than what they sought for themselves and were satisfied with, as God the Almighty said, “And those who were given knowledge said, ‘Woe to you! The reward from God is better for him who believes and does righteousness. And none is granted it except the patient.’” And the saying of And if they had believed and feared God was used as evidence by those who considered the magician to be an infidel, as is narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and a group of the Salaf. It was said: Rather, he is not an infidel, but his punishment is to behead him, as narrated by Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. They said: Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, told us on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar that he heard Bajalah ibn Abdah say: Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, wrote: Kill every male and female magician. He said: So we killed three female magicians. Al-Bukhari also included it in his Sahih. And thus it was authenticated that Hafsah, the Mother of the Believers, was bewitched by a slave girl of hers, so she ordered that she be killed. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: It was authenticated on the authority of three of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding killing the magician. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Ismail bin Muslim from Al-Hasan from Jundub Al-Azdi that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The punishment for a magician is to strike him with a sword. Then he said: We do not know it as being attributed to the Prophet except from this source, and Ismail bin Muslim is considered weak in hadith, and the correct version is from Al-Hasan from Jundub as a mursal. I said: Al-Tabarani narrated it from another source from Al-Hasan from Jundub as a mursal. And God knows best. It has been narrated from multiple chains of transmission that Al-Walid bin Uqbah had a magician playing in front of him. He would strike a man’s head and then shout at him, and his head would be returned to him. The people said: Glory be to God, He brings the dead back to life. A righteous man from the Muhajireen saw him, so the next day he came with his sword wrapped around him and went to play that game. The man drew his sword and struck the magician’s neck, and said: If he is telling the truth, then let him revive himself. Then he recited the verse of God, Do you then practice magic while you are seeing? Al-Walid became angry because he did not ask his permission to do so, so he imprisoned him and then released him. And God knows best. Imam Abu Bakr Al-Khalal said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Abu Ishaq told me on the authority of Haritha, who said: There was a man playing with one of the princes, then a soldier came with his sword drawn and killed him. He said: I think he was a magician. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, attributed the story of Umar and Hafsa to magic that constitutes polytheism, and God knows best. Chapter Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated in his interpretation of the Mu’tazila that they denied the existence of magic. He said: And perhaps they disbelieved whoever believed in its existence. He said: As for the Sunnis, they allowed that the magician could fly in the air and turn a human into a donkey, and a donkey into a human, except that they said: God creates things when the magician says those incantations and specific words. As for the one who has an effect on that being the heavens and the stars, then no, contrary to the philosophers, astrologers, and Sabians. Then he provided evidence for the occurrence of magic and that it is by the creation of God Almighty by His Almighty saying: And they do not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. And from the report that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bewitched, and that magic worked on him and the story of that woman with Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and what that woman mentioned about her coming to Babylon and learning magic. He said: And from what is mentioned in this chapter of many stories, then he said after this. The fifth issue is that knowledge of magic is not ugly or forbidden - the scholars agreed on this because knowledge in itself is noble, and also because of the generality of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” And because if magic were not known, it would not be possible to differentiate between it and a miracle, and knowledge that a miracle is a miracle is obligatory, and whatever the obligation depends on is obligatory. This requires that acquiring knowledge of magic be obligatory, and whatever is obligatory, how can it be forbidden and ugly? This is his wording on this issue, and this statement is questionable from several aspects, one of which is his saying: Knowledge of magic is not ugly rationally, so his opponents from the Mu’tazila forbid this, even if he meant that it is not ugly religiously, so in this noble verse there is an ugliness to learning magic, and in the Sahih: Whoever goes to a fortune teller or a soothsayer has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad, and in the Sunan: Whoever ties a knot and blows into it has practiced magic, and his saying: and there is no prohibition, the scholars have agreed on that, how could it not be prohibited with what we have mentioned from the verse and the hadith and the agreement of the scholars requires that the imams of the scholars or most of them have stated this issue, and where are their texts on that? Then, its inclusion in the science of magic in the generality of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” There is a consideration in this, because this verse only indicates the praise of those who know Islamic knowledge. And why did I say that this is from it? Then, it is an advancement to the obligation of learning it, because knowledge of the miracle cannot be obtained except through it. It is weak, rather corrupt, because the greatest miracle of our Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the Great Qur’an, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy. Then, the knowledge that it is a miracle does not depend on the knowledge of magic at all. Then, it is known by necessity that the Companions, the Followers, the Imams of the Muslims and their common folk knew the miracle and differentiated between it and other things, and they did not know magic, nor did they know it, nor did they teach it. And God knows best. Then Abu Abdullah al-Razi mentioned that there are eight types of magic: The first is the magic of the liars and the Kasdaniyyin, who used to worship the seven wandering planets, which are the moving ones, and they believed that they governed the world and that they bring good and evil. They are the ones to whom God sent Abraham, peace be upon him, to invalidate their statement and reject their doctrine. He investigated it thoroughly in The Book of the Hidden Secret, in Addressing the Sun and the Stars attributed to him, as mentioned by Judge Ibn Khallikan and others. It is said that he repented from it, and it is said that he wrote it in order to show virtue, not as a matter of belief. This is what is thought of him, except that he mentioned in it their method in addressing each of these seven planets and the manner in which they do, what they wear, and what they adhere to. He said: And the second type is the magic of those with delusions and strong souls. Then he provided evidence that delusion has an effect in that a person can walk on a bridge placed on the ground, but he cannot walk on it if it is extended over a river or something similar. He said: And just as the doctors agreed to forbid the frightened from looking at red things, and the possessed from looking at things that are very shiny or rotating, and that is only because souls were created obedient to delusions. He said: The wise have agreed that the evil eye is true - and he can prove that with what is proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye is true, and if there were anything that could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye. He said: So if you know this, then we say that the soul that does these actions may be very strong, so it does not need to resort to tools and instruments in these actions, and it may be weak, so it needs to resort to these tools. The truth of this is that if the soul is elevated above the body and strongly attracted to the world of the heavens, it becomes as if it is a spirit from the heavenly spirits, so it is strong in influencing the materials of this world. If it is weak and strongly attached to this physical self, then at that time it has no influence at all except in this body. Then he advised to treat this disease by reducing food, cutting off from people and showing off. I said: What he is referring to is dealing with the state, and it is of two types: sometimes it is a correct, legitimate state, in which one deals with what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, have commanded, and one leaves what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, have forbidden. These states are gifts from God the Almighty and miracles for the righteous of this nation, and this is not called magic in the Sharia. Sometimes the situation is corrupt and its owner does not comply with what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded, and does not act in that way. This is the situation of the wretched who oppose the Sharia, and God giving them these situations does not indicate His love for them. Likewise, the Antichrist has supernatural powers that are indicated by many hadiths, even though he is condemned in the Sharia, may God curse him, and likewise those who resemble him from those who oppose the Muhammadan Sharia, upon its owner the best prayers and peace. Explaining this would take a long time and this is not the place for it. He said: The third type of magic is seeking help from earthly spirits, who are the jinn, contrary to the philosophers and the Mu'tazila, who are divided into two groups: believers and infidels, who are the devils. He said: The communication of the speaking souls with them is easier than their communication with the heavenly spirits, because of the relevance and closeness between them. Then the masters of the craft and the masters of experience have witnessed that communication with these earthly spirits results in a few easy works of incantation, smoke, and abstraction. This type is called incantations and the work of subjugation. He said: The fourth type of magic is imagination, taking the eyes, and magic. It is based on the fact that sight may err and be occupied with a specific thing and not with something else. Do you not see the skilled magician showing off the work of something that astounds the minds of those who look at it and takes their eyes to it until, when they are exhausted by the preoccupation with that thing by talking and the like, he does something else very quickly. Then something else appears to them other than what they expected, and they are very amazed by it. If he were silent and did not speak in a way that would divert the thoughts to the opposite of what he wants to teach, and the souls and imaginations were not moved to other than what he wants to bring out, the observers would be aware of everything he does. He said And whenever the conditions are beneficial to good sight, some type of defect is more severe, the work is better, such as if the magician sits in a very bright or dark place, so the seeing power does not stop at its conditions in this case. I said Some commentators said: The magic of the magicians before Pharaoh was only a form of sorcery, and for this reason the Almighty said: So when they cast, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them and produced a great magic. And the Almighty said: It appeared to him from their magic that it was moving. They said: And it was not moving in reality, and God knows best. The fifth type of magic: The amazing works that appear from the assembly of machines based on geometric proportions, such as a knight on a horse with a trumpet in his hand, every hour of the day he strikes the trumpet without anyone touching him - and from them are the images that the Romans and Indians depicted so that the observer cannot distinguish between them and a human being until they depict them laughing and crying, until he said: These faces are from the subtle matters of imagination. He said: And the magic of Pharaoh’s magicians was of this type I said meaning what some of the commentators said: They took those ropes and sticks and filled them with mercury so that they began to twist because of what was in them of that mercury, so it seemed to the observer that they were moving of their own free will. Al-Razi said: And from this category is the assembly of a watch box, and the science of dragging weights with light machines falls under this category. He said: And this in reality should not be considered magic because it has known and certain causes that whoever looks at them can do. I said And of this kind are the tricks of the Christians upon their common people with what they show them of lights, such as the case of the garbage of the church that they have in the city of Jerusalem, and the trick they use of secretly bringing fire into the church and lighting that lamp with a clever craft that is popular with the common people among them. As for the elite, they acknowledge that, but they interpret that they are uniting their companions in their religion, so they see that as permissible for them. And there is a doubt about them for the ignorant fools among the worshippers of the Karamiyyah who see the permissibility of fabricating hadiths in encouragement and intimidation, so they are included in the number of those about whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire. And his saying: Talk about me and do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me will enter the Fire. Then he mentioned here a story about some monks, which is that he heard the voice of a bird with a sad voice and weak movement, so when the birds heard it, they took pity on it and went and threw olive fruits into its nest to eat them. So this monk proceeded to make a bird in his shape and reached the point of making it hollow, so when the wind entered it, a sound like the sound of a bird was heard from it, and he secluded himself in a monastery that he built and claimed that it was on the grave of one of their righteous people, and he hung that bird in a place in it, so when it was the time of the olives, he opened a door on its side so that the wind would enter inside this image, and every bird in its shape would also hear its sound, so the birds would come and carry a lot of olives, and you would not see it among the Christians. Except for that olive in this monastery, and they do not know what caused it, so he tempted them with that and made them think that this was one of the miracles of the owner of this grave, upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection. (Al-Razi said: The sixth type of magic) is seeking help from the properties of medicines, meaning in this case foods and ointments. He said: Know that there is no way to deny the properties, because the effect of magnets is observable. I said Many of those who claim poverty and trick ignorant people with these properties fall into this category, claiming that they are conditions for him, such as mixing with fire and holding snakes, and other such impossibilities. He said: The seventh type of magic is the attachment of the heart, which is that the magician claims that he knows the Greatest Name and that the jinn obey him and submit to him in most matters. If it happens that the listener is weak-minded and has little discernment, he believes that it is true and his heart is attached to it and a kind of terror and fear occurs in his soul. If fear occurs, the sensitive powers weaken, and then the magician is able to do whatever he wants. I said This type is called al-tanbalah and it is only popular among the weak-minded among the sons of Adam. In the science of physiognomy there is guidance in knowing the mind from its deficiency. If the one who is being al-tanbalah is skilled in the science of physiognomy, he knows who among the people will submit to him and who will not. He said: The eighth type of magic is seeking to gossip and bring people closer together in light and pleasant ways, and this is common among people. I said Gossip is of two types: sometimes it is for the purpose of causing discord among people and dividing the hearts of the believers, then this is forbidden and agreed upon. But if it is for the purpose of reforming among people and uniting the Muslims’ word, as stated in the hadith, He is not a liar who divulges good, or it is for the purpose of discouraging and dividing the masses of the infidels, then this is a required matter, as stated in the hadith, War is deception, and as Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud did in dividing the word of the Confederates and Banu Qurayzah: he came to these people and spread to them some words about these people, and he conveyed from these people to those people something else, then he made a distinction between that and the souls became estranged and separated. Only the one with penetrating insight can do such a thing, and God is the One sought for help. Then Al-Razi said: This is the summary of the discussion on the types of magic and the explanation of its types and kinds. I said Many of these mentioned types were included in the art of magic because of the subtlety of their perceptions, because magic in the language is an expression for what is subtle and hidden because of it, and for this reason it came in the hadith: Indeed, some eloquence is magic. And it was called suhoor because it occurs hidden at the end of the night, and magic is the lung, which is the place of food and it was called that because of its concealment and the subtlety of its passages to the parts of the body and its wrinkles, as Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr to Utbah: His magic swelled, meaning his lung swelled from fear. And Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died between my throat and my chest, and God Almighty said: They bewitched the eyes of the people, meaning they concealed their knowledge from them, and God knows best. Abu Abdullah Al-Qurtubi said: We believe that magic is true and has a reality, and God creates with it what He wills, contrary to the Mu’tazila and Abu Ishaq Al-Isfarayni of the Shafi’is, who said: It is deception and imagination. He said: And from magic is that which is done by sleight of hand, like sorcery, and the sorcerer is the mailman due to his lightness of movement. Ibn Faris said: This word is not from the speech of the Bedouins. Al-Qurtubi said: And from it is that which is spoken by memorizing incantations of the names of God Almighty, and it may be from the covenants of the devils and it may be medicines and smokes and other than that. He said: And his saying, peace be upon him: Indeed, some eloquence is magic may be praise as a group says, and it may be a censure of eloquence. He said: This is more correct. He said: Because it corrects falsehood until the listener thinks that it is true, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Perhaps some of you will be more eloquent in his argument than others, so I will rule in his favor. The hadith. Chapter The minister Abu al-Muzaffar Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Hubayrah, may God have mercy on him, mentioned in his book Al-Ishraf ala Madhahib al-Ashraf a chapter on magic and said: They agreed that magic has a reality except for Abu Hanifa, who said: It has no reality according to him. They differed about the one who learns magic and uses it. Abu Hanifa, Malik and Ahmad said that he is a disbeliever because of that. Among the companions of Abu Hanifa, there are those who said that if he learns it to guard against it or avoid it, then he is not a disbeliever, and the one who learns it believing that it is permissible or that it benefits him is a disbeliever. Likewise, the one who believes that the devils do whatever he wants for him is a disbeliever. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: If he learns magic, we say to him, Describe your magic to us. If he describes what necessitates disbelief, such as what the people of Babylon believed about drawing closer to the seven planets and that they do what is sought from them, then he is a disbeliever. If it does not necessitate disbelief, then if he believes that it is permissible, then he is a disbeliever. Ibn Hubayrah said: Is he killed simply because of his doing and using it? Malik and Ahmad said: Yes. Ash-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifa said: No. If someone kills a person with his magic, then he is to be killed according to Malik, Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abu Hanifa said: He is to be killed unless he repeats it or admits to it with regard to a specific person. If he kills, then he is to be killed as a prescribed punishment according to them, except Ash-Shafi'i who said: He is to be killed in this case as retaliation. He said: If the magician repents, is his repentance accepted? Malik, Abu Hanifa and Ahmad said in the well-known opinion from them: It is not to be accepted. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad said in the other narration: It is to be accepted. As for the magician of the People of the Book, according to Abu Hanifa, he is to be killed just as a Muslim magician is to be killed. Malik, Ahmad and Ash-Shafi'i said: He is not to be killed, meaning because of the story of Labid ibn Al-A'sam. They differed concerning the Muslim female magician. According to Abu Hanifa, she is not to be killed, but she is to be imprisoned. The three said that her ruling is the same as that of a man, and God knows best. Abu Bakr Al-Khalal said: Abu Bakr Al-Marwazi told us: Umar ibn Harun read to Abu Abdullah - meaning Ahmad ibn Hanbal - that Yunus told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri: He said: The Muslim sorcerer is killed, but the polytheist sorcerer is not killed, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bewitched by a Jewish woman, but he did not kill her. Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Malik, may God have mercy on him, that he said about the dhimmi, he is killed if he kills his sorcery. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad narrated two narrations on the authority of Malik about the dhimmi who is bewitched: One of them is that he is asked to repent, and if he converts to Islam, otherwise he is killed. The second is that he is killed even if he converts to Islam. As for the Muslim sorcerer, if his sorcery includes disbelief, he is considered a disbeliever according to the four imams and others, based on the words of God the Almighty: And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ But Malik said: If he is found out, his repentance is not accepted, because he is like a heretic. If he repents before he is found out and comes to us repentant, we accept him. If he kills, his sorcery is killed. Al-Shafi’i said: If he says, I did not intend to kill, then he is mistaken and blood money is due on him. Question And does the magician ask for a solution for his magic? Saeed bin Al-Musayyab permitted it, as narrated by Al-Bukhari, and Amer Al-Shaabi said: There is nothing wrong with spreading it, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri disliked it. And in the Sahih, on the authority of Aisha, she said: O Messenger of God, why didn’t you spread it? He said: As for God, He has healed me, and I feared that I would open evil upon the people. And Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Wahb: He said: Seven leaves of Sidr are taken and crushed between two stones, then they are mixed with water and the Throne Verse is recited over them and the bewitched person drinks three sips of it, then he washes with the rest of it, for what is with him will go away. And it is good for the man who takes it from his wife. I said The most beneficial thing to use to remove magic is what God revealed to His Messenger to remove it, and they are the two Mu’awwidhat, and in the hadith: The one seeking refuge has not sought refuge with anything like them. And likewise the recitation of the Throne Verse, for it repels the devils.
2:103: And the Almighty said: And they do not teach anyone until they say, 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.' Abu Ja`far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, on the authority of Qays ibn `Ibad, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: So when the one who came to them wanted to practice magic, they forbade him with the strongest prohibition and said to him: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. This is because they knew good and evil, disbelief and faith, so they knew that magic is from disbelief. He said: So if he refused them, they ordered him to go to such and such a place, and when he came to him, he saw Satan and taught him, and when he learned him, a light came out of him, and he looked at him shining in the sky and said: Oh, what a pity! Oh, what did he do? And on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, he said in the interpretation of this verse: Yes, the two angels sent down magic to teach people the affliction with which God wanted to test people, so He took a covenant from them that they would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Qatada said: He took a covenant from them that they would not They would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, meaning a trial with which we have been afflicted, so do not disbelieve. As-Suddi said: If a person came to them wanting to practice magic, they would admonish him and say to him: Do not disbelieve, we are only a trial. If he refused, they would say to him: Go to these ashes and urinate on them. When he urinates on them, a light comes out of it and shines until it enters the sky, and that is faith. Something black like smoke comes and enters his ears, and everything, and that is the wrath of God. If he tells them about that, they would teach him magic. This is the statement of God the Most High: And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ (al-Baqarah 2:170) Sunayd said on the authority of Hajjaj on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding this verse: None would dare to practice magic except a disbeliever. As for the trial, it is the test and choice, and from it is the saying of the poet: He tempted people in their religion and left Ibn Affan in a state of evil for a long time. And also the saying of the Almighty, informing about Moses, peace be upon him, where he said: It is only your trial, meaning your trial, your test, and your examination, with which You misguide whom You will and guide whom You will. Some of them have used this verse as evidence for the disbelief of those who learn magic, and they have cited as evidence for it the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar, who told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “Whoever goes to a soothsayer or magician and believes what he says, has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.” This is a sound chain of transmission and it has other corroborating evidence. And the saying of the Almighty: And they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, meaning that people learn from Harut and Marut the science of magic and what they do with it in what they do of reprehensible actions, by which they cause separation between spouses, despite the mixing and harmony between them, and this is from the doing of the devils, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Talhah bin Nafi’, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The devil places his throne on the water and then sends out his armies among the people. The one closest to him in status is the one who causes the greatest temptation. One of them comes and says: ‘I kept on with so-and-so until I left him saying such-and-such.’ Iblis says: ‘No, by God, I did nothing!’ And one of them comes and says: ‘I did not leave him until I separated him from his family.’ He acknowledges it, brings him close, embraces him and says: ‘Yes, you are.’” The reason for separation between spouses through magic is what a man or woman imagines of the other in terms of bad appearance, character, or something similar, or a contract, or hatred, or something similar to the reasons that necessitate separation. ‘Man’ refers to a man and its feminine form is ‘woman.’ Both of them are dual, but they are not plural, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Except by the decree of God. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Except by God’s leaving him alone with what He willed. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. He said: Yes, whoever God wills, He gives them power over him, and whoever God does not will, He does not give them power over him, and they cannot do anything to anyone except by permission of God, as God the Almighty said. And in a narration from Al-Hasan, he said: This magic does not harm anyone except the one who engages in it. And the Almighty’s saying: And they learn that which harms them and does not benefit them means that it harms them in their religion and has no benefit that matches its harm. And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter means that the Jews who exchanged magic for following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that whoever did what they did, that he will have no share in the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: No share. And Abd Al-Razzaq said from Muammar from Qatadah: He will have no share in the Hereafter with God. And Abd Al-Razzaq said, and Al-Hasan said: He has no religion. And Saad said from Qatadah: He will have no share in the Hereafter He said: And the People of the Book knew in what God entrusted them with that the magician will have no share in the Hereafter. And the Almighty’s saying: “And evil is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew. And if they had believed and feared God, the reward from God would have been better, if they only knew.” The Almighty says: And evil is the substitute that they exchanged for magic in place of faith. And following the Messenger, if they had knowledge of what they were admonished with, And if they had believed and feared God, the reward from God would have been better for them. That is, if they had believed in God and His Messengers and feared the forbidden things, God’s reward for that would have been better for them than what they sought for themselves and were satisfied with, as God the Almighty said, “And those who were given knowledge said, ‘Woe to you! The reward from God is better for him who believes and does righteousness. And none is granted it except the patient.’” And the saying of And if they had believed and feared God was used as evidence by those who considered the magician to be an infidel, as is narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and a group of the Salaf. It was said: Rather, he is not an infidel, but his punishment is to behead him, as narrated by Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. They said: Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, told us on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar that he heard Bajalah ibn Abdah say: Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, wrote: Kill every male and female magician. He said: So we killed three female magicians. Al-Bukhari also included it in his Sahih. And thus it was authenticated that Hafsah, the Mother of the Believers, was bewitched by a slave girl of hers, so she ordered that she be killed. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: It was authenticated on the authority of three of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding killing the magician. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Ismail bin Muslim from Al-Hasan from Jundub Al-Azdi that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The punishment for a magician is to strike him with a sword. Then he said: We do not know it as being attributed to the Prophet except from this source, and Ismail bin Muslim is considered weak in hadith, and the correct version is from Al-Hasan from Jundub as a mursal. I said: Al-Tabarani narrated it from another source from Al-Hasan from Jundub as a mursal. And God knows best. It has been narrated from multiple chains of transmission that Al-Walid bin Uqbah had a magician playing in front of him. He would strike a man’s head and then shout at him, and his head would be returned to him. The people said: Glory be to God, He brings the dead back to life. A righteous man from the Muhajireen saw him, so the next day he came with his sword wrapped around him and went to play that game. The man drew his sword and struck the magician’s neck, and said: If he is telling the truth, then let him revive himself. Then he recited the verse of God, Do you then practice magic while you are seeing? Al-Walid became angry because he did not ask his permission to do so, so he imprisoned him and then released him. And God knows best. Imam Abu Bakr Al-Khalal said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Abu Ishaq told me on the authority of Haritha, who said: There was a man playing with one of the princes, then a soldier came with his sword drawn and killed him. He said: I think he was a magician. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, attributed the story of Umar and Hafsa to magic that constitutes polytheism, and God knows best. Chapter Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated in his interpretation of the Mu’tazila that they denied the existence of magic. He said: And perhaps they disbelieved whoever believed in its existence. He said: As for the Sunnis, they allowed that the magician could fly in the air and turn a human into a donkey, and a donkey into a human, except that they said: God creates things when the magician says those incantations and specific words. As for the one who has an effect on that being the heavens and the stars, then no, contrary to the philosophers, astrologers, and Sabians. Then he provided evidence for the occurrence of magic and that it is by the creation of God Almighty by His Almighty saying: And they do not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. And from the report that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bewitched, and that magic worked on him and the story of that woman with Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and what that woman mentioned about her coming to Babylon and learning magic. He said: And from what is mentioned in this chapter of many stories, then he said after this. The fifth issue is that knowledge of magic is not ugly or forbidden - the scholars agreed on this because knowledge in itself is noble, and also because of the generality of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” And because if magic were not known, it would not be possible to differentiate between it and a miracle, and knowledge that a miracle is a miracle is obligatory, and whatever the obligation depends on is obligatory. This requires that acquiring knowledge of magic be obligatory, and whatever is obligatory, how can it be forbidden and ugly? This is his wording on this issue, and this statement is questionable from several aspects, one of which is his saying: Knowledge of magic is not ugly rationally, so his opponents from the Mu’tazila forbid this, even if he meant that it is not ugly religiously, so in this noble verse there is an ugliness to learning magic, and in the Sahih: Whoever goes to a fortune teller or a soothsayer has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad, and in the Sunan: Whoever ties a knot and blows into it has practiced magic, and his saying: and there is no prohibition, the scholars have agreed on that, how could it not be prohibited with what we have mentioned from the verse and the hadith and the agreement of the scholars requires that the imams of the scholars or most of them have stated this issue, and where are their texts on that? Then, its inclusion in the science of magic in the generality of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” There is a consideration in this, because this verse only indicates the praise of those who know Islamic knowledge. And why did I say that this is from it? Then, it is an advancement to the obligation of learning it, because knowledge of the miracle cannot be obtained except through it. It is weak, rather corrupt, because the greatest miracle of our Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the Great Qur’an, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy. Then, the knowledge that it is a miracle does not depend on the knowledge of magic at all. Then, it is known by necessity that the Companions, the Followers, the Imams of the Muslims and their common folk knew the miracle and differentiated between it and other things, and they did not know magic, nor did they know it, nor did they teach it. And God knows best. Then Abu Abdullah al-Razi mentioned that there are eight types of magic: The first is the magic of the liars and the Kasdaniyyin, who used to worship the seven wandering planets, which are the moving ones, and they believed that they governed the world and that they bring good and evil. They are the ones to whom God sent Abraham, peace be upon him, to invalidate their statement and reject their doctrine. He investigated it thoroughly in The Book of the Hidden Secret, in Addressing the Sun and the Stars attributed to him, as mentioned by Judge Ibn Khallikan and others. It is said that he repented from it, and it is said that he wrote it in order to show virtue, not as a matter of belief. This is what is thought of him, except that he mentioned in it their method in addressing each of these seven planets and the manner in which they do, what they wear, and what they adhere to.
