He said: And the second type is the magic of those with delusions and strong souls. Then he provided evidence that delusion has an effect in that a person can walk on a bridge placed on the ground, but he cannot walk on it if it is extended over a river or something similar. He said: And just as the doctors agreed to forbid the frightened from looking at red things, and the possessed from looking at things that are very shiny or rotating, and that is only because souls were created obedient to delusions. He said: The wise have agreed that the evil eye is true - and he can prove that with what is proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye is true, and if there were anything that could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye. He said: So if you know this, then we say that the soul that does these actions may be very strong, so it does not need to resort to tools and instruments in these actions, and it may be weak, so it needs to resort to these tools. The truth of this is that if the soul is elevated above the body and strongly attracted to the world of the heavens, it becomes as if it is a spirit from the heavenly spirits, so it is strong in influencing the materials of this world. If it is weak and strongly attached to this physical self, then at that time it has no influence at all except in this body. Then he advised to treat this disease by reducing food, cutting off from people and showing off. I said: What he is referring to is dealing with the state, and it is of two types: sometimes it is a correct, legitimate state, in which one deals with what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, have commanded, and one leaves what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, have forbidden. These states are gifts from God the Almighty and miracles for the righteous of this nation, and this is not called magic in the Sharia. Sometimes the situation is corrupt and its owner does not comply with what God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded, and does not act in that way. This is the situation of the wretched who oppose the Sharia, and God giving them these situations does not indicate His love for them. Likewise, the Antichrist has supernatural powers that are indicated by many hadiths, even though he is condemned in the Sharia, may God curse him, and likewise those who resemble him from those who oppose the Muhammadan Sharia, upon its owner the best prayers and peace. Explaining this would take a long time and this is not the place for it. He said: The third type of magic is seeking help from earthly spirits, who are the jinn, contrary to the philosophers and the Mu'tazila, who are divided into two groups: believers and infidels, who are the devils. He said: The communication of the speaking souls with them is easier than their communication with the heavenly spirits, because of the relevance and closeness between them. Then the masters of the craft and the masters of experience have witnessed that communication with these earthly spirits results in a few easy works of incantation, smoke, and abstraction. This type is called incantations and the work of subjugation. He said: The fourth type of magic is imagination, taking the eyes, and magic. It is based on the fact that sight may err and be occupied with a specific thing and not with something else. Do you not see the skilled magician showing off the work of something that astounds the minds of those who look at it and takes their eyes to it until, when they are exhausted by the preoccupation with that thing by talking and the like, he does something else very quickly. Then something else appears to them other than what they expected, and they are very amazed by it. If he were silent and did not speak in a way that would divert the thoughts to the opposite of what he wants to teach, and the souls and imaginations were not moved to other than what he wants to bring out, the observers would be aware of everything he does. He said And whenever the conditions are beneficial to good sight, some type of defect is more severe, the work is better, such as if the magician sits in a very bright or dark place, so the seeing power does not stop at its conditions in this case. I said Some commentators said: The magic of the magicians before Pharaoh was only a form of sorcery, and for this reason the Almighty said: So when they cast, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them and produced a great magic. And the Almighty said: It appeared to him from their magic that it was moving. They said: And it was not moving in reality, and God knows best. The fifth type of magic: The amazing works that appear from the assembly of machines based on geometric proportions, such as a knight on a horse with a trumpet in his hand, every hour of the day he strikes the trumpet without anyone touching him - and from them are the images that the Romans and Indians depicted so that the observer cannot distinguish between them and a human being until they depict them laughing and crying, until he said: These faces are from the subtle matters of imagination. He said: And the magic of Pharaoh’s magicians was of this type I said meaning what some of the commentators said: They took those ropes and sticks and filled them with mercury so that they began to twist because of what was in them of that mercury, so it seemed to the observer that they were moving of their own free will. Al-Razi said: And from this category is the assembly of a watch box, and the science of dragging weights with light machines falls under this category. He said: And this in reality should not be considered magic because it has known and certain causes that whoever looks at them can do. I said And of this kind are the tricks of the Christians upon their common people with what they show them of lights, such as the case of the garbage of the church that they have in the city of Jerusalem, and the trick they use of secretly bringing fire into the church and lighting that lamp with a clever craft that is popular with the common people among them. As for the elite, they acknowledge that, but they interpret that they are uniting their companions in their religion, so they see that as permissible for them. And there is a doubt about them for the ignorant fools among the worshippers of the Karamiyyah who see the permissibility of fabricating hadiths in encouragement and intimidation, so they are included in the number of those about whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire. And his saying: Talk about me and do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me will enter the Fire. Then he mentioned here a story about some monks, which is that he heard the voice of a bird with a sad voice and weak movement, so when the birds heard it, they took pity on it and went and threw olive fruits into its nest to eat them. So this monk proceeded to make a bird in his shape and reached the point of making it hollow, so when the wind entered it, a sound like the sound of a bird was heard from it, and he secluded himself in a monastery that he built and claimed that it was on the grave of one of their righteous people, and he hung that bird in a place in it, so when it was the time of the olives, he opened a door on its side so that the wind would enter inside this image, and every bird in its shape would also hear its sound, so the birds would come and carry a lot of olives, and you would not see it among the Christians. Except for that olive in this monastery, and they do not know what caused it, so he tempted them with that and made them think that this was one of the miracles of the owner of this grave, upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection. (Al-Razi said: The sixth type of magic) is seeking help from the properties of medicines, meaning in this case foods and ointments. He said: Know that there is no way to deny the properties, because the effect of magnets is observable. I said Many of those who claim poverty and trick ignorant people with these properties fall into this category, claiming that they are conditions for him, such as mixing with fire and holding snakes, and other such impossibilities. He said: The seventh type of magic is the attachment of the heart, which is that the magician claims that he knows the Greatest Name and that the jinn obey him and submit to him in most matters. If it happens that the listener is weak-minded and has little discernment, he believes that it is true and his heart is attached to it and a kind of terror and fear occurs in his soul. If fear occurs, the sensitive powers weaken, and then the magician is able to do whatever he wants. I said This type is called al-tanbalah and it is only popular among the weak-minded among the sons of Adam. In the science of physiognomy there is guidance in knowing the mind from its deficiency. If the one who is being al-tanbalah is skilled in the science of physiognomy, he knows who among the people will submit to him and who will not. He said: The eighth type of magic is seeking to gossip and bring people closer together in light and pleasant ways, and this is common among people. I said Gossip is of two types: sometimes it is for the purpose of causing discord among people and dividing the hearts of the believers, then this is forbidden and agreed upon. But if it is for the purpose of reforming among people and uniting the Muslims’ word, as stated in the hadith, He is not a liar who divulges good, or it is for the purpose of discouraging and dividing the masses of the infidels, then this is a required matter, as stated in the hadith, War is deception, and as Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud did in dividing the word of the Confederates and Banu Qurayzah: he came to these people and spread to them some words about these people, and he conveyed from these people to those people something else, then he made a distinction between that and the souls became estranged and separated. Only the one with penetrating insight can do such a thing, and God is the One sought for help. Then Al-Razi said: This is the summary of the discussion on the types of magic and the explanation of its types and kinds. I said Many of these mentioned types were included in the art of magic because of the subtlety of their perceptions, because magic in the language is an expression for what is subtle and hidden because of it, and for this reason it came in the hadith: Indeed, some eloquence is magic. And it was called suhoor because it occurs hidden at the end of the night, and magic is the lung, which is the place of food and it was called that because of its concealment and the subtlety of its passages to the parts of the body and its wrinkles, as Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr to Utbah: His magic swelled, meaning his lung swelled from fear. And Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died between my throat and my chest, and God Almighty said: They bewitched the eyes of the people, meaning they concealed their knowledge from them, and God knows best. Abu Abdullah Al-Qurtubi said: We believe that magic is true and has a reality, and God creates with it what He wills, contrary to the Mu’tazila and Abu Ishaq Al-Isfarayni of the Shafi’is, who said: It is deception and imagination. He said: And from magic is that which is done by sleight of hand, like sorcery, and the sorcerer is the mailman due to his lightness of movement. Ibn Faris said: This word is not from the speech of the Bedouins. Al-Qurtubi said: And from it is that which is spoken by memorizing incantations of the names of God Almighty, and it may be from the covenants of the devils and it may be medicines and smokes and other than that. He said: And his saying, peace be upon him: Indeed, some eloquence is magic may be praise as a group says, and it may be a censure of eloquence. He said: This is more correct. He said: Because it corrects falsehood until the listener thinks that it is true, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Perhaps some of you will be more eloquent in his argument than others, so I will rule in his favor. The hadith. Chapter The minister Abu al-Muzaffar Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Hubayrah, may God have mercy on him, mentioned in his book Al-Ishraf ala Madhahib al-Ashraf a chapter on magic and said: They agreed that magic has a reality except for Abu Hanifa, who said: It has no reality according to him. They differed about the one who learns magic and uses it. Abu Hanifa, Malik and Ahmad said that he is a disbeliever because of that. Among the companions of Abu Hanifa, there are those who said that if he learns it to guard against it or avoid it, then he is not a disbeliever, and the one who learns it believing that it is permissible or that it benefits him is a disbeliever. Likewise, the one who believes that the devils do whatever he wants for him is a disbeliever. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: If he learns magic, we say to him, Describe your magic to us. If he describes what necessitates disbelief, such as what the people of Babylon believed about drawing closer to the seven planets and that they do what is sought from them, then he is a disbeliever. If it does not necessitate disbelief, then if he believes that it is permissible, then he is a disbeliever. Ibn Hubayrah said: Is he killed simply because of his doing and using it? Malik and Ahmad said: Yes. Ash-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifa said: No. If someone kills a person with his magic, then he is to be killed according to Malik, Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abu Hanifa said: He is to be killed unless he repeats it or admits to it with regard to a specific person. If he kills, then he is to be killed as a prescribed punishment according to them, except Ash-Shafi'i who said: He is to be killed in this case as retaliation. He said: If the magician repents, is his repentance accepted? Malik, Abu Hanifa and Ahmad said in the well-known opinion from them: It is not to be accepted. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad said in the other narration: It is to be accepted. As for the magician of the People of the Book, according to Abu Hanifa, he is to be killed just as a Muslim magician is to be killed. Malik, Ahmad and Ash-Shafi'i said: He is not to be killed, meaning because of the story of Labid ibn Al-A'sam. They differed concerning the Muslim female magician. According to Abu Hanifa, she is not to be killed, but she is to be imprisoned. The three said that her ruling is the same as that of a man, and God knows best. Abu Bakr Al-Khalal said: Abu Bakr Al-Marwazi told us: Umar ibn Harun read to Abu Abdullah - meaning Ahmad ibn Hanbal - that Yunus told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri: He said: The Muslim sorcerer is killed, but the polytheist sorcerer is not killed, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bewitched by a Jewish woman, but he did not kill her. Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Malik, may God have mercy on him, that he said about the dhimmi, he is killed if he kills his sorcery. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad narrated two narrations on the authority of Malik about the dhimmi who is bewitched: One of them is that he is asked to repent, and if he converts to Islam, otherwise he is killed. The second is that he is killed even if he converts to Islam. As for the Muslim sorcerer, if his sorcery includes disbelief, he is considered a disbeliever according to the four imams and others, based on the words of God the Almighty: And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ But Malik said: If he is found out, his repentance is not accepted, because he is like a heretic. If he repents before he is found out and comes to us repentant, we accept him. If he kills, his sorcery is killed. Al-Shafi’i said: If he says, I did not intend to kill, then he is mistaken and blood money is due on him. Question And does the magician ask for a solution for his magic? Saeed bin Al-Musayyab permitted it, as narrated by Al-Bukhari, and Amer Al-Shaabi said: There is nothing wrong with spreading it, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri disliked it. And in the Sahih, on the authority of Aisha, she said: O Messenger of God, why didn’t you spread it? He said: As for God, He has healed me, and I feared that I would open evil upon the people. And Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Wahb: He said: Seven leaves of Sidr are taken and crushed between two stones, then they are mixed with water and the Throne Verse is recited over them and the bewitched person drinks three sips of it, then he washes with the rest of it, for what is with him will go away. And it is good for the man who takes it from his wife. I said The most beneficial thing to use to remove magic is what God revealed to His Messenger to remove it, and they are the two Mu’awwidhat, and in the hadith: The one seeking refuge has not sought refuge with anything like them. And likewise the recitation of the Throne Verse, for it repels the devils.
2:104: God the Most High forbade His believing servants from imitating the disbelievers in their position and actions, because the Jews used to suffer from speech that contained ambiguity because of what they intended to disparage, may God's curses be upon them. So if they wanted to say, Listen to us, they would say, Ra'ina, and they would show off with recklessness, as God the Most High said: "Among those who are Jews are those who distort words from their [proper] usages and say, 'We hear and disobey,' and 'Hear,' but we do not hear, and 'Ra'ina,' a twisting of their tongues and an attack on the religion. Had they said, 'We hear and we obey,' and 'Hear, and unzurna,' it would have been better for them and more upright. But God has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a few." Likewise, the hadiths came with reports about them that when they greeted, they would only say, Death be upon you, and death is death. For this reason, we were commanded to respond to them with, And upon you, and our response to them is only answered, but their response to us is not answered. The point is that God the Most High forbade the believers from imitating the disbelievers in word and action, as He said, "O you who have believed, do not Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit told us, Hassan ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Munib al-Jarshi, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was sent before the Hour with the sword so that God alone would be worshipped, with no partner for Him, and my provision was made under the shade of my spear, and humiliation and disgrace were made for whoever disobeys my command, and whoever imitates a people is one of them.” Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Abu Shaybah, on the authority of Abu al-Nadhir Hashim, who told us on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim, Whoever imitates a people is one of them. This indicates: a strong prohibition, threat and warning against imitating the disbelievers in their words, actions, clothing, festivals, worship and other matters of theirs that were not prescribed for us and we do not approve of them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Naim bin Hammad told us, Abdullah bin Mubarak told us, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Ma’n and Awn, or one of them, that a man came to Abdullah bin Mas’ud and said, Give me a testament. He said, When you hear God say, ‘O you who believe,’ then listen to it, for it is either good that He commands or evil that He forbids. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Khaithamah, he said, What do you read in the Qur’an, ‘O you who believe,’ for in the Torah it says, ‘O you poor people.’ Muhammad bin Ishaq said, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ra’ana, meaning listen to us. Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, O you who believe, do not say ra’ana, he said, “They used to say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘Listen to us,’ for ra’ana is like saying ‘ata’ana.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Malik, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Atiyah Al-Awfi and Qatadah, something similar to that. Mujahid said: Do not say ‘ra’ana’ do not say something different. In another narration, do not say ‘listen to us and we will listen to you’. Ata’ said: Do not say ‘ra’ana’, it was a dialect used by the Ansar, so God forbade it. Al-Hasan said: Do not say ‘ra’ana’ he said ‘ra’an’ is a mocking statement. God forbade them from mocking the words of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and what he called them to of Islam. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, that he said something similar. Abu Sakhr said: Do not say ‘ra’ana’, but say ‘unzurna’ he said: Whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned away, someone from the believers who had a need would call out to him and he would say: ‘Listen to us’. God greatly glorified His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that that should be said to him. Al-Suddi said: There was a Jewish man from Banu Qaynuqa’ called Rifa’ah ibn Zayd who used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whenever he met him he would speak to him and say: Give me your ear and listen without being submissive. The Muslims used to think that the prophets used to exaggerate in this way, so some of them used to say: Listen without being submissive and without being submissive. It is like the one in Surat An-Nisa’. So God instructed the believers not to say ra’ana. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said something similar to this. Ibn Jarir said: The correct thing to say about this to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is similar to what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ra’ana. Because it is a word that God Almighty disliked for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say, similar to what was mentioned about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Do not say ‘karam’ to grapes, but say ‘habala’, and do not say ‘abdi’ but say ‘fatay’, and the like. And the Almighty’s saying: Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists do not like that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. With this, the Almighty clarifies the intensity of the enmity of the disbelievers among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists, whom God Almighty warned against imitating the believers, in order to sever the affection between them. And the Almighty drew attention to the blessings He bestowed upon the believers of the complete and perfect law that He legislated for their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the Almighty says: And God chooses for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.

2:106: Ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: Whatever verse We abrogate means what We change from a verse. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: Whatever verse We abrogate means what We erase from a verse. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: Whatever verse We abrogate means what We confirm its writing and change its ruling. It was narrated on the authority of the companions of Abdullah ibn Masoud may God be pleased with them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah and Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi. Ad-Dahhak said: Whatever verse We abrogate means what We abrogate. Ata’ said: As for what We abrogate, it means what We leave out of the Qur’an. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It means what We leave out, so it was not revealed to Muhammad (may God bless him and grant him peace). Al-Suddi said: Whatever verse We abrogate means to seize it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: He means to seize it and remove it, such as his statement: The old man and the old woman, if they commit adultery, stone them both to death, and his statement: If the son of Adam had two valleys full of gold, he would seek a third for them. Ibn Jarir said: Whatever verse We abrogate means what we transfer from the ruling of a verse to another, so we change it and alter it, and that is by turning the permissible into the forbidden, and the forbidden into the permissible, and the permissible into the prohibited, and that does not happen except in the case of commands and prohibitions, prohibitions, generalizations, preventions, and permissibility. As for the report, there is no abrogating or abrogated in it, and the origin of abrogation is the abrogation of the Book, which is its transfer from one copy to another, so likewise the meaning of abrogating a ruling to another is only its transfer and the transfer of its expression to another, and it does not matter whether its ruling or its writing is abrogated, since both of its states are abrogated. As for the scholars of Usul al-Fiqh, their expressions differed regarding the definition of abrogation, and the matter is close, because the meaning of legal abrogation is known to scholars, and some of them noted that the ruling is lifted by a later legal proof. This includes the abrogation of a lighter verse by a heavier verse and vice versa, and abrogation not to its replacement. As for the details of the rulings on abrogation and mentioning its types and conditions, they are explained in detail in Usul al-Fiqh. At-Tabarani said: Abu Sunbul Ubayd God ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid told us, my father told us, al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Arqam, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: Two men recited a surah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had taught them, and they used to recite it. One night they stood up to pray, but they could not find a letter of it. In the morning they went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is among what was abrogated and forgotten, so they were distracted from it. Al-Zuhri used to recite it: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, with a damma on the light nun. Sulayman ibn al-Arqam is weak. Abu Bakr bin Al-Anbari narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of Nasr bin Dawud, on the authority of Abu Ubaidullah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Saleh, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Yunus and Uqayl, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Umamah bin Sahl bin Hanif, a similar hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qurtubi mentioned it. God Almighty said: Or We cause it to be forgotten, it was read in two ways: We cause it to be forgotten and We cause it to be delayed. As for the one who reads it with the opening of the noon and the hamza after the seen, its meaning is that we delay it. Ali bin Abi Talhah said: on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause it to be forgotten, meaning whatever verse We change or leave, we do not change it. Mujahid said on the authority of the companions of Ibn Masoud: Or We cause it to be forgotten, meaning we confirm its writing and change its ruling. Abd bin Umair, Mujahid and Ata’ said: Or We cause it to be forgotten, meaning we delay it and postpone it. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: Or We cause it to be forgotten, We delay it and do not abrogate it. Al-Suddi said: It is also the same, and so is Al-Rabi’ bin Anas. Ad-Dahhak said: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, meaning the abrogating and the abrogated. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, We delay it with us. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ubaydullah bin Ismail Al-Baghdadi told us, Khalaf told us, Al-Khaffaf told us, on the authority of Ismail, meaning Ibn Aslam, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, delivered a sermon to us and said: God Almighty says: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, meaning We delay it. As for the reading of or cause it to be forgotten, Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, he said: God Almighty would make His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forget whatever He wills, and abrogate whatever He wills. Ibn Jarir said: Suwad bin Abdullah told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: Regarding His statement: or We cause it to be forgotten, he said: Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to us a Qur’an and then forgot it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Nufayl told us, Muhammad bin Al-Zubayr Al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, meaning Al-Jazari, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the things that were sent down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the revelation at night and he would forget it during the day, so God Almighty revealed: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ja’far bin Nufayl told me, he is not Al-Hajjaj bin Artah, he is a sheikh of ours from Al-Jazari. Ubaid bin Umair said: Or We cause it to be forgotten, we remove it from you. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Rabi’ah, he said: I heard Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas recite: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. From a verse or We make you forget it.” He said: I said to him, Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab recites or We make you forget it. He said: Sa`d said: The Qur’an was not revealed to al-Musayyab or to the family of al-Musayyab. He said: God Almighty said: We will make you recite, and you will not forget. “And remember your Lord when you forget.” And Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise from Hisham, and al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Abu Hatim al-Razi, from Adam, from Shu`bah, from Ya`la ibn Ata’, with it, and he said: It meets the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: And he narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka`b, Qatadah, and Ikrimah something similar to what Sa`id said. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us, Sufyan al-Thawri told us: on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar said: Ali is the best of us in jurisprudence and my father is the best of us in knowledge, and we leave out some of what my father said, because my father said: I will not leave out anything I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God says: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar said: Ali is the best of us in jurisprudence and my father is the best of us in knowledge, and we leave out some of what my father said, because my father said: I will not leave out anything I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God said: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, and His statement: We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it, means in the ruling with respect to the interests of those charged with the duties, as Ali bin Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: We bring forth [one] better than it, and he says: It is better for you in benefit and more lenient for you. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Whatever verse We abrogate so that we do not act upon it or cause it to be forgotten, meaning that we postpone it until we bring it or something similar to it. Al-Suddi said: We bring something better than it or similar to it, meaning: We bring something better than what we abrogated or something similar to what we left. Qatada said: He brought something better than it or similar to it. He said: A verse that contains alleviation, a concession, a command, and a prohibition. His statement: Do you not know that God has power over all things? Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? And that you have not besides God any protector or helper? He guides His servants, the Most High, with this, to the fact that He is the One who disposes of His creation as He wills. He has the power to create and command, and He is the One who disposes. Just as He created them as He wills, and makes happy whomever He wills, and makes miserable whomever He wills, and makes healthy whomever He wills and sick whomever He wills, and guides whomever He wills, and disappoints whomever He wills, so He rules over His servants as He wills. He makes lawful what He wills, and forbids what He wills, and permits what He wills, and prohibits what He wills. He is the One who rules as He wills. There is no objector to His ruling, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they are questioned. He tests His servants and their obedience to His messengers by abrogating it. He commands something because of the benefit in it that He knows, then He forbids it because of what He knows. So obedience, all obedience, is in complying with His command and following His messengers in belief. What they told, and compliance with what they were commanded, and leaving what they were warned against. In this position, a great response and eloquent clarification of the disbelief of the Jews and the falsification of their doubts, may God curse them, in claiming the impossibility of abrogation, either rationally, as some of them claimed out of ignorance and disbelief, or by transmission, as others of them fabricated and lied. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: The interpretation of the verse: Did you not know, O Muhammad, that I have the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and their authority, without anyone else? I rule in them and in what is in them as I will, and I command in them and in what is in them as I will, and I forbid what I will, and I abrogate, change and alter, from My rulings that I rule over My servants, as I will when I will, and I confirm in them what I will. Then he said: And this report, even if it was an address from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of report, about His greatness, then it is from Him, may His praise be glorified, a denial of the Jews, who denied the abrogation of the rulings of the Torah and denied the prophethood of Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, for coming with what they came with from God. God, by changing what God changed of the ruling of the Torah, so God informed them that He has the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and their authority, and that creation is the people of His kingdom, and His obedience and they must hear and obey His command and prohibition, and that He has the right to command them as He wishes and prohibit them from what He wishes, and to abrogate what He wishes, and to approve what He wishes, and to establish what He wishes of His approval, command and prohibition. I said What makes the Jews research the issue of abrogation is disbelief and stubbornness, for there is nothing in reason that indicates the impossibility of abrogation in the rulings of God Almighty, because He rules as He wishes, just as He does what He wants, even though this has occurred in His previous books and past laws, just as He permitted Adam to marry his daughters to his sons, then He forbade that, and just as He permitted Noah, after he left the ship, to eat all animals, then He abrogated the permissibility of some of them, and the marriage of two sisters was permissible for Israel and his sons, and this was forbidden in the law of the Torah and after it, and He ordered Abraham, peace be upon him, to slaughter his son, then He abrogated it before the act, and He ordered the majority of the Children of Israel to kill whoever worshipped Him. The calf was removed from them, then killing was lifted so that killing would not eradicate them, and many things that would take too long to mention, and they admit that and turn away from it. What is answered about these evidences with verbal answers does not divert the indication to the meaning, since it is the intended purpose, and as in their books it is famous from the good report of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the command to follow him, it indicates the obligation to follow him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that no action is accepted except according to his law, and whether it is said that the previous laws are directed to his mission, may God bless him and grant him peace, this is not called abrogation because of his saying: Then complete the fast until night, and it is said: It is absolute, and that the law of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, abrogated it, so in any case the obligation to follow him is determined, because he came with a book and it is the last book to be covenanted by God Almighty, so in this position God Almighty explained the permissibility of abrogation, in response to the Jews, upon them be the curse of God, where God Almighty said: Do you not know that God has power over all things? * Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? The verse, so just as He has the dominion without dispute, so too does He have the power to rule as He wills, Is not His the creation and the command? And it was read in Surat Al Imran, which was revealed at the beginning of it as an address to the People of the Book, that abrogation occurred in the words of God Almighty: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel made unlawful to himself the verse, as will be explained. All Muslims agree on the permissibility of abrogation in the rulings of God Almighty, because of the great wisdom in that, and all of them said that it occurred. Abu Muslim Al-Asbahani, the interpreter, said: Nothing of that occurred in the Qur’an, and his statement is weak, rejected, and despicable. He was arbitrary in his answers to what occurred of abrogation, including the issue of the waiting period of four months and ten after the year, he did not answer that with acceptable speech, and the issue of changing the Qiblah to the Kaaba from the Holy House, he did not answer anything, and including that is the abrogation of a Muslim’s patience with ten infidels to patience with two, and including that is the abrogation of the obligation of charity before speaking to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and other things, and God knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It means what We leave out, so it was not revealed to Muhammad (may God bless him and grant him peace). Al-Suddi said: Whatever verse We abrogate means to seize it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: He means to seize it and remove it, such as his statement: The old man and the old woman, if they commit adultery, stone them both to death, and his statement: If the son of Adam had two valleys full of gold, he would seek a third for them. Ibn Jarir said: Whatever verse We abrogate means what we transfer from the ruling of a verse to another, so we change it and alter it, and that is by turning the permissible into the forbidden, and the forbidden into the permissible, and the permissible into the prohibited, and that does not happen except in the case of commands and prohibitions, prohibitions, generalizations, preventions, and permissibility. As for the report, there is no abrogating or abrogated in it, and the origin of abrogation is the abrogation of the Book, which is its transfer from one copy to another, so likewise the meaning of abrogating a ruling to another is only its transfer and the transfer of its expression to another, and it does not matter whether its ruling or its writing is abrogated, since both of its states are abrogated. As for the scholars of Usul al-Fiqh, their expressions differed regarding the definition of abrogation, and the matter is close, because the meaning of legal abrogation is known to scholars, and some of them noted that the ruling is lifted by a later legal proof. This includes the abrogation of a lighter verse by a heavier verse and vice versa, and abrogation not to its replacement. As for the details of the rulings on abrogation and mentioning its types and conditions, they are explained in detail in Usul al-Fiqh. At-Tabarani said: Abu Sunbul Ubayd God ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid told us, my father told us, al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Arqam, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: Two men recited a surah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had taught them, and they used to recite it. One night they stood up to pray, but they could not find a letter of it. In the morning they went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is among what was abrogated and forgotten, so they were distracted from it. Al-Zuhri used to recite it: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, with a damma on the light nun. Sulayman ibn al-Arqam is weak. Abu Bakr bin Al-Anbari narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of Nasr bin Dawud, on the authority of Abu Ubaidullah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Saleh, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Yunus and Uqayl, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Umamah bin Sahl bin Hanif, a similar hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qurtubi mentioned it. God Almighty said: Or We cause it to be forgotten, it was read in two ways: We cause it to be forgotten and We cause it to be delayed. As for the one who reads it with the opening of the noon and the hamza after the seen, its meaning is that we delay it. Ali bin Abi Talhah said: on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause it to be forgotten, meaning whatever verse We change or leave, we do not change it. Mujahid said on the authority of the companions of Ibn Masoud: Or We cause it to be forgotten, meaning we confirm its writing and change its ruling. Abd bin Umair, Mujahid and Ata’ said: Or We cause it to be forgotten, meaning we delay it and postpone it. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: Or We cause it to be forgotten, We delay it and do not abrogate it. Al-Suddi said: It is also the same, and so is Al-Rabi’ bin Anas. Ad-Dahhak said: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, meaning the abrogating and the abrogated. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, We delay it with us. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ubaydullah bin Ismail Al-Baghdadi told us, Khalaf told us, Al-Khaffaf told us, on the authority of Ismail, meaning Ibn Aslam, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, delivered a sermon to us and said: God Almighty says: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, meaning We delay it. As for the reading of or cause it to be forgotten, Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, he said: God Almighty would make His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forget whatever He wills, and abrogate whatever He wills. Ibn Jarir said: Suwad bin Abdullah told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: Regarding His statement: or We cause it to be forgotten, he said: Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to us a Qur’an and then forgot it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Nufayl told us, Muhammad bin Al-Zubayr Al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, meaning Al-Jazari, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the things that were sent down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the revelation at night and he would forget it during the day, so God Almighty revealed: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ja’far bin Nufayl told me, he is not Al-Hajjaj bin Artah, he is a sheikh of ours from Al-Jazari. Ubaid bin Umair said: Or We cause it to be forgotten, we remove it from you. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Rabi’ah, he said: I heard Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas recite: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. From a verse or We make you forget it.” He said: I said to him, Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab recites or We make you forget it. He said: Sa`d said: The Qur’an was not revealed to al-Musayyab or to the family of al-Musayyab. He said: God Almighty said: We will make you recite, and you will not forget. “And remember your Lord when you forget.” And Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise from Hisham, and al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Abu Hatim al-Razi, from Adam, from Shu`bah, from Ya`la ibn Ata’, with it, and he said: It meets the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: And he narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka`b, Qatadah, and Ikrimah something similar to what Sa`id said. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us, Sufyan al-Thawri told us: on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar said: Ali is the best of us in jurisprudence and my father is the best of us in knowledge, and we leave out some of what my father said, because my father said: I will not leave out anything I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God says: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar said: Ali is the best of us in jurisprudence and my father is the best of us in knowledge, and we leave out some of what my father said, because my father said: I will not leave out anything I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God said: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, and His statement: We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it, means in the ruling with respect to the interests of those charged with the duties, as Ali bin Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: We bring forth [one] better than it, and he says: It is better for you in benefit and more lenient for you. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Whatever verse We abrogate so that we do not act upon it or cause it to be forgotten, meaning that we postpone it until we bring it or something similar to it. Al-Suddi said: We bring something better than it or similar to it, meaning: We bring something better than what we abrogated or something similar to what we left. Qatada said: He brought something better than it or similar to it. He said: A verse that contains alleviation, a concession, a command, and a prohibition. His statement: Do you not know that God has power over all things? Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? And that you have not besides God any protector or helper? He guides His servants, the Most High, with this, to the fact that He is the One who disposes of His creation as He wills. He has the power to create and command, and He is the One who disposes. Just as He created them as He wills, and makes happy whomever He wills, and makes miserable whomever He wills, and makes healthy whomever He wills and sick whomever He wills, and guides whomever He wills, and disappoints whomever He wills, so He rules over His servants as He wills. He makes lawful what He wills, and forbids what He wills, and permits what He wills, and prohibits what He wills. He is the One who rules as He wills. There is no objector to His ruling, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they are questioned. He tests His servants and their obedience to His messengers by abrogating it. He commands something because of the benefit in it that He knows, then He forbids it because of what He knows. So obedience, all obedience, is in complying with His command and following His messengers in belief. What they told, and compliance with what they were commanded, and leaving what they were warned against. In this position, a great response and eloquent clarification of the disbelief of the Jews and the falsification of their doubts, may God curse them, in claiming the impossibility of abrogation, either rationally, as some of them claimed out of ignorance and disbelief, or by transmission, as others of them fabricated and lied. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: The interpretation of the verse: Did you not know, O Muhammad, that I have the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and their authority, without anyone else? I rule in them and in what is in them as I will, and I command in them and in what is in them as I will, and I forbid what I will, and I abrogate, change and alter, from My rulings that I rule over My servants, as I will when I will, and I confirm in them what I will. Then he said: And this report, even if it was an address from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of report, about His greatness, then it is from Him, may His praise be glorified, a denial of the Jews, who denied the abrogation of the rulings of the Torah and denied the prophethood of Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, for coming with what they came with from God. God, by changing what God changed of the ruling of the Torah, so God informed them that He has the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and their authority, and that creation is the people of His kingdom, and His obedience and they must hear and obey His command and prohibition, and that He has the right to command them as He wishes and prohibit them from what He wishes, and to abrogate what He wishes, and to approve what He wishes, and to establish what He wishes of His approval, command and prohibition. I said What makes the Jews research the issue of abrogation is disbelief and stubbornness, for there is nothing in reason that indicates the impossibility of abrogation in the rulings of God Almighty, because He rules as He wishes, just as He does what He wants, even though this has occurred in His previous books and past laws, just as He permitted Adam to marry his daughters to his sons, then He forbade that, and just as He permitted Noah, after he left the ship, to eat all animals, then He abrogated the permissibility of some of them, and the marriage of two sisters was permissible for Israel and his sons, and this was forbidden in the law of the Torah and after it, and He ordered Abraham, peace be upon him, to slaughter his son, then He abrogated it before the act, and He ordered the majority of the Children of Israel to kill whoever worshipped Him. The calf was removed from them, then killing was lifted so that killing would not eradicate them, and many things that would take too long to mention, and they admit that and turn away from it. What is answered about these evidences with verbal answers does not divert the indication to the meaning, since it is the intended purpose, and as in their books it is famous from the good report of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the command to follow him, it indicates the obligation to follow him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that no action is accepted except according to his law, and whether it is said that the previous laws are directed to his mission, may God bless him and grant him peace, this is not called abrogation because of his saying: Then complete the fast until night, and it is said: It is absolute, and that the law of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, abrogated it, so in any case the obligation to follow him is determined, because he came with a book and it is the last book to be covenanted by God Almighty, so in this position God Almighty explained the permissibility of abrogation, in response to the Jews, upon them be the curse of God, where God Almighty said: Do you not know that God has power over all things? * Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? The verse, so just as He has the dominion without dispute, so too does He have the power to rule as He wills, Is not His the creation and the command? And it was read in Surat Al Imran, which was revealed at the beginning of it as an address to the People of the Book, that abrogation occurred in the words of God Almighty: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel made unlawful to himself the verse, as will be explained. All Muslims agree on the permissibility of abrogation in the rulings of God Almighty, because of the great wisdom in that, and all of them said that it occurred. Abu Muslim Al-Asbahani, the interpreter, said: Nothing of that occurred in the Qur’an, and his statement is weak, rejected, and despicable. He was arbitrary in his answers to what occurred of abrogation, including the issue of the waiting period of four months and ten after the year, he did not answer that with acceptable speech, and the issue of changing the Qiblah to the Kaaba from the Holy House, he did not answer anything, and including that is the abrogation of a Muslim’s patience with ten infidels to patience with two, and including that is the abrogation of the obligation of charity before speaking to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and other things, and God knows best.
2:108: In this noble verse, God the Almighty forbade the believers from asking the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) too much about things before they happen, as God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them when the Qur’an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you.” That is, if you ask about their details after they are revealed, they will be made clear to you. Do not ask about something before it happens, for it may be forbidden because of that question. For this reason, it is stated in Sahih: The greatest sin of the Muslims is the one who asks about something that is not forbidden, but it is forbidden because of his question. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about a man who finds a man with his wife, if he speaks, he speaks about a serious matter, and if he remains silent, he remains silent about something similar, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) disliked the questions and criticized them. Then God revealed the ruling of cursing. For this reason, it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade idle talk, wasting money, and asking too many questions.” In Sahih Muslim, it is said: “Leave me as I have left you, for those who came before you were destroyed because of their excessive questioning and disagreement with their prophets. So if I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can, and if I forbid you from something, avoid it.” This was only said after he informed them, “That God had prescribed Hajj for them, and a man said every year: O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent about him for three days, then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, and if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory, and if it had been obligatory, you would not have been able to do it. Then he said: Leave me as I have left you.” This is why Anas bin Malik said: We were forbidden to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about anything, so we liked it when a man from the desert came and asked him and we were listening. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Abu Kurayb told us, Ishaq bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: If a year would come upon me, I would want to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about something, but I would be afraid of it, and we would wish for the Bedouins. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I have never seen a people better than the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They only asked him about twelve issues, all of which are in the Qur’an: They ask you about wine and gambling, “They ask you about the sacred month,” and They ask you about orphans, meaning this and similar matters. And the Almighty’s saying: Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And no, rather you want, or it is in its place in the question, and it is a denial, and it includes the believers and the disbelievers, for he, peace be upon him, is the Messenger of God to everyone, as the Almighty said: “The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. But they asked Moses something greater than that, and they said, ‘Show us God openly.’ So the thunderbolt seized them because of their wrongdoing.” Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Rafi’ ibn Huraymila and Wahb ibn Zayd said: O Muhammad, bring us a book that you bring down to us from the heaven so that we may read it, and cause rivers to gush forth for us so that we may follow you and believe you. So God revealed from their saying: Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the right path. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah regarding the words of God Almighty: Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? He said: A man said: O Messenger of God, if our expiation were like the expiations of the Children of Israel, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, we do not seek it - three times - what God has given you is better than what He has given the Children of Israel. When one of the Children of Israel committed a sin, he would find it written on his door and its expiation. If he expiated it, it would be a disgrace for him in this world, and if he did not expiate it, it would be a disgrace for him in the Hereafter. So what God has given you is better than what He gave the Children of Israel.” He said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God, he will find God Forgiving and Merciful. He said: The five daily prayers and from one Friday to the next are expiation for what is between them. He said: “Whoever intends to do an evil but does not do it, it is not recorded against him, but if he does it, one evil is recorded for him, and whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, one good deed is recorded for him, and if he does it, ten times the like thereof is recorded for him. And none perishes with God except one who is perishing.” So God revealed: “Or Do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? Mujahid said: Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? That God should show them openly. He said: The Quraysh asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to make Safa gold for them. He said: Yes, and it is for you like the table for the Children of Israel. But they refused and went back. Al-Suddi and Qatadah said something similar to this, and God knows best. What is meant is that God condemned whoever asked the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, about something in a way that was obstinate and suggestive, as the Children of Israel asked Moses, peace be upon him, out of obstinacy, denial, and stubbornness. God Almighty said: “And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief,” meaning whoever buys faith for disbelief, has certainly strayed from the right path, meaning he has strayed from the straight path into ignorance and misguidance. This is the case of those who turned away from believing in the prophets, following them and submitting to them, to opposing them and denying them, and suggesting to them questions that they do not need in a manner of obstinacy and disbelief, as God Almighty said: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction? Hell, they will burn in it, and wretched is the settlement. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Hardship is exchanged for ease.
2:109: God Almighty warns His believing servants against following the path of the infidels from the People of the Book, and He informs them of their enmity towards them inwardly and outwardly, and what they contain of envy towards the believers, despite their knowledge of their virtue and the virtue of their Prophet, and He commands His believing servants to forgive, pardon and endure, until the command of God comes of victory and conquest, and He commands them to establish prayer and pay zakat, and He urges them to do so and encourages them to do so, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab were among the Jews who were most envious of the Arabs, since God had singled them out for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were striving to turn people away from Islam as much as they could, so God revealed about them, Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back 1:13. And Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Zuhri, in his saying, the Most High: And many of the People of the Scripture wish that they could turn you back, he said: He is Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Yaman told us, Shu’ayb told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik told me, on the authority of his father, that Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf the Jew was a poet, and he used to satirize the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And regarding him, God revealed: And many of the People of the Scripture wish that they could turn you back, to His saying: So pardon and overlook. And al-Dahhak said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, that an illiterate Messenger would inform them of what was in their hands of books, messengers, and verses, then he would believe in all of that just as they believed in it, but they denied it out of disbelief, envy, and malice. And likewise God the Most High said: Disbelievers, out of envy from themselves after the truth had become clear to them, meaning after the truth had become clear to them, they were not ignorant of anything of it, but envy led them to deny, so He reproached them, rebuked them, and blamed them most severely, and He prescribed for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And for the believers, what they are upon of belief, faith and acknowledgment of what God has revealed to them, and what was revealed before them, with His honor and abundant reward and His assistance to them. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said, From themselves from themselves, and Abu Al-Aaliyah said, After the truth has become clear to them, after it became clear that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, they find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, so they disbelieved in him out of envy and malice, since he was from someone other than them, and so said Qatada and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and His statement, So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command, is like His statement, the Most High, And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God, much abuse 1:13. Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command, that was abrogated by His statement, Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and His statement, Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, until His statement, while they are subdued, so this abrogated His pardon of the polytheists, and so said Abu Al-Aliyah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Qatadah and Al-Suddi said that it was abrogated by the verse of the sword. This is also indicated by the words of God the Almighty: until God brings about His command. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: Abu Al-Yaman told us: Shu’aib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri: Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me that Usamah bin Zaid told him: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and his companions used to forgive the polytheists and the People of the Book, as God commanded them, and they used to be patient in the face of harm. God the Almighty said: “So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command. Indeed, God is over all things competent.” The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to interpret forgiveness as what God commanded him to do, until God permitted killing them, and God killed those of the leaders of Quraysh who He killed. The chain of transmission of this hadith is sound, but I have not seen it in any of the six books, but it has a basis in the two Sahihs on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid. And the Almighty’s saying: And establish prayer and give zakat, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with God, urges them to occupy themselves with what benefits them and will be rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection, such as establishing prayer and giving zakat, so that God will grant them victory in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand, The Day when the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them, and they will have the curse, and they will have the worst home, and for this reason the Almighty said: Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do, meaning that the Almighty does not neglect the work of a worker, nor does it go to waste with Him, whether it is good or evil, for He will reward every worker for his work. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: In the words of God Almighty: Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do, this is report from God to those believers whom He addressed with these verses, that whatever good or evil they do, secretly or openly, He is Seeing of it and nothing is hidden from Him, so He rewards them for good with good, and for evil with the same. And this statement, even though it was presented in the form of report, contains a promise and a threat, a command and a warning, and that is because He informed the people that He is Seeing of all their deeds, so that they may find in His obedience since that is stored up for them with Him, until He rewards them for it, as God Almighty said: And whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with God, and so that they may beware of disobeying Him. He said: As for His words Seeing, then it is Seeing, diverted to Seeing, just as He diverted Creator to Innovator, and Painful to Painful, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibn Bakir told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Abu al-Khair, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting this verse: All-Hearing, All-Seeing, saying: All-Seeing of all things.
