And likewise God the Most High said: Disbelievers, out of envy from themselves after the truth had become clear to them, meaning after the truth had become clear to them, they were not ignorant of anything of it, but envy led them to deny, so He reproached them, rebuked them, and blamed them most severely, and He prescribed for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And for the believers, what they are upon of belief, faith and acknowledgment of what God has revealed to them, and what was revealed before them, with His honor and abundant reward and His assistance to them. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said, From themselves from themselves, and Abu Al-Aaliyah said, After the truth has become clear to them, after it became clear that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, they find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, so they disbelieved in him out of envy and malice, since he was from someone other than them, and so said Qatada and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and His statement, So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command, is like His statement, the Most High, And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God, much abuse 1:13. Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command, that was abrogated by His statement, Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and His statement, Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, until His statement, while they are subdued, so this abrogated His pardon of the polytheists, and so said Abu Al-Aliyah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Qatadah and Al-Suddi said that it was abrogated by the verse of the sword. This is also indicated by the words of God the Almighty: until God brings about His command. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: Abu Al-Yaman told us: Shu’aib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri: Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me that Usamah bin Zaid told him: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and his companions used to forgive the polytheists and the People of the Book, as God commanded them, and they used to be patient in the face of harm. God the Almighty said: “So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command. Indeed, God is over all things competent.” The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to interpret forgiveness as what God commanded him to do, until God permitted killing them, and God killed those of the leaders of Quraysh who He killed. The chain of transmission of this hadith is sound, but I have not seen it in any of the six books, but it has a basis in the two Sahihs on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid. And the Almighty’s saying: And establish prayer and give zakat, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with God, urges them to occupy themselves with what benefits them and will be rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection, such as establishing prayer and giving zakat, so that God will grant them victory in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand, The Day when the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them, and they will have the curse, and they will have the worst home, and for this reason the Almighty said: Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do, meaning that the Almighty does not neglect the work of a worker, nor does it go to waste with Him, whether it is good or evil, for He will reward every worker for his work. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: In the words of God Almighty: Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do, this is report from God to those believers whom He addressed with these verses, that whatever good or evil they do, secretly or openly, He is Seeing of it and nothing is hidden from Him, so He rewards them for good with good, and for evil with the same. And this statement, even though it was presented in the form of report, contains a promise and a threat, a command and a warning, and that is because He informed the people that He is Seeing of all their deeds, so that they may find in His obedience since that is stored up for them with Him, until He rewards them for it, as God Almighty said: And whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with God, and so that they may beware of disobeying Him. He said: As for His words Seeing, then it is Seeing, diverted to Seeing, just as He diverted Creator to Innovator, and Painful to Painful, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibn Bakir told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Abu al-Khair, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting this verse: All-Hearing, All-Seeing, saying: All-Seeing of all things.
2:111: The Almighty shows the deception of the Jews and Christians in what they are in, as each group of Jews and Christians claimed that no one will enter Paradise except those who follow their religion, as God informed us about them in Surat Al-Ma'idah, that they said: We are the sons of God and His beloved, so God the Almighty belied them by what He told them that He would punish them for their sins, and if they were as they claimed, the matter would not have been like that, and as mentioned before from their claim, that the fire will not touch them except for a few days, then they will move to Paradise, and God responded to them in that, and thus He said to them in this claim that they claimed without evidence, argument or proof, so He said: Those are their wishful thinking, and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Wishful thinking that they wished from God without right, and so did Qatadah and Al-Rabi' bin Anas, then God the Almighty said: Say meaning O Muhammad, Bring your proof, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Al-Suddi and Al-Rabi' bin Anas said: Your proof, and Qatadah said: Your proof for that: If you are truthful, meaning in what you claim, then He said God the Almighty said: Yes, whoever submits his face to God and is a doer of good, meaning whoever sincerely works for God alone, with no partner for Him, as God the Almighty said: But if they argue with you, say, ‘I have submitted my face to God, and whoever follows me,’ verse. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi’ said: Yes, whoever submits his face to God, meaning whoever is sincere to God. Saeed bin Jubair said: Yes, whoever submits, sincerely his face, meaning his religion, and is a doer of good, meaning he follows the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in it. For an accepted deed, there are two conditions: one of them is that it be correct and sincerely for God alone, and the other is that it be correct and in accordance with the Shari’ah. So whenever it is sincere but not correct, it is not accepted. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected. Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Aisha from him, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the work of monks and those like them, even if it is assumed that they are sincere in it for God, it is not accepted from them, until it is in following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was sent to them and to all people, and about them and their likes God the Almighty said: And We will present to them whatever deeds they have done and make them as scattered dust. And God the Almighty said: And those who disbelieve - their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty person thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it is nothing. And God the Almighty said: Some faces that Day will be humbled, toiling and exhausted, burning in a blazing Fire, given to drink from a boiling spring. It was narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar, may God be pleased with him, that he interpreted it in reference to monks, as will come. However, if the deed is in accordance with the Shari’ah, in its outward appearance, but its doer does not sincerely intend God, then it is also rejected by its doer, and this is the case of hypocrites and ostentatious people, as God the Almighty said: “Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, but it is He who will deceive them. And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering God except a little.” And God the Almighty said: So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who are showing off, and withhold aid. For this reason God the Almighty said: “So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord No one. And He said in this noble verse: “Yes, whoever submits his face to God while he is a doer of good.” And His statement: “Then they will have their reward with their Lord. And no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.” The Almighty guaranteed them for that the attainment of rewards, and He secured them from what they fear of the forbidden. So there is no fear upon them in what they will face, nor will they grieve over what has passed of what they will leave behind, as Saeed bin Jubair said, So there is no fear upon them meaning in the Hereafter, nor will they grieve meaning they will not grieve over death. And the Almighty said: And the Jews say, ‘The Christians are not upon anything,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews are not upon anything,’ and they recite the Scripture, with which the Almighty showed their contradiction, hatred, enmity, and stubbornness, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Christians of Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Jewish rabbis came to them and they disputed before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rafi’ ibn Huraymila said: ‘You are not upon anything,’ and he disbelieved in Jesus and the Gospel. And a Christian man from Najran said to the Jews: ‘You are not upon anything,’ and he denied the prophethood of Moses and disbelieved in the Torah. So God revealed regarding their statement: And the Jews say, ‘The Christians are not upon anything,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews are not upon anything,’ and they recite the Scripture, meaning that each one recites in his book a confirmation of the one who disbelieved in him, that the Jews disbelieved in Jesus while they had the Torah, in which was what God took from them on the tongue of Moses to confirm. In Jesus and in the Gospel what Jesus brought by confirming Moses, and what came from the Torah from God, and each one disbelieves in what is in the hand of his companion, and Mujahid said in his interpretation of this verse: The first Jews and Christians were on something, but they innovated and split up, “And the Christians said, ‘The Jews are not on anything. ’” He said: Yes, the first Jews were on something, but they innovated and split up, and from him is another narration like the saying of Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas in his interpretation of this verse: “And the Jews said, ‘The Christians are not on anything. ’ And the Christians said, ‘The Jews are not on anything. ’” These are the People of the Book who were at the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this statement requires that each of the two groups was truthful in what it accused the other group of, but the apparent context of the verse requires that they be blamed for what they said, despite their knowledge of the opposite, and for this reason God Almighty said: And they recite the Book, meaning while they know the law of the Torah and the Gospel, each of which was permissible at one time, but they contradicted each other out of stubbornness, disbelief, and in opposition to the corrupt, as mentioned previously from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah in the first narration from him in its interpretation, and God knows best. His statement: Thus said those who do not know, like their statement, shows the ignorance of the Jews and Christians in what they said to each other, and this is from the category of allusion and indication. There is a difference of opinion as to who is meant by the statement of God the Almighty: Those who do not know. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and Qatadah said: Thus said those who do not know, and they said: And the Christians said like the Jews said and said. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Ata’, who are these who do not know? He said that nations existed before the Jews and Christians and before the Torah and the Gospel. Al-Suddi also said, Those who do not know said, meaning the Arabs. They said that Muhammad is not on anything. Abu Jaafar bin Jarir chose that it is general and suitable for all, and there is no conclusive evidence to specify one of these statements. It is more appropriate to apply it to all, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying, Then God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ, means that God Almighty will gather them on the Day of Resurrection and will separate them with His just judgment, in which He will not be unjust or oppressive, even the weight of an atom. This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat Al-Hajj, “Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Sabeans or Christians or Magians or polytheists—God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is, over all things, Witness.” And as God Almighty said, “Say, ‘Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Opener, the Knowing.’”

2:114: The commentators differed about the meaning of those who prevented the mosques of God and sought to destroy them, with two opinions: One of them is what Al-Awfi narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in his statement: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned in them? He said: They are the Christians. Mujahid said: They are the Christians who used to throw harmful things into the Holy House and prevent people from praying in it. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And sought to destroy it. He said: It is Bukhtanasr and his companions, who destroyed the Holy House, and the Christians helped him in that. Saeed said on the authority of Qatada: He said: Those are the enemies of God, the Christians, their hatred of the Jews led them to help the Babylonian Magian Bukhtanasr to destroy the Holy House. Al-Suddi said: They supported Bukhtanasr in destroying the Holy House, until he destroyed it and ordered that the corpses be thrown into it. The Romans only helped him in its destruction because the Children of Israel killed John the Baptist, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, the second opinion, what Ibn Jarir narrated: Yunus bin Abdul-A’la told me, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned therein and strives toward their destruction? He said: These are the polytheists who prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah from entering Mecca, until he slaughtered his sacrificial animal at Dhu Tuwa, and he made peace with them and said to them: No one would prevent anyone from entering this House, and a man would meet the killer of his father or brother and not prevent him. They said: He who killed our fathers on the day of Badr should not enter upon us while we were Remaining, and in his saying: And strived for its destruction, he said when they cut off those who would populate it with his remembrance and come to it for Hajj and Umrah. Ibn Abi Hatim said, on the authority of Salamah, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Quraysh prevented the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from praying at the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque, so God revealed: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned therein? Then Ibn Jarir chose the first statement, and argued that Quraysh did not strive for the destruction of the Kaaba, but as for the Romans, they strived to destroy the Holy House. I said What appears, and God knows best, is the second statement as Ibn Zayd said. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that if the Christians prevented the Jews from praying in the Holy House, their religion would be more correct than the religion of the Jews, and they would be closer to them, and the mention of God from the Jews would not be accepted at that time, because they had been cursed before by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary, because they disobeyed and transgressed. Also, when God Almighty directed blame at the Jews and Christians, He proceeded to blame the polytheists who expelled the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from Mecca, and prevented them from praying in the Sacred Mosque. As for his reliance on the fact that the Quraysh did not strive to destroy the Kaaba, what destruction is greater than what they did? They expelled the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) and his companions from it, and took control of it with their idols, rivals and polytheism, as God the Almighty said: "And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them while they hinder [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram, and they were not its guardians? Its guardians are only the righteous, but most of them do not know." And God the Almighty said: "It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they testify against themselves by disbelief. For those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day and establish prayer and give zakah and do not fear except God. It is expected that those will be among the [rightly] guided." And God the Almighty said: "They are the ones who disbelieved and hindered you from al-Masjid al-Haram, and the offering was held back from reaching its destination. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, lest you tread upon them and there should befall you from them a blemish without knowledge. So God may admit into His mercy whom He wills. Had they separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment." And God the Almighty said: "The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day and establish prayer and give zakah and do not fear except God. So it is expected that those will be among the [rightly] guided." He fears none but God. If someone like that is expelled from it and turned away from it, what destruction of it is greater than that? What is meant by its construction is not only its decoration and the erection of its image, but rather its construction is by the remembrance of God in it and the establishment of His law in it, and raising it from defilement and polytheism. And the Almighty’s saying: It is not for them to enter it except in fear, this is a report that means a request, i.e. do not allow these people, if you are able to do so, to enter it, except under a truce and a tribute. For this reason, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca, he ordered that the following year, in the year nine, it be announced in the courtyards of Mina: “No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, nor shall he circumambulate the House naked. And whoever has a term, his term shall be until his term.” This was only a confirmation and action of the Almighty’s saying: O you who believe, indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. Some of them said: It is not appropriate for them to enter the mosques of God except in fear, in a state of awe and trembling from the believers, lest they should attack them, let alone seize them and prevent the believers from them. The meaning is that there was nothing but the right and the duty except that, were it not for the oppression of the infidels and others. It was said that this is good report from God to the Muslims, that He will make them victorious over the Sacred Mosque and over all the other mosques, and that He will humiliate the polytheists before them. So that none of them would enter the Sacred Mosque except in fear that he would be seized and punished or killed if he did not convert to Islam. And God fulfilled this promise, as mentioned before in preventing the polytheists from entering the Sacred Mosque, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded that there should not remain two religions in the Arabian Peninsula, and that the Jews and Christians should be expelled from it, and praise and thanks be to God. This is nothing but honoring the environs of the Sacred Mosque and purifying the spot in which God sent His Messenger to all people, as a bearer of good tidings and a warner, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. This is their disgrace in this world, because the reward is of the same kind as the deed. Just as they turned the believers away from the Sacred Mosque, they were turned away from it, and just as they were expelled from Mecca, they were expelled from it. And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment for what they violated of the sanctity of the House, and their desecration of it by erecting idols around it, and calling upon other than God at it, and circumambulating it naked, and other actions of theirs that God and His Messenger hate. As for those who interpreted the Holy House, Ka’b al-Ahbar said: When the Christians gained control of the Holy House, they destroyed it. Then when God sent Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, He revealed to him: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned therein and strives toward their ruin? It is not for them to enter them except in fear. The verse, so there is no Christian on earth who enters the Holy House except in fear. Al-Suddi said: There is no Roman on earth who enters it today. Except that he is afraid that his neck will be struck, or he has been frightened into paying the jizya, so he pays it. Qatada said: They do not enter the mosques except stealthily. I said This does not negate that it is included in the meaning of the generality of the verse, because when the Christians wronged the Holy House by desecrating the rock, towards which the Jews used to pray, they were punished by law and destiny with humiliation in it, except at times in time when the Holy House was filled with them. Likewise the Jews, when they also disobeyed God in it, more than the disobedience of the Christians, their punishment was greater, and God knows best. And these interpreted the disgrace in this world. The emergence of the Mahdi according to Al-Suddi, Ikrimah and Wa’il bin Dawud, and Qatada interpreted it as paying the jizyah with their own hands while they are humiliated, and the correct view is that disgrace in this world is more general than all of that, and the hadith was narrated with seeking refuge from the disgrace of this world and the torment of the Hereafter, as Imam Ahmad said: Al-Haytham bin Kharijah informed us, Muhammad bin Ayoub bin Maysarah bin Halbas informed us, I heard my father narrating on the authority of Bishr bin Arta’ah, he said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate: O God, make our end good in all matters and save us from the disgrace of this world and the torment of the Hereafter. This is a good hadith, and it is not in any of the six books, and his companion, Bishr bin Arta’ah, has no other hadith other than it, and other than the hadith that hands are not cut off in conquest.
2:115: And this, and God knows best, is a consolation for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, who were expelled from Mecca and left their mosque and place of prayer. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray in Mecca facing Jerusalem with the Kaaba in front of him. When he arrived in Medina, he was directed towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, then God turned him to the Kaaba later. This is why God Almighty says: “To God belong the east and the west. So wherever you turn, there is the face of God.” Abu Ubaid al-Qasim ibn Salam said in the Book of Abrogation and Abrogated: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad told us, Ibn Jurayj and Uthman ibn Ata’ told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that was abrogated for us from the Qur’an, according to what was mentioned to us, and God knows best, was the matter of the qibla. God Almighty said: “To God belong the east and the west. So wherever you turn, there is the face of God.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced him and prayed facing Jerusalem and left the Ancient House, then he turned him to his Ancient House and abrogated it. He said: And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The first thing that was abrogated from the Qur’an was the qiblah, and that was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, and its people were Jews, God commanded him to face Jerusalem, so the Jews rejoiced, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced it for a few months, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved the qiblah of Abraham, and he used to supplicate and look at the sky, so God revealed: We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven until His saying: So turn your faces toward it. The Jews were suspicious of that, and said: What turned them away from the qiblah that they were facing? So God revealed: “Say: To God belongs the East and the West,” and He said: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. He said: The qiblah of God is wherever you turn, east or west. Mujahid said: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. Wherever you are, you have a qiblah that you face. The Kaaba, and Ibn Abi Hatim said after narrating the previous trace from Ibn Abbas in abrogating the qiblah from Ata from him, and it was narrated from Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Hasan, Ata Al-Khurasani, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and Zaid bin Aslam something similar to that, and Jarir said and others said: Rather, God revealed this verse before He imposed facing the Kaaba, and He only revealed it to teach His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions that they may face their faces in prayer wherever they wish from the directions of the east and the west, because they do not face in any direction or direction except that He, the Most High, is in that direction and direction, because the Easts and the Wests belong to Him, and no place is devoid of Him, as He, the Most High, said: And neither nearer than that nor more, but He is with them wherever they are. They said: Then that was abrogated by the obligation that was imposed on them to face the Sacred Mosque, thus he said. And in His statement that no place is devoid of Him, if He meant His knowledge, the Most High, then it is correct, for His knowledge encompasses all information, but as for His Essence, the Most High, it is not confined to any of His creation, God is far above that, far above that. Ibn Jarir said, and others said: Rather, this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as permission from God to pray voluntarily, wherever he faces, east or west, while traveling, and in times of combat and intense fear. Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Idris told us, Abdul Malik - he is Ibn Abi Sulayman - told us, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he used to pray wherever his mount faced him, and he mentioned that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do that and interpreted this verse as So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. It was narrated by Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh, through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abdul Malik Ibn Abi Sulayman, and its origin is in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Umar and Amir Ibn Rabi’ah, without mentioning the verse. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, that when he was asked about the prayer of fear, he would describe it, then he would say: If the fear is more severe than that, pray while standing on your feet, or while riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it. Nafi’ said: I do not think that Ibn Umar mentioned that except on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Question Al-Shafi’i did not differentiate, according to the well-known opinion, between travelling a distance and travelling by contagion. According to all of them, it is permissible to voluntarily perform it on a mount, which is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, contrary to Malik and his group. Abu Yusuf and Abu Sa’id al-Istakhri chose voluntary prayer on an animal in the city. Abu Yusuf narrated it on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, and Abu Ja’far al-Tabari chose it, even for the pedestrian. Ibn Jarir said and others said: Rather, the verse was revealed about a people who were blind to the direction of the Qiblah, so they did not know which side it was, so they prayed in different directions. God Almighty said: To Me belong the Easts and the Wests, so wherever you turn your faces, there is My Face and it is your Qiblah. He informs you thereby that your prayer is valid. Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi told us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Abu al-Rabi’ al-Samman told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of his father, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a dark, black night, and we stopped at a place, and a man began to take stones and make a place of prayer in which to pray. When morning came, we found that we had prayed in a direction other than the qiblah, so we said, O Messenger of God, we have prayed this night in a direction other than the qiblah, so God the Most High revealed: To God belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn, there is the face of God al-Baqarah 2:17. Then he narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Wakee’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’ al-Samman, in a similar manner. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Mahmud bin Ghailan on the authority of Wakee’ and Ibn Majah on the authority of Yahya bin Hakim on the authority of Abu Dawud on the authority of Abu Al-Rabi’ Al-Samman. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah on the authority of Saeed bin Sulaiman on the authority of Abu Al-Rabi’ Al-Samman, whose name is Ash’ath bin Saeed Al-Basri, and he is weak in hadith. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good hadith, but its chain of transmission is not that strong, and we do not know it except from the hadith of Al-Ash’ath Al-Samman, and Ash’ath is weak in hadith. I say: His sheikh, Asim, is also weak. Al-Bukhari said: He is a rejected hadith narrator. Ibn Ma’een said: He is weak and cannot be relied upon. Ibn Hibban said: He is abandoned, and God knows best. And he narrated from another path, from Jabir, so Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said in the interpretation of this verse: Ismail bin Ali bin Ismail told us, Al-Hasan bin Ali bin Shabib told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Al-Hasan told me, he said: I found in my father’s book, Abdul Malik Al-Azrami told us, from Ata’, from Jabir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a detachment, and I was in it, and darkness befell us, so we did not know the qiblah, so a group of us said: We know the qiblah, it is here towards the north, so they prayed and drew lines, and when they woke up and the sun rose, those lines became not towards the qiblah, so when we returned from our journey, we asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he remained silent, and God Almighty revealed: And to God belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn, there is the face of God. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad bin Ubaidullah Al-Azrami from Ata’ from Jabir with it, and Al-Daraqutni said: It was read to Abdullah bin Abdul Aziz and I was listening, Dawud bin Amr told you, Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Wasiti told us, from Muhammad bin Salim, from Ata’, from Jabir, he said: We were with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) on a journey and a cloud hit us, so we were confused and disagreed about the direction of the qiblah, so each man of us prayed separately and one of us would draw a line in front of him so that we would know where we were. We mentioned that to the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), but he did not order us to repeat it, and he said: Your prayer is sufficient. Then Ad-Daraqutni said: This is what he said on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salim, and another said on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah Al-Azrami on the authority of Ata’, and they are both weak. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) sent out a detachment and they were caught in a fog and they could not find their way to the qiblah, so they prayed in a direction other than the qiblah. Then it became clear to them after the sun had risen that they had prayed in a direction other than the qiblah. When they came to the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), they told him, so God revealed regarding this verse: To God belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn, there is the face of God. These chains of transmission are weak, and perhaps some of them support each other. As for repeating the prayer for someone who realizes his mistake, there are two opinions of the scholars, and this is Evidence of non-judgment, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: And others said: Rather, this verse was revealed because of the Negus, as Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Hisham ibn Muadh told us, my father told me on the authority of Qatada that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A brother of yours has died, so pray over him. They said: Should we pray over a man who is not a Muslim? He said: So the verse was revealed: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture is he who believes in God and in what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly submissive to God. Qatada said: They said that he did not pray toward the Qiblah, so God revealed: And to God belong the East and the West, so wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. This is strange, and God knows best. It has been said that he used to pray toward Jerusalem before the scribe conveyed it to the Kaaba, as Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Qatada. Al-Qurtubi mentioned that when he died, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him, and that was taken from those who went to pray over the absent. He said: This is specific to our companions from three aspects - one of them - that when he, peace be upon him, saw him when he prayed over him, the earth was folded up for him. The second is that since he had no one to pray over him, he prayed over him, and Ibn al-Arabi chose this. Al-Qurtubi said: It is unlikely that there would be a Muslim king who had no one from his people who followed his religion. Ibn al-Arabi answered this by saying that perhaps they did not have the legitimacy of praying over the dead. This is a good answer. The third is that he, peace and blessings be upon him, only prayed over him so that this would be like a way of bringing the rest of the kings together, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated in his interpretation of this verse from the hadith of Abu Ma`shar from Muhammad bin `Amr bin `Alqamah from Abu Salamah from Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whatever is between the east and the west is the qiblah for the people of Madinah, the people of Ash-Sham, and the people of Iraq. And it has relevance here. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Abu Ma`shar, whose name is Najih bin `Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi al-Madani, with it: Whatever is between the east and the west is the qiblah. And Al-Tirmidhi said: It was narrated from other sources from Abu Hurairah, and some of the people of knowledge spoke about Abu Ma`shar because of his memory. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: Al-Hasan bin Bakr al-Marwazi told me, Al-Mu`alla bin Mansur told us, Abdullah bin Ja`far al-Mukhrami told us, from `Uthman bin Muhammad bin Al-Akhns from Abu Sa`id al-Maqburi from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whatever is between the east and the west is the qiblah. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is authentic. And it was narrated from Al-Bukhari that he said: This is stronger and more authentic than the hadith of Abu Ma`shar. Al-Tirmidhi said: And It was narrated on the authority of more than one of the Companions, Whatever is between the East and the West is the Qiblah, including Omar ibn al-Khattab, Ali, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them all. Ibn Umar said: If you place the west on your right and the east on your left, then what is between them is a qibla, if you face the qibla. Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Ali bin Ahmad bin Abd al-Rahman told us, Yaqub bin Yusuf, a client of Banu Hashim, told us, Shu`ayb bin Ayyub told us, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: What is between the east and the west is a qibla. Ad-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi narrated it. The famous one said on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with them both, his statement. Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that wherever you turn your faces in your supplication to Me, there is My face, and I will answer your supplication, as al-Qasim told us, al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: When the verse Call upon Me, I will answer you was revealed, they said: To where, so the verse So wherever you turn, there is the face of God was revealed. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of His statement Indeed, God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing is that He encompasses all of His creation with sufficiency, generosity, and favor. As for His statement All-Knowing, it means: He is All-Knowing of their deeds. Nothing of them escapes Him, and nothing is hidden from His knowledge. Rather, He is All-Knowing of them all.
2:116: This noble verse and the one that follows it contain a response to the Christians, upon them be the curses of God, and also those like them from the Jews and the polytheists of the Arabs who made the angels daughters of God, so God belied all of them in their claim and their saying that God has a son, so God the Most High said: Glory be to Him meaning He is exalted, sanctified and far above that, Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth meaning the matter is not as they fabricated, rather His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, and He is the One who controls them, and He is their Creator, Provider, Destiner, Subject, Guide, and Disposer of them as He wills, and all are His slaves and His property, so how could He have a son from them when a son is only born from two proportional things, and He, the Blessed and Exalted, has no peer or partner in His greatness and pride, nor does He have a companion, so how could He have a son? As God the Almighty said: “Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He has no wife and He created all things? And He is Knowing of all things?” And God the Almighty said: “And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ You have certainly done a thing monstrous. The heavens almost burst from it and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation. That they attribute to the Most Gracious a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Gracious that He should take a son. Indeed, everyone in the heavens and the earth will come to the Most Gracious as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them precisely. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.” And God the Almighty said: “Say, ‘He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is born. And there is none comparable to Him.’” So God the Almighty has established in these noble verses that He is the Great Master who has no peer or likeness and that all things besides Him were created and nurtured for Him, so how could He have a son from them? And for this reason Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation of this verse from al-Baqarah 2:Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hussein, Nafi bin Jubair - he is Ibn Mut’am - told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty said: The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so, and he insulted Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, he claims that I am not able to restore him as he was, and as for his insulting Me, it is his saying that I have a son, so glory be to Me that I should take a wife or a son.” Al-Bukhari transmitted it only from this source. Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Kamil told us, Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Tirmidhi told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Muhammad Al-Farawi told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “And God Almighty says: The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so, and he insulted Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying: He will not restore me as I began. And the first creation is not easier for Me than its restoration.” As for his cursing me, he said: “God has taken a son. I am God, the One, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.” In the two Sahihs, it is narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “No one is more patient with the harm he hears than God. They attribute to Him a son, and He provides for them and cures them.” And his saying: All are obedient to Him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja’ informed us, Asbat informed us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Obserious means praying. Ikrimah and Abu Malik said: All are obedient to Him acknowledging servitude to Him. Saeed bin Jubayr said: All are obedient to Him, meaning sincerity. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: He says: All are obedient to Him, meaning standing on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Suddi said: All are obedient to Him, meaning obedient on the Day of Resurrection. Khasif said on the authority of Mujahid: All are obedient to Him, he said: obedient. He said: Be a human being and it was. He said: Be a donkey and it was. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: All have obedient and devout ones. He said: The obedience of the disbeliever is in the prostration of his shadow, even though he is reluctant. This statement from Mujahid, which is the choice of Ibn Jarir, brings together all the statements, which is that devoutness, obedience, and submission to God is a lawful and predestined act, as God Almighty said: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and so do their shadows in the mornings and the evenings. A hadith has been reported in which there is an explanation of devoutness in the Qur’an, what is meant by it, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yusuf Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr Ibn al-Harith told me that Diraaj Abu al-Samh told him on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every letter of the Qur’an in which devoutness is mentioned is obedience. Imam Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Hasan Ibn Musa on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah on the authority of Diraaj with his chain of transmission similar to it, but in this chain of transmission there is a weakness that cannot be relied upon, and the attribution of this hadith to the Prophet is objectionable, and it may be the words of a companion or someone less than him, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Originator of the heavens and the earth means: Their Creator without a previous example. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: This is what the language requires, and from this the newly introduced thing is called an innovation, as it came in Sahih Muslim: “For every newly introduced thing is an innovation, and innovation is of two types: Sometimes it is a religious innovation, like his saying: “For every newly introduced thing is an innovation and every innovation is misguidance,” and sometimes it is a linguistic innovation, like the saying of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn Al-Khattab, about his gathering them for the Tarawih prayer and their continuation: What an excellent innovation this is! Ibn Jarir said: Originator of the heavens and the earth is their Creator, and it is a verb that is changed to a verb, just as the painful is changed to the painful, and the hearer is changed to the hearer. The meaning of the creator is the originator and the originator, that which no one precedes him in creating and innovating like it. He said: Therefore the innovator in religion is called an innovator because he innovates in it what no one else has preceded him in, and likewise every innovator in word or deed, in which no one preceded him, the Arabs call him an innovator. This includes the words of A’sha bin Tha’laba in praise of Hudha bin Ali al-Hanafi: He claims to say the words of the masters of men if they show him firmness or whatever he wants he innovates That is, He creates what He wills. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of the words, Glory be to God, is that He has a son, and He is the Owner of what is in the heavens and the earth, and all of them bear witness to Him by indicating His Oneness, and acknowledge His obedience, and He is their Creator, Maker, and Originator, without a root or example that they follow. This is an announcement from God to His servants that among those who bear witness to this is the Messiah, to whom they attributed his sonship to God, and an announcement from Him to them that the One who created the heavens and the earth without a root and without an example is the One who created the Messiah, Jesus, without a father by His power. This is good speech and a correct expression from Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. And the Almighty’s saying: And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. With this, the Almighty clarifies the perfection of His power and the greatness of His authority, and that when He decrees a matter and wants it to be, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ that is, once, and it is, that is, it exists, according to what He willed, as the Almighty said: His command, when He intends a thing, is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. And the Almighty said: Our command to a thing when We intend it is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. And the Almighty said: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. And the poet said: If he wants something, he just says to it, Be, and it is. He also pointed out that Jesus was created with the word Be, and he was, as God commanded him. God Almighty said: “The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.”
2:117: This noble verse and the one that follows it contain a response to the Christians, upon them be the curses of God, and also those like them from the Jews and the polytheists of the Arabs who made the angels daughters of God, so God belied all of them in their claim and their saying that God has a son, so God the Most High said: Glory be to Him meaning He is exalted, sanctified and far above that, Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth meaning the matter is not as they fabricated, rather His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, and He is the One who controls them, and He is their Creator, Provider, Destiner, Subject, Guide, and Disposer of them as He wills, and all are His slaves and His property, so how could He have a son from them when a son is only born from two proportional things, and He, the Blessed and Exalted, has no peer or partner in His greatness and pride, nor does He have a companion, so how could He have a son? As God the Almighty said: “Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He has no wife and He created all things? And He is Knowing of all things?” And God the Almighty said: “And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ You have certainly done a thing monstrous. The heavens almost burst from it and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation. That they attribute to the Most Gracious a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Gracious that He should take a son. Indeed, everyone in the heavens and the earth will come to the Most Gracious as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them precisely. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.” And God the Almighty said: “Say, ‘He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is born. And there is none comparable to Him.’” So God the Almighty has established in these noble verses that He is the Great Master who has no peer or likeness and that all things besides Him were created and nurtured for Him, so how could He have a son from them? And for this reason Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation of this verse from al-Baqarah 2:Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hussein, Nafi bin Jubair - he is Ibn Mut’am - told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty said: The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so, and he insulted Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, he claims that I am not able to restore him as he was, and as for his insulting Me, it is his saying that I have a son, so glory be to Me that I should take a wife or a son.” Al-Bukhari transmitted it only from this source. Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Kamil told us, Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Tirmidhi told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Muhammad Al-Farawi told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “And God Almighty says: The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so, and he insulted Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying: He will not restore me as I began. And the first creation is not easier for Me than its restoration.” As for his cursing me, he said: “God has taken a son. I am God, the One, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.” In the two Sahihs, it is narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “No one is more patient with the harm he hears than God. They attribute to Him a son, and He provides for them and cures them.” And his saying: All are obedient to Him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja’ informed us, Asbat informed us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Obserious means praying. Ikrimah and Abu Malik said: All are obedient to Him acknowledging servitude to Him. Saeed bin Jubayr said: All are obedient to Him, meaning sincerity. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: He says: All are obedient to Him, meaning standing on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Suddi said: All are obedient to Him, meaning obedient on the Day of Resurrection. Khasif said on the authority of Mujahid: All are obedient to Him, he said: obedient. He said: Be a human being and it was. He said: Be a donkey and it was. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: All have obedient and devout ones. He said: The obedience of the disbeliever is in the prostration of his shadow, even though he is reluctant. This statement from Mujahid, which is the choice of Ibn Jarir, brings together all the statements, which is that devoutness, obedience, and submission to God is a lawful and predestined act, as God Almighty said: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and so do their shadows in the mornings and the evenings. A hadith has been reported in which there is an explanation of devoutness in the Qur’an, what is meant by it, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yusuf Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr Ibn al-Harith told me that Diraaj Abu al-Samh told him on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every letter of the Qur’an in which devoutness is mentioned is obedience. Imam Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Hasan Ibn Musa on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah on the authority of Diraaj with his chain of transmission similar to it, but in this chain of transmission there is a weakness that cannot be relied upon, and the attribution of this hadith to the Prophet is objectionable, and it may be the words of a companion or someone less than him, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Originator of the heavens and the earth means: Their Creator without a previous example. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: This is what the language requires, and from this the newly introduced thing is called an innovation, as it came in Sahih Muslim: “For every newly introduced thing is an innovation, and innovation is of two types: Sometimes it is a religious innovation, like his saying: “For every newly introduced thing is an innovation and every innovation is misguidance,” and sometimes it is a linguistic innovation, like the saying of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn Al-Khattab, about his gathering them for the Tarawih prayer and their continuation: What an excellent innovation this is! Ibn Jarir said: Originator of the heavens and the earth is their Creator, and it is a verb that is changed to a verb, just as the painful is changed to the painful, and the hearer is changed to the hearer. The meaning of the creator is the originator and the originator, that which no one precedes him in creating and innovating like it. He said: Therefore the innovator in religion is called an innovator because he innovates in it what no one else has preceded him in, and likewise every innovator in word or deed, in which no one preceded him, the Arabs call him an innovator. This includes the words of A’sha bin Tha’laba in praise of Hudha bin Ali al-Hanafi: He claims to say the words of the masters of men if they show him firmness or whatever he wants he innovates That is, He creates what He wills. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of the words, Glory be to God, is that He has a son, and He is the Owner of what is in the heavens and the earth, and all of them bear witness to Him by indicating His Oneness, and acknowledge His obedience, and He is their Creator, Maker, and Originator, without a root or example that they follow. This is an announcement from God to His servants that among those who bear witness to this is the Messiah, to whom they attributed his sonship to God, and an announcement from Him to them that the One who created the heavens and the earth without a root and without an example is the One who created the Messiah, Jesus, without a father by His power. This is good speech and a correct expression from Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. And the Almighty’s saying: And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. With this, the Almighty clarifies the perfection of His power and the greatness of His authority, and that when He decrees a matter and wants it to be, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ that is, once, and it is, that is, it exists, according to what He willed, as the Almighty said: His command, when He intends a thing, is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. And the Almighty said: Our command to a thing when We intend it is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. And the Almighty said: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. And the poet said: If he wants something, he just says to it, Be, and it is. He also pointed out that Jesus was created with the word Be, and he was, as God commanded him. God Almighty said: “The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.”
2:118: Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Rafi bin Huraymila said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, if you are a messenger from God as you say, then say to God and He will speak to us so that we may hear His speech. So God revealed in that regard from His saying: And those who do not know say, ‘Why does God not speak to us or a sign come to us?’ Mujahid said: And those who do not know say, ‘Why does God not speak to us or a sign come to us?’ The Christians said that it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. He said: Because the context is about them, and there is consideration in that. Al-Qurtubi narrated: Why does God not speak to us? That is, He addresses us with your prophethood, O Muhammad. I said: This is the apparent meaning of the context, and God knows best. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi bin Anas, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi said in their interpretation of this verse: This is the saying of the Arab infidels: Likewise said those before them like their saying, he said: They are the Jews and Christians, and this saying is supported by Those who say this are the polytheists of the Arabs. God the Almighty says: “And when a sign comes to them, they say, ‘We will not believe until we are given the like of that which was given to the messengers of God. God knows best with whom to place His message. Those who commit crimes will be struck by humiliation before God and a severe punishment for what they used to plot.” The verse. God the Almighty says: And they say, ‘We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.’ to His saying: Say, ‘Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?’ The verse. God the Almighty says: And those who do not expect to meet Us say, ‘Why are angels not sent down to us or why do we not see our Lord?’ The verse. God the Almighty says: Rather, each one of them wants to be given spread-out pages. And other verses indicating the disbelief of the polytheists of the Arabs, their arrogance, their stubbornness, and their asking for what they have no need for. It is only disbelief and stubbornness, as those who came before them from the nations of the People of the Book and others said, as God the Almighty says: “The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven - and they asked Moses even greater than that. They said, ‘Show us God plainly.’” The verse. God the Almighty says: And when you said, ‘O Moses, we will not believe you until we see God plainly,’ and the Almighty’s saying: Their hearts were alike, meaning the hearts of the polytheists of the Arabs were alike the hearts of those who came before them in disbelief, stubbornness, and insolence, as the Almighty said: Thus, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, ‘A magician or a madman.’ They enjoined upon one another to do so. And the Almighty’s saying: We have made clear the signs for a people who are certain, meaning that We have made clear the evidence of the truthfulness of the messengers, in a way that does not require another question or additional information for those who are certain, believe, follow the messengers, and understand what they brought from God Almighty. As for those whose hearts and hearing God has sealed, and whose sight He has placed a veil over, God said about them: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment.
2:119: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Shaiban al-Nahwi, Qatadah told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “It was revealed to me: ‘Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. ’ He said: ‘A bringer of good tidings of Paradise and a warner of the Fire. ’ And His saying: ‘And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire. ’ Most of them read it as ‘And do not ask’ with a damma on the ta’, as a report. In the reading of Abi ibn Ka’b, and ‘And do not ask’, and in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, ‘And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire. ’ Ibn Jarir transmitted it, meaning: We do not ask you about the disbelief of those who disbelieve in you, like His saying: ‘You are only responsible for conveying the message, and upon Us is the reckoning. ’ And like His saying, the Most High: ‘So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them. ’ The verse, and like His saying, the Most High: ‘We know best what they say, and you are not a compeller over them. So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat. ’ And similar verses. Others read: ‘And do not ask’ “About the companions of Hellfire” with the opening of the ta’ for prohibition, meaning: do not ask about their condition, as Abd al-Razzaq said: Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I wonder what happened to my parents. I wonder what happened to my parents. I wonder what happened to my parents?” Then the verse was revealed: And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire. He did not mention them until God Almighty took him. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, and they spoke about it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b in a similar manner. Al-Qurtubi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka’b. Al-Qurtubi said: This is like saying do not ask about so-and-so, meaning: he has reached beyond what you think. We mentioned in al-Tadhkirah that God revived his parents so that we believed in him, and we responded to his saying: My father and your father are in Hellfire. I said: The hadith narrated during the lifetime of his parents, peace be upon them, is not in any of the six books or others, and its chain of transmission is weak, and God knows best. Then Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told me, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Dawud ibn Abi Asim told me on his authority, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day: Where are my parents? Then this verse was revealed: ‘Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire.’” This is a mursal like the one before it, and Ibn Jarir rejected this statement narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b and others in that regard, because it is impossible for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to doubt the matter of his parents, and he chose the first reading. What he followed here is questionable, because it is possible that this was during his seeking forgiveness for his parents, before he knew about their matter, so when he knew that, he disavowed them and informed them that they were among the people of Hellfire, as this is proven in the Sahih. There are many similar and analogous narrations to this, but what Ibn Jarir mentioned is not necessary, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Falih bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, who said: I met Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, and I said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah as he is described in the Qur’an. O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good tidings, a warner, and a protection for the unlettered. And you are My servant and Messenger. I have named you Al-Mutawakkil. He is neither rude nor harsh nor loud in the markets. He does not repel evil with evil, but pardons and forgives. He will not take him until He establishes through him the crooked religion, by which they say, There is no god but God. He opens through him blind eyes, deaf ears, and sealed hearts. Al-Bukhari is the only one who narrated it. He narrated it in Al-Buyu’ on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sinan on the authority of Falih on his authority. His follower, Abdul Aziz ibn Abi Salamah, said on the authority of Hilal: And Saeed ibn Hilal said on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam. And he narrated it in the interpretation on the authority of Abdullah on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Hilal on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-Aas on his authority, and he mentioned something similar. So this Abdullah is Ibn Salih, as he stated clearly in the Book of Etiquette. And Ibn Masoud Al-Dimashqi claimed that he is Abdullah ibn Raja’. And Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in the interpretation of this verse from Al-Baqarah, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ayoub on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Bara’, on the authority of Al-Mu’afa ibn Sulayman on the authority of Falih on his authority, and he added: Ata’ said: Then I met Ka’b Al-Ahbar and asked him, and they did not differ on a single word except that Ka’b said in his interpretation: Blind eyes, deaf ears, and insincere hearts.
2:120: Ibn Jarir said: What is meant by His Most High’s saying: And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their religion is that neither the Jews nor the Christians, O Muhammad, will ever be pleased with you, so leave seeking what pleases them and agrees with them, and turn to seeking the pleasure of God in calling them to the truth with which God sent you. And His Most High’s saying: Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance of God is the [only] guidance’ means: Say, O Muhammad, that the guidance of God with which He sent me is the [only] guidance, meaning it is the straight, correct, complete, comprehensive religion. Qatada said regarding His saying: Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance of God is the [only] guidance, that is,... a dispute that God taught to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, with which they dispute with the people of misguidance. Qatada said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: A group of my nation will continue to fight for the truth, victorious, and those who oppose them will not harm them until the command of God comes. I said: This hadith is narrated in Sahih on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have from God neither protector nor helper. This is a severe threat and warning to the nation against following the ways of the Jews and Christians after what they have learned from the Qur’an and Sunnah. We seek refuge with God from that, for the address is to the Messenger and the command is for his nation. Many jurists have used as evidence his statement, until you follow their religion, where he singled out religion to mean that all disbelief is one religion, like the statement of God the Almighty: To you be your religion, and to me mine. Based on this, Muslims and disbelievers do not inherit from each other, and each one of them inherits from his companion, whether he is from the people of his religion or not, because they are all one religion. This is the view of al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifah, and Ahmad in one narration from him. He said in another narration, like the statement of Malik, that people of two different religions do not inherit from each other, as came in the hadith, and God knows best. And his saying: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it with its true recitation. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah: They are the Jews and Christians, and this is the saying of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Sa`id said on the authority of Qatadah: They are the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim ibn Musa and Abdullah ibn Imran al-Isfahani told us, he said: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, Usamah ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab: They recite it with its true recitation. He said: When he comes to mentioning Paradise, he asks God for Paradise, and when he comes to mentioning Hell, he seeks refuge in God from Hell. Abu al-`Aliyah said: Ibn Mas`ud said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the true recitation of it is to make lawful what it makes lawful and to make unlawful what it makes unlawful, and to recite it as God revealed it, and not to distort the words from their places, and not to interpret anything of it other than its interpretation. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise, on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah and Mansur ibn al-Mu`tamir on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, he said: Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, said: They make lawful what He makes lawful and forbid what He forbids, and they do not distort it from its proper places. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar to that was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They act according to its clear verses and believe in its ambiguous verses, and they leave what is unclear to them to its All-Knower. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur`ah informed us, Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Ibn Abi Za`idah informed us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They recite it with its true recitation, he said: They follow it with its true following. Then he recited: And the moon when it follows it, meaning: follows it. He said: Something similar to that was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Ata`, Mujahid, Abu Razin, and Ibrahim al-Nakha`i. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Zubayd told us on the authority of Marra on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, regarding his statement: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed. Al-Qurtubi said: Nasr ibn `Isa narrated on the authority of Malik on the authority of Nafi` on the authority of Ibn `Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed. Then he said in its chain of transmission more than one of the unknowns, as mentioned by al-Khatib, except that its meaning is correct. Abu Musa al-Ash`ari said: Whoever follows the Qur’an will descend with it to the gardens of Paradise. On the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab: They are those who, when they pass by a verse of mercy, ask for it from God, and when they pass by a verse of torment, seek refuge from it. He said: This meaning has been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he passed by a verse of mercy, he would ask, and when he passed by a verse of torment, he would seek refuge. His statement: Those believe in it is report about those to whom We gave the Scripture, they recite it with its true recitation. That is: whoever among the people of the books revealed to the previous prophets established his book with its true establishment, believed in what I sent you with, O Muhammad, as God the Almighty said: And if they had established the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed from above them and from beneath their feet. The verse: Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to you from your Lord. That is: If you establish it with the true establishment and believe in it with the true belief and believe what is in it of the report of the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and attributes, and the command to follow him, support him, and assist him, that will lead you to the truth and to follow good in this world and the hereafter, as God the Almighty said: And if they had established the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed from above them and from beneath their feet. The verse: Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to you from your Lord. That is: If you establish it with the true establishment and believe in it with the true belief and believe what is in it of the report about the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and attributes, and the command to follow him, support him, and assist him, that will lead you to the truth and to follow good in this world and the hereafter, as God the Almighty said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel 10:13. God the Almighty also said: “Say, ‘Believe in him or do not believe.’ Indeed, those who were given knowledge before him - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration. And they say, ‘Glory be to our Lord! The promise of our Lord has surely been fulfilled.’” That is, if what we were promised regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is to be fulfilled, God the Almighty also said: “Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it.” Those will be given their reward twice for what they were patient and avert evil with good, and spend from what We have provided them.” God the Almighty also said: “And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered ones, ‘Have you submitted?’ For if they submit, then they are rightly guided. But if they turn away, upon you is only the conveyance. And God is Seeing of His servants.” For this reason God the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in it - then it is those who are the losers. God the Almighty also said: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties - the Fire is his promised destination. In Sahih: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one from this nation, Jew or Christian, hears of me and does not believe in me but that he will enter Hell.
2:121: Ibn Jarir said: What is meant by His Most High’s saying: And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their religion is that neither the Jews nor the Christians, O Muhammad, will ever be pleased with you, so leave seeking what pleases them and agrees with them, and turn to seeking the pleasure of God in calling them to the truth with which God sent you. And His Most High’s saying: Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance of God is the [only] guidance’ means: Say, O Muhammad, that the guidance of God with which He sent me is the [only] guidance, meaning it is the straight, correct, complete, comprehensive religion. Qatada said regarding His saying: Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance of God is the [only] guidance, that is,... a dispute that God taught to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, with which they dispute with the people of misguidance. Qatada said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: A group of my nation will continue to fight for the truth, victorious, and those who oppose them will not harm them until the command of God comes. I said: This hadith is narrated in Sahih on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have from God neither protector nor helper. This is a severe threat and warning to the nation against following the ways of the Jews and Christians after what they have learned from the Qur’an and Sunnah. We seek refuge with God from that, for the address is to the Messenger and the command is for his nation. Many jurists have used as evidence his statement, until you follow their religion, where he singled out religion to mean that all disbelief is one religion, like the statement of God the Almighty: To you be your religion, and to me mine. Based on this, Muslims and disbelievers do not inherit from each other, and each one of them inherits from his companion, whether he is from the people of his religion or not, because they are all one religion. This is the view of al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifah, and Ahmad in one narration from him. He said in another narration, like the statement of Malik, that people of two different religions do not inherit from each other, as came in the hadith, and God knows best. And his saying: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it with its true recitation. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah: They are the Jews and Christians, and this is the saying of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Sa`id said on the authority of Qatadah: They are the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim ibn Musa and Abdullah ibn Imran al-Isfahani told us, he said: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, Usamah ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab: They recite it with its true recitation.
