He said: When he comes to mentioning Paradise, he asks God for Paradise, and when he comes to mentioning Hell, he seeks refuge in God from Hell. Abu al-`Aliyah said: Ibn Mas`ud said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the true recitation of it is to make lawful what it makes lawful and to make unlawful what it makes unlawful, and to recite it as God revealed it, and not to distort the words from their places, and not to interpret anything of it other than its interpretation. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise, on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah and Mansur ibn al-Mu`tamir on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, he said: Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, said: They make lawful what He makes lawful and forbid what He forbids, and they do not distort it from its proper places. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar to that was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They act according to its clear verses and believe in its ambiguous verses, and they leave what is unclear to them to its All-Knower. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur`ah informed us, Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Ibn Abi Za`idah informed us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They recite it with its true recitation, he said: They follow it with its true following. Then he recited: And the moon when it follows it, meaning: follows it. He said: Something similar to that was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Ata`, Mujahid, Abu Razin, and Ibrahim al-Nakha`i. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Zubayd told us on the authority of Marra on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, regarding his statement: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed. Al-Qurtubi said: Nasr ibn `Isa narrated on the authority of Malik on the authority of Nafi` on the authority of Ibn `Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed. Then he said in its chain of transmission more than one of the unknowns, as mentioned by al-Khatib, except that its meaning is correct. Abu Musa al-Ash`ari said: Whoever follows the Qur’an will descend with it to the gardens of Paradise. On the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab: They are those who, when they pass by a verse of mercy, ask for it from God, and when they pass by a verse of torment, seek refuge from it. He said: This meaning has been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he passed by a verse of mercy, he would ask, and when he passed by a verse of torment, he would seek refuge. His statement: Those believe in it is report about those to whom We gave the Scripture, they recite it with its true recitation. That is: whoever among the people of the books revealed to the previous prophets established his book with its true establishment, believed in what I sent you with, O Muhammad, as God the Almighty said: And if they had established the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed from above them and from beneath their feet. The verse: Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to you from your Lord. That is: If you establish it with the true establishment and believe in it with the true belief and believe what is in it of the report of the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and attributes, and the command to follow him, support him, and assist him, that will lead you to the truth and to follow good in this world and the hereafter, as God the Almighty said: And if they had established the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed from above them and from beneath their feet. The verse: Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to you from your Lord. That is: If you establish it with the true establishment and believe in it with the true belief and believe what is in it of the report about the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and attributes, and the command to follow him, support him, and assist him, that will lead you to the truth and to follow good in this world and the hereafter, as God the Almighty said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel 10:13. God the Almighty also said: “Say, ‘Believe in him or do not believe.’ Indeed, those who were given knowledge before him - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration. And they say, ‘Glory be to our Lord! The promise of our Lord has surely been fulfilled.’” That is, if what we were promised regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is to be fulfilled, God the Almighty also said: “Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it.” Those will be given their reward twice for what they were patient and avert evil with good, and spend from what We have provided them.” God the Almighty also said: “And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered ones, ‘Have you submitted?’ For if they submit, then they are rightly guided. But if they turn away, upon you is only the conveyance. And God is Seeing of His servants.” For this reason God the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in it - then it is those who are the losers. God the Almighty also said: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties - the Fire is his promised destination. In Sahih: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one from this nation, Jew or Christian, hears of me and does not believe in me but that he will enter Hell.
2:122: A similar verse was mentioned at the beginning of the Surah and was repeated here to emphasize and urge people to follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whose description, name, command, and nation they find in their books. He warned them against concealing this and concealing what He bestowed upon them, and He commanded them to remember the blessings of God upon them, both worldly and religious, and not to envy their Arab cousins for what God had provided them with by sending the final Messenger from among them, and not to let that lead them to envy him for opposing him, denying him, and deviating from agreeing with him. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment.
2:123: A similar verse was mentioned at the beginning of the Surah and was repeated here to emphasize and urge people to follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whose description, name, command, and nation they find in their books. He warned them against concealing this and concealing what He bestowed upon them, and He commanded them to remember the blessings of God upon them, both worldly and religious, and not to envy their Arab cousins for what God had provided them with by sending the final Messenger from among them, and not to let that lead them to envy him for opposing him, denying him, and deviating from agreeing with him. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment.
2:124: God Almighty says, pointing out the honor of His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, and that God Almighty made him an imam for the people to follow in monotheism when he carried out what God Almighty charged him with of commands and prohibitions. For this reason, He said: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words meaning: And remember, O Muhammad, to these polytheists and the People of the Book who claim the religion of Abraham but are not upon it, but rather what he is upon is straight, you and those with you are believers, remind them of God’s test of Abraham, meaning: His testing of him with what He charged him with of commands and prohibitions so he fulfilled them meaning: He fulfilled all of them as God Almighty said: And Abraham who fulfilled meaning: and in all that was prescribed for him, he acted upon it, may God’s prayers be upon him. God Almighty said: “Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Him. * Grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. * And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. * Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham.” And God the Almighty said: “Say: ‘Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists. ’” And God the Almighty said: “Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was inclining toward truth, a Muslim [submitting to God], and he was not of the polytheists. Indeed, the people most deserving of Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who believe. And God is the ally of the believers.” And God the Almighty said: with words meaning: with laws, commands, and prohibitions. Words are used to mean predestined words, such as God the Almighty’s statement about Mary, peace be upon her: And she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures and was among the devout. And they are used to mean legal words, such as God the Almighty’s statement: And the word of your Lord was fulfilled in truth and justice. That is, His legal words, and they are either a statement of truth, or a request for justice if they were a command or a prohibition. And from that is this noble verse: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words, and he fulfilled them, meaning: he carried them out. He said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, meaning: a reward for what he did, as he carried out. By giving orders and leaving prohibitions, God made him a role model for people, and an imam to be followed and emulated. There is a difference of opinion regarding the specific words with which God tested Abraham, peace be upon him. Narrations were narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that Ibn Abbas said: God tested him with rituals. Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i narrated it likewise on the authority of al-Tamimi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abdul Razzaq also said, Muammar told us on the authority of Ibn Tawus on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, ‘And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words,’ he said: He tested him with purity, five for the head and five for the body. On the head, trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, inhaling water from the nose, using the siwak, and parting the hair. On the body, trimming the nails, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, plucking the armpit hair, and washing traces of feces and urine with water. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, Abu Salih, and Abu Al-Jild. I say: Close to this is what was established in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Ten are from the fitrah: trimming the moustache, letting the beard grow, using the siwak, inhaling water from the nose, trimming the nails, washing the knuckles, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, and using water to clean the hair. I forgot the tenth, unless it was rinsing the mouth.” Waki` said: The reduction of water means istinja`. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “The fitrah is five: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the moustache, clipping the nails, and plucking the armpit hair.” And its wording is from Muslim. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A`la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Lahi`ah told me, on the authority of Ibn Hubayrah, on the authority of Hanash ibn Abdullah al-San`ani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to say in his interpretation of this verse: And when his Lord tried Abraham with commands, and he fulfilled them, he said: Ten are six for humans and four for the sacred places. As for those for humans, they are shaving the pubic hair, plucking the armpit hair, and circumcision. Ibn Hubayrah used to say: These three are one, as well as trimming the nails, trimming the moustache, using the siwak, and washing on Friday. And the four that are for the sacred places: Tawaf, running between Safa and Marwah, stoning the Jamarat, and Ifadah. Dawud bin Abi Hind said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: No one was tested with this religion and fulfilled it completely except Abraham. God Almighty said: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands, and he fulfilled them. I said to him: What are the commands that God tested Abraham with and he fulfilled them? He said: Islam is thirty arrows, ten of which are verses in Bara’ah: The repentant, the worshippers to the end of the verse, and ten verses at the beginning of Surah: The believers have succeeded, and A questioner asked about a punishment to come, and ten verses in al-Ahzab 33:Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women to the end of the verse. So he completed them all, so Bara’ah was written for him. God said: And Abraham who fulfilled This is how Al-Hakim, Abu Ja’far Ibn Jarir, and Abu Muhammad Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with their chains of transmission to Dawud Ibn Abi Hind. This is the wording of Ibn Abi Hatim. Muhammad Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abi Muhammad on the authority of Sa’id or Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The words with which God tested Abraham and he completed them: Separation from his people for the sake of God when he was commanded to leave them, and his argument with Nimrod for the sake of God when he made him stand up to the danger of the matter in which he disagreed, and his patience in being thrown into the fire to burn him for the sake of God despite the horror of that from their matter, and the emigration after that from his homeland and country for the sake of God when he was commanded to leave. About them and what he was commanded to do of hospitality and patience with it with himself and his money, and what he was afflicted with of slaughtering his son when he was commanded to slaughter him, and when he went through with that from God and made him sincere in the affliction, God said to him: Submit, he said I submit to the Lord of the worlds despite what had happened of disagreement and separation from the people. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja informed us, Ismail bin Aliyah informed us, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan, meaning Al-Basri, And when his Lord tested Abraham with commands, and he fulfilled them, he said: He tested him with a star, so He was pleased with him, and He tested him with the moon, so He was pleased with him, and He tested him with the sun, so He was pleased with him, and He tested him with the migration, so He was pleased with him, and He tested him with circumcision, so He was pleased with him, and He tested him with his son, so He was pleased with him. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr bin Muadh informed us, Yazid bin Zari’ informed us, Saeed informed us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Al-Hasan used to say: By God, He tested him with a matter, so he was patient with it. He tested him with the star, the sun, and the moon, so he did well in that and knew that his Lord is eternal and will not cease, so he turned his face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists. Then He tested him with the migration, so he left his country and his people until he reached Ash-Sham, migrating to God, then He tested him with the fire before the migration, so he was patient. And he tested him with the slaughter of his son and circumcision, so he was patient with that. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma`mar informed us from someone who heard al-Hasan say in his saying: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words, he said: God tested him with the slaughter of his son and with the fire and with the planet and the sun and the moon. And Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar informed us, Salm ibn Qutaybah informed us, Abu Hilal informed us from al-Hasan: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words, he said: He tested him with the planet and the sun and the moon, so he found him patient. And al-`Awfi said in his interpretation from Ibn `Abbas: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words, so he fulfilled them, among them: He said, ‘Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people,’ and among them: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, and among them are the verses concerning the ritual and the station that was made for Abraham and the provision that was provided to the inhabitants of the House, and Muhammad was sent in their religion. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah informed us, Shababah informed us from Warqa’ from Ibn Abi Najih on the authority of Mujahid, in the words of God Almighty: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands, and he fulfilled them, God said to Abraham: I am testing you with a matter, so what is it? He said: Will you make me a leader for the people? He said: Yes. He said: And from my descendants? He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. He said: Will you make the House a place of return for the people? He said: Yes. He said: And security? He said: Yes. He said: And make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You? He said: Yes. He said: And provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in God? He said: Yes, Ibn Nujayh said: I heard it from Ikrimah, so I presented it to Mujahid and he did not deny it. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it from other sources on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain commands, and he fulfilled them, he said: He was tested with the verses that came after it, Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people. He said: And of my descendants? He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain commands, he said: The words, Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, and His statement, And when We made the House a place of assembly for the people and a place of safety, and His statement, And take, from the station of Abraham, a place of prayer, and His statement, And We enjoined upon Abraham and Ishmael, the verse, and His statement, And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and Ishmael, the verse, he said: So all of that is from the words with which Abraham was tested. Al-Suddi said: The words With which his Lord tested Abraham: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You.” Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from among themselves. Al-Qurtubi said: In Al-Muwatta’ and others, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed that he heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab say: Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to be circumcised, the first to host guests, the first to clip his nails, the first to trim his moustache, and the first to grow gray. When he saw the gray hair, he said: What is this? He said: Dignity. He said: O Lord, increase my dignity. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Sa`d ibn Ibrahim on the authority of his father who said: The first person to preach from the pulpit was Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Someone else said: The first person to shed the mail, the first to strike with the sword, the first to use a miswak, the first to clean oneself with water, and the first to wear trousers. It was narrated on the authority of Mu`adh ibn Jabal who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If I take a pulpit, my father Ibrahim took it, and if I take a staff, my father Ibrahim took it. I said: This is a hadith that is not proven, and God knows best. Then Al-Qurtubi began to speak about the legal rulings related to these things. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said, in sumMaryam 19:It is possible that what is meant by the words is all of what was mentioned, and it is possible that it is some of that, and it is not permissible to be certain that any of them is specifically meant except by a hadith or consensus. He said: There is no authentic report on that, transmitted by one person or transmitted by a group, which must be accepted. He said: However, two reports have been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a similar meaning. One of them is what Abu Kurayb narrated to us. Shadin bin Sa`d narrated to us. Zaban bin Fa`id narrated to me on the authority of Sahl bin Mu`adh bin Anas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Shall I not tell you why God called Abraham His friend, the one who fulfilled? Because he used to say every morning and every evening: ‘Glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. To Him be praise in the heavens and the earth and in the evening and when you reach the noonday.’” He said: The other is what Abu Kurayb narrated to us. Al-Hasan narrated to us on the authority of `Atiyyah. Isra`il narrated to us on the authority of Ja`far bin al-Zubayr on the authority of al-Qasim on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And Abraham who fulfilled. He said: Do you know what he fulfilled? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: And in the work of his day, four rak`ahs during the day. Adam narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah and `Abd bin Hamid on the authority of Yunus bin Muhammad on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated it, then Ibn Jarir began to weaken these two hadiths, and it is as he said: It is not permissible to narrate them except by clarifying their weakness, and their weakness is from many aspects, because each of the two chains of transmission includes more than one weak narrator, along with what is in the text of the hadith that indicates its weakness, and God knows best. Then Ibn Jarir said: If someone were to say: What Mujahid, Abu Salih, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said is more correct than what others said, it would be a school of thought, because his statement: Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people and his statement: And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, saying, 'Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf' and the rest of the verses that are similar to that are like the statement of the words that God mentioned that He tested Abraham with, I say: What he said firstly, that the words include all that was mentioned, is stronger than what he permitted from the statement of Mujahid and those who said the like of it, because the context indicates something other than what they said, and God knows best. And his saying: And of my descendants, he said: My covenant shall not include the wrongdoers. When God made Abraham an Imam, he asked God that the Imams after him be from his descendants, and He responded to that and informed him that there would be wrongdoers from his descendants and that God’s covenant would not include them and they would not be Imams, so they would not be followed. The evidence that his request was responded to is the saying of God the Almighty in Surat al-Ankabut 29:And We made among his descendants prophethood and the Book. So every prophet that God sent, and every book that God revealed after Abraham, was in his descendants, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. As for the saying of God the Almighty: He said, ‘My covenant shall not include the wrongdoers,’ they differed on that. Khasif said on the authority of Mujahid regarding His saying: He said, ‘My covenant shall not include the wrongdoers,’ he said: There will be wrongdoers among your descendants. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: He said, ‘My covenant shall not include the wrongdoers,’ he said: I will not have an unjust Imam. In another narration: I will not make an unjust Imam to be followed. Sufyan said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid regarding the words of God the Almighty: “He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers,” he said: There will be no unjust leader to be followed. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Malik bin Ismail told us, Sharik told us on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid regarding his words: And of my descendants, he said: As for whoever among them is righteous, I will make him an imam to be followed, but as for whoever is unjust, no, not even a blessing. Saeed bin Jubair said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers, what is meant by it is the polytheist, there will be no unjust imam, he says there will be no polytheist imam. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’, he said: Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people, he said: And of my descendants, so he refused to make an unjust imam from his descendants. I said to Ata’, what was his covenant? He said his command, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr bin Thawr Al-Qaysari informed us in what he wrote to me, Al-Faryabi informed us, Ismail informed us, Samak bin Harb informed us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God said to Abraham, I will make you an imam for the people. He said, And from my descendants? He refused to do so, then He said, My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Saeed or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He said, “And from my descendants? He said, My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. He informs him that there will be among his descendants a wrongdoer who will not be entitled to his covenant and he should not be given any of his command, even if he is from the descendants of his friend, and a doer of good in whom his call will be carried out and what he wanted from his request will be achieved. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, My covenant does not include the wrongdoers, meaning: There is no covenant for a wrongdoer upon you in his wrongdoing that you obey him in it. Ibn Jarir said, Ishaq told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Muslim al-Awar, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, My covenant does not include the wrongdoers, meaning, there is no covenant for the wrongdoers, and if you make a covenant with him, he will break it. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ata’, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, who said, There is no covenant for the wrongdoer. Abd al-Razzaq said, Muammar told us on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His statement, My covenant does not include the wrongdoers, he said, “The covenant of God in the Hereafter does not include the wrongdoers. As for this world, the wrongdoer has reached it, so he believed in it, ate, and lived.” Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Ata’, and Ikrimah said the same. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said, The covenant of God that He has made with His servants is His religion, meaning, His religion does not include the wrongdoers. Do you not see that He said, And We blessed him and Isaac, and among their descendants are those who do good and those who are clearly wrongdoers to themselves. He says, Not all of your descendants, O Ibrahim, are on the truth. This was also narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ata’, and Muqatil bin Hayyan. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, No enemy of Mine who disobeys Me will attain My obedience, and I do not grant it to anyone except a friend who obeys Me. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad bin Hamid told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Saeed Al-Asadi told us, Salim bin Saeed Al-Damaghani told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saad bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Sulami, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: My covenant does not include the oppressors, meaning there is no obedience except in what is right. Al-Suddi said: My covenant does not include the oppressors, meaning my covenant is my prophethood. These are the statements of the commentators of the Salaf regarding this verse, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, may God Almighty have mercy on them. Ibn Jarir chose that this verse, although it is clear in the report that God’s covenant of leadership does not include an oppressor, contains information from God to Abraham, peace be upon him, that there will be among your descendants those who are oppressors to themselves, as mentioned previously by Mujahid and others. And God knows best. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad Al-Maliki said: The oppressor is not fit to be a caliph, a ruler, a mufti, a witness, or a narrator.
2:125: And when We made the House a place of assembly for the people and a place of safety. And take, [O Muhammad], the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer. Al-Awfi said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the Almighty’s statement: And when We made the House a place of return for mankind, meaning: They do not satisfy their desire in it, they come to it and then return to their families and then return to it. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A place of return for mankind, meaning they return. Both were narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when We made the House a place of return for mankind, he said: They return to it and then go back. He said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah and Saeed bin Jubayr, in one narration, and Ata’, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Atiyah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Al-Dahhak, something similar to that. Ibn Jarir said: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told me, Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, he said: Abu Amr, meaning Al-Awza’i, said: Abdah bin Abi Lubabah told me regarding the words of God Almighty: And when We made the House a place of return for mankind, he said: No one turns away from it, and he thinks that he has had his fill of it. Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, he said: Ibn Zayd said: And when We made the House a place of return for mankind, he said: They return to it from all countries and come to it. How beautiful is what the poet said in this meaning, Al-Qurtubi included it: Make the house a place of rest for them, not a place where they can spend their time. Saeed ibn Jubayr said in the other narration, and Ikrimah, Qatadah and Ata’ al-Khurasani said, A place of assembly for the people, meaning a gathering place, and security. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning security for the people. Abu Jaafar al-Razi said, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: And when We made the House a place of assembly for the people and a place of security, meaning security from the enemy and that weapons should be placed in it. In the pre-Islamic period, people would be snatched from around them while they were safe and not being abused. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ata’, As-Suddi, Qatadah and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, who said: Whoever enters it is safe. The meaning of what these imams interpreted this verse with is that God Almighty mentions the honor of the House and what He has described it with in law and destiny, from it being a place of assembly for people, meaning He has made it a place that souls yearn for and yearn for, and they do not satisfy their desire from it even if they visit it every year in response from God Almighty to the supplication of His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, in His saying: So make the hearts of the people yearn toward them, until He said: Our Lord, and accept the supplication. And God Almighty describes it as having made it safe for whoever enters it to be safe, and if he had done what he did and then entered it, he would have been safe. And Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: A man would meet the killer of his father or brother in it, and he would not be exposed to him, as described in Surat al-Ma’idah in His saying: God has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of support for people, meaning He would ward off evil from them because of their glorification of it, as Ibn Abbas said: If people did not perform Hajj to this House, God would have collapsed the sky on the earth. And this honor is only due to the honor of its builder first, who is the friend of the Most Merciful, as God Almighty said: And when We appointed for Abraham a place The House that you do not associate anything with Me. And God Almighty said: “Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In it are clear signs - the Station of Abraham. And whoever enters it shall be safe.” In this noble verse, He pointed out the Station of Abraham and commanded us to pray near it. He said: And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. The commentators differed about what is meant by the Station. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Shaiba al-Numairi told us, Abu Khalaf told us, meaning Abdullah ibn Isa, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. He said: The Station of Abraham is the entire Sanctuary. A similar narration was narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’, and he also said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah told us, Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked Ata’ about And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. He said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: As for the Station of Abraham mentioned here, it is this Station of Abraham which is in the mosque. Then he said: The Station of Abraham is considered much like the Station of Abraham of the entire Hajj. Then Ata’ explained it to me and said: The definition and two prayers at Arafat, and al-Mash’ar, and Mina, and the stoning of the Jamarat, and the Tawaf between al-Safa and al-Marwah. I said: Did Ibn Abbas explain it? He said: No. But he said the Station of Abraham is the entire Hajj. I said: Did you hear that for all of this? He said: Yes, I heard it from him. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Abdullah bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. He said: The stone is the station of Abraham, the Prophet of God, whom God made a mercy. He used to stand on it and hand Ismail the stones to him. If he had washed his head, as they say, his feet would have been torn apart. Al-Suddi said: The station is the stone that Ismail’s wife placed under the feet of Abraham until she washed his head. Al-Qurtubi narrated it and declared it weak, but others preferred it. Al-Razi narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, he heard Jabir narrating about the pilgrimage of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the circumambulation, Umar said to him: Is this the station of our father? He said: Yes. He said: Should we not take it as a place of prayer? Then God the Almighty revealed, And take, [O Muhammad], the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer. Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, who said: Umar said: I said: O Messenger of God, is this the standing place of our Lord’s friend? He said: Yes. He said: Should we not take it as a place of prayer? Then, And take, [O Muhammad], the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer was revealed. Ibn Mardawayh said: Du’laj ibn Ahmad told us, Ghailan ibn Abd al-Samad told us, Masruq ibn al-Marzban told us, Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he passed by the standing place of Abraham and said: O Messenger of God, should we not stand at the standing place of our Lord’s friend? He said: Yes. He said: Should we not take it as a place of prayer? It was not long before the verse And take, from the station of Abraham, a place of prayer was revealed. Ibn Mardawayh said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Qazwini told us, Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, al-Junayd told us, Hisham ibn Khalid told us, al-Walid told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood at the station of Abraham on the day of the conquest of Mecca, Umar said to him: O Messenger of God, is this the station of Abraham about which God said: And take, from the station of Abraham, a place of prayer. He said: Yes. Al-Walid said: I said to Malik: Is this how he told you and they took? He said: Yes, this is how it appears in this narration, and it is strange. Al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Al-Walid ibn Muslim something similar to it. Al-Bukhari said: Chapter on his statement, And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, a place of rest where they will return and where they will be rewarded. Musaddad told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab said: I agreed with my Lord on three things, or my Lord agreed with me on three things. I said: O Messenger of God, if you took the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, then And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer was revealed. I said: O Messenger of God, the righteous and the wicked enter upon you, so why don’t you command the mothers of the believers to wear the hijab? Then God revealed the verse of the hijab. He said: I was informed that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had reprimanded some of his wives, so I went to them and said: Either you stop or God will replace you with better wives than you, until one of his wives came and said: O Umar, is there not in the Messenger of God what he can admonish his wives for you to admonish them? So God revealed: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, Muslims (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Abi Maryam said: Yahya ibn Ayoub informed us, Hamid told me, he said: I heard Anas from Umar may God be pleased with them both, this is how Al-Bukhari narrated it here, and he suspended the second chain of transmission from his sheikh Saeed ibn Al-Hakam, known as Ibn Abi Maryam Al-Masry, and Al-Bukhari was the only one who narrated from him from among the authors of the six books, and the rest narrated from him through an intermediary, and his purpose in suspending this chain of transmission was to show the connection of the chain of transmission of the hadith, and he did not support it because there is something wrong with Abu Ayoub Al-Ghafiqi, as Imam Ahmad said about him: he has a poor memory, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Humayd told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I agreed with my Lord, the Almighty, in three matters. I said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer? Then the verse And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer was revealed. I said: O Messenger of God, the righteous and the wicked enter upon your women, so why don’t you order them to cover themselves? Then the verse of hijab was revealed. The wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered around him in jealousy, so I said to them: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. Then the verse was revealed in the same way. Then Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Yahya and Ibn Abi Uday, both of them on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Umar, that he said: I agreed with my Lord in three matters, or my Lord agreed with me in three matters, and he mentioned it. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Umar, Ibn Awn, Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Ahmad ibn Mani’, Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Al-Sabah, all of them on the authority of Hisham ibn Bashir. It was also narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abd bin Hamid, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Munhal, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah and Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Hannad, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Za’idah, both of them on the authority of Hamid, who is the son of Tirwayh Al-Tawil, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. It was narrated by Imam Ali bin Al-Madini on the authority of Zaid bin Zari’, on the authority of Hamid, on his authority, and he said: This is from the authentic hadith, and he is from Basra. It was narrated by Imam Muslim bin Hajjaj in his Sahih with another chain of transmission and different wording, and he said: Uqbah bin Makram told us, Saeed bin Amir told us, on the authority of Juwayriyah bin Asma’, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I agreed with my Lord in three matters: regarding the veil, regarding the prisoners of Badr, and regarding the Station of Abraham. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Ansari told us, Hamid al-Tawil told us on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: My Lord agreed with me on three matters, or I agreed with my Lord on three matters. I said, O Messenger of God, if you took the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, then the verse And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer was revealed. I said, O Messenger of God, if women were veiled, then the verse of veiling was revealed. The third: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy died, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to pray over him. I said, O Messenger of God, will you pray over this infidel hypocrite? He said: Leave me alone, O Ibn Al-Khattab! Then the verse was revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. This chain of transmission is also sound, and there is no contradiction between this and that, rather both are sound and the implication of the number, if it is contradicted by an explicit statement, is given precedence over it. And God knows best. Ibn Jurayj said: Ja’far informed me, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked three times and walked four until he finished, he went to the Station of Abraham and prayed two rak’ahs behind it, then he recited: And take, [O Muhammad], from the Station of Abraham a place of prayer. Ibn Jarir said: Yusuf ibn Salman informed us, Hatim ibn Ismail informed us, Ja’far ibn Muhammad informed us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, touched the corner, walked three times and walked four, then he went to the Station of Abraham and recited: And take, [O Muhammad], from the Station of Abraham a place of prayer. He placed the Station between him and the House, and prayed two rak’ahs. This is part of the long hadith that Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Hatim ibn Ismail, and Al-Bukhari narrated with his chain of transmission. On the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, he said: I heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and circumambulated the House seven times and prayed two rak’ahs behind the Maqam. All of this indicates that what is meant by the Maqam is the stone on which Abraham, peace be upon him, stood to build the Kaaba. When the wall rose, Ismail, peace be upon him, brought it to him so that he could stand on it and hand him the stones, which he would place in his hand to raise the wall. Whenever he completed one side, he would move to the other side and circumambulate the Kaaba, standing on it. Whenever he finished a wall, he would move it to the side next to it, and so on until the walls of the Kaaba were completed, as will be explained in the story of Abraham and Ismail in building the House, narrated by Ibn Abbas in Bukhari. The traces of his feet were visible in it, and this remained well-known and was known to the Arabs in their pre-Islamic period. For this reason, Abu Talib said in his famous poem, Lamiyah: And Abraham's footsteps in the rock were wet on his bare feet, without sandals. The Muslims realized this in it, as Abdullah bin Wahb said: Yunus bin Yazid told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab: Anas bin Malik told them, he said: I saw the station with his fingers, peace be upon him, and the soles of his feet, except that it was removed by the people wiping it with their hands. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr bin Muadh told us Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, they were only commanded to pray at it and they were not commanded to wipe it. This nation has taken on a burden that the nations before it did not take on. It has been mentioned to us that someone saw the trace of his heel and fingers on it, and this nation continued to wipe it off until it was worn away and erased. I said This station was attached to the wall of the Kaaba in ancient times, and its location is known today, next to the door, next to the Black Stone, to the right of the one entering the door, in the separate spot there. When Abraham, peace be upon him, finished building the House, he placed it next to the wall of the Kaaba, or he finished building there and left it there. For this reason, and God knows best, he ordered prayer there upon finishing circumambulation. It was appropriate for it to be next to the Station of Abraham, where the construction of the Kaaba ended. It was only the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who was one of the guided imams and rightly-guided caliphs whom we were ordered to follow, who moved it away from the wall of the Kaaba. He is one of the two men about whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Follow the example of those who come after me, Abu Bakr and Umar. He is the one upon whose death the Qur’an was revealed in prayer next to him. For this reason, none of his companions, may God be pleased with them all, denied that. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: He told me: Ata and others of our companions said: The first thing that was transmitted was by Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. Abd al-Razzaq also said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hamid al-Araj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The first to move the Maqam to its current location was Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Bayhaqi said: Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Fadhil al-Qattan told us, Judge Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Kamil told us, Abu Ismail Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Salami told us, Abu Thabit told us, al-Darawardi told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: That the Maqam was attached to the House during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and during the time of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, then Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, moved it. This is a sound chain of transmission with what was mentioned above. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Umar al-Adani told us, he said: Sufyan said, meaning Ibn Uyaynah, who was the imam of the Meccans in his time: The Maqam was in the courtyard of the House during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then Umar moved it to its place after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And after his saying, And take, from the station of Abraham, a place of prayer, he said: The flood swept it away after Umar moved it from this location, so Umar returned it to it. Sufyan said: I do not know how much was between it and the Kaaba before it was moved. Sufyan said: I do not know whether it was attached to it or not. These narrations support what we have mentioned, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ibn Umar, who is Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Hakeem, told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab bin Abi Tamam, told us, Adam, who is Ibn Abi Iyas, told us in his interpretation, Sharik told us on the authority of Ibrahim bin Al-Muhajir on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab said: O Messenger of God, if we prayed behind the station, then God revealed, And take, from the station of Abraham, a place of prayer, so the station was near the House, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, moved it to this location. Mujahid said: Umar used to have an opinion and the Qur’an would be revealed according to it. This is a mursal from Mujahid, and it contradicts what was mentioned previously from the narration of Abd al-Razzaq from Muammar, from Hamid al-A’raj, from Mujahid: that the first one to postpone the Maqam to its current location was Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. This is more authentic than the chain of transmission of Ibn Mardawayh, with the support of what was mentioned previously, and God knows best. And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, Purify My House for those who go around it, and those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: His statement, And We enjoined Abraham and Ishmael, meaning: God commanded them to purify it from harm and impurity, and that nothing of that should touch it. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Ata’: What is His covenant? He said: His command. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said, And We enjoined Abraham, meaning: We commanded him to do so. He said: It appears that this letter is transitive with to because it means we preceded and inspired. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stay there, he said: from idols. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said, Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, meaning that that is from idols, obscenities, false speech, and filth. Ibn Abi Hatim said, and it was narrated on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair, Abu al-Aaliyah, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ata’ and Qatadah, Purify My House meaning, There is no god but God from polytheism. As for the Almighty’s statement, For those who circumambulate, circumambulating the House is well-known. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr that he said in the Almighty’s statement, For those who circumambulate, meaning whoever comes to it from a foreign land, and those who stay there, those who reside there. And thus it was narrated on the authority of Qatadah and al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, that they interpreted those who stay there as its people who reside there, as Saeed ibn Jubayr said. Yahya al-Qattan said on the authority of Abdul-Malik, he is Ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’ regarding his statement, and those who stay there, he said: Whoever visits him from the cities and stays with him and says to us, while we are neighbors, you are among those who stay there. And Waki’ said on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If he is sitting, then he is among those who stay there. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa ibn Ismail told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Thabit told us, he said: We said On the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair: I see myself as speaking to the Emir to prevent those who sleep in the Sacred Mosque, for they become ritually impure and urinate. He said: Do not do that, for Ibn Umar was asked about them and he said: They are those who are staying in seclusion. And Abd bin Hamid narrated it on the authority of Sulayman bin Harb on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on his authority. I said It has been proven in Sahih that the correct view is that Ibn Umar used to sleep in the mosque of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and he was single. As for the words of God the Almighty: And bowing and prostration, Wakee’ said on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And bowing and prostration, he said: If he is praying, then it is from bowing and prostration, and Ata’ and Qatadah said the same. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: The meaning of the verse is, And We commanded Abraham and Ishmael to purify My House for those who perform Tawaf. The purification that We commanded in the House is to purify it from idols and the worship of idols in it and from polytheism. Then he raised a question and said: If it is said: Was there anything of that which He commanded to purify before Abraham built the House near it? He answered in two ways: One of them that He commanded them to purify it from what was worshipped there at the time of the people of Noah of idols and statues, so that this would be a tradition for those after them, since God Almighty had made Abraham an imam to be followed, as Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said, Purify My House. He said: From the idols that they worship, which the polytheists used to venerate. I said This answer is based on the fact that idols were worshipped there before Abraham, peace be upon him, and proving this requires evidence from the infallible Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The second answer He ordered them to be sincere in building it for God alone, with no partner for Him, so they should build it purified from polytheism and doubt, as He, the Most High, said: Is he who lays his foundation on piety to God and His pleasure better, or he who lays his foundation on the brink of a crumbling precipice? He said: Likewise, His statement: And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, ‘Purify My House’ means build it purified from polytheism and doubt, as As-Suddi said: Purify My House build My House for those who circumambulate it. The summary of this answer is that God, the Most High, ordered Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, to build the Kaaba in His name alone, with no partner for Him, for those who circumambulate it, those who stay near it, and those who pray to it from bowing and prostrating, as God, the Most High, said: “And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], ‘Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who circumambulate it and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate’” 3:10. The jurists differed as to which is better, praying at the House or circumambulating it? Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: Circumambulating it is better for the people of the cities. The majority said: Prayer is absolutely better, and the direction of each of them is mentioned in the Book of Rulings, and what is meant by that is the response to the polytheists who used to associate partners with God at His House, which was founded on worshipping Him alone, with no partner for Him, and then despite that they turned away His believing people from it, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God and from the Sacred Mosque, which We have made for mankind, equal for the one who stays therein and the visitor. And whoever intends to do wrong therein - We will make him taste a painful punishment.” Then He mentioned that the House was only founded for those who worship God alone, with no partner for Him, either by circumambulation or prayer, so He mentioned in Surat Al-Hajj its three parts: its standing, bowing, and prostration, and He did not mention those who stay there because it was mentioned equal for the one who stays therein and the visitor. In this noble verse, He mentioned those who circumambulate and those who stay, and He was satisfied with mentioning bowing and prostration instead of standing, because He has known that there is no bowing or prostration except after standing. And in that also is a response to those who do not perform Hajj from the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, because they believe in the virtue of Abraham the Friend and Ishmael, and they know that he built this House for circumambulation during Hajj. And Umrah and other things, and for seclusion and prayer near it, and they do not do any of that, so how can they be following the example of Khalil when they do not do what God has prescribed for him? Moses, son of Imran, and other prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, performed Hajj to the House, as the infallible one who does not speak from his own desires informed us: It is only a revelation revealed. The meaning of the statement is: And We charged Abraham meaning We preceded with Our revelation to Abraham and Ishmael to purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stay there and those who bow and prostrate meaning purify it from polytheism and doubt, and build it purely for God, a fortress for those who perform Tawaf and those who stay there and those who bow and prostrate. Purifying the mosques is taken from this noble verse, and from the Almighty’s saying: “In houses which God has permitted to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein. He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings.” And from the Sunnah from many hadiths about the command to purify and perfume them and other things about protecting them from harm and impurities and the like. That is why he, peace be upon him, said: The mosques were built for what they were built for. I have collected a separate section on this, praise and thanks be to God. People have differed about the first one to build the Kaaba. Some have said: The angels before Adam. This was narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Baqir Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn al-Husayn. Al-Qurtubi mentioned it and narrated its wording, but it is strange. Others have said: Adam, peace be upon him. `Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of `Ata`, Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, and others: That Adam built it from five mountains: Hira`, Mount Sinai, Mount Zeitan, Mount Lebanon, and al-Judi. This is also strange. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, Ka`b al-Ahbar, Qatadah, and Wahb ibn Munabbih: That the first one to build it was Seth, peace be upon him. Most of those who mention this take it from the books of the People of the Book, which are not to be believed, denied, or relied upon on their own. However, if a hadith is authentic about that, then it is on the head and the eye.
2:126: And the Almighty said: And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day.' Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us: `Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed, Abraham made the House of God sacred and made it secure, and I have made Medina sacred, and what is between its two lava plains, so its game is not to be hunted and its trees are not to be cut." And thus it was narrated by al-Nasa’i on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Bandar, and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and `Amr ibn al-Naqid, both of them on the authority of Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri. Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa`ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, and Abu Kurayb told us, `Abd al-Rahim al-Razi told us, they all said: We heard Ash`ath on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s Messenger (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Ibrahim was the servant and friend of God, and I am the servant and messenger of God. Ibrahim made Mecca sacred, and I made Medina sacred, and what is between its two lava plains: its wood and its game. No weapon is to be carried in it for fighting, and no tree is to be cut down except for camel fodder.” This chain of transmission is strange and is not found in any of the six books. The origin of the hadith is in Sahih Muslim from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: When the people saw the first fruits, they would bring them to the Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him). When the Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) took them, he would say: “O God, bless us in our fruits, and bless us in our city, and bless us in our sa’, and bless us in our mudd. O God, Ibrahim is Your servant and friend and Your Prophet, and I am Your servant and Your Prophet. He called upon You for Mecca, and I call upon You for Medina with the same as he called upon You for Mecca, and the same with it.” Then he would call his youngest child and give him that fruit. In another version: Blessing with blessing. Then he would give him the youngest of the children who were present with him - the wording of Muslim. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Qutaybah ibn Sa`id told us, Bakr ibn Mudar told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Haad, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr ibn `Uthman, on the authority of Rafi` ibn Khadijan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ibrahim made Mecca sacred, and I make what is between its two lava plains sacred. Muslim alone transmitted it, so he narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Bakr ibn Mudar, and his wording is the same. In the two Sahihs, “On the authority of Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Talhah: Find me a young boy from among your boys to serve me. So Abu Talhah took me out with him, and I used to serve the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whenever he stopped. And he said in the hadith: Then he came forward until Uhud appeared to him, and he said: This is a mountain that loves us and we love it. So when he looked out over Medina, he said: O God, I make what is between its two mountains sacred just as Ibrahim made Mecca sacred. O God, bless them in their mudd and their sa`.” And in a wording of theirs: “O God, bless them in their measure, and bless them in their Al-Bukhari added, meaning the people of Medina. They also narrated from Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, make Medina twice as blessed as you made Mecca.” And from Abdullah bin Zaid bin Asim, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Abraham made Mecca sacred and supplicated for it, and I made Medina sacred as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I made supplication for it in its mudd and sa’ like what Abraham made supplication for Mecca.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and this is his wording. And from Muslim and his wording is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Abraham made Mecca sacred and supplicated for its people, and I made Medina sacred as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I made supplication for it in its sa’ and mudd like what Abraham made supplication for the people of Mecca.” And from Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “O God, Abraham made Mecca sacred and made it sacred, and I made Medina sacred between its two valleys, that no blood should be shed in it, no weapons should be carried in it for fighting, and no tree should be cut down in it except for fodder. O God, bless us in Our city, O God, bless our Saa’ for us, O God, bless our Mud for us, O God, make with the blessing two blessings.” The hadith, narrated by Muslim, and the hadiths about the prohibition of the city are many, but we have only mentioned those related to the prohibition of Abraham, peace be upon him, of Mecca, because of what is in that of the noble verse. And those who believed that the prohibition of Mecca was only on the tongue of Abraham the Friend held fast to it, and it was said: It has been prohibited since it was created with the earth, and this is more apparent and stronger, and God knows best. There are other hadiths that indicate that God the Almighty made Mecca sacred before He created the heavens and the earth, as stated in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: “God made this city sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was not permitted for me except for an hour of the day, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorns should not be cut, its game should not be frightened, its lost property should not be picked up except by one who knows it, and its solitude should not be found.” Al-Abbas said: O Messenger of God, except for the idhkhir, for it is for their udders and for their houses. He said: Except the idhkhir. This is the wording of Muslim, and they have something similar from Abu Hurairah. Then Al-Bukhari said after that: Abaan ibn Salih said, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Muslim, on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaibah: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say something similar. This that Al-Bukhari suspended was narrated by Imam Abu Abdullah ibn Majah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr, on the authority of Yunus ibn Bakir, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abaan ibn Salih, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yanaq, on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaibah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivering a sermon in the year of the conquest, and he said: “O people, God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred until the Day of Resurrection. Its trees shall not be cut, its game shall not be driven away, and its lost property shall not be taken except by one who announces it.” Al-Abbas said: Except for the idhkhir, for it is for houses and graves. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Except for the idhkhir. And on the authority of Abu Shuraih al-Adawi, that he said to Amr ibn Sa`id while he was sending out the missions to Mecca: “Give me permission, O prince, to tell you a statement that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the next day on the day of the conquest. My ears heard it, my heart retained it, and my eyes saw it when he spoke it. He praised God and extolled Him, then said: “Mecca has been made sacred by God and not by the people. It is not permissible for a person who believes in God and the Last Day to shed blood in it, or to cut down a tree in it, for one of the It was said to Abu Shuraih: What did Amr say to you? He said: I know that better than you, Abu Shuraih. The Sacred Sanctuary does not protect a sinner, a fugitive from blood, or a fugitive from ruin. Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, and this is its wording. If this is known, then there is no contradiction between these hadiths indicating that God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and the hadiths indicating that Abraham, peace be upon him, made it sacred, because Abraham conveyed from God His ruling concerning it and His prohibition of it, and that it had always been a sacred land before Abraham, peace be upon him, built it. Just as the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was written with God as the Seal of the Prophets, and Adam was still kneaded in his clay, and despite this Abraham, peace be upon him, said, “Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from among themselves” [al-Masjid an-Nabawi], and God answered his supplication with what He had previously known and decreed. That is why it is stated in the hadith that they said, O Messenger of God, tell us about the beginning of your affair. He said, “The supplication of my father Abraham, peace be upon him, and the good report of Jesus, son of Mary, and my mother saw as if a light came out of her that illuminated the palaces of Ash-Sham.” That is, tell us about the beginning of the appearance of your affair, as will come soon, God willing. As for the issue of preferring Mecca over Medina, as is the opinion of the majority, or Medina over Mecca, as is the opinion of Malik and his followers, it will be mentioned in another place with its evidence, God willing, and He is trustworthy. And the Almighty said, reporting from Abraham, that he said: My Lord, make this a secure city, meaning from fear, meaning that its people will not be terrified. And God did that by law and decree, as in His Almighty’s saying: And whoever enters it shall be safe, and His saying: Do they not see that We have made a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched all around them? and other verses. And the hadiths have come before regarding the prohibition of fighting in it. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: It is not permissible for anyone to carry weapons in Mecca. And he said in this Surah: My Lord, make this a secure city. That is, make this spot a secure city. This was appropriate because it was before the construction of the Kaaba. God the Almighty said in Surah Ibrahim: And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, make this city secure.’ This was appropriate there because, by God, it is as if the supplication occurred a second time after the construction of the House and the settlement of its people in it, and after the birth of Isaac, who was thirteen years younger than Ishmael. For this reason, he said at the end of the supplication: “Praise be to God, who has given me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.” And God the Almighty said: And provide his family with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day. He said: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b: “He said: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.” He said: This is the saying of God the Almighty. This is the saying of Mujahid and `Ikrimah, and it is what Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, corrected it. He said: Others read: “He said: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.” They made that part of the supplication of Abraham, as Abu Ja`far narrated on the authority of al-Rabi` on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah. He said: Ibn `Abbas used to say that, the saying of Abraham asking his Lord: Whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little.” Abu Ja`far said on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Salim on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little. He said: And whoever disbelieves - I will provide for him for a little. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When Abraham was removed from the call to the one whom God refused to give him authority, he was cut off from God and His love and separated from those who disobeyed his command, even if they were from his descendants, when he knew that there would be among them a wrongdoer whose covenant would not reach him, with God’s information to him about that, God said: And whoever disbelieves - then I will provide for the righteous and the wicked, and I will provide for him for a little.” Hatim ibn Ismail said on the authority of Hamid al-Kharrat on the authority of `Ammar al-Dahni on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn `Abbas regarding the words of God Almighty: My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with good things. The fruits of those who believe in God and the Last Day.” Ibn Abbas said: “Ibrahim used to restrict them to the believers, but not to the people. So God revealed: And whoever disbelieves, I will provide for them as I provide for the believers. Shall I create a creation for whom I do not provide? I will give them enjoyment for a little; then I will force them to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is that destination.” Then Ibn Abbas recited: “To each We provide, these and those, from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord is not forbidden.” Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. It was narrated from Ikrimah and Mujahid, something similar to that as well. This is like the statement of God the Most High: “Indeed, those who invent falsehood against God will not succeed. Enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment for what they used to disbelieve.” And the statement of God the Most High: “And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts. We will give them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment.” And His statement: “And had it not been that mankind would have become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses and stairways upon which they ascend. And for their houses, doors and couches upon which they will ascend.” They recline * and adornments. And indeed, all that is for the enjoyment of the life of this world and the Hereafter, with your Lord is for the righteous. And His statement: Then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination. That is, then I will force him after his enjoyment in this world and We will spread over him from its shade to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination. Its meaning is that God Almighty will look at them and give them respite, then He will seize them with the grip of the Mighty, the Powerful, as in His statement, the Most High: And how many a town was I granted respite while it was unjust? Then I seized it, and to Me is the destination. And in the two Sahihs: “No one is more patient with the harm he hears than God. Indeed, they attribute to Him a son, while He provides for them and heals them.” And in the Sahih also: Indeed, God grants respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then he recited the statement of the Most High: “And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are unjust. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.” And some of them recited: He said, ‘And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little.’ The verse, making it part of the supplication of Abraham, and it is an anomalous reading that contradicts the seven reciters, and the structure of the context rejects its meaning, and God knows best, for the pronoun in He said: It refers to God Almighty in the reading of the majority, and the context requires it. According to this anomalous reading, the pronoun in said refers to Abraham, and this is contrary to the order of speech, and God Almighty is the All-Knowing. As for the Almighty’s saying: “And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], ‘Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.’” The foundations are the plural of qa’idah, which is the pillar and foundation. The Almighty says: And mention, O Muhammad, to your people, Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, building the House and raising its foundations, and they were saying, “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” Al-Qurtubi and others narrated on the authority of Abi and Ibn Mas’ud that they were reciting, “And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], ‘Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.’” I said This is indicated by their saying after it, Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. The verse, so they were doing a good deed, and they were asking God Almighty to accept from them, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunais al-Makki on the authority of Wahib ibn al-Ward that he recited, “And when Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, were raising their foundations, [saying], ‘Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.’” The foundations of the House and Ishmael, our Lord accept from us.” Then he cries and says: O Khalil al-Rahman, the pillars of the House of the Most Merciful are being raised and you are afraid that it will not be accepted from you. This is as God the Most High narrated about the state of the sincere believers in His statement: And those who give what they give meaning they give what they give of charity, expenditures and offerings while their hearts are fearful meaning afraid that it will not be accepted from them, as came in the authentic hadith on the authority of Aisha on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as will come in its place. Some of the commentators said: The one who was raising the foundations was Ibrahim and the supplicant was Ishmael, and the correct view is that they were both raising and saying as will be explained. Al-Bukhari narrated here a hadith which we will quote and then follow it with related narrations.
