Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub Al-Sakhtiyani and Kathir bin Kathir bin Abdul Muttalib bin Abi Wada’ah - one of them adds more than the other - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The first time women used lanyards was before the mother of Ismail, who used lanyards to erase her traces on Sarah. Then Ibrahim brought her and her son Ismail while she was breastfeeding him, until he placed them near the House, near a tree above Zamzam at the top of the mosque, and there was no one in Mecca at that time, nor was there any water. So he placed them there and placed near them a bag of dates and a water skin with water. Then Ibrahim turned and went away, and Ismail’s mother followed him and said: O Ibrahim, where are you going and leaving us in this valley with no one to accompany us? And nothing? She said that to him repeatedly, but he did not pay attention to her. She said: Has God commanded you to do this? He said: Yes. She said: Then He will not let us down. Then she returned. So Abraham set out until he was at the pass where they could not see him, facing the House. Then he supplicated with these supplications and raised his hands, saying, Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, until he reached they give thanks. And the mother of Ismail began to suckle Ismail and drink from that water, until what was in the water skin was used up, she became thirsty and her son became thirsty, and she began to look at him writhing—or he said: floundering—so she set out, hating to look at him, and she found Safa to be the nearest mountain on earth to her, so she stood on it and then faced the valley to see if she could see anyone, but she did not see anyone. So she descended from Safa until she reached the valley, raised the edge of her armor and ran as a person struggles until she passed the valley, then she came to Marwa and stood on it and looked to see if she could see anyone, but she did not see anyone. She did that seven times. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, That is why people ran between them. When she approached Marwa, she heard a voice and said, Hush. She wanted herself - then she listened and heard also, so she said: I have heard if you have help, so behold, the king is at the place of Zamzam, so he searched with his heel, or he said: with his wing, until the water appeared, so she began to surround it and say with her hand like this, and she began to scoop from the water in her water skin and it was bubbling after she scooped, Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on the mother of Ismail, if she had left Zamzam - or he said: if she had not scooped from the water - Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.” He said: So she drank and breastfed her son, so the king said to her: Do not fear loss, for here is a house for God that this boy and his father will build, and God does not neglect His people, and the house was high above the ground like a hill, and the floods would come to it and take from its right and left, and it was like that until a group of Jurhum or a family of Jurhum passed by them coming from the road of Kada, so they stopped at the bottom of Mecca, and they saw a circling bird, so they said: This bird is circling On water, as we knew this valley and there was no water in it, so they sent one or two men running, and if they were at water, they returned and he informed them of the water, so they came. He said: And the mother of Ismail was at the water, so they said: Do you give us permission to stay with you? She said: Yes, but you have no right to our water. They said: Yes. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ishmael’s mother found that and she loved company. So they dismounted and sent for their people, so they dismounted with them, until there were some households there from them, and the boy grew up and learned Arabic from them, and they liked him and were pleased with him when he grew up. When he reached puberty, they married him to a woman from them, and Ishmael’s mother died. Abraham came after Ishmael had married to look at his estate, but he did not find Ishmael. He asked his wife about him, and she said: He went out seeking us. Then he asked her about their living and their condition, and she said: We are human beings, we are in hardship and difficulty. So she complained to him, and he said: When your husband comes, greet him and tell him to change the threshold of his door. When Ishmael came, it seemed as if he had sensed something, so he said: Has anyone come to you? She said: Yes, an old man of such and such came to us and asked us about you, so I told him. He asked me how we lived, so I told him that we were in hardship and difficulty. He said: Did he advise you about anything? She said: Yes, he ordered me to greet you and say: Change the threshold of your door. He said: That is my father and he ordered me to leave you, so go back to your family. He divorced her and married another woman from them. Ibrahim stayed away from them as long as God willed, then he came to them later and did not find him. He went to his wife and asked her about him. She said: He went out seeking us. He said: How are you? He asked her about their livelihood and their condition. She said: We are well and comfortable, and praised God the Almighty. He said: What is your food? She said: Meat. He said: What is your drink? She said: Water. He said: O God, bless them in the meat and water. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “And they did not have grain at that time. If they had, he would have prayed for it for them.” He said: So no one would be alone with them except in Mecca without agreeing to it. He said: So when your husband comes, greet him with my greetings and tell him to fix the threshold of his door. When Ismail came, he said: Has anyone come to you? She said: Yes, a well-mannered old man came to us, and she praised him. He asked me about you, so I told him. He asked me how we lived. I told him that I was fine. He said: Did he advise you about anything? She said: Yes, and he sends you his greetings and orders you to strengthen the threshold of your door. He said: That is my father and you are the threshold. He ordered me to hold you back. Then he stayed away from them as God willed. Then he came after that and Ishmael was sharpening his arrows under a tree near Zamzam. When he saw him, he went to him, and they did as a father does with his son and a son does with his father. Then he said: O Ishmael, God has commanded me to do something. He said: Do what your Lord has commanded you. He said: Will you help me? He said: And I will help you. He said: God has commanded me to build a house here, and he pointed to a high hill above what was around it. He said: Then they raised the foundations of the house, and Ismail began to bring stones and Abraham built, until when the building was high, he brought this stone and placed it for him, and he stood on it while he was building and Ismail was handing him the stones, and they were saying: Our Lord, accept from us, for You are the Hearing, the Knowing. He said: So they began to build until they circled around the house and they were saying: Our Lord, accept from us, for You are the Hearing, the Knowing. And Abd bin Hamid narrated it from Abd al-Razzaq in full, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Abdullah bin Hammad al-Tabarani, and Ibn Jarir from Ahmad bin Thabit al-Razi, both of them from Abd al-Razzaq in short. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ismail bin Ali told us, Bishr bin Musa told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Azraqi told us, Muslim bin Khalid al-Zanji told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Jurayj, on the authority of Kathir bin Kathir, who said: I, Uthman bin Abi Sulayman, and Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Husayn were with some people with Saeed bin Jubair at the top of the mosque at night, and Saeed bin Jubair said: Ask me before you do not see me, so they asked him about the station, and he began to tell them on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned the hadith in full. Then Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abu Amir Abdul Malik bin Amr told us, Ibrahim bin Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Kathir bin Kathir, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When what happened between Abraham and his family happened, he went out with Ishmael and Ishmael’s mother, and with them was a water skin. Ishmael’s mother began to drink from the skin, and her milk flowed over her child, until they reached Mecca. He placed them under a tree, then Abraham returned to his family, and Ishmael’s mother followed him until they reached Kada’. She called out to him from behind him: O Abraham, to whom are you leaving us? He said: To God. He said: So she returned and began to drink from the water skin and her milk flowed to her child, until when the water ran out she said: If I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone. So she climbed Safa and looked to see if she could sense anyone, but she did not sense anyone. When she reached the valley she ran until she reached Marwa and did that for seven laps until she completed seven. Then she said: If I went and looked what the child did. So she went and looked and saw that he was still in his condition as if he was gasping for death. Her soul could not be satisfied, so she said: If I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone. So she went and climbed Safa and looked and looked to see if she could sense anyone, but she did not sense anyone. When she reached the valley she ran until she reached Marwa and did that for seven laps until she completed seven. Then she said: If I went and looked what the child did. So she went and looked and saw that he was still in his condition as if he was gasping for death. Her soul could not be satisfied, so she said: If I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone. So she went and climbed Safa, and looked and looked, but she did not see anyone until she had completed seven days. Then she said: If only you had gone and looked, what would have happened? Then she saw a voice and said: Help, if there is any good with you. Then it was Gabriel, peace be upon him. He said: So he said with his heel: Like this, and he touched his heel on the ground, and water gushed forth. Umm Ismail was astonished, and she began to dig. He said: Abu al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you had left it, the water would have appeared. He said: So she began to drink from the water and her milk flowed to her child. He said: Some people from Jurhum passed by the valley, and they saw a bird as if they were unaware of that, and they said: Birds do not exist except on water. So they sent their messenger, and he looked and it was in the water. He came to them and informed them, so they came to her and said: O mother of Ismail, do you give us permission to be with you and live with you? Then her son reached puberty and married one of their women. He said: Then it occurred to Abraham, peace be upon him, and he said to his family: I am going to see my estate. He came and greeted them. He said: Where is Ishmael? His wife said: He went hunting. He said: Tell him when he comes: Change the threshold of your door. When she told him, he said: You are the one, go to your family. He said: Then it occurred to Abraham, peace be upon him, and he said: I am going to see my estate. He came and said: Where is Ishmael? His wife said: He went hunting. She said: Why don't you come down and eat and drink? He said: What is your food and what is your drink? She said: Our food is meat, and our drink is water. He said: O God, bless them in their food and drink. He said: Abu al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Blessing through the supplication of Abraham. He said: Then it occurred to Abraham, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to his family: I am going to leave my estate. So he came and met Ismail from behind Zamzam, fixing some arrows for him. He said: O Ismail, your Lord, the Almighty, has commanded me to build a house for him. He said: Obey your Lord, the Almighty. He said: He has commanded me to help you with it. He said: Then I will do it - or something like that - He said: So he stood up and Abraham began to build and Ismail handed him the stones, and they said: Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. He said: Until the building rose and the old man was too weak to carry the stones, so he stood on the stone of the station and began to hand it the stones and they said: Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. This is how it was narrated from these two sources in the Book of the Prophets. It is strange that Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Hakim narrated it in his book Al-Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm on the authority of Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz on the authority of Abu Ali Ubaid God bin Abdul Majeed Al-Hanafi on the authority of Ibrahim bin Nafi’ on his authority, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. This is what he said. Al-Bukhari narrated it, as you see, from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Nafi’, and it seems that there is an abbreviation in it, as he did not mention the matter of slaughtering. He said: It came in the Sahih that the horns of the ram were hanging from the Kaaba, and it came that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to visit his family in Mecca quickly on Al-Buraq, then he would return to his family in the Holy Land. And God knows best. Rather, it contains places that are attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which Ibn Abbas explicitly stated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, in this context that which contradicts some of this, as Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, they said: Muammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Haritha ibn Mudrib, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, he said: When Abraham was ordered to build the House, Ismail and Hajar went out with him. He said: When he arrived in Mecca, he saw above his head in the place of the House something like a cloud in it like a head, so he spoke to it and said: O Abraham, build in my shadow, or he said: according to my measure, and do not increase or decrease. So when he built, he went out and left Ismail and Hajar behind, so Hajar said: O Abraham, to whom do you entrust us? He said: To God. She said: Go, for He will not let us down. He said: So Ishmael became very thirsty. Hagar went up to Safa and looked, but saw nothing. She came to Marwa and saw nothing. Then she returned to Safa and looked, but saw nothing. She did that seven times, and said: O Ishmael, die where I will not see you. She came to him while he was prostrating his foot from thirst. Gabriel called her and said: Who are you? She said: I am Hagar, the mother of Abraham’s son. He said: To whom has He entrusted you both? She said: We entrust you both to God. He said: And you both to Kaf. He said: So the boy probed the ground with his finger, and Zamzam gushed forth and began to hold back the water. He said: Leave it, for it is a quencher. In this context, it is clear that he built the House before he left her. It may be possible that it was preserved that he first put a fence and a stone around it, not that he built it to the top, until Ishmael grew up, so they built it together, as God the Most High said. Then Ibn Jarir said: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara: That a man went to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: Will you not tell me about the House, is it the first House built on the earth? He said: No, but it is the first House built in the pool, the Station of Abraham, and whoever enters it is safe, and if you wish I will tell you how it was built: God revealed to Abraham to build a House for me on the earth, and Abraham was fed up with that, so God sent the Sakina, which is a strong wind with two heads, and one of them followed the other until it reached Mecca and rolled over the site of the House like the folding of a veil, and He ordered Abraham to build where the Sakina would settle, so Abraham built and the stone remained, so the boy went looking for something, so Abraham said: Find me a stone as I command you, he said: The boy went looking for a stone for him, so he brought it to him and found that he had installed the Black Stone in its place, he said: O my father, who brought you this stone? He said: It was brought to me by someone who did not rely on your construction. Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought it from heaven and completed it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Bishr ibn Asim, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar, who said: The House was a scum on the water forty years before God created the earth, and from it the earth was spread out. Saeed said: Ali ibn Abi Talib told us: Abraham came from the land of Armenia, and with him was the serenity guiding him to take up residence in the House as a spider takes up residence in a house. He said: Then it revealed stones that only thirty men could carry a stone, so I said: O Abu Muhammad, God says: And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House He said: That was later. Al-Suddi said: God Almighty commanded Abraham and Ishmael to build the House, Build My House for those who go around it, and those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate. So Abraham set out until he came to Mecca. He and Ishmael stood up and took up their pickaxes, not knowing where the House was. Then God sent a wind called the Khajuj wind, which had two wings and a head in the form of a snake. It revealed to them around the Kaaba the foundation of the first House. They followed it with pickaxes, digging until they laid the foundation. That is when God Almighty says: And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House, “And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House.” When they had built the foundations and reached the place of the corner, Abraham said to Ishmael: My son, find me a beautiful stone that I may place here. He said: O my father, I am lazy and ignorant. He said: I will do that. So he set out to find a stone for him, and he brought him a stone, but he was not satisfied with it. So he said: Bring me a stone better than this. So he set out to find a stone for him, and Gabriel brought him the Black Stone from India. It was white, a white ruby like a thujamah. Adam had brought it down from Paradise, but it had turned black from the sins of the people. Then Ishmael brought him a stone and found it at the corner. He said: O my father, who brought you this? He said: He brought it from someone who is more active than you, so they built and they were calling upon the words that Abraham tested his Lord with, so he said: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” In this context, there is evidence that the foundations of the House were built before Abraham, and Abraham was only guided to it and given it a place to live. Some have gone to this, as Imam Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House. He said, the foundations that were the foundations of the House before that. Abdul Razzaq also said: Hisham bin Hassan told us on the authority of Suwar, the son-in-law of Ata’, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, who said: When God sent Adam down from Paradise, his feet were on the ground and his head was in the sky, hearing the speech of the people of the sky and their supplications, and he was comforted by them. So the angels were afraid until they complained to God in their supplications and prayers, so God Almighty lowered him to the ground. When he lost what he used to hear from them, he became lonely, until he complained about that to God in his supplications and prayers, so he turned towards Mecca and the place of his feet was a village, and his steps A desert, until he reached Mecca, and God sent down a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, and it was in the place of the House now, and he kept circling it until God sent down the flood, and that ruby was lifted up, until God sent Abraham, peace be upon him, and he built it, that is the saying of God Almighty: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Ata’, he said: Adam said: I do not hear the voices of the angels, so he said: Because of your sin, but descend to the earth and build me a house, then surround it as you saw the angels surrounding my house that is in the heaven. And the people claim that he built it from five mountains: from Hira’, Mount Zayta, Mount Sinai, and al-Judi, and its suburb was from Hira’, so this was the building of Adam until Abraham, peace be upon him, built it later, and this is correct up to Ata’, but in some of it there is something strange, and God knows best. Abdul Razzaq also said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada, who said: God placed the House with Adam when God sent Adam down to Earth, and his descent was in the land of India, and his head was in the sky and his feet were on the earth, so the angels feared him, then it decreased to sixty cubits, and Adam was saddened when he lost the voices of the angels and their glorification, so he complained about that to God Almighty, so God said: O Adam, I have sent down a House for you to circumambulate as one circumambulates around My Throne, and to pray at it as one prays at My Throne, so Adam went to it, and he went out and stretched out his steps for him, so between every two steps there was a wilderness, and that wilderness did not cease after that, so Adam came to the House and circumambulated it, and after him from the prophets. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Humayd, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God placed the House on the four pillars of water before the creation of the world by two thousand years, then the earth was rolled out from under the House. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah ibn Abi Nujayh told me, on the authority of Mujahid and other scholars: When God designated the location of the House for Abraham, he went out to it from Syria, and Ishmael and his mother Hagar went out with him, and Ishmael was a small child who was being breastfed. And they were carried, as he told me, on Buraq, and Gabriel was with him, guiding him to the location of the House and the landmarks of the Sanctuary. Gabriel went out with him, and he would not pass by a village without saying: Is this where you were commanded, O Gabriel? Gabriel would say: Go with him, until he brought him to Mecca, which at that time was Udah, Salim and Samar, and in it were people called the Amalekites outside Mecca and its environs. And the House at that time was a red, muddy hill, so Abraham said to Gabriel: Was I commanded to place them here? He said: Yes, so he took them to the place of the Black Stone and settled them there, and he ordered Hajar, the mother of Ismail, to build a hut there, and he said: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House until His saying: that they may be grateful. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, Hamid informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: God created the location of this House two thousand years before He created anything, and its pillars are in the seventh earth. And Laith ibn Abi Salim said the same on the authority of Mujahid: The foundations are in the seventh earth. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father informed us, Amr ibn Rafi’ informed us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muawiyah informed us, on the authority of Abd al-Mu’min ibn Khalid, on the authority of Aliya ibn Ahmar: Dhul-Qarnayn came to Mecca and found Abraham and Ismail building the foundations of the House from five mountains. So he said: What do you have to do with my land? He said: We are two commanded servants, we were commanded to build this Kaaba. He said: Bring the proof of what you claim. Five rams stood up and said: We bear witness that Abraham and Ishmael were two servants who were commanded to build this Kaaba. He said: I am satisfied and I submit, then he left. Al-Azraqi mentioned in the History of Mecca that Dhul-Qarnayn circumambulated the House with Abraham, peace be upon him, and this indicates that he was an advanced man in his time, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him said: The Almighty’s saying: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House (Al-Qawa’id: 33). The foundations: its foundation, the singular of which is Qawa’id, and the singular of Qawa’id among women is Qawa’id. Ismail told us: Malik told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, that Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr told Abdullah bin Umar on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Did you not see that when your people built the House, they limited themselves to the foundations of Abraham? I said: O Messenger of God, will you not return it to the foundations of Abraham? He said: Had it not been for the recent disbelief of your people. Abdullah bin Umar said: If Aisha heard this from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I do not see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) leaving out touching the two corners next to the Black Stone, except that the House was not completed on the foundations of Abraham (peace be upon him). It was narrated in Hajj on the authority of Al-Qa'nabi, and in the Hadiths of the Prophets on the authority of Abdullah bin Yusuf and Muslim, on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya, and from the hadith of Ibn Wahb and Al-Nasa'i on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Qasim, all on the authority of Malik with it. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Nafi' who said: I heard Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Abi Quhafah, narrating to Abdullah bin Umar on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: "Had it not been that your people had recently converted from ignorance - or he said: from disbelief - I would have spent the treasure of the Ka'ba in the way of God, and I would have made its door in the ground and included the Black Stone in it." Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah bin Musa informed us on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Aswad, who said: Ibn Al-Zubayr said to me: Aisha used to tell you many secret hadiths, so what did she tell you about the Ka'ba? He said: I said: She told me: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Aisha, were it not that your people had recently converted to disbelief, I would have demolished the Kaaba and made two doors for it: one for people to enter through and one for them to exit through.” So Ibn al-Zubayr did so. Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it, and he narrated it like this in the Book of Knowledge of his Sahih. Muslim said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Yahya told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “Were it not that your people had recently converted to disbelief, I would have demolished the Kaaba and made it on the foundation of Abraham, for when the Quraysh built the House, they shortened it, and they would have made a successor for it.” He said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb told us, they said: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Hisham, with this chain of transmission, and Muslim is the only one to narrate it. He said: Muhammad ibn Hatim told me, Ibn Mahdi told me, Salim ibn Hayyan told us, on the authority of Sa’id, meaning Ibn Mina’. He said: I heard Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr say: My aunt, meaning Aisha, may God be pleased with her, told me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Aisha, if your people were not recent converts to polytheism, I would have demolished the Kaaba and leveled it with the ground, and I would have made an eastern door and a western door for it, and I would have added six cubits of stone to it, for the Quraysh had shortened it when they built the Kaaba.” This is also unique to him. He was transferred with them in the stones when he was thirty-five years old. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in the biography: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached thirty-five years of age, the Quraysh gathered to build the Kaaba, and they intended to do so in order to roof it and were afraid to demolish it, but it was only rubble above the height of a person, so they wanted to raise it and roof it. This was because a group of people had stolen the treasure of the Kaaba, which was in a well inside the Kaaba. The one who found the treasure was Duwaik, a client of Banu Malih bin Amr from Khuza’ah, so the Quraysh cut off his hand, and people claim that those who stole it placed it with Duwaik. The sea had thrown a ship to Jeddah belonging to a Roman merchant, and it was shattered, so they took its wood and prepared it to roof it. There was a Coptic carpenter in Mecca, so he prepared for them some of what would repair it. There was a snake that came out of the well of the Kaaba into which it threw what was given to it every day, and it would hang itself on the wall of the Kaaba, and it was one of the things they feared, because no one would approach it except that it would shake, scrape, and open its mouth. They feared her. One day, while she was standing on the wall of the Kaaba as she used to do, God sent a bird to her and snatched her away. The Quraysh said: We hope that God is pleased with what we want. We have a gentle worker and wood, and God has spared us from the snake. When they decided to demolish and rebuild it, Abu Wahb ibn Amr ibn Aaidh ibn Abd ibn Imran ibn Makhzum stood up and took a stone from the Kaaba, which jumped out of his hand until it returned to its place. He said: O people of the Quraysh, do not include in its construction anything from your earnings except what is good. Do not include in it the dowry of a prostitute, nor a sale based on usury, nor the oppression of any of the people. Ibn Ishaq said: People attribute these words to Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Makhzum. He said: Then the Quraysh divided the Kaaba, so the section of the door went to the Banu Abd Manaf and Zuhrah, and the area between the Black Corner and the Yemeni Corner went to the Banu Makhzum and tribes of the Quraysh. They joined them, and the back of the Kaaba belonged to Banu Jumah and Sahm, and the split in the stone belonged to Banu Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy, Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusayy, and Banu Adi ibn Kaab ibn Luayy, which is al-Hutaym. Then the people feared its demolition and were afraid of it, so al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said, I will start with you in demolishing it. So he took the pickaxe and stood over it saying, “O God, do not be afraid. O God, we only want good.” Then he demolished from the side of the two corners, and the people waited that night and said, “We will wait. If it is hit, we will not demolish anything of it, and we will return it as it was. If nothing is hit, then God is pleased with what we have done.” So al-Walid went to work that night, and he demolished and the people demolished with him, until when the demolition reached the foundation, the foundation of Abraham, peace be upon him, they came upon green stones like spears, some of which were attached to others. He said, Someone who narrates the hadith told me that a man from Quraysh who was demolishing it inserted a lever between two of its stones in order to remove one of them as well. When the stone moved, all of Mecca revolted, and they stopped that foundation. Ibn Ishaq said: Then the tribes of Quraysh gathered stones to build it, each tribe gathered separately, then they built it until the building reached the place of the corner, meaning the Black Stone, then they disputed about it, each tribe wanted to raise it to its place without the other, until they discussed and disagreed and prepared for battle, so Banu Abd al-Dar brought a bowl filled with blood, then they and Banu Adi bin Kaab bin Luay agreed to die, and they put their hands in that blood in that bowl and they called it the blood lick, so Quraysh remained like that for four or five nights, then they gathered in the mosque and consulted and divided equally, so some of the narrators claimed that Abu Umayyah bin al-Mughira bin Abdullah bin Amr bin Makhzum, who was at that time the oldest of all Quraysh, said: O people of Quraysh, make between you in what you disagree about the first one to enter through the door of this mosque to judge between you in it, so they did, and the first to enter was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when they saw him they said: This is the trustworthy one, we are satisfied, this is Muhammad. When he reached them and they told him the report, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bring me a garment. So it was brought to him, and he took the corner, meaning the Black Stone, and placed it in it with his hand. Then he said: Let each tribe take a corner of the garment and then lift it all together. So they did until they reached its place, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed it with his hand, then he built on it. The Quraysh used to call the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before the revelation came down, the Trustworthy One. So when they finished building and built it as they wanted, Al-Zubayr ibn Abdul Muttalib said, regarding the matter of the snake for which the Quraysh feared the construction of the Kaaba: I was surprised when the eagle aimed at the snake while it was in a state of agitation. It used to have a kesheesh and sometimes it used to have a thawb. If we set out to establish, the building will be feared and you will be afraid But when we feared the punishment, a punishment came pouring forth from it. Then she took her to herself and left us with a building without a veil. So we gathered to build our foundations and soil. Tomorrow we will raise the foundation from it and there will be no clothes on our faults The king honored the Banu Luay with it, so his origins are not lost to them. And Banu Adi gathered there, and once they were led by Kalb. So the king gave us honor for that, and he seeks reward from God. Ibn Ishaq said: The Kaaba was eighteen cubits high during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was covered with Coptic, then it was covered with brocade, and the first to cover it with brocade was Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf. I said It remained as the Quraysh built it until it was burned at the beginning of the emirate of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr after the year sixty and at the end of the reign of Yazid bin Muawiyah, when they besieged Ibn Al-Zubayr. Then Ibn Al-Zubayr demolished it to the ground and built it on the foundations of Abraham, peace be upon him, and inserted the stone into it, and made for it an eastern door and a western door attached to the ground as he heard that from his aunt Aisha, the mother of the believers, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It remained like that during the period of his emirate until Al-Hajjaj killed him, and he returned it to what it was by the order of Abdul Malik bin Marwan to do so, as Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, Ibn Abi Zaidah told us, Ibn Abi Sulayman told us on the authority of Ata’, who said: When the House was burned during the time of Yazid bin Muawiyah when the people of Ash-Sham invaded it, and what happened happened, Ibn Al-Zubayr left it. Al-Zubayr, until the people arrived at the season, wanted to form a party among them or seek their protection against the people of Ash-Sham. When the people left, he said: O people, advise me regarding the Kaaba, should I demolish it and then rebuild it, or repair what is damaged in it? Ibn Abbas said: I have a different opinion about it. I think that you should repair what is damaged in it, and leave a house that the people were safe upon, and stones that the people were safe upon, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent upon. Ibn Al-Zubayr said: If one of them had his house burned down, he would not be satisfied until he renovated it, so how about the house of your Lord, the Almighty and Majestic? I seek counsel from my Lord for three days, then I am determined to do my thing. When three days had passed, he decided to demolish it, but the people avoided it lest something from the sky descend upon the first person to ascend it. Then a man climbed it and threw stones from it. When the people did not see anything happen to it, they followed one another and demolished it until they reached the ground. Ibn al-Zubayr made pillars to cover them with curtains until its construction rose. Ibn al-Zubayr said: I heard Aisha, may God be pleased with her, say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Were it not that the people had recently converted from disbelief, and that I did not have the means to build it, I would have added five cubits of stone to it, and made a door for people to enter through, and a door for them to exit through.” He said: I find what I can spend, and I am not afraid of people. He said: So he added five cubits of stone to it until he showed it a foundation. The people looked at it, so he built the structure on it. The length of the Kaaba was eighteen cubits, but when he added to it, he shortened it, so he added ten cubits at the beginning and made two doors for it: one for entering through, and one for exiting through. And the other comes out of it. When Ibn al-Zubayr was killed, al-Hajjaj wrote to Abd al-Malik asking him to permit him to do so and informing him that Ibn al-Zubayr had put the building on a foundation that the just people of Mecca had seen. Abd al-Malik wrote to him: We are not against Ibn al-Zubayr’s taint in anything. As for what he added to its height, he approved it, and as for what he added of stones, he returned it to its building, and closed the door that he opened, so he demolished it and returned it to its building. Al-Nasa’i narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Hanad, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Za’idah, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He did not mention the story, and the Sunnah was an approval of what Abd God ibn al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, had done, because he was the one whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved. However, he feared that some people’s hearts would reject it because of their newness to Islam and their recent history of disbelief. However, this Sunnah was hidden from Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and for this reason, when it was confirmed on the authority of Aisha, she narrated it on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: We wished that we had left it. And he did not take over, as Muslim said: Muhammad bin Hatim told me, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, Ibn Jurayj told us: I heard Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair and Al-Walid bin Ata’ narrating on the authority of Al-Harith bin Abdullah bin Abi Rabi’ah, Abdullah bin Ubaid said: Al-Harith bin Abdullah delegated to Abdul Malik bin Marwan during his caliphate, and Abdul Malik said: I do not think that Abu Habib, meaning Ibn Al-Zubayr, heard from Aisha what he claimed he heard from her, Al-Harith said: Yes, I heard it from her. He said: I heard her say what? He said: She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your people have shortened the construction of the House, and were it not for the recent conversion to polytheism, I would have restored what they had left of it. If your people decide to rebuild it after me, then come and I will show you what they have left of it.” So I saw it was close to seven cubits. This is the hadith of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, and Al-Walid bin Ata’ added to it: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And I would have made two doors for it placed in the ground: one to the east and one to the west. Do you know why your people raised its door? She said: No. He said: To strengthen it so that no one would enter it except those they wanted. So when a man wanted to enter it, they would call him until he climbed up, until when he was about to enter, they would push him and he would fall. Abdul Malik said: So I said to Al-Harith: Did you hear her say that? He said: Yes. He said: So he poked it for a while with his stick, then he said: I wish I had left it and not carried it. Muslim said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Jabalah told us, Abu Asim H told us, and Abd ibn Hamid told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, both of them on the authority of Ibn Jurayj with this chain of transmission like the hadith of Abu Bakr. He said: Muhammad ibn Hatim told us, Abdullah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi told us, Hatim ibn Abi Saghira told us on the authority of Abu Qaz’ah: While Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was circumambulating the House, he said: May God kill Ibn al-Zubayr, for he lies about the Mother of the Believers. He said: I heard her say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Aisha, were it not for the recent disbelief of your people, I would have demolished the Kaaba so that I could add more stones to it, for your people have fallen short in building it. Al-Harith ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi’ah said: Do not say this, O Commander of the Faithful, for I heard the Mother of the Believers say this. He said: If I had heard it before I demolished it, I would have left it as Ibn al-Zubayr had built it. This hadith is as if it is definitely attributed to Aisha, because it has been narrated from her through multiple authentic chains of transmission on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Yazid, al-Harith ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. This indicates that what Ibn al-Zubayr did was correct, and if it had been left, it would have been good. But after the matter returned to this state, some scholars were reluctant to change its state, as was mentioned about the Commander of the Faithful, Harun al-Rashid, or his father, al-Mahdi, that he asked Imam Malik about demolishing the Kaaba and returning it to what Ibn al-Zubayr had done. Malik said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, do not make the Kaaba of God a playground for kings. No one wants to demolish it except that he demolishes it. Al-Rashid left that. It was narrated by Iyad and al-Nawawi. And it will remain like this - and God knows best - until the end of time until it is destroyed by Dhu al-Sawiqatain from Abyssinia, as was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Kaaba will be destroyed by Dhu al-Sawiqatain from Abyssinia. They both reported it. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, It is as if I see a black man with a hump, tearing it out stone by stone. Narrated by al-Bukhari. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Haranin informed us. Muhammad ibn Salamah informed us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahidin on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The Kaaba will be destroyed by Dhu al-Sawiqatain from Abyssinia, who will strip it of its ornaments and will strip it of its covering. It is as if I see…” To him, Asli’ Afid’a, who strikes it with his shovel and pickaxe - Fad’a: a deviation between the foot and the shin bone - and this, and God knows best, will only happen after the emergence of Gog and Magog, as it came in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They will perform Hajj to the House and Umrah after the emergence of Gog and Magog. And the Almighty’s saying, narrating the supplication of Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, “Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.” Ibn Jarir said: By that they mean, And make us submissive to Your command, submissive to Your obedience, and we do not associate anyone with You in obedience, nor in worship other than You. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ismail told us on the authority of Raja’ ibn Hibban al-Hasani al-Qurashi, Maqal ibn Ubayd God told us on the authority of Abd al-Karim, And make us Muslims [in submission] to You, he said: sincere to You, And from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You, he said: sincere. He also said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, al-Muqaddami told us, Sa’id ibn Amir told us on the authority of Salam ibn Abi Mut’i’ regarding this verse, And make us Muslims, he said: They were Muslims, but they asked him to be steadfast. Ikrimah said, Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You. God said, I have done so. “And from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You.” God said, I have done so. As-Suddi said, And from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. They both mean the Arabs. Ibn Jarir said, “The correct interpretation is that it includes the Arabs and others, because from the descendants of Abraham are the Children of Israel, and God the Most High said, “And among the people of Moses is a nation guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby.” I say, As-Suddi does not deny what Ibn Jarir said, because singling them out for that does not negate others, and the context is the Arabs, and that is why He said after it, Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. What is meant by this is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was sent among them as God Almighty said: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves. However, this does not negate his message to the red and the black, as God Almighty said: Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all,’ and other conclusive evidence. This supplication was made by Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, as God Almighty informed us about His pious and believing servants in His saying: And those who say, ‘Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous.’ This amount is desired by the Sharia, because part of the perfection of loving the worship of God Almighty is to love that there be from his offspring someone who worships God alone, with no partner. And for this reason, when God the Almighty said to Abraham, peace be upon him, Indeed, I will make you a leader for mankind, He said, And of my descendants. He said, My covenant does not include the wrongdoers, which is His saying, And keep me and my children away from worshipping idols. It has been proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he said, “When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him.” And show us our rituals, Ibn Jarir said on the authority of Ata’, And show us our rituals, he brought them out for us so that we may learn them. Mujahid said, Show us our rituals, meaning our slaughterhouses. Something similar was also narrated on the authority of Ata’ and Qatadah. Saeed bin Mansour said: Itab bin Bashir told us on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim said, Show us our rituals. Gabriel showed him to him and brought him to the House. He said, Raise the foundations. So he raised the foundations and completed the building. Then he took him by the hand and led him out and went with him to Safa. He said, This is one of the symbols of God. Then he went with him to Marwah. He said, This is one of the symbols of God. Then he went with him towards Mina. When he reached Aqaba, Satan was standing by the tree. He said, Say ‘Allahu Akbar’ and throw it. So he said, Allahu Akbar and threw it. Then Satan went and stood at the middle Jamarat. When Gabriel and Ibrahim passed by him, he said to him, Say ‘Allahu Akbar’ and throw it. So he said, Allahu Akbar and threw it. Then the evil Satan went away. The evil one wanted to include something in the Hajj, but he could not. So he took Ibrahim by the hand until he came to the Sacred Monument. He said, This is the Sacred Monument. So Ibrahim took Ibrahim by the hand and brought him to Arafat. He said, Do you understand what I showed you? He said it three times. He said, Yes. Abu Majlaz and Qatadah narrated something similar to this. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Abu al-Asim al-Ghanawi, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim was shown the commands of the rituals, Satan appeared to him at the Mas’a, so Ibrahim raced him, then Gabriel took him until he came to Mina. He said: This is the place where people stop. When he reached Jamrat al-Aqaba, Satan appeared to him, so he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. Then he brought him to Jamrat al-Qawwa, and Satan appeared to him, so he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. He brought him all together and said: This is al-Mash’ar. Then he brought him to Arafat, and he said: This is Arafat. Gabriel said to him: Do you recognize it?
2:127: And the Almighty said: And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day.' Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us: `Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed, Abraham made the House of God sacred and made it secure, and I have made Medina sacred, and what is between its two lava plains, so its game is not to be hunted and its trees are not to be cut." And thus it was narrated by al-Nasa’i on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Bandar, and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and `Amr ibn al-Naqid, both of them on the authority of Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri. Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa`ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, and Abu Kurayb told us, `Abd al-Rahim al-Razi told us, they all said: We heard Ash`ath on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s Messenger (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Ibrahim was the servant and friend of God, and I am the servant and messenger of God. Ibrahim made Mecca sacred, and I made Medina sacred, and what is between its two lava plains: its wood and its game. No weapon is to be carried in it for fighting, and no tree is to be cut down except for camel fodder.” This chain of transmission is strange and is not found in any of the six books. The origin of the hadith is in Sahih Muslim from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: When the people saw the first fruits, they would bring them to the Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him). When the Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) took them, he would say: “O God, bless us in our fruits, and bless us in our city, and bless us in our sa’, and bless us in our mudd. O God, Ibrahim is Your servant and friend and Your Prophet, and I am Your servant and Your Prophet. He called upon You for Mecca, and I call upon You for Medina with the same as he called upon You for Mecca, and the same with it.” Then he would call his youngest child and give him that fruit. In another version: Blessing with blessing. Then he would give him the youngest of the children who were present with him - the wording of Muslim. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Qutaybah ibn Sa`id told us, Bakr ibn Mudar told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Haad, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr ibn `Uthman, on the authority of Rafi` ibn Khadijan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ibrahim made Mecca sacred, and I make what is between its two lava plains sacred. Muslim alone transmitted it, so he narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Bakr ibn Mudar, and his wording is the same. In the two Sahihs, “On the authority of Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Talhah: Find me a young boy from among your boys to serve me. So Abu Talhah took me out with him, and I used to serve the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whenever he stopped. And he said in the hadith: Then he came forward until Uhud appeared to him, and he said: This is a mountain that loves us and we love it. So when he looked out over Medina, he said: O God, I make what is between its two mountains sacred just as Ibrahim made Mecca sacred. O God, bless them in their mudd and their sa`.” And in a wording of theirs: “O God, bless them in their measure, and bless them in their Al-Bukhari added, meaning the people of Medina. They also narrated from Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, make Medina twice as blessed as you made Mecca.” And from Abdullah bin Zaid bin Asim, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Abraham made Mecca sacred and supplicated for it, and I made Medina sacred as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I made supplication for it in its mudd and sa’ like what Abraham made supplication for Mecca.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and this is his wording. And from Muslim and his wording is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Abraham made Mecca sacred and supplicated for its people, and I made Medina sacred as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I made supplication for it in its sa’ and mudd like what Abraham made supplication for the people of Mecca.” And from Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “O God, Abraham made Mecca sacred and made it sacred, and I made Medina sacred between its two valleys, that no blood should be shed in it, no weapons should be carried in it for fighting, and no tree should be cut down in it except for fodder. O God, bless us in Our city, O God, bless our Saa’ for us, O God, bless our Mud for us, O God, make with the blessing two blessings.” The hadith, narrated by Muslim, and the hadiths about the prohibition of the city are many, but we have only mentioned those related to the prohibition of Abraham, peace be upon him, of Mecca, because of what is in that of the noble verse. And those who believed that the prohibition of Mecca was only on the tongue of Abraham the Friend held fast to it, and it was said: It has been prohibited since it was created with the earth, and this is more apparent and stronger, and God knows best. There are other hadiths that indicate that God the Almighty made Mecca sacred before He created the heavens and the earth, as stated in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: “God made this city sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was not permitted for me except for an hour of the day, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorns should not be cut, its game should not be frightened, its lost property should not be picked up except by one who knows it, and its solitude should not be found.” Al-Abbas said: O Messenger of God, except for the idhkhir, for it is for their udders and for their houses. He said: Except the idhkhir. This is the wording of Muslim, and they have something similar from Abu Hurairah. Then Al-Bukhari said after that: Abaan ibn Salih said, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Muslim, on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaibah: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say something similar. This that Al-Bukhari suspended was narrated by Imam Abu Abdullah ibn Majah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr, on the authority of Yunus ibn Bakir, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abaan ibn Salih, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yanaq, on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaibah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivering a sermon in the year of the conquest, and he said: “O people, God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred until the Day of Resurrection. Its trees shall not be cut, its game shall not be driven away, and its lost property shall not be taken except by one who announces it.” Al-Abbas said: Except for the idhkhir, for it is for houses and graves. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Except for the idhkhir. And on the authority of Abu Shuraih al-Adawi, that he said to Amr ibn Sa`id while he was sending out the missions to Mecca: “Give me permission, O prince, to tell you a statement that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the next day on the day of the conquest. My ears heard it, my heart retained it, and my eyes saw it when he spoke it. He praised God and extolled Him, then said: “Mecca has been made sacred by God and not by the people. It is not permissible for a person who believes in God and the Last Day to shed blood in it, or to cut down a tree in it, for one of the It was said to Abu Shuraih: What did Amr say to you? He said: I know that better than you, Abu Shuraih. The Sacred Sanctuary does not protect a sinner, a fugitive from blood, or a fugitive from ruin. Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, and this is its wording. If this is known, then there is no contradiction between these hadiths indicating that God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and the hadiths indicating that Abraham, peace be upon him, made it sacred, because Abraham conveyed from God His ruling concerning it and His prohibition of it, and that it had always been a sacred land before Abraham, peace be upon him, built it. Just as the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was written with God as the Seal of the Prophets, and Adam was still kneaded in his clay, and despite this Abraham, peace be upon him, said, “Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from among themselves” [al-Masjid an-Nabawi], and God answered his supplication with what He had previously known and decreed. That is why it is stated in the hadith that they said, O Messenger of God, tell us about the beginning of your affair. He said, “The supplication of my father Abraham, peace be upon him, and the good report of Jesus, son of Mary, and my mother saw as if a light came out of her that illuminated the palaces of Ash-Sham.” That is, tell us about the beginning of the appearance of your affair, as will come soon, God willing. As for the issue of preferring Mecca over Medina, as is the opinion of the majority, or Medina over Mecca, as is the opinion of Malik and his followers, it will be mentioned in another place with its evidence, God willing, and He is trustworthy. And the Almighty said, reporting from Abraham, that he said: My Lord, make this a secure city, meaning from fear, meaning that its people will not be terrified. And God did that by law and decree, as in His Almighty’s saying: And whoever enters it shall be safe, and His saying: Do they not see that We have made a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched all around them? and other verses. And the hadiths have come before regarding the prohibition of fighting in it. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: It is not permissible for anyone to carry weapons in Mecca. And he said in this Surah: My Lord, make this a secure city. That is, make this spot a secure city. This was appropriate because it was before the construction of the Kaaba. God the Almighty said in Surah Ibrahim: And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, make this city secure.’ This was appropriate there because, by God, it is as if the supplication occurred a second time after the construction of the House and the settlement of its people in it, and after the birth of Isaac, who was thirteen years younger than Ishmael. For this reason, he said at the end of the supplication: “Praise be to God, who has given me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.” And God the Almighty said: And provide his family with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day. He said: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b: “He said: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.” He said: This is the saying of God the Almighty. This is the saying of Mujahid and `Ikrimah, and it is what Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, corrected it. He said: Others read: “He said: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.” They made that part of the supplication of Abraham, as Abu Ja`far narrated on the authority of al-Rabi` on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah. He said: Ibn `Abbas used to say that, the saying of Abraham asking his Lord: Whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little.” Abu Ja`far said on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Salim on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little. He said: And whoever disbelieves - I will provide for him for a little. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When Abraham was removed from the call to the one whom God refused to give him authority, he was cut off from God and His love and separated from those who disobeyed his command, even if they were from his descendants, when he knew that there would be among them a wrongdoer whose covenant would not reach him, with God’s information to him about that, God said: And whoever disbelieves - then I will provide for the righteous and the wicked, and I will provide for him for a little.” Hatim ibn Ismail said on the authority of Hamid al-Kharrat on the authority of `Ammar al-Dahni on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn `Abbas regarding the words of God Almighty: My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with good things. The fruits of those who believe in God and the Last Day.” Ibn Abbas said: “Ibrahim used to restrict them to the believers, but not to the people. So God revealed: And whoever disbelieves, I will provide for them as I provide for the believers. Shall I create a creation for whom I do not provide? I will give them enjoyment for a little; then I will force them to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is that destination.” Then Ibn Abbas recited: “To each We provide, these and those, from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord is not forbidden.” Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. It was narrated from Ikrimah and Mujahid, something similar to that as well. This is like the statement of God the Most High: “Indeed, those who invent falsehood against God will not succeed. Enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment for what they used to disbelieve.” And the statement of God the Most High: “And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts. We will give them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment.” And His statement: “And had it not been that mankind would have become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses and stairways upon which they ascend. And for their houses, doors and couches upon which they will ascend.” They recline * and adornments. And indeed, all that is for the enjoyment of the life of this world and the Hereafter, with your Lord is for the righteous. And His statement: Then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination. That is, then I will force him after his enjoyment in this world and We will spread over him from its shade to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination. Its meaning is that God Almighty will look at them and give them respite, then He will seize them with the grip of the Mighty, the Powerful, as in His statement, the Most High: And how many a town was I granted respite while it was unjust? Then I seized it, and to Me is the destination. And in the two Sahihs: “No one is more patient with the harm he hears than God. Indeed, they attribute to Him a son, while He provides for them and heals them.” And in the Sahih also: Indeed, God grants respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then he recited the statement of the Most High: “And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are unjust. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.” And some of them recited: He said, ‘And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little.’ The verse, making it part of the supplication of Abraham, and it is an anomalous reading that contradicts the seven reciters, and the structure of the context rejects its meaning, and God knows best, for the pronoun in He said: It refers to God Almighty in the reading of the majority, and the context requires it. According to this anomalous reading, the pronoun in said refers to Abraham, and this is contrary to the order of speech, and God Almighty is the All-Knowing. As for the Almighty’s saying: “And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], ‘Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.’” The foundations are the plural of qa’idah, which is the pillar and foundation. The Almighty says: And mention, O Muhammad, to your people, Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, building the House and raising its foundations, and they were saying, “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” Al-Qurtubi and others narrated on the authority of Abi and Ibn Mas’ud that they were reciting, “And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], ‘Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.’” I said This is indicated by their saying after it, Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. The verse, so they were doing a good deed, and they were asking God Almighty to accept from them, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunais al-Makki on the authority of Wahib ibn al-Ward that he recited, “And when Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, were raising their foundations, [saying], ‘Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.’” The foundations of the House and Ishmael, our Lord accept from us.” Then he cries and says: O Khalil al-Rahman, the pillars of the House of the Most Merciful are being raised and you are afraid that it will not be accepted from you. This is as God the Most High narrated about the state of the sincere believers in His statement: And those who give what they give meaning they give what they give of charity, expenditures and offerings while their hearts are fearful meaning afraid that it will not be accepted from them, as came in the authentic hadith on the authority of Aisha on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as will come in its place. Some of the commentators said: The one who was raising the foundations was Ibrahim and the supplicant was Ishmael, and the correct view is that they were both raising and saying as will be explained. Al-Bukhari narrated here a hadith which we will quote and then follow it with related narrations. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub Al-Sakhtiyani and Kathir bin Kathir bin Abdul Muttalib bin Abi Wada’ah - one of them adds more than the other - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The first time women used lanyards was before the mother of Ismail, who used lanyards to erase her traces on Sarah. Then Ibrahim brought her and her son Ismail while she was breastfeeding him, until he placed them near the House, near a tree above Zamzam at the top of the mosque, and there was no one in Mecca at that time, nor was there any water. So he placed them there and placed near them a bag of dates and a water skin with water. Then Ibrahim turned and went away, and Ismail’s mother followed him and said: O Ibrahim, where are you going and leaving us in this valley with no one to accompany us? And nothing? She said that to him repeatedly, but he did not pay attention to her. She said: Has God commanded you to do this? He said: Yes. She said: Then He will not let us down. Then she returned. So Abraham set out until he was at the pass where they could not see him, facing the House. Then he supplicated with these supplications and raised his hands, saying, Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, until he reached they give thanks. And the mother of Ismail began to suckle Ismail and drink from that water, until what was in the water skin was used up, she became thirsty and her son became thirsty, and she began to look at him writhing—or he said: floundering—so she set out, hating to look at him, and she found Safa to be the nearest mountain on earth to her, so she stood on it and then faced the valley to see if she could see anyone, but she did not see anyone. So she descended from Safa until she reached the valley, raised the edge of her armor and ran as a person struggles until she passed the valley, then she came to Marwa and stood on it and looked to see if she could see anyone, but she did not see anyone. She did that seven times. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, That is why people ran between them. When she approached Marwa, she heard a voice and said, Hush. She wanted herself - then she listened and heard also, so she said: I have heard if you have help, so behold, the king is at the place of Zamzam, so he searched with his heel, or he said: with his wing, until the water appeared, so she began to surround it and say with her hand like this, and she began to scoop from the water in her water skin and it was bubbling after she scooped, Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on the mother of Ismail, if she had left Zamzam - or he said: if she had not scooped from the water - Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.” He said: So she drank and breastfed her son, so the king said to her: Do not fear loss, for here is a house for God that this boy and his father will build, and God does not neglect His people, and the house was high above the ground like a hill, and the floods would come to it and take from its right and left, and it was like that until a group of Jurhum or a family of Jurhum passed by them coming from the road of Kada, so they stopped at the bottom of Mecca, and they saw a circling bird, so they said: This bird is circling On water, as we knew this valley and there was no water in it, so they sent one or two men running, and if they were at water, they returned and he informed them of the water, so they came. He said: And the mother of Ismail was at the water, so they said: Do you give us permission to stay with you? She said: Yes, but you have no right to our water. They said: Yes. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ishmael’s mother found that and she loved company. So they dismounted and sent for their people, so they dismounted with them, until there were some households there from them, and the boy grew up and learned Arabic from them, and they liked him and were pleased with him when he grew up. When he reached puberty, they married him to a woman from them, and Ishmael’s mother died. Abraham came after Ishmael had married to look at his estate, but he did not find Ishmael. He asked his wife about him, and she said: He went out seeking us. Then he asked her about their living and their condition, and she said: We are human beings, we are in hardship and difficulty. So she complained to him, and he said: When your husband comes, greet him and tell him to change the threshold of his door. When Ishmael came, it seemed as if he had sensed something, so he said: Has anyone come to you? She said: Yes, an old man of such and such came to us and asked us about you, so I told him. He asked me how we lived, so I told him that we were in hardship and difficulty. He said: Did he advise you about anything? She said: Yes, he ordered me to greet you and say: Change the threshold of your door. He said: That is my father and he ordered me to leave you, so go back to your family. He divorced her and married another woman from them. Ibrahim stayed away from them as long as God willed, then he came to them later and did not find him. He went to his wife and asked her about him. She said: He went out seeking us. He said: How are you? He asked her about their livelihood and their condition. She said: We are well and comfortable, and praised God the Almighty. He said: What is your food? She said: Meat. He said: What is your drink? She said: Water. He said: O God, bless them in the meat and water. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “And they did not have grain at that time. If they had, he would have prayed for it for them.” He said: So no one would be alone with them except in Mecca without agreeing to it. He said: So when your husband comes, greet him with my greetings and tell him to fix the threshold of his door. When Ismail came, he said: Has anyone come to you? She said: Yes, a well-mannered old man came to us, and she praised him. He asked me about you, so I told him. He asked me how we lived. I told him that I was fine. He said: Did he advise you about anything? She said: Yes, and he sends you his greetings and orders you to strengthen the threshold of your door. He said: That is my father and you are the threshold. He ordered me to hold you back. Then he stayed away from them as God willed. Then he came after that and Ishmael was sharpening his arrows under a tree near Zamzam. When he saw him, he went to him, and they did as a father does with his son and a son does with his father. Then he said: O Ishmael, God has commanded me to do something. He said: Do what your Lord has commanded you. He said: Will you help me? He said: And I will help you. He said: God has commanded me to build a house here, and he pointed to a high hill above what was around it. He said: Then they raised the foundations of the house, and Ismail began to bring stones and Abraham built, until when the building was high, he brought this stone and placed it for him, and he stood on it while he was building and Ismail was handing him the stones, and they were saying: Our Lord, accept from us, for You are the Hearing, the Knowing. He said: So they began to build until they circled around the house and they were saying: Our Lord, accept from us, for You are the Hearing, the Knowing. And Abd bin Hamid narrated it from Abd al-Razzaq in full, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Abdullah bin Hammad al-Tabarani, and Ibn Jarir from Ahmad bin Thabit al-Razi, both of them from Abd al-Razzaq in short. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ismail bin Ali told us, Bishr bin Musa told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Azraqi told us, Muslim bin Khalid al-Zanji told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Jurayj, on the authority of Kathir bin Kathir, who said: I, Uthman bin Abi Sulayman, and Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Husayn were with some people with Saeed bin Jubair at the top of the mosque at night, and Saeed bin Jubair said: Ask me before you do not see me, so they asked him about the station, and he began to tell them on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned the hadith in full. Then Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abu Amir Abdul Malik bin Amr told us, Ibrahim bin Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Kathir bin Kathir, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When what happened between Abraham and his family happened, he went out with Ishmael and Ishmael’s mother, and with them was a water skin.
