Saeed said: Ali ibn Abi Talib told us: Abraham came from the land of Armenia, and with him was the serenity guiding him to take up residence in the House as a spider takes up residence in a house. He said: Then it revealed stones that only thirty men could carry a stone, so I said: O Abu Muhammad, God says: And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House He said: That was later. Al-Suddi said: God Almighty commanded Abraham and Ishmael to build the House, Build My House for those who go around it, and those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate. So Abraham set out until he came to Mecca. He and Ishmael stood up and took up their pickaxes, not knowing where the House was. Then God sent a wind called the Khajuj wind, which had two wings and a head in the form of a snake. It revealed to them around the Kaaba the foundation of the first House. They followed it with pickaxes, digging until they laid the foundation. That is when God Almighty says: And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House, “And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House.” When they had built the foundations and reached the place of the corner, Abraham said to Ishmael: My son, find me a beautiful stone that I may place here. He said: O my father, I am lazy and ignorant. He said: I will do that. So he set out to find a stone for him, and he brought him a stone, but he was not satisfied with it. So he said: Bring me a stone better than this. So he set out to find a stone for him, and Gabriel brought him the Black Stone from India. It was white, a white ruby like a thujamah. Adam had brought it down from Paradise, but it had turned black from the sins of the people. Then Ishmael brought him a stone and found it at the corner. He said: O my father, who brought you this? He said: He brought it from someone who is more active than you, so they built and they were calling upon the words that Abraham tested his Lord with, so he said: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” In this context, there is evidence that the foundations of the House were built before Abraham, and Abraham was only guided to it and given it a place to live. Some have gone to this, as Imam Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House. He said, the foundations that were the foundations of the House before that. Abdul Razzaq also said: Hisham bin Hassan told us on the authority of Suwar, the son-in-law of Ata’, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, who said: When God sent Adam down from Paradise, his feet were on the ground and his head was in the sky, hearing the speech of the people of the sky and their supplications, and he was comforted by them. So the angels were afraid until they complained to God in their supplications and prayers, so God Almighty lowered him to the ground. When he lost what he used to hear from them, he became lonely, until he complained about that to God in his supplications and prayers, so he turned towards Mecca and the place of his feet was a village, and his steps A desert, until he reached Mecca, and God sent down a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, and it was in the place of the House now, and he kept circling it until God sent down the flood, and that ruby was lifted up, until God sent Abraham, peace be upon him, and he built it, that is the saying of God Almighty: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Ata’, he said: Adam said: I do not hear the voices of the angels, so he said: Because of your sin, but descend to the earth and build me a house, then surround it as you saw the angels surrounding my house that is in the heaven. And the people claim that he built it from five mountains: from Hira’, Mount Zayta, Mount Sinai, and al-Judi, and its suburb was from Hira’, so this was the building of Adam until Abraham, peace be upon him, built it later, and this is correct up to Ata’, but in some of it there is something strange, and God knows best. Abdul Razzaq also said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada, who said: God placed the House with Adam when God sent Adam down to Earth, and his descent was in the land of India, and his head was in the sky and his feet were on the earth, so the angels feared him, then it decreased to sixty cubits, and Adam was saddened when he lost the voices of the angels and their glorification, so he complained about that to God Almighty, so God said: O Adam, I have sent down a House for you to circumambulate as one circumambulates around My Throne, and to pray at it as one prays at My Throne, so Adam went to it, and he went out and stretched out his steps for him, so between every two steps there was a wilderness, and that wilderness did not cease after that, so Adam came to the House and circumambulated it, and after him from the prophets. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Humayd, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God placed the House on the four pillars of water before the creation of the world by two thousand years, then the earth was rolled out from under the House. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah ibn Abi Nujayh told me, on the authority of Mujahid and other scholars: When God designated the location of the House for Abraham, he went out to it from Syria, and Ishmael and his mother Hagar went out with him, and Ishmael was a small child who was being breastfed. And they were carried, as he told me, on Buraq, and Gabriel was with him, guiding him to the location of the House and the landmarks of the Sanctuary. Gabriel went out with him, and he would not pass by a village without saying: Is this where you were commanded, O Gabriel? Gabriel would say: Go with him, until he brought him to Mecca, which at that time was Udah, Salim and Samar, and in it were people called the Amalekites outside Mecca and its environs. And the House at that time was a red, muddy hill, so Abraham said to Gabriel: Was I commanded to place them here? He said: Yes, so he took them to the place of the Black Stone and settled them there, and he ordered Hajar, the mother of Ismail, to build a hut there, and he said: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House until His saying: that they may be grateful. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, Hamid informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: God created the location of this House two thousand years before He created anything, and its pillars are in the seventh earth. And Laith ibn Abi Salim said the same on the authority of Mujahid: The foundations are in the seventh earth. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father informed us, Amr ibn Rafi’ informed us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muawiyah informed us, on the authority of Abd al-Mu’min ibn Khalid, on the authority of Aliya ibn Ahmar: Dhul-Qarnayn came to Mecca and found Abraham and Ismail building the foundations of the House from five mountains. So he said: What do you have to do with my land? He said: We are two commanded servants, we were commanded to build this Kaaba. He said: Bring the proof of what you claim. Five rams stood up and said: We bear witness that Abraham and Ishmael were two servants who were commanded to build this Kaaba. He said: I am satisfied and I submit, then he left. Al-Azraqi mentioned in the History of Mecca that Dhul-Qarnayn circumambulated the House with Abraham, peace be upon him, and this indicates that he was an advanced man in his time, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him said: The Almighty’s saying: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House (Al-Qawa’id: 33). The foundations: its foundation, the singular of which is Qawa’id, and the singular of Qawa’id among women is Qawa’id. Ismail told us: Malik told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, that Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr told Abdullah bin Umar on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Did you not see that when your people built the House, they limited themselves to the foundations of Abraham? I said: O Messenger of God, will you not return it to the foundations of Abraham? He said: Had it not been for the recent disbelief of your people. Abdullah bin Umar said: If Aisha heard this from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I do not see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) leaving out touching the two corners next to the Black Stone, except that the House was not completed on the foundations of Abraham (peace be upon him). It was narrated in Hajj on the authority of Al-Qa'nabi, and in the Hadiths of the Prophets on the authority of Abdullah bin Yusuf and Muslim, on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya, and from the hadith of Ibn Wahb and Al-Nasa'i on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Qasim, all on the authority of Malik with it. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Nafi' who said: I heard Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Abi Quhafah, narrating to Abdullah bin Umar on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: "Had it not been that your people had recently converted from ignorance - or he said: from disbelief - I would have spent the treasure of the Ka'ba in the way of God, and I would have made its door in the ground and included the Black Stone in it." Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah bin Musa informed us on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Aswad, who said: Ibn Al-Zubayr said to me: Aisha used to tell you many secret hadiths, so what did she tell you about the Ka'ba? He said: I said: She told me: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Aisha, were it not that your people had recently converted to disbelief, I would have demolished the Kaaba and made two doors for it: one for people to enter through and one for them to exit through.” So Ibn al-Zubayr did so. Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it, and he narrated it like this in the Book of Knowledge of his Sahih. Muslim said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Yahya told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “Were it not that your people had recently converted to disbelief, I would have demolished the Kaaba and made it on the foundation of Abraham, for when the Quraysh built the House, they shortened it, and they would have made a successor for it.” He said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb told us, they said: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Hisham, with this chain of transmission, and Muslim is the only one to narrate it. He said: Muhammad ibn Hatim told me, Ibn Mahdi told me, Salim ibn Hayyan told us, on the authority of Sa’id, meaning Ibn Mina’. He said: I heard Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr say: My aunt, meaning Aisha, may God be pleased with her, told me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Aisha, if your people were not recent converts to polytheism, I would have demolished the Kaaba and leveled it with the ground, and I would have made an eastern door and a western door for it, and I would have added six cubits of stone to it, for the Quraysh had shortened it when they built the Kaaba.” This is also unique to him. He was transferred with them in the stones when he was thirty-five years old. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in the biography: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached thirty-five years of age, the Quraysh gathered to build the Kaaba, and they intended to do so in order to roof it and were afraid to demolish it, but it was only rubble above the height of a person, so they wanted to raise it and roof it. This was because a group of people had stolen the treasure of the Kaaba, which was in a well inside the Kaaba. The one who found the treasure was Duwaik, a client of Banu Malih bin Amr from Khuza’ah, so the Quraysh cut off his hand, and people claim that those who stole it placed it with Duwaik. The sea had thrown a ship to Jeddah belonging to a Roman merchant, and it was shattered, so they took its wood and prepared it to roof it. There was a Coptic carpenter in Mecca, so he prepared for them some of what would repair it. There was a snake that came out of the well of the Kaaba into which it threw what was given to it every day, and it would hang itself on the wall of the Kaaba, and it was one of the things they feared, because no one would approach it except that it would shake, scrape, and open its mouth. They feared her. One day, while she was standing on the wall of the Kaaba as she used to do, God sent a bird to her and snatched her away. The Quraysh said: We hope that God is pleased with what we want. We have a gentle worker and wood, and God has spared us from the snake. When they decided to demolish and rebuild it, Abu Wahb ibn Amr ibn Aaidh ibn Abd ibn Imran ibn Makhzum stood up and took a stone from the Kaaba, which jumped out of his hand until it returned to its place. He said: O people of the Quraysh, do not include in its construction anything from your earnings except what is good. Do not include in it the dowry of a prostitute, nor a sale based on usury, nor the oppression of any of the people. Ibn Ishaq said: People attribute these words to Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Makhzum. He said: Then the Quraysh divided the Kaaba, so the section of the door went to the Banu Abd Manaf and Zuhrah, and the area between the Black Corner and the Yemeni Corner went to the Banu Makhzum and tribes of the Quraysh. They joined them, and the back of the Kaaba belonged to Banu Jumah and Sahm, and the split in the stone belonged to Banu Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy, Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusayy, and Banu Adi ibn Kaab ibn Luayy, which is al-Hutaym. Then the people feared its demolition and were afraid of it, so al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said, I will start with you in demolishing it. So he took the pickaxe and stood over it saying, “O God, do not be afraid. O God, we only want good.” Then he demolished from the side of the two corners, and the people waited that night and said, “We will wait. If it is hit, we will not demolish anything of it, and we will return it as it was. If nothing is hit, then God is pleased with what we have done.” So al-Walid went to work that night, and he demolished and the people demolished with him, until when the demolition reached the foundation, the foundation of Abraham, peace be upon him, they came upon green stones like spears, some of which were attached to others. He said, Someone who narrates the hadith told me that a man from Quraysh who was demolishing it inserted a lever between two of its stones in order to remove one of them as well. When the stone moved, all of Mecca revolted, and they stopped that foundation. Ibn Ishaq said: Then the tribes of Quraysh gathered stones to build it, each tribe gathered separately, then they built it until the building reached the place of the corner, meaning the Black Stone, then they disputed about it, each tribe wanted to raise it to its place without the other, until they discussed and disagreed and prepared for battle, so Banu Abd al-Dar brought a bowl filled with blood, then they and Banu Adi bin Kaab bin Luay agreed to die, and they put their hands in that blood in that bowl and they called it the blood lick, so Quraysh remained like that for four or five nights, then they gathered in the mosque and consulted and divided equally, so some of the narrators claimed that Abu Umayyah bin al-Mughira bin Abdullah bin Amr bin Makhzum, who was at that time the oldest of all Quraysh, said: O people of Quraysh, make between you in what you disagree about the first one to enter through the door of this mosque to judge between you in it, so they did, and the first to enter was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when they saw him they said: This is the trustworthy one, we are satisfied, this is Muhammad. When he reached them and they told him the report, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bring me a garment. So it was brought to him, and he took the corner, meaning the Black Stone, and placed it in it with his hand. Then he said: Let each tribe take a corner of the garment and then lift it all together. So they did until they reached its place, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed it with his hand, then he built on it. The Quraysh used to call the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before the revelation came down, the Trustworthy One. So when they finished building and built it as they wanted, Al-Zubayr ibn Abdul Muttalib said, regarding the matter of the snake for which the Quraysh feared the construction of the Kaaba: I was surprised when the eagle aimed at the snake while it was in a state of agitation. It used to have a kesheesh and sometimes it used to have a thawb. If we set out to establish, the building will be feared and you will be afraid But when we feared the punishment, a punishment came pouring forth from it. Then she took her to herself and left us with a building without a veil. So we gathered to build our foundations and soil. Tomorrow we will raise the foundation from it and there will be no clothes on our faults The king honored the Banu Luay with it, so his origins are not lost to them. And Banu Adi gathered there, and once they were led by Kalb. So the king gave us honor for that, and he seeks reward from God. Ibn Ishaq said: The Kaaba was eighteen cubits high during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was covered with Coptic, then it was covered with brocade, and the first to cover it with brocade was Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf. I said It remained as the Quraysh built it until it was burned at the beginning of the emirate of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr after the year sixty and at the end of the reign of Yazid bin Muawiyah, when they besieged Ibn Al-Zubayr. Then Ibn Al-Zubayr demolished it to the ground and built it on the foundations of Abraham, peace be upon him, and inserted the stone into it, and made for it an eastern door and a western door attached to the ground as he heard that from his aunt Aisha, the mother of the believers, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It remained like that during the period of his emirate until Al-Hajjaj killed him, and he returned it to what it was by the order of Abdul Malik bin Marwan to do so, as Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, Ibn Abi Zaidah told us, Ibn Abi Sulayman told us on the authority of Ata’, who said: When the House was burned during the time of Yazid bin Muawiyah when the people of Ash-Sham invaded it, and what happened happened, Ibn Al-Zubayr left it. Al-Zubayr, until the people arrived at the season, wanted to form a party among them or seek their protection against the people of Ash-Sham. When the people left, he said: O people, advise me regarding the Kaaba, should I demolish it and then rebuild it, or repair what is damaged in it? Ibn Abbas said: I have a different opinion about it. I think that you should repair what is damaged in it, and leave a house that the people were safe upon, and stones that the people were safe upon, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent upon. Ibn Al-Zubayr said: If one of them had his house burned down, he would not be satisfied until he renovated it, so how about the house of your Lord, the Almighty and Majestic? I seek counsel from my Lord for three days, then I am determined to do my thing. When three days had passed, he decided to demolish it, but the people avoided it lest something from the sky descend upon the first person to ascend it. Then a man climbed it and threw stones from it. When the people did not see anything happen to it, they followed one another and demolished it until they reached the ground. Ibn al-Zubayr made pillars to cover them with curtains until its construction rose. Ibn al-Zubayr said: I heard Aisha, may God be pleased with her, say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Were it not that the people had recently converted from disbelief, and that I did not have the means to build it, I would have added five cubits of stone to it, and made a door for people to enter through, and a door for them to exit through.” He said: I find what I can spend, and I am not afraid of people. He said: So he added five cubits of stone to it until he showed it a foundation. The people looked at it, so he built the structure on it. The length of the Kaaba was eighteen cubits, but when he added to it, he shortened it, so he added ten cubits at the beginning and made two doors for it: one for entering through, and one for exiting through. And the other comes out of it. When Ibn al-Zubayr was killed, al-Hajjaj wrote to Abd al-Malik asking him to permit him to do so and informing him that Ibn al-Zubayr had put the building on a foundation that the just people of Mecca had seen. Abd al-Malik wrote to him: We are not against Ibn al-Zubayr’s taint in anything. As for what he added to its height, he approved it, and as for what he added of stones, he returned it to its building, and closed the door that he opened, so he demolished it and returned it to its building. Al-Nasa’i narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Hanad, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Za’idah, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He did not mention the story, and the Sunnah was an approval of what Abd God ibn al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, had done, because he was the one whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved. However, he feared that some people’s hearts would reject it because of their newness to Islam and their recent history of disbelief. However, this Sunnah was hidden from Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and for this reason, when it was confirmed on the authority of Aisha, she narrated it on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: We wished that we had left it. And he did not take over, as Muslim said: Muhammad bin Hatim told me, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, Ibn Jurayj told us: I heard Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair and Al-Walid bin Ata’ narrating on the authority of Al-Harith bin Abdullah bin Abi Rabi’ah, Abdullah bin Ubaid said: Al-Harith bin Abdullah delegated to Abdul Malik bin Marwan during his caliphate, and Abdul Malik said: I do not think that Abu Habib, meaning Ibn Al-Zubayr, heard from Aisha what he claimed he heard from her, Al-Harith said: Yes, I heard it from her. He said: I heard her say what? He said: She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your people have shortened the construction of the House, and were it not for the recent conversion to polytheism, I would have restored what they had left of it. If your people decide to rebuild it after me, then come and I will show you what they have left of it.” So I saw it was close to seven cubits. This is the hadith of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, and Al-Walid bin Ata’ added to it: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And I would have made two doors for it placed in the ground: one to the east and one to the west. Do you know why your people raised its door? She said: No. He said: To strengthen it so that no one would enter it except those they wanted. So when a man wanted to enter it, they would call him until he climbed up, until when he was about to enter, they would push him and he would fall. Abdul Malik said: So I said to Al-Harith: Did you hear her say that? He said: Yes. He said: So he poked it for a while with his stick, then he said: I wish I had left it and not carried it. Muslim said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Jabalah told us, Abu Asim H told us, and Abd ibn Hamid told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, both of them on the authority of Ibn Jurayj with this chain of transmission like the hadith of Abu Bakr. He said: Muhammad ibn Hatim told us, Abdullah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi told us, Hatim ibn Abi Saghira told us on the authority of Abu Qaz’ah: While Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was circumambulating the House, he said: May God kill Ibn al-Zubayr, for he lies about the Mother of the Believers. He said: I heard her say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Aisha, were it not for the recent disbelief of your people, I would have demolished the Kaaba so that I could add more stones to it, for your people have fallen short in building it. Al-Harith ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi’ah said: Do not say this, O Commander of the Faithful, for I heard the Mother of the Believers say this. He said: If I had heard it before I demolished it, I would have left it as Ibn al-Zubayr had built it. This hadith is as if it is definitely attributed to Aisha, because it has been narrated from her through multiple authentic chains of transmission on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Yazid, al-Harith ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. This indicates that what Ibn al-Zubayr did was correct, and if it had been left, it would have been good. But after the matter returned to this state, some scholars were reluctant to change its state, as was mentioned about the Commander of the Faithful, Harun al-Rashid, or his father, al-Mahdi, that he asked Imam Malik about demolishing the Kaaba and returning it to what Ibn al-Zubayr had done. Malik said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, do not make the Kaaba of God a playground for kings. No one wants to demolish it except that he demolishes it. Al-Rashid left that. It was narrated by Iyad and al-Nawawi. And it will remain like this - and God knows best - until the end of time until it is destroyed by Dhu al-Sawiqatain from Abyssinia, as was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Kaaba will be destroyed by Dhu al-Sawiqatain from Abyssinia. They both reported it. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, It is as if I see a black man with a hump, tearing it out stone by stone. Narrated by al-Bukhari. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Haranin informed us. Muhammad ibn Salamah informed us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahidin on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The Kaaba will be destroyed by Dhu al-Sawiqatain from Abyssinia, who will strip it of its ornaments and will strip it of its covering. It is as if I see…” To him, Asli’ Afid’a, who strikes it with his shovel and pickaxe - Fad’a: a deviation between the foot and the shin bone - and this, and God knows best, will only happen after the emergence of Gog and Magog, as it came in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They will perform Hajj to the House and Umrah after the emergence of Gog and Magog. And the Almighty’s saying, narrating the supplication of Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, “Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.” Ibn Jarir said: By that they mean, And make us submissive to Your command, submissive to Your obedience, and we do not associate anyone with You in obedience, nor in worship other than You. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ismail told us on the authority of Raja’ ibn Hibban al-Hasani al-Qurashi, Maqal ibn Ubayd God told us on the authority of Abd al-Karim, And make us Muslims [in submission] to You, he said: sincere to You, And from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You, he said: sincere. He also said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, al-Muqaddami told us, Sa’id ibn Amir told us on the authority of Salam ibn Abi Mut’i’ regarding this verse, And make us Muslims, he said: They were Muslims, but they asked him to be steadfast. Ikrimah said, Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You. God said, I have done so. “And from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You.” God said, I have done so. As-Suddi said, And from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. They both mean the Arabs. Ibn Jarir said, “The correct interpretation is that it includes the Arabs and others, because from the descendants of Abraham are the Children of Israel, and God the Most High said, “And among the people of Moses is a nation guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby.” I say, As-Suddi does not deny what Ibn Jarir said, because singling them out for that does not negate others, and the context is the Arabs, and that is why He said after it, Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. What is meant by this is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was sent among them as God Almighty said: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves. However, this does not negate his message to the red and the black, as God Almighty said: Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all,’ and other conclusive evidence. This supplication was made by Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, as God Almighty informed us about His pious and believing servants in His saying: And those who say, ‘Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous.’ This amount is desired by the Sharia, because part of the perfection of loving the worship of God Almighty is to love that there be from his offspring someone who worships God alone, with no partner. And for this reason, when God the Almighty said to Abraham, peace be upon him, Indeed, I will make you a leader for mankind, He said, And of my descendants. He said, My covenant does not include the wrongdoers, which is His saying, And keep me and my children away from worshipping idols. It has been proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he said, “When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him.” And show us our rituals, Ibn Jarir said on the authority of Ata’, And show us our rituals, he brought them out for us so that we may learn them. Mujahid said, Show us our rituals, meaning our slaughterhouses. Something similar was also narrated on the authority of Ata’ and Qatadah. Saeed bin Mansour said: Itab bin Bashir told us on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim said, Show us our rituals. Gabriel showed him to him and brought him to the House. He said, Raise the foundations. So he raised the foundations and completed the building. Then he took him by the hand and led him out and went with him to Safa. He said, This is one of the symbols of God. Then he went with him to Marwah. He said, This is one of the symbols of God. Then he went with him towards Mina. When he reached Aqaba, Satan was standing by the tree. He said, Say ‘Allahu Akbar’ and throw it. So he said, Allahu Akbar and threw it. Then Satan went and stood at the middle Jamarat. When Gabriel and Ibrahim passed by him, he said to him, Say ‘Allahu Akbar’ and throw it. So he said, Allahu Akbar and threw it. Then the evil Satan went away. The evil one wanted to include something in the Hajj, but he could not. So he took Ibrahim by the hand until he came to the Sacred Monument. He said, This is the Sacred Monument. So Ibrahim took Ibrahim by the hand and brought him to Arafat. He said, Do you understand what I showed you? He said it three times. He said, Yes. Abu Majlaz and Qatadah narrated something similar to this. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Abu al-Asim al-Ghanawi, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim was shown the commands of the rituals, Satan appeared to him at the Mas’a, so Ibrahim raced him, then Gabriel took him until he came to Mina. He said: This is the place where people stop. When he reached Jamrat al-Aqaba, Satan appeared to him, so he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. Then he brought him to Jamrat al-Qawwa, and Satan appeared to him, so he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. He brought him all together and said: This is al-Mash’ar. Then he brought him to Arafat, and he said: This is Arafat. Gabriel said to him: Do you recognize it?
2:129: God Almighty says, informing about the completion of Abraham's call to the people of the sanctuary that God would send among them a Messenger from among them, that is, from the descendants of Abraham. This answered call was in accordance with God's previous decree in appointing Muhammad, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, as a Messenger to the illiterate people to them and to all the non-Arabs among mankind and jinn, as Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Salih, on the authority of Saeed ibn Suwaid al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abd al-A'la ibn Hilal al-Sulami, on the authority of al-Arbadh ibn Sariyah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, I am with God the Seal of the Prophets, and Adam was still kneaded in his clay. I will inform you of the beginning of that, the call of my father Abraham, and the glad tidings of Jesus about me, and the vision that my mother saw, and so do the mothers of the prophets see." And Ibn Wahb, al-Layth, and his scribe Abdullah ibn Salih narrated it on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Salih, and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam followed him on the authority of Saeed ibn Suwaid with it. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Nadr informed us, al-Faraj informed us, Luqman ibn Aamer said: I heard Abu Umamah say: I said, O Messenger of God: What was the beginning of your affair? He said: “The supplication of my father Abraham, and the good report of Jesus about me. And my mother saw that a light came out of her that illuminated the palaces of Ash-Sham.” What is meant is that the first person to be mentioned and made famous among the people was Abraham, peace be upon him, and his mention among the people continued to be mentioned, famous, and widespread until the Seal of the Prophets of the Children of Israel revealed his name by lineage, and he is Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, when he stood up among the Children of Israel as a preacher and said: I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and giving good tidings of a Messenger to come after me whose name is Ahmad. That is why he said in this hadith: The supplication of my father Abraham and the good tidings of Jesus, son of Mary. And his saying: And my mother saw that a light came out of her that illuminated the palaces of Ash-Sham, it was said that it was a dream she saw when she dreamt of him, and she told it to her people, so it spread among them and became famous, and that was a prelude and the specialization of Ash-Sham for the appearance of his light, indicating the stability of his religion and prophethood in the lands of Ash-Sham, and for this reason Ash-Sham will be at the end of time a stronghold for Islam and its people, and in it Jesus, son of Mary, will descend when he descends in Damascus with its eastern white minaret, and for this reason it came in the two Sahihs: A group of my nation will continue to prevail upon the truth, and they will not be harmed by those who let them down or those who oppose them until the command of God comes and they are like that. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari: And they are in Ash-Sham. Abu Ja`far Al-Razi said on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah regarding his saying: Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among themselves, meaning the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it was said to him: Your request has been answered, and it will happen at the end of time, and this is what Al-Suddi and Qatadah said, and the Almighty’s saying: And He will teach them the Book, meaning the Qur’an, and wisdom, meaning the Sunnah, as Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Muqatil bin Hayyan said. Abu Malik and others, and it was said: Understanding is in religion and there is no contradiction, And purifies them Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas meaning obedience to God and Muhammad bin Ishaq said And teaches them the Book and wisdom he said good so they do it and evil so they avoid it, and informs them of God’s pleasure with them if they obey Him so that they may increase their obedience to Him and avoid what angers Him of disobedience to Him, and His saying Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise meaning the Exalted who is not incapable of anything, and He is able to do all things, the Wise in His actions and words, so He places things in their proper places due to His knowledge, wisdom and justice.
2:130: The Almighty says in response to the infidels regarding what they innovated and invented of associating partners with God, which is contrary to the religion of Abraham, the friend of God, the leader of the monotheists, for he exclusively monotheized his Lord, the Almighty, and did not call upon anyone other than Him nor did he associate partners with Him for the blink of an eye, and he disavowed every deity other than Him, differing in that from the rest of his people until he disavowed his father, saying, “O my people, indeed I am disassociated from what you associate with Him. Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God.” And the Almighty says, And when Abraham said to his father and his people, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from what you worship, except for He who created me, for He will guide me.’ And the Almighty says, “And Abraham’s seeking of forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was kind and forbearing.” And the Almighty says, “Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God. Grateful for His favors. He chose him.” And guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. " For this and similar reasons, the Most High said: And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham from his way and method, so he would oppose it and turn away from it except one who makes a fool of himself? That is, he wronged himself with his foolishness and bad management by abandoning the truth for misguidance, as he opposed the path of the one chosen in this world for guidance and right direction from his young age until God took him as a friend, and in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous and happy ones. So whoever abandons this way, his path, and his religion, and follows the path of misguidance and error, what foolishness is greater than this? Or what injustice is greater than this? As God Almighty said: Indeed, associating others with God is a great wrong. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Qatadah said: This verse was revealed about the Jews. They created a path that was not from God, and they contradicted the religion of Abraham in what they created. The truth of this statement is attested by God Almighty’s statement: “Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim [submitting to God]. And he was not of the polytheists. Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who believe. And God is the ally of the believers.” And the Almighty’s saying: When his Lord said to him, ‘Submit,’ he said, ‘I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.’ That is, God commanded him to be sincere, surrender, and obey, so he responded to that in terms of law and destiny. And His saying: And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons, and so did Jacob. That is, he enjoined this religion, which is submission to God, or the pronoun refers to the word, which is His saying: I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds. Because of their keenness on it and their love for it, they preserved it until death, and enjoined it upon their sons after them, as in the Almighty’s saying: And He made it a word remaining among his descendants. Some of the predecessors read and Jacob in the accusative case, in apposition to his sons, as if Abraham enjoined upon his sons and his grandson Jacob, son of Isaac, and he was present at that. Al-Qushayri claimed, as Al-Qurtubi narrated from him, that Jacob was only born after the death of Abraham, and something like this needs sound evidence. It appears, and God knows best, that Isaac gave birth to Jacob during the lifetime of Abraham and Sarah, because the good report came to them in His saying: So We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. And it was read in the accusative case. Jacob here is on the removal of the preposition, so if Jacob had not existed during their lifetime, there would not have been much benefit in mentioning him among the descendants of Isaac. Also, God Almighty said in Surat al-Ankabut 29:And We gave him Isaac and Jacob and placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book 22:13, and He said in another verse: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift 22:13. This indicates that he existed during his lifetime. Also, he was the builder of the Holy House, as stated in the previous books, and it was proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Dharr: I said: O Messenger of God, which mosque was established first? He said: The Sacred Mosque. I said: Then which? He said: The Holy House. I said: How much time is between them? He said: Forty years, the hadith, so Ibn Hibban claimed that between Solomon, who he believed was the builder of the Holy House - and he only renovated it after its destruction and decorated it - and Abraham, there were forty years, and this is something that Ibn Hibban denied, because the period between them exceeds thousands of years, and God knows best. Also, Jacob’s will to his sons will be mentioned soon, and this indicates that he is here among those who recommend. And his saying, O my sons, God has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except as Muslims, meaning, do good in your life, and adhere to this so that God may grant you death upon it, because a person usually dies as he was, and is resurrected as he died, and God the Generous has made it His custom that whoever intends good, He will guide him to it and make it easy for him, and whoever intends righteousness, He will remain upon it. This does not contradict what came in the authentic hadith: “A man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a span or an arm’s length between him and it, then what is written will overtake him and he will do the deeds of the people of Hell and enter it. A man may do the deeds of the people of Hell until there is only a span or an arm’s length between him and it, then what is written will overtake him and he will do the deeds of the people of Paradise and enter it.” Because it came in some narrations of this hadith that he will do the deeds of the people of Paradise as it appears to people and the deeds of the people of Hell as it appears to people. And God the Most High said: “But as for him who gives and fears God * And believes in the best * We will ease him toward ease * But as for him who withholds and considers himself free of need * And denies the best * We will ease him toward difficulty.”

2:133: God Almighty says, arguing against the polytheists among the Arabs, the sons of Ishmael, and against the infidels among the children of Israel - he is Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, peace be upon them - that when death approached Jacob, he advised his sons to worship God alone, with no partner for Him, so he said to them, "What will you worship after me? They said, We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac." This is from the perspective of emphasis, because Ishmael was his uncle. Nahhas said: The Arabs call the uncle a father, as Al-Qurtubi transmitted. This noble verse was used as evidence by those who made the grandfather a father and excluded the brothers with him, as is the saying of Al-Siddiq, narrated by Al-Bukhari from him through Ibn Abbas and Ibn Al-Zubayr, then Al-Bukhari said: And there is no disagreement about it, and Aisha, the mother of the believers, went to it, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Tawus, and Ata’ said it, and it is the doctrine of Abu Hanifa and more than one of the predecessors and successors, and Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad said in the well-known view from him that he shares with the brothers, and this was narrated from Omar, Othman, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Zaid bin Thabit, and a group of The predecessors and successors, and the two companions of Abu Hanifa, Judge Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, chose it, and there is another place for its confirmation, and his saying one God means we unify Him in divinity and do not associate anything with Him, and we are Muslims to Him meaning obedient and submissive, as God Almighty said: And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned. Islam is the religion of all the prophets, even if their laws were diverse and their methods differed, as God Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god except Me, so worship Me.’ And there are many verses and hadiths on this, including his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, We, the group of prophets, are children of one religion. And God Almighty said: That is a nation that has passed away, meaning it has passed away, It shall have what it earned, and you shall have what you have earned, meaning that the predecessors who passed away from your fathers from the prophets and righteous people, your affiliation with them will not benefit you if you do not do good that benefits you, because For them is their deeds that they did, and for you is your deeds. And you will not be asked about what they used to do. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’ and Qatadah said: That is a nation that has passed on, meaning Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the tribes. That is why it is stated in the hadith: Whoever is slowed down by his deeds will not be hastened by his lineage.

2:135: Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abdullah bin Suriya the one-eyed said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is no guidance except what we are upon, so follow us, O Muhammad, and you will be guided. The Christians said the same, so God Almighty revealed: And they said, ‘Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided.’ And His statement: Say, ‘Rather, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth.’ That is, we do not want what you have called us to of Judaism and Christianity, but we follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, meaning upright. Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi and Isa bin Jariyah said this, and Khasif said on the authority of Mujahid, sincerely. Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, pilgrim. This was also narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Atiyah, and al-Suddi. Abu al-Aaliyah said: The one who is inclining toward truth is the one who faces the House in his prayer, and he sees that his pilgrimage is upon him if he is able to do so. Mujahid and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: Hanif means a follower. Abu Qilabah said: Hanif is the one who believes in all the messengers from the first to the last of them. Qatada said: Hanifism is the testimony that there is no god but God, which includes prohibiting mothers, daughters, maternal aunts, paternal aunts, and what God Almighty has prohibited, as well as circumcision.
2:136: God the Almighty guided His believing servants to believe in what was revealed to them through His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in detail, and what was revealed to the previous prophets in general. He specified some of the messengers, and mentioned the rest of the prophets in general, and that they should not differentiate between any of them, but rather believe in all of them, and not be like those about whom God said, “And they want to make distinction between God and His messengers and say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and they want to adopt a way in between. Those are the disbelievers, truly.” Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Uthman bin Amrah told us, Ali bin Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic for the people of Islam, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Do not believe the People of the Book and do not disbelieve them, and say, ‘We believe in God and what God has revealed.’ Muslim, Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Uthman bin Hakim on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the two rak’ahs before dawn most often with the verse We believe in God and what has been revealed to us and the other with We believe in God and bear witness that we are Muslims. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’ and Qatadah said: The tribes are the sons of Jacob, twelve men, each of whom gave birth to a nation of people, so they were called the tribes. Al-Khalil bin Ahmad and others said: The tribes of the Children of Israel are like the tribes of the Children of Ishmael. Al-Zamakhshari said in Al-Kashshaf: The tribes are the tribes of the Children of Israel. This requires that what is meant by the tribes here are the peoples of the Children of Israel and what God sent down of revelation to the prophets who were present among them, as Moses said to them, Remember the favor of God upon you when He made prophets among you and made you kings verse, and God Almighty said, And We divided them into twelve tribes. Al-Qurtubi said: They were called the tribes from the word sabt, which means succession, so they are a group. It was said that its origin is from sabt, with a fat-ha, which means trees, meaning in abundance, like a single tree, a tribe. Al-Zajjaj said: Its origin is shown to you by what Muhammad bin Ja’far Al-Anbari told us, Abu Nujayd Al-Daqqaq told us, Al-Aswad bin Aamer told us, Israel told us on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: All the prophets are from the Children of Israel except ten: Noah, Hud, Salih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. And Ishmael and Muhammad, peace be upon them. Al-Qurtubi said: The grandson is the group and tribe that go back to one origin. Qatada said: God commanded the believers to believe in Him and to believe in all His books and His messengers. Sulayman ibn Habib said: We were only commanded to believe in the Torah and the Gospel, and not to act upon what is in them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mus`ab al-Suri informed us, Mu`ammil informed us, `Ubayd God ibn Abi Hamid informed us on the authority of Abu al-Malih, on the authority of Mu`qil ibn Yasar, who said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: Believe in the Torah, the Psalms, and the Gospel, and let the Qur’an suffice you.
2:137: God Almighty says: If they believe, meaning the unbelievers from the People of the Book and others, in the same way that you have believed, O believers, in believing in all the Books of God and His Messengers and they do not differentiate between any of them, then they have been guided, meaning they have attained the truth and have been guided to it. But if they turn away, meaning from the truth to falsehood after the proof has been established against them, “then they are only in dissension. So God will suffice you against them,” meaning He will grant you victory over them and make you triumph over them. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la read to me, Ibn Wahb told us, Ziyad bin Yunus told us, Nafi’ bin Abi Na’im told us, he said: He sent to one of the caliphs the copy of the Qur’an of Uthman bin Affan to fix it, Ziyad said: So I said to him: People say that his copy of the Qur’an was in his lap when he was killed and blood fell on God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Nafi’ said: My eyes saw the blood on this verse, and it has been presented. And his saying the dye of God, Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: the religion of God, and this is also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Ibrahim, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Abdullah bin Kathir, Atiyah Al-Awfi, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and As-Suddi, and something similar to that. And the accusative of the dye of God is either for incitement like his saying the nature of God, meaning adhere to that, and some of them said: instead of his saying the religion of Ibrahim. And Sibawayh said: It is a confirmed source that is accusative for his saying We believe in God, like his saying the promise of God, and it was mentioned in a hadith narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ash’ath ibn Ishaq from Sa’id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Children of Israel said: O Messenger of God, does your Lord dye? He said: Fear God. Then his Lord called out to him: O Moses, they asked you: Does your Lord dye? Say: Yes, I dye colors: red, white, and black, and all colors are from my dye.” And God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The dye of God, and who is better than God at dyeing? This is how it appears in the narration of Ibn Mardawayh, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and in the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim it is with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and this is more likely if its chain of transmission is sound, and God knows best.

2:139: God the Almighty says, guiding His Prophet, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, to avoid arguing with the polytheists: “Say: Do you argue with us about God?” That is, do you debate with us about the oneness of God, sincerity to Him, obedience, following His commands, and abandoning His prohibitions? And He is our Lord and your Lord The One who controls us and you, deserving of sincerity of divinity to Him alone, with no partner for Him. And for Us are our deeds, and for You are your deeds That is, we are innocent of you and what you worship, and you are innocent of us, as He said in the other verse: “And if they deny you, then say: To Me is my work, and to You is your work. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do.” And God the Almighty said: “But if they argue with you, then say: I have submitted myself to God, and so have those who follow me.” To the end of the verse. And God the Almighty said, informing about Abraham: “And his people argued with him. He said: Do you argue with me about God?” To the end of the verse. And God the Almighty said: Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord? The verse. And He said in this noble verse: And for Us are our deeds, and for You are your deeds, and We are for Him. We are sincere meaning we are innocent of you as you are innocent of us, and we are sincere to Him, meaning in worship and turning to Him. Then God Almighty denied their claim that Abraham and those who were mentioned after him of the prophets and the tribes were of their religion, either Judaism or Christianity, so He said: "Say: Are you more knowledgeable or is God?" meaning rather God knows best. He informed us that they were neither Jews nor Christians, as God Almighty said: "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim [submitting to God]. And he was not of the polytheists" and the verse that follows it. And His statement: And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God? Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: They used to read in the Book of God that came to them that the religion is Islam and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God and that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the tribes were innocent of Judaism and Christianity, so they bore witness to that for God, and they acknowledged it for themselves for God, so they concealed God's testimony to them regarding that. His statement: And God is not unaware of what you do is a severe threat and warning, meaning that His knowledge encompasses your knowledge and He will reward you for it. Then the Almighty said: That is a nation that has passed on, meaning that it has gone. Its is what it earned, and yours is what you have earned, meaning their is their deeds, and yours is yours. And you will not be asked about what they used to do. Your affiliation with them without following them will not benefit you. Do not be deceived by merely being related to them until you are obedient like them to the commands of God and follow His messengers who were sent as bearers of good tidings and warners. For whoever disbelieves in one prophet has disbelieved in all the messengers, especially the master of the prophets and the seal of the messengers and the messenger of the Lord of the worlds to all of mankind and jinn who are accountable. May the prayers and peace of God be upon him and upon all of God’s prophets, all of them.
