2:142: It was said: What is meant by the fools here are the polytheists of the Arabs, as Al-Zajjaj said. It was also said: The Jewish rabbis, as Mujahid said. It was also said: The hypocrites, as Al-Suddi said. The verse is general in all of these, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Naim told us, he heard Zuhair from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Bara’ may God be pleased with him: That the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) prayed towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, and he liked that his qiblah be towards the House, and that he prayed the first prayer he prayed was the afternoon prayer, and some people prayed with him, and a man who was praying with him came out and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing, and he said: I bear witness by God that I prayed with the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) towards Mecca, so they turned as they were towards the House, and those who died facing the qiblah before it was changed towards the House were men who were killed and we did not know what to say about them, so God revealed: “And God would not let your faith go to waste. Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful.” Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it from this source, and Muslim narrated it from another source, and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told me from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Bara’, who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) used to pray towards Jerusalem, and he would often look at the sky awaiting God’s command, so God revealed: We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the heaven, so We will surely turn you to it. A Muslim man said: We wish we knew the knowledge of those who died among us before we turned toward the qiblah, and how about our prayers toward the Holy House. So God revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. And the foolish people, who are the People of the Book, said: What has turned them away from the qiblah they used to face? So God revealed: The foolish people will say to the end of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Al-Hasan bin Atiyah told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had prayed toward the Holy House for sixteen months, and he loved to face toward the Kaaba, so God revealed: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque.” He said: So he faced toward the Kaaba, and the foolish people, who are the Jews, said: What has turned them away from the qiblah they used to face? So God revealed: “Say: To God belongs the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.” And Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God's Messenger (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) when he migrated to Medina, God ordered him to face Jerusalem, so the Jews rejoiced, so the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) faced it for about a month and a half. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) loved the direction of Abraham's qiblah, so he used to supplicate to God and look at the sky, so God the Almighty revealed: Then turn your faces toward it, meaning toward it. The Jews were suspicious of that and said: Why did He turn them away from the qiblah they were facing? So God revealed: "Say: To God belong the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path." Many hadiths have been narrated on this subject, and the gist of the matter is that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) was ordered to face the rock of Jerusalem, so he was in Mecca praying between the two corners, so the Kaaba would be in front of him while he was facing the rock of Jerusalem. When he migrated to Medina, it was impossible to combine them, so God ordered him to face Jerusalem, Ibn Abbas and the majority said, then these differed, was the order to do so by the Qur'an or by something else according to two opinions? Al-Qurtubi narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Ikrimah, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri: That the direction towards Jerusalem was by his own efforts, peace be upon him. What is meant is that the direction towards Jerusalem after his arrival, peace be upon him, in Medina, and the matter continued like that for several months, and he used to pray and implore a lot that he would be directed towards the Kaaba, which is the qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him. So that was answered and he was ordered to turn towards the ancient house. So the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, addressed the people and informed them of that. The first prayer he prayed towards it was the afternoon prayer, as mentioned in the two Sahihs, the narration of Al-Bara’. And it was mentioned by Al-Nasa’i from the narration of Abu Saeed bin Al-Mu’alla that it was the noon prayer, and he said: I and my companion were the first to pray towards the Kaaba. More than one of the interpreters and others mentioned that the change of the qiblah was revealed to the Messenger of God after he had prayed two rak’ahs of the noon prayer, and that was in the mosque of Bani Salamah, so it was called the mosque of the two qiblahs. And in the hadith of Nuwaylah bint Muslim: That the report of that came to them while they were praying the noon prayer, she said: So the men changed to the place of the women and the women changed to the place of the men. This was mentioned by Sheikh Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr Al-Namri. As for the people of Quba', but the report did not reach them until the dawn prayer of the second day, as it came in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn 'Umar may God be pleased with them both, that he said: While the people were in Quba' praying the dawn prayer, someone came to them and said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) received a Qur'an tonight and he was commanded to face the Ka'bah, so they faced it. Their faces were towards Ash-Sham, so they turned towards the Ka'bah. This is evidence that the abrogating ruling is not binding until after it is known, even if it was revealed and communicated beforehand, because they were not commanded to repeat the 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers, and God knows best. When this happened, some of the hypocrites, doubters and infidels among the Jews became suspicious, deviated from the right path, and became confused and doubtful, and they said: What has turned them away from the qiblah which they were facing? That is, they said: Why do these people sometimes face this and sometimes face that? So God revealed their answer in His saying: “Say: To God belong the East and the West,” meaning the rule, the management and the entire command belong to Him. So wherever you turn, there is the face of God. And Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the East or the West, but righteousness is of him who believes in God, meaning the whole affair is in obeying God’s commands. Wherever He directs us, we turn. Obedience is in obeying His command, even if we turn in different directions every day. We are His slaves and at His disposal, and His servants, wherever He directs us, we turn. And He, the Most High, has great care for His slave and Messenger Muhammad, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him and his nation, as He guided them to the Qiblah of Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, and made their turning to the Kaaba, built in His name alone, with no partner for Him, the most honorable of the houses of God on earth, as it is the building of Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him. For this reason He said: “Say: To God belong the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.” Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Ali bin Asim, on the authority of Husayn bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Ash’ath, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, meaning regarding the People of the Book: “They do not envy us for anything as much as they envy us for Friday, to which God has guided us and from which they have gone astray, and for the Qiblah, to which God has guided us and from which they have gone astray, and for our saying behind the imam: ‘Amen.’” And the Almighty said: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. The Almighty says: We only turned you to the Qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him, and chose it for you to make you the best of the nations so that you will be witnesses over the nations on the Day of Resurrection, because everyone acknowledges your virtue. The middle here means the best, and the best, as it is said: Quraysh is the middle of the Arabs in lineage and home, meaning the best of them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the middle among his people, meaning the most honorable of them in lineage, and from this is the middle prayer which is the best of the prayers, which is the afternoon prayer, as proven in the Sahihs and other books. And when God made this nation the middle, He distinguished it with the most perfect laws, the most correct methods, and the clearest doctrines, as the Almighty said: “He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty - the religion of your father Abraham. He named you Muslims before and in this, that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people.” And Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us from Al-A’mash from Abu Salih from Abu Sa’id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Noah will be called on the Day of Resurrection. The Resurrection, and it will be said to him: Did you deliver the message? He will say: Yes. His people will be called and it will be said to them: Did he deliver it to you? They will say: No warner came to us, and no one came to us. It will be said to Nuh 71:Who will bear witness for you? He will say: Muhammad and his nation. He said: This is what God said: {And thus We have made you a just community}. He said: The middle way is justice. So you will be called and you will bear witness for him that you delivered the message, then I will bear witness against you. Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A'mash. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, Al-A'mash told us on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Prophet will come on the Day of Resurrection with two men or more than that. His people will be called and it will be said: Did this man deliver the message to you? They will say: No. It will be said to him: Did you deliver the message to your people? He will say: Yes. It will be said: Who will bear witness for you? He will say: Muhammad and his nation. Muhammad and his nation will be called and it will be said to them: Did this man deliver the message to his people? They will say: Yes. It will be said: What is your knowledge? They will say: Our Prophet came to us and informed us that the Messengers have conveyed the message.” This is what the Almighty said: And thus We have made you a just community, meaning: just, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you. Ahmad also said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Almighty’s statement: And thus We have made you a just community, he said: just. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Abd Al-Wahid bin Ziyad from Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i from Al-Mughirah bin Utaybah bin Nabas, a scribe for us told me from Jabir bin Abdullah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “My nation and I will be on a hill on the Day of Resurrection, overlooking the creation. There is no one among the people who does not wish that he was one of us, and there is no prophet who his people denied except that we bear witness that he has conveyed the message of his Lord, may He be glorified and exalted.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak and Ibn Mardawayh also, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Mus’ab bin Thabit from Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi from Jabir bin Abd God said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) attended a funeral in Banu Maslamah and I was next to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Some of them said: By God, O Messenger of God, what a good man he was! He was chaste and a Muslim and... They spoke well of him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You are as you say. The man said: God knows what is hidden, but as for what we saw from him, that is it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is due, it is due. Then he attended a funeral in Banu Haritha and I was next to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Some of them said: O Messenger of God, what a bad man he was if he spoke harshly. They spoke ill of him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to some of them: You are as you say. The man said: God knows what is hidden, but as for what we saw from him, that is it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is due. Mus`ab ibn Thabit said: Then Muhammad ibn Ka`b said to us: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke the truth. Then he recited: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. Then Al-Hakim said: This is a sound chain of transmission, although they did not include it. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus ibn Muhammad told us: Dawud ibn Abi Al-Furat told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Buraydah, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, that he said: I came to Madinah and found it a disease had broken out there, and they were dying a terrible death. So I sat with Umar ibn Al-Khattab, and a funeral passed by him, and he praised its owner, so he said: It is due, it is due. Then another passed by and he spoke ill of it, so Umar said: It is due. Abu Al-Aswad said: It is not due, O Commander of the Faithful. He said: I said as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Any Muslim for whom four people testify to his goodness, God will admit him to Paradise. We said: And three? He said: And three? We said: And two? He said: And two. Then we did not ask him about one. And this is how Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Al-Furat. Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Yahya told us, Abu Qilabah al-Raqashi told us, Abu al-Walid told us, Nafi’ ibn Umar told us, Umayyah ibn Safwan told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhair al-Thaqafi, on the authority of his father, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about prophecy: ‘You will soon know the best of you from the worst of you.’ They said: ‘How, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘With good praise and bad praise. You are God’s witnesses on earth.’” It was narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, and Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, Abd al-Malik ibn Umar, and Shuraih on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, on his authority. And the Almighty said: “And We did not make the Qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom God has guided.” God the Almighty says: We only prescribed for you, O Muhammad, to face first toward the Holy House, then We turned you away from it to the Kaaba, so that the state of those who follow you and obey you and face with you wherever you face would be made clear, from those who turn back on their heels, that is, apostatize from their religion, even though this act, which is turning the face from the Holy House to the Kaaba, is great in the souls except for those whose hearts God has guided and who are certain of the truth of the Messenger, and that everything he brought is the truth in which there is no doubt, and that God does what He wills and decrees what He wills, so He has the right to charge His servants with whatever He wills and abrogate whatever He wills, and He has complete wisdom and conclusive proof in all of that, unlike those in whose hearts is disease, for whenever a matter occurs, it causes them doubt, just as those who believe become certain and believe, as God the Almighty said: “And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ But as for those who believe, And it increased their faith, and they rejoiced. And as for those in whose hearts is disease, it increased their uncleanness upon their uncleanness.” And God Almighty said: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss. For this reason, those who remained steadfast in believing in the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and following him in that and heading where God commanded them without doubt or suspicion were among the leaders of the Companions. Some of them went to the extent that the first of the Muhajireen and Ansar were those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs. Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation of this verse: Musaddad told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: While the people were praying the dawn prayer in the Quba Mosque, a man came and said: The Qur’an has been revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he has been commanded to face the Kaaba, so face it. So they headed towards the Kaaba. Muslim narrated it from another source on the authority of Ibn Umar, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan Al-Thawri, and he has that they were bowing and then turned towards the Kaaba while they were bowing. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, similarly. This indicates the perfection of their obedience to God and His Messenger and their submission to the commands of God Almighty, may God be pleased with them all. And his saying: And God would not let your faith be lost meaning that your prayers towards the Holy House before that would not have been lost in the reward of God. And in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i on the authority of al-Baraa’ he said: A group of people died who used to pray towards the Holy House, so the people said: What is their situation in that? Then God revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas and authenticated it. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And God would never let your faith go to waste, meaning in the first Qiblah and your belief in your Prophet and following him to the other Qiblah, meaning that He would give you the reward for both. Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: And God would never let your faith go to waste, meaning that God would never let Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, go to waste with him wherever he went. Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful. In the Sahih, it is reported that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a woman from the captives who had been separated from her child. Whenever she found a child from the captives, she would take him and hold him to her chest while she was going around to watch her child. When she found him, she hugged him to her and breastfed him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you think that this woman would throw her child into the fire when she is able not to throw him? They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: By God, God is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child.
2:143: It was said: What is meant by the fools here are the polytheists of the Arabs, as Al-Zajjaj said. It was also said: The Jewish rabbis, as Mujahid said. It was also said: The hypocrites, as Al-Suddi said. The verse is general in all of these, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Naim told us, he heard Zuhair from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Bara’ may God be pleased with him: That the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) prayed towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, and he liked that his qiblah be towards the House, and that he prayed the first prayer he prayed was the afternoon prayer, and some people prayed with him, and a man who was praying with him came out and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing, and he said: I bear witness by God that I prayed with the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) towards Mecca, so they turned as they were towards the House, and those who died facing the qiblah before it was changed towards the House were men who were killed and we did not know what to say about them, so God revealed: “And God would not let your faith go to waste. Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful.” Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it from this source, and Muslim narrated it from another source, and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told me from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Bara’, who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) used to pray towards Jerusalem, and he would often look at the sky awaiting God’s command, so God revealed: We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the heaven, so We will surely turn you to it. A Muslim man said: We wish we knew the knowledge of those who died among us before we turned toward the qiblah, and how about our prayers toward the Holy House. So God revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. And the foolish people, who are the People of the Book, said: What has turned them away from the qiblah they used to face? So God revealed: The foolish people will say to the end of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Al-Hasan bin Atiyah told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had prayed toward the Holy House for sixteen months, and he loved to face toward the Kaaba, so God revealed: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque.” He said: So he faced toward the Kaaba, and the foolish people, who are the Jews, said: What has turned them away from the qiblah they used to face? So God revealed: “Say: To God belongs the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.” And Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God's Messenger (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) when he migrated to Medina, God ordered him to face Jerusalem, so the Jews rejoiced, so the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) faced it for about a month and a half. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) loved the direction of Abraham's qiblah, so he used to supplicate to God and look at the sky, so God the Almighty revealed: Then turn your faces toward it, meaning toward it. The Jews were suspicious of that and said: Why did He turn them away from the qiblah they were facing? So God revealed: "Say: To God belong the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path." Many hadiths have been narrated on this subject, and the gist of the matter is that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) was ordered to face the rock of Jerusalem, so he was in Mecca praying between the two corners, so the Kaaba would be in front of him while he was facing the rock of Jerusalem. When he migrated to Medina, it was impossible to combine them, so God ordered him to face Jerusalem, Ibn Abbas and the majority said, then these differed, was the order to do so by the Qur'an or by something else according to two opinions? Al-Qurtubi narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Ikrimah, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri: That the direction towards Jerusalem was by his own efforts, peace be upon him. What is meant is that the direction towards Jerusalem after his arrival, peace be upon him, in Medina, and the matter continued like that for several months, and he used to pray and implore a lot that he would be directed towards the Kaaba, which is the qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him. So that was answered and he was ordered to turn towards the ancient house. So the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, addressed the people and informed them of that. The first prayer he prayed towards it was the afternoon prayer, as mentioned in the two Sahihs, the narration of Al-Bara’. And it was mentioned by Al-Nasa’i from the narration of Abu Saeed bin Al-Mu’alla that it was the noon prayer, and he said: I and my companion were the first to pray towards the Kaaba. More than one of the interpreters and others mentioned that the change of the qiblah was revealed to the Messenger of God after he had prayed two rak’ahs of the noon prayer, and that was in the mosque of Bani Salamah, so it was called the mosque of the two qiblahs. And in the hadith of Nuwaylah bint Muslim: That the report of that came to them while they were praying the noon prayer, she said: So the men changed to the place of the women and the women changed to the place of the men. This was mentioned by Sheikh Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr Al-Namri. As for the people of Quba', but the report did not reach them until the dawn prayer of the second day, as it came in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn 'Umar may God be pleased with them both, that he said: While the people were in Quba' praying the dawn prayer, someone came to them and said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) received a Qur'an tonight and he was commanded to face the Ka'bah, so they faced it. Their faces were towards Ash-Sham, so they turned towards the Ka'bah. This is evidence that the abrogating ruling is not binding until after it is known, even if it was revealed and communicated beforehand, because they were not commanded to repeat the 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers, and God knows best. When this happened, some of the hypocrites, doubters and infidels among the Jews became suspicious, deviated from the right path, and became confused and doubtful, and they said: What has turned them away from the qiblah which they were facing? That is, they said: Why do these people sometimes face this and sometimes face that? So God revealed their answer in His saying: “Say: To God belong the East and the West,” meaning the rule, the management and the entire command belong to Him. So wherever you turn, there is the face of God. And Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the East or the West, but righteousness is of him who believes in God, meaning the whole affair is in obeying God’s commands. Wherever He directs us, we turn. Obedience is in obeying His command, even if we turn in different directions every day. We are His slaves and at His disposal, and His servants, wherever He directs us, we turn. And He, the Most High, has great care for His slave and Messenger Muhammad, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him and his nation, as He guided them to the Qiblah of Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, and made their turning to the Kaaba, built in His name alone, with no partner for Him, the most honorable of the houses of God on earth, as it is the building of Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him. For this reason He said: “Say: To God belong the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.” Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Ali bin Asim, on the authority of Husayn bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Ash’ath, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, meaning regarding the People of the Book: “They do not envy us for anything as much as they envy us for Friday, to which God has guided us and from which they have gone astray, and for the Qiblah, to which God has guided us and from which they have gone astray, and for our saying behind the imam: ‘Amen.’” And the Almighty said: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. The Almighty says: We only turned you to the Qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him, and chose it for you to make you the best of the nations so that you will be witnesses over the nations on the Day of Resurrection, because everyone acknowledges your virtue. The middle here means the best, and the best, as it is said: Quraysh is the middle of the Arabs in lineage and home, meaning the best of them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the middle among his people, meaning the most honorable of them in lineage, and from this is the middle prayer which is the best of the prayers, which is the afternoon prayer, as proven in the Sahihs and other books. And when God made this nation the middle, He distinguished it with the most perfect laws, the most correct methods, and the clearest doctrines, as the Almighty said: “He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty - the religion of your father Abraham. He named you Muslims before and in this, that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people.” And Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us from Al-A’mash from Abu Salih from Abu Sa’id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Noah will be called on the Day of Resurrection. The Resurrection, and it will be said to him: Did you deliver the message? He will say: Yes. His people will be called and it will be said to them: Did he deliver it to you? They will say: No warner came to us, and no one came to us. It will be said to Nuh 71:Who will bear witness for you? He will say: Muhammad and his nation. He said: This is what God said: {And thus We have made you a just community}. He said: The middle way is justice. So you will be called and you will bear witness for him that you delivered the message, then I will bear witness against you. Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A'mash. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, Al-A'mash told us on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Prophet will come on the Day of Resurrection with two men or more than that. His people will be called and it will be said: Did this man deliver the message to you? They will say: No. It will be said to him: Did you deliver the message to your people? He will say: Yes. It will be said: Who will bear witness for you? He will say: Muhammad and his nation. Muhammad and his nation will be called and it will be said to them: Did this man deliver the message to his people? They will say: Yes. It will be said: What is your knowledge? They will say: Our Prophet came to us and informed us that the Messengers have conveyed the message.” This is what the Almighty said: And thus We have made you a just community, meaning: just, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you. Ahmad also said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Almighty’s statement: And thus We have made you a just community, he said: just. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Abd Al-Wahid bin Ziyad from Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i from Al-Mughirah bin Utaybah bin Nabas, a scribe for us told me from Jabir bin Abdullah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “My nation and I will be on a hill on the Day of Resurrection, overlooking the creation. There is no one among the people who does not wish that he was one of us, and there is no prophet who his people denied except that we bear witness that he has conveyed the message of his Lord, may He be glorified and exalted.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak and Ibn Mardawayh also, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Mus’ab bin Thabit from Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi from Jabir bin Abd God said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) attended a funeral in Banu Maslamah and I was next to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Some of them said: By God, O Messenger of God, what a good man he was! He was chaste and a Muslim and... They spoke well of him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You are as you say. The man said: God knows what is hidden, but as for what we saw from him, that is it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is due, it is due. Then he attended a funeral in Banu Haritha and I was next to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Some of them said: O Messenger of God, what a bad man he was if he spoke harshly. They spoke ill of him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to some of them: You are as you say. The man said: God knows what is hidden, but as for what we saw from him, that is it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is due. Mus`ab ibn Thabit said: Then Muhammad ibn Ka`b said to us: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke the truth. Then he recited: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. Abu Al-Aswad said: It is not due, O Commander of the Faithful. He said: I said as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Any Muslim for whom four people testify to his goodness, God will admit him to Paradise. We said: And three? He said: And three? We said: And two? He said: And two. Then we did not ask him about one. And this is how Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Al-Furat. 2:144: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The first thing that was abrogated from the Qur’an was the qiblah, and that was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina and most of its people were Jews, so God commanded him to face Jerusalem. The Jews were happy, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced it for a few months, and he loved the qiblah of Abraham, so he would call to God and look at the sky, so God revealed: We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven until His saying: So turn your faces toward it. The Jews were suspicious of that and said: “What has turned them away from the qiblah which they were facing? Say: To God belongs the East and the West.” And He said: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. And God the Most High said: And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn on his heels. And Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Al-Qasim Al-Umari on the authority of his uncle Ubaidullah bin Umar on the authority of Dawud bin Al-Hussain on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his prayer facing Jerusalem, he would raise his head toward the sky, so God revealed: “So We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram,” toward the Kaaba, toward the gutter, which Gabriel, peace be upon him, led in prayer. Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Ata’, on the authority of Yahya ibn Qamtah, who said: I saw Abdullah ibn Amr sitting in al-Masjid al-Haram facing the gutter, and he recited this verse: So We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased, he said toward the gutter of the Kaaba. Then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, but they did not narrate it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Arafah, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Ata’, on his authority. And so said another, and it is one of the two sayings of Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him, that the purpose is to hit the Kaaba itself, and the other saying, and the majority are of the opinion, is that what is meant is facing it, as Al-Hakim narrated from the hadith of Muhammad bin Ishaq from Umair bin Ziyad Al-Kindi from Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, Turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. He said, The direction is before it. Then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. This is the saying of Abu Al-Aliyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and others. And as mentioned previously in the other hadith, Whatever is between the east and the west is the qiblah. Al-Qurtubi said: Ibn Jurayj narrated from Ata’ from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The House is the qiblah for the people of the mosque, and the mosque is the qiblah for the people of the sanctuary, and the sanctuary is the qiblah for the people of the earth in its east and west from my nation.” Abu Na’im Al-Fadl bin Dukayn said: Zuhair narrated to us from Abu Ishaq from Al-Baraa’ that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) prayed towards the Holy House for sixteen months, or seventeen months, and he liked his qiblah towards the House? He prayed the afternoon prayer and some people prayed with him. A man who was praying with him came out and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing and said: I bear witness to God that I prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before Mecca. So they turned around as they were before the House. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of al-Bara’ who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, he prayed towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved to turn towards the Kaaba, so the verse Indeed We have seen the turning of your face, toward the heaven was revealed, so he turned towards the Kaaba. And al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id ibn al-Mu’alla who said: We used to go to the mosque during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we would pray in it. One day we passed by and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting on the pulpit, so I said: Something has happened, so I sat down, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: Indeed We have seen the turning of your face, toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased until he finished the verse, so I said to my companion: Come, let us bow two rak’ahs before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descends, so that we will be the first to pray, so we hid ourselves and prayed it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came down and prayed the noon prayer for the people that day. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: The first prayer that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards the Kaaba was the noon prayer, and it is the middle prayer. It is well-known that the first prayer that he prayed towards the Kaaba was the afternoon prayer, and for this reason the report from the people of Quba was delayed until the dawn prayer. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman Ibn Ahmad told us, Al-Husayn Ibn Ishaq Al-Tastari told us, Raja Ibn Muhammad Al-Saqti told us, Ishaq Ibn Idris told us, Ibrahim Ibn Ja`far told us, my father told me on the authority of his grandmother, Umm Abi Nuwaylah Bint Muslim, who said: We prayed the noon or afternoon prayer in the mosque of Bani Haritha, so we faced the mosque of Ilya and prayed two rak`ahs. Then someone came to tell us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had faced the Sacred House, so the women moved in the place of the men and the men in the place of the women, so we prayed the two remaining prostrations while facing the Sacred House. Then a man from Bani Haritha told me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those are men who believe in the unseen. Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad Ibn Ali Ibn Dahim narrated to us Ahmad bin Hazim narrated to us Malik bin Ismail Al-Nahdi narrated to us Qais narrated to us from Ziyad bin Alama from Ammarah bin Aws who said: While we were praying towards the Holy House and we were bowing, a caller called out at the door: The Qiblah has been changed to the Kaaba. He said: I bear witness that our Imam has deviated, so he and the men and boys turned while they were bowing towards the Kaaba. And His saying: And wherever you are, turn your faces towards it is an order from God the Almighty to face the Kaaba from all directions of the earth, east, west, north and south. Nothing is excluded from this except the voluntary prayer while travelling, for he prays it wherever his back and heart are directed towards the Kaaba. And likewise in the case of sword fighting, he prays in any case. And likewise, whoever is ignorant of the direction of the Qiblah prays according to his own effort even if he is mistaken in the matter itself, because God the Almighty does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. Question The Malikis have used this verse as evidence that the worshipper should look in front of him and not at the place of his prostration, as was stated by al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Abu Hanifa. The Malikis said, with his saying: Turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque, if he looked at the place of his prostration, he would need to do so by bowing, which is contrary to the perfection of standing. Some of them said: The worshipper should look at his chest while standing. Sharik al-Qadi said: While standing, he should look at the place of his prostration, as the majority of the group said, because it is more effective in submission and more emphatic in humility, and the hadith has been reported about it. As for while bowing, he should look at the place of his feet, while while prostrating, at the place of his nose, and while sitting, at his lap. And His statement: And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord, meaning, the Jews who denied your reception and your turning away from the Holy House, know that God Almighty will direct you to it with what is in their books from their prophets of the description and attribute of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation, and what God Almighty has singled him out with and honored him with of the great, complete Sharia, but the People of the Scripture conceal that among themselves out of envy, disbelief, and stubbornness, and for this reason God Almighty threatens them with His statement: And God is not unaware of what they do.
2:145: The Almighty tells about the disbelief of the Jews, their stubbornness, and their opposition to what they know about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that if he had established against them every proof of the truth of what he brought to them, they would not have followed him and abandoned their desires, as the Almighty said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them until they see the painful punishment. That is why He said here, And even if you brought to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your Qiblah. And His saying, And you will not follow their Qiblah, is a report of the intensity of the Messenger’s following of what God the Almighty commanded him to do, and that just as they adhere to their opinions and desires, he also adheres to God’s command, obedience to Him, and following what pleases Him, and that he does not follow their desires in all his circumstances, nor does he face Jerusalem because it is the Qiblah of the Jews, but rather that is by the command of God the Almighty. Then the Almighty warned against opposing the truth that the scholar knows to his desires, for the scholar’s proof is more correct than anyone else’s, and that is why He said, addressing the Messenger, and what is meant by that is the nation And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers.
2:146: God the Almighty tells us that the scholars of the People of the Book know the truth of what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought to them as one of them knows his own son, and the Arabs used to give an example of the truth of something with this, as stated in the hadith: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to a man with a young son of yours, ‘Is this your son?’ He said, ‘Yes, O Messenger of God, I bear witness to that.’ He said, ‘As for him, he will not harm you nor will he harm him.’” Al-Qurtubi said: It is narrated on the authority of Umar that he said to Abdullah bin Salam, ‘Do you know Muhammad as you know your son?’ He said, ‘Yes and more. The trustworthy one descended from the heavens to the trustworthy one on earth with his description, so I recognized him, and I do not know what happened to his mother.’ I said It may be that what is meant is, ‘They recognize him as they recognize their own sons,’ from among the sons of all people. No one would doubt or hesitate to recognize his son if he saw him from among the sons of all people. Then the Almighty informed us that despite this scientific verification and mastery, they conceal the truth, meaning they conceal from people what is in their books about the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they know. Then the Almighty confirmed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers and informed them that what the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought is the truth in which there is no doubt or suspicion, so He said: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.

2:148: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And to each is a direction towards which he turns, meaning by that the people of religions, he says that each tribe has a qiblah that they are pleased with, and the direction of God is where the believers turn. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The Jew has a direction towards which he turns, and the Christian has a direction towards which he turns, and He has guided you, O nation, to the qiblah which is the qiblah. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ata’, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas and As-Suddi something similar to this. Mujahid said in the other narration, and Al-Hasan ordered every people to pray towards the Kaaba. Ibn Abbas, Abu Ja’far Al-Baqir and Ibn Amir read: And for each is a direction towards which he turns. This verse is similar to the words of God Almighty: “To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had God willed, He would have made you one community, but that He might test you in what He has given you. So race to [do] good. To God is your return all together.” And He said here: “Wherever you may be, God will bring you all together. Indeed, God is over all things competent.” That is, He is able to gather you from the earth, even if your bodies and bodies are scattered.
2:149: This is a third command from God Almighty to face the Sacred Mosque from all parts of the earth. They differed about the wisdom of this repetition three times. It was said that it is an emphasis because it is the first abrogation that occurred in Islam, as stated by Ibn Abbas and others. It was said that it is rather revealed according to circumstances. The first command is for those who are watching the Kaaba, the second is for those who are in Mecca and are absent from it, and the third is for those who are in the rest of the countries. This is how Fakhr al-Din al-Razi explained it. Al-Qurtubi said: The first is for those who are in Mecca, the second is for those who are in the rest of the cities, and the third is for those who have traveled. Al-Qurtubi preferred this answer, and it was said: He only mentioned it because it is related to what came before or after it in the context. He said: First, We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased to His saying, “And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And God is not unaware of what they do.” So he mentioned in this context his response to his request and his command to the qiblah that he wanted to face and was pleased with. And he said in the second command, “And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And God is not unaware of what you do.” So he mentioned that it is the truth from God and his ascension to the first station, since it was in accordance with the pleasure of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he clarified that it is also the truth from God, who loves it and is pleased with it. And he mentioned in the third command the wisdom of cutting off the argument of the dissenters from the Jews who were making excuses by facing the Messenger toward their qiblah, and they knew from what was in their books that he would be turned toward the qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him, until The Kaaba, and likewise the polytheists of the Arabs lost their argument when the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was turned away from the qiblah of the Jews to the qiblah of Abraham, which is more honorable. They used to venerate the Kaaba and were amazed by the Messenger facing it. Other answers were given about the wisdom of repetition, and Al-Razi and others have elaborated on them, and God knows best. His statement, So that the people will have no argument against you, means the People of the Book, for they know that it is a characteristic of this nation to face the Kaaba, so if they lose that characteristic of it, they may use it as an argument against the Muslims, and so that they will not use it as an argument based on the Muslims’ agreement with them in facing Jerusalem. This is more evident. Abu Al-Aaliyah said, So that the people will have no argument against you, meaning the People of the Book when they said: Muhammad was turned toward the Kaaba. They said: The man longed for his father’s house and the religion of his people. Their argument against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was his turning to the Sacred House, that they said, he will return to our religion as he returned to our Qiblah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar to this was narrated from Mujahid, Ata’, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Qatadah and As-Suddi. These people said about His statement, Except those who did wrong among them, meaning the polytheists of Quraysh. Some of them presented the argument of the oppressors, which is refuted, that they said: This man claims that he is on the religion of Abraham, but he did not turn back from it. The answer is that God Almighty chose for him to face Jerusalem, first because of His wisdom in that, so he obeyed his Lord Almighty in that, then he turned him to the qiblah of Abraham, which is the Kaaba, so he complied with God’s command in that as well. He, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is obedient to God in all his circumstances, he does not deviate from God’s command for the blink of an eye, and his nation follows him. His saying, So do not fear them, but fear Me, means do not fear the likeness of the obstinate oppressors and single out fear for Me, for He is the One Who deserves to be feared. His saying, And that I may complete My favor upon you, is in apposition to so that people will have no argument against you, meaning, I may complete My favor upon you in what I have prescribed for you of facing the Kaaba, so that the Sharia may be completed for you from all its aspects. And that you may be guided, meaning to what the nations have gone astray from, We have guided you to it and made you special with it. For this reason, this nation is the most honorable and best of nations.

2:151: The Almighty reminds His believing servants of the blessings He bestowed upon them by sending the Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, reciting to them the clear verses of God, and purifying them, that is, cleansing them from the vices of morals, the filth of souls, and the actions of the Age of Ignorance, and bringing them out of darkness into the light and teaching them the Book, which is the Qur’an, and wisdom, which is the Sunnah, and teaching them what they did not know before. In the Age of Ignorance, they were ignorant people who used to be fools with their pure minds. Then, by the blessing of his message and the good fortune of his embassy, they moved to the state of saints and the qualities of scholars. They became the people with the deepest knowledge, the most pious of hearts, the least pretentious, and the most truthful in speech. God the Almighty said: God has conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them 1:13. He also condemned those who did not appreciate the value of this blessing, saying: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin? 1:13. Ibn Abbas said: By the favor of God, he meant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. For this reason, God urged the believers to acknowledge this favor and to respond to it by remembering and thanking Him. He said: “So remember Me, and I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.” 1:13. Mujahid said, in His statement: Just as We have sent among you a Messenger from among you, he means: Just as you did, so remember Me. Abdullah bin Wahb said: On the authority of Hisham bin Sa’d, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, that Moses, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, how can I thank You? His Lord said to him: “Remember Me and do not forget Me. If you remember Me, you have thanked Me, and if you forget Me, you have denied Me.” Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Suddi and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God remembers whoever remembers Him, increases his gratitude and punishes whoever disbelieves in Him. Some of the Salaf said about the words of God the Most High: Fear God as He should be feared: It means that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not denied. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Ammarah Al-Saydalani told us, Makhul Al-Azdi told us: I said to Ibn Umar: Do you think that the murderer, the drinker of alcohol, the thief and the adulterer remember God, and God the Most High said: Then remember Me, I will remember you? He said: If God remembers this one, God will remember him with His curse until he is silent. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said about the words: Then remember Me, I will remember you: He said: Remember Me in what I have enjoined upon you, and I will remember you in what I have enjoined upon you upon Myself. Saeed bin Jubair said: Remember Me with My obedience, and I will remember you with My forgiveness, and in another narration, with My mercy. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: Remember Me, and I will remember you, he said: God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. And in the authentic hadith: “God Almighty says: Whoever remembers Me to himself, I will remember him to Myself, and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I will remember him in an assembly better than it.” Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, said: O son of Adam, if you remember Me in yourself, I will remember you in Myself. If you remember Me in an assembly, I will remember you in an assembly of angels - or he said, in an assembly better than it - and if you come a handspan closer to Me, I will come a cubit closer to you, and if you come a cubit closer to Me, I will come a fathom closer to you, and if you come to Me walking, I will come to you running.” Its chain of transmission is authentic. Al-Bukhari included it on the authority of Qatada, and according to him Qatada said: God is closer in mercy, and His statement: And be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful is an order from God, the Almighty, to thank Him and promised more good for thanking Him, saying: “And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.” Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Fadala - a man from Qays - Abu Raja’ told us. Al-Attardi said: Imran bin Husayn came out to us wearing a silk cloak that we had never seen him wearing before or after that. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever God bestows a blessing upon, God loves to see the effect of His blessing on His creation. And Ruh said once: On His servant.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Ammarah Al-Saydalani told us, Makhul Al-Azdi told us: I said to Ibn Umar: Do you think that the murderer, the drinker of alcohol, the thief and the adulterer remember God, and God the Most High said: Then remember Me, I will remember you? He said: If God remembers this one, God will remember him with His curse until he is silent. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said about the words: Then remember Me, I will remember you: He said: Remember Me in what I have enjoined upon you, and I will remember you in what I have enjoined upon you upon Myself. Saeed bin Jubair said: Remember Me with My obedience, and I will remember you with My forgiveness, and in another narration, with My mercy. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: Remember Me, and I will remember you, he said: God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. And in the authentic hadith: “God Almighty says: Whoever remembers Me to himself, I will remember him to Myself, and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I will remember him in an assembly better than it.” Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, said: O son of Adam, if you remember Me in yourself, I will remember you in Myself. If you remember Me in an assembly, I will remember you in an assembly of angels - or he said, in an assembly better than it - and if you come a handspan closer to Me, I will come a cubit closer to you, and if you come a cubit closer to Me, I will come a fathom closer to you, and if you come to Me walking, I will come to you running.” Its chain of transmission is authentic. Al-Bukhari included it on the authority of Qatada, and according to him Qatada said: God is closer in mercy, and His statement: And be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful is an order from God, the Almighty, to thank Him and promised more good for thanking Him, saying: “And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.” Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Fadala - a man from Qays - Abu Raja’ told us. Al-Attardi said: Imran bin Husayn came out to us wearing a silk cloak that we had never seen him wearing before or after that. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever God bestows a blessing upon, God loves to see the effect of His blessing on His creation. And Ruh said once: On His servant.
2:153: When the Almighty proceeded from explaining the command to be grateful, He proceeded to explain patience, guidance, and seeking help through patience and prayer. The servant is either in a blessing, so he is grateful for it, or in a calamity, so he is patient with it, as stated in the hadith: “It is amazing for the believer that God does not decree for him a decree except that it is good for him: if he is granted ease, so he is grateful, it is good for him, and if he is afflicted with hardship, so he is patient, it is good for him.” The Almighty explained that the best means of assistance to bear calamities are patience and prayer, as stated previously in His statement: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive. In the hadith, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed by something, he would pray. Patience is of two types: patience in abstaining from forbidden things and sins, and patience in performing acts of obedience and devotion. The second type is more rewarding because it is the intended meaning. As for the third patience, which is patience in the face of calamities and misfortunes, this is also obligatory, like seeking forgiveness for faults, as Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Patience is of two types: patience for God with what He loves, even if it is difficult for the souls and bodies, and patience for God from what He hates, even if desires incline towards it. Whoever is like this is among the patient ones upon whom peace will be granted, God willing. Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin said: When God gathers the first and the last, a caller will call out, Where are the patient ones so that they may enter Paradise before the reckoning? He said: Then a group of people will stand up and the angels will meet them and say: Where are you going, O children of Adam? They will say: To Paradise. They will say: Before the reckoning? They will say: Yes. They will say: Who are you? They said: We are the patient ones. They said: What was your patience? They said: We were patient in obeying God and we were patient in avoiding disobeying God until God took us. They said: You are as you said, enter Paradise, for what is the best reward for the workers I said: And evidence for this is the saying of God Almighty: Only the patient will be given their reward without account. Saeed bin Jubair said: Patience is the servant’s acknowledgment to God of what he has done to him, and his seeking reward from God, hoping for His reward. And a man may be impatient while he is patient, and nothing is seen from him except patience. God the Almighty says: And say not of those who are killed in the way of God, ‘They are dead.’ Rather, they are alive. God the Almighty informs us that the martyrs are alive and provided for in their intermediate state, as it came in Sahih Muslim: The souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they take refuge in lamps suspended beneath the Throne. Then your Lord looked at them and said: What do you seek? They said: O our Lord, what do we seek, when You have given us what You have not given to any of Your creation? Then He returned to them with something similar. When they saw that they would not be left without being asked, they said: We want You to return us to the worldly home so that we may fight in Your cause until we are killed in Your cause once again - because of what they see of the reward of martyrdom - then the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, says: I have written that they will not return to it. In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Imam al-Shafi’i on the authority of Imam Malik on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b ibn Malik on the authority of his father, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The soul of the believer is a bird hanging from the trees of Paradise until God returns it to its body on the Day of Resurrection. This indicates that it also includes all believers, even though the martyrs have been specifically mentioned in the Qur’an as an honor, a sign of respect, and a sign of glorification.

2:155: God the Almighty told us that He tests His servants, that is, He examines and tests them, as He the Almighty said: And We will surely test you until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause of God] and the patient, and We will make evident your report. Sometimes with ease and sometimes with hardship such as fear and hunger, as He the Almighty said: So God made them taste the garment of hunger and fear. The hungry and the fearful both show that, and that is why He said the garment of hunger and fear. And He said here: with a little fear and hunger, that is, with a little of that, and a loss of wealth, that is, the loss of some of it, and lives, such as the death of friends, relatives, and loved ones, and fruits, that is, the gardens and farms do not yield as they usually do. Some of the Salaf said: Some of the palm trees would only bear fruit once. All of this and the like are ways by which God tests His servants. Whoever is patient, He will reward him, and whoever despairs, He will punish him. That is why God the Almighty said: And give good tidings to the patient. Some commentators have related that what is meant by fear here is the fear of God, and by hunger, fasting in Ramadan, and by loss of wealth, zakat, and by souls, diseases, and by fruits, children. There is a view on this, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty explained who are the patient ones He thanked, saying: Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, ‘Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.’ That is, they consoled themselves with this saying for what befell them and knew that they belong to God and that He disposes of His servants as He wills, and they knew that not an atom’s weight will be lost with Him on the Day of Resurrection. That caused them to acknowledge that they are His servants and that they will return to Him in the Hereafter. That is why God the Almighty informed them of what He gave them for that, saying: On them are blessings from their Lord and mercy. That is, praise from God for them. Saeed bin Jubair said: That is, security from punishment. And those are the ones who are guided. The Commander of the Faithful, Omar bin Al-Khattab, said: What excellent just men and what excellent bonus. Upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy. These are the two just men. And those are the ones who are guided. This bonus is what is placed between the two just men and it is an increase in the burden. Likewise, these men were given their reward and were given an increase as well. There are many hadiths that have been narrated about the reward for seeking God’s help, which is to say, Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un We belong to God and to Him we shall return when faced with calamities. Among them is what Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Laith, meaning Ibn Sa’d, narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Usamah ibn al-Haad, from Amr ibn Abi Amr, from al-Muttalib, from Umm Salamah, who said: Abu Salamah came to me one day from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a statement that made me happy. He said: “No Muslim is afflicted with a calamity and seeks God’s help upon his calamity and then says, ‘O God, reward me for my calamity and replace it with something better,’ except that that will be done to him.” Umm Salamah said: So I memorized that from him, and when Abu Salamah died, I sought God’s help and said, ‘O God, reward me for my calamity and replace it with something better.’ Then I came to my senses and said, ‘How can I find someone better than Abu Salamah?’ When my waiting period was over, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked permission to see me while I was tanning a hide for myself. I washed my hands of the qaz and gave him permission. I placed for him a leather cushion stuffed with palm fibers, and he sat on it and proposed to me. When he finished speaking, I said: O Messenger of God, it is not that I do not desire you, but I am a woman who is extremely jealous and I fear that you will see something in me that will punish me. I am a woman who has reached old age and I have children. He said: As for what you mentioned about jealousy, God Almighty will remove it from you. As for what you mentioned about old age, the same thing that happened to me happened to you. As for what you mentioned about children, your children are my children. She said: She surrendered to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her. Umm Salamah then said: God replaced Abu Salamah with someone better than him: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In Sahih Muslim, she said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no servant who is afflicted with a calamity and says: ‘To God we belong and to Him we shall return.’ O God, reward me for my calamity and replace it for me with something better than it, except that God will reward him for his calamity and replace it for him with something better than it.” She said: When Abu Salamah died, I said: As the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded me, and God replaced him with someone better than him: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid and Ibad bin Ibad told us: Hisham bin Abi Hisham told us: Ibad bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Fatimah bint al-Husayn, on the authority of her father, al-Husayn bin Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no Muslim man or woman who is afflicted with a calamity and remembers it, even if it happened a long time ago - and Ibad said it happened a long time ago - and says ‘I seek refuge in God from God,’ but God renews it for him and gives him a reward like the reward of the day he was afflicted.” Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Hisham bin Ziyad on the authority of his mother on the authority of Fatimah bint al-Husayn on the authority of her father. Ismail bin Aliyah and Yazid bin Harun narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Ziyad on the authority of his father thus on the authority of Fatimah on the authority of her father. Imam Ahmad said: I heard Yahya bin Ishaq al-Silhini, I heard Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Abu Sinan, who said: I buried a son of mine and while I was in the grave, Abu Talhah - meaning al-Khawlani - took me by the hand and took me out and said to me: Shall I not give you good report? I said: Yes. He said: Ad-Dahhak bin Abd al-Rahman bin Awzab told me on the authority of Abu Musa who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God said: O Angel of Death, have you taken the son of My servant? Have you taken the joy of his eyes and the fruit of his heart? He said: Yes. He said: What did he say? He said: He praised You and sought refuge in You. He said: Build a house for him in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Ishaq on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak and mentioned it. And thus Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Suwaid bin Nasr on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak on his authority, and he said: It is good and strange. Abu Sinan’s name is Isa bin Sinan.
