In Sahih Muslim, she said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no servant who is afflicted with a calamity and says: ‘To God we belong and to Him we shall return.’ O God, reward me for my calamity and replace it for me with something better than it, except that God will reward him for his calamity and replace it for him with something better than it.” She said: When Abu Salamah died, I said: As the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded me, and God replaced him with someone better than him: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid and Ibad bin Ibad told us: Hisham bin Abi Hisham told us: Ibad bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Fatimah bint al-Husayn, on the authority of her father, al-Husayn bin Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no Muslim man or woman who is afflicted with a calamity and remembers it, even if it happened a long time ago - and Ibad said it happened a long time ago - and says ‘I seek refuge in God from God,’ but God renews it for him and gives him a reward like the reward of the day he was afflicted.” Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Hisham bin Ziyad on the authority of his mother on the authority of Fatimah bint al-Husayn on the authority of her father. Ismail bin Aliyah and Yazid bin Harun narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Ziyad on the authority of his father thus on the authority of Fatimah on the authority of her father. Imam Ahmad said: I heard Yahya bin Ishaq al-Silhini, I heard Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Abu Sinan, who said: I buried a son of mine and while I was in the grave, Abu Talhah - meaning al-Khawlani - took me by the hand and took me out and said to me: Shall I not give you good report? I said: Yes. He said: Ad-Dahhak bin Abd al-Rahman bin Awzab told me on the authority of Abu Musa who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God said: O Angel of Death, have you taken the son of My servant? Have you taken the joy of his eyes and the fruit of his heart? He said: Yes. He said: What did he say? He said: He praised You and sought refuge in You. He said: Build a house for him in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Ishaq on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak and mentioned it. And thus Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Suwaid bin Nasr on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak on his authority, and he said: It is good and strange. Abu Sinan’s name is Isa bin Sinan.
2:158: Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman bin Dawud al-Hashimi narrated to us, Ibraaheem bin Saad narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha, he said: I said, What do you think of the statement of God the Most High: "Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs Umrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them"? I said: By God, there is no blame upon anyone for not walking between them. Aisha said, What a bad thing you have said, my nephew! If it had been as I interpreted it, there would have been no blame upon him for not walking between them. However, it was revealed because the Ansar, before they converted to Islam, used to perform the ritual of Ihram at the tyrant Manat, which they used to worship near al-Mushallal. Some of its people were reluctant to walk between as-Safa and al-Marwah. So they asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about that and they said: O Messenger of God, we were reluctant to walk between as-Safa and al-Marwah during the pre-Islamic era. Then God the Almighty revealed: "Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs Umrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them." Aisha said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made it an ordinance to walk between them, so no one should neglect walking between them. They both included it in the two Sahihs. In a narration on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: So I narrated this hadith to Abu Bakr bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham. He said: This is not what I had heard of, and I heard men of knowledge say: The people - except for those whom Aisha mentioned - used to say: Our walking between these two stones is from the practice of the Age of Ignorance. Others from the Ansar said: We were only commanded to walk around the House, and we were not commanded to walk between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. Then God the Almighty revealed: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. Abu Bakr bin Abd Al-Rahman said: Perhaps it was revealed about these and those. Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Malik on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha in a similar manner. Then Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim bin Sulayman, who said: I asked Anas about Safa and Marwa. He said: We used to think that they were from the pre-Islamic era, but when Islam came, we refrained from them, so God Almighty revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his interpretation on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The devils used to separate Safa and Marwa all night long, and there were gods between them. When Islam came, they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about circumambulating between them, so this verse was revealed. Al-Sha’bi said: Isaf and Na’ilah were on Al-Safa and Na’ilah was on Al-Marwah, and they used to touch them. After Islam, they were embarrassed to circumambulate between them, so this verse was revealed. I said Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Book of the Biography that Isaf and Na’ilah were two human beings, so they committed adultery inside the Ka’bah and turned into two stones, so the Quraysh set them up facing the Ka’bah for people to learn from. When their time had passed, they were enslaved, then moved to Al-Safa and Al-Marwah, and they were set up there, so whoever circumambulated Al-Safa and Al-Marwah would touch them. For this reason, Abu Talib said in his famous poem: Where the Ash'aris dismount their camels at the place where the torrents of Isaf and Na'il meet. In Sahih Muslim, from the long hadith of Jabir, it says that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his circumambulation of the House, he returned to the corner and touched it, then he exited from the door of Safa while saying, Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. Then he said, I begin with what God began with. In the narration of al-Nasa’i, Begin with what God began with. Imam Ahmad said: Shuraih told us, Abdullah bin al-Mu’ammil told us, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaibah, on the authority of Habibah bint Abi Tajra’ah, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulating between Safa and Marwa, and the people were in front of him, and he was behind them, and he was walking, until I could see his knees from the intensity of his walking, and his garment was spinning around him, and he was saying, Strive, for God has prescribed walking for you. Then Imam Ahmad narrated it from Abd al-Razzaq: Muammar told us, on the authority of Wasil, the freed slave of Abu Uyaynah, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaydah, on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaibah, that a woman told her that she heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, between Safa and Marwa saying, Sa’i has been prescribed for you, so strive. This hadith was used as evidence for the school of thought of those who… He believes that walking between Safa and Marwa is a pillar of Hajj, as is the doctrine of Al-Shafi’i and those who agreed with him, and a narration from Ahmad, which is the well-known opinion from Malik. It was said that it is obligatory and not a pillar, so if he leaves it intentionally or unintentionally, he must make up for it with blood money, and this is a narration from Ahmad and a group says the same. It was said rather it is recommended, and Abu Hanifa, Al-Thawri, Al-Sha’bi and Ibn Sirin went to it, and it was narrated from Anas, Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas, and it was reported from Malik in Al-Utbiyyah. Al-Qurtubi said: They used as evidence the words of God Almighty: And whoever volunteers good and the first opinion is more likely because he, peace be upon him, circumambulated between them and said: So that you may learn from me your rituals. So everything he did in that pilgrimage is obligatory and must be done in Hajj, except what is excluded by evidence, and God knows best. His words, peace be upon him, Strive, for God has prescribed striving for you have been presented, for God Almighty has made clear that circumambulating between Safa and Marwa is one of the rituals of God, that is, what God Almighty prescribed for Abraham in the rituals of Hajj. It was presented in the hadith of Ibn Abbas that the origin of that is taken from Hajar’s circumambulation and her going back and forth between Safa and Marwa in search of water for her son when their water ran out and their provisions when he left them. Abraham, peace be upon him, was there, and no one was with them. When she feared for her son there, and they ran out of what they had, she stood up seeking help from God, the Almighty, and she kept going back and forth in this honorable spot between Safa and Marwa, humbled, fearful, anxious, compelled, and needy before God, the Almighty, until God removed her distress, comforted her loneliness, relieved her hardship, and caused Zamzam to spring forth for her, whose water is food that nourishes, and a cure for illness. The one who strives between them should be mindful of his poverty, humiliation, and need of God, in guiding his heart, improving his condition, and forgiving his sins. He should seek refuge in God, the Almighty, to relieve his shortcomings and faults, and to guide him to the straight path, and to make him steadfast on it until his death, and to transform him from his state of sins and transgressions to a state of perfection, forgiveness, rectitude, and uprightness, as He did with Hajar, peace be upon her. And his saying, And whoever volunteers good, it was said that he increased his circumambulation between them according to what is obligatory, an eighth and a ninth, and so on. And it was said that he circumambulates between them in a voluntary Hajj or a voluntary Umrah. And it was said that what is meant is a voluntary good in all acts of worship. This was narrated by Al-Razi, and the third was attributed to Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and God knows best. And his saying, Then God is Appreciative and Knowing, meaning that He rewards for little with much, and is Knowing of the extent of the reward, so He does not withhold reward from anyone. “He does not wrong by as much as an atom’s weight. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.”
2:159: This is a severe warning to those who conceal what the Messengers brought of clear evidence of the correct objectives, and the guidance that benefits the hearts after what God Almighty made clear to His servants from His books that He sent down to His Messengers. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It was revealed about the People of the Book, they concealed the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then He informed that everything curses them for their actions, so just as the scholar is sought forgiveness for by everything, even the fish in the water, and the bird in the air, these are unlike the scholars, so God curses them and those who curse curse them. It was reported in the hadith with chains of transmission that strengthen each other on the authority of Abu Hurairah and others that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is asked about knowledge and conceals it, will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire. What is in the Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurairah is that he said: If it were not for a verse in the Book of God, I would not have told anyone anything Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance the verse, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Arfa narrated to us, Ammar bin Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Zadhan Abi Amr, on the authority of Al-Bara bin Azib, who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at a funeral, and he said: “The unbeliever will be struck between his eyes, and every creature will hear it except the two heavy beasts, and every creature that hears his voice will curse him. This is what God Almighty said: ‘Those are the ones whom God curses and those who curse them’ meaning the creatures of the earth.” Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Sabah, on the authority of Aamer bin Muhammad, and Ata bin Abi Rabah said: Every creature, the jinn, and mankind. Mujahid said: When the earth becomes barren, the animals will say: This is because of the sinners of the sons of Adam. God cursed the sinners of the sons of Adam. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Qatadah said: ‘And those who curse them’ meaning the angels and the believers curse them. It was mentioned in the hadith that everything seeks forgiveness for the scholar, even the whales in the sea. It was mentioned in this verse that the one who conceals knowledge will be cursed by God, the angels, and the people. They all, and the cursers as well, are all eloquent and foreign, either in the language of speech or the situation, that if he had a mind and on the Day of Resurrection, and God knows best. Then God the Most High excluded from these those who repented to Him, saying: Except for those who repent, amend, and make clear meaning, they returned from what they were doing, amended their actions, and made clear to the people what they were concealing. For them I will turn in forgiveness, and I am the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful. This indicates that the one who calls to disbelief or innovation, if he repents to God, God will turn in forgiveness for him. It has been reported that previous nations did not accept repentance from such people among them, but this is from the law of the Prophet of Repentance and the Prophet of Mercy, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him. Then God the Most High informed about those who disbelieved in Him and their condition continued until their death, that “upon them is the curse of God and of the angels and of mankind, all together. They will abide therein” meaning in the curse that accompanies them until the Day of Resurrection, then the companionship, so they are in the fire of Hell, in which the punishment will not be lightened for them meaning it will not decrease from what they are in nor will they be reprieved meaning it will not change for them for a single hour or cease, rather it is continuous and permanent, so we seek refuge in God from that. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Qatada said that the unbeliever will be brought to the stand on the Day of Resurrection and God will curse him, then the angels will curse him, then all of the people will curse him. Chapter There is no disagreement about the permissibility of cursing the infidels. Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and the imams who came after him, cursed the infidels in the Qunut and other prayers. As for the specific infidel, a group of scholars have said that he should not be cursed because we do not know how God will seal him. Some of them used as evidence the verse, Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - upon them is the curse of God and of the angels and of the people, all together. Another group said: Rather, it is permissible to curse the specific infidel. The jurist Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi al-Maliki chose this view, but he used as evidence a hadith that is weak. Others used as evidence the words of the Prophet, peace be upon him, in the story of the one who was brought drunk and he was flogged. A man, may God curse him, said: How often he is brought. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: Do not curse him, for he loves God and His Messenger. This indicates that whoever does not love God and His Messenger is cursed, and God knows best.

Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and the imams who came after him, cursed the infidels in the Qunut and other prayers. As for the specific infidel, a group of scholars have said that he should not be cursed because we do not know how God will seal him. Some of them used as evidence the verse, Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - upon them is the curse of God and of the angels and of the people, all together. Another group said: Rather, it is permissible to curse the specific infidel. The jurist Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi al-Maliki chose this view, but he used as evidence a hadith that is weak. Others used as evidence the words of the Prophet, peace be upon him, in the story of the one who was brought drunk and he was flogged. A man, may God curse him, said: How often he is brought. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: Do not curse him, for he loves God and His Messenger. This indicates that whoever does not love God and His Messenger is cursed, and God knows best.
2:163: The Almighty informs us about His uniqueness in divinity, that He has no partner or equal, rather He is God, the One, the Unique, the Self-Sufficient, there is no god but Him, and that He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The explanation of these two names has been presented at the beginning of Al-Fatihah, and in the hadith on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab on the authority of Asma bint Yazid bin Al-Sakn on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, “The greatest name of God is in these two verses: ‘And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’ and ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. God - there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.’” Then he mentioned the evidence of His uniqueness in divinity by creating the heavens and the earth and what is in them and what is between them of the creatures that He created and originated, indicating His oneness, so He said:
2:164: God Almighty says: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth - that in its height, its softness, its vastness, its planets, its fixed stars, and the rotation of its orbit - and this earth in its density, its lowness, its mountains, its seas, its deserts, its valleys, its civilization, and what it contains of benefits, and the alternation of night and day. This comes and then goes and is succeeded by another and follows it, not being delayed for a moment, as God Almighty said: “It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. Each, in an orbit, floats.” Sometimes this lengthens and that shortens, and sometimes this takes from that and then they borrow, as God Almighty said: He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, meaning He increases this in this and this in this, and the ships that sail through the sea with that which benefits people, meaning in harnessing the sea by carrying ships from one side to the other for the livelihood of people and benefiting from what the people of that region have, and this was transferred to these and what God sends down from the sky of water and revives the earth with it after its death, as God Almighty said: “And a sign for them is the dead earth. We have given it life and produced from it grain from which they eat. And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused springs to gush forth therein, that they may eat of its fruit and that which their hands have made. Will they not then be grateful? Glory be to Him who created in pairs all things that the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know.” And He has dispersed therein of every kind. Beast meaning, with its different shapes, colors, benefits, smallness and largeness, and He knows all of that and provides for it, nothing of that is hidden from Him, as the Most High said: "And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All is in a clear register." And the disposition of the winds meaning, sometimes it brings mercy, sometimes it brings torment, sometimes it comes as a herald of good tidings before the clouds, sometimes it drives them, sometimes it gathers them, sometimes it scatters them, sometimes it directs them, then sometimes it comes from the south, which is the Levant, sometimes it comes from the direction of Yemen, sometimes it is a south wind, which is the eastern wind that strikes the face of the Kaaba, and sometimes it is a west wind that penetrates from the direction of the back of the Kaaba. People have written many books on winds, rain and weather conditions, regarding their languages and rulings. Explaining this would take too long here, and God knows best. And the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth means that they move between the sky and the earth, controlled to whatever lands and places God wills, as God Almighty directs them: Are signs for a people who understand meaning that in these things there are clear indications of the Oneness of God Almighty, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding * Who remember God while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], ‘Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You! Protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim told us, Abu Saeed Al-Dashtaki told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Quraysh came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, we want you to call upon your Lord to make Safa into gold for us, so that we can buy horses and weapons with it, and we will believe in you and fight with you. He said: Trust me that if I call upon my Lord and He makes Safa into gold for you, you will believe in me. So they trusted him, so he called upon his Lord, and Gabriel came to him and said: Your Lord has given them Safa into gold on the condition that if they do not believe in you, He will punish them with a punishment that He has not punished anyone in the worlds. Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, my Lord, but leave me and my people, so that I may call upon them day by day. So God revealed this verse: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the [great] ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people Al-An’am 2:17. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ja`far ibn Abi al-Mughira, and he added at the end of it: How do they ask you about al-Safa while they see signs greater than al-Safa? Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father told us, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Shibl told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of `Ata’, who said: “And your God is one God. There is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful” was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina. Then the infidels of Quraysh in Mecca said: How can one God be sufficient for the people? Then God the Almighty revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the [great] ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people to His saying: are signs for a people who reason. By this they know that He is one God, and that He is the God of all things, and the Creator of all things. And Wakee’ ibn al-Jarrah said: Sufyan told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Dahha, he said: When And your God is one God to the end of the verse was revealed, the polytheists said: If it is like this, then let him bring us a sign. So God the Almighty revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day to His saying: are signs for a people who reason. Narrated by Adam ibn Abi Iyas on the authority of Abu Ja’far, who is al-Razi, on the authority of Sa’eed ibn Masruq, the father of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu al-Dahha, with it.
2:165: God the Almighty mentions the state of those who associate partners with Him in this world and their fate in the Hereafter, as they have made equals for Him, i.e., likes and counterparts, worshipping them along with Him and loving them as they love Him, and He is God, there is no god but Him, and He has no opposite, no equal, and no partner with Him. In the two Sahihs, “On the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, which sin is the greatest? He said: To make an equal for God while He created you.” And His statement: And those who believe are stronger in love for God and because of their love for God and their complete knowledge of Him and their reverence and monotheism for Him, they do not associate anything with Him, but rather they worship Him alone, and put their trust in Him, and resort to Him in all their affairs. Then the Almighty threatened the polytheists who wronged themselves with that, saying: And if only those who did wrong could see when they see the punishment that all power belongs to God. Some of them said: The meaning of the speech is that if they saw the punishment, they would know then that all power belongs to God, meaning that the rule belongs to Him alone, with no partner, and that all things are under His control, dominion and authority. And that God is severe in punishment, as He said: So on that Day no one will punish with His punishment, nor will anyone be bound with His bond. He says: If they knew what they would see there and what would befall them of the terrible, reprehensible, and terrible matter due to their polytheism and disbelief, they would stop what they were in of misguidance. Then He informed about their disbelief in their idols and the disavowal of those who were followed, saying: When those who followed disavowed those who followed. The angels who they claimed to worship in the worldly abode disavowed them, so the angels said: “We disavow ourselves before You. They did not worship us.” And they said: “Glory be to You! You are our protector instead of them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn, most of them with them.” Believers, and the jinn also disavow them and renounce their worship of them, as God Almighty said: “And who is more astray than he who calls upon those besides God who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, while they, of their call, are unaware? And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship.” God Almighty also said: “And they have taken besides God deities that they may be a source of honor for them. No! They will disbelieve in their worship and will be opponents to them.” Abraham said to his al-Nas 114:“You have only taken idols besides God out of affection among yourselves in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse each other, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.” God Almighty also said: “And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, some of them returning their words to others. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, ‘If it were not for you, we would have been believers. ’ Those who were oppressed will say to those who were oppressed, ‘Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals. ’ And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, ‘Rather, it was [your] plotting by night and by day when you ordered us to We disbelieve in God and attribute to Him equals, and they concealed their regret when they saw the punishment. And We placed shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do? And God the Almighty said: And Satan said, when the matter was decided, “Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot be your savior, nor can you be my savior. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.” And His statement: And they saw the punishment, and their means were cut off, meaning they witnessed the punishment of God, and their means and means of salvation were cut off, and they did not find any way out or escape from the Fire. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And their ties were cut off. Al-Mawadda said, and Mujahid said the same in the narration of Ibn Abi Nujayh. His statement: “And those who followed said, ‘If only we had another chance, we could disown them as they disowned us. ’” That is, if only we could return to the worldly home so that we could disown these people and their worship, so we would not pay attention to them, but rather we would unify God Almighty with that. For this reason, He said: Thus will God show them their deeds as regrets for them. That is, they will go away and vanish, as God Almighty said: And We will present to them whatever deeds they did and make them as scattered dust. And God Almighty said: The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes, which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. And God Almighty said: And those who disbelieve - their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty person thinks is water. And God Almighty said: And they will never emerge from the Fire.

2:168: When the Almighty made clear that there is no god but Him, and that He is the Independent Creator, He began to make clear that He is the Provider for all of His creation. He mentioned in one place: gratitude that He permitted them to eat from what is on the earth in a state of being lawful from God and good, meaning pleasant in itself and not harmful to the body or the mind. He forbade them from following the footsteps of Satan, which are his ways and paths in what he led his followers astray in, such as prohibiting the Baha’ir, the Sa’ib, the Wasa’il, and the like, which he had made attractive to them in their ignorance, as in the hadith of ‘Iyad ibn Himar in Sahih Muslim on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, “God Almighty says: All wealth that I have granted to My servants is lawful for them - and in it - and if I created My servants as monotheists, then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and forbade them what I had made lawful for them.” And Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad told us, Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn Shaybah Al-Masri told us, Al-Husayn ibn ‘Abd Ar-Rahman Al-Ihtiyazi, Abu Abdullah Al-Jawzjani, a companion of Ibrahim bin Adham, told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: This verse was recited to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful and good. Then Saad bin Abi Waqqas stood up and said: O Messenger of God, ask God to make me one whose supplication is answered. He said: O Saad, make your food pure, and your supplication will be answered. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, a man may throw a forbidden morsel into his stomach, and it will not be accepted from him for forty days. And any servant whose flesh grows from ill-gotten gains and usury, the Fire is more deserving of him. And His saying: “Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.” And the Most High said: Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me, while they are an enemy to you? An evil exchange for the wrongdoers. Qatadah and As-Suddi said about His saying: And do not follow the footsteps of Satan: Every disobedience to God is from the footsteps of Satan. Ikrimah said: They are the temptations of Satan. Mujahid said: His steps or he said his mistakes. Abu Majlaz said: They are vows in disobedience. Al-Sha’bi said: A man vowed to slaughter his son, so Masruq gave him a fatwa to slaughter a ram, and he said: This is from the footsteps of Satan. Abu Ad-Duha said on the authority of Masruq that Abdullah ibn Mas’ud was brought milk and salt, and he began to eat, so a man from the people withdrew, so Ibn Mas’ud said: Give it to your companion. He said: I do not want it. He said: Are you fasting? He said: No. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I have forbidden myself to eat udder milk ever. Ibn Mas`ud said: This is from the footsteps of Satan, so eat and atone for your oath. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. He also said: My father told us, Hassan bin Abdullah Al-Masry told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Rafi`, who said: I was angry one day with my wife, and she said: One day she is Jewish and one day she is Christian, and every slave of hers is free if you do not divorce your wife. So I went to Abdullah bin Umar, who said: This is from the footsteps of Satan. Zaynab bint Umm Salamah said the same, and she was the most knowledgeable woman in Madinah at that time. I went to Asim and Ibn Umar, and they said the same thing. Abd bin Hamid said: Abu Na`im told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abd Al-Karim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whatever is an oath or vow made in anger is from the footsteps of Satan, and its atonement is the atonement for an oath. His statement: He only commands you to do evil and immorality and to say about God that which you do not know. That is, your enemy, Satan, only commands you to do evil deeds, the most serious of which is immorality, such as adultery and the like, and more serious than that is saying about God without knowledge. This includes every unbeliever and every innovator as well.

He said: I do not want it. He said: Are you fasting? He said: No. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I have forbidden myself to eat udder milk ever. Ibn Mas`ud said: This is from the footsteps of Satan, so eat and atone for your oath. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. He also said: My father told us, Hassan bin Abdullah Al-Masry told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Rafi`, who said: I was angry one day with my wife, and she said: One day she is Jewish and one day she is Christian, and every slave of hers is free if you do not divorce your wife. So I went to Abdullah bin Umar, who said: This is from the footsteps of Satan. Zaynab bint Umm Salamah said the same, and she was the most knowledgeable woman in Madinah at that time. I went to Asim and Ibn Umar, and they said the same thing. Abd bin Hamid said: Abu Na`im told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abd Al-Karim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whatever is an oath or vow made in anger is from the footsteps of Satan, and its atonement is the atonement for an oath. His statement: He only commands you to do evil and immorality and to say about God that which you do not know. That is, your enemy, Satan, only commands you to do evil deeds, the most serious of which is immorality, such as adultery and the like, and more serious than that is saying about God without knowledge. This includes every unbeliever and every innovator as well.
2:170: God the Almighty says: And when it is said to these disbelieving polytheists: Follow what God has revealed to His Messenger, and abandon what you are doing of misguidance and ignorance, they say in response to that: Rather, we follow what we found our fathers doing, i.e., the worship of idols and rivals. God the Almighty says, denouncing them: Or even if their fathers i.e., those whom they follow and imitate did not understand anything nor were they guided i.e., they had no understanding or guidance. Ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That it was revealed about a group of Jews whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called to Islam, and they said: Rather, we follow what we found our fathers doing, so God revealed this verse, then He gave them an example. God the Almighty said: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is an evil example. He said: And the example of those who disbelieve meaning in what they are in of error, misguidance and ignorance is like that of straying animals that do not understand what is said to them. Rather, when their shepherd calls to them, that is, calls them to what guides them, they do not understand what he says or comprehend it, but only hear his voice. This is what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata’, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, something similar to this. It was said: This is an example given to them in their supplication to idols that do not hear, see or comprehend anything. Ibn Jarir chose this, but the first is more appropriate, because idols do not hear, comprehend or see anything, and they do not have the power to strike or have life in them. His statement, Deaf, dumb and blind means deaf to hearing the truth, dumb and unable to utter it, blind to seeing its path and course. So they do not reason meaning they do not know anything and do not understand it.

2:172: God the Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to eat from the good things that God the Almighty has provided for them, and to thank Him for that if they are His servants. Eating from what is lawful is a reason for supplication and worship to be accepted, just as eating from what is unlawful prevents supplication and worship from being accepted. As stated in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abu al-Nadr told us, al-Fudayl ibn Marzuq told us, on the authority of Adi ibn Thabit, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people, God is good and does not accept anything but that which is good. God has commanded the believers with what He commanded the Messengers, saying: ‘O Messengers, eat from the good things and do righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing.’ And He said: ‘O you who have believed, eat from the good things that We have provided for you.’ Then he mentioned a man who travels a long way, disheveled and covered in dust, stretching his hands to the sky: ‘O Lord, O Lord,’ while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with what is unlawful. So how can that be answered?” Muslim narrated it in his Sahih and at-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Fadil ibn Marzuq. When God the Almighty bestowed His provision upon them and guided them to eat from His goodness, He mentioned that He did not forbid them from that except for dead animals, which are those that die a natural death without being slaughtered, whether they were strangled, beaten to death, fallen, gored, or attacked by a wild animal. The majority of scholars have singled out dead animals from the sea for the words of God the Almighty: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as will come, God willing. The hadith of ambergris in Sahih, Musnad, Muwatta’ and Sunan states that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said about the sea: Its water is pure and its dead animals are lawful. Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ibn Majah and Ad-Darqutni narrated the hadith of Ibn Umar with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace be upon him): “Two dead animals are lawful for us: the blood of fish and locusts, the liver and the spleen.” This will be confirmed, God willing, in Surat Al-Ma’idah. Question The milk of a dead animal and its eggs attached to it are impure according to Al-Shafi’i and others, because they are part of it. Malik said in a narration: It is pure except that it becomes impure by proximity, and likewise the rennet of a dead animal is disputed, and what is well-known among them is that it is impure. They brought up against themselves the companions eating the cheese of the Magians, so Al-Qurtubi said in the interpretation here that a small amount of it mixes with milk, and a small amount of impurity is excused if it mixes with a lot of liquid. Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Saif bin Harun from Sulayman Al-Tamimi, from Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, from Salman, may God be pleased with him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about ghee, cheese, and fur, and he said: What is permissible is what God has permitted in His Book, and what is forbidden is what God has forbidden in His Book, and what He was silent about is what He has excused. Likewise, the meat of the pig was forbidden to them, whether it was slaughtered or died a natural death, and its fat is included in the ruling on its meat, either by predominance or because the meat includes that or by analogy according to an opinion. Likewise, what was dedicated to other than God was forbidden to them, which is what was slaughtered in a name other than His, the Most High, such as idols, rivals, arrows, and the like, for which the people of ignorance used to slaughter. Al-Qurtubi reported on the authority of Ibn Atiyah that he narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he was asked about a woman who held a wedding for her entertainment and slaughtered a camel in it, so he said: It is not to be eaten because it was slaughtered for an idol. Al-Qurtubi reported on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she was asked about what the non-Arabs slaughter for their festivals and then give as gifts to the Muslims, so she said: Whatever is slaughtered for that day, do not eat from it, and eat from their trees. Then God Almighty permitted eating that in case of necessity and need for it when other foods are not available, so He said: But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], meaning without transgression or aggression, which is exceeding the limit, there is no sin upon him, meaning in eating that, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Mujahid said: Whoever is forced by necessity, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], cutting off the way or separating from the leaders, or going out in disobedience to God, then he has a concession, but whoever goes out seeking [it] or transgressing [it] or in disobedience to God, then he has no concession even if he is forced to do so. This was also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr. Saeed said in a narration from him and Muqatil bin Hayyan: Not transgressing means not considering it permissible. Al-Suddi said: Not transgressing means seeking his desire in it. Adam bin Abi Iyas said: Damrah told us on the authority of Uthman bin Ata’, who is Al-Khurasani, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement not transgressing he said: He does not roast the dead animal to desire it, nor cook it, nor eat anything except the clot, and he carries with him what reaches him the permissible, then when it reaches him he throws it away, and this is his statement nor transgressing and he says he does not transgress with it the permissible. And from Ibn Abbas: He does not get his fill of it, and Al-Suddi interpreted it as transgression. And from Ibn Abbas not transgressing nor transgressing he said not transgressing in the dead animal and he does not transgress in eating it. And Qatada said: So whoever is forced, not transgressing nor transgressing, he said: Not transgressing in the dead animal means in eating it that he transgresses the permissible to the forbidden while he finds an alternative to it. Al-Qurtubi narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: But whoever is forced, meaning he is forced to do that without his choice. Question If a person in need finds a dead animal and someone else’s food in a way that does not cause any harm or injury, then it is not permissible for him to eat the dead animal, but rather he may eat someone else’s food without disagreement - this is what he said - then he said: And if he eats it, in this case, is he liable or not? There are two sayings in it, which are two narrations from Malik, then he brought from Sunan Ibn Majah from the hadith of Shu’bah from Abu Iyas Ja’far ibn Abi Wahshiyyah: I heard ‘Ibad ibn Shurahbil al-Ghubri say: A famine struck us in a year, so I came to Madinah, and I came to a garden, so I took an ear of wheat, rubbed it, and ate it, and put some of it in my cloak. Then the owner of the garden came and hit me and took my garment, so I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him, so he said to the man, I did not feed him when he was hungry or working, nor did I teach him when he was ignorant. So he ordered him to return his garment to him, so he ordered him to have a wasq of food or half a wasq, a sound, strong, good chain of transmission with many corroborating evidences: including the hadith of ‘Amr ibn Shu’ayb from his father, from his grandfather: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about hanging fruit, so he said, Whoever takes some of it from someone in need with his mouth, not making a storehouse, then there is nothing upon him, the hadith, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said about his statement, “There is no sin upon him. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful”: Regarding what he ate out of necessity, and we have been informed, and God knows best, that it is not more than three mouthfuls. Saeed bin Jubair said: Forgiving for what he ate of what is forbidden, Merciful for making what is forbidden permissible for him out of necessity. Waki’ said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Whoever is forced and does not eat or drink and then dies, will enter Hell. This requires that eating carrion by someone forced is an obligation, not a concession. Abu Al-Hasan Al-Tabari, known as Al-Kaya Al-Harasi, a companion of Al-Ghazali in his work, said: This is what is correct according to us, like breaking the fast for the sick and the like.

2:174: God Almighty says: "Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book" meaning the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the books that they had in their hands, which testified to his message and prophethood. They concealed that so that their leadership and what they used to take from the Arabs of gifts and presents due to their veneration of them would not be lost. They feared - may God curse them - that if they revealed that, people would follow him and abandon them. So they concealed that in order to preserve what they had obtained from that, which was a small amount. So they sold themselves for that and exchanged guidance, following the truth, believing the Messenger, and believing in what came from God for that small amount. So they failed and lost in this world and the hereafter. As for this world, God showed His servants the truthfulness of His Messenger by what He established and placed with him of clear signs and decisive evidence. So those who feared to follow him believed him, and they became his helper in fighting them, and they incurred wrath upon wrath, and God condemned them in His book is in more than one place, including this noble verse: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price, which is the worldly life, those eat nothing into their bellies except fire, meaning that they only eat what they eat in exchange for concealing the truth, a fire that will burn in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will be burned in a Blaze. And in the authentic hadith on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, He who eats or drinks from vessels of gold or silver is only swallowing fire from Hell into his belly. And His statement: And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment. This is because the Most High is angry with them, because they concealed what was known, and thus they deserved anger, so He will not look at them nor purify them, that is, He will not praise them or commend them, but He will punish them with a painful punishment. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh mentioned here the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “There are three whom God will not speak to, nor look at, nor purify, and for them is a painful punishment: an old adulterer, a lying king, and an arrogant beggar.” Then the Most High said, informing about them: Those are the ones who have purchased error in place of guidance. That is, they exchanged guidance, which is the dissemination of what is in their books of the description of the Messenger and the mention of his mission and the good report of him from the books of the prophets and following him and believing in him. They replaced that and exchanged it for error, which is denying him and disbelieving in him and concealing his attributes in their books. And the torment. “With forgiveness” means they compensated for forgiveness with punishment, which is what they undertook from its mentioned causes. And the Almighty’s saying: How patient they are with the Fire informs us that they are in a severe, great, and terrifying punishment. Whoever sees them in it will be amazed at their patience with that despite the severity of the punishment, torment, and shackles they are in, God forbid. And it was said that the meaning of His saying: How patient they are with the Fire is how persistent they are in committing sins that will lead them to the Fire. And the Almighty’s saying: That is because God has sent down the Book in truth means that they only deserved this severe punishment because God Almighty sent down His Books to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the prophets before him to establish the truth and invalidate falsehood. And these people took God’s verses as a mockery, for their Book commanded them to show and spread knowledge, but they opposed it and denied it. And this final Messenger calls them to God Almighty and commands them to do good and forbids them from evil, but they deny him, oppose him, reject him, and conceal his description. So they mocked the revealed verses of God. On His messengers, for this reason they deserved punishment and torment, and for this reason He said, “That is because God has sent down the Book in truth. And indeed, those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension.”
