So they mocked the revealed verses of God. On His messengers, for this reason they deserved punishment and torment, and for this reason He said, “That is because God has sent down the Book in truth. And indeed, those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension.”
2:176: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book meaning the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the books that they had in their hands, which testified to his message and prophethood. They concealed that so that their leadership and what they used to take from the Arabs of gifts and presents due to their veneration of them would not be lost. They feared - may God curse them - that if they revealed that, people would follow him and abandon them. So they concealed that in order to preserve what they had obtained from that, which was a small amount. So they sold themselves for that and exchanged guidance, following the truth, believing the Messenger, and believing in what came from God for that small amount. So they failed and lost in this world and the hereafter. As for this world, God showed His servants the truthfulness of His Messenger by what He established and placed with him of clear signs and decisive evidence. So those who feared to follow him believed him, and they became his helper in fighting them, and they incurred wrath upon wrath, and God condemned them in His book is in more than one place, including this noble verse: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price, which is the worldly life, those eat nothing into their bellies except fire, meaning that they only eat what they eat in exchange for concealing the truth, a fire that will burn in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will be burned in a Blaze. And in the authentic hadith on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, He who eats or drinks from vessels of gold or silver is only swallowing fire from Hell into his belly. And His statement: And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment. This is because the Most High is angry with them, because they concealed what was known, and thus they deserved anger, so He will not look at them nor purify them, that is, He will not praise them or commend them, but He will punish them with a painful punishment. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh mentioned here the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “There are three whom God will not speak to, nor look at, nor purify, and for them is a painful punishment: an old adulterer, a lying king, and an arrogant beggar.” Then the Most High said, informing about them: Those are the ones who have purchased error in place of guidance. That is, they exchanged guidance, which is the dissemination of what is in their books of the description of the Messenger and the mention of his mission and the good report of him from the books of the prophets and following him and believing in him. They replaced that and exchanged it for error, which is denying him and disbelieving in him and concealing his attributes in their books. And the torment. “With forgiveness” means they compensated for forgiveness with punishment, which is what they undertook from its mentioned causes. And the Almighty’s saying: How patient they are with the Fire informs us that they are in a severe, great, and terrifying punishment. Whoever sees them in it will be amazed at their patience with that despite the severity of the punishment, torment, and shackles they are in, God forbid. And it was said that the meaning of His saying: How patient they are with the Fire is how persistent they are in committing sins that will lead them to the Fire. And the Almighty’s saying: That is because God has sent down the Book in truth means that they only deserved this severe punishment because God Almighty sent down His Books to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the prophets before him to establish the truth and invalidate falsehood. And these people took God’s verses as a mockery, for their Book commanded them to show and spread knowledge, but they opposed it and denied it. And this final Messenger calls them to God Almighty and commands them to do good and forbids them from evil, but they deny him, oppose him, reject him, and conceal his description. So they mocked the revealed verses of God. On His messengers, for this reason they deserved punishment and torment, and for this reason He said, “That is because God has sent down the Book in truth. And indeed, those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension.”
2:177: This verse contains great sentences, general principles, and a straight belief, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ubaid bin Hisham Al-Halabi told us, Ubaid God bin Amr told us, on the authority of Amer bin Shafi, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Dharr: that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: What is faith? So he recited to him, Righteousness is not that you turn your faces to the end of the verse. He said: Then he asked him again, so he recited it to him, then he asked him and he said: If you do a good deed, your heart loves it, and if you do a bad deed, your heart hates it. This is disconnected, because Mujahid did not meet Abu Dharr, as he died long ago. Al-Mas'udi said: Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman told us, he said: A man came to Abu Dharr and said: What is faith? So he recited to him this verse: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces away until he finished it. The man said: I did not ask you about righteousness. Abu Dharr said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he pointed with his hand: When a believer does a good deed, it pleases him and he hopes for its reward, and when he learns of a bad deed, it saddens him and he fears its punishment. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. This is also disconnected, and God knows best. As for the discussion of the interpretation of this verse, when God Almighty first ordered the believers to face Jerusalem and then turned them to the Kaaba, this was difficult for a group of the People of the Book and some Muslims, so God Almighty revealed a statement of His wisdom in that, which is that what is meant is only obedience to God Almighty, compliance with His commands, and facing wherever He directs and following what He has legislated, for this is righteousness, piety and complete faith. There is no righteousness or obedience in the necessity of facing towards the east or west if it is not by the command of God and His law, and for this reason He said: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces towards the east or the west, but righteousness is of him who believes in God and the Last Day 10:13, as He said about sacrifices and gifts: Neither their meat nor their blood reaches God, but what reaches Him is piety from you. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: Righteousness is not that you pray and do not work, for this was when he moved from Mecca to Medina and the obligatory duties and punishments were revealed, so God ordered the obligatory duties and working with them, and something similar was narrated from Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil, and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The Jews used to face towards the west, and the Christians used to face towards the west. Accept before the east, then God the Almighty said: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west. He says: This is the speech of faith and its reality is action. It was narrated from Al-Hasan and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas something similar. Mujahid said: But righteousness is what is established in the hearts of obedience to God the Almighty. Ad-Dahhak said: But righteousness and piety are that you perform the obligatory duties in their proper manner. Al-Thawri said: But righteousness is from one who believes in God the verse. He said: These are all types of righteousness, and he spoke the truth, may God have mercy on him, for whoever is described by this verse has entered into the bonds of Islam in its entirety, and has taken hold of all the gatherings of goodness, which is belief in God and that there is no god but Him, and has believed in the existence of the angels who are messengers between God and His messengers. And the Book is a generic name that includes the books sent down from heaven to the prophets, until it was sealed with the most honorable of them, which is the Qur’an, which dominates the books that came before it, to which all goodness ended, and it included all happiness in this world and the hereafter, and with it abrogated all other books that came before it, and he believed in all the prophets of God from the first of them to the last of them, Muhammad, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him and them all, and his saying: And he gives money out of love for it means he gives it while he loves it and desires it. This was stated by Ibn Mas’ud, Sa’id ibn Jubayr and others from the early Muslims and later Muslims, as was proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The best charity is that you give it while you are healthy and miserly, hoping to become rich and fearing poverty. Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Shu’bah and Ath-Thawri from Mansur, from Zubayd, from Marra, from Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he gives money out of love for it means that you give it while you are healthy and miserly, hoping to become rich and fearing poverty. Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it. I said It was narrated by Wakee’ from Al-A’mash and Sufyan from Zubayd, from Marra, from Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission ending with him, and this is more authentic, and God knows best. God Almighty said: “And they feed food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive. We feed you only for the sake of God. We desire from you neither reward nor thanks.” And God Almighty said: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. And his saying: And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in need is another pattern that is higher than this, which is that they give preference to what they are forced to, and these people give and feed what they love. And his saying: Those of kinship are the man’s relatives and they are the most deserving of being given charity as established in the hadith: “Charity given to the poor is charity, and to a relative is two things: charity and maintaining kinship ties, so they are the most deserving of you, your kindness and your giving.” And God Almighty has commanded kindness to them in more than one place in His Noble Book. And orphans are those who have no earner, and their fathers died while they were weak and young before reaching puberty and the ability to earn a living. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma’mar informed us on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of al-Nazzal ibn Sabra, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no orphanhood after puberty. “And the needy” are those who do not find what is sufficient for them in their food, clothing and housing, so they are given what will satisfy their need and their poverty. And in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s Messenger (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The poor person is not the one who travels around and is satisfied with one or two dates and one or two mouthfuls of food, but the poor person is the one who does not find enough money to make him independent and is not noticed so that charity is given to him.” The wayfarer is the traveler who has exhausted his means and is given what will take him to his country, and likewise the one who wants to travel in obedience and is given what is sufficient for him on his way and his return, and this includes the guest, as Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The wayfarer is the guest who stays with the Muslims, and this is what Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Ja`far al-Baqir, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, al-Rabi` bin Anas and Muqatil bin Hayyan said. And the beggars are those who come forward to ask for something and are given from the zakat and charity, as Imam Ahmad said: Waki` and Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us on the authority of Mus`ab bin Muhammad, on the authority of Ya`la bin Abi Yahya, on the authority of Fatimah bint al-Husayn, on the authority of her father - Abd al-Rahman Husayn bin Ali said: He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The beggar has a right, even if he comes on a horse. Narrated by Abu Dawud. And in the slaves, meaning those who are freed from slavery and cannot find anything to pay for their slavery. We will discuss many of these categories in the verse on charity in Bara’ah, God willing. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid told us, Sharik told us on the authority of Abu Hamza on the authority of al-Sha’bi, Fatima bint Qays told me that she asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Is there a right on wealth other than zakat? She said: So he recited to me, And he gives away his wealth, for the love of it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Adam bin Iyas and Yahya bin Abdul Hamid, both of them from Sharik from Abu Hamza from Al-Sha’bi from Fatima bint Qais, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, There is a right in wealth other than zakat. Then he recited, “Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but righteousness is [in] one who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets and gives away his wealth, for the love of it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and to free slaves.” Ibn Majah and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and Abu Hamza Maymun Al-A’war was declared weak. It was narrated by Sayyar and Ismail bin Salim from Al-Sha’bi. His saying, And he establishes prayer and gives zakat, means he completes the actions of prayer at their appointed times, bowing, prostrating, being calm and humble in the lawful and acceptable manner. His saying, And he gives zakat, may mean that what is meant by it is the purification of the soul and its deliverance from base and vile morals. Such as His statement: He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it. And the statement of Moses to Pharaoh: Would you like to be purified? And I will guide you to your Lord so that you may fear Him. And the statement of the Most High: And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakat. It is possible that what is meant is the zakat of money, as Saeed bin Jubayr and Muqatil bin Hayyan said, and what is mentioned of giving to these mentioned directions and categories is only voluntary giving, righteousness, and kinship. For this reason, it was mentioned in the hadith from Fatima bint Qais that there is a right in money other than zakat, and God knows best. And his saying: And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made a covenant, is like his saying: Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the contract. The opposite of this characteristic is hypocrisy, as is authenticated in the hadith: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted, he betrays.” And in another hadith: And when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he betrays, and when he disputes, he is immoral. And his saying: And those who are patient in poverty and hardship and at the time of battle, meaning in the case of poverty, which is poverty, and in the case of sickness and ailments, which is hardship, and at the time of battle, meaning in the case of fighting and meeting enemies. This was said by Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn `Abbas, Abu `Aliyah, Marra al-Hamdani, Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi` ibn Anas, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, and others. Rather, the accusative of the patient is to praise and urge patience in these circumstances due to its severity and difficulty, and God knows best, and He is the One sought for help and upon whom reliance is placed. And his saying: Those are the ones who have been truthful, meaning these are those who Those who were truthful in their faith were described by these qualities, because they achieved faith in the heart through words and actions. These are the ones who were truthful, and those are the righteous, because they avoided the forbidden things and performed acts of obedience.
2:178: God Almighty says: Justice in retaliation is prescribed for you, O believers. Your free man for your free man, your male for your male, and your female for your female. Do not transgress and transgress as those before you transgressed and changed the ruling of God concerning them. The reason for that was Qurayzah and Nadir. Banu Nadir had raided Qurayzah in the pre-Islamic era and subdued them. So if a Nadhri killed a Qurazi, he was not killed for it, but ransomed with one hundred wasqs of dates. And if a Qurazi killed a Nadhri, he was killed. And if they ransomed him, they ransomed him with two hundred wasqs of dates, double the blood money of Qurayzah. So God commanded justice in retaliation, and not to follow the path of the corrupt and distorters who contradict God’s rulings concerning them out of disbelief and transgression. God Almighty said: “Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder: the free man for the free man, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.” And he mentioned in the reason for its revelation what Imam Abu Muhammad bin Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Zur’ah told us, he told us Yahya bin Abdullah bin Bakir narrated to me Abdullah bin Lahi’ah narrated to me Ata bin Dinar narrated to me from Saeed bin Jubair regarding the statement of God the Almighty: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those killed, meaning if it was intentional, a free man for a free man. This is because two tribes of Arabs fought in the pre-Islamic period shortly before Islam, and there was killing and wounding between them until they killed slaves and women. None of them took revenge from the other until they converted to Islam. One of the two tribes would attack the other in terms of number and wealth, so they swore that they would not be satisfied until a slave from among us killed a free man from among them, and a woman from among us killed a man from among them. So, The free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female was revealed about them, abrogated by a life for a life. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And the female for the female, is that they did not kill a man for a woman, but they killed a man for a man and a woman for a woman. So God revealed: A life for a life, an eye for an eye, and He made the free men and women equal in retribution for intentional killing, in a life and less than a life. He made Slaves are equal among themselves in terms of intent in the soul and in what is less than the soul, their men and women, and it was also narrated on the authority of Abu Malik that it was abrogated by his saying, a soul for a soul. Question Abu Hanifa held that a free man is killed for a slave, due to the generality of the verse of Al-Ma’idah. Al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Laila, and Dawud held this view, and it was narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah, and Al-Hakam. Al-Bukhari, Ali ibn Al-Madini, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Al-Thawri said in a narration on his authority: The master is killed for his slave, due to the generality of the hadith of Al-Hasan on the authority of Samurah: Whoever kills his slave, we will kill him, and whoever mutilates his slave, we will mutilate him, and whoever castrates him, we will castrate him. The majority disagreed with them and said: A free man is not killed for a slave, because a slave is a commodity, and if he is killed by mistake, no blood money is due for him, but rather his value is due for him, and because he is not to be killed for his limb, so it is more appropriate for a soul. The majority held that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever, due to what was proven in Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever. There is no authentic hadith or interpretation that contradicts this. As for Abu Hanifa, he held that he is to be killed for him, due to the generality of the verse of Al-Ma’idah. Question Al-Hasan and Ata’ said: A man is not killed for killing a woman because of this verse. The majority disagreed with them because of the verse of Al-Ma’idah and because of the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: The blood of Muslims is equal. Al-Layth said: If a man kills his wife, he is not killed for her in particular. Question The doctrine of the four imams and the majority is that a group is killed for one person. Omar said about a boy who was killed by seven people, and he killed them. He said: If the people of Sana’a conspired against him, I would have killed them. No one among the companions was known to have opposed him in his time. This is like consensus. A narration was reported from Imam Ahmad: A group is not killed for one person, and no one is killed for a soul except one soul. Ibn al-Mundhir reported it from Muadh, Ibn al-Zubayr, Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, al-Zuhri, Ibn Sirin, and Habib ibn Abi Thabit. Then Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is more correct, and there is no argument for those who permit killing a group. What we mentioned has been proven from Ibn al-Zubayr. If the companions differ, then the way to do it is to look into it. His saying: But if someone is pardoned by his brother for anything, then there should be a just follow-up and payment to him with kindness. Pardon means accepting the blood money in the case of premeditated murder. This was also reported from Abu al-Aaliyah, Abu al-Sha’tha’, Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ata’, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Ad-Dahhak said from Ibn Abbas: But if someone is pardoned by his brother for anything, meaning: “So... He left him something from his brother, meaning taking the blood money after the blood money was due, and that is forgiveness. “Then follow up with what is acceptable,” he says: So the claimant must follow up with what is acceptable if he accepts the blood money, and pay it to him with kindness, meaning from the killer without harm or against you, meaning defense. Al-Hakim narrated from the hadith of Sufyan on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And pay the claim with kindness. And this is what Saeed bin Jubair, Abu al-Sha’tha’ Jabir bin Zaid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ata’ al-Khurasani, al-Rabi’ bin Anas, al-Suddi, and Muqatil bin Hayyan said. Question Malik, may God have mercy on him, said in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim from him, which is the well-known opinion, and Abu Hanifa and his companions, and al-Shafi’i and Ahmad in one of his two opinions: The blood money guardian does not have the right to pardon the blood money except with the consent of the killer. The rest said: He has the right to pardon it even if he does not consent. Question A group of the Salaf went to the fact that women do not have a pardon, including Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Zuhri, Ibn Shubramah, Al-Layth, and Al-Awza’i, and the rest disagreed with them. His statement: That is a concession from your Lord and a mercy, God Almighty says: The taking of blood money for premeditated murder was only prescribed for you as a concession from God upon you and a mercy to you from what was inevitable for the nations before you of killing or pardon, as Saeed bin Mansour said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, Mujahid told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Retaliation was prescribed for the Children of Israel for murder, but pardon was not prescribed for them, so God said to this nation: “Retaliation is prescribed for you for murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female. But whoever pardons something from his brother,” so pardon is to accept the blood money for premeditated murder. It was narrated by more than one person on the authority of Amr, and Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, and a group narrated it on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas in a similar manner, and Qatada said: That is a concession from your Lord, may God have mercy on this nation and feed them blood money, and it was not permissible for anyone before them, so the people of The Torah is nothing but retaliation and forgiveness, and there is no blood money between them. The people of the Gospel were only forgiveness, which they were commanded to do, and it was made for this nation retaliation, forgiveness, and blood money. And thus it was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, something similar to this. And His statement, But whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment. God Almighty says: Whoever kills after taking or accepting the blood money, for him is a painful and severe punishment from God. And thus it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Suddi and Muqatil bin Hayyan that he is the one who is killed after taking the blood money, as Muhammad bin Ishaq said from Al-Harith bin Fadil, from Sufyan bin Abi Al-Awja’, from Abu Shuraih Al-Khuza’i, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever is afflicted by murder or madness, he has a choice of one of three things: either he takes retaliation, or he pardons, or he takes the blood money. If he wants the fourth, then seize him, and whoever transgresses after that, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein.” Narrated by Ahmad. And Saeed bin Abi Arouba said from Qatadah from Al-Hasan from Samurah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not pardon a man who was killed after taking the blood money, meaning I do not accept the blood money from him, rather I kill him. And His statement, And there is life for you in retaliation, God Almighty says: And in the law of retaliation for you, which is killing the killer, there is great wisdom, which is the preservation and protection of lives, because if the killer knows that he will be killed, he refrains from doing so, so there is life for souls. And in the previous books: Killing is the most effective way to prevent killing, so this phrase came in the Qur’an more eloquent, expressive and concise: And there is life for you in retaliation, Abu Al-Aaliyah said: God made retaliation life, so how many a man wants to kill but is prevented for fear of being killed. And likewise it was narrated from Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Malik, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi bin Anas and Muqatil bin Hayyan: O you of understanding, that you may become righteous, meaning: O you of intellects, understanding and forbearance, that you may be deterred and abandon the prohibitions and sins of God, and righteousness is a comprehensive name for doing good deeds and abandoning evil deeds.

Al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Laila, and Dawud held this view, and it was narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah, and Al-Hakam. The majority disagreed with them and said: A free man is not killed for a slave, because a slave is a commodity, and if he is killed by mistake, no blood money is due for him, but rather his value is due for him, and because he is not to be killed for his limb, so it is more appropriate for a soul. The majority held that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever, due to what was proven in Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever. There is no authentic hadith or interpretation that contradicts this. As for Abu Hanifa, he held that he is to be killed for him, due to the generality of the verse of Al-Ma’idah. Question Al-Hasan and Ata’ said: A man is not killed for killing a woman because of this verse. The majority disagreed with them because of the verse of Al-Ma’idah and because of the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: The blood of Muslims is equal. Al-Layth said: If a man kills his wife, he is not killed for her in particular. Question The doctrine of the four imams and the majority is that a group is killed for one person. Omar said about a boy who was killed by seven people, and he killed them. He said: If the people of Sana’a conspired against him, I would have killed them. No one among the companions was known to have opposed him in his time. This is like consensus. A narration was reported from Imam Ahmad: A group is not killed for one person, and no one is killed for a soul except one soul. Ibn al-Mundhir reported it from Muadh, Ibn al-Zubayr, Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, al-Zuhri, Ibn Sirin, and Habib ibn Abi Thabit. Then Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is more correct, and there is no argument for those who permit killing a group. What we mentioned has been proven from Ibn al-Zubayr. If the companions differ, then the way to do it is to look into it. His saying: But if someone is pardoned by his brother for anything, then there should be a just follow-up and payment to him with kindness. Pardon means accepting the blood money in the case of premeditated murder. This was also reported from Abu al-Aaliyah, Abu al-Sha’tha’, Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ata’, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Ad-Dahhak said from Ibn Abbas: But if someone is pardoned by his brother for anything, meaning: “So... He left him something from his brother, meaning taking the blood money after the blood money was due, and that is forgiveness. “Then follow up with what is acceptable,” he says: So the claimant must follow up with what is acceptable if he accepts the blood money, and pay it to him with kindness, meaning from the killer without harm or against you, meaning defense. Al-Hakim narrated from the hadith of Sufyan on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And pay the claim with kindness. And this is what Saeed bin Jubair, Abu al-Sha’tha’ Jabir bin Zaid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ata’ al-Khurasani, al-Rabi’ bin Anas, al-Suddi, and Muqatil bin Hayyan said. Question Malik, may God have mercy on him, said in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim from him, which is the well-known opinion, and Abu Hanifa and his companions, and al-Shafi’i and Ahmad in one of his two opinions: The blood money guardian does not have the right to pardon the blood money except with the consent of the killer. The rest said: He has the right to pardon it even if he does not consent. Question A group of the Salaf went to the fact that women do not have a pardon, including Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Zuhri, Ibn Shubramah, Al-Layth, and Al-Awza’i, and the rest disagreed with them. His statement: That is a concession from your Lord and a mercy, God Almighty says: The taking of blood money for premeditated murder was only prescribed for you as a concession from God upon you and a mercy to you from what was inevitable for the nations before you of killing or pardon, as Saeed bin Mansour said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, Mujahid told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Retaliation was prescribed for the Children of Israel for murder, but pardon was not prescribed for them, so God said to this nation: “Retaliation is prescribed for you for murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female. But whoever pardons something from his brother,” so pardon is to accept the blood money for premeditated murder. It was narrated by more than one person on the authority of Amr, and Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, and a group narrated it on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas in a similar manner, and Qatada said: That is a concession from your Lord, may God have mercy on this nation and feed them blood money, and it was not permissible for anyone before them, so the people of The Torah is nothing but retaliation and forgiveness, and there is no blood money between them. The people of the Gospel were only forgiveness, which they were commanded to do, and it was made for this nation retaliation, forgiveness, and blood money. And thus it was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, something similar to this. And His statement, But whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment. God Almighty says: Whoever kills after taking or accepting the blood money, for him is a painful and severe punishment from God. And thus it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Suddi and Muqatil bin Hayyan that he is the one who is killed after taking the blood money, as Muhammad bin Ishaq said from Al-Harith bin Fadil, from Sufyan bin Abi Al-Awja’, from Abu Shuraih Al-Khuza’i, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever is afflicted by murder or madness, he has a choice of one of three things: either he takes retaliation, or he pardons, or he takes the blood money. If he wants the fourth, then seize him, and whoever transgresses after that, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein.” Narrated by Ahmad. And Saeed bin Abi Arouba said from Qatadah from Al-Hasan from Samurah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not pardon a man who was killed after taking the blood money, meaning I do not accept the blood money from him, rather I kill him. And His statement, And there is life for you in retaliation, God Almighty says: And in the law of retaliation for you, which is killing the killer, there is great wisdom, which is the preservation and protection of lives, because if the killer knows that he will be killed, he refrains from doing so, so there is life for souls. And in the previous books: Killing is the most effective way to prevent killing, so this phrase came in the Qur’an more eloquent, expressive and concise: And there is life for you in retaliation, Abu Al-Aaliyah said: God made retaliation life, so how many a man wants to kill but is prevented for fear of being killed. And likewise it was narrated from Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Malik, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi bin Anas and Muqatil bin Hayyan: O you of understanding, that you may become righteous, meaning: O you of intellects, understanding and forbearance, that you may be deterred and abandon the prohibitions and sins of God, and righteousness is a comprehensive name for doing good deeds and abandoning evil deeds.
2:180: This noble verse included the command to make a will for parents and relatives, and this was obligatory according to the most correct of the two opinions before the revelation of the verse of inheritance. When the verse of inheritance was revealed, this was abrogated, and the inheritances that were determined became an obligation from God that those who deserved it would take without a will and did not bear the favor of the testator. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith in the Sunan and elsewhere on the authority of Amr ibn Kharijah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon and he said: God has given every person with a right his right, so there is no will for an heir. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn Aliyah told us on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: Ibn Abbas sat and recited Surat Al-Baqarah until he came to this verse: If he leaves wealth, a bequest to parents and relatives. He said: This verse was abrogated. Saeed ibn Mansur narrated it likewise, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Yunus, and Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, and he said: It is authentic according to their conditions. Ali ibn Abu Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, The bequest is for parents and near relatives, said: No one inherits with the parents except for the bequest for the near relatives, so God revealed the verse of inheritance, so He explained the inheritance of the parents and approved the bequest of the near relatives in one-third of the deceased’s wealth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, Ibn Jurayj and Uthman bin Ata’ told us on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The bequest is for parents and near relatives: This verse abrogated it: For men is a share of what the parents and near relatives leave, and for women is a share of what the parents and near relatives leave, whether it be little or much - an obligatory share. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Abu Musa, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata’, Saeed bin Jubayr, Muhammad bin Sirin, Ikrimah, Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Tawus, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Shuraih, Al-Dahhak and Al-Zuhri: that this verse is abrogated, abrogated by The verse of inheritance and the wonder of Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Omar Al-Razi, may God have mercy on him, how he narrated in his great interpretation on the authority of Abu Muslim Al-Isfahani that this verse is not abrogated, but rather it is explained by the verse of inheritance, and its meaning is that what God has commanded of inheritance from parents and relatives has been prescribed for you from His saying, God commands you concerning your children. He said: And this is the saying of most of the interpreters and respected jurists. He said: And among them are those who said: It is abrogated in those who inherit, but it is established in those who do not inherit, and this is the doctrine of Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Masruq, Tawus, Al-Dahhak, Muslim bin Yasar, and Al-Ala bin Ziyad. I said And this is also what Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Rabi bin Anas, Qatadah and Muqatil bin Hayyan said. However, according to the opinion of these people, this is not called abrogation in our later terminology, because the verse of inheritance only lifted the ruling of some individuals indicated by the generality of the verse of will, because the closest relatives are more general than those who inherit and do not inherit, so the ruling of those who inherit was lifted according to what was specified for them, and the other remained as indicated by the first verse. This is only possible according to the opinion of some of them: that the will at the beginning of Islam was only recommended until it was abrogated. As for those who say: that it was obligatory, which is apparent from the context of the verse, then it must be abrogated by the verse of inheritance, as most of the commentators and respected jurists said, because the obligation of the will for the parents and the closest inheritors is abrogated by consensus, rather it is forbidden according to the previous hadith: Indeed, God has given every person with a right his right, so there is no will for an heir. So the verse of inheritance is an independent ruling and an obligation from God for the people of the obligatory shares and the agnates, by which the ruling of these is lifted. In general, the relatives who do not have an inheritance are recommended to bequeath to them from a third, based on the verse of the will and its comprehensiveness, and because it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not right for a Muslim who has something to bequeath to spend two nights without having his will written with him. Ibn Umar said: Not a night has passed since I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say that without me having my will with me. The verses and hadiths commanding kindness to relatives and treating them well are very numerous. Abd bin Hamid said in his Musnad: “Abdullah told us on the authority of Mubarak bin Hassan, on the authority of Nafi’, who said: Abdullah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty says: O son of Adam, two things, neither of which is yours: I made for you a share in your wealth when I took you by the throat to purify you and make you pure with it, and the prayers of My servants upon you after your term has passed.” His statement, If he leaves behind good, means wealth, was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Abu al-A’liyyah, Atiyah al-Awfi, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi’. Ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Qatadah and others. Then some of them said: The will is permissible whether the money is little or much, like inheritance. And some of them said: He only makes a will if he leaves behind a large amount of money. Then they differed about its amount. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, who said: It was said to Ali, may God be pleased with him: A man from Quraysh died and left behind three hundred or four hundred dinars and did not make a will. He said: It is nothing. God only said: If he leaves behind good. He also said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamadani told us, Abduh, meaning Ibn Sulayman, told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father: Ali entered upon a man from his people to visit him, so he said to him: Should I make a will? Ali said to him: God said, If he leaves behind any good, a bequest. He only left behind a small amount, so leave it for your father. Al-Hakim said: Aban told me on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, If he leaves behind any good. Ibn Abbas said: He who does not leave behind sixty dinars has not left behind any good. Al-Hakim said: Tawus said: He who does not leave behind eighty dinars has not left behind any good. Qatada said: It was said: A thousand or more. And his saying with kindness means with gentleness and kindness, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Ahmad told us, Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Bashar told us, Surur bin Al-Mughira told me on the authority of Ibad bin Mansour on the authority of Al-Hasan, his saying: It is prescribed for you when death approaches one of you, he said: Yes, a will is a right upon every Muslim to make a will when death approaches him with kindness and not evil. What is meant by kindness is that he makes a will for his relatives that does not oppress his heirs, without extravagance or stinginess, as is proven in the two Sahihs: “Saad said: O Messenger of God, I have wealth and no one inherits from me except my daughter, so should I bequeath two-thirds of my wealth? He said: No. He said: Then half? He said: No. He said: Then a third? He said: A third, and a third is a lot. If you leave your heirs rich, it is better than leaving them poor, supporting people.” And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, Ibn Abbas said: If people reduced their share from a third to a quarter, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A third, and a third is a lot. And Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed, the client of Banu Hashim, on the authority of Ziyad bin Utbah bin Hanzala, heard Hanzala bin Judhaym bin Hanifa: His grandfather Hanifa bequeathed one hundred camels to an orphan in his care. This was difficult for his sons, so they went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Hanifa said: I bequeathed one hundred camels to an orphan of mine, which we used to call a mount. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, no, no, the charity is five, otherwise ten, otherwise fifteen, otherwise twenty, otherwise twenty-five, otherwise thirty, otherwise thirty-five, and if it is more, then forty. And he mentioned the hadith in full. And His statement, “But whoever changes it after he has heard it, then his sin is only upon those who change it. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.” God the Almighty says: So whoever changes the will and distorts it, changing its ruling and adding to it or subtracting from it, and this includes concealing it by way of priority, then his sin is only upon those who change it. Ibn Abbas and others said: The reward of the deceased has fallen upon God, and the sin is attached to those who changed it. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. That is, He has seen what the deceased has bequeathed and He is aware of that and what the legatees have changed. And God the Almighty says, But whoever fears from a testator injustice or sin, Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and al-Suddi said: Injustice is an error, and this includes all types of error, such as adding an heir by way of intermediary or means, such as if he bequeathed the sale of a certain thing out of favoritism or bequeathed to his daughter’s son to increase it or something similar from the means, either by mistake and not intentionally but by his nature and the strength of his compassion without insight, or intentionally. A sinner in that, so the guardian in this case, should correct the issue and amend the will in the legal manner, and change what the deceased bequeathed to what is closest to him and most similar to the matters in order to combine the intention of the testator and the legal path, and this correction and reconciliation is not a change in anything, and for this reason he linked this and explained it to the prohibition of that, so that it is known that this is not a way of that, and God knows best, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas bin Al-Waleed bin Muzaid narrated to us, my father told me on the authority of Al-Awza’i, Al-Zuhri said: Urwah narrated to me on the authority of Aisha on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: What is returned from the charity of the transgressor during his life is what is returned from the will of the transgressor upon his death. And thus Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Al-Abbas bin Al-Waleed with it, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Waleed bin Muzaid made a mistake in it, and this statement is only from Urwah, and Al-Waleed bin Muslim narrated it on the authority of Al-Awza’i, so he did not go beyond Urwah with it, and Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf narrated to us, Hisham bin Ammar, narrated to us Omar bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Insolence in making a will is one of the major sins. This is also questionable in its being attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The best that has been reported in this regard is what Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar Ash’ath bin Abdullah narrated to us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man may do the deeds of good people for seventy years, then when he makes a will, he is unfair in his will, and his deeds are concluded with evil and he enters Hell. A man may do evil deeds for seventy years, then he is just in his will, and his deeds are concluded with good deeds and he enters Paradise.” Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: These are the limits set by God, so do not transgress them 10:13.

And God the Almighty says, But whoever fears from a testator injustice or sin, Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and al-Suddi said: Injustice is an error, and this includes all types of error, such as adding an heir by way of intermediary or means, such as if he bequeathed the sale of a certain thing out of favoritism or bequeathed to his daughter’s son to increase it or something similar from the means, either by mistake and not intentionally but by his nature and the strength of his compassion without insight, or intentionally. A sinner in that, so the guardian in this case, should correct the issue and amend the will in the legal manner, and change what the deceased bequeathed to what is closest to him and most similar to the matters in order to combine the intention of the testator and the legal path, and this correction and reconciliation is not a change in anything, and for this reason he linked this and explained it to the prohibition of that, so that it is known that this is not a way of that, and God knows best, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas bin Al-Waleed bin Muzaid narrated to us, my father told me on the authority of Al-Awza’i, Al-Zuhri said: Urwah narrated to me on the authority of Aisha on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: What is returned from the charity of the transgressor during his life is what is returned from the will of the transgressor upon his death. And thus Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Al-Abbas bin Al-Waleed with it, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Waleed bin Muzaid made a mistake in it, and this statement is only from Urwah, and Al-Waleed bin Muslim narrated it on the authority of Al-Awza’i, so he did not go beyond Urwah with it, and Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf narrated to us, Hisham bin Ammar, narrated to us Omar bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Insolence in making a will is one of the major sins. This is also questionable in its being attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The best that has been reported in this regard is what Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar Ash’ath bin Abdullah narrated to us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man may do the deeds of good people for seventy years, then when he makes a will, he is unfair in his will, and his deeds are concluded with evil and he enters Hell. A man may do evil deeds for seventy years, then he is just in his will, and his deeds are concluded with good deeds and he enters Paradise.” Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: These are the limits set by God, so do not transgress them 10:13.
2:182: This noble verse included the command to make a will for parents and relatives, and this was obligatory according to the most correct of the two opinions before the revelation of the verse of inheritance. When the verse of inheritance was revealed, this was abrogated, and the inheritances that were determined became an obligation from God that those who deserved it would take without a will and did not bear the favor of the testator. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith in the Sunan and elsewhere on the authority of Amr ibn Kharijah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon and he said: God has given every person with a right his right, so there is no will for an heir. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn Aliyah told us on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: Ibn Abbas sat and recited Surat Al-Baqarah until he came to this verse: If he leaves wealth, a bequest to parents and relatives. He said: This verse was abrogated. Saeed ibn Mansur narrated it likewise, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Yunus, and Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, and he said: It is authentic according to their conditions. Ali ibn Abu Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, The bequest is for parents and near relatives, said: No one inherits with the parents except for the bequest for the near relatives, so God revealed the verse of inheritance, so He explained the inheritance of the parents and approved the bequest of the near relatives in one-third of the deceased’s wealth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, Ibn Jurayj and Uthman bin Ata’ told us on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The bequest is for parents and near relatives: This verse abrogated it: For men is a share of what the parents and near relatives leave, and for women is a share of what the parents and near relatives leave, whether it be little or much - an obligatory share. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Abu Musa, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata’, Saeed bin Jubayr, Muhammad bin Sirin, Ikrimah, Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Tawus, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Shuraih, Al-Dahhak and Al-Zuhri: that this verse is abrogated, abrogated by The verse of inheritance and the wonder of Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Omar Al-Razi, may God have mercy on him, how he narrated in his great interpretation on the authority of Abu Muslim Al-Isfahani that this verse is not abrogated, but rather it is explained by the verse of inheritance, and its meaning is that what God has commanded of inheritance from parents and relatives has been prescribed for you from His saying, God commands you concerning your children. He said: And this is the saying of most of the interpreters and respected jurists. He said: And among them are those who said: It is abrogated in those who inherit, but it is established in those who do not inherit, and this is the doctrine of Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Masruq, Tawus, Al-Dahhak, Muslim bin Yasar, and Al-Ala bin Ziyad. I said And this is also what Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Rabi bin Anas, Qatadah and Muqatil bin Hayyan said. However, according to the opinion of these people, this is not called abrogation in our later terminology, because the verse of inheritance only lifted the ruling of some individuals indicated by the generality of the verse of will, because the closest relatives are more general than those who inherit and do not inherit, so the ruling of those who inherit was lifted according to what was specified for them, and the other remained as indicated by the first verse. This is only possible according to the opinion of some of them: that the will at the beginning of Islam was only recommended until it was abrogated. As for those who say: that it was obligatory, which is apparent from the context of the verse, then it must be abrogated by the verse of inheritance, as most of the commentators and respected jurists said, because the obligation of the will for the parents and the closest inheritors is abrogated by consensus, rather it is forbidden according to the previous hadith: Indeed, God has given every person with a right his right, so there is no will for an heir. So the verse of inheritance is an independent ruling and an obligation from God for the people of the obligatory shares and the agnates, by which the ruling of these is lifted. In general, the relatives who do not have an inheritance are recommended to bequeath to them from a third, based on the verse of the will and its comprehensiveness, and because it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not right for a Muslim who has something to bequeath to spend two nights without having his will written with him. Ibn Umar said: Not a night has passed since I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say that without me having my will with me. The verses and hadiths commanding kindness to relatives and treating them well are very numerous. Abd bin Hamid said in his Musnad: “Abdullah told us on the authority of Mubarak bin Hassan, on the authority of Nafi’, who said: Abdullah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty says: O son of Adam, two things, neither of which is yours: I made for you a share in your wealth when I took you by the throat to purify you and make you pure with it, and the prayers of My servants upon you after your term has passed.” His statement, If he leaves behind good, means wealth, was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Abu al-A’liyyah, Atiyah al-Awfi, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi’. Ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Qatadah and others. Then some of them said: The will is permissible whether the money is little or much, like inheritance. And some of them said: He only makes a will if he leaves behind a large amount of money. Then they differed about its amount. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, who said: It was said to Ali, may God be pleased with him: A man from Quraysh died and left behind three hundred or four hundred dinars and did not make a will. He said: It is nothing. God only said: If he leaves behind good. He also said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamadani told us, Abduh, meaning Ibn Sulayman, told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father: Ali entered upon a man from his people to visit him, so he said to him: Should I make a will? Ali said to him: God said, If he leaves behind any good, a bequest. He only left behind a small amount, so leave it for your father. Al-Hakim said: Aban told me on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, If he leaves behind any good. Ibn Abbas said: He who does not leave behind sixty dinars has not left behind any good. Al-Hakim said: Tawus said: He who does not leave behind eighty dinars has not left behind any good. Qatada said: It was said: A thousand or more. And his saying with kindness means with gentleness and kindness, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Ahmad told us, Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Bashar told us, Surur bin Al-Mughira told me on the authority of Ibad bin Mansour on the authority of Al-Hasan, his saying: It is prescribed for you when death approaches one of you, he said: Yes, a will is a right upon every Muslim to make a will when death approaches him with kindness and not evil. What is meant by kindness is that he makes a will for his relatives that does not oppress his heirs, without extravagance or stinginess, as is proven in the two Sahihs: “Saad said: O Messenger of God, I have wealth and no one inherits from me except my daughter, so should I bequeath two-thirds of my wealth? He said: No. He said: Then half? He said: No. He said: Then a third? He said: A third, and a third is a lot. If you leave your heirs rich, it is better than leaving them poor, supporting people.” And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, Ibn Abbas said: If people reduced their share from a third to a quarter, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A third, and a third is a lot. And Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed, the client of Banu Hashim, on the authority of Ziyad bin Utbah bin Hanzala, heard Hanzala bin Judhaym bin Hanifa: His grandfather Hanifa bequeathed one hundred camels to an orphan in his care. This was difficult for his sons, so they went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Hanifa said: I bequeathed one hundred camels to an orphan of mine, which we used to call a mount. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, no, no, the charity is five, otherwise ten, otherwise fifteen, otherwise twenty, otherwise twenty-five, otherwise thirty, otherwise thirty-five, and if it is more, then forty. And he mentioned the hadith in full. And His statement, “But whoever changes it after he has heard it, then his sin is only upon those who change it. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.” God the Almighty says: So whoever changes the will and distorts it, changing its ruling and adding to it or subtracting from it, and this includes concealing it by way of priority, then his sin is only upon those who change it. Ibn Abbas and others said: The reward of the deceased has fallen upon God, and the sin is attached to those who changed it. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. That is, He has seen what the deceased has bequeathed and He is aware of that and what the legatees have changed. And God the Almighty says, But whoever fears from a testator injustice or sin, Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and al-Suddi said: Injustice is an error, and this includes all types of error, such as adding an heir by way of intermediary or means, such as if he bequeathed the sale of a certain thing out of favoritism or bequeathed to his daughter’s son to increase it or something similar from the means, either by mistake and not intentionally but by his nature and the strength of his compassion without insight, or intentionally. A sinner in that, so the guardian in this case, should correct the issue and amend the will in the legal manner, and change what the deceased bequeathed to what is closest to him and most similar to the matters in order to combine the intention of the testator and the legal path, and this correction and reconciliation is not a change in anything, and for this reason he linked this and explained it to the prohibition of that, so that it is known that this is not a way of that, and God knows best, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas bin Al-Waleed bin Muzaid narrated to us, my father told me on the authority of Al-Awza’i, Al-Zuhri said: Urwah narrated to me on the authority of Aisha on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: What is returned from the charity of the transgressor during his life is what is returned from the will of the transgressor upon his death. And thus Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Al-Abbas bin Al-Waleed with it, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Waleed bin Muzaid made a mistake in it, and this statement is only from Urwah, and Al-Waleed bin Muslim narrated it on the authority of Al-Awza’i, so he did not go beyond Urwah with it, and Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf narrated to us, Hisham bin Ammar, narrated to us Omar bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Insolence in making a will is one of the major sins. This is also questionable in its being attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The best that has been reported in this regard is what Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar Ash’ath bin Abdullah narrated to us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man may do the deeds of good people for seventy years, then when he makes a will, he is unfair in his will, and his deeds are concluded with evil and he enters Hell. A man may do evil deeds for seventy years, then he is just in his will, and his deeds are concluded with good deeds and he enters Paradise.” Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: These are the limits set by God, so do not transgress them 10:13.
2:183: The Almighty says, addressing the believers in this verse, and commanding them to fast, which is to abstain from food, drink, and sexual intercourse, with a pure intention for the sake of God, the Almighty, because it purifies and cleanses the souls from bad mixtures and bad morals. He mentioned that just as He made it obligatory for them, He made it obligatory for those who came before them, so they have an example in it, and these should strive to perform this obligation more fully than those did, as God, the Almighty, said: “To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had God willed, He would have made you one community, but to test you in what He has given you, so race to [do] good.” The verse, and for this reason He said here, O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous. Because fasting purifies the body and narrows the paths of Satan, and for this reason it is proven in the two Sahihs, O group of young people, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, and whoever is not able, then let him fast, for it is a restraint for him. Then He explained the amount of fasting and that it is not every day. So that it would not be difficult for the souls to become weak in carrying it and performing it, but rather in a numbered number of days. This was the case at the beginning of Islam, they would fast three days of every month, then this was abrogated by fasting the month of Ramadan as will be explained. It has been narrated that fasting was at first as it was the case with the nations before us, three days of every month, on the authority of Muadh, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Ata’, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, and he added: This continued to be prescribed from the time of Noah until God abrogated it by fasting the month of Ramadan. Abbad bin Mansour said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous * For a numbered number of days. He said: Yes, by God, fasting was decreed upon every nation that has passed, just as it was decreed upon us, for a full month and a numbered number of days, a known number. Something similar was narrated on the authority of As-Suddi. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri, who said: Saeed ibn Abi Ayoub told me, Abdullah ibn al-Walid told me, on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, a man from the people of Medina, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fasting Ramadan was prescribed by God for the nations before you, in a long hadith from which he summarized that. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you was revealed. It was prescribed for them that if one of them prays the `Isha prayer and sleeps, food, drink and women are forbidden to him until the same time. Ibn Abi al-`Aliyah, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Rabi` ibn Anas, `Ata` al-Khurasani said something similar to that. `Ata` al-Khurasani said on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: As it was prescribed for those before you meaning the People of the Book. A similar narration was narrated on the authority of al-Sha`bi, al-Suddi and `Ata` al-Khurasani. Then he explained the ruling on fasting as it was at the beginning of Islam, saying: But whoever among you is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. That is, the sick and the traveler do not fast while they are ill or on a journey, because of the hardship that is upon them, rather they break their fast and make it up later on from other days. As for the healthy resident who is able to fast, he has the choice between fasting and feeding. If he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast and feeds a poor person for each day. If he feeds, More than one poor person for each day is better, and if he fasts, it is better than feeding others. This was said by Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Tawus, Muqatil bin Hayyan and others from the Salaf. That is why God Almighty said: “And upon those who can do it is a ransom - the feeding of a poor person. But whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you, if you only knew.” Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, al-Mas’udi told us, Amr ibn Murrah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, who said: Prayer was changed in three ways, and fasting was changed in three ways. As for the ways of prayer, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and he prayed for seventeen months towards the Holy House. Then God Almighty revealed to him: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the heaven. So We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased.” So God directed him towards Mecca for this year. He said: They would gather for prayer and call each other to prayer, until they became weak or almost weak. Then a man from the Ansar called Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Abd Rabbih came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I saw in a dream, and if I said that I was not asleep, I would be telling the truth. While I was between sleeping and awake, I saw a person wearing two green garments, and he faced the qiblah and said: God is Great, God is Great, I bear witness that there is no god but God. Muthanna - until he finished the call to prayer, then he waited an hour and then said the same as he had said except that he added to it: The prayer has begun twice. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Teach it to Bilal, so let him call to prayer with it. Bilal was the first to call to prayer with it. He said: And Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, came and said: O Messenger of God, he circumambulated me as he circumambulated him, except that he preceded me. So these are two situations. He said: And they used to come to prayer and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, preceded them with some of it, so a man would point to a man, so how much did he pray? He said: One or two, so he prays them, then he joins the people in their prayer. He said: Then Muadh came and said: I never find him in a state except that I am in it, then I completed what I had preceded. He said: So he came and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had preceded him in some of it. He said: So he stayed with him. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished, he stood up and completed it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Muadh has prescribed for you, so do it like this. These are three states. As for the states of fasting, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and began to fast three days of every month and fasted Ashura. Then God imposed fasting on him, and God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you to His saying: And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom of feeding a poor person. So whoever wanted to fast, he fasted, and whoever wanted to feed a poor person, and that was sufficient for him. Then God Almighty revealed the other verse: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur’an to His saying: So whoever witnesses the month among you, let him fast it. So God established Fasting is permissible for a healthy resident, and it is permissible for the sick and the traveler, and feeding is established for the elderly who are unable to fast. These are two cases. He said: They used to eat, drink, and come to women as long as they did not sleep. When they slept, they refrained. Then a man from the Ansar called Sarmah worked while fasting until evening. Then he came to his family and prayed the Isha prayer, then slept. He did not eat or drink until morning, so he became fasting. The Messenger of God saw him and he had exerted himself greatly, so he said: Why do I see you exerting yourself greatly? He said: O Messenger of God, I did some work yesterday and came when I came, so I threw myself down and slept, and became fasting. He said: Omar had had intercourse with women after he had slept, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so God, the Almighty, revealed: “Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives. They are your garments and you are their garments. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has ordained for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread, then complete the fast until the night.” Abu Dawud included it in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from the hadith of al-Mas’udi with it. Al-Bukhari and Muslim included it from the hadith of al-Zuhri from Urwah from Aisha that she said: Ashura used to be fasted, but when the obligation of Ramadan was revealed, whoever wanted to fast could fast and whoever wanted to break the fast could break the fast. Al-Bukhari narrated something similar from Ibn Umar and Ibn Mas’ud. And the Almighty’s saying: And upon those who are hard to fast is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person, as Mu’adh, may God be pleased with him, said: In the beginning, whoever wanted to fast could fast, and whoever wanted to break his fast could break his fast and feed a poor person for each day. And thus, Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ that he said when the verse And upon those who are hard to fast is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person was revealed: whoever wanted to break his fast could pay the ransom until the verse after it was revealed and abrogated it. And it was also narrated on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: It is abrogated. And Al-Suddi said on the authority of Marra on the authority of Abdullah, he said when this verse was revealed: And upon those who are hard to fast is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person, he said: It says And upon those who are hard to fast, meaning they take on the burden of it. Abdullah said: So whoever wanted to fast could fast, and whoever wanted to break his fast could feed a poor person. But whoever does it voluntarily, he said: feed another poor person, “it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you,” and they were like that until it was abrogated by So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. And Al-Bukhari also said: Ishaq told us, Ruh narrated to us, Zakariya bin Ishaq narrated to us, Amr bin Dinar narrated to us from Ata’: He heard Ibn Abbas recite: And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person. Ibn Abbas said: It is not abrogated. It is the old man and the old woman who are able to fast, so they feed a poor person for each day. And more than one person narrated similarly from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah said: Abd al-Raheem bin Sulayman narrated to us from Ash’ath bin Suwar, from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas, he said: This verse And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person was revealed about the old man who is not able to fast, then it became weak and he was permitted to feed a poor person for each day. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad narrated to us, al-Husayn bin Bahram al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Wahb bin Baqiyah narrated to us, Khalid bin Abdullah narrated to us from Ibn Abi Laila, he said: I entered upon Ata’ in Ramadan while he was eating, so he said: Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person. The ransom of feeding a poor person.” So whoever wanted to fast could fast, and whoever wanted to break the fast could break the fast and feed a poor person. Then the first was abrogated for the elderly person who had passed away. If he wanted to feed a poor person for each day, he could break the fast. So the bottom line is that abrogation is established for the healthy resident person by requiring him to fast, as He said, So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. As for the elderly person who has passed away and is unable to fast, he may break the fast and does not have to make it up, because he does not have a condition that he can reach in which he can make it up. But is it obligatory for him, if he breaks the fast, to feed a poor person for each day if he has a grandmother? There are two opinions of scholars: One of them is that he is not obligated to feed because he is too weak to do so due to his age, so he is not obligated to pay a ransom like a child, because God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, and this is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. The second, which is correct and is the opinion of most scholars, is that he is obligated to pay a ransom for each day, as Ibn Abbas and others of the Salaf interpreted it according to the reading of those who read and upon those who are able to do it meaning they are able to do it, as Ibn Mas’ud and others said. This is the choice of Al-Bukhari, for he said: As for the old man if he is not able to fast, Anas fed a poor person for each day after he grew old, a year or two after he had grown old, bread and meat, and he broke his fast. This which Al-Bukhari suspended was attributed to Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili in his Musnad, and he said: Abdullah bin Mu’adh told us, my father told us, Imran told us on the authority of Ayoub bin Abi Tamima, who said: Anas was too weak to fast, so he made a bowl of tharid, and invited thirty poor people and fed them. It was narrated by Abd bin Hamid on the authority of Ruh bin Ubadah, on the authority of Imran, who is Ibn Hadhir, on the authority of Ayoub, on his authority. Abd also narrated it from the hadith of six of the companions of Anas on the authority of Anas with the same meaning. Among the things that are included in this meaning are the pregnant woman and the breastfeeding woman if they fear for themselves or their children. There is much disagreement among the scholars concerning them. Some of them said: They break the fast, pay the ransom, and make up the fast. It was said: They pay the ransom only and do not make up the fast. It was said: They must make up the fast without ransom. It was said: They break the fast and do not pay the ransom or make up the fast. We have explained this issue in detail in the book on fasting that we devoted to it. Praise and thanks be to God.
2:184: The Almighty says, addressing the believers in this verse, and commanding them to fast, which is to abstain from food, drink, and sexual intercourse, with a pure intention for the sake of God, the Almighty, because it purifies and cleanses the souls from bad mixtures and bad morals.
