He mentioned that just as He made it obligatory for them, He made it obligatory for those who came before them, so they have an example in it, and these should strive to perform this obligation more fully than those did, as God, the Almighty, said: “To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had God willed, He would have made you one community, but to test you in what He has given you, so race to [do] good.” The verse, and for this reason He said here, O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous. Because fasting purifies the body and narrows the paths of Satan, and for this reason it is proven in the two Sahihs, O group of young people, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, and whoever is not able, then let him fast, for it is a restraint for him. Then He explained the amount of fasting and that it is not every day. So that it would not be difficult for the souls to become weak in carrying it and performing it, but rather in a numbered number of days. This was the case at the beginning of Islam, they would fast three days of every month, then this was abrogated by fasting the month of Ramadan as will be explained. It has been narrated that fasting was at first as it was the case with the nations before us, three days of every month, on the authority of Muadh, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Ata’, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, and he added: This continued to be prescribed from the time of Noah until God abrogated it by fasting the month of Ramadan. Abbad bin Mansour said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous * For a numbered number of days. He said: Yes, by God, fasting was decreed upon every nation that has passed, just as it was decreed upon us, for a full month and a numbered number of days, a known number. Something similar was narrated on the authority of As-Suddi. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri, who said: Saeed ibn Abi Ayoub told me, Abdullah ibn al-Walid told me, on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, a man from the people of Medina, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fasting Ramadan was prescribed by God for the nations before you, in a long hadith from which he summarized that. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you was revealed. It was prescribed for them that if one of them prays the `Isha prayer and sleeps, food, drink and women are forbidden to him until the same time. Ibn Abi al-`Aliyah, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Rabi` ibn Anas, `Ata` al-Khurasani said something similar to that. `Ata` al-Khurasani said on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: As it was prescribed for those before you meaning the People of the Book. A similar narration was narrated on the authority of al-Sha`bi, al-Suddi and `Ata` al-Khurasani. Then he explained the ruling on fasting as it was at the beginning of Islam, saying: But whoever among you is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. That is, the sick and the traveler do not fast while they are ill or on a journey, because of the hardship that is upon them, rather they break their fast and make it up later on from other days. As for the healthy resident who is able to fast, he has the choice between fasting and feeding. If he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast and feeds a poor person for each day. If he feeds, More than one poor person for each day is better, and if he fasts, it is better than feeding others. This was said by Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Tawus, Muqatil bin Hayyan and others from the Salaf. That is why God Almighty said: “And upon those who can do it is a ransom - the feeding of a poor person. But whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you, if you only knew.” Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, al-Mas’udi told us, Amr ibn Murrah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, who said: Prayer was changed in three ways, and fasting was changed in three ways. As for the ways of prayer, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and he prayed for seventeen months towards the Holy House. Then God Almighty revealed to him: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the heaven. So We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased.” So God directed him towards Mecca for this year. He said: They would gather for prayer and call each other to prayer, until they became weak or almost weak. Then a man from the Ansar called Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Abd Rabbih came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I saw in a dream, and if I said that I was not asleep, I would be telling the truth. While I was between sleeping and awake, I saw a person wearing two green garments, and he faced the qiblah and said: God is Great, God is Great, I bear witness that there is no god but God. Muthanna - until he finished the call to prayer, then he waited an hour and then said the same as he had said except that he added to it: The prayer has begun twice. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Teach it to Bilal, so let him call to prayer with it. Bilal was the first to call to prayer with it. He said: And Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, came and said: O Messenger of God, he circumambulated me as he circumambulated him, except that he preceded me. So these are two situations. He said: And they used to come to prayer and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, preceded them with some of it, so a man would point to a man, so how much did he pray? He said: One or two, so he prays them, then he joins the people in their prayer. He said: Then Muadh came and said: I never find him in a state except that I am in it, then I completed what I had preceded. He said: So he came and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had preceded him in some of it. He said: So he stayed with him. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished, he stood up and completed it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Muadh has prescribed for you, so do it like this. These are three states. As for the states of fasting, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and began to fast three days of every month and fasted Ashura. Then God imposed fasting on him, and God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you to His saying: And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom of feeding a poor person. So whoever wanted to fast, he fasted, and whoever wanted to feed a poor person, and that was sufficient for him. Then God Almighty revealed the other verse: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur’an to His saying: So whoever witnesses the month among you, let him fast it. So God established Fasting is permissible for a healthy resident, and it is permissible for the sick and the traveler, and feeding is established for the elderly who are unable to fast. These are two cases. He said: They used to eat, drink, and come to women as long as they did not sleep. When they slept, they refrained. Then a man from the Ansar called Sarmah worked while fasting until evening. Then he came to his family and prayed the Isha prayer, then slept. He did not eat or drink until morning, so he became fasting. The Messenger of God saw him and he had exerted himself greatly, so he said: Why do I see you exerting yourself greatly? He said: O Messenger of God, I did some work yesterday and came when I came, so I threw myself down and slept, and became fasting. He said: Omar had had intercourse with women after he had slept, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so God, the Almighty, revealed: “Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives. They are your garments and you are their garments. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has ordained for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread, then complete the fast until the night.” Abu Dawud included it in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from the hadith of al-Mas’udi with it. Al-Bukhari and Muslim included it from the hadith of al-Zuhri from Urwah from Aisha that she said: Ashura used to be fasted, but when the obligation of Ramadan was revealed, whoever wanted to fast could fast and whoever wanted to break the fast could break the fast. Al-Bukhari narrated something similar from Ibn Umar and Ibn Mas’ud. And the Almighty’s saying: And upon those who are hard to fast is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person, as Mu’adh, may God be pleased with him, said: In the beginning, whoever wanted to fast could fast, and whoever wanted to break his fast could break his fast and feed a poor person for each day. And thus, Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ that he said when the verse And upon those who are hard to fast is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person was revealed: whoever wanted to break his fast could pay the ransom until the verse after it was revealed and abrogated it. And it was also narrated on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: It is abrogated. And Al-Suddi said on the authority of Marra on the authority of Abdullah, he said when this verse was revealed: And upon those who are hard to fast is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person, he said: It says And upon those who are hard to fast, meaning they take on the burden of it. Abdullah said: So whoever wanted to fast could fast, and whoever wanted to break his fast could feed a poor person. But whoever does it voluntarily, he said: feed another poor person, “it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you,” and they were like that until it was abrogated by So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. And Al-Bukhari also said: Ishaq told us, Ruh narrated to us, Zakariya bin Ishaq narrated to us, Amr bin Dinar narrated to us from Ata’: He heard Ibn Abbas recite: And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person. Ibn Abbas said: It is not abrogated. It is the old man and the old woman who are able to fast, so they feed a poor person for each day. And more than one person narrated similarly from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah said: Abd al-Raheem bin Sulayman narrated to us from Ash’ath bin Suwar, from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas, he said: This verse And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person was revealed about the old man who is not able to fast, then it became weak and he was permitted to feed a poor person for each day. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad narrated to us, al-Husayn bin Bahram al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Wahb bin Baqiyah narrated to us, Khalid bin Abdullah narrated to us from Ibn Abi Laila, he said: I entered upon Ata’ in Ramadan while he was eating, so he said: Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person. The ransom of feeding a poor person.” So whoever wanted to fast could fast, and whoever wanted to break the fast could break the fast and feed a poor person. Then the first was abrogated for the elderly person who had passed away. If he wanted to feed a poor person for each day, he could break the fast. So the bottom line is that abrogation is established for the healthy resident person by requiring him to fast, as He said, So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. As for the elderly person who has passed away and is unable to fast, he may break the fast and does not have to make it up, because he does not have a condition that he can reach in which he can make it up. But is it obligatory for him, if he breaks the fast, to feed a poor person for each day if he has a grandmother? There are two opinions of scholars: One of them is that he is not obligated to feed because he is too weak to do so due to his age, so he is not obligated to pay a ransom like a child, because God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, and this is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. The second, which is correct and is the opinion of most scholars, is that he is obligated to pay a ransom for each day, as Ibn Abbas and others of the Salaf interpreted it according to the reading of those who read and upon those who are able to do it meaning they are able to do it, as Ibn Mas’ud and others said. This is the choice of Al-Bukhari, for he said: As for the old man if he is not able to fast, Anas fed a poor person for each day after he grew old, a year or two after he had grown old, bread and meat, and he broke his fast. This which Al-Bukhari suspended was attributed to Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili in his Musnad, and he said: Abdullah bin Mu’adh told us, my father told us, Imran told us on the authority of Ayoub bin Abi Tamima, who said: Anas was too weak to fast, so he made a bowl of tharid, and invited thirty poor people and fed them. It was narrated by Abd bin Hamid on the authority of Ruh bin Ubadah, on the authority of Imran, who is Ibn Hadhir, on the authority of Ayoub, on his authority. Abd also narrated it from the hadith of six of the companions of Anas on the authority of Anas with the same meaning. Among the things that are included in this meaning are the pregnant woman and the breastfeeding woman if they fear for themselves or their children. There is much disagreement among the scholars concerning them. Some of them said: They break the fast, pay the ransom, and make up the fast. It was said: They pay the ransom only and do not make up the fast. It was said: They must make up the fast without ransom. It was said: They break the fast and do not pay the ransom or make up the fast. We have explained this issue in detail in the book on fasting that we devoted to it. Praise and thanks be to God.
2:185: God Almighty praises the month of fasting from among all the other months by choosing it from among them to send down the Great Qur’an, and as He singled it out for that, the hadith has been reported that it is the month in which the divine books were sent down to the prophets. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, said: Abu Saeed, the client of Banu Hashim, told us, Imran Abu al-Awam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu al-Malih, on the authority of Wathilah, meaning Ibn al-Asqa’: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The scrolls of Abraham were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, and the Torah was sent down on the sixth of Ramadan, and the Gospel was sent down on the thirteenth of Ramadan, and God sent down the Qur’an on the twenty-fourth of Ramadan.” It has been narrated from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah, in which it says: The Psalms were sent down on the twelfth of Ramadan, and the Gospel on the eighteenth, and the rest is as mentioned above. It was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. As for the scrolls, the Torah, the Psalms, and the Gospel, each of them was sent down to the prophet to whom it was sent down all at once, and as for the Qur’an, it was sent down all at once to the house of The glory of the lowest heaven, and that was in the month of Ramadan on the Night of Decree, as God Almighty said: Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree and He said: Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night then it was sent down after it in parts according to the events to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, this is how it was narrated from other sources on the authority of Ibn Abbas, as Israel said on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Al-Mujalid, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that he asked Atiyah bin Al-Aswad and he said: Doubt entered my heart, the statement of God Almighty: The month of Ramadan in which was sent down the Qur’an and His statement: Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree and it was sent down in Shawwal, and in Dhu Al-Qa’dah, and in Dhu Al-Hijjah, and in Muharram and Safar and the month of Rabi’, so Ibn Abbas said: It was sent down in Ramadan on the Night of Decree and on a blessed night all at once, then it was sent down according to the positions of the stars in measured recitation in the months and days, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh and this is its wording, and in the narration of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas he said, the Qur’an was sent down in the middle of the month of Ramadan until The lowest heaven, then it was placed in the House of Honor, then it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in twenty years to answer the people’s words. In the narration of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Qur’an was revealed in the month of Ramadan on the Night of Decree, to this lowest heaven all at once, and God would make His Prophet do whatever He willed, and the polytheists would not come with an example to argue with except that God would bring them an answer, and that is His saying: “And those who disbelieve say, ‘Why was the Qur’an not sent down to him all at once?’ Thus that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have recited it distinctly. And they do not bring you an example except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.” And His saying: A guidance for mankind and clear proofs of guidance and the criterion. This is praise for the Qur’an that God revealed as guidance for the hearts of the servants of those who believed in it, believed in it, and followed it. And clear proofs meaning clear and evident evidence and arguments for those who understood and contemplated them, indicating the correctness of what it brought of guidance that contradicts misguidance, and right guidance that contradicts error, and distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and lawful and unlawful. It was narrated from some of the predecessors: that he hated that It is said except for the month of Ramadan, and it is not said Ramadan. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad bin Bakkar bin Al-Rayyan told us, Abu Ma`shar told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka`b Al-Qurazi and Sa`id is Al-Maqburi on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Do not say Ramadan, for Ramadan is one of the names of God the Most High, but say the month of Ramadan. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Muhammad bin Ka`b something similar to that, and Ibn Abbas and Zaid bin Thabit permitted it. I said Abu Ma`shar is Najih bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Madani, the Imam of the battles and biographies, but there is weakness in it, and his son Muhammad narrated it on his authority and made it attributed to Abu Hurairah, and Al-Hafiz Ibn `Adi denounced it, and he is worthy of denial, for it is abandoned, and he made a mistake in attributing this hadith to the Prophet. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, defended this in his book and said: Chapter: It is said Ramadan, and he cited hadiths on that, including: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and in the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven, and the like, and his saying: So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it. This is an obligation imposed on whoever witnesses it. The beginning of the month, i.e. he was residing in the country when the month of Ramadan began, and he was physically healthy, he must fast without fail. This verse abrogated the previous permission for whoever was healthy and resident to break the fast and pay the ransom by feeding a poor person for each day, as was explained above. When fasting was made obligatory, he repeated the permission for the sick and the traveler to break the fast on the condition of making up for it. He said, And whoever is sick or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Its meaning is: And whoever has a sickness in his body that makes fasting difficult or harmful for him, or is on a journey, i.e. in a state of travel, then he may break the fast. So if he breaks the fast, he must make up for the days he broke the fast during the journey. For this reason, He said, God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship. i.e. He only permitted you to break the fast in a state of illness and travel, even though it is obligatory for the healthy resident, as an ease for you and a mercy to you. Here are some issues related to this verse one of them is that a group of the Salaf went to the point that whoever was residing at the beginning of the month and then traveled during it, he is not allowed to break the fast due to the excuse of travel in this case because of His saying: So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. Rather, breaking the fast is permitted for a traveler who began the month while he was traveling. This statement is strange. Abu Muhammad Ibn Hazm transmitted it in his book Al-Muhalla from a group of the Companions and Followers, and what he transmitted from them is questionable, and God knows best, for it has been proven from the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he went out in the month of Ramadan for the conquest campaign, so he traveled until he reached Al-Kadeed, then he broke the fast, and he ordered the people to break the fast. This was transmitted by the two authors of the Sahih. Second Others from the Companions and Followers went to the obligation of breaking the fast while traveling based on his saying, Then a number from other days. The correct opinion of the majority is that the matter in that is optional and not mandatory, because they used to go out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the month of Ramadan. He said: Some of us were fasting and some of us were not fasting. The fasting person did not criticize the one who was not fasting, nor the one who was not fasting criticize the one who was fasting. If breaking the fast was what was obligatory, he would have denounced their fasting. Rather, what was proven from the actions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that he was fasting in such a situation, based on what was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the month of Ramadan in intense heat, to the point that one of us would put his hand on his head from the intensity of the heat, and none of us was fasting except the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abdullah ibn Rawahah. Third A group, including al-Shafi’i, said: Fasting while traveling is better than breaking the fast based on the actions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as mentioned above. A group said: Rather, breaking the fast is better, taking advantage of the concession, and because it was proven that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about fasting while traveling, and he said: Whoever breaks the fast, it is good, and whoever fasts, there is no blame upon him. And he said in another hadith: You should follow the concession that God has granted you. And a group said: They are the same, based on the hadith of Aisha that Hamza bin Amr Al-Aslami said: O Messenger of God, I fast a lot, should I fast while traveling? He said: If you wish, then fast, and if you wish, then break the fast. And it is in the two Sahihs. And it was said: If fasting is difficult, then breaking the fast is better, based on the hadith of Jabir: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man who had been shaded, so he said: What is this? They said: He is fasting. So he said: It is not righteousness to fast while traveling.” Bukhari and Muslim. But if he turns away from the Sunnah and sees that breaking the fast is disliked, then he must break the fast, and fasting is forbidden for him. In this case, based on what came in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and others, based on the authority of Ibn Umar, Jabir, and others: Whoever does not accept the concession of God will have a sin like the mountains of Arafah. Fourth Is the judgement required to be consecutive or is it permissible to separate it? There are two opinions: One of them is that it must be consecutive because the judgement is similar to the performance. The second It is not obligatory to fast consecutively, rather if he wishes he may separate it, or if he wishes he may continue it. This is the opinion of the majority of the early and later generations, and the evidence has been proven on this basis because consecutive fasting is only obligatory in the month due to the necessity of performing it in the month. As for after the end of Ramadan, what is meant is fasting a number of days that he did not break his fast. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Then a number of other days. Then God the Almighty said: God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Salamah Al-Khuza’i told us, Ibn Hilal told us, on the authority of Humayd ibn Hilal Al-Adawi, on the authority of Abu Qatada, on the authority of the Bedouin who heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The best of your religion is the easiest, the best of your religion is the easiest. Ahmad also said: Yazid ibn Harun told us, Asim ibn Hilal told us, Amir ibn Urwah Al-Faqimi told us, Abu Urwah told me, he said: We were waiting for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he came out with his head dripping from ablution or washing, so he prayed. When he finished the prayer, the people began to ask him: Is there any difficulty for us in such-and-such? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The religion of God is in ease - he said it three times - and Imam Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it in his interpretation of this verse from the hadith of Muslim bin Ibrahim on the authority of Asim bin Hilal with it. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, Abu At-Tayyah told us, I heard Anas bin Malik say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Make things easy and do not make them difficult, and be calm and do not repel. They included it in the two Sahihs. In the two Sahihs also, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Mu`adh and Abu Musa when he sent them to Yemen: Give good tidings and do not repel, and make things easy and do not make them difficult, and cooperate and do not differ. In the Sunan and Musnads, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was sent with the easy-going Hanafi school. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Mardawayh said in his interpretation: Abdullah bin Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Yahya bin Abi Talib told us, Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, Abu Mas`ud Al-Hariri told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of Muhjan bin Al-Adra’: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he saw a man praying and he saw him for a while, so he said, “Do you think he is praying sincerely?” I said, O Messenger of God, this is the one who prays the most in Madinah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Do not hear him, lest you destroy him. He said, God intends ease for this nation and does not intend hardship for them. The meaning of his statement, God intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you, and that you may complete the number is that He only permitted you to break the fast due to illness, travel, and similar excuses because He intends ease for you, and He only commanded you to make it up so that you may complete the number of your month. His statement, And glorify God for having guided you, means that you remember God when you finish your worship, as He said, So when you have completed your rites, remember God as you remember your fathers or with a greater remembrance. And he said, “So when you have completed the prayer, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God. And remember God often that you may succeed.” And he said, “And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. And during part of the night glorify Him and at the ends of prostration.” That is why the Sunnah came with the desirability of glorifying and praising Him. And the Takbir after the obligatory prayers. Ibn Abbas said: We did not know that the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had ended except by the Takbir. For this reason, many scholars took the legitimacy of the Takbir on Eid al-Fitr from this verse: And that you may complete the number and glorify God for having guided you. Even Dawud ibn Ali al-Isfahani al-Zahiri went to the extent of its obligation on Eid al-Fitr due to the apparent command in his statement: And that you may glorify God for having guided you. In contrast to this is the school of Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, that it is not permissible to say the Takbir on Eid al-Fitr, and the rest are of the opinion that it is desirable, with differences in the details of some branches among them. And his statement: And perhaps you will be grateful means if you do what God has commanded you of obeying Him by performing His obligations, leaving His prohibitions, and observing His limits, then perhaps you will be among those who are grateful for that.
2:186: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Yahya bin Al-Mughira told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdah bin Abi Barzah Al-Sijistani, on the authority of Al-Salt bin Hakim bin Muawiyah bin Haidah Al-Qushayri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that a Bedouin said: O Messenger of God, is our Lord near so that we may talk to Him, or is He far so that we may call upon Him? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent, then God revealed: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.” If you command them to call upon Me, then call upon Me, I will respond. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Hamid Al-Razi, on the authority of Jarir, on his authority. Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Al-Sheikh Al-Asbahani narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Hamid, on the authority of Jarir, on his authority. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Jaafar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked: Where is our Lord? Then God Almighty revealed, “And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me,” the verse. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ that he was informed when the verse, And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you,’ was revealed, the people said, If only we knew at what hour we would call upon Me? Then the verse was revealed: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.” Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Wahhab bin Abdul Majeed Al Thaqafi told us, Khalid Al Hadaa’ told us on the authority of Abu Uthman Al Nahdi, on the authority of Abu Musa Al Ash’ari, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a military expedition, and we would not ascend a hill or ascend a hill or descend a valley without raising our voices in glorification. He said: He came close to us and said: “O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent, but rather you are calling upon one who is All-Hearing and All-Seeing. Indeed, the One you are calling upon is nearer to each one of you than the neck of his mount. O Abdullah bin Qais, shall I not teach you a word from the treasures of Paradise? There is no power and no strength except with God.” They included it in the two Sahihs and the rest of the group on the authority of Abu Uthman Al Nahdi, whose name was Abdul Rahman bin Mal, on his authority in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman bin Dawud told us, Shu’bah told us, Qatadah told us on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “God the Most High says: ‘I am with My servant as he thinks I am, and I am with him when he calls upon Me.’” Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir told us, Ismail ibn Ubayd God told us on the authority of Karima bint Khashkhash al-Muzaniyya, who said: Abu Hurayrah told us that he heard the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, say: “God the Most High says: ‘I am with My servant as long as he remembers Me and his lips move in remembrance of Me.’” I said This is like the saying of the Most High: Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good, and His saying to Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them: Indeed, I am with you both, hearing and seeing. What is meant by this is that the Most High does not disappoint the supplication of a supplicant, nor does anything distract Him from it, rather He is the Hearer of supplication, so in it is encouragement to supplicate, and that supplication is not lost with Him, as Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, a man told us: that he heard Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, narrating on the authority of Salman, meaning al-Farisi, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Indeed, God, the Most High, is ashamed for a servant to stretch out his hands to Him asking Him for good in them and He returns them empty. Yazid said: Name this man for me, and they said: Ja`far ibn Maymun. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Ja`far ibn Maymun, the author of al-Anmat, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib, and some of them narrated it without attributing it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, on his authority. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Amir told us, Ali bin Dawud Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji told us, on the authority of Abu Sa`id: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no Muslim who calls upon God Almighty with a supplication in which there is no sin or severing of family ties, except that God will give him one of three things: Either He will hasten his supplication for him, or He will save it for him in the Hereafter, or He will divert from him an equivalent amount of evil.” They said: Then we should make many supplications? He said: God is more. Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Mansour Al-Kousaj told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Ibn Thauban told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr: that Ubadah bin As-Samit told them: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no Muslim man on the face of the earth who calls upon God, the Almighty, with a supplication except that God will grant it to him, or will avert from him an evil equivalent to it, so long as he does not call for a sin or the severing of family ties.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf Al-Firyabi, on the authority of Ibn Thauban, who is Abdul Rahman bin Thabit bin Thauban, on his authority, and he said: It is good, authentic, strange from this source. Imam Malik said on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Ubaid, the freed slave of Ibn Azhar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: One of you will be answered as long as he is not hasty, saying, ‘I called upon God but He did not answer me.’ They narrated it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Malik on his authority, and this is the wording of Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him and reward him with Paradise. Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu At-Tahir narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to me, Muawiyah bin Salih narrated to me, on the authority of Rabia bin Yazid, on the authority of Abu Idris Al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The servant’s supplication will continue to be answered as long as he does not supplicate for a sin or the severing of family ties, as long as he is not impatient. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is impatient? He said: He says, ‘I have supplicated and supplicated, but I have not seen that I have been answered.’ So he becomes frustrated at that and stops supplicating. Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Samad narrated to us, Abu Hilal narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The servant will continue to be well as long as he is not impatient. They said: How can he be impatient? He said: He says I called upon my Lord and He did not answer me. Imam Abu Ja`far al-Tabari said in his interpretation: Yunus ibn `Abd al-A`la told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Abu Sakhr told me: Yazid ibn `Abdullah ibn Qusayt told him on the authority of `Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of `Aishah, may God be pleased with her, that she said: There is no believing servant who calls upon God with a supplication and it goes away until it is hastened for him in this world or stored up for him in the Hereafter if he does not hasten or despairs. `Urwah said: I said: O mother, how did He hasten him and make him despair? She said: He says: I asked and was not given, and I called and was not answered. Ibn Qusayt said: I heard Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab say the same as `Aishah. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi`ah told us, Bakr ibn `Amr told us on the authority of Abu `Abd al-Rahman al-Hubbali on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hearts are vessels, and some of them are more receptive than others. So if you ask God, O people, then ask Him while you are certain of the answer, for He does not answer a servant except with a weak heart.” He called upon Him from the heart of a heedless person. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ayoub told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi Nafi’ ibn Ma’dikarib told us in Baghdad, Ibn Abi Nafi’ ibn Ma’dikarib told me, he said: Aisha and I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the verse, I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon Me. He said: O Lord, the question of Aisha, so Gabriel descended and said: God sends you peace. This is My righteous servant with sincere intention and a pure heart. He says, O Lord, so I say, At Your service, and I fulfill his need. This is a strange hadith from this aspect. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Jabir bin Abdullah told me: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me’” 10:13. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, I have commanded supplication and I have entrusted myself to the response. Here I am, O God, here I am, here I am, You have no partner. Here I am, for all praise and blessings are Yours, and the kingdom has no partner. I bear witness that You are One, One, Self-Sufficient, Who neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him. I bear witness that Your promise is true, and that meeting You is true, and Paradise is true, and Hell is true, and the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and You will resurrect those in the graves.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Al-Hasan bin Yahya Al-Azdi and Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Qat’i told us, they said: Al-Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, Salih Al-Maddi told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God Almighty says, O son of Adam, one for you, one for Me, and one between Me and You. And between you, as for that which is Mine, then worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. As for that which is yours, then whatever you do of anything, I will pay it for you. As for that which is between Me and you, then from you is the supplication, and upon Me is the response.” And in His, the Most High, mentioning this verse that motivates supplication interspersed between the rulings of fasting, there is guidance to strive in supplication upon completing the number, and even upon every breaking of the fast, as Imam Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated in his Musnad: Abu Muhammad al-Maliki told us on the authority of Amr, he is the son of Shu’ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Abdullah ibn Amr, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: For the fasting person when he breaks his fast there is a supplication that is answered. So when Abdullah ibn Amr broke his fast, he would call his family and children and supplicate. Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said in his Sunan: Hisham ibn Ammar told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abdullah al-Madani, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abi Malikah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The fasting person has a supplication that will not be rejected when he breaks his fast. Ubayd God ibn Abi Malekah said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say when he broke his fast: O God, I ask You by Your mercy that encompasses all things to forgive me. In Musnad al-Imam Ahmad and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whose supplication will not be rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the oppressed. God will raise it above the clouds on the Day of Resurrection and the gates of heaven will be opened for it. He will say, ‘By My might, I will support you, even if after a while.’”
2:187: This is a concession from God Almighty to the Muslims, and a lifting of what was the case at the beginning of Islam, for if one of them broke his fast, he was only permitted to eat, drink and have intercourse until the evening prayer or sleep before that, so when he slept or prayed the evening prayer, food, drink and intercourse were forbidden to him until the next night, so they found great difficulty in that, and the obscenity here is intercourse, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ata’, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Tawus, Salim bin Abdullah, Amr bin Dinar, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Zuhri, Al-Dahhak, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Suddi, Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Muqatil bin Hayyan, and his saying They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: meaning they are a dwelling for you and you are a dwelling for them, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: They are a blanket for you and you are a blanket for them, and the gist of it is: the man and the woman each mix with the other and touch and sleep with him, so it was appropriate to grant them a concession in Intercourse during the night of Ramadan, lest it be difficult for them and make them feel embarrassed. The poet said: If the bedfellow bends her neck, she falls and becomes like a garment for him The reason for the revelation of this verse is as mentioned in the long hadith of Muadh. Abu Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib: If a man of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was fasting and slept before breaking his fast, he would not eat for a similar period. Qais bin Sarmah Al-Ansari was fasting and that day he was working in his land. When it was time to break his fast, he came to his wife and said: Do you have any food? She said: No, but I will go and look for some for you. Sleep overcame him and he slept. His wife came and when she saw him sleeping she said: What a disappointment! Did you sleep? When it was noon, he fainted and mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: “Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives. They are your garments and you are their garments. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has ordained for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread.” They rejoiced greatly at that. Al-Bukhari’s wording here is from Abu Ishaq: I heard Al-Baraa’ say: When the fast of Ramadan was revealed, they would not approach women all of Ramadan, and there were men who were deceiving themselves, so God revealed: God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you and pardoned you. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When the Muslims prayed the ‘Isha’ prayer in the month of Ramadan, women and food were forbidden to them until the same time the following day. Then some of the Muslims had intercourse with women and food in the month of Ramadan after the ‘Isha’ prayer, among them ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattab, so they complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he (Peace be upon him) said: “God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them” (Al-Awfi: 113). And Musa bin Uqbah narrated on the authority of Kurayb on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Before the revelation of what was revealed about fasting was revealed about them, the people used to eat and drink and it was permissible for them to do things with women. So if one of them slept, he would not eat or drink and would not have intercourse with his wife until he broke his fast the following day. It has reached us that after Umar bin Al-Khattab slept and fasting was obligatory upon him, he had intercourse with his wife, then he came to the Prophet (Peace be upon him) and said: I complain to God and to you about what I did. He said: What did you do? He said: My soul tempted me, so I had intercourse with my wife after I slept, and I wanted to fast. They claimed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You were not worthy of doing that. Then the Book was revealed: Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives. Sa`d ibn Abi `Aruba said on the authority of Qays ibn Sa`d, on the authority of `Ata` ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, regarding the words of God Almighty: “Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives. They are your garments and you are their garments. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has ordained for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread. Then complete the fast until the night.” He said: Before this verse was revealed, if the Muslims prayed the last `Isha’ prayer, food, drink, and women were forbidden to them until they broke their fast. And `Umar ibn al-Khattab had intercourse with his wife after the `Isha’ prayer, and Surmah ibn Qays al-Ansari was overcome by sleep after the Maghrib prayer, so he slept and was not satisfied. Food, and he did not wake up until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the evening prayer, so he got up and ate and drank, and when morning came he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of that, so God revealed at that time: Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives meaning by the approach is intercourse with women “They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them. God knows that you were betraying yourselves” meaning you were having intercourse with women and eating and drinking after the evening prayer So He turned to you and pardoned you, so now go to them meaning have intercourse with them and seek what God has decreed for you meaning children and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread, then complete the fast until nightfall so that was forgiveness and mercy from God, and Hisham said on the authority of Hisayn ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, got up and said: O Messenger of God, I wanted to have intercourse with my wife last night in the way a man wants his wife, and she said: She had fallen asleep, so I thought she was ill so I had intercourse with her, so it was revealed in Umar said: It is permissible for you to have sexual relations with your wives on the night of fasting. This is how Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila. Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abu Lahi’ah, Musa ibn Jubayr, the freed slave of Banu Salamah, told me that he heard Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik narrating on the authority of his father who said: When a man fasted during Ramadan and went to sleep in the evening, food, drink, and women were forbidden to him until he broke his fast the next day. Umar ibn al-Khattab returned from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night, and he had spent the evening with him. He found that his wife had fallen asleep, so he wanted to see her. She said: I slept. He said: You did not sleep. Then he had intercourse with her. Ka’b ibn Malik did the same thing. Umar ibn al-Khattab went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. Then God revealed: “God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you and pardoned you. So now have sexual relations with them.” This is how it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and others regarding the reason for the revelation of this verse about Umar. Ibn Al-Khattab and whoever did as he did, and in Sarmah Ibn Qais, he permitted sexual intercourse and eating and drinking throughout the night out of mercy, permission and gentleness. And His statement: And seek what God has decreed for you, Abu Hurairah, Ibn Abbas, Anas, Shuraih al-Qadi, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ata’, al-Rabi’ bin Anas, al-Suddi, Zaid bin Aslam, al-Hakam bin Utbah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others said: He means children. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: And seek what God has decreed for you, meaning sexual intercourse. Amr bin Malik al-Bakri said on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And seek what God has decreed for you, he said: The Night of Decree. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, he said: Qatadah said: Seek the dispensation that God has decreed for you, meaning: what God has made lawful for you. Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: How do you read this verse: And seek what God has decreed for you? He said: Whichever you want, you should read it with the first one. Ibn Jarir chose that the verse is more general than all of this. And His saying, And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night], then complete the fast until the nightfall, God Almighty permitted eating and drinking, along with what was mentioned previously regarding the permissibility of sexual intercourse at any time of the night the fasting person wishes until the light of morning becomes distinct from the blackness of night. He expressed this by saying, The white thread is distinct from the black thread, and removed the ambiguity by saying, From dawn, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Abu Abdullah al-Bukhari: Ibn Abi Maryam told me, Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Mutraf told us, Abu Hazim told us on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d, who said: And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread was revealed, but From dawn was not revealed. When men wanted to fast, one of them would tie a white thread and a black thread to his feet, and he would continue eating until he could clearly see them. Then God revealed after From dawn, so they knew that He meant night and day. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Husayn told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, Adi bin Hatim told me: When this verse was revealed, And eat and drink until the white thread of the night becomes distinct to you from the black thread, I returned to two ropes: one black and the other white. He said: So I put them under my pillow. He said: So I began to look at them, and when the white became distinct to me from the black, I stopped. When morning came, I went to the Messenger of God and told him what I had done. He said: “Then your pillow is wide. That is only the whiteness of the day from the blackness of the night.” They included it in the two Sahihs from different chains of transmission on the authority of Adi. The meaning of his saying: Then your pillow is wide is that it could hold the two threads: the black thread and the white thread intended in this verse underneath it, for they are the whiteness of the day and the blackness of the night, so it requires that it be as wide as the east and the west. This is how it appears in the narration of Al-Bukhari, interpreted as follows: Musa bin Ismail told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Hissain, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi, who said: Adi took a white rope and a rope. Black, until part of the night he looked but could not distinguish between them, so when morning came he said, O Messenger of God, I put it under my pillow, he said, then your pillow is wide, if the white and black thread is under your pillow>and it came in some versions that your nape is wide, so some of them interpreted it as dullness, and it is weak, rather it goes back to this because if his pillow is wide then his nape is also wide, and God knows best. And it is also interpreted by the narration of Al-Bukhari, Qutaybah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, he said I said, O Messenger of God, what is the white thread from the black thread, are they the two threads? He said: Your nape is wide if you see the two threads, then he said: No, rather it is the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day. And in His permission, the Almighty, of eating until dawn is evidence of the desirability of Suhoor, because it is a type of concession and taking it is beloved. For this reason, the authentic Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reported urging Suhoor. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Eat Suhoor, for there is a blessing in Suhoor. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Amr ibn al-‘As, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The separation between our fasting and the fasting of the People of the Book is the Suhoor meal. And Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn ‘Isa, who is Ibn al-Tabba’, told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Suhoor is a blessed meal, so do not neglect it, even if one of you takes a sip of water, for God and His angels send blessings on those who eat Suhoor. And many hadiths have been reported encouraging Suhoor, even if it is just a sip of water, imitating those who eat Suhoor. And it is desirable to delay it until the time of dawn, as it was reported in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: We had our suhoor with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then we got up to pray. Anas said: I said to Zaid: How much time was there between the call to prayer and the suhoor? He said: About fifty verses. Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Salim bin Ghailan, on the authority of Sulayman bin Abi Uthman, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim al-Himsi, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My nation will continue to be fine as long as they hasten to break their fast and delay the suhoor. Many hadiths have been narrated in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called it the blessed food. In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said: We ate suhoor with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was daytime except that the sun had not risen. This is a hadith narrated only by Asim bin Abi al-Najud, al-Nasa’i said, and he interpreted it as meaning that what is meant is the nearness of daytime, as God, the Most High, said: And when they have reached their term, either keep them on acceptable terms or part from them on acceptable terms. That is, they are close to the end of their waiting period, so either keep them on acceptable terms or leave them for good. What he said is what is required to interpret the hadith as they ate suhoor without being certain. The dawn has come, so much so that some of them thought that it had come and some of them did not realize that. It has been narrated from a large group of the Salaf that they were lenient with regard to the pre-dawn meal when the dawn was approaching. This was narrated from Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Hudhayfah, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Thabit, and from a large group of the Tabi’un, including Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, Abu Majlaz, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Abu al-Dhaha, Abu Wa’il, and others from the companions of Ibn Masoud, Ata’, al-Hasan, al-Hakim ibn Uyaynah, Mujahid, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Abu al-Sha’tha’ Jabir ibn Zayd, and al-A’mash and Jabir ibn Rashid agreed with this view. We have documented the chains of transmission for this in the Book of Single Fasting, praise be to God. Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir narrated in his interpretation from some of them that it is obligatory to abstain from eating and drinking from sunrise, just as it is permissible to break the fast at sunset. I said I do not think that any of the people of knowledge would accept this statement, because it contradicts the text of the Qur’an in its saying: “And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn appears to you distinct from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the nightfall.” It was reported in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Al-Qasim on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not let the call to prayer of Bilal prevent you from your suhoor, for he calls at night, so eat and drink until you hear the call to prayer of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he does not call to prayer until dawn breaks.” The wording of Al-Bukhari. Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Muhammad bin Jabir told us on the authority of Qais bin Talq on the authority of his father that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The dawn is not the one that extends over the horizon, but the red one that appears across the horizon. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it with the wording: Eat and drink, and do not let the rising bright light mislead you, so eat and drink until the red one appears across the horizon. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of a sheikh from Banu Qushair, I heard Samurah bin Jundub say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s Messenger (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: Do not be deceived by Bilal’s call or this whiteness until dawn breaks or the dawn appears. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah and others, on the authority of Sawad bin Hanzalah, on the authority of Samurah, who said: The Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: Do not let Bilal’s call to prayer or the prolonged dawn prevent you from your suhoor meal, but it is the dawn that spreads in the horizon. He said: And Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sawadah Al-Qushayri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said: The Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: Do not let Bilal’s call to prayer or this whiteness - the pillar of dawn - deceive you until it spreads. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Zuhair bin Harb, on the authority of Ismail bin Ibrahim, he is Ibn Ulayyah, the same, and Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: Do not let Bilal’s call to prayer prevent any of you from his suhoor meal, or he said Bilal’s call, for Bilal is… It is called at night, or he said it is called to wake up your sleepers and to return your standing ones, and the dawn is not to say thus and thus until it says thus. And he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of al-Taymi, and al-Hasan ibn al-Zubayr al-Nakha’i told me, Abu Usamah told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Thawban, and it is rather the rising that takes over the horizon, so it makes prayer permissible and food forbidden, and this is a good mursal. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’: I heard Ibn Abbas say: They are two dawns, as for the one that shines in the sky, it does not make anything permissible or forbidden, but the dawn that shines on the tops of the mountains is the one that makes drinking forbidden. And Ata’ said: As for if it shines brightly in the sky, and its brightness is that it goes long in the sky, then it does not make the drink of the fasting person forbidden, nor does it make the Hajj null and void, but if it spreads over the tops of the mountains, it makes drinking forbidden for the fasting and makes the Hajj null and void. And this is a sound chain of transmission back to Ibn Abbas and Ata’, and this is how it was narrated on the authority of more than one of the predecessors, may God have mercy on them. Question And whoever made dawn the end of the permissibility of sexual intercourse, food and drink for whoever wants to fast, he provides evidence that whoever wakes up in a state of ritual impurity should perform ghusl and complete his fast and there is no blame upon him. This is the doctrine of the four imams and the majority of scholars, past and present, based on what was narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim from the hadith of Aisha and Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with them, that they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would wake up in a state of ritual impurity from sexual intercourse, not from a wet dream, then he would perform ghusl and fast. And in the hadith of Umm Salamah, according to them: Then he would not break his fast or make it up. And in Sahih Muslim from Aisha, that a man said: O Messenger of God, the prayer comes upon me while I am in a state of ritual impurity, so should I fast? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And the time for prayer comes when I am in a state of ritual impurity, so I fast. He said: You are not like us, O Messenger of God, for God has forgiven you your past and future sins. He said: By God, I hope that I will be the most fearful of God among you and the most knowledgeable of what I should avoid. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If the call to prayer is made for the dawn prayer and one of you is in a state of ritual impurity, then he should not fast that day. It is a hadith with a good chain of transmission according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, as you can see. It is in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of al-Fadl ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in Sunan al-Nasa’i on his authority on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd and al-Fadl ibn Abbas, but he did not attribute it to the Prophet. Some scholars attributed this hadith to this, and some of them went to it. This is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Salim, Ata’, Hisham ibn Urwah, and al-Hasan al-Basri. Some of them went to the distinction between someone who wakes up in a state of ritual impurity sleeping, and there is no blame on him, based on the hadith of Aisha and Umm al-Qayyim. Salamah, or by choice, then he has no fast, according to the hadith of Abu Hurairah. This is narrated from Urwah, Tawus, and Al-Hasan. Some of them differentiated between the obligatory fast, which is completed and he makes it up, and the voluntary fast, which does not harm him. It was narrated by Al-Thawri from Mansur, from Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and it is also a narration from Al-Hasan Al-Basri. Some of them claimed that the hadith of Abu Hurairah was abrogated by the hadiths of Aisha and Umm Salamah, but there is no history with it. Ibn Hazm claimed that it was abrogated by this verse, and this is also far-fetched, as there is no history, rather the apparent meaning of the history is the opposite. Some of them interpreted the hadith of Abu Hurairah as denying perfection, so he has no fast, according to the hadith of Aisha and Umm Salamah, which indicate permissibility. This approach is the closest and most comprehensive of the sayings, and God knows best. Then complete the fast until nightfall. Breaking the fast at sunset is a legal ruling, as stated in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When night comes from here and day departs from here, the fasting person has broken his fast. And on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d al-Sa`idi, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: People will continue to be fine as long as they hasten to break the fast. They both reported it. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, Al-Awza`i told us, Qurrah ibn `Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “God Almighty says: The most beloved of My servants to Me is the one who hastens to break the fast.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from other chains of narration on the authority of Al-Awza`i, and he said: This is a good, strange hadith. Ahmad also said: `Affan told us, `Ubayd God ibn Iyad told us, I heard Iyad ibn Laqit, I heard Layla, the wife of Bashir ibn al-Khasasiyah, who said: I wanted to fast two days continuously, but Bashir prevented me and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given two days of fasting, and I... God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade it and said, “The Christians do that, but fast as God has commanded you, then complete the fast until nightfall, and when nightfall comes, break your fast.” That is why the authentic hadiths forbade continuous fasting, which is to fast one day after another and not eat anything in between. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not fast continuously. They said: O Messenger of God, you fast continuously. He said: I am not like you, I spend the night with my Lord feeding me and giving me drink. They did not stop fasting continuously, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued with them for two days and two nights, then they saw the crescent moon, and he said: If the crescent moon had been delayed, I would have increased it for you, as if he was punishing them. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri with it, and they also included the prohibition of continuous fasting from the hadith of Anas and Ibn Umar, and from Aisha, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade continuous fasting out of mercy for them, so they said: You fast continuously. He said: “I am not like you. My Lord feeds me and gives me drink.” It has been proven that it is forbidden from more than one source, and it has been proven that it is one of the characteristics of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he was able to do that and was helped. What is most apparent is that this food and drink in his case was only spiritual, not physical. Otherwise, it would not be connected to the physical. But as the poet said: She has conversations about your memory that distract her from drinking and divert her from food. As for the one who wants to abstain from eating after sunset until the time of dawn, he may do so, as in the hadith of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not continue eating. Whoever among you wants to continue eating, let him continue eating until dawn.” They said: “You continue eating, O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” He said: “I am not like you. I have food to feed me and a cupbearer to drink.” They also included it in the two Sahihs. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Nu`aym told us, Abu Isra`il al-`Absi told us on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Hafs, on the authority of Umm Walad Hatib ibn Abi Balta`ah: that she passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was eating the pre-dawn meal, so he invited her to eat. She said: I am fasting. He said: How do you fast? So I mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Where are you from the connection with the family of Muhammad from dawn to dawn? Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of Ali: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to fast from dawn to dawn. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr and others from the Salaf: that they used to fast for several days, and he interpreted it from them to mean that they used to do that as a form of exercise for themselves, not that they used to do it as an act of worship, and God knows best. It is possible that they understood from the prohibition that it was guidance from the perspective of compassion, as came in the hadith of Aisha: Mercy for them, so Ibn al-Zubayr and his son Amir and those who followed their path would take the trouble to do that and do it, because they found the strength to do it. It was mentioned about them that they would first break their fast with butter and aloes lest the intestines be ruptured by food first. It was narrated about Ibn al-Zubayr that he used to fast for seven days and on the seventh day he would become the strongest and most patient of them. Abu al-A’liyah said: God only imposed fasting during the day, so when night comes, whoever wants to eat may eat and whoever wants not to eat may not eat. God the Almighty said: And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This is about a man who is in retreat in the mosque during Ramadan or other than Ramadan, so God has forbidden him to have sexual relations with women at night or during the day until he completes his retreat. Ad-Dahhak said: If a man is in retreat and leaves the mosque, he may have sexual intercourse if he wishes, so God the Almighty said: And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques. That is, do not approach them as long as you are in retreat in the mosque or elsewhere. And Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: They used to do that until this verse was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, Muhammad ibn Ka`b, Mujahid, Ata`, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Rabi` ibn Anas, and Muqatil, that they said: He should not approach her while he is in i`tikaf. What he narrated on the authority of these people is the matter agreed upon by the scholars, that women are forbidden to the one in i`tikaf as long as he is in i`tikaf in his mosque. If he goes to his house for an unavoidable need, it is not permissible for him to remain there except for the amount of time he needs to complete that need, such as relieving himself or eating. He is not allowed to kiss his wife or hug her, and he should not be occupied with anything other than his i`tikaf. He should not visit the sick, but he should ask about him while he is passing by. There are detailed rulings on i`tikaf in its chapter, some of which are agreed upon by the scholars and some of which are disputed. We have mentioned a good portion of that at the end of the Book of Fasting, praise and thanks be to God. For this reason, the jurists who compiled the books followed the Book of Fasting with the Book of i`tikaf, following the example of the Noble Qur’an, for it drew attention to the mention of i`tikaf. After mentioning fasting. And in His Almighty’s mention, seclusion after fasting is guidance and a warning about seclusion during fasting or at the end of the month of fasting, as it was proven in the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to seclude himself during the last ten days of Ramadan until God, the Almighty, took him, then his wives secluded themselves after him. They narrated it from the hadith of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her. In the two Sahihs, it is narrated that Safiyyah bint Huyayy used to visit the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was secluding himself in the mosque. She talked with him for an hour, then got up to go back to her home. That was at night, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, got up to walk with her until she reached her home, and her home was in the home of Usama bin Zaid on the outskirts of Medina. When he was on some of the way, two men from the Ansar met him. When they saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they hurried, and in another narration: they hid, meaning out of shyness from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because his family was with him. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Take it easy, she is Safiyyah bint Huyayy, meaning do not hurry, and know that she is Safiyyah bint Huyayy, meaning My wife, they said: Glory be to God, O Messenger of God, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The devil runs through the son of Adam as blood runs, and I feared that he might throw something, or he said: evil, into your hearts.” Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: He, peace be upon him, wanted to teach his nation to disavow accusations in their proper place, lest they fall into something forbidden, and they were too pious to suspect anything of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God knows best. Then what is meant by direct contact is sexual intercourse and its motives, such as kissing, embracing, and the like. As for giving something and the like, there is nothing wrong with it. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would bring his head close to me and I would touch his feet while I was menstruating, and he would not enter the house except for a human need. Aisha said: The sick person would be in the house, and I would not ask about him except when I was passing by. His saying, These are the limits of God, means this that we have explained, imposed, and defined of fasting and its rulings, what we have permitted in it, what we have forbidden, and what we have mentioned. His goals, concessions and determinations are the limits of God, that is, God has legislated them and made them clear himself, so do not approach them, that is, do not exceed them or transgress them. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil used to say in his statement, These are the limits of God, that is, to have sexual relations during i’tikaf. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: He meant these four limits, and he would recite, “Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives. They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have sexual relations with them and seek what God has ordained for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread.
