Then complete the fast until the night.” He said: My father and others from our sheikhs used to say this and recite it to us: Thus does God make clear His verses to the people, that is, just as He made clear fasting, its rulings, laws and details, so does He make clear all the rulings on the tongue of His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people that they may fear God, that is, they may know how to be guided and how to obey, as God, the Most High, said, “It is He who He sends down to His servant clear signs that He may bring you out from darkness into the light. And indeed, God is to you Kind and Merciful.
2:188: Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This is about a man who owes money and has no evidence for it, so he denies the money and takes the case to the judges, knowing that he is right, and he knows that he is a sinner who has eaten what is forbidden. This is also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, that they said: Do not take the case to court while you know that you are unjust. It was narrated in the two Sahihs on the authority of Umm Salamah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Behold, I am only a human being, and the opponents come to me, and perhaps some of you will be more eloquent in their argument than others, so I will rule in his favor. So whoever I rule in his favor regarding the right of a Muslim, then it is only a piece of fire, so let him carry it or leave it.” This noble verse and this hadith indicate that the ruling of the judge does not change something in reality, so he does not make permissible in reality something forbidden that is forbidden, nor does he make permissible something that is permissible, but it is only binding on the outside. If it matches in reality, then that is it, otherwise the judge gets his reward and the fraudster gets the penalty. And his burden, and for this reason the Almighty said: And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly or send it [in bribery] to the rulers in order to consume a portion of the wealth of the people in sin while you know. That is, you know the falsehood of what you claim and promote in your speech. Qatada said: Know, O son of Adam, that the judge’s ruling does not make permissible for you what is forbidden and does not justify for you what is false. Rather, the judge rules according to what he sees and what the witnesses testify to. The judge is a human being who makes mistakes and is right. Know that whoever has been ruled in favor of unjustly, his dispute will not be resolved until God brings them together on the Day of Resurrection, and He will rule against the one who is wronged in favor of the one who is right in a better way than what the one who is wronged ruled against the one who is right in this world.
2:189: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the new moons, so this verse was revealed: “They ask you about the new moons. Say, ‘They are markers of time for the people.’” They know by them the resolution of their religion, the number of their wives, and the time of their Hajj. Abu Ja`far said on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah: It has reached us that they said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, why were the new moons created? Then God revealed: “They ask you about the new moons. Say: They are marks of time.” He says: God has made them marks of time for the Muslims to fast and break their fast, the number of their wives, and the place of their religion. This is what was narrated from Ata’, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, something similar to this. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Abd Al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawad on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has made the new moons marks of time for the people, so fast when you see them, and break your fast when you see them. If it is hidden from you, then count thirty days.” Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Abi Rawad with it, and he said: He was trustworthy, a pious, diligent man of noble lineage, so his chain of transmission is sound, and they did not include it. Muhammad ibn Jabir said on the authority of Qays ibn Talq on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God said: God has made the new moons, so when you see the new moon, then fast, and when you see it, then break your fast, and if it is hidden from you, then complete the count as thirty days. This was also narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and from the words of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. And his saying: “And righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is of him who fears God. And enter houses from their doors.” Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah bin Musa told us on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: When they entered ihram in the pre-Islamic era, they would enter the House from its back, so God revealed: “And righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is of him who fears God. And enter houses from their doors.” And Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi narrated it likewise on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: When the Ansar returned from their journey, a man would not enter from his door, so this verse was revealed. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir: The Quraysh were called Al-Hams, and they would enter from the doors in ihram, and the Ansar and the rest of the Arabs would not enter from a door in ihram. So while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in a garden, he came out from its door, and Qutbah bin Amir from the Ansar came out with him, so they said: O Messenger of God, Qutbah bin Amir is a merchant. And he went out with you from the door, so he said to him: What made you do what you did? He said: I saw you do it, so I did as you did, so he said: I am a fool, he said to him: My religion is your religion. Then God revealed: “It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is of him who fears God. And enter houses from their doors.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Awfi narrated it from Ibn Abbas in a similar manner. It was also narrated from Mujahid, Al-Zuhri, Qatadah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Suddi, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: When some people from the pre-Islamic era wanted to travel and left their houses for the journey for which they had set out, then after leaving they decided to stay and abandon their journey, they would not enter the house from its door but would climb over it from its back. So God, the Most High, said: It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, the verse. Muhammad bin Ka’b said: When a man was in seclusion, he would not enter his house from the door of the house, so God revealed this verse. Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said: When the people of Yathrib returned from their Eid, they would enter their houses from their backs, and they thought that this was closer to righteousness. So God said: It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, and they did not think that this was closer to righteousness. And His statement: And fear God that you may be righteous. “You will succeed” means fear God, so do what He has commanded you to do and leave what He has forbidden you to do so that you may succeed tomorrow when you stand before Him and He will reward you for your perfection and completeness.
2:190: Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, regarding the words of God Almighty: And fight in the way of God those who fight you, he said: This is the first verse revealed about fighting in Medina. When it was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought whoever fought him and refrained from whoever refrained from him, until Surat Bara`ah was revealed. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same, until he said: This was abrogated by His words: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. There is a consideration in this, because His words those who fight you are only an incitement and enticement to the enemies whose concern is to fight Islam and its people, meaning just as they fight you, so kill them, as He said: And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together. That is why He said in the verse: And kill them wherever you find them and expel them from where they have expelled you, meaning so that your concern will be directed towards fighting them, just as their concern is directed towards fighting you and expelling them from their country. From which they expelled you as retribution. And his saying: “And do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” That is, fight in the cause of God, and do not transgress in that, and that includes committing the forbidden acts, as Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: such as mutilation, stealing, killing women, children, and the elderly, those who have no opinion and do not fight, and monks and those who keep monasteries, burning trees, and killing animals for no benefit, as Ibn Abbas, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and others said. For this reason, it came in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Buraidah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Fight in the cause of God and fight those who disbelieve in God. Fight and do not steal, do not betray, do not mutilate, and do not kill children or those who keep monasteries.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out his armies, he would say: “Go out in the name of God and fight in the cause of God those who disbelieve in God. Do not transgress, do not steal, do not mutilate, and do not kill children or those who keep monasteries.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad, and by Abu Dawud on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. In the Two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: A woman was found killed in one of the battles of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, denounced the killing of women and children. Imam Ahmad said: Mus`ab ibn Salam told us, Al-Ahlaj told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Abi Muslim, on the authority of Rib`i ibn Harash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us one, three, five, seven, nine, and eleven examples. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us one example and left out the rest. He said: “A people who were weak and poor fought people of tyranny and enmity. Then God made the weak prevail over them, so they turned to their enemy and used them and gave them authority, so they incurred God’s wrath upon them until the Day of Resurrection.” This is a hadith with a good chain of transmission, and its meaning is that when these weak people gained power over the strong and transgressed against them and used them in a way that was not appropriate for them, they incurred God’s wrath upon them because of this transgression. There are many hadiths and reports on this. Since jihad involves the loss of lives and the killing of men, God Almighty pointed out that what they are committing of disbelief in God, associating partners with Him, and turning people away from His path is more severe, more severe, more grievous, and more devastating than killing. Imam Ahmad said: Mus`ab ibn Salam told us, Al-Ahlaj told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Abi Muslim, on the authority of Rib`i ibn Harash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us one, three, five, seven, nine, and eleven examples. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us one example and left out the rest. He said: “A people who were weak and poor fought people of tyranny and enmity. Then God made the weak prevail over them, so they turned to their enemy and used them and gave them authority, so they incurred God’s wrath upon them until the Day of Resurrection.” This is a hadith with a good chain of transmission, and its meaning is that when these weak people gained power over the strong and transgressed against them and used them in a way that was not appropriate for them, they incurred God’s wrath upon them because of this transgression. There are many hadiths and reports on this. Since jihad involves the loss of lives and the killing of men, God Almighty pointed out that what they are committing of disbelief in God, associating partners with Him, and turning people away from His path is more severe, more severe, more grievous, and more devastating than killing. For this reason, He said: And persecution is worse than killing. Abu Malik said: That is, what you are committing is greater than killing. And for this reason he said: And persecution is worse than killing, meaning polytheism is worse than killing. And his saying: And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque, as it came in the two Sahihs, “Indeed, this city was made sacred by God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection, and it was not permitted except for an hour of the day, and this is my hour, sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Its trees should not be cut down, nor should one seclude oneself in its seclusion. If anyone seeks permission to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then say: God gave permission to His Messenger and did not give you permission.” By that he meant, may God bless him and grant him peace, his fighting his people on the day of the conquest of Mecca, for he conquered it by force and some of their men were killed at the servants’ quarters. It was said that it was a peace treaty, based on his saying: Whoever closes his door is safe, and whoever enters the mosque is safe, and whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe. And his saying: “Until they fight you therein. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.” God the Almighty says: And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque unless they initiate fighting against you therein, then you will have it then.” Fighting and killing them to repel the attacker, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged allegiance to his companions on the day of Hudaybiyyah under the tree to fight, when the clans of Quraysh and those who supported them from the tribes of Thaqeef and the Abyssinians conspired against him at that time. Then God stopped the fighting between them, saying, And it is He who stopped their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them. And He said, “And had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, lest you trample them and there should befall you on their part a sin without knowledge, that God might admit into His mercy whom He willed. Had they separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.” And His statement, But if they desist, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning if they stop fighting in the sanctuary and return to Islam and repentance, then God will forgive their sins, even if they had killed Muslims in the sanctuary of God, for no sin is too great for Him to forgive for whoever repents to Him from it. Then God commanded fighting the disbelievers until there is no fitnah, meaning polytheism, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Rabi’. And Muqatil bin Hayyan, Al-Suddi and Zaid bin Aslam said: And the religion will be for God meaning that the religion of God will be the apparent and supreme over all other religions, as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who fights bravely, fights out of pride, and fights to show off, which of them is in the way of God? He said: Whoever fights so that the word of God will be supreme is in the way of God. And in the two Sahihs: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ If they say it, then their blood and property are protected from me except for a right, and their reckoning is with God.” And His statement: But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers. God Almighty says: “If they desist from what they are doing of polytheism and fighting the believers, then refrain from them, for whoever fights them after that is a wrongdoer, and there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers.” This is the meaning of Mujahid’s statement that only those who fight should be fought should be fought, or its meaning could be that if they desist, then they are freed from the wrong, which is polytheism, so there is no aggression against them after that. What is meant by aggression here is punishment and fighting, as in His statement: So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. And His statement: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it. “And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished.” For this reason, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: The wrongdoer is the one who refused to say There is no god but God. Al-Bukhari said: His statement: And fight them until there is no more persecution is the verse. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Ubaydullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: Two men came to him during the persecution of Ibn al-Zubayr and said: The people… They were lost, and you are the son of Omar and the companion of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so what prevents you from going out? He said: What prevents me is that God has made my brother’s blood sacred. They said: Didn’t God say, And fight them until there is no more persecution? He said: We fought until there was no more persecution and religion was for God, and you want to fight until there is more persecution and religion is for other than God. Uthman bin Saleh added on the authority of Ibn Wahb, so-and-so and Haywah bin Shuraih informed me on the authority of Bakr bin Omar Al-Maghafari, that Bakir bin Abdullah told him on the authority of Nafi’ that a man came to Ibn Omar and said: O Abu Abdul Rahman, what made you perform Hajj one year and stay in Hajj the next year and abandon Jihad in the way of God Almighty, when you know what God desires? He said: O my nephew, Islam is built on five: belief in God and His Messenger, the five daily prayers, fasting Ramadan, paying zakat, and Hajj to the House. They said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, do you not hear what God mentioned in His Book: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of God.” And fight them until there is no more Fitnah. He said: We did that during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Islam was few, so a man would be tempted in his religion, either they would kill him or torture him, until Islam became widespread and there was no more Fitnah. He said: What do you say about Ali and Uthman? He said: As for Uthman, God forgave him, but as for you, you hated that He should forgive him. As for Ali, he is the cousin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his son-in-law. He pointed with his hand and said: This is his house where you can see.
2:194: Ikrimah said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, Qatadah, Muqsim, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Ata' and others, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out to perform Umrah in the year six of the Hijrah and the polytheists prevented him from entering and reaching the House and prevented him and the Muslims who were with him, in Dhul-Qa'dah, which was a sacred month, until he had settled the matter with them regarding entering the following year, so he entered it the following year, he and those who were from the Muslims, and God took revenge on them, so this verse was revealed regarding that: A sacred month for a sacred month, and for sacred things there is retaliation. Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Laith bin Sa'd told us, on the authority of Abu Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not go on a raid in the sacred month, unless he was raided and raided, and when he attended it, he stayed until it passed. This is a sound chain of transmission. That is why when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed, while he was camping at Al-Hudaibiyah, that Uthman had been killed, and he had sent him on a message to the polytheists, he pledged allegiance to his companions, who were one thousand four hundred, under the tree, to fight the polytheists. But when he was informed that Uthman had not been killed, he stopped doing that and turned towards peace and reconciliation, and what happened happened. And also when he finished fighting Hawazin on the day of Hunayn, and fortified himself against them in Taif, he turned to it and besieged it, and entered Dhu al-Qi'dah while he was besieging it with a catapult, and he continued on it until forty days were complete as was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, and when the killing of his companions increased, he turned away from it and it was not conquered, then he returned back to Mecca and performed Umrah from Al-Juhfah where he divided the spoils of Hunayn, and this Umrah of his was also in Dhu al-Qi'dah, in the year eight, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And his saying: So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you commanded justice even towards the polytheists, as he said: And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished and he said: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it. And Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his saying: So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you was revealed in Mecca where there was no power or jihad, then it was abrogated by the verse of fighting in Medina, and Ibn Jarir rejected this statement, and he said: Rather, the verse is Medinan after the Umrah of the issue, and this was attributed to Mujahid, may God have mercy on him. His saying: And fear God and know that God is with the righteous is an order to them to obey God and fear Him, and informing Him that the Almighty is with those who fear Him with victory and support in this world and the hereafter.
2:195: Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq told us, Al-Nadr told us, Shu'bah told us, Sulayman, I heard Abu Wa'il from Hudhayqah, And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction, he said: It was revealed about spending. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah from Abu Mu'awiyah from Al-A'mash, similarly. He said: It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ata', Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Muqatil bin Hayyan, something similar to that. Al-Layth bin Sa'd said from Yazid bin Abi Habib from Aslam Abu Imran, he said: A man from the Muhajireen in Constantinople charged the enemy's ranks until he broke through them, and with us was Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari. Some people said: He threw himself into destruction. Abu Ayyub said: We know best about this verse. It was only revealed about us. We accompanied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we witnessed the battles with him and supported him. When Islam spread and became apparent, we, the Ansar, gathered together as a group of confidants. We said: God has honored us by making us companions of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and by supporting him, until Islam spread and its followers increased in number. We had preferred it over our families, wealth and children. The war has ended, so we will return to our families and children and reside there. Then the verse was revealed about us: And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction. So destruction was in residing with our families and wealth and abandoning jihad. Narrated by Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Abd bin Hamid in his Tafsir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la in his Musnad, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, all from the hadith of Yazid bin Abi Habib with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih gharib, and Al-Hakim said: It meets the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Aslam Abu Imran: We were in Constantinople and Uqba bin Amir was in charge of the people of Egypt, and a man was in charge of the people of Ash-Sham who wanted Fadala bin Ubayd. A large column of Romans came out of the city, so we lined up for them. A man from the Muslims attacked the Romans until he entered among them, then he came out to us. The people shouted at him and said: Glory be to God, he threw himself into destruction. Abu Ayyub said: O people, you are interpreting this verse in a way that is not correct, but it was revealed about us, the Ansar. When God made His religion victorious and its supporters increased, we said among ourselves: If we turned to our wealth and repaired it, then God revealed this verse. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Sabi’i that a man said to Al-Bara’ bin Azib: If I attacked the enemy alone and they killed me, would I have thrown myself into destruction? He said: No, God said to His Messenger: Then fight in the way of God, you are not charged except with yourself, and this is only in the expenditure. It was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Israel from Abu Ishaq, and he said it is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Qays bin Al-Rabi’ from Abu Ishaq from Al-Baraa’, and he mentioned it and said after his saying you are not charged except with yourself, but destruction is when a man commits a sin and throws himself into destruction and does not repent. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth told us, Al-Layth told me, Abd Al-Rahman bin Khalid bin Musafir told us from Ibn Shihab from Abu Bakr bin Numayr bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham that Abd Al-Rahman Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth informed him that they had besieged Damascus and a man from Azd Shanu’ah set out and rushed to the enemy alone to meet them, so the Muslims criticized him for that and reported his hadith to Amr bin Al-Aas, so Amr sent to him and returned him, and Amr said: God said: And do not… “And throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands,” said Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in his statement, And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves into destruction, he said: This is not in fighting, rather it is in spending, that you hold back your hand from spending in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves into destruction. Hammad ibn Salamah said, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Abi Jubayr, he said: The Ansar used to give charity and spend from their wealth, then a famine struck them and they held back from spending in the cause of God, so this was revealed: And do not throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands, and al-Hasan al-Basri said: And do not throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands, he said: It is stinginess. Samak ibn Harb said, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, in his statement, And do not throw yourselves into destruction, that a man commits a sin and says: I will not be forgiven, so God revealed: “And do not throw yourselves into destruction and do good. Indeed, God loves the doers of good.” Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Abi Hatim said, and it was narrated on the authority of Ubaydah al-Salmani, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, and Abu Qilabah something similar to that, meaning something similar to the statement of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, that it is about a man who commits a sin and believes that he will not be forgiven, so he throws himself into destruction, meaning he commits many sins and perishes. And for this reason, Ali bin Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Destruction is the punishment of God. And Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir said, all of them, Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Abu Sakhr informed me on the authority of Al-Qurazi Muhammad bin Kaab, that he used to say regarding this verse: And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction. He said: The people were in the cause of God, and a man would take provisions, and he had better provisions than the other. The poor man would spend from his provisions until nothing remained of his provisions. He wanted to console his companion, so God revealed: And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction. And Ibn Wahb also said: Abdullah bin Ayyash informed me on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding the statement of God: And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction. That is because men would go out in expeditions sent by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, without providing for them, and either they would be cut off or they would be dependents, so God commanded them to spend by walking. And He said to those who have wealth, “And do good. Indeed, God loves the doers of good.” The meaning of the verse is the command to spend in the way of God, in all aspects of drawing closer to Him and obedience, especially spending money in fighting the enemy, and spending it in what strengthens the Muslims against their enemy, and informing that abandoning doing that will lead to destruction and ruin for those who adhere to it and become accustomed to it. Then He followed up with the command to do good, which is the highest level of obedience, and said, “And do good. Indeed, God loves the doers of good.”
2:196: When God the Almighty mentioned the rulings of fasting, and followed it with mentioning Jihad, He began to explain the rituals, so He commanded the completion of Hajj and Umrah. The apparent context is the completion of their actions after starting them, and for this reason He said after that: But if you are prevented, meaning you are prevented from reaching the House, and are prevented from completing them. For this reason, the scholars agreed that starting Hajj and Umrah is obligatory, whether it is said that Umrah is obligatory or recommended, as they are two opinions of the scholars, and we have mentioned them with their evidence in our book Al-Ahkam, in detail, and praise and thanks be to God. Shu’bah said: On the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali, that he said regarding this verse: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, he said: That you enter ihram from your family, and Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, and Tawus said the same. And on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, that he said regarding this verse: Completing it is that you enter ihram from your family, not intending anything but Hajj and Umrah, and you enter ihram from the miqat, not that you go out for trade or for a need, until If you are close to Mecca, I said if you perform Hajj or Umrah, that is sufficient, but the completion is that you go out for him and do not go out for anyone else, and Makhul said: Completing them both is establishing them both from the Miqat, and Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said: It has reached us that Umar said about the statement of God And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God from their completion is that you separate each one of them from the other, and that you perform Umrah in months other than the months of Hajj, for God the Most High says: Hajj is in well-known months, and Hisham said on the authority of Ibn Awn: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: Umrah in the months of Hajj is not complete, so it was said to him: So Umrah in Muharram? He said: They considered it complete, and this is what was narrated from Qatada bin Di’amah, may God have mercy on them both. This statement is questionable because it has been proven that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed four Umrahs, all of them in Dhul-Qa’dah: the Umrah of Al-Hudaybiyyah in Dhul-Qa’dah in the year six, the Umrah of Al-Qada’ in Dhul-Qa’dah in the year seven, the Umrah of Al-Ji’ranah in Dhul-Qa’dah in the year eight, and the Umrah that was with his Hajj, he entered into ihram for both of them together in Dhul-Qa’dah in the year ten. He did not perform Umrah in any other time after his migration, but he said to Umm Hani’: An Umrah in Ramadan is equal to a Hajj with me, and that is only because she had resolved to perform Hajj with him, peace be upon him, and she was freed from that because of purity, as is explained in detail in the hadith in Al-Bukhari, and Saeed bin Jubair stated that it was one of her special characteristics, and God knows best. Al-Suddi said about his statement: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God meaning perform the Hajj and Umrah. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God he said: Whoever enters into ihram for Hajj or Umrah is not permitted to exit ihram until he completes them with the completion of Hajj, on the Day of Sacrifice when he throws the pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqabah, and circumambulates the House and Safa and Marwah, then he has exited ihram. Qatada said on the authority of Zurarah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Hajj is Arafat, and Umrah is Tawaf. And this is how Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of Alqamah regarding his statement: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, he said: This is the reading of Abdullah: And complete the Hajj and Umrah to the House, do not go beyond the House with Umrah. Ibrahim said: So I mentioned that to Saeed bin Jubair, and he said: This is what Ibn Abbas said. Sufyan said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of Alqamah that he said: And perform the Hajj and Umrah to the House. And this is also narrated by Al-Thawri on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Ibrahim that he read: And perform the Hajj and Umrah to the House. Al-Sha'bi read: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God by raising the Umrah, and he said: It is not obligatory. And the opposite of that was narrated from him, and many hadiths were narrated from various chains of narration, from Anas and a group of the Companions, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, combined Hajj and Umrah in his ihram, and it was proven from him in the Sahih that he said to his companions: Whoever has an offering with him, let him enter ihram for Hajj and Umrah, and he also said in the Sahih: Umrah has been included in Hajj until the Day of Resurrection. Imam Abu Muhammad bin Abi Hatim narrated a strange hadith about the reason for the revelation of this verse. He said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Harawi told us, Ghassan Al-Harawi told us, Ibrahim bin Tahman told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Safwan bin Umayya, that he said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wearing a cloak and smeared with saffron, and said: What do you command me, O Messenger of God, regarding my Umrah?” So God revealed: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Where is the one who asked about Umrah? He said: Here I am. He said to him: Take off your clothes, then wash yourself and sniff water as much as you can, then whatever you used to do in your Hajj, do in your Umrah. This is a strange hadith and a strange context. What was reported in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ya’la bin Umayya in the story of the man who asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Al-Ji’ranah, and he said: What do you think of a man who has entered into ihram for Umrah and is wearing a cloak and perfume? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent, then the revelation came to him. Then he raised his head and said: Where is the questioner? He said: Here I am. Then he said: As for the cloak, take it off, and as for the perfume that is on you, wash it off, and whatever you did in your Hajj, do in your Umrah. He did not mention washing and inhaling water into the nose, nor did he mention the revelation of this verse. It is from Ya`la ibn Umayya, not Safwan ibn Umayya, and God knows best. And his saying, But if you are prevented, then offer whatever is easy for you of sacrificial animals. They mentioned that this verse was revealed in the sixth year, that is, the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, when the polytheists prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from reaching the House, and God revealed Surat Al-Fath in its entirety regarding that, and revealed to them a license to slaughter whatever sacrificial animals they had with them, which were seventy camels, and to shave their heads and to be released from their state of ihram. At that time, peace be upon him, ordered them to shave their heads and be released from their state of ihram, but they did not do so, waiting for the abrogation, until he went out and shaved his head, and the people did so, and among them was one who shortened his head and did not shave it, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, May God have mercy on those who shave their heads. They said, And those who cut their hair short, O Messenger of God? He said, And those who cut their hair short. They shared in their sacrificial animals, seven in a camel, and they were one thousand four hundred, and their home was at Al-Hudaybiyyah outside the sanctuary, and it was said that they were on the edge of the sanctuary, and God knows best. For this reason, the scholars differed: Is the confinement limited to the enemy, so that only the one who is confined by an enemy, not sick or otherwise, is released from his state of ihram, according to two opinions. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Tawus on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: There is no confinement except the confinement of the enemy. As for the one who is afflicted with illness, or a loss of strength, or straying, then there is nothing upon him. Rather, God the Most High said: And when you are secure, so security is not confinement. He said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Tawus, al-Zuhri, and Zayd ibn Aslam. The second opinion is that confinement is more general than being due to an enemy, or illness, or straying, and it is wandering from the road or something like that. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Hajjaj ibn al-Sawaaf told us on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Amr al-Ansari, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever is broken, or in pain, or limps, then he is released and has another Hajj upon him. He said: So I mentioned that to Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah, and they said: He is truthful. The authors of the four books narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Abu Katheer narrated it, and in a narration by Abu Dawood and Ibn Majah: from a limp, fracture or illness, and he mentioned its meaning. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Arafa, on the authority of Ismail bin Aliyah, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Abi Uthman Al-Sawaaf on his authority, then he said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Alqamah, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Al-Nakha’i, Ata’ and Muqatil bin Hayyan: being prevented by an enemy, illness or fracture. Al-Thawri said: being prevented by anything that harms him. It was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon Duba’ah bint Al-Zubayr bin Abdul Muttalib, and she said: O Messenger of God, I want to perform Hajj and I am sick. He said: Perform Hajj and stipulate that my place of residence is where you prevent me. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a similar wording. Some scholars who held the view that stipulating Hajj is valid based on this hadith, and Imam Muhammad bin Idris Al-Shafi’i based the view of the validity of this school of thought on the validity of this hadith. Al-Bayhaqi and other hadith masters said: It has been authenticated, praise be to God. And his saying, Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, Imam Malik said: On the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he used to say, Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, is a sheep. And Ibn Abbas said: The sacrificial animal is from the eight pairs of camels, cows, goats, and sheep. And Al-Thawri said on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying, Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, he said: A sheep. And so said Ata’, Mujahid, Tawus, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Qasim, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others: something similar to that, and it is the doctrine of the four imams. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa’id Al-Ashja’ told us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha and Ibn Umar: that they did not consider what is easy of the sacrificial animal except camels and cows. He said: It was narrated from Salim, Al-Qasim, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, and Saeed bin Jubair something similar to that. I said It appears that the basis of what these people have gone to is the story of Al-Hudaybiyyah, for it was not narrated from any of them that he slaughtered a sheep during his release from ihram, rather they slaughtered camels and cows. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Jabir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to share in camels and cows, every seven of us in a cow. And Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, he said: According to his wealth. And Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If he is well-off, then from camels, otherwise from cows, otherwise from sheep. Hisham bin Urwah said on the authority of his father: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal. He said: This is only between the cheap and the expensive. The evidence for the correctness of the statement of the majority in what they have gone to regarding the sufficiency of slaughtering a sheep in the case of being prevented is that God has made it obligatory to slaughter whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, meaning whatever is easy of what is called sacrificial animal, and sacrificial animal is from the livestock, which are camels, cows, and sheep, as the scholar, the sea interpreter of the Qur’an and cousin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, once gave a sacrificial animal of sheep. His statement, And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination, is connected to his statement, And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, and not to his statement, But if you are prevented, then what is easy of the sacrificial animal, as Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, claimed, because the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and his companions in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah, when the infidels of Quraysh prevented them from entering the Sacred Sanctuary, shaved and slaughtered their sacrificial animal outside the Sacred Sanctuary. However, in a state of security and arrival at the Sacred Sanctuary, shaving is not permissible until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination, and the pilgrim completes the actions of Hajj and Umrah if he is performing Qarin, or one of them if he is performing it alone or Tamattu’, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Hafsah that she said: O Messenger of God, what is the matter with the people who have completed Umrah, but you have not completed your Umrah? He said, I have tied my head and put on my sacrificial animal, so I will not complete my completion until I slaughter. And his saying: And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his head, then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. Al-Bukhari said: Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, I heard Abdullah ibn Muqal say: I sat with Ka’b ibn Ujrah in this mosque - meaning the mosque of Kufa - and I asked him about the ransom of fasting, so he said: “I was carried to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the lice were falling on my face, so he said: I did not think that the effort had reached this point for you, could you not find a sheep? I said: No. He said: Fast for three days or feed six poor people, for each poor person half a sa’ of food, and shave your head.” So it was revealed for a specific reason, but it is general for you. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Ujrah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me while I was lighting a fire under a pot and the lice were falling on my face, or he said my eyebrows, so he said: Are the lice on your head bothering you? I said: Yes. He said: Then shave it, and fast for three days. Days, or feed six poor people, or sacrifice a sacrifice.” Ayoub said: I do not know with which of them he began. Ahmad also said: Hisham told us, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Ujrah, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at al-Hudaybiyah, and we were in ihram and the polytheists had besieged it. I had plenty of money, so insects kept falling on my face. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by me and said: Are the insects on your head bothering you? He ordered him to shave. He said: And this verse was revealed: And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in the head - a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. And thus it was narrated by Affan from Shu’bah from Abu Bishr, who is Ja’far ibn Iyas, and from Shu’bah from Al-Hakam from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, and from Shu’bah from Dawud from Al-Sha’bi from Ka’b ibn Ujrah, similarly. And Imam Malik narrated it from Hamid ibn Qays, from Mujahid, from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, from Ka’b ibn Ujrah, and he mentioned it similarly. And Sa’d ibn Ishaq ibn Ka’b ibn Ujrah said from Aban ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan Al-Basri: That he heard Ka’b ibn Ujrah say: So a sheep was slaughtered. And Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. And it was also narrated from the hadith of Umar ibn Qays, and it is weak, from Ata’ from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sacrifice is a sheep, and fasting is three days, and the food is divided among six. And thus it was narrated from Ali, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Ikrimah, Ibrahim, Mujahid, Ata’, As-Suddi, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and he said: Ibn Abi Hatim: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Abdullah ibn Wahb told us that Malik ibn Anas told him, on the authority of Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Ujrah: that he was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and lice were bothering him in his head, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to shave his head, and said: Fast for three days, or feed six poor people, one mudd for each person, or sacrifice a sheep, whichever of these you do will suffice for you. And thus Layth ibn Abi Salim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice, he said: If it is or whatever you take, it will suffice for you. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata’, Tawus, al-Hasan, Hamid al-A’raj, Ibrahim, al-Nakha’i, and al-Dahhak. I said This is the doctrine of the four imams, and the majority of scholars, that he has a choice in this situation. If he wants, he may fast, or if he wants, he may give charity with a farq, which is three sa’s, half a sa’ for each poor person, which is two mudds, or if he wants, he may slaughter a sheep and give it in charity to the poor. Whichever of these he does, it is sufficient for him. And since the wording of the Qur’an in explaining the permission came with the easiest, then the easiest: A ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. And when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah to do this, he guided him to the best, then the best, and said: Sacrifice a sheep, or feed six poor people, or fast for three days, so each is good in its situation, and to God be praise and thanks. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kuraib told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said: Al-A’mash mentioned, he said: Ibrahim asked Saeed bin Jubair about this verse Then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice, so he answered him by saying that he must give food. If he has it, he should buy a sheep, and if he does not have it, he should give the value of the sheep in dirhams and replace it with food and give it in charity, otherwise he should fast for each half sa’ a day. Ibrahim said: This is how I heard Alqamah mention it. He said: When Saeed bin Jubair said to me: Who is this, how charming he is? He said: I said: This is Ibrahim. He said: How charming he is, he used to sit with us. He said: So I mentioned that to Ibrahim. He said: When I said: He used to sit with us, he was startled by it. Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Abi Imran told us, Ubaydullah bin Muadh told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: Then a ransom of fasting or charity or a sacrifice, he said: If the pilgrim has an ailment on his head, he shaves and redeems himself with whichever of these three he wants, and fasting for ten days, and charity for ten poor people, each poor person two rak’ahs: a rak’ah of dates, and a rak’ah of wheat, and the sacrifice is a sheep. Qatada said on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ikrimah regarding his statement: Then a ransom of fasting or charity or a sacrifice, he said: Feeding ten poor people. These two statements from Sa’id bin Jubayr, Alqamah, Al-Hasan and Ikrimah are strange statements in which there is a problem, because the Sunnah has been proven in the hadith of Ka’b bin Ujrah to fast for three days, not six, or to feed six poor people, or to sacrifice a sheep, and that This is optional, as indicated by the context of the Qur’an. As for this arrangement, it is only known in killing game, as is the text of the Qur’an, and the jurists there have agreed on this, contrary to this, and God knows best. Hisham said: Laith told us on the authority of Tawus that he used to say: Whatever was of blood or food, then it is in Mecca, and whatever was of fasting, then it is wherever he wants. Mujahid, Ata’ and Al-Hasan said the same. Hisham said: Hajjaj, Abdul Malik and others told us on the authority of Ata’ that he used to say: Whatever was of blood, then it is in Mecca, and whatever was of food and fasting, then it is wherever he wants. Hisham said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Ya’qub bin Khalid, Abu Asma’, the freed slave of Ibn Ja’far, told us: Uthman bin Affan performed Hajj with Ali and Al-Hussein bin Ali, then Uthman departed. Abu Asma’ said: I was with Ibn Ja’far and suddenly we saw a man sleeping and his camel at his head. He said: I said: O sleeper, wake up and it is Al-Hussein bin Ali. He said: Ibn Ja’far carried him until we brought him the watering place. He said: Ali sent for me and Asma’ bint Umays with him. He said: We treated him for about twenty nights. He said: Ali said to Al-Hussein, what do you find? He said: So he pointed with his hand to his head. He said: So Ali ordered him to shave his head, then he called for a camel and slaughtered it. If this camel was about to be shaved, then it means that he slaughtered it without Mecca. And if it was about to be released, then it is clear. And his saying: And when you are secure, whoever enjoys the ‘umrah until the Hajj, then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal means: if you are able to perform the rituals, whoever among you enjoys the ‘umrah until the Hajj, and this includes whoever enters ihram for both, or enters ihram for the ‘umrah first, and when he finishes it, he enters ihram for the Hajj, and this is the special enjoyment, and it is known in the speech of the jurists, and the general enjoyment includes both types, as indicated by the authentic hadiths, for some of the narrators say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, enjoyed himself, and another says: He combined, and there is no disagreement that he brought a sacrificial animal, and God Almighty said: And whoever enjoys the ‘umrah until the Hajj, then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal meaning, let him slaughter whatever he is able of the sacrificial animal, and the least of it is a sheep, and he may slaughter a cow, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered cows on behalf of his wives, and Al-Awza’i said, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered cows on behalf of his wives, and they were enjoying themselves, narrated by Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh, and in this is evidence of the permissibility of enjoyment, as it came In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, he said: The verse of Mut’ah was revealed in the Book of God, and we did it with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then no Qur’an was revealed prohibiting it or forbidding it, until he died. A man said whatever he wanted based on his opinion. Al-Bukhari said: It is said that it was Umar, and what Al-Bukhari said came explicitly that Umar used to forbid people from Mut’ah and say: If we take the Book of God, it commands completion, meaning His statement: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God. In fact, Umar, may God be pleased with him, did not forbid it as a prohibition of it, rather he forbade it so that people would go to the House as pilgrims and Umrah performers more often, as he, may God be pleased with him, had stated explicitly. And His saying: “And whoever cannot find a sacrificial animal, then he should fast three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned. That is ten complete.” God Almighty says: And whoever cannot find a sacrificial animal, then he should fast three days during the Hajj, meaning during the days of the rituals. The scholars said: It is better to fast them before Arafah in the ten days, said Ata’, or from the time he enters ihram, said Ibn Abbas and others, based on his saying about the Hajj. And some of them permit fasting them from the beginning of Shawwal, said Tawus, Mujahid and more than one. Al-Sha’bi permitted fasting on the day of Arafah and two days before it, and so did Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Al-Suddi, Ata’, Tawus, Al-Hakam, Al-Hasan, Hammad, Ibrahim, Abu Ja’far Al-Baqir, Al-Rabi’ and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If he cannot find a sacrificial animal, then he must fast three days during the Hajj before the day of Arafah, and if the third day of Arafah is his fast, then he is complete, and seven when he returns to his family. And so did Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Wabra, on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: He should fast one day before Tarwiyah, and the day of Tarwiyah, and the day of Arafah, and so on. Jaafar bin Muhammad narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali also: If he did not fast it or some of it before the Eid, is it permissible for him to fast it during the days of Tashreeq? There are two opinions of scholars, and they are also from Imam Al-Shafi’i. The older one is that it is permissible for him to fast them, based on the statement of Aisha and Ibn Umar in Sahih Al-Bukhari: It was not permissible to fast on the days of Tashreeq except for one who does not find a sacrificial animal. This is how Malik narrated it from Al-Zuhri from Urwah from Aisha and from Salim from Ibn Umar. It was narrated from them through other chains of transmission. Sufyan narrated it from Ja’far Ibn Muhammad from his father from Ali, that he used to say: Whoever misses fasting three days during Hajj, he should fast them on the days of Tashreeq. This is what Ubayd Ibn Umair Al-Laythi said on the authority of Ikrimah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Urwah Ibn Al-Zubayr said. They only said that because of the generality of his statement, So fasting three days during Hajj. The newer one of the two opinions is that it is not permissible to fast them on the days of Tashreeq, based on what Muslim narrated on the authority of Qutaybah Al-Hudhali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The days of Tashreeq are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God Almighty. His saying, And seven when you return, has two opinions: One of them when you return to your homes, and for this reason Mujahid said: It is a concession if he wants to fast it on the road, and this is what Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said. And the second statement: When you return to your homelands, Abd al-Razzaq said: Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed on the authority of Salim, I heard Ibn Umar say: And whoever does not find it, then fasting three days during Hajj and seven when you return. He said: When he returns to his family, and this is what was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Abu al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, and al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Abu Ja’far bin Jarir narrated the consensus on that, and al-Bukhari said: Yahya bin Bakir told us, al-Layth told us on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, that Ibn Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, enjoyed the ‘umrah during the Farewell Pilgrimage until the Hajj, and he offered a sacrifice and drove the sacrifice with him from Dhu al-Hulayfah, so he entered ihram for ‘umrah, then he entered ihram for Hajj, so the people enjoyed themselves with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began with ‘umrah until Hajj, so some of the people offered a sacrifice and drove the sacrifice, and some of them did not offer a sacrifice, so when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Mecca He said to the al-Nas 114:“Whoever among you has offered a sacrifice, he should not be released from anything that was forbidden until he has completed his Hajj. And whoever among you has not offered a sacrifice, let him circumambulate the House and Safa and Marwa and shorten his hair and let him enter ihram, then he should enter ihram for Hajj. And whoever does not find a sacrifice, let him fast three days during Hajj and seven when he returns to his family.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Al-Zuhri said: And Urwah informed me on the authority of Aisha, similar to what Salim informed me on the authority of his father. And the hadith is included in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Al-Zuhri with it. And his saying those are ten complete was said to be an emphasis, as the Arabs say: I saw with my eyes, I heard with my ears, and I wrote with my hand. And God Almighty said: nor a bird that flies with its wings and He said: nor a bird that inscribes it with your right hand and He said: And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And it was said: The meaning of complete is the command to complete them and finish them, Ibn Jarir chose it. And it was said that the meaning of complete is that it suffices for the sacrifice. Hisham said on the authority of Ibad bin Rashid on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri regarding his saying those are ten complete he said: From the guidance. And his saying, That is for those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque, Ibn Jarir said: The people of interpretation differed about who he meant by his saying, for those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque, after all of them agreed that the people of the Sacred Mosque are meant by it and that there is no mut’ah for them. Some of them said: He meant by that the people of the Sacred Mosque specifically and not others. Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan, he is al-Thawri, told us: Ibn Abbas: They are the people of the Sacred Mosque. And Ibn al-Mubarak narrated this from al-Thawri, and the group added to it. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that Ibn Abbas used to say: O people of Mecca, there is no mut’ah for you. It was made permissible for the people of the horizons and forbidden for you. One of you should only cross a valley, or he said: He should put a valley between him and the Sacred Mosque, then he should enter ihram for Umrah. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: Mut’ah is for the people, not for the people of Mecca, for those whose families are not from the Sacred Mosque. And likewise the statement of God the Almighty: That is for those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque. He said: And I have heard from Ibn Abbas something similar to what Tawus said, and others said: They are the people of the Sacred Mosque and those between it and the Miqats, as Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us from Ata’, he said: Whoever’s family is outside the Miqats is like the people of Mecca and does not perform Tamattu’. And Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir from Makhul regarding his statement: That is for those whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque, he said: Whoever is outside the Miqat. And Ibn Jurayj said from Ata’ that his family is not present at the Sacred Mosque. He said: Arafat, Muzdalifah, Arafat and Raji’. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us I heard al-Zuhri say: Whoever’s family is on a day or so, he performs Tamattu’, and in a narration from him: one day or two days. And Ibn Jarir chose the Shafi’i school of thought in that, that they are the people of the Sacred Mosque, and whoever is at a distance from it does not shorten the prayer, because whoever is like that is considered present and not a traveler, and God knows best. His saying: And fear God means in what He has commanded and forbidden you, and know that God is severe in punishment meaning for whoever disobeys His command and commits what He has warned against.
2:197: The Arab scholars differed regarding his statement, Hajj is during well-known months. Some of them said: Its meaning is Hajj is during well-known months. According to this estimation, entering ihram for Hajj during these months is more complete than entering ihram for anything else, even if that is correct. The statement that entering ihram for Hajj is valid throughout the year is the school of Malik, Abu Hanifa, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Thawri, and al-Layth ibn Sa'd said the same. They cited as evidence for them the statement of God the Almighty: "They ask you about the new moons. Say, 'They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj.'" And that it is one of the two rituals, so entering ihram with it is valid throughout the year, like Umrah. Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said that entering ihram for Hajj is not valid except during its months. If he enters ihram before them, his ihram is not valid. Is an Umrah valid? There are two opinions on this from him. The statement that it is not valid to enter ihram for Hajj except in its months is narrated from Ibn Abbas and Jabir, and it is what Ata’, Tawus and Mujahid, may God have mercy on them, say. The evidence for this is his statement, Hajj is in well-known months. The apparent meaning is the other estimation that grammarians have adopted, which is that the time of Hajj is well-known months, so he singled it out from among the other months of the year, so it indicates that it is not valid before them, like the time of prayer. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: Muslim bin Khalid informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, Umar bin Ata’ informed me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: No one should enter ihram for Hajj except in the months of Hajj because of the statement of God Almighty: Hajj is in well-known months. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it likewise, from Ahmad bin Yahya bin Malik al-Susi, from Hajjaj bin Muhammad al-A’war, from Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his interpretation through two chains of transmission, from Hajjaj bin Artah, from al-Hakim bin Utaybah, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: It is from the Sunnah not to enter ihram for Hajj except in the months of Hajj. Ibn Khuzaymah said in his Sahih: Abu Dawud narrated to us. Kurayb, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: One should not enter ihram for Hajj except during the months of Hajj, for it is part of the Sunnah of Hajj to enter ihram during the months of Hajj. This is a sound chain of transmission, and the statement of a companion from the Sunnah is considered to be in the ruling of a marfu’ hadith according to the majority, especially the statement of Ibn Abbas in interpretation of the Qur’an and its translation. A marfu’ hadith was narrated on it. Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Baqi narrated to us, Nafi’ narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: No one should enter ihram for Hajj except during the months of Hajj. Its chain of transmission is sound, but al-Shafi’i and al-Bayhaqi narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah ask: Should one enter ihram for Hajj before the months of Hajj? He said: No, and this hadith that is attributed to the Prophet is more authentic and proven than the hadith that is attributed to the Prophet. Then there remains the doctrine of a companion that is strengthened by the statement of Ibn Abbas from the Sunnah: that one should not enter ihram for Hajj except during its months, and God knows best. And his saying, well-known months, Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Umar said: They are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah, and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. This which Al-Bukhari suspended in the form of certainty, was narrated by Ibn Jarir in a connected chain of transmission. Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Abi Barzah told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar: Hajj is well-known months, he said: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah, and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. A sound chain of transmission. Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Al-Asamm, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Affan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Numayr, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Amr, and he mentioned it and said: It meets the conditions of the two sheikhs. I said It was narrated on the authority of Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayr, Ibn Abbas, Ata’, Tawus, Mujahid, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Makhul, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. This is the school of thought of Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa. Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Yusuf and Abu Thawr, may God have mercy on them, and Ibn Jarir chose this statement. He said: It is correct to use the combination of two months and some of the third for the sake of emphasis, as the Arabs say: I saw it this year and I saw it today. However, this occurred in some of the year and the day. So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him. Rather, he hastens in a day and a half. Imam Malik ibn Anas and al-Shafi’i in the old days said: They are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah and Dhul-Hijjah in their entirety. This is also a narration from Ibn Umar. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah and Dhul-Hijjah. Ibn Abi Hatim said in his interpretation: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Jurayj told me, he said: I said to Nafi’: Did you hear Abdullah ibn Umar naming the months of Hajj. He said: Yes, Abdullah used to name Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and Dhul-Hijjah. Ibn Jurayj said: This was said by Ibn Shihab, Ata' and Jabir ibn Abdullah, the companion of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a sound chain of transmission to Ibn Jurayj. This was also narrated by Tawus, Mujahid, Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah. There is a hadith in it that is attributed to the Prophet, but it is fabricated. It was narrated by Al-Hafiz ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Hisayn ibn Mukhariq, who is accused of fabrication, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The Hajj is in well-known months: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and Dhul-Hijjah." This, as you have seen, is not authentically attributed to the Prophet, and God knows best. The benefit of the Maliki school of thought is that it is until the end of Dhul-Hijjah, meaning that it is specific to Hajj, so it is disliked to perform Umrah in the rest of Dhul-Hijjah, not that Hajj is valid after the Night of Sacrifice. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abu Mu'awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shahab said: Abdullah said: Hajj is a well-known month, and there is no Umrah in it. This is a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: What those who said that the months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah meant was that these months are not the months of Umrah, but rather they are for Hajj, even if the Hajj rituals are completed with the passing of the days of Mina, as Muhammad ibn Sirin said: No one among the people of knowledge doubts that Umrah in months other than Hajj is better than Umrah in the months of Hajj. Ibn 'Awn said: I asked Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad about Umrah in the months of Hajj, and he said: They did not consider it complete. I said It has been proven from 'Umar and 'Uthman, may God be pleased with them, that they loved to perform Umrah in months other than Hajj and they forbade it in the months of Hajj. And God knows best. And his saying, So whoever has made Hajj obligatory therein means, he has made Hajj obligatory by entering into ihram, this indicates the necessity of entering into ihram for Hajj and proceeding with it. Ibn Jarir said: They agreed that what is meant by obligation here is obligation and compulsion. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So whoever has made Hajj obligatory therein means whoever enters ihram for Hajj or Umrah. Ata’ said: The obligation is ihram. Ibrahim, Ad-Dahhak and others said the same. Ibn Jarir said: Umar ibn Ata’ informed me on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said, So whoever has made Hajj obligatory therein so he should not make the Talbiyah for Hajj and then reside in a land. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Az-Zubayr, Mujahid, Ata’, Ibrahim An-Nakha’i, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Az-Zuhri and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Tawus and Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: It is the Talbiyah. And his saying, No obscenity, meaning that whoever enters ihram for Hajj or Umrah should avoid obscenity, which is sexual intercourse, as God the Almighty said: Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the intimacy with your wives. Likewise, engaging in its causes, such as touching, kissing, and the like, is forbidden, as is speaking about it in the presence of women. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus told me: Nafi’ told him that Abdullah ibn Umar used to say: Obscenity is coming to women and speaking about it to men and women if they mention it with their mouths. Ibn Wahb said: Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, something similar. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah al-Riyahi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to exhort while in ihram, and he would say: They walk with us whispering, if the bird is truthful, we will reach Lamisa Abu Al-Aaliyah said: I said: Do you speak obscene language while you are in a state of ihram? He said: Obscene language is what is said in front of women. Al-A’mash narrated it on the authority of Ziyad bin Husayn on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir also said: My father Husayn bin Qays told me: I went up with Ibn Abbas during the Hajj, and I was his friend. When it was after we had entered ihram, Ibn Abbas said: He took hold of the tail of his camel and began to twist it and recite the following verse: They walk with us whispering, if the bird is honest, we will get Lamisa He said: I said: Do you speak indecently while you are in a state of ihram? He said: Indecent speech is what is said in front of women. Abdullah bin Tawus said on the authority of his father: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God the Almighty: There shall be no obscenity nor wickedness? He said: Indecent speech is insinuation about sexual intercourse, which is called araba in the speech of the Arabs, and it is the lowest form of indecent speech. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: Indecent speech is sexual intercourse and what is less than that of obscene speech. Amr bin Dinar said the same. Ata said: They disliked insinuation, which is insinuation and it is in a state of ihram. Tawus said: It is to say to a woman, When you are released, I will have intercourse with you. Abu Al-Aaliyah said the same. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Rafth is intercourse with women, kissing, winking, and exposing her to obscene speech and the like. Ibn Abbas also said: Ibn Umar: Rafth is intercourse with women. Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibrahim, Abu Al-Aaliyah said the same on the authority of Ata’, Makhul, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Ata’ bin Yasar, Atiyyah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Rabi’, Al-Zuhri, Al-Suddi, Malik bin Anas, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Abdul Karim bin Malik, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, and others. And his saying, nor transgression, he said: Muqtasem and more than one, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, it is the sins, and likewise said Ata’, Mujahid, Tawus, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair, Muhammad bin Ka’b, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Zuhri, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Ata’ bin Yasar, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: Transgression is what is committed of the sins of God by hunting or otherwise, and likewise Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Nafi’ that Abdullah bin Umar used to say: Transgression is committing the sins of God in the Sacred Sanctuary, and others said: Transgression here is cursing, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Al-Hasan said, and these people may hold fast to what is proven in the Sahih Cursing a Muslim is transgression and fighting him is disbelief. For this reason, the scholar Abu Muhammad bin Abi Hatim narrated it here from the hadith of Sufyan Al-Thawri on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Cursing a Muslim is transgression, and fighting him is disbelief. “Kufr,” and it was narrated from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Mas’ud on the authority of his father, and from the hadith of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa’d on the authority of his father. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: “The wickedness here is slaughtering for idols. God the Most High said: ‘Or wickedness dedicated to other than God. ’” Ad-Dahhak said: “The wickedness here is insulting with nicknames. Those who said: The wickedness here is all sins, the correct thing is with them, as God the Most High forbade injustice in the sacred months, even though it is forbidden throughout the year, except that it is more emphasized in the sacred months. For this reason, He said: “Of them are four sacred months: that is the right religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein.” And He said in the sacred months: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, We will make him taste a painful punishment.
