Ibn Jarir chose that the wickedness here is committing what was forbidden in the state of ihram, such as killing game, shaving hair, cutting nails, and the like, as was mentioned previously from Ibn Umar. What we mentioned is more appropriate, and God knows best. It has been proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hazim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs Hajj to this House and does not utter obscenities or commit sins will emerge from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. His statement, And there is no disputing during Hajj, has two opinions: One of them is that there is no disputing about the time of Hajj and its rituals, and God has explained it in the most complete manner, and clarified it in the most complete manner, as Wakee’ said on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim: I heard Mujahid say, And there is no disputing during Hajj, God has explained the months of Hajj, so there is no disputing among the people about it. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, And there is no disputing during Hajj, he said: No month can be postponed and no disputing during Hajj has been made clear. Then he mentioned how the polytheists used to do in the postponement that God condemned them for. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And there is no disputing during Hajj, he said: Hajj has been established. So there is no disputing about it. Al-Suddi said the same. Hisham said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And there is no disputing during Hajj, he said: Disputing about Hajj. Abdullah bin Wahb said: Malik said: God the Almighty said: And there is no disputing during Hajj. Disputing during Hajj - and God knows best - is that the Quraysh used to stand at the sacred monument in Muzdalifah, and the Arabs and others used to stand at Arafat, and they used to argue, some saying: We are more correct and others saying: We are more correct. This is what we see, and God knows best. Ibn Wahb said on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam: They used to stand at different positions and argue, each claiming that his position was the position of Abraham, but God cut him off when He informed His Prophet of the rituals. Ibn Wahb said on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said: When the Quraysh gathered at Mina, some would say: Our Hajj is more complete than your Hajj, and those would say: Our Hajj is more complete than your Hajj. Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Jubayr bin Habib, on the authority of al-Qasim bin Muhammad that he said: Disputing during Hajj is when some of them say: Hajj is tomorrow, and some of them say: Hajj is today. Ibn Jarir chose the meaning of these statements, which is to cut off the dispute over the rituals of Hajj, and God knows best. The second opinion is that what is meant by argument here is quarrel. Ibn Jarir said: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, regarding his statement, And there is no disputing during Hajj, he said: That you argue with your companion until you anger him. And with this chain of transmission to Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, I asked Ibn Abbas about disputing, he said: Disputing is arguing with your companion until you anger him. And Muqsim and Ad-Dahhak narrated likewise from Ibn Abbas, and likewise Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ata’, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, Jabir bin Zaid, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Makhul, As-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Amr bin Dinar, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Ata’ bin Yasar, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Az-Zuhri said. And Ali bin Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And there is no disputing during Hajj, disputing and quarreling until you anger your brother and companion, so God forbade that. And Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said, And there is no disputing during Hajj, he said: They disliked disputing. And Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Omar said: Argumentation during Hajj means cursing and disputing. Ibn Wahb also narrated on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Nafi’: Ibn Omar used to say: Argumentation during Hajj means cursing, disputing and quarrels. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Hasan, Ibrahim, Tawus and Muhammad ibn Ka’b, they said: Argumentation means disputing. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said on the authority of Yahya ibn Bishr, on the authority of Ikrimah: There is no argumentation during Hajj. Argumentation means anger, that a Muslim becomes angry with you, unless you ask forgiveness of a slave and you anger him without hitting him, then there is no harm on you, God willing. I said And if he had hit him, it would have been permissible and lawful. The evidence for that is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Abdullah bin Idris told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Ibad bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as pilgrims, until when we were at Al-Arj, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dismounted, so Aisha sat next to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she sat next to my father, and the companionship of Abu Bakr and the companionship of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one with Abu Bakr’s slave, so Abu Bakr sat waiting for him until he looked at him, but he looked and he was not with his camel, so he said: Where is your camel? He said: I lost it last night, so Abu Bakr said: A camel that you lost? So he began to beat him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled and said, Look at this pilgrim, what he is doing. This is how Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. From this hadith, some of them narrated from some of the predecessors that he said: Part of completing the Hajj is beating the camels. However, it is understood from the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, Look at this pilgrim, what he is doing, as a form of gentle denunciation, that it is better to leave that, and God knows best. Imam Abd bin Hamid said in his Musnad: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of his brother Abdullah bin Ubaidullah, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever completes his rituals and the Muslims are safe from his tongue and hand, his previous sins will be forgiven. And His statement, And whatever good you do, God knows it, when He forbade them from committing evil in word or deed, He urged them to do good and informed them that He knows it and will reward them for it abundantly on the Day of Resurrection. And His statement, And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God, Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: There were people who would leave their families and they did not have provisions with them, saying: Shall we perform Hajj to the House of God and He will not feed us? So God said: Take provisions that will protect your faces from people. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid Al-Muqri told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah: That some people used to perform Hajj without provisions, so God revealed, And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God, and Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise on the authority of Amr, who is Al-Fallas, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: This hadith was narrated by Warqa’ on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said: What he narrates on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah is more authentic. I said An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sa’id ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi, on the authority of Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, on the authority of ‘Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of ‘Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas: There were people who performed Hajj without provisions, so God revealed, And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God. As for the hadith of Warqa’, it was narrated by al-Bukhari on the authority of Yahya ibn Bishr, on the authority of Shababah, and it was narrated by Abu Dawud on the authority of Abu Mas’ud Ahmad ibn al-Furat al-Razi and Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah al-Makhzumi on the authority of Shababah on the authority of Warqa’ on the authority of ‘Amr ibn Dinar on the authority of ‘Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The people of Yemen performed Hajj without provisions and they said: We are the trusting ones, so God revealed, And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God. It was narrated by ‘Abd ibn Hamid in his Tafsir on the authority of Shababah, and Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Shababah on his authority, and Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd al-Ghaffar on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: When they entered ihram and had their provisions with them, they would throw them away and start over with other provisions, so it was revealed. God the Almighty said: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is piety. So they were forbidden from that and were commanded to take provisions of flour, gruel, and cakes. This is what Ibn al-Zubayr, Abu al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Sha’bi, al-Nakha’i, Salim ibn Abdullah, Ata’ al-Khurasani, Qatadah, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: So take provisions of flour, gruel, and cakes. Waki’ ibn al-Jarrah said in his interpretation: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suqah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, And take provisions, he said: Khashkananj and gruel. Waki’ also said: Ibrahim al-Makki told us, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: It is part of a man’s generosity to make his provisions good while traveling. Hammad ibn Salamah added to this, on the authority of Abu Rayhanah, that Ibn Umar used to stipulate that whoever accompanied him should be good. And his saying, The best provision is piety, when he ordered them to take provisions for travel in this world, he guided them to provisions for the Hereafter, which is taking piety with him to it, as he said, and feathers and the clothing of piety, that is best. When he mentioned the physical clothing, he drew the guide’s attention to the spiritual clothing, which is humility, obedience and piety, and he mentioned that it is better than this and more beneficial. Ata’ al-Khurasani said in his saying, The best provision is piety, meaning provisions for the Hereafter. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Abdun told us, Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, Whoever takes provisions in this world, it will benefit him in the Hereafter. And Muqatil ibn Hayyan said, when this verse was revealed, And take provisions, a poor man from the Muslims stood up and said, O Messenger of God, we do not find anything to take provisions with us, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Take provisions with which to keep your face from people, and the best provision for you is piety. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And his saying, And fear Me, O you of understanding. He says: And fear My punishment, My chastisement, and My torment for those who disobey Me and do not obey My command, O you of minds and understanding.
2:198: Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad told us, Ibn Uyaynah told me on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhu al-Majaz were markets in the pre-Islamic era, and they considered it a sin to trade during the season, so the verse, There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord was revealed during the Hajj seasons. And this is how Abd al-Razzaq, Saeed ibn Mansur, and others narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. And for some of them, when Islam came, they felt guilty about trading, so they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, so God revealed this verse. And Ibn Jurayj narrated it likewise on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The people’s trade in the pre-Islamic era was Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhu al-Majaz, but when Islam came, it was as if they hated that until this verse was revealed. And Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They used to avoid selling and trading during the season and Hajj, saying: Days of remembrance, so God revealed: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. And Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj. And Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: There is no blame upon you for buying and selling before and after entering ihram. And Al-Awfi narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Wakee’ said: Talhah ibn Amr told us. Al-Hadrami narrated from Ata’ from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the Hajj seasons. Abd al-Rahman said, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yazid: This is how Mujahid, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Mansur ibn al-Mu’tamir, Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas and others interpreted it. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan ibn Arfa told us, Shababah ibn Suwar told us, Shu’bah told us, from Abu Umaimah, I heard Ibn Umar asked about a man who was performing Hajj and had business with him, so Ibn Umar recited There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. This is a weak hadith, but it is strong and good. It has been narrated as a marfu’ hadith. Ahmad said: Asbat told us, Al-Has ibn Amr al-Faqimi told us, from Abu Umamah al-Taimi, who said: I said to Ibn Umar: If we rent, is there a Hajj for us? He said: Do you not circumambulate the House, go to the Ma’rif, throw stones at the Jamarat, and shave your heads? He said: We said: Yes. Ibn Umar said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about what you asked me, but he did not answer him until Gabriel came down to him with this verse: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and said: You are performing Hajj. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ath-Thawri told us on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of a man from Banu Tamim, who said: A man came to Abdullah ibn Umar and said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, we go out to rent and they claim that we do not have Hajj. He said: Do you not enter ihram as they do, and circumambulate as they do, and throw stones as they do? He said: Yes. He said: Then you are a pilgrim. Then Ibn Umar said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him what you asked about, so this verse was revealed: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. And Abd ibn Humayd narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq on his authority. And this is how Abu Hudhayfah narrated this hadith on the authority of al-Thawri, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. And this is how it was narrated from other chains of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Arfa told us, Abbad ibn al-Awwam told us on the authority of al-Ala ibn al-Musayyab on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Taimi, who said: I said to Ibn Umar: We are people who rent on this route to Mecca, and there are people who claim that we do not have a Hajj. Do you think we have a Hajj? He said: Do you not enter ihram and circumambulate the House and perform the rituals? He said: I said: Yes. He said: Then you are pilgrims. Then he said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about what you asked, but he did not know what it would bring him back, or he said: He did not respond to anything until the verse: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord was revealed. So he called the man and recited it to him, and said: You are pilgrims. And this is how Mas`ud ibn Sa`d, `Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, and Sharik al-Qadi narrated it on the authority of al-`Ala` ibn al-Musayyab, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Jarir said: Taliq ibn Muhammad al-Wasiti told me, Asbat - he is Ibn Muhammad - told us, al-Hasan ibn `Amr - he is al-Fuqaimi - told us on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Taimi, who said: I said to Ibn `Umar: We are people who hire, so do we have a pilgrimage? He said: Do you not circumambulate the House, go to al-`Araf, throw stones at the Jamarat, and shave your heads? We said: Yes. He said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about what you asked me about, and he did not know what to say to him until Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down with this verse: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord to the end of the verse, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are pilgrims. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told me, Abu Ahmad told us, Ghundar told us on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muhajir on the authority of Abu Salih, the freed slave of Amr, who said: I said: O Commander of the Faithful, did you trade during the Hajj? He said: Was their livelihood anything but during the Hajj? And the Almighty said: And when you depart from Arafat, remember God at the sacred monument. Arafat is inflected, even though it is a feminine name, because it is originally a plural like Muslimat and Muminat, a specific spot was named after it and the origin was derived from it, so it was inflected. Ibn Jarir chose this. Arafat is the place of standing during Hajj, and it is the main action of Hajj. For this reason, Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunnah narrated with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Thawri on the authority of Bakir on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ya’mar Al-Dailami, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Hajj is Arafat - three days - so whoever reaches Arafat before dawn has reached it, and the days of Mina are three, so whoever hastens in two days there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays there is no sin upon him.” The time of standing is from noon on the Day of Arafat until the second dawn of the Day of Sacrifice, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood during the Farewell Pilgrimage after praying the noon prayer until the sun set, and he said, So that you may learn your rituals from me. And he said in this hadith, So whoever reaches Arafat before dawn has reached it. And this is The doctrine of Malik, Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them. Imam Ahmad held that the time for standing is from the first day of Arafah. They cited as evidence the hadith of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Urwah ibn Mudris ibn Haritha ibn Lam Al-Ta’i, who said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Muzdalifah when he went out to pray. I said: O Messenger of God, I came from Mount Tayy, I tired out my mount, and I exhausted myself. By God, I did not leave a mountain without standing on it. Is there any Hajj for me? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever witnesses this prayer of ours and stands with us until we depart, and has stood at Arafat before that, at night or during the day, then his Hajj is complete and his ritual purity is fulfilled.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan, and authenticated by Al-Tirmidhi. Then it was said: It was called Arafat because Abd Al-Razzaq narrated: Ibn Jurayj told me, he said: Ibn Al-Musayyab said: Ali bin Abi Talib said: God sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, to Abraham, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he performed Hajj with him, until when he came to Arafat he said: I know, and he had come to it once before that, so that is why it was called Arafat. Ibn Al-Mubarak said on the authority of Abd Al-Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’, he said: It was called Arafat because Gabriel used to show Abraham the rituals and say: I know, I know, so it was called Arafat. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Abu Majlaz, and God knows best. Arafat is called Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, Al-Mash’ar Al-Aqsa, and Ilal on the weight of Hilal, and the mountain in the middle of it is called Jabal Al-Rahmah. Abu Talib said in His famous poem: And at Al-Mash’ar Al-Aqsa, if they intend to go there, they will go to those opposite paths. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hammad bin Al-Hasan bin Anbasa told us, Abu Aamer told us, on the authority of Zama’ah, he is Ibn Salih, on the authority of Salamah bin Wahram, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to stand at Arafat until the sun was over the tops of the mountains, as if it were turbans on the heads of men, then they would set off. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delayed the set off from Arafat until the sun had set. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Zama’ah bin Salih, and he added: Then he stood at Muzdalifah and prayed the dawn prayer in the early morning, until everything had become light and it was the last time, then he set off. This is a good chain of transmission. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais, on the authority of Al-Miswar bin Makhramah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us a sermon while he was at Arafat, so he praised God and thanked Him, then he said: As for what follows - and whenever he gave a sermon he would say: As for what follows - this day is the greatest pilgrimage. Beware, the people of polytheism and idolatry used to set off on this day before the sun set, when the sun was over the tops of the mountains, as if it were turbans on the faces of men. And we “We pay after the sun sets, and they used to pay from the sacred monument after the sun rises if the sun is on the tops of the mountains as if it were men’s turbans on their faces, and we pay before the sun rises, our guidance is contrary to the guidance of the polytheists,” this is how Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, and this is its wording, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, both of them from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak al-Aishi from Abd al-Warith ibn Sa’id from Ibn Jurayj, and Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it, and it is authentic and proven by what we mentioned that Al-Miswar heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: not as some of our companions imagine that he has a vision without hearing, and Wakee’ said, from Shu’bah, from Ismail ibn Raja’ al-Zubaidi, from Al-Ma’rur ibn Suwaid, he said: I saw Umar, may God be pleased with him, when he paid from Arafat, as if I was looking at him, a bald man on his camel being placed, and he was saying: We have found that ifadah is placing, and in the long hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah that is in Sahih Muslim, he said in it: So he did not stop standing - meaning in Arafat - until the sun set, and it appeared He stayed up a little until the sun disappeared, and Usamah rode behind him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had pulled the reins of Al-Qaswaa so that her head would touch the saddle of his saddle, and he would say with his right hand: O people, tranquility, tranquility. Whenever he came to a mountain, he would let it down a little so that it could ascend until he came to Muzdalifah, and he prayed Maghrib and Isha with one call to prayer and two Iqama, and he did not glorify God in between them. Then he lay down until dawn came, and he prayed Fajr until dawn became clear to him with one call to prayer and one Iqama. Then he rode Al-Qaswaa until he came to Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, and he faced the Qiblah, and he supplicated to God, glorified Him, and declared His oneness, and he did not stop standing until it became very light, so he set off before the sun rose. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, that he was asked: How did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walk when he set off? He said: He would walk at the neck, and if he found a gap, he would move forward. The neck is the stretch of the gait, and the text is above it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Muhammad Ibn Bint Al-Shafi’i told us in what he wrote to me on the authority of his father or his uncle, on the authority of Sufyan Ibn Uyaynah, his saying, And when you depart from Arafat, remember God at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, which is both prayers. Abu Ishaq Al-Subai’i said, on the authority of Amr Ibn Maimun: I asked Abdullah Ibn Amr about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, and he remained silent until our mounts descended at Muzdalifah. He said, Where is the one who asked about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram? This is Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, who said, Ibn Umar said, Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram is all of Muzdalifah. Hisham said, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: He was asked about his saying, And remember God at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, and he said, This is the mountain and what is around it. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Ibn Umar saw them crowding at Qahza, so he said: Why are these crowding? Each one here has a sacred place. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Mujahid, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi bin Anas, Al-Hasan and Qatadah that they said: It is between the two mountains. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Ata’: Where is Muzdalifah? He said: When you pass through the two passages of Arafah, then that is to Muhsar. He said: The two passages of Arafah are not from Muzdalifah, but rather their passages. He said: Stand between them if you wish. He said: I prefer that you stand before Qahza, come to us because of the people’s path. I said The sacred places are the visible landmarks, and Muzdalifah was called the sacred place because it is inside the sanctuary. Is standing there a pillar of Hajj without which it is not valid, as a group of the Salaf and some of the companions of Al-Shafi’i believed, including Al-Qaffal and Ibn Khuzaymah, based on the hadith of Urwah bin Mudaris? Or is it obligatory, as is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, and is it compensated for by blood money? Or is it recommended that nothing should be omitted, as is the other opinion? There are three opinions of scholars on this, which will be expanded upon elsewhere, and God knows best. Abdullah bin Mubarak said, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, All of Arafat is a place of standing, so leave ‘Urnah, and all of Jam’ is a place of standing except Muhsir. This is a mursal hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughira told us, Saeed bin ‘Abd al-‘Aziz told us, Sulayman bin Musa told me, on the authority of Jubayr bin Mut’im, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, “All of Arafat is a place of standing, so leave ‘Urnah, and all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing, and leave Muhsir, and all of the paths of Mecca are places of sacrifice, and all of the days of Tashreeq are places of slaughter.” This is also disconnected, because this Sulayman bin Musa, who is al-Ashdaq, did not meet Jubayr bin Mut’im, but al-Walid bin Muslim and Suwayd bin ‘Abd al-‘Aziz narrated it on the authority of Sulayman, so al-Walid said, on the authority of Jubayr bin Mut’im on the authority of his father, and Suwayd said on the authority of Nafi’ bin Jubayr on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it, and God knows best. His saying, And remember Him as He has guided you, is a reminder to them of the blessings that God has bestowed upon them of guidance, clarification, and direction to the rituals of Hajj, as was the guidance of Abraham, peace be upon him. For this reason, He said, And if you were before that among those astray, it was said: before this guidance, before the Qur’an, and before the Messenger, and all of them are close, consistent, and correct.
2:199: Then - here - to connect one piece of report to another and arrange it according to it, as if God Almighty commanded the one standing at Arafat to go to Muzdalifah to remember God at the sacred monument, and He commanded him to stand with the majority of the people at Arafat, as the majority of the people used to do, they would stand there except for Quraysh, for they did not leave the sanctuary, so they would stand at the edge of the sanctuary at the lowest point of the sanctuary, and they would say: We are the people of God in His city and the inhabitants of His house. Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Muhammad bin Hazim told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said: Quraysh and those who followed their religion would stand at Muzdalifah, and they were called Al-Hams, and the rest of the Arabs would stand at Arafat, so when Islam came, God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come to Arafat, then stand there, then depart from it, so that is His saying, from where the people depart. And Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and others said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose it and narrated on his authority. Consensus, and Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jubair bin Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said: I lost my camel in Arafat, so I went to look for it, and there was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing there. I said: This is from the Hums, what is the matter with him here? They included it in the two Sahihs, then Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: What indicates that what is meant by al-Ifadah here is the Ifadah from Muzdalifah to Mina to throw the pebbles, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim only. He said: What is meant by the people is Abraham, peace be upon him. In a narration from the Imam, Ibn Jarir said: If it were not for the consensus of the proof to the contrary, it would have been the most likely. His saying, And seek forgiveness from God, for God is Forgiving and Merciful. God often commands us to remember Him after performing acts of worship. For this reason, it is proven in Sahih Muslim that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished the prayer, he would seek forgiveness from God three times. In the two Sahihs, it is recommended to glorify, praise, and magnify God thirty-three times. Ibn Jarir narrated here the hadith of Ibn Abbas bin Mirdas Al-Salami, in his seeking forgiveness, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his nation on the eve of Arafah, and we have included it in a section that we have collected on the virtue of the Day of Arafah. Ibn Mardawayh included here the hadith that Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best form of seeking forgiveness is for the servant to say: O God, You are my Lord, there is no god but You, You created me and I am Your servant, and I am bound by Your covenant and promise as much as I am able, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done, I acknowledge Your blessings upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You. Whoever says it at night and dies that night will enter Paradise, and whoever says it during the day and dies will enter Paradise.” In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, teach me a supplication that I can say in my prayer, so he said: “Say: O God, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins except You, so forgive me with a forgiveness from You.” Have mercy on me, for You are the Forgiving, the Most Merciful.” There are many hadiths about seeking forgiveness.
2:200: God Almighty commands us to remember Him and to do so frequently after completing the rituals and finishing them. And His saying, Like your remembrance of your fathers, they differed in its meaning. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’: It is like a child saying, Father, mother, meaning just as a child is constantly mentioning his father and mother, so too should you constantly mention God after completing the rituals. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said the same. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The people of the Jahiliyyah would stand during the season and one of them would say, My father used to feed and carry the loads and carry the blood money. They had no remembrance other than the deeds of their fathers. So God revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, So remember God as you remember your fathers or with a greater remembrance. Ibn Abi Hatim said: As-Suddi narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik, Abu Wa’il, and Ata’ bin Abi Rabah in one of his two opinions, and Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah in one of his narrations, and Mujahid, As-Suddi, and Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Muhammad bin Ka’b, and Muqatil bin Hayyan are similar to that, and Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise from a group, and God knows best. The purpose of it is to encourage frequent remembrance of God, the Almighty and Majestic, and for this reason the accusative of His statement, or more intense remembrance, is to distinguish, meaning like your remembrance of your fathers or more intense remembrance, and or here is to confirm the similarity in the report, like His statement, So they are like stones or even harder and His statement, They fear people as they fear God or even more intensely and And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more and So he was two bow lengths away or nearer so it is not here for doubt, certainly, but rather it is to confirm what is reported about as such or even more than that, then God, the Almighty, guided to His supplication after frequent remembrance of Him, for it is the most likely answer, and He condemned the one who does not ask Him except for the matter of his worldly life and is ignorant of his afterlife, so He said, And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he has no share in the Hereafter meaning no portion or share, and this condemnation and warning against imitating someone who is Likewise, Saeed bin Jubair said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A group of Bedouins used to come to the place of standing and say: O God, make it a year of rain, a year of fertility, and a year of good offspring, without mentioning anything about the Hereafter. So God revealed about them: And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter. And others of the believers used to come after them and say: Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. So God revealed: Those will have a share of what they have earned, and God is swift in account. For this reason, He praised those who ask Him for this world and the Hereafter, saying: And among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’ So this supplication gathered all good in this world and averted all evil, for good in this world includes every worldly desire, such as well-being, a spacious home, a beautiful wife, abundant provision, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, a pleasant mount, and beautiful praise, and other things that the commentators’ expressions included, and there is no contradiction between them, for they are all It is included in the good in this world, and as for the good in the Hereafter, the highest of that is entering Paradise and its consequences of security from the greatest terror in the gathering places, and the facilitation of the reckoning and other good matters of the Hereafter. As for salvation from the Fire, it requires facilitating its causes in this world by avoiding forbidden things and sins and abandoning doubtful and forbidden things. Al-Qasim bin Abdul-Rahman said: Whoever is given a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a patient body, has been given a good in this world, and a good in the Hereafter, and has been protected from the torment of the Fire. For this reason, the Sunnah has been reported to encourage this supplication. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Muammar told us, Abdul-Warith told us, on the authority of Abdul-Aziz, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: O God, our Lord, give us good in this world, and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire. Ahmad said: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Abdul-Aziz bin Suhaib told us, who said: Qatadah asked Anas: Which supplication was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the most frequently supplicated?? He said: He says: O God, our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire. When Anas wanted to supplicate, he would supplicate with it, and when he wanted to supplicate with a supplication, he would supplicate with it. Muslim narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Nu`aym told us, `Abd al-Salam ibn Shaddad told us, meaning Abu Talut, he said: I was with Anas ibn Malik, and Thabit said to him: Your brothers would like you to supplicate for them. He said: O God, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire. They talked for a while, until when they wanted to get up, he said: O Abu Hamza, your brothers want to get up, so supplicate to God for them. He said: Do you want me to make things difficult for you? If God gives you good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protects you from the torment of the Fire, then He has given you all good. Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Abi `Adi told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited a Muslim man who had become like a chick, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do you supplicate to God for something or ask Him for it? He said: “Yes, I used to say: ‘O God, whatever You are going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Glory be to God, you cannot bear it or are not able to do it. Why did you not say: ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and save us from the punishment of the Fire?’” He said: So he supplicated to him and He healed him. Muslim alone transmitted it, and he narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi Udayy. Imam Ash-Shafi’i said: Sa’id ibn Salim Al-Qaddah informed us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ubayd, the freed slave of As-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn As-Sa’ib: that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Corner: ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and save us from the punishment of the Fire.’” Al-Thawri also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Majah narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but there is weakness in its chain of transmission, and God knows best. Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdul-Baqi told us, Ahmad bin Al-Qasim bin Musawar told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Sulaiman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hormuz, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I never passed by the corner except that I saw an angel saying, ‘Ameen.’ So when you pass by it, say, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’” Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Zakariya Al-Anbari told us, Muhammad bin Abdul-Salam told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: I hired myself out to a people on the condition that they would carry me, and I reduced my wages for them on the condition that they would let me perform Hajj with them. Will that be acceptable? He said: You are one of those about whom God said: ‘Those will have a share of what they have earned, and God is swift in account.’ Then Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it.
