They talked for a while, until when they wanted to get up, he said: O Abu Hamza, your brothers want to get up, so supplicate to God for them. He said: Do you want me to make things difficult for you? If God gives you good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protects you from the torment of the Fire, then He has given you all good. Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Abi `Adi told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited a Muslim man who had become like a chick, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do you supplicate to God for something or ask Him for it? He said: “Yes, I used to say: ‘O God, whatever You are going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Glory be to God, you cannot bear it or are not able to do it. Why did you not say: ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and save us from the punishment of the Fire?’” He said: So he supplicated to him and He healed him. Muslim alone transmitted it, and he narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi Udayy. Imam Ash-Shafi’i said: Sa’id ibn Salim Al-Qaddah informed us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ubayd, the freed slave of As-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn As-Sa’ib: that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Corner: ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and save us from the punishment of the Fire.’” Al-Thawri also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Majah narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but there is weakness in its chain of transmission, and God knows best. Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdul-Baqi told us, Ahmad bin Al-Qasim bin Musawar told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Sulaiman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hormuz, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I never passed by the corner except that I saw an angel saying, ‘Ameen.’ So when you pass by it, say, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’” Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Zakariya Al-Anbari told us, Muhammad bin Abdul-Salam told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: I hired myself out to a people on the condition that they would carry me, and I reduced my wages for them on the condition that they would let me perform Hajj with them. Will that be acceptable? He said: You are one of those about whom God said: ‘Those will have a share of what they have earned, and God is swift in account.’ Then Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it.
2:202: God Almighty commands us to remember Him and to do so frequently after completing the rituals and finishing them. And His saying, Like your remembrance of your fathers, they differed in its meaning. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’: It is like a child saying, Father, mother, meaning just as a child is constantly mentioning his father and mother, so too should you constantly mention God after completing the rituals. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said the same. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The people of the Jahiliyyah would stand during the season and one of them would say, My father used to feed and carry the loads and carry the blood money. They had no remembrance other than the deeds of their fathers. So God revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, So remember God as you remember your fathers or with a greater remembrance. Ibn Abi Hatim said: As-Suddi narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik, Abu Wa’il, and Ata’ bin Abi Rabah in one of his two opinions, and Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah in one of his narrations, and Mujahid, As-Suddi, and Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Muhammad bin Ka’b, and Muqatil bin Hayyan are similar to that, and Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise from a group, and God knows best. The purpose of it is to encourage frequent remembrance of God, the Almighty and Majestic, and for this reason the accusative of His statement, or more intense remembrance, is to distinguish, meaning like your remembrance of your fathers or more intense remembrance, and or here is to confirm the similarity in the report, like His statement, So they are like stones or even harder and His statement, They fear people as they fear God or even more intensely and And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more and So he was two bow lengths away or nearer so it is not here for doubt, certainly, but rather it is to confirm what is reported about as such or even more than that, then God, the Almighty, guided to His supplication after frequent remembrance of Him, for it is the most likely answer, and He condemned the one who does not ask Him except for the matter of his worldly life and is ignorant of his afterlife, so He said, And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he has no share in the Hereafter meaning no portion or share, and this condemnation and warning against imitating someone who is Likewise, Saeed bin Jubair said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A group of Bedouins used to come to the place of standing and say: O God, make it a year of rain, a year of fertility, and a year of good offspring, without mentioning anything about the Hereafter. So God revealed about them: And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter. And others of the believers used to come after them and say: Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. So God revealed: Those will have a share of what they have earned, and God is swift in account. For this reason, He praised those who ask Him for this world and the Hereafter, saying: And among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’ So this supplication gathered all good in this world and averted all evil, for good in this world includes every worldly desire, such as well-being, a spacious home, a beautiful wife, abundant provision, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, a pleasant mount, and beautiful praise, and other things that the commentators’ expressions included, and there is no contradiction between them, for they are all It is included in the good in this world, and as for the good in the Hereafter, the highest of that is entering Paradise and its consequences of security from the greatest terror in the gathering places, and the facilitation of the reckoning and other good matters of the Hereafter. As for salvation from the Fire, it requires facilitating its causes in this world by avoiding forbidden things and sins and abandoning doubtful and forbidden things. Al-Qasim bin Abdul-Rahman said: Whoever is given a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a patient body, has been given a good in this world, and a good in the Hereafter, and has been protected from the torment of the Fire. For this reason, the Sunnah has been reported to encourage this supplication. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Muammar told us, Abdul-Warith told us, on the authority of Abdul-Aziz, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: O God, our Lord, give us good in this world, and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire. Ahmad said: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Abdul-Aziz bin Suhaib told us, who said: Qatadah asked Anas: Which supplication was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the most frequently supplicated?? He said: He says: O God, our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire. When Anas wanted to supplicate, he would supplicate with it, and when he wanted to supplicate with a supplication, he would supplicate with it. Muslim narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Nu`aym told us, `Abd al-Salam ibn Shaddad told us, meaning Abu Talut, he said: I was with Anas ibn Malik, and Thabit said to him: Your brothers would like you to supplicate for them. He said: O God, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire. They talked for a while, until when they wanted to get up, he said: O Abu Hamza, your brothers want to get up, so supplicate to God for them. He said: Do you want me to make things difficult for you? If God gives you good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protects you from the torment of the Fire, then He has given you all good. Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Abi `Adi told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited a Muslim man who had become like a chick, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do you supplicate to God for something or ask Him for it? He said: “Yes, I used to say: ‘O God, whatever You are going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Glory be to God, you cannot bear it or are not able to do it. Why did you not say: ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and save us from the punishment of the Fire?’” He said: So he supplicated to him and He healed him. Muslim alone transmitted it, and he narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi Udayy. Imam Ash-Shafi’i said: Sa’id ibn Salim Al-Qaddah informed us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ubayd, the freed slave of As-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn As-Sa’ib: that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Corner: ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and save us from the punishment of the Fire.’” Al-Thawri also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Majah narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but there is weakness in its chain of transmission, and God knows best. Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdul-Baqi told us, Ahmad bin Al-Qasim bin Musawar told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Sulaiman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hormuz, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I never passed by the corner except that I saw an angel saying, ‘Ameen.’ So when you pass by it, say, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’” Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Zakariya Al-Anbari told us, Muhammad bin Abdul-Salam told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: I hired myself out to a people on the condition that they would carry me, and I reduced my wages for them on the condition that they would let me perform Hajj with them. Will that be acceptable? He said: You are one of those about whom God said: ‘Those will have a share of what they have earned, and God is swift in account.’ Then Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it.
2:203: Ibn Abbas said: The numbered days are the days of Tashreeq, and the known days are the ten days. Ikrimah said: And remember God during the numbered days meaning the Takbir on the days of Tashreeq after the obligatory prayers: God is Great, God is Great. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, Musa bin Ali narrated to us on the authority of his father, who said: I heard Uqbah bin Amir say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Day of Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashreeq are our Eid, O people of Islam, and they are days of eating and drinking. Ahmad also said: Hisham narrated to us, Khalid informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Malih, on the authority of Nabisha al-Hudhali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Days of Tashreeq are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God. Muslim also narrated it. The hadith of Jubayr bin Mut`im was presented, All of Arafah is a place of standing, and all of the Days of Tashreeq are for slaughtering. The hadith of Abd al-Rahman bin Ya`mar al-Dailami was also presented, And the days of Mina are three, so whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him. Ibn Jarir said: Ya`qub bin Ibrahim and Khallad bin Aslam narrated to us, who said: Hisham narrated to us on the authority of Amr bin Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Days of Tashreeq are days of eating and remembering God. Khallad bin Aslam narrated to us, who said: Ruh, Salih told us, Ibn Shihab told me on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abdullah bin Hudhafah to circumambulate Mina: Do not fast these days, for they are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God Almighty. And Ya’qub told us, Hisham told us on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abdullah bin Hudhafah and he called out during the days of Tashreeq, saying: These are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God, except for those who have to fast from an offering. A good addition, but it is mursal, and Hisham said the same on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Bishr bin Suhaim and he called out during the days of Tashreeq, saying: These are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God. And Hisham said on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade fasting during the days of Tashreeq, saying: They are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God. And Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Hakim bin Hakim, on the authority of Masoud bin Al-Hakam Al-Zarqi, on the authority of his mother, who said: It is as if I see Ali on the white mule of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he stopped at the valley of the Ansar and he was saying: O people, these are not days of fasting, rather they are days of eating, drinking and remembering God. And Muqsim said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The numbered days are the days of Tashreeq, four days: the Day of Sacrifice, and the three days after it. And it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Abu Musa, Ata’, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Malik, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Yahya bin Abi Katheer, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Al-Zuhri, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Dahhak, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Malik bin Anas and others, something similar to that. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: There are three: the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it. Sacrifice on whichever of them you wish, and the best of them is the first. The first statement is the well-known, and the apparent meaning of the noble verse indicates this where He said: But whoever hastens within two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him. So it indicates three after the Sacrifice. It is related to His saying: And remember God during the appointed days. God mentioned the sacrifices, and it was mentioned earlier. The most correct opinion in this regard is the school of thought of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, which is that the time for the sacrifice is from the Day of Sacrifice until the end of Tashreeq. The timed remembrance after the prayers is also related to it. The absolute opinion in all cases and in its time are the opinions of the scholars, the most famous of which is the one that is practiced, which is from the dawn prayer on the Day of Arafah until the afternoon prayer on the last days of Tashreeq, which is the last of the last departure. A hadith was narrated about it by Al-Daraqutni, but it is not authentically attributed to the Prophet. God knows best. It has been proven that Omar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say the takbir in his tent, and the people of the market would say the takbir with his takbir until Mina shook with takbir. The takbir and remembrance of God when throwing the pebbles is also related to this. One of the days of Tashreeq. It was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawood and others: Circumambulating the House, walking between Safa and Marwa, and stoning the Jamarat were made to establish the remembrance of God Almighty. And when God Almighty mentioned the first and second departures, which is the dispersal of people from the Hajj season to all regions and horizons after their gathering in the sacred sites and the place of standing, He said: And fear God and know that to Him you will be gathered, as He said: And it is He who dispersed you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.
2:204: Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Al-Akhns bin Shuraik Al-Thaqafi, who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and outwardly declared Islam, but inwardly he was the opposite. And from Ibn Abbas, it was revealed about a group of hypocrites who spoke about Khubayb and his companions who were killed in Al-Raji’ and criticized them, so God revealed in condemnation of the hypocrites and praise of Khubayb and his companions: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And it was said: Rather, it is general for all the hypocrites and all the believers. This is the saying of Qatada, Mujahid, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and more than one, and it is correct. And Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Al-Layth bin Sa’d told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Nawf, who is Al-Bakali, and he was one of those who read books, he said: I find a description of some people from this nation in the revealed Book of God: A people who scheme for the world through religion, their tongues are sweeter than honey, and their hearts are more bitter than aloes, they deceive people. The udders of sheep, and their hearts are the hearts of wolves. God the Almighty says: They dare to do so and are deceived by Me. I swear by Myself that I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered. Al-Qurazi said: I pondered it in the Qur’an and found that they were the hypocrites and found it: And among the people is he whose speech about worldly life pleases you, and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart 2:10. Muhammad bin Abi Ma’shar told me: Abu Ma’shar Najih told me: I heard Sa’id al-Maqburi discussing with Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi, and Sa’id said: In some books: There are servants whose tongues are sweeter than honey, and whose hearts are more bitter than aloes. They dress up the udders of sheep for people out of softness, they chew the world with religion. God the Almighty said: You dare to do so and are deceived by Me? By My glory, I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered. Muhammad bin Ka’b said: This is in the Book of God. Sa’id said: Where is it in the Book of God? He said: The saying of God: And among the people is he whose speech about worldly life pleases you 2:10. Sa’id said: Do you know about whom this verse was revealed? Muhammad ibn Ka`b said: The verse is revealed about a man and then becomes general afterwards. This is what Al-Qurazi said, good and correct. As for his saying, And God bears witness to what is in his heart, Ibn Muhaisin read it as And God bears witness with the opening of the ya’ and the damma of the majesty to what is in his heart. Its meaning is that even if this person shows you tricks, God knows what is in his ugly heart, as God Almighty says: “When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ And God knows that you are His Messenger. And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.” The majority read it with the damma of the ya’ and the nasb of the majesty, God bears witness to what is in his heart, and its meaning is that he shows Islam to the people and confronts God with what is in his heart of disbelief and hypocrisy, as God Almighty says: They hide from the people but they do not hide from God, the verse. This is the meaning of what Ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: Its meaning is that if he shows Islam to the people, he swears and God bears witness to them that what is in his heart is in agreement with his tongue. This meaning is correct, and it was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir chose it and attributed it to Ibn Abbas and narrated it from Mujahid, and God knows best. And his saying, And he is the most stubborn of opponents, “the most stubborn” in the language means the most crooked, “and you warn with it a people who are stubborn,” meaning crooked. And thus is the hypocrite in his state of opposition, he lies and deviates from the truth and does not straighten out with it, rather he slanders and commits wickedness, as it was proven in the Sahih on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, “The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he breaks it, and when he argues he commits wickedness.” Al-Bukhari said: Qubaysah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The most hated of men to God is the most stubborn opponent. He said: Abdullah bin Yazid said: Sufyan told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ibn Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The most hated of men to God is the most stubborn opponent. And thus Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar in his statement: And he is the most stubborn opponent, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The most hated of men to God is the most stubborn opponent. And His saying, “And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And God does not love corruption.” That is, he is crooked in speech and evil in deeds. That is what he says and this is what he does. His speech is a lie, his belief is corrupt, and his actions are ugly. Striving here is the intention, as He said, reporting about Pharaoh, “Then he turned back, striving. So he was gathered together and called out. He said, ‘I am your Lord, the Most High.’ So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first world. Indeed in that is a lesson for him who fears.” And God Almighty said, O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu’ah, then proceed to the remembrance of God. That is, proceed and intend by that the Friday prayer, for the physical striving for prayer is forbidden by the Prophetic Sunnah, When you come to prayer, do not come to it while you are running, but come to it with tranquility and dignity. So this hypocrite has no concern other than corruption on the land and the destruction of crops, which is the place where crops, fruits, and animals grow, and it is the offspring of animals without which people cannot sustain themselves. And Mujahid said: If he seeks to cause corruption on earth, God will withhold rain, and the crops and offspring will perish. And God does not love corruption, meaning He does not love someone who has this characteristic, nor someone who does that. And His saying, And when it is said to him, ‘Fear God,’ pride in sin takes hold of him, meaning, if this wicked person is admonished in his speech and actions, and it is said to him, ‘Fear God, desist from your speech and actions, and return to the truth,’ he refuses and rejects, and pride and anger take hold of him in sin, meaning because of what he included of sins. This verse is similar to the saying of God Almighty: “And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve disapproval. They almost assault those who recite to them Our verses. Say, ‘Shall I inform you of [someone] worse than that? The Fire which God has promised to those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination.’” That is why He said in this verse, So Hell is sufficient for him, and wretched is the resting place, meaning it is sufficient punishment for him in that. And His saying, And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God, when He informed about the hypocrites and their reprehensible qualities, He mentioned the praiseworthy qualities of the believers, saying, And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. Ibn Abbas, Anas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, and Ikrimah said: A group: It was revealed about Suhaib bin Sinan Al-Rumi, and that is because when he converted to Islam in Mecca and wanted to migrate, the people prevented him from migrating with his money, and if he wanted to give it up and migrate, he did, so he got rid of them and gave them his money, so God revealed this verse about him, so Omar bin Al-Khattab and a group met him at the edge of Al-Harrah and they said to him: The sale is profitable, so he said: And you, may God not make your trade a loss, and what is that? So he told him that God revealed this verse about him, and it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: The sale is profitable, Suhaib. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ibrahim told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Rustah told us, Sulaiman bin Dawud told us, Jaafar bin Sulaiman Al-Dhabi told us, Awf told us on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi on the authority of Suhaib, he said: When I wanted to migrate from Mecca to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Quraysh said to me: O Suhaib, you have come to us and you have no money, and you and your money will leave, by God that will never happen, so I said to them: Do you think that if I give you my money, will you leave me? They said: Yes, so I gave them my money, so they left me, so I went out until I arrived in Madinah, and the report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: Suhaib has profited, Suhaib has profited twice, and Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: Suhaib came as an immigrant towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group of Quraysh followed him, so he got down from his mount and threw away what was in his quiver, then he said: O people of Quraysh, you know that I am the best archer among you, and by God, you will not reach me until I shoot every arrow in my quiver, then I will strike with my sword whatever is left in my hand of it, then do what you want, and if you want, I will show you my money and my property in Mecca and you will leave me alone, they said: Yes, so when he arrived to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The sale is profitable, and he said: And the verse was revealed: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is Kind to His servants.” As for the majority, they interpreted that to mean that it was revealed about every mujahid in the way of God, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, God He has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed. This is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur’an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is what is the great attainment. When Hisham bin Amir charged between the two lines, some of the people denounced him, so Umar bin Al-Khattab, Abu Hurairah, and others responded to them, and recited this verse: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is Kind to His servants.”
2:205: Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Al-Akhns bin Shuraik Al-Thaqafi, who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and outwardly declared Islam, but inwardly he was the opposite. And from Ibn Abbas, it was revealed about a group of hypocrites who spoke about Khubayb and his companions who were killed in Al-Raji’ and criticized them, so God revealed in condemnation of the hypocrites and praise of Khubayb and his companions: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And it was said: Rather, it is general for all the hypocrites and all the believers. This is the saying of Qatada, Mujahid, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and more than one, and it is correct. And Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Al-Layth bin Sa’d told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Nawf, who is Al-Bakali, and he was one of those who read books, he said: I find a description of some people from this nation in the revealed Book of God: A people who scheme for the world through religion, their tongues are sweeter than honey, and their hearts are more bitter than aloes, they deceive people. The udders of sheep, and their hearts are the hearts of wolves. God the Almighty says: They dare to do so and are deceived by Me. I swear by Myself that I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered. Al-Qurazi said: I pondered it in the Qur’an and found that they were the hypocrites and found it: And among the people is he whose speech about worldly life pleases you, and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart 2:10. Muhammad bin Abi Ma’shar told me: Abu Ma’shar Najih told me: I heard Sa’id al-Maqburi discussing with Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi, and Sa’id said: In some books: There are servants whose tongues are sweeter than honey, and whose hearts are more bitter than aloes. They dress up the udders of sheep for people out of softness, they chew the world with religion. God the Almighty said: You dare to do so and are deceived by Me? By My glory, I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered. Muhammad bin Ka’b said: This is in the Book of God. Sa’id said: Where is it in the Book of God? He said: The saying of God: And among the people is he whose speech about worldly life pleases you 2:10. Sa’id said: Do you know about whom this verse was revealed? Muhammad ibn Ka`b said: The verse is revealed about a man and then becomes general afterwards. This is what Al-Qurazi said, good and correct. As for his saying, And God bears witness to what is in his heart, Ibn Muhaisin read it as And God bears witness with the opening of the ya’ and the damma of the majesty to what is in his heart. Its meaning is that even if this person shows you tricks, God knows what is in his ugly heart, as God Almighty says: “When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ And God knows that you are His Messenger. And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.” The majority read it with the damma of the ya’ and the nasb of the majesty, God bears witness to what is in his heart, and its meaning is that he shows Islam to the people and confronts God with what is in his heart of disbelief and hypocrisy, as God Almighty says: They hide from the people but they do not hide from God, the verse. This is the meaning of what Ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: Its meaning is that if he shows Islam to the people, he swears and God bears witness to them that what is in his heart is in agreement with his tongue. This meaning is correct, and it was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir chose it and attributed it to Ibn Abbas and narrated it from Mujahid, and God knows best. And his saying, And he is the most stubborn of opponents, “the most stubborn” in the language means the most crooked, “and you warn with it a people who are stubborn,” meaning crooked. And thus is the hypocrite in his state of opposition, he lies and deviates from the truth and does not straighten out with it, rather he slanders and commits wickedness, as it was proven in the Sahih on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, “The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he breaks it, and when he argues he commits wickedness.” Al-Bukhari said: Qubaysah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The most hated of men to God is the most stubborn opponent. He said: Abdullah bin Yazid said: Sufyan told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ibn Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The most hated of men to God is the most stubborn opponent. And thus Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar in his statement: And he is the most stubborn opponent, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The most hated of men to God is the most stubborn opponent. And His saying, “And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And God does not love corruption.” That is, he is crooked in speech and evil in deeds. That is what he says and this is what he does. His speech is a lie, his belief is corrupt, and his actions are ugly. Striving here is the intention, as He said, reporting about Pharaoh, “Then he turned back, striving. So he was gathered together and called out. He said, ‘I am your Lord, the Most High.’ So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first world. Indeed in that is a lesson for him who fears.” And God Almighty said, O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu’ah, then proceed to the remembrance of God. That is, proceed and intend by that the Friday prayer, for the physical striving for prayer is forbidden by the Prophetic Sunnah, When you come to prayer, do not come to it while you are running, but come to it with tranquility and dignity. So this hypocrite has no concern other than corruption on the land and the destruction of crops, which is the place where crops, fruits, and animals grow, and it is the offspring of animals without which people cannot sustain themselves. And Mujahid said: If he seeks to cause corruption on earth, God will withhold rain, and the crops and offspring will perish. And God does not love corruption, meaning He does not love someone who has this characteristic, nor someone who does that. And His saying, And when it is said to him, ‘Fear God,’ pride in sin takes hold of him, meaning, if this wicked person is admonished in his speech and actions, and it is said to him, ‘Fear God, desist from your speech and actions, and return to the truth,’ he refuses and rejects, and pride and anger take hold of him in sin, meaning because of what he included of sins. This verse is similar to the saying of God Almighty: “And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve disapproval. They almost assault those who recite to them Our verses. Say, ‘Shall I inform you of [someone] worse than that? The Fire which God has promised to those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination.’” That is why He said in this verse, So Hell is sufficient for him, and wretched is the resting place, meaning it is sufficient punishment for him in that. And His saying, And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God, when He informed about the hypocrites and their reprehensible qualities, He mentioned the praiseworthy qualities of the believers, saying, And among mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. Ibn Abbas, Anas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, and Ikrimah said: A group: It was revealed about Suhaib bin Sinan Al-Rumi, and that is because when he converted to Islam in Mecca and wanted to migrate, the people prevented him from migrating with his money, and if he wanted to give it up and migrate, he did, so he got rid of them and gave them his money, so God revealed this verse about him, so Omar bin Al-Khattab and a group met him at the edge of Al-Harrah and they said to him: The sale is profitable, so he said: And you, may God not make your trade a loss, and what is that? So he told him that God revealed this verse about him, and it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: The sale is profitable, Suhaib. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ibrahim told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Rustah told us, Sulaiman bin Dawud told us, Jaafar bin Sulaiman Al-Dhabi told us, Awf told us on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi on the authority of Suhaib, he said: When I wanted to migrate from Mecca to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Quraysh said to me: O Suhaib, you have come to us and you have no money, and you and your money will leave, by God that will never happen, so I said to them: Do you think that if I give you my money, will you leave me? They said: Yes, so I gave them my money, so they left me, so I went out until I arrived in Madinah, and the report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: Suhaib has profited, Suhaib has profited twice, and Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: Suhaib came as an immigrant towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group of Quraysh followed him, so he got down from his mount and threw away what was in his quiver, then he said: O people of Quraysh, you know that I am the best archer among you, and by God, you will not reach me until I shoot every arrow in my quiver, then I will strike with my sword whatever is left in my hand of it, then do what you want, and if you want, I will show you my money and my property in Mecca and you will leave me alone, they said: Yes, so when he arrived to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The sale is profitable, and he said: And the verse was revealed: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is Kind to His servants.” As for the majority, they interpreted that to mean that it was revealed about every mujahid in the way of God, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, God He has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed. This is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur’an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is what is the great attainment. When Hisham bin Amir charged between the two lines, some of the people denounced him, so Umar bin Al-Khattab, Abu Hurairah, and others responded to them, and recited this verse: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is Kind to His servants.”

Ibn Abbas, Anas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, and Ikrimah said: A group: It was revealed about Suhaib bin Sinan Al-Rumi, and that is because when he converted to Islam in Mecca and wanted to migrate, the people prevented him from migrating with his money, and if he wanted to give it up and migrate, he did, so he got rid of them and gave them his money, so God revealed this verse about him, so Omar bin Al-Khattab and a group met him at the edge of Al-Harrah and they said to him: The sale is profitable, so he said: And you, may God not make your trade a loss, and what is that? So he told him that God revealed this verse about him, and it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: The sale is profitable, Suhaib. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ibrahim told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Rustah told us, Sulaiman bin Dawud told us, Jaafar bin Sulaiman Al-Dhabi told us, Awf told us on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi on the authority of Suhaib, he said: When I wanted to migrate from Mecca to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Quraysh said to me: O Suhaib, you have come to us and you have no money, and you and your money will leave, by God that will never happen, so I said to them: Do you think that if I give you my money, will you leave me? They said: Yes, so I gave them my money, so they left me, so I went out until I arrived in Madinah, and the report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: Suhaib has profited, Suhaib has profited twice, and Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: Suhaib came as an immigrant towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group of Quraysh followed him, so he got down from his mount and threw away what was in his quiver, then he said: O people of Quraysh, you know that I am the best archer among you, and by God, you will not reach me until I shoot every arrow in my quiver, then I will strike with my sword whatever is left in my hand of it, then do what you want, and if you want, I will show you my money and my property in Mecca and you will leave me alone, they said: Yes, so when he arrived to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The sale is profitable, and he said: And the verse was revealed: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is Kind to His servants.” As for the majority, they interpreted that to mean that it was revealed about every mujahid in the way of God, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, God He has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed. This is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur’an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is what is the great attainment. When Hisham bin Amir charged between the two lines, some of the people denounced him, so Umar bin Al-Khattab, Abu Hurairah, and others responded to them, and recited this verse: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is Kind to His servants.”
2:208: God the Almighty says, commanding His believing servants who believe in Him and His Messenger to take all the bonds of Islam and its laws, and to act upon all its commands, and to abandon all its prohibitions, as much as they are able to do so. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Tawus, Ad-Dahhak, Ikrimah, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement, “Enter into peace,” meaning Islam. Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, “Enter into peace,” meaning obedience. Qatadah also said: Treason. And His statement, all of it, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ikrimah, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, As-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak all said, and Mujahid said: That is, do all the deeds and aspects of righteousness. Ikrimah claimed that it was revealed about a group of Jews and others who converted to Islam, such as Abdullah bin Salam, Asad bin Ubaid, Tha’laba, and a group who asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to observe the Sabbath and to recite the Torah at night. So God commanded them to establish the rituals of Islam and to occupy themselves with them to the exclusion of anything else. There is a problem with mentioning Abdullah bin Salam with these people, as it is unlikely that he would ask permission to observe the Sabbath while he, despite his complete faith, would realize that it was abrogated, lifted, invalidated, and replaced by the holidays of Islam. Some commentators make his statement all a state of those who enter, meaning enter into Islam, all of you. The first correct statement is that they were all ordered to work with all the branches of faith and the laws of Islam, which are very many, as much as they were able to do, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Sabah told us, Al-Haitham bin Yaman told me, Ismail bin Zakariya told us, Muhammad bin Awn told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, O you who have believed, enter into Islam completely. This is how he read it in the accusative case, meaning the believers of the People of the Book, for they were holding fast to some matters of the Torah and the laws that were revealed to them, so God said, Enter into Islam completely, meaning: Enter into the laws of the religion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and do not leave any of them, and faith in the Torah and what is in it is sufficient for you. His statement, And do not follow the footsteps of Satan, means work with obedience and avoid what Satan orders you to do, for he only orders you to evil and immorality and to say about God that which you do not know, and he only calls you to… His party will be among the companions of the Blaze.” That is why He said, Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. Mutraf said: The most deceitful of God’s servants to God’s servants is Satan. And His statement, But if you slip after the clear proofs have come to you, that is, you deviate from the truth after the proofs have been established against you, then know that God is Mighty, that is, in His vengeance, no fugitive can escape Him, and no victor can overcome Him. He is Wise in His judgments, His reversal, and His confirmation. That is why Abu al-Aaliyah, Qatadah, and al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Mighty in His vengeance, Wise in His command. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Mighty in His victory over those who disbelieve in Him if He wills, Wise in His excuse and argument to His servants.

2:210: God Almighty says, threatening the disbelievers in Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, Do they await anything but that God should come to them in shades of clouds and the angels? meaning on the Day of Resurrection to separate the judgment between the first and the last, and He will reward every worker for his work, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. For this reason, God Almighty said, And the matter has been decided, and to God all matters will return. God Almighty also said, No! When the earth is crushed to powder, crushed, and your Lord comes with angels, rank upon rank, and Hell is brought forth on that Day, man will remember, but how can he receive remembrance? And He said, Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come? The verse. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir mentioned here the hadith of the images in its entirety from the beginning on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is a well-known hadith that was narrated by more than one of the narrators of the Musnads and others. It says in it: When people are concerned about their situation on the plains, they intercede with their Lord through the prophets one by one from Adam and those after him, and they all turn away from it until they reach Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they come to him, he says, I am for it, I am for it. So he goes and prostrates to God beneath the Throne, and intercedes with God that He may come to decide the judgment between the servants, and God accepts his intercession and he comes in the shades of clouds after the lowest heaven is split open and the angels in it descend, then the second, then the third, until the seventh, and the bearers of the Throne and the Cherubim descend. He said: And the Almighty, the Majestic, descends in the shades of clouds and the angels, and they have a resounding recitation of their glorification, saying: Glory be to the Possessor of the Kingdom and the Sovereignty, Glory be to the Possessor of Might and Power, Glory be to the Living Who does not die, Glory be to the One Who… He causes the creation to die, but He does not die. Glory be to the Holy, Lord of the angels and the spirit. Glory be to the Holy, glory be to our Lord, the Most High, glory be to the Possessor of authority and greatness. Glory be to Him, glory be to Him forever and ever. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh has included here some strange hadiths, and God knows best. Among them is what he narrated from the hadith of Al-Munhal ibn Amr on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn Abdullah ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God will gather the first and the last for an appointed time on a known day, standing with their eyes fixed on the heavens, awaiting the passing of judgment. And God will descend in the canopies of clouds from the Throne to the Footstool.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Abu Bakr ibn Muqaddam told us, Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, I heard Abdul Jalil Al-Qaysi narrating on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr: Do they await anything but that God should come to them in the canopies of clouds? He said: When He descends, there are seventy thousand veils between Him and His creation, including light, darkness, and water. Then the water makes a sound in that darkness that makes hearts tremble. He said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Dimashqi told us, al-Walid told us. He said: I asked Zuhair ibn Muhammad about the statement of God, Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds? He said: Canopies of clouds strung together with rubies, crowned with pearls and emeralds. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, In the shade of clouds, he said: It is not the clouds and it was never except for the Children of Israel in their wandering when they went astray. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, Do they await anything but that God should come to them in the shade of clouds and the angels? He said: And the angels come in the shade of clouds, and God the Most High comes as He wills, and in some readings it is Do they await anything but that God should come to them in the shade of clouds? It is like His saying, And the Day the heaven will split open with clouds and the angels will be sent down in succession.
2:211: God Almighty says, informing about the Children of Israel: How many clear signs did they witness with Moses, i.e. conclusive proof of his truthfulness in what he brought to them, his plot, his staff, his splitting the sea, and his striking the rock, and the shade that clouds provided for them in the intense heat, and the sending down of manna and quails, and other signs indicating the existence of the chosen doer, and the truthfulness of the one through whose hands these miracles occurred. Despite this, many of them turned away from it and exchanged God’s blessing for disbelief, i.e. they exchanged faith in it for disbelief in it and turning away from it. And whoever exchanges God’s blessing after it has come to him, then indeed, God is severe in penalty. As God Almighty said, informing about the disbelievers of Quraysh 106:Have you not seen those who exchanged God’s blessing for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction? Hell, they will burn in it, and wretched is the settlement. Then God Almighty informed about His beautification of the worldly life for the disbelievers who were satisfied with it, and were reassured by it, and they collected wealth and prevented it from being used for the purposes they were commanded to, which would please God with them. They mocked those who believed, who turned away from it and spent what they had of it in obedience to their Lord, and gave it seeking the face of God. For this reason, they won the happiest position and the most abundant fortune on the Day of Resurrection. They were above those in their gathering, their resurrection, their journey, and their abode. They settled in the ranks in the highest of the high, while those remained in the lowest of the low. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And God provides for whom He wills without account. That is, He provides for whomever He wills of His creation and gives him abundant and generous gifts without limit or count in this world and the Hereafter, as came in the hadith: Son of Adam, spend, I will spend on you. And the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Spend, Bilal, and do not fear any shortage from the Lord of the Throne. And God the Almighty said: And whatever you spend, He will replace it. And in the Sahih, “Two angels descend from the heavens every morning, and one of them says: O God, give to the spender a replacement, and the other says: O God, give to the withholder destruction.” And in the Sahih, “The son of Adam says: My money, my money.” And do you have from your wealth anything except what you have eaten and finished, what you have worn out, what you have given in charity and spent, and everything else that is gone and left to the people?” And in Musnad al-Imam Ahmad, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The world is the home of those who have no home, and the wealth of those who have no wealth, and it is the place where those who have no mind gather.
