2:213: Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Dawud told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were ten centuries between Noah and Adam, all of them upon a law of truth, then they differed, so God sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners. He said: And this is how it is in the reading of Abdullah: Mankind was but one community, then they differed. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Bandar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. This is how Abu Ja`far al-Razi narrated on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b, that he used to read it: Mankind was one community, then God sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners. `Abd al-Razzaq said: Mu`mar told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Mankind was one community, he said: They were all upon guidance, then they differed, “then God sent the prophets,” so the first to be sent was Noah. And this is what Mujahid said, as Ibn Abbas said first. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, People were one nation, meaning they were infidels. Then God sent prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners. The first statement on the authority of Ibn Abbas is more authentic in chain of transmission and meaning, because people were on the religion of Adam until they worshipped idols, so God sent Noah, peace be upon him, to them, and he was the first messenger whom God sent to the people of the earth. And for this reason the Almighty said: “And He sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning that over which they differed. And none differed over it except those who were given it after the clear proofs had come to them, out of jealousy between themselves.” That is, after the proofs had been established against them, and what drove them to that was the jealousy of some of them against others. “So God guided those who believed to the truth over which they differed, by His permission. And God guides whom He wills to a straight path.” And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Sulayman al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, regarding His statement: So God guided those who believed to the truth over which they differed, by His permission, the verse, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We are the last and the first on the Day of Resurrection. We are the first people to enter Paradise, but they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them, so God guided us to the truth over which they differed, by His permission. So this is the day over which they differed, and God guided us to it. So the people will follow us in it. Tomorrow will be for the Jews and the day after tomorrow for the Christians.” Then Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus. On the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Ibn Wahb said, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, regarding His statement, Then God guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed, by His permission, they differed about Friday, so the Jews took Saturday and the Christians took Sunday, so God guided the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Friday. They differed about the qiblah, so the Christians faced the east and the Jews faced Jerusalem, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to the qiblah. They differed about prayer, so some of them bowed and did not prostrate, and some of them prostrated and did not bow, and some of them prayed while talking, and some of them prayed while walking, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to the truth from that. They differed about fasting, so some of them fasted part of the day, and some of them fasted from part of the food, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to the truth from that. They differed about Abraham, peace be upon him. The Jews said: He was a Jew, and the Christians said: He was a Christian, and God made him a monotheist Muslim, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to the truth from that. They differed about Jesus, peace be upon him, so the Jews denied him and said a great slander about his mother, and the Christians made him a god and a son, and God made him his spirit and his word, so God guided the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the truth from that, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said in his statement So God guided those who believed to the truth about which they differed, by His permission meaning when they differed they were on what the messengers brought before the difference, they remained on sincerity to God Almighty alone, and worshipping Him with no partner, and establishing prayer and giving zakat, so they remained on the first matter that was before the difference and avoided the difference and they were witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection, witnesses over the people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, the people of Shu’aib and the people of Pharaoh, that their messengers had conveyed to them, and that they had denied their messengers, and in the reading of Abi bin Ka’b: And that they may be witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection, and God guides whom He wills to a straight path. Abu Al-Aaliyah used to say about this verse: The way out from doubts, misguidance and temptations. And his saying, by His permission, meaning by His knowledge of them and what He has guided them to. Ibn Jarir said, And God guides whom He wills, meaning of His creation, to a straight path, meaning He has wisdom and conclusive proof. In Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Aisha, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, got up at night to pray, he would say, “O God, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me to the truth in that over which they differ, by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.” And in the well-known supplication, “O God, show us the truth as truth, and enable us to follow it, and show us falsehood as falsehood, and enable us to avoid it, and do not make it ambiguous to us so that we go astray, and make us leaders for the righteous.”
2:214: God the Almighty says: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise before you are tested, informed and examined as He did with the nations before you? That is why He said: And there has not yet come to you such as came to those who passed on before you - poverty and hardship touched them which are diseases, ailments, pains, calamities and misfortunes. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Marra Al-Hamdani, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi', As-Suddi and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Poverty means poverty, and hardship means illness, and they were shaken in fear of the enemies with a severe earthquake, and they were tested with a great test, as came in the authentic hadith on the authority of Khabbab bin Al-Arat, who said: We said: O Messenger of God, will you not seek victory for us, will you not supplicate to God for us? He said: “Those who came before you, one of them would have a saw placed on the parting of his head, reaching his feet, but that would not distract him from his religion, and he would be combed with iron combs between his flesh and bones, but that would not distract him from his religion.” Then he said: By God, God will complete this matter until a rider will travel from Sana’a to Hadramaut, fearing none but God and the wolf for his sheep, but you are a people who are impatient. God Almighty said: “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left to say, ‘We believe’ and they will not be tested? And We have certainly tested those before them, and God will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.” This was a great aspect of this for the Companions, may God be pleased with them, on the Day of the Confederates, as God Almighty said: “When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when eyes turned away and hearts reached to the throats, and you assumed about God [various] assumptions. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking. And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, ‘God and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion.’” When Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan, Did you fight him? he said, Yes. He said, How was the war between you? He said, It was a contest, he would prevail over us and we would prevail over him. He said, Thus are the messengers who are tested and then have the final outcome. His statement, The example of those who passed on before you, means their way, as God the Almighty said, So We destroyed those more severe than them in force, and the example of the former peoples has passed on. And His statement, And they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, ‘When is the victory of God?’ That is, they would seek victory over their enemies and call for relief and a way out when their situation is difficult and hard. God the Almighty said, Indeed, the victory of God is near, as He said, “For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.” And as hardship occurs, the like of victory descends, and for this reason He said, Indeed, the victory of God is near. And in the hadith of Abu Razin, Your Lord is amazed at the despair of His servants and the nearness of His rain, so He looks at them despairing, and He continues to laugh, knowing that their relief is near.
2:215: Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse is about voluntary spending. Al-Suddi said: Zakat abrogated it, and there is a view on this. The meaning of the verse is: They ask you how they should spend. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said this. Then God the Almighty explained this to them, saying: “Say: Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler.” That is, spend it on these causes. As it came in the hadith: Your mother and your father and your sister and your brother, then your nearest and dearest. Maymun ibn Mihran recited this verse, then said: These are the places of spending. He did not mention drums or flutes or wooden pictures or wall coverings in them. Then God the Almighty said: And whatever good you do, indeed, God is Knowing of it. That is, whatever good deed you do, God knows it and will reward you for it with the greatest reward, for He does not wrong anyone by as much as an atom’s weight.
2:216: This is an affirmation from God the Almighty for jihad upon Muslims to prevent the evil of the enemies from the domain of Islam. Al-Zuhri said: Jihad is obligatory upon everyone who fights or stays behind. The one who stays behind must help if he is asked for help, help if he is asked for help, and if he is called upon to mobilize, go out, and if he does not need him, he stays behind. I said For this reason it is proven in the Sahih: Whoever dies without fighting or thinking of fighting, dies a death of ignorance. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said on the day of the conquest: There is no migration after the conquest, but jihad and intention, and if you are called upon to mobilize, then go out. And his saying and it is hateful to you means it is difficult and hard for you, and it is so, because he will either be killed or wounded with the hardship of travel and fighting the enemies. Then God the Almighty said: And perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you meaning because fighting is followed by victory and triumph over the enemies and taking control of their lands, their money, their children and their offspring. And perhaps you love a thing while it is bad for you. This is general in all matters. A person may love something while it is not good or in his best interest. For example, refraining from fighting may be followed by the enemy seizing control of the country and ruling it. Then God the Almighty said: And God knows, while you do not know. That is, He knows the consequences of things better than you do, and He knows what is best for you in this world and the hereafter, so respond to Him and submit to His command, so that you may be guided.
2:217: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us on the authority of his father, al-Hadrami told me on the authority of Abu al-Suwar, on the authority of Jundub ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a group of people, and sent Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah over them. When he went to go, he cried out of longing to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he detained him. Then he sent Abdullah ibn Jahsh over them in his place, and wrote him a letter and ordered him not to read the letter until he reached such and such a place, and he said, "Do not force anyone of your companions to travel with you. When he read the letter, he said, I hear and obey God and His Messenger." So he told them the report and read the letter to them. Two men returned, and the rest of them remained. They met Ibn al-Hadrami and killed him, and they did not know whether that day was from Rajab or Jumada. So the polytheists said to the Muslims, "You have been killed in the sacred month. Then God revealed, They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, 'Fighting in it is great.'" The verse, and Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Malik and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and on the authority of Marra on the authority of Ibn Masoud, “They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. Say, ‘Fighting therein is great’” (Al-Akhbar 1:17). That is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a detachment, and they were seven men, led by Abdullah bin Jahsh Al-Asadi, and among them were Ammar bin Yasir, Abu Hudhayfah bin Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas, Utbah bin Ghazwan Al-Sulami, an ally of Banu Nawfal, and Suhayl bin Bayda’, Aamer bin Fuhayrah, and Waqid bin Abdullah Al-Yarbu’i, an ally of Umar bin Al-Khattab. He wrote a letter to Ibn Jahsh and ordered him not to read it until he reached Batn Malal. When he reached Batn Malal, he opened the letter and it said, Go until you reach Batn Nakhl. He said to his companions, “Whoever wants to die, let him go and make a will, for I am making a will and I am going to do what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered.” So he set out, and Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas and Utbah lagged behind him. They lost their mount and lagged behind looking for it. Ibn Jahsh set out to Batn Nakhl, and he was… By Al-Hakam bin Kaysan and Uthman bin Abdullah bin Al-Mughira, and he escaped and killed Amr, he was killed by Waqid bin Abdullah, so it was the first spoils of war for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they returned to Medina with two prisoners and the money they had taken, the people of Mecca wanted to ransom the two prisoners for him. They said: Muhammad claims that he follows the obedience of God, and he was the first to make the sacred month permissible and killed our companion in Rajab. The Muslims said: We only killed him in Jumada, and he was killed on the first night of Rajab and the last night of Jumada. The Muslims sheathed their swords when Rajab began, and God revealed, taunting the people of Mecca: “They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say: Fighting in it is great.” It is not permissible. What you have done, O group of polytheists, is greater than killing in the sacred month when you disbelieved in God and turned away from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. And expelling the people of the Sacred Mosque from it when they expelled Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions is greater than killing in the sight of God. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. Say, ‘Fighting therein is a great sin.’” That is because the polytheists turned away the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and prevented him from the mosque in a sacred month. He said: So God granted victory to His Prophet in a sacred month of the following year, and the polytheists criticized the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for fighting in a sacred month, so God said, And averting from the way of God and disbelieving in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people therefrom are greater in the sight of God than fighting in it, and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a detachment, and they encountered Amr ibn al-Hadrami as he was coming from Taif on the last night of Jumada and the first night of Rajab, and that the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, thought that that night was from Jumada and it was the first night of Rajab, but they did not realize it, so one of them killed him and took what he had with him, and the polytheists sent to taunt him about that, so God Almighty said, “They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. Say, ‘Fighting therein is a great sin. And averting from the way of God and disbelieving in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people therefrom” expelling the people of al-Masjid al-Haram was greater than what happened to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And peace be upon him, and polytheism is worse than it, and thus Abu Saeed Al-Baqal narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that it was revealed in the expedition of Abdullah bin Jahsh and the killing of Amr bin Al-Hadrami, and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Al-Saib Al-Kalbi told me on the authority of Abu Saleh, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he said: It was revealed in what happened to Amr bin Al-Hadrami, They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein to the end of the verse, and Abdul Malik bin Hisham, the narrator of the biography, said on the authority of Ziyad bin Abdullah Al-Bakkai, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar Al-Madani, may God have mercy on him, in his book of the biography, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abdullah bin Jahsh bin Rabab Al-Asadi in Rajab on his return from the first Badr, and he sent with him eight men from the Muhajireen, none of them from the Ansar, and he wrote him a letter and ordered him not to look at it until he had traveled for two days, then he would look at it and proceed as he ordered him, and not to force anyone from his companions, and the companions of Abdullah bin Jahsh were from the Muhajireen, then from Banu Abd Shams bin Abd Manaf Abu Hudhayfah bin Utbah bin Rabi’ah bin Abd Shams bin Abdul Manaf, and among their allies: Abdullah bin Jahsh, who was the leader of the people, and Ukasha bin Muhsin, one of Banu Asad bin Khuzaymah, an ally of them, and from Banu Nawfal bin Abdul Manaf, Utbah bin Ghazwan bin Jabir, an ally of them, and from Banu Zuhra bin Kilab, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, and from Banu Ka’b, Adi bin Amir bin Rabi’ah, an ally of them, other than Ibn Wa’il, and Waqid bin Abdullah bin Abdul Manaf bin Arin bin Tha’laba bin Yarbu’, one of Banu Tamim, an ally of them, and Khalid bin Al-Bukair, one of Banu Saad bin Laith, an ally of them, and from Banu Al-Harith bin Fihr, Suhayl bin Bayda’. When Abdullah bin Jahsh had traveled for two days, he opened the letter and looked and found in it: When you look in my letter about this, then proceed until you descend to Nakhal between Mecca and Al-Ta’if and watch the Quraysh there and learn for us their report. When Abdullah bin Jahsh looked at the letter, he said: I hear and obey, then he said to his companions: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, has ordered me to proceed to He said: “I will watch the Quraysh until I bring him report from them. He has forbidden me to force any of you. Whoever among you wants martyrdom and desires it, let him go, and whoever dislikes it, let him return. As for me, I will go with the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” So his companions went with him, and none of them remained behind him. He traveled through the Hijaz until he reached a mine above the branch called Najran. Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas and `Utbah ibn Ghazwan lost a camel of theirs that they were following, so they stayed behind in pursuit of it. `Abdullah ibn Jahsh and the rest of his companions went on until they reached Nakhl. A caravan of the Quraysh passed by him carrying raisins, fat, and merchandise from the Quraysh. In it was `Amr ibn al-Hadrami, whose name was `Abdullah ibn `Ibad, one of the Sadaf, and `Uthman ibn `Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah and his brother Nawfal ibn `Abdullah al-Makhzumiyan, and al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, a client of Hisham ibn al-Mughirah. When the people saw them, they feared them, and they had camped close to them. `Ukasha ibn Muhsin, who had shaved his head, and when they saw him, they felt safe and said: Ammar, you will not be harmed by them, and the people consulted about them, and that was on the last day of Rajab, and the people said: By God, if you leave the people tonight, they will enter the sanctuary, so they will protect themselves from you, and if you kill them, you will kill them in the sacred month, so the people hesitated and were afraid to advance against them, then they encouraged themselves against them, and they agreed to kill whoever they could of them and take what they had with them, so Waqid bin Abdullah Al-Tamimi shot Amr bin Al-Hadrami with an arrow and killed him, and Uthman bin Abdullah and Al-Hakam bin Kaysan were taken prisoner, and the people escaped Nawfal bin Abdullah and defeated them, and Abdullah bin Jahsh and his companions came with the caravan and the two prisoners until they arrived to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina. Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the family of Abdullah bin Jahsh mentioned that Abdullah said to his companions: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has a fifth of what we have taken as spoils, and that was before God imposed a fifth of the spoils, so he set aside a fifth for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The caravan, and divided the rest among his companions. Ibn Ishaq said: When they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: I did not command you to fight in the sacred month. So he stopped the caravan and the two prisoners, and refused to take anything from that. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that, the people’s hands fell and they thought that they were doomed, and their Muslim brothers rebuked them for what they did. The Quraysh said: Muhammad and his companions have made the sacred month permissible, and they have shed blood in it, and taken money in it, and taken men captive in it. Those Muslims who were in Mecca who responded to him said: They only did what they did in Sha’ban. The Jews said: They took that as an omen against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Amr ibn al-Hadrami killed him. Waqid ibn Abdullah. Amr lived the war, and al-Hadrami attended the war, and Waqid ibn Abdullah started the war. So God made that upon them and not for them. When the people increased in that, God revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say: Fighting in it is a great sin, and averting from the way of God is a great sin.” And disbelief in Him and the Sacred Mosque and the expulsion of its people from it is greater in the sight of God. And fitnah is greater than killing.” That is, if you were killed in the sacred month, then they have prevented you from the path of God while disbelieving in Him, and from the Sacred Mosque and your expulsion from it while you are its people. It is greater in the sight of God than killing those you killed from them. And fitnah is greater than killing. That is, they were tempting the Muslim in his religion until they returned him to disbelief after his belief, so that is greater in the sight of God than killing. And they will not cease to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. That is, then they persist in the worst and greatest of that, without repenting or desisting. Ibn Ishaq said: When the Qur’an was revealed with this matter and God relieved the Muslims from the hardship they were in, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, seized the caravan and the two prisoners, and the Quraysh sent to him a ransom for Uthman ibn Abdullah and Al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We will not ransom them for you until our two companions come forward, meaning Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas and `Utbah ibn Ghazwan, for we will We fear for you regarding them, so if you kill them, we will kill your two companions. So Sa`d and `Utbah came, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ransomed them from them. As for Al-Hakam bin Kaysan, he converted to Islam and his conversion was good, and he stayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he was killed as a martyr on the day of Bir Ma`unah. As for `Uthman bin `Abdullah, he went to Mecca and died there as an unbeliever. Ibn Ishaq said: When what happened to `Abdullah bin Jahsh and his companions became clear when the Qur’an was revealed, they hoped for reward and said: O Messenger of God, do we hope to have a raid in which we will be given the reward of the mujahidin? Then God the Almighty revealed: “Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of God - those are the ones who hope for the mercy of God. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” So God placed the greatest hope in that. Ibn Ishaq said: The hadith in this is from Al-Zuhri and Yazid bin Ruman, from Urwah. Yunus bin Bakir narrated from Muhammad bin Ishaq, from Yazid bin Ruman, from Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, close to this context. Musa bin Uqbah narrated from Al-Zuhri himself something similar to that, and Shuaib bin Abi Hamza narrated from Al-Zuhri from Urwah bin Al-Zubayr something similar to this as well. In it, Ibn Al-Hadrami was the first to be killed between the Muslims and the polytheists. A delegation of the infidels of Quraysh rode until they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, and they said: Is fighting permissible in the sacred month? Then God revealed, They ask you about the sacred month, the verse, and Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi has exhaustively discussed this in his book, Evidence of Prophethood. Then Ibn Hisham said, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: It was mentioned on the authority of some of the family of Abdullah that Abdullah divided the spoils among his family, and he made four-fifths of it for those who gave it, and one-fifth for God and His Messenger, so it happened as Abdullah bin Jahsh had done with that caravan. Ibn Hisham said: It was the first spoils that the Muslims took, and Amr bin Al-Hadrami was the first to be killed by the Muslims, and Uthman bin Abdullah and Al-Hakam bin Kaysan were the first to be taken captive by the Muslims. Ibn Ishaq said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said in the battle of Abdullah bin Jahsh, and it is said: Rather, Abdullah bin Jahsh said it when the Quraysh said: Muhammad and his companions have made the sacred month permissible, so they shed blood in it, took money in it, and took men captive in it. Ibn Hisham said: It is for Abdullah bin Jahsh. You consider murder in a forbidden manner a great sin, and worse than that, if only a mature person could see the right path. You turned away from what Muhammad said and disbelieved in him, and God is the witness and the seer. And you expel the people of God from the mosque, lest anyone be seen prostrating to God in the house. Even if you reproach us for killing him and spread rumors about Islam, he is a rebel and an envious person. We watered our spears with the help of Ibn Al-Hadrami in a palm tree when he kindled the war. Blood and Ibn Abdullah Othman are among us, and he is being disputed by the rancor of the chains.

Ibn Ishaq said: When the Qur’an was revealed with this matter and God relieved the Muslims from the hardship they were in, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, seized the caravan and the two prisoners, and the Quraysh sent to him a ransom for Uthman ibn Abdullah and Al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We will not ransom them for you until our two companions come forward, meaning Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas and `Utbah ibn Ghazwan, for we will We fear for you regarding them, so if you kill them, we will kill your two companions. So Sa`d and `Utbah came, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ransomed them from them. As for Al-Hakam bin Kaysan, he converted to Islam and his conversion was good, and he stayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he was killed as a martyr on the day of Bir Ma`unah. As for `Uthman bin `Abdullah, he went to Mecca and died there as an unbeliever. Ibn Ishaq said: When what happened to `Abdullah bin Jahsh and his companions became clear when the Qur’an was revealed, they hoped for reward and said: O Messenger of God, do we hope to have a raid in which we will be given the reward of the mujahidin? Then God the Almighty revealed: “Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of God - those are the ones who hope for the mercy of God. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” So God placed the greatest hope in that. Ibn Ishaq said: The hadith in this is from Al-Zuhri and Yazid bin Ruman, from Urwah. Yunus bin Bakir narrated from Muhammad bin Ishaq, from Yazid bin Ruman, from Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, close to this context. Musa bin Uqbah narrated from Al-Zuhri himself something similar to that, and Shuaib bin Abi Hamza narrated from Al-Zuhri from Urwah bin Al-Zubayr something similar to this as well. In it, Ibn Al-Hadrami was the first to be killed between the Muslims and the polytheists. A delegation of the infidels of Quraysh rode until they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, and they said: Is fighting permissible in the sacred month? Then God revealed, They ask you about the sacred month, the verse, and Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi has exhaustively discussed this in his book, Evidence of Prophethood. Then Ibn Hisham said, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: It was mentioned on the authority of some of the family of Abdullah that Abdullah divided the spoils among his family, and he made four-fifths of it for those who gave it, and one-fifth for God and His Messenger, so it happened as Abdullah bin Jahsh had done with that caravan. Ibn Hisham said: It was the first spoils that the Muslims took, and Amr bin Al-Hadrami was the first to be killed by the Muslims, and Uthman bin Abdullah and Al-Hakam bin Kaysan were the first to be taken captive by the Muslims. Ibn Ishaq said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said in the battle of Abdullah bin Jahsh, and it is said: Rather, Abdullah bin Jahsh said it when the Quraysh said: Muhammad and his companions have made the sacred month permissible, so they shed blood in it, took money in it, and took men captive in it. Ibn Hisham said: It is for Abdullah bin Jahsh. You consider murder in a forbidden manner a great sin, and worse than that, if only a mature person could see the right path. You turned away from what Muhammad said and disbelieved in him, and God is the witness and the seer. And you expel the people of God from the mosque, lest anyone be seen prostrating to God in the house. Even if you reproach us for killing him and spread rumors about Islam, he is a rebel and an envious person. We watered our spears with the help of Ibn Al-Hadrami in a palm tree when he kindled the war. Blood and Ibn Abdullah Othman are among us, and he is being disputed by the rancor of the chains.
2:219: Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf bin Al-Waleed told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Omar, that he said: When the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then this verse in Al-Baqarah was revealed: “They ask you about alcohol and gambling. Say, ‘There is great sin in them.’” So Omar was called, and it was recited to him, and he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in An-Nisa’ was revealed: O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. So the caller of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would call out when he called for prayer: Do not approach prayer while drunk. So Omar was called, and it was recited to him, and he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Al-Ma’idah was revealed, so Omar was called, and it was recited to him, and when he reached: Will you then desist? Omar said: We have desisted, we have desisted. This is how Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Israel on the authority of Abu Ishaq. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Al-Thawri on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, whose name is Amr ibn Shurahbil Al-Hamadani Al-Kufi, on the authority of Umar, and he has no other narrations from him, but Abu Zur’ah said: He did not hear from him, and God knows best. Ali ibn Al-Madini said: This is a sound and authentic chain of transmission, and Al-Tirmidhi authenticated it. Ibn Abi Hatim added after his words We have finished that it takes away money and takes away the mind. This hadith will also come with what Ahmad narrated through the chain of transmission of Abu Hurayrah also when he said in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:Intoxicants, gambling, idolatry, and divining arrows are all defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid them that you may be successful. The verses. So his statement: They ask you about wine and gambling As for wine, as the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: It is everything that clouds the mind, as will be explained in Surat Al-Ma’idah. The same applies to gambling, which is betting. And his saying, Say, ‘In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people.’ As for their sin, it is in religion, and as for the benefits, they are worldly in that they benefit the body, digest food, remove waste, sharpen some minds, and provide the pleasure of the intense, enrapturing intensity that is in them, as Hassan ibn Thabit said in his pre-Islamic period: We drink it and it leaves us kings and lions, and the encounter does not stop us. And likewise selling it and benefiting from its price, and what some of them used to gamble and spend on themselves or their children, but these benefits do not equal its harm and its greater corruption, because it is related to the mind and religion, and for this reason God the Most High said: And their sin is greater than their benefit, and for this reason this verse was a prelude to the prohibition of alcohol absolutely, and it was not explicit but rather implied, and for this reason Omar may God be pleased with him said when it was recited to him: O God, make clear to us regarding alcohol a clear statement, until the explicit prohibition of it was revealed in Surat Al-Ma’idah “O you who have believed, indeed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?” And the discussion of that will come in Surat Al-Ma’idah, God willing, and in Him is trustworthy. Ibn Omar, Al-Sha’bi, Mujahid, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: This is the first verse revealed about wine: “They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, ‘There is great sin in them.’” Then the verse in Surat An-Nisa was revealed, then the verse in Surat Al-Ma’idah was revealed, forbidding wine. His saying, "And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, 'The excess.'" It has been read in the accusative and in the nominative, and both are good, straightforward and close. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa ibn Ismail told us, Abaan told us, Yahya told us, that he was informed that Muadh ibn Jabal and Tha'laba came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we have slaves and families from our wealth, so God revealed, They ask you, what they should spend. Al-Hakam said, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, "And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, 'The excess.'" He said: What is left over from your family. This is how it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Mujahid, Ata', Ikrimah, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Qasim, Salim, Ata' Al-Khurasani, Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and more than one, that they said regarding His saying, Say, 'The excess,' meaning the excess. And on the authority of Tawus: the little of everything. And on the authority of Al-Rabi' also: the best and purest of your wealth, and everything goes back to the excess. And Abd bin Hamid said in his interpretation: Hudha bin Khalifa narrated to us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the verse, “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘The excess.’” He said, That is so that your wealth does not become exhausted and you sit and ask people. And the evidence for that is what Ibn Jarir narrated: Ali bin Muslim narrated to us, Abu Asim narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, I have a dinar. He said: Spend it on yourself. He said: I have another. He said: Spend it on your family. He said: I have another. He said: Spend it on your children. He said: I have another. He said: Then you are more knowledgeable. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, and Muslim also included it on the authority of Jabir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man, “Start with yourself and give charity to yourself. If there is anything left over, then give it to your family. If there is anything left over from your family, then give it to your relatives. If there is anything left over from your relatives, then give it like this and like this.” And he also narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best charity is that which is given from surplus wealth, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand, and start with those under your care. And in the hadith also: O son of Adam, if you give away your surplus, it is better for you, and if you keep it, it is worse for you, and you are not to be blamed for what is sufficient. Then it was said that it was abrogated by the verse on zakat, as narrated by Ali bin Abi Talhah and Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it was said by Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Al-Suddi, and it was said that it was explained by the verse on zakat, as Mujahid and others said, and this is more correct. And His statement, Thus does God make clear to you the verses that you may give thought * In this world and the Hereafter. That is, just as He has detailed, explained and clarified these rulings for you, He also makes clear to you the rest of the verses regarding His rulings, promises and threats, that you may give thought to this world and the Hereafter. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means the passing of this world and its passing away, and the coming of the Hereafter and its permanence. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of al-Sa`q al-`Ayshi, who said: I witnessed al-Hasan reciting this verse from al-Baqarah, That you may give thought * In this world and the Hereafter. He said: By God, it is for whoever gives thought to it, so that he may know that this world is a place of trial and then a place of passing away, and so that he may know that the Hereafter is a place of reward and then a place of permanence. And this is what Qatada, Ibn Jurayj and others said. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So that you may know the superiority of the Hereafter over this world. And in a narration on the authority of Qatada: So prefer the Hereafter over the first. And His saying: “And they ask you about orphans. Say: ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer. And if God had willed, He could have made you weak.’” The verse, Ibn Jarir said: Sufyan ibn Waki’ told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verses And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best and Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire, and they will burn in a Blaze were revealed, the one who had an orphan went and separated his food from his food and his drink from his drink, and he would keep some of his food for him until he ate it or spoiled it. This was difficult for them, so they mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: “And they ask you about orphans. Say: ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers.’” So they mixed their food with their food and their drink with their drink. Thus, Abu Dawood, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib. And likewise, Ali bin Abi Talha narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and likewise, Al-Suddi narrated it on the authority of Abu Malik and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra on the authority of Ibn Masoud with a similar wording. And likewise, more than one person mentioned the reason for the revelation of this verse, such as Mujahid, Ata’, Al-Sha’bi, Ibn Abi Laila, Qatadah, and more than one person from the Salaf and Khalaf. Waki’ bin Al-Jarrah said: Hisham, the companion of Al-Dastawai, told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: I hate for the orphan’s money to be with me alone, until I mix his food with my food, and his drink with my drink. So His statement, “Say: ‘Improvement for them is best’” means alone. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers means if you mix your food with their food and your drink with their drink, there is no harm upon you, because they are your brothers in religion. For this reason, He said, And God knows the corrupter from the reformer meaning He knows whose intention and purpose is corruption or reform. And His statement, “And if God had willed, He could have made you suffer. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise” means if God had willed, He could have made things difficult for you and made you suffer, but He made things easy for you and made things easy. On your behalf, and He permitted you to mix with them in the best way. God Almighty said: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best. Rather, He permitted eating from it for the poor in a reasonable manner, either on condition that he guarantees a replacement for the one who is well off, or for free, as will be explained in Surat An-Nisa, God willing, and in Him is trustworthy.

2:221: This is a prohibition from God the Almighty on the believers, that they marry polytheist women who worship idols. Then, if its generality is intended, and that it includes every polytheist, whether a woman of the Book or a pagan, then He has made an exception from that the women of the People of the Book by saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation, chaste, not fornicating. Ali bin Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: And do not marry polytheist women until they believe: God has excluded from that the women of the People of the Book, and this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Makhul, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Zaid bin Aslam, Ar-Rabi bin Anas, and others said. It was said: Rather, what is meant by that are polytheists who worship idols, and it does not mean the People of the Book in its entirety, and the meaning is close to the first, and God knows best. As for what Ibn Jarir narrated: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-Asqalani told me, my father told us, Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram al-Fazari told us, Shahr ibn Hawshab told us, he said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abbas say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade all kinds of women, except for those who were believing emigrants, and he forbade every woman of a religion other than Islam. God the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in faith, his work has become worthless. Talhah ibn Abdullah married a Jewish woman, and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman married a Christian woman. Umar ibn al-Khattab became extremely angry, to the point that he wanted to attack them. They said, We will divorce them, O Commander of the Faithful, and do not get angry. He said, If their divorce is permissible, their marriage is permissible, but I will snatch them from you as a small, ugly thing. It is a very strange hadith, and this trace is also strange from Umar. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: After narrating the consensus on the permissibility of marrying women of the Book, Umar disliked that so that people would not lose interest in Muslim women, or for other reasons. As Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Idris told us, al-Salt ibn Bahram told us, on the authority of Shuqaiq, who said: Hudhayfah married a Jewish woman, so Umar wrote to him: Let her go. He wrote to him: Do you claim that it is forbidden, so let her go? He said: I do not claim that it is forbidden, but I fear that they will take the believing women among them. This is a sound chain of transmission. Al-Khalal narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Al-Salt, something similar. Ibn Jarir said: Musa ibn Abd Al-Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Sufyan ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Zaid ibn Wahb, who said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab said: A Muslim man may marry a Christian woman, but a Christian man may not marry a Muslim woman. He said: This is more sound in chain of transmission than the first. Then he said: Tamim ibn Al-Muntasir told us, Ishaq Al-Azraqi told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Suwar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We marry the women of the People of the Book, but they do not marry our women. Then he said: This report, even if there is something in its chain of transmission, is accepted because of the consensus of all of the ummah on it. This is what Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Burqan, on the authority of Maimun ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he disliked marrying the People of the Book, and he interpreted And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Umar said: I do not know of any polytheism greater than saying: Her Lord is Jesus. Abu Bakr al-Khalal al-Hanbali said: Muhammad ibn Harun told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, and Muhammad ibn Ali told me, Salih ibn Ahmad told us, that they asked Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Hanbal about the statement of God: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. He said: The polytheistic Arab women who worship idols. And His statement: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even though she might please you. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Rawahah, who had a black slave woman, so he became angry with her and slapped her, then he became frightened and came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what had happened to them. He said to him: What is it? He said: You fast, pray, perform ablution well, and bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God. He said: O Abu Abdullah, this is a believer. He said: By Him Who sent you with the truth, I will free her and marry her. So he did, and some Muslims criticized him and said: He married his female slave. They wanted to marry to polytheists and marry them out of desire for their lineage. So God revealed: “A believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even though she might please you. And do not marry polytheists until they believe. And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he might please you.” And Abd bin Hamid said: Ja’far bin Ziyad al-Ifriqi told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Do not marry women for their beauty, for perhaps their beauty will ruin them. And do not marry them for their wealth, for perhaps their wealth will make them transgress. And marry them for their religion, for a black, hairless slave woman with religion is better.” The African is weak. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A woman is married for four reasons: for her wealth, her lineage, her beauty, and her religion. So get the one who is religious.” May your hands be covered with dust.” Muslim narrated on the authority of Jabir something similar, and he narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The world is but a provision, and the best provision of the world is a righteous woman. His statement, And do not marry polytheist men until they believe, means do not marry polytheist men to believing women, as God Almighty said: They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them. Then God Almighty said: And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even if he pleases you, meaning a believing man - even if he is an Ethiopian slave - is better than a polytheist, even if he is a secret leader. Those invite to the Fire, meaning their company and mixing with them encourages the love of the world, acquiring it, and preferring it over the Hereafter, and the consequences of that are dire. And God invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission, meaning by His law and what He has commanded and what He has forbidden. And He makes clear His verses to the people that perhaps they will be reminded.
2:222: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, that when a Jewish woman among them menstruated, they would not eat with her or have intercourse with her in their homes. So he asked the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty revealed: “They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harmful thing, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are pure.” Until he finished the verse, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do everything except intercourse. This reached the Jews and they said: This man does not want to leave anything of our affair without contradicting us in it. So Asid ibn Hudayr and Ubad ibn Bishr came and said: O Messenger of God, the Jews said: Such and such, so should we not have intercourse with them? The face of the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) changed until we thought that he was angry with them. They went out and we met them with a gift of milk for the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him). He sent after them and gave them something to drink, so they knew that he was not angry with them. Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd ibn Salamah. His saying, "So keep away from women during menstruation means the vagina, because he said, Do everything except intercourse." For this reason, many scholars, or most of them, held that it is permissible to have intercourse with a menstruating woman except the vagina. Abu Dawud also said: Musa ibn Ismail told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of some of the wives of the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), that if he wanted to do something to a menstruating woman, he would throw a cloth over her vagina. Abu Dawud also said: Al-Qa'nabi told us, Abdullah, meaning Ibn Umar Ibn Ghanim, told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Ammarah Ibn Ghurab that his aunt told him that she asked Aisha, saying: One of us menstruates and she and her husband do not have a bed except one bed. She said: I will tell you what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did. He entered and went to his mosque. Abu Dawud said: She meant the mosque of her house. He had not finished until my eyes overcame me and the cold hurt him. He said: Come closer to me. I said: I am menstruating. He said: Uncover your thighs. I uncovered my thighs. He placed his cheek and chest on my thigh and I leaned over him until he became warm and he fell asleep (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: `Abd al-Wahhab told us, Ayyub told us from the book of Abu Qilabah, that Masruq rode to `Aishah and said: Peace be upon the Prophet and his family. `Aishah said: Welcome, welcome. They gave him permission and he entered and said: I want to ask you about something and I am shy. She said: I am your mother and you are my son. He said: What is a man entitled to from his wife when she is menstruating? She said to him: Everything except her private parts. It was also narrated on the authority of Humayd ibn Mas`adah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zari`, on the authority of `Uyaynah ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Jushan, on the authority of Marwan al-Asfar, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I said to `Aishah: What is permissible for a man to do with his wife when she is menstruating? She said: Everything except intercourse. This is the statement of Ibn `Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and `Ikrimah. Ibn Jarir also narrated on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Abi Zaydah, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Maymun ibn Mihran, on the authority of `Aishah, who said to him: What is above the izar. I said It is permissible to lie with her and eat with her without disagreement. `Aishah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to order me to wash his head while I was menstruating, and he used to recline on my lap while I was menstruating and recite the Qur’an. In Sahih from her, she said: I used to sweat while I was menstruating and give it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would put his mouth where I had put my mouth, and I would drink the drink and I would give it to him and he would put his mouth where I had drunk from. Abu Dawud said: Musaddad told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Jabir ibn Subh, I heard Khalas al-Hijri say: I heard Aisha say: I and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were in one garment and I was menstruating and menstruating, so if something of mine got on him, he would wash the place where it had been and not repeat it, and if something got on him - meaning his garment - he would wash the place where it had been and not repeat it and prayed in it. As for what Abu Dawud narrated, Saeed ibn al-Jabbar told us, Abdul Aziz - meaning Ibn Muhammad - told us, on the authority of Abu al-Yaman, on the authority of Umm Dhara, on the authority of Aisha that she said: When I menstruated, I would get off the mat and not approach the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor would we approach him until we were pure, so it is understood as a precaution and a precaution. Others said: It is only permissible for him to have intercourse with her except what is under the izar, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, who said: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to have intercourse with one of his wives, he would put on a waist wrapper while she was menstruating. This is the wording of al-Bukhari, and they both have something similar on the authority of Aisha. Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Ala’, on the authority of Hizam ibn Hakeem, on the authority of his uncle Abdullah ibn Sa’d al-Ansari, that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: What is permissible for me to do with my wife while she is menstruating? He said: What is above the izar. Abu Dawud also has: “On the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what is permissible for me to do with my wife while she is menstruating? He said: What is above the izar, and refraining from that is better.” This is a narration on the authority of Aisha, as mentioned above, and Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab and Shuraih. These hadiths and similar hadiths are evidence for those who hold that what is above the izaar is permissible, and this is one of the two opinions in the Shafi’i school of thought, may God have mercy on him, which was preferred by many Iraqis and others. Their basis is that the vagina is sacred, so it is forbidden so that one does not reach the point of engaging in what God Almighty has forbidden, which the scholars have unanimously agreed to prohibit, which is intercourse in the vagina. Then whoever does that has sinned, so he should seek God’s forgiveness and repent to Him. Is he required to make expiation for that or not? There are two opinions on this: One of them Yes, because of what Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the one who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, he should give in charity a dinar or half a dinar. In a wording by al-Tirmidhi: If it is red blood, then a dinar, and if it is yellow blood, then half a dinar. Imam Ahmad also narrated on his authority that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stipulated that a menstruating woman should be given a dinar, and if he has intercourse with her after the blood has gone away and she has not performed ghusl, then half a dinar. The second opinion which is the new correct opinion of the Shafi’i school of thought and the opinion of the majority is that there is nothing wrong with that, rather he seeks forgiveness from God the Almighty because they did not authenticate this hadith, as it was narrated as a marfu’ as mentioned above, and as a mawquf, which is the correct opinion according to many of the Imams of Hadeeth. So the words of God the Almighty: And do not approach them until they are pure are an interpretation of His words: So keep away from women during menstruation and He forbade approaching them by intercourse as long as menstruation is present, and its implication is that it is permissible if it stops. Imam Abu Abdullah Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Hanbal said in what he dictated in At-Ta’a’: And His words: “And they ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harmful thing, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are pure. Then when they have purified themselves, then come to them from the place of purity” the verse, purity indicates that he should come near her, so when Maymunah and Aisha said: When one of us menstruated, she would put on a wrapper and enter with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in his garment, this indicates that he only meant intercourse. His saying, Then when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where God has commanded you, contains encouragement and guidance to have intercourse with them after bathing. Ibn Hazm held that intercourse is obligatory after every menstrual period, based on his saying, Then when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where God has commanded you, and he has no basis for that, because this is a command after a prohibition. There are statements by scholars of the principles of jurisprudence, some of whom say that it is obligatory like the absolute, these need the answer of Ibn Hazm, and some of whom say: it is permissible, and they make the prohibition precedent over it an indication that diverts it from obligation, and there is consideration in it, and what the evidence is based on is that the ruling is returned to what the matter was before the prohibition, so if it was obligatory, then it is obligatory like his saying: So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists or permissible, then it is permissible like his saying: And when you are released from ihram, then hunt “And when the prayer is completed, then disperse within the land” and on this statement the evidence is combined, and it was narrated by al-Ghazali and others, so some of the imams of the later scholars chose it and it is correct, and the scholars agreed that if a woman’s menstruation stops, she is not permissible until she washes with water or performs tayammum if that is not possible for her with its condition, except that Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, says, in the case of her bleeding stopping for the most part of menstruation, which is ten days according to him: that she is permissible as soon as it stops and does not need to wash, and God knows best, and Ibn Abbas said: Until they are purified meaning from the blood, So if “Purify yourself means with water. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Al-Layth bin Saad, and others said. And his statement, from where God has commanded you, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: meaning the vagina. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you, meaning in the vagina and do not go beyond it to anything else, for whoever does any of that has transgressed. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ikrimah said: From where God has commanded you, meaning stay away from them, and this indicates in this case the prohibition of anal intercourse, as will be explained soon, God willing. Abu Razin, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak and others said: Then have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you, meaning when they are pure and not menstruating. That is why He said: Indeed, God loves those who repent, meaning from sin, even if they have committed it repeatedly, and He loves those who purify themselves, meaning those who are free from filth and harm, which is what they were forbidden from, such as having intercourse with a menstruating woman or in a place other than the place of intercourse. And his saying, Your women are a place of cultivation for you. Ibn Abbas said: The place of cultivation is the place of the child. So go to your place of cultivation however you wish. That is, however you wish. He said: I heard Jabir say: The Jews used to say: If a man has intercourse with her from behind, the child will be born cross-eyed. So the verse, Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so go to your place of cultivation however you wish. was revealed. Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Malik bin Anas, Ibn Jurayj and Sufyan bin Saeed Ath-Thawri told me: Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir told them: Jabir bin Abdullah told him that the Jews said to the Muslims: Whoever has intercourse with a woman while she is facing away, the child will be born cross-eyed. So God revealed: Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so approach your place of cultivation however you wish. Ibn Jurayj said in the hadith: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In front or from behind, if that is in the vagina. And in the hadith of Bahz bin Hakim bin Mu’awiyah bin Haidah Al-Qushayri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that he said: O Messenger of God, what do we have intercourse with our women from them and what do we leave? He said: Your place of cultivation, go to your place of cultivation however you wish, except that you do not strike the face, do not insult, and do not abandon her except in the house. The hadith was narrated by Ahmad and the people of Sunan. Another hadith - Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Aamer ibn Yahya, on the authority of Hanash ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: Some people from Himyar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about some things. A man said to him: I love women, so what do you think of me? So God revealed: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth however you wish. Imam Ahmad narrated it. Yahya ibn Ghailan told us, Rashdin told us, Al-Hasan ibn Thauban told me on the authority of Aamer ibn Yahya Al-Maghafari on the authority of Hanash, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed about some people from the Ansar who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about some things. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Go to her in any case, if it is in the vagina. Another hadith - Abu Ja`far al-Tahawi said in his book Mushkil al-Hadith: Ahmad ibn Dawud ibn Musa told us, Ya`qub ibn Kasib told us, `Abdullah ibn Nafi` told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Sa`d, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of `Ata` ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, that a man had intercourse with a woman in her anus, and the people denounced him for that, so God revealed, Your women are a place of cultivation for you, the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ya`qub, and al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili narrated it on the authority of al-Harith ibn Shuraih, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Nafi` with it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Ubaidullah bin Uthman bin Khathim told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Sabit, who said: I entered upon Hafsa bint Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr, and I said: I am going to ask you about something and I am too shy to ask you. She said: Do not be shy, my nephew. He said: About having intercourse with women from behind? She said: Umm Salamah told me that the Ansar loved women and the Jews used to say: Whoever obeys his wife, his child will be cross-eyed. When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, they married the women of the Ansar and they obeyed them. A woman refused to obey her husband and said: I will not do that until I come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So she went to Umm Salamah and mentioned that to her. She said: Sit down until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, comes. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, the Ansar woman was too shy to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so she went out and asked him. He said: Call the Ansar woman. So she called her and he recited to her this verse: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth when or how ye will 1:177 with one eye. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Khathim, with it, and he said it is good. I said It was narrated on the authority of Hammad bin Abi Hanifa on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Khathim, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mahak, on the authority of Hafsa, the Mother of the Believers, that a woman came to her and said: My husband comes to me with his face covered and facing forward, and I dislike it. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: There is nothing wrong with it if it is in one valve. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Yaqub - meaning al-Qummi - narrated to us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I am ruined. He said: What ruined you? He said: I moved my saddle last night. He said: So he did not answer him at all. He said: Then God revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, this verse: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth however you will “Come forward and backward, but avoid the anal intercourse and menstruation.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Hamid, on the authority of Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashib, and he said: Hasan Gharib. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Al-Harith bin Shureih told us, Abdullah bin Nafi’ told us, Hisham bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: A man had intercourse with his wife during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: So-and-so has intercourse with his wife. Then God Almighty revealed: Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so go to your place of cultivation however you wish. Abu Dawud said: Abdul Aziz bin Yahya Abu Al-Asbagh told us: Muhammad, meaning Ibn Salamah, told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abaan bin Salih, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Umar said - and may God forgive him - or he was mistaken. Rather, there was a tribe of the Ansar, who were idolaters, with this tribe of the Jews, who were People of the Book, and they saw that they had superiority over them in knowledge, so they imitated many of their actions. And it was the custom of the People of the Book that they would not approach women except on the verge, and that was the most concealing way for a woman to be. So this tribe of the Ansar had taken that from their actions, and this tribe of the Quraysh used to treat women in an abhorrent manner, and they would enjoy them facing forward, facing backward, and lying down. So when the Muhajireen came to Medina, a man from them married a woman from the Ansar, and he went to do that to her, but she disapproved of him and said: We were only approached on the verge, so do that, otherwise avoid me. So their affair spread and reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: Your women are a tilth unto you. So come to your tilth however you wish” meaning, facing, turning, and lying down, meaning the subject of the child. Abu Dawud is the only one who narrated it, and the authenticity of it is attested to by the hadiths that preceded it, especially the narration of Umm Salamah, as it is similar to this context. This hadith was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abaan bin Salih, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I presented the Qur’an to Ibn Abbas from its beginning to its end, stopping at every verse of it and asking him about it, until I reached this verse: Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish. Ibn Abbas said: This tribe of Quraysh used to enjoy women in Mecca and take pleasure in them. So he mentioned the story in its entire context, and Ibn Abbas’s statement that Ibn Umar – and may God forgive him – was mistaken, is as if he was referring to what Al-Bukhari narrated: Ishaq told us, Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Nafi’, who said: When Ibn Umar recited the Qur’an, he would not speak until he finished it, so I took from him One day he recited Surah Al-Baqarah until he reached a place and said: Do you know when it was revealed? I said: No. He said: It was revealed about such and such, then he went on. And on the authority of Abd Al-Samad he said: My father told me, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, Then go to your tilth however you wish, he said: To come to her in... This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it, and he is the only one who narrated it from this source. And Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told me, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Nafi’, he said: I recited one day: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth however you wish, and Ibn Umar said: Do you know when it was revealed? I said: No. He said: It was revealed about having intercourse with women in their back passages. And Abu Qilabah told me: Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Warith told us, my father told me, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, Then go to your tilth however you wish, he said: In the back passage. And it was narrated from the hadith of Malik, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, but it is not authentic. Al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Bilal, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that a man came to his wife from behind and felt intense pain from that, so God revealed: Your wives are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth however you will. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: If this had been narrated by Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of Ibn Umar, people would not have been so fond of Nafi'. This is his explanation for this hadith. It was narrated by Abdullah bin Nafi` on the authority of Dawud bin Qays, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata` bin Yasar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and he mentioned it. This hadith is based on what came before, which is that he comes to her in her vagina from her anus, because of what Al-Nasa`i narrated on the authority of Ali bin Uthman Al-Nufaili on the authority of Sa`id bin Isa, on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Fadalah on the authority of Abdullah bin Sulayman Al-Tawil, on the authority of Ka`b bin Alqamah, on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr, that he told him that he said to Nafi`, the freed slave of Ibn Umar, that he has spoken too much to you, that you say on the authority of Ibn Umar that he issued a fatwa that women may be approached in their anuses. He said: They lied about me, but I will tell you how the matter was. Ibn Umar presented the Qur’an one day while I was with him until he reached Your women are as a tilth for you, so go to your tilth when or how you will. He said: O Nafi`, do you know who ordered this verse? I said: No. He said: We, the Quraysh, used to take women as slaves, but when we entered Medina and married the women of the Ansar, they wanted from her what we wanted, but they hated that and considered it a great sin. The women of the Ansar had adopted the Jewish way of life, that they would only have intercourse on their sides. So God revealed: Your women are a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth however you wish. This is a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of al-Tabarani, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Zakariya ibn Yahya al-Katib al-Umari, on the authority of Mufadhal ibn Fadala, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Alqamah, and he mentioned it. We have narrated from Ibn Umar the opposite of that explicitly, and that it is not permissible or lawful, as will come, even though this statement has been attributed to a group of the jurists of Medina and others, and some of them attributed it to Imam Malik in the book al-Sirr, and most people deny that it is sound from Imam Malik, may God have mercy on him. There are many hadiths narrated through various chains of transmission warning against doing and engaging in it. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Salih, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Be ashamed, for God is not ashamed of the truth. It is not permissible for you to approach women in their private parts.” Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, on the authority of Khuzaymah bin Thabit, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade a man from approaching his wife in her anus. Another way Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, I heard my father narrating on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Usamah bin Al-Haad, that Ubayd God bin Al-Hussain Al-Walibi told him that Abdullah Al-Waqfi told him that Khuzaymah bin Thabit Al-Khatmi told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Be shy, for God is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their backsides.” Narrated by Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah on the authority of Khuzaymah bin Thabit, and there is much disagreement in its chain of transmission. Another hadith Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Othman, on the authority of Mukhrama bin Sulayman, on the authority of Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will not look at a man who has intercourse with a man or a woman in the anus. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good, strange hadith, and Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih in this way, and Ibn Hazm also authenticated it, but Al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Hanad, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, with it as a mursal.
