And Abd said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, that a man asked Ibn Abbas about having intercourse with a woman in her anus. He said: You are asking me about disbelief. Its chain of transmission is sound. And al-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak on the authority of Muammar, with a similar wording. And Abd also said in his interpretation: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakim told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: I used to have intercourse with my wife in her anus, and I heard the statement of God, Your women are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth however you will, so I thought that this was permissible for me. So he said: You pervert! His statement, Approach your tilth however you will, is standing, sitting, facing, and with your back, in their faces. Do not go beyond that to anything else. Another Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who has intercourse with his wife in her anus is the lesser sodomy. Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Hudbah told me, Hammam told us, he said: Qatada was asked about he who has intercourse with his wife in her anus, so Qatada said: Amr ibn Shu`ayb told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the lesser sodomy. Qatada said: Uqbah ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told me, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi `Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayyub, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-`As, his statement, and this is more correct, and God knows best. And Abd ibn Hamid also narrated it on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Hamid al-A`raj, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, with a chain of transmission ending with his statement. Another way Ja`far al-Faryabi said: Ibn Lahi`ah told us on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An`am, on the authority of Abu `Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are seven whom God will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and He will say, ‘Enter the Fire with those who enter: the one who does it, the one to whom it is done, the one who has sexual intercourse with his hand, the one who has sexual intercourse with an animal, the one who has sexual intercourse with a woman in her anus, the one who has intercourse between a woman and her daughter, the one who commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife, and the one who harms his neighbor until he curses him.” Ibn Lahi`ah and his sheikh are weak. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Isa bin Hattan, on the authority of Muslim bin Salam, on the authority of Ali bin Talq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade women from being approached from behind, for God is not ashamed of the truth. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Abu Muawiyah and Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Muawiyah also, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, with an addition, and he said: It is a good hadith. Some people include this hadith in the Musnad of Ali bin Abi Talib as it appears in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, and the correct version is that it is Ali bin Talq. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever has intercourse with his wife in her anus, God will not look at him. Ahmad also said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Suhayl told us, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God will not look at a man who has intercourse with his wife in her anus. Ibn Majah narrated it in this way on the authority of Suhayl. Ahmad also said: Wakee’ told us on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cursed is he who has intercourse with his wife in her anus. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated it in this way on the authority of Wakee’. Another way Al-Hafiz Abu Naim Al-Isfahani said: Ahmad bin Al-Qasim bin Al-Rayyan told us, Abu Abdul-Rahman Al-Nasa’i told us, Hannad and Muhammad bin Ismail told us, and the wording is his, they said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cursed is he who comes to a woman in her anus. This hadith is not like this in Sunan Al-Nasa’i, but rather what is in it is on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Mukhallad, as mentioned above. Our Sheikh, Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahabi, said: Ahmad bin Al-Qasim bin Al-Rayyan narrated this hadith with this chain of transmission, and they made a mistake in it and weakened it. Another way - Narrated by Muslim bin Khalid Al-Zanji on the authority of Al-Ala bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Cursed is he who comes to women from behind. There is talk about Muslim bin Khalid, and God knows best. Another way - It was narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunnah from the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Hakim al-Athram, on the authority of Abu Tamimah al-Hujaimi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has intercourse with a menstruating woman, or a woman in her anus, or a soothsayer and believes him, has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad. Al-Tirmidhi said: Al-Bukhari weakened this hadith, and what Al-Bukhari said about the hadith of Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Taymiyyah: He is not to be followed in his hadith. Another way - Al-Nasa'i said: Uthman bin Abdullah told us, Sulayman bin Abdul Rahman told us from his book, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Muhammad Al-San'ani, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Be ashamed before God as you should be. Do not approach women from behind.” Al-Nasa'i is the only one who narrated it from this source. Hamzah bin Muhammad Al-Kinani Al-Hafiz said: This is a rejected and false hadith from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, from the hadith of Abu Salamah, and from the hadith of Saeed. If Abdul Malik heard it from Saeed, then he only heard it after the disagreement. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Salamah that he used to forbid that. As for Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then no. His words end. He was good and did a good job of criticizing, except that Abdul Malik bin Muhammad Al-San'ani is not known to have mixed up, and no one mentioned that except Hamzah from Al-Kinani, and he is trustworthy. However, Dahim, Abu Hatim, and Ibn Hibban spoke about him and said: It is not permissible to use it as evidence, and God knows best. It was followed by Zaid bin Yahya bin Ubaid on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz. It was narrated through two other chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Salamah, but not all of them are authentic. Another way - Al-Nasa’i said: Ishaq bin Mansur told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Men coming to women from behind is disbelief. Then Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of al-Thawri on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. He also narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Nudaymah on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Bakr bin Khunais narrated it on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever comes to men or women from behind has disbelieved. The chain of transmission is more authentic, and Bakr bin Khunais was deemed weak by more than one of the imams, and others abandoned him. Another hadith - Muhammad ibn Abaan al-Balkhi said: Waki` told us, Zam`ah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, and on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Yazid ibn al-Had, they said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God is not ashamed of the truth. Do not approach women from behind.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it. Sa`id ibn Ya`qub al-Talaqani told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Yaman, on the authority of Zam`ah ibn Salih, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn al-Had, on the authority of Umar, he said: Do not approach women from behind. Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Yazid ibn Abi Hakim told us, on the authority of Zam`ah ibn Salih, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Had al-Laythi, he said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Be ashamed of God, for God is not ashamed of the truth. Do not approach women from behind. The suspended hadith is more authentic. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ghundar and Muadh ibn Muadh told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of `Isa ibn Hattan, on the authority of Muslim ibn Salam, on the authority of Talq ibn Yazid or Yazid ibn Talq, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God is not ashamed of the truth. Do not approach women in their anal openings.” And more than one person narrated it in the same way on the authority of Shu`bah, and `Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of `Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of `Isa ibn Hattan, on the authority of Muslim ibn Salam, on the authority of Talq ibn `Ali, and it is more likely that he is `Ali ibn Talq, as mentioned above, and God knows best. Another hadith - Abu Bakr al-Athram said in his Sunan: Abu Muslim al-Harami told us, the brother of Anis ibn Ibrahim told us, that his father Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qa’qa’ told him, on the authority of his father Abu al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, Women’s private parts are forbidden. It was narrated by Ismail ibn ‘Ali, Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu’bah, and others on the authority of Abu ‘Abdullah al-Shaqri, whose name is Salamah ibn Tamam, a trustworthy narrator, on the authority of Abu al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission ending with him, and this is more authentic. Another path - Ibn Adi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Muhamali told us, Saeed bin Yahya Al-Thawri told us, Muhammad bin Hamza told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not approach women in their backsides. Muhammad bin Hamza is Al-Jazari, and his sheikh is criticized. It has been narrated from the hadith of Ubayy bin Ka’b, Al-Bara’ bin Azib, Uqbah bin Amir, Abu Dharr, and others, and each of them has criticism that makes the hadith invalid, and God knows best. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Al-Salt bin Bahram, on the authority of Abu Al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Abu Juwayriyah, who said: A man asked Ali about approaching a woman in her anus, so he said: You have gone astray, may God have gone astray with you. Have you not heard the statement of God, the Almighty: Do you commit such immorality as no one before you has done before you from among the worlds? The statement of Ibn Mas’ud, Abu Al-Darda’, Abu Hurairah, Ibn Abbas, and Abdullah bin Umar, may God be pleased with them, that he forbids it has already been mentioned. Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God al-Darimi said in his Musnad: Abd God ibn Salih told us, al-Layth told us, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Yaqub, on the authority of Saeed ibn Yasar Abi al-Habbab, who said: I said to Ibn Umar: What do you say about female slaves? Is it permissible to make them sour? He said: What is making them sour? He mentioned the anus, and he said: Does any Muslim do that? Ibn Wahb and Qutaybah narrated it in the same way on the authority of al-Layth. This is a sound chain of transmission and a clear text from him prohibiting that. So everything that was reported on his authority that is open to interpretation is rejected based on this decisive hadith. Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Abd al-Hakam told me, Abu Zaid Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Umar told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim told me, on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, that it was said to him: O Abu Abdullah, people narrate on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah that he said: The slave or the foreigner lied about Abu Abdullah. Malik said: I bear witness on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman that he told me on the authority of Salim ibn Abd God on the authority of Ibn Umar the same as Nafi’ said. It was said to him: Al-Harith bin Ya'qub narrates on the authority of Abu Al-Habbab Saeed bin Yasar that he asked Ibn Umar and said to him: O Abu Abdul Rahman, we buy female slaves, so should we dye them? He said: What is dyeing? He mentioned the anus, and Ibn Umar said: Uff, ff! Does a believer do that? Or did he say: Muslim? Malik said: I bear witness on the authority of Rabi'ah, who told me on the authority of Abu Al-Habbab, on the authority of Ibn Umar, the same as what Nafi' said. Al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi' bin Sulayman, on the authority of Asbagh bin Al-Faraj, the jurist, Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Qasim told us: I said to Malik: We have in Egypt Al-Layth bin Saad narrating on the authority of Al-Harith bin Ya'qub, on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, who said: I said to Ibn Umar: We buy female slaves, so should we dye them? He said: What is dyeing? I said: We come to them from their anuses. He said: Uff, ff, or does a Muslim do that? Malik said to me: I bear witness on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, that he asked Ibn Umar, and he said: There is nothing wrong with it. Al-Nasa'i also narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah: Ibn Umar saw no harm in a man approaching a woman from behind. Muammar ibn Isa narrated on the authority of Malik that this is forbidden. Abu Bakr ibn Ziyad al-Naysaburi said: Ismail ibn Husayn told me, Israel ibn Ruh told me, I asked Malik ibn Anas: What do you say about approaching women from behind? He said: You are only an Arab people. Is the field anything other than the place where the crops are planted? Do not pass over the vagina. I said: O Abu Abdullah, they say that you say that. He said: They lie about me, they lie about me. This is what is proven from him, and it is the saying of Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and all their companions. It is the saying of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Abu Salamah, Ikrimah, Tawus, Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid ibn Jabr, Al-Hasan and others from the Salaf, that they denounced it most strongly, and some of them called his action disbelief, which is the doctrine of the majority of scholars. Something about this has been reported from some of the jurists of Madinah, to the point that they reported it from Imam Malik, and its authenticity is questionable. Al-Tahawi said: Asbagh ibn Al-Faraj narrated from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I have not met anyone whom I follow in my religion who doubts that it is permissible, meaning anal intercourse with a woman. Then he recited: Your women are a place of cultivation for you, and said: What is clearer than this? This is the story of At-Tahawi. Al-Hakim, Ad-Darqutni and Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi narrated from Imam Malik through chains of transmission that necessitate that it is permissible, but there is severe weakness in the chains of transmission. Our Sheikh, the Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahabi, has exhaustively examined them in a volume he compiled on that subject, and God knows best. At-Tahawi said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam narrated to us that he heard Al-Shafi’i say: There is nothing authentically reported from the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) regarding its permissibility or prohibition, and by analogy it is permissible. Abu Bakr Al-Khatib narrated that on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Sayrafi on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm. I heard Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam say, and he mentioned it. Abu Nasr Al-Sabbagh said: Al-Rabi’ used to swear by God that there is no god but Him. He meaning Ibn Abdul-Hakam lied about Al-Shafi’i in that, because Al-Shafi’i explicitly stated that it is forbidden in six of his books, and God knows best. And His statement, And prepare for yourselves, meaning by doing acts of obedience while complying with what He has forbidden you to do, such as abstaining from forbidden things. For this reason, He said, And fear God and know that you will meet Him, meaning He will hold you accountable for all your deeds. And give good tidings to the believers, meaning those who obey God in what He has commanded them, and abstain from what He has forbidden them. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Waqid told me, on the authority of Ata’, who said: I think it was on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And prepare for yourselves, he said: You say Bismillah before intercourse. It was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If one of you, when he wants to have intercourse with his wife, says: In the name of God, O God, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You have provided us, then if a child is destined between them during that time, Satan will never harm him.”
2:223: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, that when a Jewish woman among them menstruated, they would not eat with her or have intercourse with her in their homes. So he asked the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty revealed: “They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harmful thing, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are pure.” Until he finished the verse, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do everything except intercourse. This reached the Jews and they said: This man does not want to leave anything of our affair without contradicting us in it. So Asid ibn Hudayr and Ubad ibn Bishr came and said: O Messenger of God, the Jews said: Such and such, so should we not have intercourse with them? The face of the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) changed until we thought that he was angry with them. They went out and we met them with a gift of milk for the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him). He sent after them and gave them something to drink, so they knew that he was not angry with them. Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd ibn Salamah. His saying, So keep away from women during menstruation means the vagina, because he said, Do everything except intercourse. For this reason, many scholars, or most of them, held that it is permissible to have intercourse with a menstruating woman except the vagina. Abu Dawud also said: Musa ibn Ismail told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of some of the wives of the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), that if he wanted to do something to a menstruating woman, he would throw a cloth over her vagina. Abu Dawud also said: Al-Qa'nabi told us, Abdullah, meaning Ibn Umar Ibn Ghanim, told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Ammarah Ibn Ghurab that his aunt told him that she asked Aisha, saying: One of us menstruates and she and her husband do not have a bed except one bed. She said: I will tell you what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did. He entered and went to his mosque. Abu Dawud said: She meant the mosque of her house. He had not finished until my eyes overcame me and the cold hurt him. He said: Come closer to me. I said: I am menstruating. He said: Uncover your thighs. I uncovered my thighs. He placed his cheek and chest on my thigh and I leaned over him until he became warm and he fell asleep (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: `Abd al-Wahhab told us, Ayyub told us from the book of Abu Qilabah, that Masruq rode to `Aishah and said: Peace be upon the Prophet and his family. `Aishah said: Welcome, welcome. They gave him permission and he entered and said: I want to ask you about something and I am shy. She said: I am your mother and you are my son. He said: What is a man entitled to from his wife when she is menstruating? She said to him: Everything except her private parts. It was also narrated on the authority of Humayd ibn Mas`adah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zari`, on the authority of `Uyaynah ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Jushan, on the authority of Marwan al-Asfar, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I said to `Aishah: What is permissible for a man to do with his wife when she is menstruating? She said: Everything except intercourse. This is the statement of Ibn `Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and `Ikrimah. Ibn Jarir also narrated on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Abi Zaydah, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Maymun ibn Mihran, on the authority of `Aishah, who said to him: What is above the izar. I said It is permissible to lie with her and eat with her without disagreement. `Aishah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to order me to wash his head while I was menstruating, and he used to recline on my lap while I was menstruating and recite the Qur’an. In Sahih from her, she said: I used to sweat while I was menstruating and give it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would put his mouth where I had put my mouth, and I would drink the drink and I would give it to him and he would put his mouth where I had drunk from. Abu Dawud said: Musaddad told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Jabir ibn Subh, I heard Khalas al-Hijri say: I heard Aisha say: I and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were in one garment and I was menstruating and menstruating, so if something of mine got on him, he would wash the place where it had been and not repeat it, and if something got on him - meaning his garment - he would wash the place where it had been and not repeat it and prayed in it. As for what Abu Dawud narrated, Saeed ibn al-Jabbar told us, Abdul Aziz - meaning Ibn Muhammad - told us, on the authority of Abu al-Yaman, on the authority of Umm Dhara, on the authority of Aisha that she said: When I menstruated, I would get off the mat and not approach the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor would we approach him until we were pure, so it is understood as a precaution and a precaution. Others said: It is only permissible for him to have intercourse with her except what is under the izar, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, who said: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to have intercourse with one of his wives, he would put on a waist wrapper while she was menstruating. This is the wording of al-Bukhari, and they both have something similar on the authority of Aisha. Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Ala’, on the authority of Hizam ibn Hakeem, on the authority of his uncle Abdullah ibn Sa’d al-Ansari, that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: What is permissible for me to do with my wife while she is menstruating? He said: What is above the izar. Abu Dawud also has: “On the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what is permissible for me to do with my wife while she is menstruating? He said: What is above the izar, and refraining from that is better.” This is a narration on the authority of Aisha, as mentioned above, and Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab and Shuraih. These hadiths and similar hadiths are evidence for those who hold that what is above the izaar is permissible, and this is one of the two opinions in the Shafi’i school of thought, may God have mercy on him, which was preferred by many Iraqis and others. Their basis is that the vagina is sacred, so it is forbidden so that one does not reach the point of engaging in what God Almighty has forbidden, which the scholars have unanimously agreed to prohibit, which is intercourse in the vagina. Then whoever does that has sinned, so he should seek God’s forgiveness and repent to Him. Is he required to make expiation for that or not? There are two opinions on this: One of them Yes, because of what Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the one who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, he should give in charity a dinar or half a dinar. In a wording by al-Tirmidhi: If it is red blood, then a dinar, and if it is yellow blood, then half a dinar. Imam Ahmad also narrated on his authority that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stipulated that a menstruating woman should be given a dinar, and if he has intercourse with her after the blood has gone away and she has not performed ghusl, then half a dinar. The second opinion which is the new correct opinion of the Shafi’i school of thought and the opinion of the majority is that there is nothing wrong with that, rather he seeks forgiveness from God the Almighty because they did not authenticate this hadith, as it was narrated as a marfu’ as mentioned above, and as a mawquf, which is the correct opinion according to many of the Imams of Hadeeth. So the words of God the Almighty: And do not approach them until they are pure are an interpretation of His words: So keep away from women during menstruation and He forbade approaching them by intercourse as long as menstruation is present, and its implication is that it is permissible if it stops. Imam Abu Abdullah Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Hanbal said in what he dictated in At-Ta’a’: And His words: “And they ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harmful thing, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are pure. Then when they have purified themselves, then come to them from the place of purity” the verse, purity indicates that he should come near her, so when Maymunah and Aisha said: When one of us menstruated, she would put on a wrapper and enter with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in his garment, this indicates that he only meant intercourse. His saying, Then when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where God has commanded you, contains encouragement and guidance to have intercourse with them after bathing. Ibn Hazm held that intercourse is obligatory after every menstrual period, based on his saying, Then when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where God has commanded you, and he has no basis for that, because this is a command after a prohibition. There are statements by scholars of the principles of jurisprudence, some of whom say that it is obligatory like the absolute, these need the answer of Ibn Hazm, and some of whom say: it is permissible, and they make the prohibition precedent over it an indication that diverts it from obligation, and there is consideration in it, and what the evidence is based on is that the ruling is returned to what the matter was before the prohibition, so if it was obligatory, then it is obligatory like his saying: So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists or permissible, then it is permissible like his saying: And when you are released from ihram, then hunt “And when the prayer is completed, then disperse within the land” and on this statement the evidence is combined, and it was narrated by al-Ghazali and others, so some of the imams of the later scholars chose it and it is correct, and the scholars agreed that if a woman’s menstruation stops, she is not permissible until she washes with water or performs tayammum if that is not possible for her with its condition, except that Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, says, in the case of her bleeding stopping for the most part of menstruation, which is ten days according to him: that she is permissible as soon as it stops and does not need to wash, and God knows best, and Ibn Abbas said: Until they are purified meaning from the blood, So if “Purify yourself means with water. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Al-Layth bin Saad, and others said. And his statement, from where God has commanded you, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: meaning the vagina. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you, meaning in the vagina and do not go beyond it to anything else, for whoever does any of that has transgressed. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ikrimah said: From where God has commanded you, meaning stay away from them, and this indicates in this case the prohibition of anal intercourse, as will be explained soon, God willing. Abu Razin, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak and others said: Then have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you, meaning when they are pure and not menstruating. That is why He said: Indeed, God loves those who repent, meaning from sin, even if they have committed it repeatedly, and He loves those who purify themselves, meaning those who are free from filth and harm, which is what they were forbidden from, such as having intercourse with a menstruating woman or in a place other than the place of intercourse. And his saying, Your women are a place of cultivation for you. Ibn Abbas said: The place of cultivation is the place of the child. So go to your place of cultivation however you wish. That is, however you wish. He said: I heard Jabir say: The Jews used to say: If a man has intercourse with her from behind, the child will be born cross-eyed. So the verse, Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so go to your place of cultivation however you wish. was revealed. Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Malik bin Anas, Ibn Jurayj and Sufyan bin Saeed Ath-Thawri told me: Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir told them: Jabir bin Abdullah told him that the Jews said to the Muslims: Whoever has intercourse with a woman while she is facing away, the child will be born cross-eyed. So God revealed: Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so approach your place of cultivation however you wish. Ibn Jurayj said in the hadith: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In front or from behind, if that is in the vagina. And in the hadith of Bahz bin Hakim bin Mu’awiyah bin Haidah Al-Qushayri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that he said: O Messenger of God, what do we have intercourse with our women from them and what do we leave? He said: Your place of cultivation, go to your place of cultivation however you wish, except that you do not strike the face, do not insult, and do not abandon her except in the house. The hadith was narrated by Ahmad and the people of Sunan. Another hadith - Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Aamer ibn Yahya, on the authority of Hanash ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: Some people from Himyar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about some things. A man said to him: I love women, so what do you think of me? So God revealed: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth however you wish. Imam Ahmad narrated it. Yahya ibn Ghailan told us, Rashdin told us, Al-Hasan ibn Thauban told me on the authority of Aamer ibn Yahya Al-Maghafari on the authority of Hanash, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed about some people from the Ansar who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about some things. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Go to her in any case, if it is in the vagina. Another hadith - Abu Ja`far al-Tahawi said in his book Mushkil al-Hadith: Ahmad ibn Dawud ibn Musa told us, Ya`qub ibn Kasib told us, `Abdullah ibn Nafi` told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Sa`d, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of `Ata` ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, that a man had intercourse with a woman in her anus, and the people denounced him for that, so God revealed, Your women are a place of cultivation for you, the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ya`qub, and al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili narrated it on the authority of al-Harith ibn Shuraih, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Nafi` with it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Ubaidullah bin Uthman bin Khathim told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Sabit, who said: I entered upon Hafsa bint Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr, and I said: I am going to ask you about something and I am too shy to ask you. She said: Do not be shy, my nephew. He said: About having intercourse with women from behind? She said: Umm Salamah told me that the Ansar loved women and the Jews used to say: Whoever obeys his wife, his child will be cross-eyed. When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, they married the women of the Ansar and they obeyed them. A woman refused to obey her husband and said: I will not do that until I come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So she went to Umm Salamah and mentioned that to her. She said: Sit down until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, comes. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, the Ansar woman was too shy to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so she went out and asked him. He said: Call the Ansar woman. So she called her and he recited to her this verse: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth when or how ye will 1:177 with one eye. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Khathim, with it, and he said it is good. I said It was narrated on the authority of Hammad bin Abi Hanifa on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Khathim, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mahak, on the authority of Hafsa, the Mother of the Believers, that a woman came to her and said: My husband comes to me with his face covered and facing forward, and I dislike it. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: There is nothing wrong with it if it is in one valve. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Yaqub - meaning al-Qummi - narrated to us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I am ruined. He said: What ruined you? He said: I moved my saddle last night. He said: So he did not answer him at all. He said: Then God revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, this verse: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth however you will “Come forward and backward, but avoid the anal intercourse and menstruation.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Hamid, on the authority of Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashib, and he said: Hasan Gharib. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Al-Harith bin Shureih told us, Abdullah bin Nafi’ told us, Hisham bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: A man had intercourse with his wife during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: So-and-so has intercourse with his wife. Then God Almighty revealed: Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so go to your place of cultivation however you wish. Abu Dawud said: Abdul Aziz bin Yahya Abu Al-Asbagh told us: Muhammad, meaning Ibn Salamah, told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abaan bin Salih, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Umar said - and may God forgive him - or he was mistaken. Rather, there was a tribe of the Ansar, who were idolaters, with this tribe of the Jews, who were People of the Book, and they saw that they had superiority over them in knowledge, so they imitated many of their actions. And it was the custom of the People of the Book that they would not approach women except on the verge, and that was the most concealing way for a woman to be. So this tribe of the Ansar had taken that from their actions, and this tribe of the Quraysh used to treat women in an abhorrent manner, and they would enjoy them facing forward, facing backward, and lying down. So when the Muhajireen came to Medina, a man from them married a woman from the Ansar, and he went to do that to her, but she disapproved of him and said: We were only approached on the verge, so do that, otherwise avoid me. So their affair spread and reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: Your women are a tilth unto you. So come to your tilth however you wish” meaning, facing, turning, and lying down, meaning the subject of the child. Abu Dawud is the only one who narrated it, and the authenticity of it is attested to by the hadiths that preceded it, especially the narration of Umm Salamah, as it is similar to this context. This hadith was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abaan bin Salih, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I presented the Qur’an to Ibn Abbas from its beginning to its end, stopping at every verse of it and asking him about it, until I reached this verse: Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish. Ibn Abbas said: This tribe of Quraysh used to enjoy women in Mecca and take pleasure in them. So he mentioned the story in its entire context, and Ibn Abbas’s statement that Ibn Umar – and may God forgive him – was mistaken, is as if he was referring to what Al-Bukhari narrated: Ishaq told us, Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Nafi’, who said: When Ibn Umar recited the Qur’an, he would not speak until he finished it, so I took from him One day he recited Surah Al-Baqarah until he reached a place and said: Do you know when it was revealed? I said: No. He said: It was revealed about such and such, then he went on. And on the authority of Abd Al-Samad he said: My father told me, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, Then go to your tilth however you wish, he said: To come to her in... This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it, and he is the only one who narrated it from this source. And Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told me, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Nafi’, he said: I recited one day: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth however you wish, and Ibn Umar said: Do you know when it was revealed? I said: No. He said: It was revealed about having intercourse with women in their back passages. And Abu Qilabah told me: Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Warith told us, my father told me, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, Then go to your tilth however you wish, he said: In the back passage. And it was narrated from the hadith of Malik, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, but it is not authentic. Al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Bilal, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that a man came to his wife from behind and felt intense pain from that, so God revealed: Your wives are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth however you will. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: If this had been narrated by Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of Ibn Umar, people would not have been so fond of Nafi'. This is his explanation for this hadith. It was narrated by Abdullah bin Nafi` on the authority of Dawud bin Qays, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata` bin Yasar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and he mentioned it. This hadith is based on what came before, which is that he comes to her in her vagina from her anus, because of what Al-Nasa`i narrated on the authority of Ali bin Uthman Al-Nufaili on the authority of Sa`id bin Isa, on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Fadalah on the authority of Abdullah bin Sulayman Al-Tawil, on the authority of Ka`b bin Alqamah, on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr, that he told him that he said to Nafi`, the freed slave of Ibn Umar, that he has spoken too much to you, that you say on the authority of Ibn Umar that he issued a fatwa that women may be approached in their anuses. He said: They lied about me, but I will tell you how the matter was. Ibn Umar presented the Qur’an one day while I was with him until he reached Your women are as a tilth for you, so go to your tilth when or how you will. He said: O Nafi`, do you know who ordered this verse? I said: No. He said: We, the Quraysh, used to take women as slaves, but when we entered Medina and married the women of the Ansar, they wanted from her what we wanted, but they hated that and considered it a great sin. The women of the Ansar had adopted the Jewish way of life, that they would only have intercourse on their sides. So God revealed: Your women are a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth however you wish. This is a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of al-Tabarani, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Zakariya ibn Yahya al-Katib al-Umari, on the authority of Mufadhal ibn Fadala, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Alqamah, and he mentioned it. We have narrated from Ibn Umar the opposite of that explicitly, and that it is not permissible or lawful, as will come, even though this statement has been attributed to a group of the jurists of Medina and others, and some of them attributed it to Imam Malik in the book al-Sirr, and most people deny that it is sound from Imam Malik, may God have mercy on him. There are many hadiths narrated through various chains of transmission warning against doing and engaging in it. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Salih, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Be ashamed, for God is not ashamed of the truth. It is not permissible for you to approach women in their private parts.” Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, on the authority of Khuzaymah bin Thabit, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade a man from approaching his wife in her anus. Another way Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, I heard my father narrating on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Usamah bin Al-Haad, that Ubayd God bin Al-Hussain Al-Walibi told him that Abdullah Al-Waqfi told him that Khuzaymah bin Thabit Al-Khatmi told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Be shy, for God is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their backsides.” Narrated by Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah on the authority of Khuzaymah bin Thabit, and there is much disagreement in its chain of transmission. Another hadith Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Othman, on the authority of Mukhrama bin Sulayman, on the authority of Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will not look at a man who has intercourse with a man or a woman in the anus. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good, strange hadith, and Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih in this way, and Ibn Hazm also authenticated it, but Al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Hanad, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, with it as a mursal. And Abd said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, that a man asked Ibn Abbas about having intercourse with a woman in her anus. He said: You are asking me about disbelief. Its chain of transmission is sound. And al-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak on the authority of Muammar, with a similar wording. And Abd also said in his interpretation: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakim told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: I used to have intercourse with my wife in her anus, and I heard the statement of God, Your women are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth however you will, so I thought that this was permissible for me. So he said: You pervert! His statement, Approach your tilth however you will, is standing, sitting, facing, and with your back, in their faces. Do not go beyond that to anything else. Another Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who has intercourse with his wife in her anus is the lesser sodomy. Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Hudbah told me, Hammam told us, he said: Qatada was asked about he who has intercourse with his wife in her anus, so Qatada said: Amr ibn Shu`ayb told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the lesser sodomy. Qatada said: Uqbah ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told me, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi `Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayyub, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-`As, his statement, and this is more correct, and God knows best. And Abd ibn Hamid also narrated it on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Hamid al-A`raj, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, with a chain of transmission ending with his statement. Another way Ja`far al-Faryabi said: Ibn Lahi`ah told us on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An`am, on the authority of Abu `Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are seven whom God will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and He will say, ‘Enter the Fire with those who enter: the one who does it, the one to whom it is done, the one who has sexual intercourse with his hand, the one who has sexual intercourse with an animal, the one who has sexual intercourse with a woman in her anus, the one who has intercourse between a woman and her daughter, the one who commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife, and the one who harms his neighbor until he curses him.” Ibn Lahi`ah and his sheikh are weak. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Isa bin Hattan, on the authority of Muslim bin Salam, on the authority of Ali bin Talq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade women from being approached from behind, for God is not ashamed of the truth. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Abu Muawiyah and Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Muawiyah also, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, with an addition, and he said: It is a good hadith. Some people include this hadith in the Musnad of Ali bin Abi Talib as it appears in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, and the correct version is that it is Ali bin Talq. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever has intercourse with his wife in her anus, God will not look at him. Ahmad also said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Suhayl told us, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God will not look at a man who has intercourse with his wife in her anus. Ibn Majah narrated it in this way on the authority of Suhayl. Ahmad also said: Wakee’ told us on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cursed is he who has intercourse with his wife in her anus. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated it in this way on the authority of Wakee’. Another way Al-Hafiz Abu Naim Al-Isfahani said: Ahmad bin Al-Qasim bin Al-Rayyan told us, Abu Abdul-Rahman Al-Nasa’i told us, Hannad and Muhammad bin Ismail told us, and the wording is his, they said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cursed is he who comes to a woman in her anus. This hadith is not like this in Sunan Al-Nasa’i, but rather what is in it is on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Mukhallad, as mentioned above. Our Sheikh, Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahabi, said: Ahmad bin Al-Qasim bin Al-Rayyan narrated this hadith with this chain of transmission, and they made a mistake in it and weakened it. Another way - Narrated by Muslim bin Khalid Al-Zanji on the authority of Al-Ala bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Cursed is he who comes to women from behind. There is talk about Muslim bin Khalid, and God knows best. Another way - It was narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunnah from the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Hakim al-Athram, on the authority of Abu Tamimah al-Hujaimi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has intercourse with a menstruating woman, or a woman in her anus, or a soothsayer and believes him, has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad. Al-Tirmidhi said: Al-Bukhari weakened this hadith, and what Al-Bukhari said about the hadith of Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Taymiyyah: He is not to be followed in his hadith. Another way - Al-Nasa'i said: Uthman bin Abdullah told us, Sulayman bin Abdul Rahman told us from his book, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Muhammad Al-San'ani, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Be ashamed before God as you should be. Do not approach women from behind.” Al-Nasa'i is the only one who narrated it from this source. Hamzah bin Muhammad Al-Kinani Al-Hafiz said: This is a rejected and false hadith from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, from the hadith of Abu Salamah, and from the hadith of Saeed. If Abdul Malik heard it from Saeed, then he only heard it after the disagreement. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Salamah that he used to forbid that. As for Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then no. His words end. He was good and did a good job of criticizing, except that Abdul Malik bin Muhammad Al-San'ani is not known to have mixed up, and no one mentioned that except Hamzah from Al-Kinani, and he is trustworthy. However, Dahim, Abu Hatim, and Ibn Hibban spoke about him and said: It is not permissible to use it as evidence, and God knows best. It was followed by Zaid bin Yahya bin Ubaid on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz. It was narrated through two other chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Salamah, but not all of them are authentic. Another way - Al-Nasa’i said: Ishaq bin Mansur told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Men coming to women from behind is disbelief. Then Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of al-Thawri on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. He also narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Nudaymah on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Bakr bin Khunais narrated it on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever comes to men or women from behind has disbelieved. The chain of transmission is more authentic, and Bakr bin Khunais was deemed weak by more than one of the imams, and others abandoned him. Another hadith - Muhammad ibn Abaan al-Balkhi said: Waki` told us, Zam`ah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, and on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Yazid ibn al-Had, they said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God is not ashamed of the truth. Do not approach women from behind.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it. Sa`id ibn Ya`qub al-Talaqani told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Yaman, on the authority of Zam`ah ibn Salih, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn al-Had, on the authority of Umar, he said: Do not approach women from behind. Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Yazid ibn Abi Hakim told us, on the authority of Zam`ah ibn Salih, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Had al-Laythi, he said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Be ashamed of God, for God is not ashamed of the truth. Do not approach women from behind. The suspended hadith is more authentic. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ghundar and Muadh ibn Muadh told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of `Isa ibn Hattan, on the authority of Muslim ibn Salam, on the authority of Talq ibn Yazid or Yazid ibn Talq, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God is not ashamed of the truth. Do not approach women in their anal openings.” And more than one person narrated it in the same way on the authority of Shu`bah, and `Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of `Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of `Isa ibn Hattan, on the authority of Muslim ibn Salam, on the authority of Talq ibn `Ali, and it is more likely that he is `Ali ibn Talq, as mentioned above, and God knows best. Another hadith - Abu Bakr al-Athram said in his Sunan: Abu Muslim al-Harami told us, the brother of Anis ibn Ibrahim told us, that his father Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qa’qa’ told him, on the authority of his father Abu al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, Women’s private parts are forbidden. It was narrated by Ismail ibn ‘Ali, Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu’bah, and others on the authority of Abu ‘Abdullah al-Shaqri, whose name is Salamah ibn Tamam, a trustworthy narrator, on the authority of Abu al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission ending with him, and this is more authentic. Another path - Ibn Adi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Muhamali told us, Saeed bin Yahya Al-Thawri told us, Muhammad bin Hamza told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not approach women in their backsides. Muhammad bin Hamza is Al-Jazari, and his sheikh is criticized. It has been narrated from the hadith of Ubayy bin Ka’b, Al-Bara’ bin Azib, Uqbah bin Amir, Abu Dharr, and others, and each of them has criticism that makes the hadith invalid, and God knows best. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Al-Salt bin Bahram, on the authority of Abu Al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Abu Juwayriyah, who said: A man asked Ali about approaching a woman in her anus, so he said: You have gone astray, may God have gone astray with you. Have you not heard the statement of God, the Almighty: Do you commit such immorality as no one before you has done before you from among the worlds? The statement of Ibn Mas’ud, Abu Al-Darda’, Abu Hurairah, Ibn Abbas, and Abdullah bin Umar, may God be pleased with them, that he forbids it has already been mentioned. Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God al-Darimi said in his Musnad: Abd God ibn Salih told us, al-Layth told us, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Yaqub, on the authority of Saeed ibn Yasar Abi al-Habbab, who said: I said to Ibn Umar: What do you say about female slaves? Is it permissible to make them sour? He said: What is making them sour? He mentioned the anus, and he said: Does any Muslim do that? Ibn Wahb and Qutaybah narrated it in the same way on the authority of al-Layth. This is a sound chain of transmission and a clear text from him prohibiting that. So everything that was reported on his authority that is open to interpretation is rejected based on this decisive hadith. Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Abd al-Hakam told me, Abu Zaid Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Umar told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim told me, on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, that it was said to him: O Abu Abdullah, people narrate on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah that he said: The slave or the foreigner lied about Abu Abdullah. Malik said: I bear witness on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman that he told me on the authority of Salim ibn Abd God on the authority of Ibn Umar the same as Nafi’ said. It was said to him: Al-Harith bin Ya'qub narrates on the authority of Abu Al-Habbab Saeed bin Yasar that he asked Ibn Umar and said to him: O Abu Abdul Rahman, we buy female slaves, so should we dye them? He said: What is dyeing? He mentioned the anus, and Ibn Umar said: Uff, ff! Does a believer do that? Or did he say: Muslim? Malik said: I bear witness on the authority of Rabi'ah, who told me on the authority of Abu Al-Habbab, on the authority of Ibn Umar, the same as what Nafi' said. Al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi' bin Sulayman, on the authority of Asbagh bin Al-Faraj, the jurist, Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Qasim told us: I said to Malik: We have in Egypt Al-Layth bin Saad narrating on the authority of Al-Harith bin Ya'qub, on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, who said: I said to Ibn Umar: We buy female slaves, so should we dye them? He said: What is dyeing? I said: We come to them from their anuses. He said: Uff, ff, or does a Muslim do that? Malik said to me: I bear witness on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, that he asked Ibn Umar, and he said: There is nothing wrong with it. Al-Nasa'i also narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah: Ibn Umar saw no harm in a man approaching a woman from behind. Muammar ibn Isa narrated on the authority of Malik that this is forbidden. Abu Bakr ibn Ziyad al-Naysaburi said: Ismail ibn Husayn told me, Israel ibn Ruh told me, I asked Malik ibn Anas: What do you say about approaching women from behind? He said: You are only an Arab people. Is the field anything other than the place where the crops are planted? Do not pass over the vagina. I said: O Abu Abdullah, they say that you say that. He said: They lie about me, they lie about me. This is what is proven from him, and it is the saying of Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and all their companions. It is the saying of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Abu Salamah, Ikrimah, Tawus, Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid ibn Jabr, Al-Hasan and others from the Salaf, that they denounced it most strongly, and some of them called his action disbelief, which is the doctrine of the majority of scholars. Something about this has been reported from some of the jurists of Madinah, to the point that they reported it from Imam Malik, and its authenticity is questionable. Al-Tahawi said: Asbagh ibn Al-Faraj narrated from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I have not met anyone whom I follow in my religion who doubts that it is permissible, meaning anal intercourse with a woman. Then he recited: Your women are a place of cultivation for you, and said: What is clearer than this? This is the story of At-Tahawi. Al-Hakim, Ad-Darqutni and Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi narrated from Imam Malik through chains of transmission that necessitate that it is permissible, but there is severe weakness in the chains of transmission. Our Sheikh, the Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahabi, has exhaustively examined them in a volume he compiled on that subject, and God knows best. At-Tahawi said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam narrated to us that he heard Al-Shafi’i say: There is nothing authentically reported from the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) regarding its permissibility or prohibition, and by analogy it is permissible. Abu Bakr Al-Khatib narrated that on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Sayrafi on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm. I heard Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam say, and he mentioned it. Abu Nasr Al-Sabbagh said: Al-Rabi’ used to swear by God that there is no god but Him. He meaning Ibn Abdul-Hakam lied about Al-Shafi’i in that, because Al-Shafi’i explicitly stated that it is forbidden in six of his books, and God knows best. And His statement, And prepare for yourselves, meaning by doing acts of obedience while complying with what He has forbidden you to do, such as abstaining from forbidden things. For this reason, He said, And fear God and know that you will meet Him, meaning He will hold you accountable for all your deeds. And give good tidings to the believers, meaning those who obey God in what He has commanded them, and abstain from what He has forbidden them. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Waqid told me, on the authority of Ata’, who said: I think it was on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And prepare for yourselves, he said: You say Bismillah before intercourse. It was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If one of you, when he wants to have intercourse with his wife, says: In the name of God, O God, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You have provided us, then if a child is destined between them during that time, Satan will never harm him.”
2:224: God the Almighty says: Do not let your oaths to God the Almighty prevent you from righteousness and maintaining kinship ties if you swear to abandon them, as God the Almighty says: “And let not those among you who are blessed and wealthy swear not to give to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of God. And let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that God should forgive you?” So persisting in the oath is a sin for its owner, as is breaking it by expiation, as Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, he said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, if one of you were to swear an oath against his wife, it would be a sin for him before God, more than giving the expiation that God has made obligatory upon him. And Muslim narrated it like this on the authority of Muhammad bin Rafi’ on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, and Ahmad narrated it on his authority on his authority, then Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq bin Mansour told us, Yahya bin Salih narrated to us, Muawiyah - he is Ibn Salam - narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya - he is Ibn Abi Katheer - on the authority of Ikrimah - on the authority of Abu Hurairah - he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever seeks to take an oath against his wife, he has committed a greater sin, and expiation will not suffice. And Ali bin Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not make God an object of your oaths, he said: Do not make an object of your oath that you do not do good, but expiate for your oath and do good. And this is what Masruq, Al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Mujahid, Tawus, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Ata’, Ikrimah, Makhul, Al-Zuhri, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Dahhak, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and Al-Suddi, may God have mercy on them, said. What these majority said is supported by what is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, if God wills, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I will do what is better and absolve myself of it. And it is also proven in them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, “O Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, do not ask for leadership, for if you are given it without asking for it, you will be helped in it, and if you are given it upon asking for it, you will be left to it. If you swear an oath and then see something better than it, then do what is better and expiate for your oath.” Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him expiate for his oath and do what is better. Imam Ahmad said, Abu Sa`id, a freed slave of Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Khalifa ibn Khayyat narrated to us, `Amr ibn Shu`ayb narrated to me on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, then leaves it, its expiation is for it. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Abu `Ubayd God ibn al-Akhnas on the authority of `Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said, The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “There is no vow or oath in what the son of Adam does not own, nor in disobedience to God, nor in severing family ties. Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him abandon it and do what is better. If he abandons it, its expiation is its expiation.” Then Abu Dawud said: The hadiths from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are all let him expiate for his oath, and they are the authentic ones. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told us, Ali bin Masaher told us, on the authority of Haritha bin Muhammad, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath to sever family ties and commit a sin, then his righteousness is that he breaks it and goes back on his oath. This is a weak hadith. Then Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Masruq, and Al-Sha’bi that they said: There is no oath in a sin and no expiation for it. And His statement, God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths, meaning that He will not punish you or hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths you utter, which are oaths that the swearer does not intend, but rather they come out of his mouth normally without complication or emphasis, as was established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever swears and says in his oath by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, let him say, ‘There is no god but God.’ This was said to people who had recently left the pre-Islamic period and had converted to Islam, but their tongues had become accustomed to swearing by Al-Lat without intending it. So they were commanded to pronounce the word of sincerity as they had pronounced that word without intending it to be like this. For this reason, God, the Most High, said, But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned, and in the other verse, for what you have made indecisive oaths. Abu Dawud said Chapter on idle oaths: Humayd ibn Mas`adah al-Shami told us, Hayyan, meaning Ibn Ibrahim, told us, Ibrahim, meaning al-Sa`igh, told us, on the authority of `Ata`: Concerning idle oaths, he said: `Aishah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Idle oaths are a man’s words in his home: ‘No, by God,’ and ‘Yes, by God.’” Then Abu Dawud said: It was narrated by Dawud ibn al-Furat on the authority of Ibrahim al-Sa`igh, on the authority of `Ata`, on the authority of `Aishah, with no chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Al-Zuhri, `Abd al-Malik, and Malik ibn Mughul all narrated it on the authority of `Ata`, on the authority of `Aishah, with no chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. I said And thus Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Layla narrated it on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission ending with him. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hanad on the authority of Wakee’, Abda and Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha regarding His statement, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, “No, by God,” and Yes, by God. Then he narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Humayd on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father on her authority, and with it on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Al-Qasim on her authority, and with it on the authority of Salamah on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Ata’ on her authority. And Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha regarding His statement, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, she said: They are the people who argue about a matter, and this one says: No, by God, yes, by God, and no, by God, they argue about a matter and their hearts are not settled on it. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us, Abda told us, meaning Ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, regarding the statement of God, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, she said: It is a man saying, No, by God, and Yes, by God. My father told us, Abu Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth, told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Urwah, who said: Aisha used to say: Unintentional oaths are only in jest and playfulness, which is a man saying, No, by God, and Yes, by God. There is no expiation for that, rather the expiation is for what he has resolved in his heart to do and then does not do it. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas in one of his two opinions, and Al-Sha’bi and Ikrimah in one of his two opinions, and Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, Abu Salih, and Al-Dahhak in one of his two opinions, and Abu Qilabah and Al-Zuhri something similar to that. The second aspect It was read to Yunus bin Abdul A’la, Ibn Wahb told us, Al-Thiqa told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha that she used to interpret this verse, meaning His statement, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, and she would say: It is something that one of you swears by, intending nothing but the truth, but it is not what he swore by. Then he said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Ibn Abbas in one of his two opinions, and Sulayman bin Yasar and Sa’id bin Jubayr and Mujahid in one of his two opinions, and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i in one of his two opinions, and Al-Hasan and Zurarah bin Awfa and Abu Malik and Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Bakr bin Abdullah, and one of the two opinions of Ikrimah and Habib bin Abi Thabit and Al-Suddi and Makhul and Muqatil and Tawus and Qatadah and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and Yahya bin Sa’id and Rabi’ something similar to that. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi told us, Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Muradi told us, Awf al-A'rabi told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by some people who were shooting, meaning they were archery, and with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a man from his companions. A man from the people stood up and said: By God, you are right, and by God, you are wrong. The one who was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The man broke his oath, O Messenger of God. He said: No, the oaths of archers are futile, for which there is no expiation or punishment. This is a good mursal from al-Hasan. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Both statements were narrated from Aisha. Issam ibn Rawwad told us, Adam told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: It is his saying: No, by God, and yes, by God, and he thinks that he is telling the truth, but it is not so. Other statements - Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: It is a man who swears an oath about something and then forgets it. Zaid bin Aslam said: It is a man saying: May God blind my sight if I do not do such and such, or may God take away my wealth if I do not come to you tomorrow. This is what it is. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Musaddad bin Khalid told us, Khalid told us, Ata told us, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A vain oath is when you swear while you are angry. My father told me: Abu Al-Jamahir told us, Saeed bin Bashir told us, Abu Bishr told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A vain oath is when you forbid what God has made lawful for you. This is something for which there is no expiation. This is also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. Abu Dawud said Chapter on swearing in anger: Muhammad ibn al-Munhal told us, Yazid ibn Zurai’ told us, Habib al-Mu’allim told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab: There were two brothers from the Ansar between whom there was an inheritance, so one of them asked his companion about the division, so he said: If you ask me again about the division, then all of what I have is in the curtain of the Ka’bah, so ‘Umar said to him: The Ka’bah does not need your money, atone for your oath, and speak to your brother, for I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: There is no oath upon you, nor a vow to disobey the Lord Almighty, nor to sever family ties, nor about what you do not own. And His statement, But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned, Ibn ‘Abbas, Mujahid and more than one said: It means that one swears an oath about something while knowing that it is false. Mujahid and others said: It is like the statement of God, the Most High, But He will hold you accountable for what you have deliberated upon 1:10. And God is Forgiving and Forbearing, meaning He is Forgiving of His servants and Forbearing with them.
