Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Abu `Ubayd God ibn al-Akhnas on the authority of `Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said, The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “There is no vow or oath in what the son of Adam does not own, nor in disobedience to God, nor in severing family ties. Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him abandon it and do what is better. If he abandons it, its expiation is its expiation.” Then Abu Dawud said: The hadiths from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are all let him expiate for his oath, and they are the authentic ones. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told us, Ali bin Masaher told us, on the authority of Haritha bin Muhammad, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath to sever family ties and commit a sin, then his righteousness is that he breaks it and goes back on his oath. This is a weak hadith. Then Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Masruq, and Al-Sha’bi that they said: There is no oath in a sin and no expiation for it. And His statement, God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths, meaning that He will not punish you or hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths you utter, which are oaths that the swearer does not intend, but rather they come out of his mouth normally without complication or emphasis, as was established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever swears and says in his oath by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, let him say, ‘There is no god but God.’ This was said to people who had recently left the pre-Islamic period and had converted to Islam, but their tongues had become accustomed to swearing by Al-Lat without intending it. So they were commanded to pronounce the word of sincerity as they had pronounced that word without intending it to be like this. For this reason, God, the Most High, said, But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned, and in the other verse, for what you have made indecisive oaths. Abu Dawud said Chapter on idle oaths: Humayd ibn Mas`adah al-Shami told us, Hayyan, meaning Ibn Ibrahim, told us, Ibrahim, meaning al-Sa`igh, told us, on the authority of `Ata`: Concerning idle oaths, he said: `Aishah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Idle oaths are a man’s words in his home: ‘No, by God,’ and ‘Yes, by God.’” Then Abu Dawud said: It was narrated by Dawud ibn al-Furat on the authority of Ibrahim al-Sa`igh, on the authority of `Ata`, on the authority of `Aishah, with no chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Al-Zuhri, `Abd al-Malik, and Malik ibn Mughul all narrated it on the authority of `Ata`, on the authority of `Aishah, with no chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. I said And thus Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Layla narrated it on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission ending with him. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hanad on the authority of Wakee’, Abda and Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha regarding His statement, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, “No, by God,” and Yes, by God. Then he narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Humayd on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father on her authority, and with it on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Al-Qasim on her authority, and with it on the authority of Salamah on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Ata’ on her authority. And Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha regarding His statement, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, she said: They are the people who argue about a matter, and this one says: No, by God, yes, by God, and no, by God, they argue about a matter and their hearts are not settled on it. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us, Abda told us, meaning Ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, regarding the statement of God, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, she said: It is a man saying, No, by God, and Yes, by God. My father told us, Abu Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth, told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Urwah, who said: Aisha used to say: Unintentional oaths are only in jest and playfulness, which is a man saying, No, by God, and Yes, by God. There is no expiation for that, rather the expiation is for what he has resolved in his heart to do and then does not do it. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas in one of his two opinions, and Al-Sha’bi and Ikrimah in one of his two opinions, and Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, Abu Salih, and Al-Dahhak in one of his two opinions, and Abu Qilabah and Al-Zuhri something similar to that. The second aspect It was read to Yunus bin Abdul A’la, Ibn Wahb told us, Al-Thiqa told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha that she used to interpret this verse, meaning His statement, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, and she would say: It is something that one of you swears by, intending nothing but the truth, but it is not what he swore by. Then he said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Ibn Abbas in one of his two opinions, and Sulayman bin Yasar and Sa’id bin Jubayr and Mujahid in one of his two opinions, and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i in one of his two opinions, and Al-Hasan and Zurarah bin Awfa and Abu Malik and Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Bakr bin Abdullah, and one of the two opinions of Ikrimah and Habib bin Abi Thabit and Al-Suddi and Makhul and Muqatil and Tawus and Qatadah and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and Yahya bin Sa’id and Rabi’ something similar to that. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi told us, Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Muradi told us, Awf al-A'rabi told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by some people who were shooting, meaning they were archery, and with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a man from his companions. A man from the people stood up and said: By God, you are right, and by God, you are wrong. The one who was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The man broke his oath, O Messenger of God. He said: No, the oaths of archers are futile, for which there is no expiation or punishment. This is a good mursal from al-Hasan. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Both statements were narrated from Aisha. Issam ibn Rawwad told us, Adam told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: It is his saying: No, by God, and yes, by God, and he thinks that he is telling the truth, but it is not so. Other statements - Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: It is a man who swears an oath about something and then forgets it. Zaid bin Aslam said: It is a man saying: May God blind my sight if I do not do such and such, or may God take away my wealth if I do not come to you tomorrow. This is what it is. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Musaddad bin Khalid told us, Khalid told us, Ata told us, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A vain oath is when you swear while you are angry. My father told me: Abu Al-Jamahir told us, Saeed bin Bashir told us, Abu Bishr told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A vain oath is when you forbid what God has made lawful for you. This is something for which there is no expiation. This is also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. Abu Dawud said Chapter on swearing in anger: Muhammad ibn al-Munhal told us, Yazid ibn Zurai’ told us, Habib al-Mu’allim told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab: There were two brothers from the Ansar between whom there was an inheritance, so one of them asked his companion about the division, so he said: If you ask me again about the division, then all of what I have is in the curtain of the Ka’bah, so ‘Umar said to him: The Ka’bah does not need your money, atone for your oath, and speak to your brother, for I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: There is no oath upon you, nor a vow to disobey the Lord Almighty, nor to sever family ties, nor about what you do not own. And His statement, But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned, Ibn ‘Abbas, Mujahid and more than one said: It means that one swears an oath about something while knowing that it is false. Mujahid and others said: It is like the statement of God, the Most High, But He will hold you accountable for what you have deliberated upon 1:10. And God is Forgiving and Forbearing, meaning He is Forgiving of His servants and Forbearing with them.
2:226: Ila' is an oath. If a man swears not to have intercourse with his wife for a period of time, it is either less than four months or more. If it is less, then he can wait for the period to end and then have intercourse with his wife. She must be patient and she does not have the right to demand a divorce from him during this period. This is as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore an oath from his wives for a month, and it was revealed at twenty-nine. He said that the month is twenty-nine, and they both have something similar on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab. However, if the period exceeds four months, then the wife has the right to demand a divorce from her husband when four months have passed, either he returns, i.e. has intercourse, or he divorces her, and the ruler forces him to do this. This is so that he does not harm her. For this reason, God the Almighty said: For those who swear an oath from their wives, i.e. they swear to abstain from intercourse with their wives. This indicates that Ila' is specific to wives and not female slaves, as is the view of the majority. A waiting period of four months, i.e. the husband waits four months from the time of the oath, then he stops and demands a divorce. Or divorce, and for this reason he said, If they return, meaning if they return to what they were doing, and it is a metaphor for intercourse. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Masruq, Al-Sha’bi, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and more than one, including Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. Then God is Forgiving and Merciful, because of the previous negligence in their rights due to the oath. His saying, Then God is Forgiving and Merciful, indicates one of the two opinions of the scholars, which is the old opinion from Al-Shafi’i that if the master returns after four months, there is no expiation upon him. This is supported by what was mentioned in the hadith in the verse before it from Amr ibn Shu’ayb from his father from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, then abandons it, its expiation is its expiation, as narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and Al-Tirmidhi. What the majority are upon, and what is new from the Shafi’i school of thought, is that he must expiate due to the generality of the obligation of expiation upon every swearer, as was also mentioned in the authentic hadiths, and God knows best. And his saying, And if they decide to divorce, indicates that divorce does not occur merely after the passage of four months, as the majority of later scholars say. Others have said that it occurs after the passage of four months as a divorce. This is narrated with authentic chains of transmission on the authority of Umar, Uthman, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, and Zaid bin Thabit. This is what Ibn Sirin, Masruq, Al-Qasim, Salim, Al-Hasan, Abu Salamah, Qatadah, Shuraih Al-Qadi, Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb, Ata’, Abu Salamah bin Abdul-Rahman, Sulayman bin Tarkhan Al-Taymi, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Al-Suddi say. Then it was said that she is divorced after the passage of four months as a revocable divorce. This was said by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Abu Bakr bin Abdul-Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham, Makhul, Rabi’ah, Al-Zuhri, and Marwan bin Al-Hakam. It was also said that she is divorced as an irrevocable divorce. This was narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Masoud, Uthman, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, and Zaid bin Thabit. This is what Ata’, Jabir bin Zaid, Masruq, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah, and Ibrahim say. And Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb, Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, and al-Hasan ibn Salih, so everyone who said: She is divorced after the passage of four months, obligated her to observe the waiting period, except what was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Sha’tha’: that if she menstruated three times, then there is no waiting period for her, and this is the opinion of al-Shafi’i, and what the majority of the later scholars are of the view is that he should be stopped and demanded either of this or that, and no divorce will occur upon her merely by its passage. Malik narrated from Nafi’ from Abdullah ibn Umar that he said: If a man swears to divorce his wife, no divorce will occur upon him even if four months have passed until he is stopped, and either he divorces her or he returns to her, and al-Bukhari included it. Ash-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah told us on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, who said: I met a dozen of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), all of whom would stop the mawla. Ash-Shafi’i said: The minimum was thirteen. Ash-Shafi’i narrated it on the authority of ‘Ali may God be pleased with him that he would stop the mawla. Then he said: And this is what we say, and it is in agreement with what we narrated on the authority of ‘Umar, Ibn ‘Umar, ‘A’ishah, ‘Uthman, Zayd ibn Thabit, and a dozen of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is what Ash-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him said. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, on the authority of ‘Ubayd God ibn ‘Umar, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, who said: I asked twelve men from the companions about a man who stops his wife, and all of them said: There is nothing on him until four months have passed, in which case he should stop the mawla. If he returns, then fine, otherwise he should divorce. Ad-Darqutni narrated it on the authority of Suhayl. I said It is narrated on the authority of Omar, Othman, Ali, Abu Darda, Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, Ibn Omar, and Ibn Abbas. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, Mujahid, Tawus, Muhammad bin Kaab, and Al-Qasim say the same. It is the school of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad bin Hanbal, and their companions, may God have mercy on them. It is also the choice of Ibn Jarir. It is the statement of Al-Layth, Ishaq bin Rahawayh, Abu Ubaid, Abu Thawr, and Dawud. All of these said: If he does not return, he is obligated to divorce her. If he does not divorce her, the judge divorces him. The divorce is revocable, and she has the right to take her back during the waiting period. Malik was the only one who said that he is not permitted to take her back until he has intercourse with her during the waiting period. This is very strange. The jurists and others have mentioned, regarding the reason for postponing the divorce by four months, the trace narrated by Imam Malik bin Anas, may God have mercy on him, in Al-Muwatta’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, who said: Omar bin Al-Khattab went out at night and heard a woman saying: This night has become long and dark, and I have no friend but him. By God, if it weren’t for God, I would have moved the sides of this bed. Omar asked his daughter Hafsa, may God be pleased with her: How long can a woman be patient without her husband? She said: Six months or four months. Omar said: I will not detain anyone from the armies for more than that. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Al-Sa’ib bin Jubair, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, who had met the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: I kept hearing the hadith of Omar that he went out one night to tour the city, and he used to do that a lot, when he passed by an Arab woman who had closed her door, and she was saying: This night has become long and I have visited its side, and I am kept awake by the fact that I have no companion but him. Oh, how he is, sometimes and sometimes, as if his eyebrows were a moon in the darkness of the night. He is pleased with him who plays near him, he is gentle in heart and not contained by his relatives By God, if it were not for God and nothing else, the sides of this bed would have been torn down. But I fear a guard assigned to our breaths, whose writer time never tires of writing. The fear of my Lord and shyness prevent me, and the honor of my husband prevents me from getting his ships Then he mentioned the rest of that, as mentioned above or something similar. This has been narrated through various chains of transmission and is one of the well-known hadiths.

By God, if it weren’t for God, I would have moved the sides of this bed. Omar asked his daughter Hafsa, may God be pleased with her: How long can a woman be patient without her husband? She said: Six months or four months. Omar said: I will not detain anyone from the armies for more than that. 2:228: This is an order from God, the Most High, to divorced women who have had intercourse with their husbands, to wait for three menstrual periods, meaning that one of them should remain after her husband divorces her for three menstrual periods, then marry if she wishes. The four imams excluded from this generality the female slave if she is divorced, for she has two waiting periods according to them because she is half that of a free woman, and the menstrual period cannot be divided, so a full menstrual period is completed for her. And because Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muzahir ibn Aslam al-Makhzumi al-Madani, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The divorce of a female slave is two divorces, and her waiting period is two menstrual periods. Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah. However, Muzahir’s statement is completely weak. Al-Hafiz al-Daraqutni and others said: The correct version is that it is from the statement of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad himself, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Atiyah al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Al-Daraqutni said: The correct version is what he narrated. Salem and Nafi` on the authority of Ibn `Umar said, and this is how it was narrated on the authority of `Umar ibn al-Khattab. They said: There was no known disagreement among the Companions, and some of the Salaf said: Rather, her waiting period is like the waiting period of a free woman due to the generality of the verse, and because this is an innate matter, so free women and slave women were the same in this. This statement was narrated by Sheikh Abu `Umar ibn `Abd al-Barr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin and some of the people of the apparent meaning and he weakened it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Yaman told us, Ismail told us, meaning Ibn `Ayyash, on the authority of `Amr ibn Muhajir, on the authority of his father, that Asma` bint Yazid ibn al-Sakn al-Ansariyyah said: I was divorced during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the divorced woman did not have a waiting period, so God, the Almighty, revealed when Asma` was divorced the waiting period for divorce, so from this perspective it was for her the waiting period for divorce, meaning and divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods, and this is a strange hadith from this perspective. The predecessors, successors and imams differed about what is meant by menses, and there are two opinions: [One of them] is that what is meant by them are purifications. Malik said in Al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha that Hafsa bint Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr passed away when she began bleeding from her third menses, so she mentioned that to Amra bint Abd al-Rahman, and she said: Urwah is right. Some people argued with her about that and said: God Almighty says in His Book three menstrual periods. Aisha said: You are right, and do you know what menses are? Rather, the menses are the pure ones. Malik said, on the authority of Ibn Shihab: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman say: I did not meet any of our jurists except that he said that, meaning the statement of Aisha. Malik said, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, that he used to say: If a man divorces his wife, and she begins to bleed from the third menses, then she is free from him and he is free from her. Malik said: This is the matter with us. And he narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas, Zaid ibn Thabit, Salim, al-Qasim, Urwah, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman, Aban ibn Uthman, Ata ibn Abi Rabah, Qatadah, al-Zuhri and the rest of the seven jurists. It is the school of Malik, al-Shafi’i and more than one, Dawud and Abu Thawr, and it is a narration from Ahmad. They used as evidence for it the words of God Almighty: Then divorce them during their waiting period, meaning during the periods of purity. And since the period of purity in which he divorces is considered, it indicates that it is one of the three menses that are commanded. For this reason, these people said: The woman in waiting period ends her waiting period and becomes separated from her husband by the onset of the third menses. The minimum period for which a dowry is given is: In it, the woman’s waiting period is thirty-two days and two moments, and Abu Ubaid and others cited as evidence for that the words of the poet, Al-A’sha: Every year you are a brave warrior, and your determination to conquer is tightened to its furthest point. A wealth inheritance, and originally a high status, because of the menstrual periods of your women that were lost in it He praises an Arab prince who preferred conquest to residence, until the days of purity were lost to his women, and he did not have intercourse with them. [The second opinion] - That what is meant by menstruation is menstruation, so the waiting period does not end until she is purified from the third menstruation. Others added: And she washes herself from it, and the shortest time in which a woman believes that her waiting period has ended is thirty-three days and a moment. Al-Thawri said: On the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said: We were with Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, when a woman came to him and said: My husband divorced me after one or two days, so he came to me and I had taken off my clothes and closed my door. Omar said to Abdullah bin Masoud: I see her as his wife before it is permissible for her to pray. He said: And I see that, and thus it was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, Omar, Othman, Ali, Abu Al-Darda, Ubadah bin Al-Samit, Anas bin Malik, Ibn Masoud, Muadh, Ubayy bin Kaab, Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Alqamah, Al-Aswad, Ibrahim, Mujahid, Ata’, Tawus, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, Muhammad bin Sirin, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Rabi’, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Al-Suddi, Makhul, Al-Dahhak, and Ata Al-Khurasani that they said: They said: Menses are menstruation. This is the view of Abu Hanifa and his companions, and the most correct of the two narrations from Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Al-Athram narrated from him that he said: The great companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Menses are menstruation. This is the view of Al-Thawri, Al-Awza’i, Ibn Abi Laila, Ibn Shubramah, Al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy, Abu Ubaid, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. This is supported by what came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Al-Mundhir ibn Al-Mughira on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr on the authority of Fatimah bint Abi Hubaish, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Leave prayer during your menstruation days. If this were correct, it would be clear that the menstruation is the menstruation. However, Abu Hatim said about this Al-Mundhir: He is unknown and not well-known. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. Ibn Jarir said: The origin of the term menses in the speech of the Arabs is the time for the coming of something that is usually at a known time, and for the passing of something that is usually at a known time. This expression requires that it be shared between both, and some of the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence have adopted this view, and God knows best. This is what Al-Asma'i said: The menstrual cycle is the time. Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala' said: The Arabs call menstruation a menstrual cycle, and they call purity a menstrual cycle, and they call purity and menstruation together a menstrual cycle. Sheikh Abu Omar ibn Abdul Barr said: The scholars of the Arabic language and the jurists do not differ that what is meant by the menstrual cycle is menstruation, and what is meant by purity is purity. They only differed about what is meant by the verse, which is in two opinions. - And his saying: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs meaning pregnancy or menstruation, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Dahhak and more than one. And his saying: If they believe in God and the Last Day is a threat to them for going against the truth. This indicates that the reference in this is to them because it is a matter that is only known from their side and it is often difficult to establish evidence for that, so the matter is returned to them and they are threatened in it so that they do not tell anything other than the truth, either because of their haste for the waiting period to end or their desire to prolong it for the purposes that she has in that, so she was commanded to tell the truth in that without adding or subtracting. - And his saying: And their husbands have more right to take them back in that case if they want reconciliation. That is, her husband who divorced her has more right to take her back, as long as she is in her waiting period, if his intention in taking her back is reconciliation and goodness. This is in the case of revocable divorces. As for the irrevocably divorced women, at the time of the revelation of this verse, they were not irrevocably divorced. Rather, that was because they restricted it to the three divorces. As for the time of the revelation of this verse, the man had more right to take back his wife even if he divorced her a hundred times. So when they restricted the verse after it to three divorces, people had irrevocably divorced women and those who were not irrevocably divorced. If you contemplate this, you will see the weakness of what some of the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence have taken in their citation of the issue of the pronoun returning, whether it is a specification of what preceded it from the wording of generality or not, with this noble verse, because the example of it does not match what they mentioned. And God knows best. - And his saying, And they have rights similar to those over them, according to what is equitable, meaning, they have rights over men like what men have over them, so each one of them should give the other what is due from him according to what is equitable, as was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Jabir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage, “So fear God with regard to women, for you have taken them as a trust from God and you have made their private parts lawful for you by the word of God. And you have rights over them that they should not let anyone you dislike share your bed. But if they do that, then beat them, but not severely. And they have their food and clothing according to what is equitable.” And in the hadith of Buhaiz bin Hakim on the authority of Muawiyah bin Haidah Al-Qushayri on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather, that he said: O Messenger of God, what is the right of the wife of one of us? He said: Feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike her in the face, do not insult her, and do not abandon her except in the house. And Wakee’ said, on the authority of Bashir ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I like to adorn myself for my wife just as I like my wife to adorn herself for me, because God says: And women have rights similar to those against them, according to what is equitable. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. And His statement: And men have a degree over them means in virtue in character, morals, status, obedience to commands, spending, taking care of interests, and virtue in this world and the hereafter, as God the Almighty said: Men are the maintainers and protectors of women, because God has given one more strength than the other and because they spend for maintenance from their wealth. And His saying, And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, meaning He is Exalted in His vengeance against those who disobey Him and violate His command, and Wise in His command, law, and decree.
2:229: This noble verse removes what was the case at the beginning of Islam, that the man had more right to take his wife back even if he divorced her a hundred times as long as she was in her waiting period. Since this was harmful to the wives, God limited them to three divorces, and permitted taking her back once or twice, and made it completely clear in the third, saying, Divorce is two times, then either keep her in an acceptable manner or release her with kindness. Abu Dawud, may God have mercy on him, said in his Sunan Chapter on the abrogation of taking her back after the three divorces. Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Marwazi told us, Ali bin al-Husayn bin Waqid told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “Divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods. It is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs,” the verse, and it indicates that if a man divorced his wife, he had more right to take her back even if he divorced her three times, but that was abrogated and he said, Divorce is twice, the verse, and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Zakariya bin Yahya on the authority of Ishaq bin Ibrahim on the authority of Ali bin al-Husayn on his authority, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun bin Ishaq told us, Abdah, meaning Ibn Sulayman, told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, that a man said to his wife, I will never divorce you and I will never take you in, she said, How is that? He said: I divorce you, and when your time comes, I will take you back. So she came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him, so God the Almighty revealed: Divorce is twice. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid and Ibn Idris, and Abd ibn Hamid narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Ja`far ibn `Awn, all of them on the authority of Hisham on the authority of his father, who said: A man had more right to take his wife back even if he divorced her as he wished as long as she was in her waiting period. And a man from the Ansar became angry with his wife and said: By God, I will not take you in or leave you. She said: How is that? He said: “I divorce you, and when your time comes, I will take you back. Then I divorce you, and when your time comes, I will take you back.” So she mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so God the Almighty revealed: Divorce is twice. He said: So the people faced divorce, those who had divorced and those who had not. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Sulayman on the authority of Ya`la bin Shabib, the freed slave of Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Aishah, and he mentioned it in a manner similar to what was mentioned above. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Ya`la bin Shabib, on his authority, then he narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Idris, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, in a mursal chain of transmission, and he said: This is more authentic. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Ya`qub bin Hamid bin Kasib, on the authority of Ya`la bin Shabib, on his authority, and he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic. Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Ismail ibn Abdullah told us, Muhammad ibn Hamid told us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: There was no time for divorce, where a man could divorce his wife and then take her back, as long as the waiting period had not expired. There was something between a man from the Ansar and his family that happened between people, so he said: By God, I will leave you, neither divorced nor married. So he kept divorcing her until the waiting period was about to end, then he took her back. He did that repeatedly, so God Almighty revealed about it: “Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.” So He set the time for divorce to be three, with no return after the third time until she marries another husband. And this is how it was narrated from Qatada, without a chain of transmission, as-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jarir mentioned it likewise, and he chose that this is the interpretation of this verse. And his saying, Either keep her in an acceptable manner or release her with kindness, meaning if you divorce her once or twice, then you have the choice as long as her waiting period remains, between returning her to you with the intention of reforming her and treating her well, or leaving her until her waiting period ends and then separating from you and releasing her, treating her well, without wronging her in any of her rights or harming her. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If a man divorces his wife twice, then let him fear God in that, meaning the third, so he should either keep her in an acceptable manner and treat her well, or release her with kindness and not wrong her in any of her rights. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, reciting, Ibn Wahb told us, Sufyan al-Thawri told me, Ismail ibn Sami’ told me, he said: I heard Abu Razin say: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of the statement of God, the Almighty, Either keep her in an acceptable manner or release her with kindness, where is the third? He said: Release with kindness. Abd bin Hamid narrated it in his interpretation, and its wording is: Yazid bin Abi Hakim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, that Abu Razin al-Asadi said: A man said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of God’s statement, Divorce is twice, so where is the third? He said: Release with kindness the third time. Imam Ahmad also narrated it. And thus it was narrated by Saeed bin Mansour on the authority of Khalid bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ismail bin Zakariya and Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee, on the authority of Abu Razin, on his authority. And thus it was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh also on the authority of Qais bin Ar-Rabi’ on the authority of Ismail bin Samee, on the authority of Abu Razin, on his authority, without a chain of transmission. And it was also narrated by Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it, then he said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Abdul Rahim told us, Ahmad bin Yahya told us, Ubaidullah bin Jarir bin Jabalah told us, Ibn Aishah told us, Hammad bin Salamah bin Qatada told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, God mentioned divorce twice, so where is the third? He said: Keeping her in kindness or releasing her with kindness. And His statement: And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them means it is not lawful for you to annoy them or make things difficult for them, so that they may ransom themselves from you with what you have given them of dowries or some of it, as God Almighty said: And do not prevent them in order to take away part of what you have given them unless they commit a clear immorality. As for if the woman gives him something willingly, God Almighty said: But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it in enjoyment and good health. As for if the spouses quarrel, and the woman does not fulfill the rights of the man and hates him and is unable to live with him, then she may ransom herself from him with what he has given her, and there is no blame on her for giving it to him, and there is no blame on him for accepting that from her. For this reason God Almighty said: “And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them unless they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God. But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, then there is no blame upon either of them for what she ransoms herself with” verse. As for if she has no excuse and she asks for ransom from him, Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, they both said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Thawban, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without a valid reason, the fragrance of Paradise will be forbidden to her. This is how it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abdul Wahhab bin Abdul Majeed Al-Thaqafi, and he said: Hasan: He said: It is narrated on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, and some of them narrated it on the authority of Ayoub with this chain of transmission and did not trace it back to the Prophet. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Rahman told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, and he mentioned Abu Asma’ and mentioned Thawban, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without a valid reason, the fragrance of Paradise will be forbidden to her. This is how it was narrated by Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Hammad bin Zaid. Another way - Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Layth bin Abi Idris, on the authority of Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without a valid reason, God will forbid her the scent of Paradise. And he said: Those who seek divorce by khul’ are hypocrites. Then Ibn Jarir and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it together, on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Muzahim bin Dawud bin Aliyah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Layth - he is Ibn Abi Sulaym - on the authority of Abu Al-Khattab, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who seek divorce by khul’ are hypocrites. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange from this aspect and its chain of transmission is not strong. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Ayoub told us, Hafs bin Bishr told us, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Suwar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Thabit bin Yazid, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The women who seek divorce and are forced to divorce are the hypocrites. It is strange from this perspective and weak. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Those who divorce themselves and those who have their hair removed are hypocrites. Another hadith - Ibn Majah said: Bakr bin Khalaf Abu Bishr told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ja`far bin Yahya bin Thauban, on the authority of his uncle `Amara bin Thauban, on the authority of `Ata`, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A woman should not ask her husband for divorce for no reason, lest she find the fragrance of Paradise, even though its fragrance can be detected from a distance of forty years. Then a large group of the Salaf and Imams of the Khalaf said: It is not permissible to divorce by khul’ unless the discord and rebellion are on the part of the woman, in which case it is permissible for the man to accept the ransom. They cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God. They said: So divorce by khul’ was not legislated except in this case, so it is not permissible in any other case except with evidence, and the basic principle is that it is not permissible. Among those who held this view are Ibn Abbas, Tawus, Ibrahim, Ata’, Al-Hasan and the majority, until Malik and Al-Awza’i said: If he takes something from her and it is harmful to her, it must be returned to her, and the divorce is revocable. Malik said: This is the matter that I found people doing. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, held that divorce by khul’ is permissible in the case of discord and upon agreement, by way of priority and more appropriate, and this is the view of all his companions as a whole. Sheikh Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr narrated in his book Al-Istidhkar on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Muzani that he held that divorce by khul’ was abrogated by His words: And if you have given one of them a great amount, do not take back anything from it. Ibn Jarir narrated it from him, and this is a weak statement and a source that is rejected by its speaker. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, mentioned that this verse was revealed regarding Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas and his wife Habeeba bint Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Let us mention the chains of transmission of her hadith and the differences in its wording. Imam Malik said in his Muwatta’, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Amra bint Abd al-Rahman ibn Saeed ibn Zararah: She told him on the authority of Habeeba bint Sahl al-Ansariyya, that she was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out for the dawn prayer and found Habeeba bint Sahl at his door in the early hours of the morning. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is this? She said: I am Habeeba bint Sahl. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: Neither I nor Thabit ibn Qays, her husband. When her husband Thabit ibn Qays came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: This is Habeeba bint Sahl, and she has mentioned what God willed her to mention. Habeeba said: O Messenger of God, everything that he gave me is with me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take from her. So he took from her and she stayed with her family. Thus, Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi on the authority of Malik with his chain of transmission similarly. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of al-Qa’nabi on the authority of Malik and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslimah on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim on the authority of Malik. Another hadith - On the authority of Aisha, Abu Dawud and Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Muammar told us, Abu Aamer told us, Amr al-Sadousi told us on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, “That Habibah bint Sahl was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and he beat her and some of her bones were broken. She came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the morning prayer and complained to him about him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Thabit and said: Take some of her wealth and leave her. He said: Is that right, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: I gave her two gardens as a dowry, so they are in her hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take them and leave her. So he did.” This is the wording of Ibn Jarir, and Abu Amr al-Sadousi is Saeed ibn Salamah ibn Abi al-Hussam. Another hadith in it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, Al-Bukhari said: Azhar bin Jameel told us, Abdul-Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, Khalid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “The wife of Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I do not find fault with him in his character or religion, but I hate disbelief in Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you return his garden to him? She said: Yes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Accept the garden and divorce her once.” And this is how Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Azhar bin Jameel with his chain of transmission similarly, and Al-Bukhari also narrated it on his authority, on the authority of Ishaq Al-Wasiti, on the authority of Khalid, who is Ibn Abdullah Al-Tahhan, on the authority of Khalid, who is Ibn Mihran Al-Hadha’a, on the authority of Ikrimah, with something similar. And this is how Al-Bukhari also narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and in some of them it is that she said: I cannot stand him, meaning out of hatred. This hadith is from the singularity of Al-Bukhari from this source. Then he said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah, that Jamilah, may God be pleased with her - thus he said - and it is well-known that her name was Habeebah as mentioned above, but Imam Abu Abdullah ibn Battah said: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Yusuf Al-Tabbakh told me, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ubayd God ibn Umar Al-Qawariri told us, Abdul A’la told me, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Jamilah bint Salul came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: By God, I do not blame Thabit ibn Qays for his religion or character, but I hate disbelief in Islam and I cannot stand it out of hatred. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Will you return his garden to him? She said: Yes, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered him to take what he had brought and not to increase it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Musa ibn Harun, who said: Azhar ibn Marwan told us, Abd al-A’la told us something similar. Ibn Majah narrated it in this way on the authority of Azhar ibn Marwan with a similar chain of transmission, and it is a good, straight chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya ibn Wadh told us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rabah, on the authority of Jamila bint Abdullah ibn Abi ibn Salul, that she was married to Thabit ibn Qays and rebelled against him, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent to her and said: O Jamila, what do you dislike about Thabit? She said: By God, I do not dislike his religion or his character, except that I dislike his ugliness. So he said to her: Will you return the garden to him? She said: Yes, so she returned the garden and they were separated. Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, al-Mu’tamar ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I read to Fadil on the authority of Abu Jarir that he asked Ikrimah: Did khul’ have a basis? He said: Ibn Abbas used to say: The first divorce in Islam was regarding the sister of Abdullah bin Ubayy. She came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, nothing will ever bring my head and his head together. I lifted the side of the tent and saw him approaching with a group of people. He was the blackest of them all, the shortest of them all, and the ugliest of them all. Her husband said: O Messenger of God, I have given her the best of my wealth, a garden for me. If she returns my garden to me, he said: What do you say? She said: Yes, and if he wants, I will give him more. He said: So he separated them. Another hadith - Ibn Majah said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: Habeeba bint Sahl was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and he was an ugly man. She said, O Messenger of God, by God, if it were not for the fear of God, whenever he comes to me I would spit in his face. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Will you return his garden to him? She said, Yes. So she returned his garden to him. He said, “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, separated them.” The Imams, may God have mercy on them, differed as to whether it is permissible for a man to ransom her with more than he gave her. The majority of scholars are of the view that this is permissible, based on the generality of the Almighty’s statement: There is no blame upon them for what she ransoms herself with. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Katheer, the freed slave of Ibn Samra, that Umar brought a rebellious woman, and he ordered her to go to Katheer’s house of dung. Then he called for her and said: How did you find her? She said: I have not found comfort since I was with him except this night that you kept me locked up. So he said to her husband: Take it off, even if it is just her earring. Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Katheer, the freed slave of Ibn Samra, and he mentioned something similar, and he added: He kept her locked up in it for three days. Saeed ibn Abi Arooba said on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman: A woman came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and complained about her husband, so he made her spend the night in the dung house. When morning came, he said to her: How did you find your place? She said: I have not been with him on a night that was more comforting to my eyes than this night. He said: Take even her turban. Al-Bukhari said: Uthman permitted khul’ without the turban of her head. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Aqil, that al-Rabi’ bint Mu’adh bin Afra’ told him, she said: I had a husband who would belittle me when he was present, and deprive me when he was away. She said: I made a mistake one day, so I said to him: I will divorce you with everything I own. He said: Yes. She said: So I did. She said: My uncle Mu’adh bin Afra’ took the dispute to Uthman bin Affan, and he permitted khul’ and ordered him to take the turban of my head or something less than it, or she said: something less than the turban of the head. The meaning of this is that it is permissible for him to take from her everything she has, little or much, and not leave her anything but the turban of her hair. Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb, al-Hasan bin Salih, and Uthman al-Batti say this. This is the view of Malik, al-Layth, al-Shafi’i, and Abu Thawr, and Ibn Jarir chose it. The companions of Abu Hanifa said: If there is harm From her side, it is permissible for him to take from her what he gave her, but it is not permissible to increase it. If he increases it, it is permissible in court. If the harm is on his part, it is not permissible for him to take anything from her. If he takes it, it is permissible in court. Imam Ahmad, Abu Ubaid, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: It is not permissible for him to take more than what he gave her. This is the opinion of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Ata’, Amr ibn Shu’ayb, al-Zuhri, Tawus, al-Hasan, al-Sha’bi, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. Muammar and al-Hakam said: Ali used to say: He should not take from the woman who has been divorced by khul’ more than what he gave her. Al-Awza’i said: The judges do not permit him to take from her more than what he gave her. I said: This statement is supported by what was mentioned previously from the narration of Qatada on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the story of Thabit bin Qais, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to take from her the garden and not to take more, and by what Abd bin Hamid narrated where he said: Qubaysah informed us on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked taking from her more than what he gave her, meaning the woman who had been divorced by khul’, and they interpreted the meaning of the verse to mean there is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with meaning from what he gave her, because of what he said before: “And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them unless they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God. But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, there is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with” meaning from that, and this is how Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas used to recite it: there is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with narrated by Ibn Jarir, for this reason he said after it: “These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of God - it is those who are the wrongdoers.” Chapter Al-Shafi’i said: Our companions differed regarding khul’. Sufyan informed us on the authority of Umar ibn Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding a man who divorced his wife twice and then she divorced him after that, he may marry her if he wishes, because God the Most High says: “Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. And it is not lawful for you to take back anything you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God. But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, there is no blame upon them for what she gives herself for ransom. These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of God - it is those who are the wrongdoers. * But if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him. But if he divorces her, then there is no blame upon them if they return to each other.” Al-Shafi’i said: Sufyan informed us on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Everything that money permits is not divorce. And other than Al-Shafi’i narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That Ibrahim ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Waqas asked him: A man divorced his wife twice, then she divorced him. Can he marry her? He said: Yes, Khul’ is not a divorce. God mentioned divorce at the beginning and end of the verse, and Khul’ is in between, so Khul’ is nothing. Then he recited, Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. And he recited, But if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband. This is what Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, went to, that Khul’ is not a divorce but rather annulment, is a narration from the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan and Ibn Umar, and it is the saying of Tawus and Ikrimah, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abu Thawr, and Dawud ibn Ali al-Zahiri say, and it is the old school of al-Shafi’i, and it is the apparent meaning of the noble verse. The second saying about Khul’ is that it is an irrevocable divorce unless he intends more than that. Malik said, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jahman, the freed slave of the Aslamis, on the authority of Umm Bakr al-Aslamiyyah: that she sought Khul’ from her husband, Abdullah Khalid ibn Asid, so they went to Uthman ibn Affan about that, and he said: It is a divorce unless it is…” If you name something, then it is what you name it. Al-Shafi’i said: I do not know of Jahman. Ahmad ibn Junbal also weakened this narration, and God knows best. Something similar to it has been narrated from Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, and Ibn Umar, and Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, Ata’, Shuraih, al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim, and Jabir ibn Zayd say the same. Malik, Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, Abu Uthman al-Batti, and al-Shafi’i in al-Jadid agreed with it. However, the Hanafis hold that whenever the divorcee intends one or two divorces, or issues one divorce, then it is one irrevocable divorce. If he intends three, then it is three. Al-Shafi’i has another opinion regarding khul’, which is that whenever it is not done with the wording of divorce and is devoid of evidence, then it is nothing at all. Question Malik, Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Ishaq bin Rahawayh in a narration from them, which is the well-known one, said that the waiting period of a woman who has been divorced by khul’ is the same as that of a woman who has been divorced by khul’, which is three menstrual cycles, if she is one of those who menstruate. This was narrated from ‘Umar, ‘Ali and Ibn ‘Umar, and Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab, Sulayman bin Yasar, ‘Urwah, Salim, Abu Salamah, ‘Umar bin ‘Abd Al-‘Aziz, Ibn Shihab, Al-Hasan, Al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Abu ‘Iyadh, Khulas bin ‘Umar, Qatadah, Sufyan Al-Thawri, Al-Awza’i, Al-Layth bin Sa’d and Abu Al-‘Ubaid said the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is the opinion of most of the scholars among the Companions and others, and their basis for this is that khul’ is a divorce, so she must observe the waiting period like all other divorced women. The second opinion is that she must observe one menstrual cycle to purify her womb. Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Yahya bin Sa’id narrated to us from Nafi’ from Ibn ‘Umar: Al-Rabi’ divorced her husband by khul’, so her uncle ‘Uthman may God be pleased with him came and said: She must observe the waiting period of one menstrual cycle. He said: Ibn Omar used to say: She waits for three menstrual periods, until Uthman said this, and Ibn Omar used to issue fatwas based on it, and he used to say: Uthman is the best and most knowledgeable of us. And Abdah told us on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: The waiting period for a woman who has been divorced by khul’ is one menstrual period. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Her waiting period is one menstrual period. This is what Ikrimah, Aban ibn Uthman, and everyone mentioned above who says that khul’ is annulment are obligated to say this. They provided evidence for this with what Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated, where he said: Each of them: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Baghdadi told us, Ali ibn Bahr told us, Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Amr ibn Muslim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the wife of Thabit ibn Qays divorced her husband during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her to observe a waiting period of one menstrual period. Then al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan ghareeb. Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Amr ibn Muslim, on the authority of Ikrimah, as a mursal. Another hadith - Al-Tirmidhi said: Mahmoud bin Ghailan told us, Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Muhammad bin Abd al-Rahman told us, and he is a client of the family of Talhah, on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bint Mu’adh bin Afra’, that she divorced her husband by khul’ during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her, or she was ordered, to observe a waiting period of one menstrual cycle. Al-Tirmidhi said: The correct version is that she was ordered to observe a waiting period of one menstrual cycle. Another path - Ibn Majah said: Ali bin Salamah Al-Naysaburi told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim bin Saad told us, my father told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Ubadah bin Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin Al-Samit told me on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bint Mu’adh bin Afra, he said: I said to her: Tell me your story, she said: I divorced my husband by khul’, then I came to Uthman and asked Uthman: What is my waiting period? He said: There is no waiting period for you unless you have recently been divorced, then you stay with him until you menstruate once, she said: In that, he followed the ruling of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the case of Maryam Al-Mughaliyah, who was married to Thabit bin Qays, so she divorced him by khul’. Ibn Lahi’ah narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Salamah and Muhammad bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Thauban on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bint Mu’adh, she said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) order the wife of Thabit bin Qays when she divorced him by khul’ to observe a waiting period of one menstrual period. Question The one who divorces her by khul’ does not have the right to return to the woman who was divorced by khul’ during the waiting period without her consent, according to the four imams and the majority of scholars, because she has taken possession of herself because of what she gave him. It was narrated from Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, Mahan al-Hanafi, Saeed bin al-Musayyab, and al-Zuhri that they said: If he returns to her what he gave her, he is permitted to return to her during the waiting period without her consent, and this is the choice of Abu Thawr, may God have mercy on him. Sufyan al-Thawri said: If the divorce is without the word of divorce, then it is a separation and he has no right over her, and if it is called a divorce, then he has the right to return to her as long as she is in the waiting period, and Dawud bin Ali al-Dhahiri says the same, and everyone agreed that the one who divorces her by khul’ can marry her during the waiting period, and Sheikh Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr narrated from a group: That it is not permissible for him to do so, just as it is not permissible for anyone else, and this is an odd and rejected statement. Question Is he allowed to pronounce another divorce on her during the waiting period? There are three opinions of scholars: One He is not allowed to do so, because she has become his wife and has separated from him. This is what Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Ikrimah, Jabir ibn Zayd, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and Abu Thawr say. The second Malik said: If the khul’ is followed by a divorce without them remaining silent, it is valid. If they remain silent, it is not valid. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: This is similar to what was narrated from Uthman, may God be pleased with him. The third He is allowed to divorce her in any case as long as she is in the waiting period. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri, and al-Awza’i. This is what Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, Shuraih, Tawus, Ibrahim, al-Zuhri, al-Hakim, al-Hakam, and Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman say. This was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud and Abu al-Darda’. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: This is not proven from them. And His statement, “These are the limits set by God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of God - it is those who are the wrongdoers,” meaning that these are the laws that He has legislated for you. They are His limits, so do not transgress them, as is proven in the authentic hadith, “God has set limits, so do not transgress them. He has imposed obligations, so do not neglect them. He has forbidden prohibitions, so do not violate them. He has remained silent about things out of mercy for you, not out of forgetfulness, so do not ask about them.” This verse may be used as evidence by those who believe that combining three divorces with one word is forbidden, as is the doctrine of the Malikis and those who agree with them. Rather, the Sunnah according to them is to pronounce one divorce, based on the statement, Divorce is twice. Then he said, “These are the limits set by God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of God - it is those who are the wrongdoers.” They support this with the hadith of Mahmud ibn Labid, which was narrated by al-Nasa’i in his Sunan, where he said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Mukhramah ibn Bakir, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed about a man who divorced his wife three times at once, so he stood up angrily and said, Is he playing with the Book of God while I am among you? Until a man stood up and said, O Messenger of God, should I not kill him? - there is an interruption in it.
2:230: And the Almighty’s saying: But if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband, meaning that if a man divorces his wife with a third divorce after he has issued divorce twice, then she is forbidden to him until she marries another husband, meaning until another husband has intercourse with her in a valid marriage. So if he has intercourse with her outside of marriage, even if he is in the possession of the right hand, she is not lawful to the first, because he is not a husband. Likewise, if she marries but the husband does not consummate the marriage with her, she is not lawful to the first. It is well-known among many jurists that Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, may God have mercy on him, said: The purpose of making her lawful to the first is achieved merely by the contract with the second, and there is doubt about its authenticity from him, although Sheikh Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr narrated it from him in Al-Istidhkar, and God knows best. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, on the authority of Salim ibn Razin, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn `Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a man who marries a woman and then divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, and another husband marries her and divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, can she return to the first one? He said, No, until she tastes his honey and he tastes her honey. This is how it appears in the narration of Ibn Jarir. Imam Ahmad narrated it and said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, who said: I heard Salim ibn Razin narrating on the authority of Salim ibn `Abdullah, meaning Ibn `Umar, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn `Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a man who has a wife and divorces her, then a man marries her and divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, so she returns to her first husband. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Until she tastes the honey. This is how it was narrated by al-Nasa’i on the authority of `Amr ibn `Ali al-Fallas and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar Bandar, both of them on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja`far Ghandar, on the authority of Shu`bah, on his authority. This is also from the narration of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab on the authority of Ibn `Amr, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, contrary to what is reported from him. So it is unlikely that it would contradict what he narrated without a basis, and God knows best. Ahmad, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Jarir also narrated this hadith on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Razin ibn Sulayman al-Ahmadi, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who divorces his wife three times, then another man marries her, closes the door, lowers the curtain, then divorces her before consummating the marriage with her. Is she permissible for the first wife? He said: No, until she tastes the honey. This is the wording of Ahmad, and in a narration by Ahmad it is Sulayman ibn Razin. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Muhammad ibn Dinar told us, Yahya ibn Yazid al-Hana’i told us on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who had a wife and he divorced her three times, and she married a man after him and he divorced her before consummating the marriage with her, is she permissible for her first husband? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, until the other has tasted her honey and she has tasted his honey. And this is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Anmati on the authority of Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, Muhammad ibn Dinar told us, and he mentioned it I said and Muhammad ibn Dinar ibn Sandal Abu Bakr al-Azdi then al-Tahi al-Basri and he is called Ibn Abi al-Furat, they differed about him, some of them weakened him, and some of them strengthened him and accepted him and deemed him good, and Abu Dawud mentioned that it was before his death, and God knows best. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Ayyas al-Asqalani told us, my father told us, Shaiban told us, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of Abi al-Harith al-Ghifari, on the authority of Abi Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, regarding a woman whose husband divorces her three times, then she marries someone else, and he divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, and the first one wants to take her back. He said, No, until the other one tastes her honey. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Shaiban, who is Ibn Abd al-Rahman, with it - and Abi al-Harith is not well-known. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Yahya told us, on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha: A man divorced his wife three times, so she married another husband, but he divorced her before he had intercourse with her. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Is she permissible for the first wife? He said: No, until he tastes her honey as the first wife tasted. Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Al-Nasa’i through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar Al-Umari, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr, on the authority of his aunt Aisha, on his authority. Another way - Ibn Jarir said: Ubayd God ibn Ismail al-Habbari, Sufyan ibn Wakee’ and Abu Hisham al-Rafa’i told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who divorced his wife, and she married another man, and he consummated the marriage with her, then he divorced her before having intercourse with her. Is she permissible for her first husband? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: She is not permissible for her first husband until the other tastes her honey and she tastes his honey. Abu Dawud narrated it likewise on the authority of Musaddad and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Abu Kurayb, both of them on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, who is Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Dharee’, with it. Another way - Muslim said in his Sahih: Muhammad bin Al-Ala Al-Hamadani told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a woman whom a man marries and then divorces, and she marries a man who divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, is she permissible for her first husband? He said, Not until he tastes its honey. Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Fadil told us, Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, all of them on the authority of Hisham with this chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah Muhammad ibn Hazim on the authority of Hisham with it, and Muslim was the only one to narrate it from the other two chains of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated it in this way on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aishah, with a similar or similar chain of transmission. This is a good chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir also narrated it on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud’an on the authority of his father’s wife Amina Umm Muhammad, on the authority of Aishah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a similar chain of transmission. This chain of transmission is an abridged version of the hadith narrated by al-Bukhari. Amr ibn Ali told us, Yahya told us on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, my father told me on the authority of Aishah, with a similar chain of transmission on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Abdah told us on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that Rifa’ah al-Qurazi married a woman and then divorced her. She came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him that he did not come to her and that he had nothing with him except the hem of a garment. He said, Not until you taste his honey and he tastes your honey. This is the only one to narrate it from this source. Another way - Imam Ahmad said: Abdul-A’la told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, she said: The wife of Rifa’ah Al-Qurazi entered while Abu Bakr and I were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: Rifa’ah divorced me irrevocably, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Zubayr married me, and he only has something like a fringe, and she took a fringe from her robe, and Khalid bin Saeed bin Al-Aas was at the door and he was not given permission, so he said: O Abu Bakr, will you not forbid this woman from what she says loudly in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not do more than smile, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is as if you want to go back to Rifa’ah, not until you taste his honey and he tastes your honey. And this is how Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, and Muslim from the hadith of Abd Al-Razzaq, and Al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Yazid bin Zari’, all three of them from Muammar with it, and in the hadith of Abd Al-Razzaq with Muslim, that Rifa’ah divorced her the last of three. Divorces. It was narrated by all except Abu Dawud on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, al-Bukhari on the authority of Aqil, Muslim on the authority of Yunus ibn Yazid, and he has the last three divorces. Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Ayoub ibn Musa, and Salih ibn Abi al-Akhdar narrated it, all of them on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha on his authority. Malik said, on the authority of Al-Miswar bin Rifa’ah Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Az-Zubayr bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Az-Zubayr: Rifa’ah bin Samwal divorced his wife Tamimah bint Wahb three times during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She married Abd Al-Rahman bin Az-Zubayr, but he objected to her and could not touch her, so he separated from her. Rifa’ah bin Samwal wanted to marry her, and he was her first husband who had divorced her.
