He mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he forbade him from marrying her, and said, She is not lawful for you until you taste the honey. This is how the authors of Al-Muwatta’ narrated it on the authority of Malik, and there is an interruption in it. Ibrahim bin Tahman and Abdullah bin Wahb narrated it on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Rifa’ah, on the authority of Az-Zubayr bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Az-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, and he connected it. Chapter What is meant by the second husband is that he desires the woman, intending to continue living with her, as is permissible in marriage. Imam Malik stipulated, however, that the second husband should have intercourse with her in a permissible manner. If he has intercourse with her while she is in a state of ihram, fasting, or in seclusion, or menstruating, or in postpartum bleeding, or the husband is fasting, in a state of ihram, or in seclusion, she is not permissible for the first husband by this intercourse. Likewise, if the second husband is a dhimmi, she is not permissible for the Muslim by his marriage, because the marriages of infidels are invalid in his view. Al-Hasan al-Basri stipulated, as narrated by Sheikh Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr, that the second husband should ejaculate, as if he adhered to what he understood from his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, until you taste his honey and he tastes your honey. This necessitates that the woman also ejaculates. What is meant by honey is not semen, because Imam Ahmad and al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Behold, honey is intercourse. But if the second husband only intended to make her permissible for the first husband, then this is the one who makes the second husband permissible. The hadiths have been narrated about him denouncing and cursing him, and whenever he states his intention in the contract, the marriage is invalid according to the majority of imams. Mentioning the hadiths mentioned in this regard The first hadith On the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Qais, on the authority of Al-Huzayl, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed: the tattooer and the one who gets tattooed, the hair extensions and the one who gets extensions, the one who allows someone to do something for him and the one for whom he allows it, the one who consumes usury and the one who pays it.” Then Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it through different chains of transmission on the authority of Sufyan, who is Al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Qais, whose name is Abd Al-Rahman ibn Tharwan Al-Awdi, on the authority of Hazil ibn Shurahbil Al-Awdi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with it. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. He said: This is what the scholars of knowledge among the Companions, including Umar, Uthman and Ibn Umar, acted upon, and it is the opinion of the jurists among the Followers, and it is narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas. Another way On the authority of Ibn Masoud. Imam Ahmad said: Zakariya bin Adi told us, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Abu al-Wasil, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God has cursed the one who performs tahlil and the one for whom it is performed. Another way - Imam Ahmad and Al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah on the authority of Al-Harith Al-A’war on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The one who consumes usury, the one who pays it, its two witnesses, and its scribe if they know about it, the one who connects and the one who receives it, the one who withholds charity and the one who transgresses in it, the one who turns back on his heels as an Arab after his migration, the one who permits something and the one for whom it is permitted, are cursed by the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of Resurrection. The second hadith On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who consumes usury, the one who pays it, the two who witness it, the one who writes it down, the tattoo artist and the one who gets tattooed for beauty, the one who withholds charity, the one who permits it and the one for whom it is permitted. He used to forbid wailing.” And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Jabir, who is Ibn Yazid Al-Ju’fi, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, and this is how it was narrated from the hadith of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, Husayn bin Abdul Rahman, Mujalid bin Sa’id, and Ibn Awn, on the authority of Amir Al-Sha’bi, on this authority. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Al-Sha’bi, on this authority. Then Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Abdullah told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who practices usury, the one who consumes it, the one who writes it down, the one who witnesses it, the one who permits it and the one for whom it is permitted. The third hadith On the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him. Al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Ash’ath bin Abdul Rahman bin Yazid Al-Ayami told us, Mujalid told us on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, and on the authority of Al-Harith on the authority of Ali: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who performs tahlil and the one for whom it is performed.” Then he said: Its chain of transmission is not reliable. Mujalid was declared weak by more than one of the people of knowledge, including Ahmad bin Hanbal, who said: It was narrated by Ibn Numayr on the authority of Mujalid on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah on the authority of Ali, who said: This is a mistake on the part of Ibn Numayr, and the first hadith is more authentic. Hadith 4 On the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, may God be pleased with him. Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said, Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih al-Masri told us, my father told us, I heard al-Layth ibn Sa`d say: Abu al-Mus`ab Musharrah, who is Ibn Ha`an, said, Uqbah ibn Amir, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Shall I not tell you about the borrowed billy goat? They said, “Yes, O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” He said, It is the one who allows a divorce, may God curse the one who allows a divorce and the one for whom it is allowed. Ibn Majah is the only one to narrate it. This is how Ibrahim ibn Ya`qub al-Jawzjani narrated it on the authority of Uthman ibn Salih on the authority of al-Layth, then he said: They strongly objected to Uthman in this hadith. I said This Uthman is one of the trustworthy narrators. Al-Bukhari narrated it on his authority in his Sahih, then others followed him, so Ja`far al-Firyabi narrated it on the authority of al-`Abbas, known as Ibn Fariq, on the authority of Abu Salih Abdullah ibn Salih, on the authority of al-Layth, so he was absolved of responsibility, and God knows best. Hadith Five On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Ibn Majah said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Amer told us, on the authority of Zama’ah bin Salih, on the authority of Salamah bin Wahram, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who performs tahlil and the one for whom it is performed. Another way - Imam Al-Hafiz, the preacher of Damascus, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Yaqub Al-Jawzjani Al-Saadi said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Ibrahim bin Ismail bin Abi Hanifa told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Al-Hussain, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the marriage of a muhallil, and he said: No, except a marriage of desire, not a marriage of deception, nor mockery of the Book of God, then he tastes its honey. These two chains of transmission are strengthened by what Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Hamid on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman on the authority of Musa bin Abi Al-Furat on the authority of Amr bin Dinar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. So both this mursal and the one before it are strengthened by the other, and God knows best. The sixth hadith On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir told us, Abdullah, who is Ibn Jaafar, told us, on the authority of Uthman Ibn Muhammad Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who performs the tahlil and the one for whom the tahlil is performed. This is how Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Jawzjani, Al-Bayhaqi narrated it on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Jaafar Al-Qurashi, and Ahmad Ibn Hanbal, Ali Ibn Al-Madini, Yahya Ibn Ma’in, and others authenticated him. Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Uthman Ibn Muhammad Al-Akhnasi, who authenticated Ibn Ma’in on the authority of Sa’id Al-Maqburi, and it is agreed upon. The seventh hadith On the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both. Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sagani told us, Saeed ibn Abi Maryam told us, Abu Yaman Muhammad ibn Mutraf al-Madani told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Nafi’, on the authority of his father, that he said: A man came to Ibn Umar and asked him about a man who divorced his wife three times, and his brother married her without any conspiracy on his part to make her permissible for his brother. Is she permissible for the first wife? He said: No, except for a marriage of desire. We used to consider this as fornication during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he said: This is a hadith with a sound chain of transmission, and they did not include it. Al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Nafi’ on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Umar. This wording indicates that it is a marfu’ religious marriage. This is how Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, Al-Jawzjani, Harb Al-Kirmani, and Abu Bakr Al-Athram narrated from the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’ on the authority of Qubaysah bin Jabir, on the authority of Umar, that he said: No one who is to be permitted to marry a woman or for whom a marriage is permitted is brought to me except that I stone them both. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Ibn Lahi’ah on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Ashja’ on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar, that a man was brought to Uthman bin Affan who had married a woman in order to make her permissible for her husband, so he separated them. This was also narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Abbas, and more than one of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. And His statement, But if he divorces her, meaning the second husband after consummating the marriage with her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other, meaning the woman and the first husband, if they think they can keep within the limits of God, meaning they live together in kindness. Mujahid said, “if they think that their marriage was not based on deception. “And these are the limits of God,” meaning His laws and rulings, He makes them clear, meaning He explains them, for a people who know. The Imams, may God have mercy on them, differed as to whether a man divorced his wife once or twice and left her until her waiting period had ended, then she married another man, and he had intercourse with her and then divorced her and her waiting period had ended, then the first man married her. Should she return to him with what remained of the three divorces, as is the view of Malik, al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and it is the view of a group of the Companions, may God be pleased with them? Or the second husband may have cancelled what came before him of the divorce, so if she returns to the first man, she returns with the total of the three divorces, as is the view of Abu Hanifa and his companions, may God have mercy on them. Their argument is that if the second husband cancelled the three divorces, then he should cancel what remained of them by way of priority and necessity, and God knows best.
2:231: This is an order from God, the Almighty, to men, if one of them divorces a woman with a divorce in which he has the right to take her back, that he should treat her well when her waiting period has ended, and there is nothing left of her except an amount in which he can take her back, so he can either keep her, that is, return her to the protection of his marriage, with kindness, which is that he witnesses her return, and intends to treat her with kindness, or release her, that is, leave her until her waiting period has ended and send her out of his house in a way that is better, without discord, quarreling, or slander. God, the Almighty, said: And do not keep them, to cause them harm, in order to aggravate their condition. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Masruq, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi', Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and more than one said: A man would divorce a woman, and when her waiting period was about to end, he would take her back, to cause her harm, so that she would not go to someone else, then he would divorce her so that she would observe her waiting period, and when her waiting period was about to end, he would divorce her so that her waiting period would be prolonged, so God forbade them from doing that. He threatened them with it, saying: And whoever does that has wronged himself, meaning by disobeying the command of God Almighty. And the Almighty said: And do not take the verses of God in jest. Ibn Jarir said regarding this verse: Abu Kurayb told us, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, on the authority of Abd al-Salam bin Harb, on the authority of Yazid bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu al-Ala al-Awdi, on the authority of Hamid bin al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Musa, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry with the Ash’aris, so Abu Musa came to him and said: O Messenger of God, are you angry with the Ash’aris? He said: “One of you says, ‘I have divorced you, I have taken you back.’ This is not the divorce of the Muslims. Divorce the woman before her waiting period.” Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Khalid al-Dallal, who is Yazid bin Abd al-Rahman, and there is some discussion about him. Masruq said: He is the one who divorces without meaning to, and harms his wife by divorcing her and taking her back so that her waiting period is prolonged. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ata’ al-Khurasani, al-Rabi’ and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He is the man who divorces and says: I was joking, or frees or marries and says: I was joking, so God revealed: And do not take the verses of God in jest, and God obligated him to do that. Ibn Mardawayh said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad told us, Abu Ahmad al-Sayrafi told us, Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sammar told me, on the authority of Ismail ibn Yahya, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man divorced his wife while he was joking, not intending divorce, so God revealed: And do not take the verses of God in jest, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, obligated him to divorce her. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Issam bin Rawad told us, Adam told us, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who is Al-Basri, who said: A man would divorce and say: I was joking, and he would free and say: I was joking, and he would marry and say: I was joking. Then God revealed: And do not take the verses of God in jest, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever divorces or frees or marries or is given in marriage in marriage, seriously or in jest, it is permissible for him. And Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sulayman bin Arqam, on the authority of Al-Hasan, similarly, and this is a mursal. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, on the authority of Amr bin Ubayd, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, with a chain of transmission ending with him. He also said: Ahmad bin Al-Hasan bin Ayoub told us, Yaqub bin Abi Yaqub told us, Yahya bin Abdul Hamid told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Salamah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And do not take the verses of God in jest. He said: During the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a man would say to another man: I have married you to my daughter, then he would say: I was joking, and he would say: I have been freed, and he would say: I was joking. Then God revealed: And do not take the verses of God in jest. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Three things, if said in jest or not, are valid for him: divorce, freeing a woman, and marriage.” The well-known hadith in this hadith, which was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib ibn Idrak, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Mahak, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Three things, if said in earnest, are serious and if said in jest, are serious: marriage, divorce, and taking a woman back.” Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. And His statement, And remember the favor of God upon you, meaning in His sending the Messenger with guidance and clear proofs to you, and what He has revealed to you of the Book and wisdom, meaning the Sunnah, advising you thereby, meaning commanding you, forbidding you, and threatening you for committing forbidden acts, and fear God, meaning in what you do and what you leave, and know that God is Knowing of all things, meaning nothing of your secret or public affairs is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for that.
2:232: Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This verse was revealed about a man who divorces his wife once or twice, and her waiting period ends, then he decides to marry her and take her back, and the woman wants that but her guardians prevent her from doing so, so God forbade them from preventing her. And Al-Awfi narrated the same from him on the authority of Ibn Abbas as well, and Masruq, Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i, Al-Zuhri and Al-Dahhak also said: It was revealed about that, and what they said is apparent from the verse, and it indicates that a woman does not have the right to marry herself, and that marriage requires a guardian, as Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir said regarding this verse, as it came in the hadith: A woman does not marry a woman, and a woman does not marry herself, for the adulteress is the one who marries herself. And in another narration: There is no marriage except with a sane guardian and two just witnesses. And there is a dispute among the scholars on this issue, which is explained in its place in the books of branches, and we have established that in the book of rulings, and praise and thanks be to God. It was narrated that this verse was revealed about Muqal ibn Yasar Al-Muzani and his sister. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said in his Sahih book when interpreting this verse: Ubaydullah ibn Saeed told us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi told us, Abbad ibn Rashid told us, Al-Hasan told us, he said: Muqal ibn Yasar told me, he said: I had a sister who was proposed to me. Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim said on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, Muqal ibn Yasar told me, and Abu Muammar told us, and Abdul Warith told us, Yunus told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, that the husband of Muqal ibn Yasar divorced her sister, so he left her until her waiting period ended and proposed to her, but Muqal refused, so the verse was revealed: So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands and this is how Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Muqal ibn Yasar, and Al-Tirmidhi also authenticated it, and its wording is on the authority of Muqal ibn Yasar, that he married his sister to a Muslim man, during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he handed her over to him and she remained with him as she was, then he divorced her once and did not take her back until her waiting period was over, so he loved her and she loved him, then he proposed to her while the suitor was with her, and he said to him: O son of a son of a son of a son! I honored you with her and married you to her, so you divorced her, and by God she will never return to you, the last thing you have to do. He said: So God knew his need for her and her need for her husband, so God revealed: {And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term} until His saying: {and you do not know}. When Muqal heard it, he said: I hear and obey my Lord, then he called him and said: I marry you to her and honor you. Ibn Mardawayh added: And I have atoned for my oath. Ibn Jarir narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: She is Jamal bint Yasar, who was married to Abu al-Badah. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i, who said: She is Fatima bint Yasar. And more than one of the predecessors mentioned this way, that this verse was revealed about Muqal bin Yasar and his sister. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Jabir bin Abdullah and his cousin, but the first is correct, and God knows best. And His statement, This is admonished for whoever among you believes in God and the Last Day, meaning, this which We have forbidden you from preventing female guardians from marrying their husbands if they agree among themselves on what is good, he should follow it, be admonished by it, and be affected by it. Whoever among you, O people, believes in God and the Last Day, meaning, believes in God’s law, and fears God’s threat and punishment in the Hereafter, and the reward therein, that is purer for you and cleaner, meaning, following God’s law in returning female guardians to their husbands, and abandoning zeal in that is purer for you and cleaner for your hearts. And God knows, meaning of the interests, in what He commands and forbids, while you do not know, meaning, the best in what you do, nor in what you leave.
2:233: This is guidance from God Almighty to mothers to breastfeed their children completely, which is two years, and breastfeeding after that is not considered. That is why He said, For whoever wants to complete breastfeeding. Most of the imams have said that breastfeeding does not prohibit anything except what is less than two years old. So if the newborn breastfeeds and is older than that, he is not prohibited. Al-Tirmidhi said: (Chapter: What came that breastfeeding does not prohibit except in infancy and before two years) Qutaybah told us, Abu Awanah told us on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, on the authority of Umm Salamah, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Nothing prohibits from breastfeeding except what opens the intestines in the breast and was before weaning. This is a good and authentic hadith, and the practice is based on this according to most of the people of knowledge from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others, that breastfeeding does not prohibit except what was before two years, and what was after two complete years, then it does not prohibit anything, and Fatimah bint al-Mundhir bin al-Zubayr bin al-Awwam, and she is the wife of Hisham bin Urwah. I said Al-Tirmidhi was the only one to narrate this hadith and its narrators meet the conditions of the two Sahihs. The meaning of his saying except what was in the breast is in the places of breastfeeding before the two years, as came in the hadith narrated by Ahmad on the authority of Wakee’ and Ghandar on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: When Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, he said: My son died in the breast, he has a wet nurse in Paradise. Al-Bukhari narrated it in this way from the hadith of Shu’bah. He, peace be upon him, only said that because his son Ibrahim, peace be upon him, died when he was one year and ten months old, so he said: He has a wet nurse, meaning she completed his breastfeeding. This is supported by what Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Al-Haytham bin Jameel on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Nothing is forbidden by breastfeeding except what was in the two years. Then he said: And no one narrated it on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah except Al-Haytham bin Jameel, and he is a trustworthy hafiz. I said Imam Malik narrated it in Al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Al-Darawardi narrated it on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he added, And whatever is after two years is nothing. This is more authentic. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no breastfeeding after weaning, and no orphanhood after puberty. The full evidence of this hadith is in the words of God the Almighty: “And his weaning is in two years. So be grateful to Me.” And He said: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months. The statement that breastfeeding does not make a child forbidden after two years is narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, Jabir, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Umar, Umm Salamah, Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Ata’ and the majority. It is the view of al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, al-Thawri, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad and Malik in one narration. It was narrated on his authority that its duration is two years and two months, and in another narration: and three months. Abu Hanifa said: two years and six months. And Zafar ibn al-Hudhayl said: As long as he is breastfeeding, then until three years. This is a narration from al-Awza’i. Malik said: If the boy is weaned before two years, and a woman breastfeeds him after he is weaned, he is not forbidden because he has become like food. This is a narration from al-Awza’i. It has been narrated from ‘Umar and ‘Ali that they said: There is no breastfeeding after weaning. It is possible that they meant two years, like the majority of scholars say: Whether he is weaned or not. It is possible that they meant the action, like the statement of Malik, and God knows best. It has been narrated in the two Sahihs from ‘Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she saw that breastfeeding by an adult has an effect on the prohibition. This is the statement of ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah and al-Layth ibn Sa’d. ‘Aisha used to order whomever she chose to enter upon her from among the men for some of her wives, so she would breastfeed him. She used as evidence for that the hadith of Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhaifah, where the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the wife of Abu Hudhaifah to breastfeed him and he was an adult, so he would enter upon her with that breastfeeding. The rest of the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused that, and they saw that as one of the special characteristics. This is the statement of the majority of scholars. The argument of the majority, who are the four imams, the seven jurists, the great companions, and all the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except for Aisha, is what was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Look at your brothers, for breastfeeding is only for famine. We will discuss the issues of breastfeeding and what is related to breastfeeding an adult, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And your mothers who breastfed you. And His statement: And the father of the child shall bear the cost of their food and clothing according to what is acceptable, meaning, the father of the child shall bear the cost of the mothers and their clothing according to what is acceptable, that is, according to what is customary among their peers in their country, without extravagance or stinginess, according to his ability in terms of wealth, moderation, or stinginess, as God Almighty said: “Let one with an abundance spend according to his abundance, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend according to what God has given him. God does not charge a soul except [according to] what He has given it. God will grant, after hardship, ease.” Ad-Dahhak said: If a man divorces his wife and has a child from her, and she breastfeeds his child for him, then the father must bear her cost and clothing according to what is acceptable. And his saying: A mother shall not be harmed by her child means that she should push him away from her in order to harm his father by raising him, but she does not have the right to push him away if she gives birth to him until she gives him milk, without which he usually cannot survive, then after that she has the right to push him away from her if she wishes, but if she is harming his father, then that is not permissible for her, just as it is not permissible for him to take him away from her just to harm her, and for this reason he said: And no child shall have his child meaning that he wants to take the child away from her in order to harm her, as stated by Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Az-Zuhri, As-Suddi, Ath-Thawri, Ibn Zayd, and others. God the Almighty said: And the heir has the same obligation. It was said: In not causing harm to his relative, as stated by Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi and Al-Dahhak. It was also said: He has the same obligation as the father of the child has in terms of spending on the mother of the child and fulfilling her rights and not harming her, which is the opinion of the majority. Ibn Jarir discussed this in detail in his interpretation. It was used as evidence by those of the Hanafis and Hanbalis who held that relatives must spend on each other, and it was narrated on the authority of ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattab and the majority of the Salaf. This is supported by the hadith of Al-Hasan on the authority of Samurah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, Whoever owns a mahram relative, he must free him. It was mentioned that breastfeeding after two years may harm the child, either in his body or his mind. Sufyan Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah: He saw a woman breastfeeding after two years, so he said: Do not breastfeed him. And his saying: But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and after consulting each other, there is no blame upon them. That is, if the child’s parents agree to wean him before two years, and they see that this is in his best interest, and they consult each other about it and agree on it, then there is no blame upon them in that. It is taken from this that one of them alone doing that without the other is not sufficient, and it is not permissible for one of them to do that alone without consulting the other, as Al-Thawri and others said. This is a precaution for the child and an obligation to look into his matter, and it is from the mercy of God to His servants, as He has restricted the parents in raising their child, and guided them to what is good for them and him, as He said in Surat al-Talaq 65:“And if they nurse for you, then give them their payment and consult among yourselves in an acceptable manner. But if you disagree, then another woman may nurse for him.” And the Almighty said: And if you wish to have your children nursed by other women, there is no blame upon you if you give them what you have given them in an acceptable manner. That is, if the mother and father agree that he should take the child from her, either because of an excuse on her part or because of an excuse on his part, then there is no blame upon them for giving it, nor upon him for accepting it from her if he gives her her previous wages in a way that is better, and he has someone else nurse her for his child in return for wages in an acceptable manner. This was said by more than one person. And His statement: And fear God that is in all your affairs, and know that God is Seeing of what you do. That is, nothing of your affairs or your words is hidden from Him.
2:234: This is an order from God to women whose husbands die, to observe a waiting period of four months and ten nights, and this ruling includes wives who have been consummated with and those who have not been consummated with by consensus, and its basis for those who have not been consummated with is the generality of the noble verse, and this hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan and authenticated by Al-Tirmidhi: that Ibn Masoud was asked about a man who married a woman and then he died, and he did not consummate the marriage with her and did not give her a dowry, so they went back to him repeatedly about that, so he said I will say about her according to my opinion, if it is correct then it is from God, and if it is wrong then it is from me and Satan, and God and His Messenger are innocent of it: She is entitled to the full dowry, and in another version: She is entitled to the dowry of her equal, neither less nor more, and she must observe the waiting period, and she is entitled to the inheritance, so Muqal bin Yasar Al-Ashja’i stood up and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rule in the case of Baru’ bint Washiq, so Abdullah was very happy about that, and in another narration: Then some men from Ashja’ stood up and said: We bear witness that The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled in the case of Baru’ bint Washiq. No one is excluded from this except a woman whose husband died while she was pregnant. Her waiting period is until she gives birth, even if she does not stay after that for more than a moment, due to the generality of the statement: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. Ibn Abbas used to think that she should wait until the longer of the two terms after giving birth, or four months and ten days, to reconcile the two verses. This is a good approach and a strong approach, were it not for the Sunnah’s confirmation in the hadith of Subay’ah al-Aslamiyyah, which was narrated in the two Sahihs through more than one chain of transmission, that her husband Sa’d ibn Khawlah died while she was pregnant, and she did not wait long before she gave birth after his death. In another narration: She gave birth a few nights after him. When she recovered from her confinement, she adorned herself for the suitor. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba’kak came to her and said to her: Why do I see you adorned? Perhaps you are hoping to marry? By God, you will not marry until four months and ten days have passed. Subai'ah said: When he said that to me, I gathered my clothes around me in the evening, and I came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and asked him about that, and he gave me a fatwa that I had become permissible when I gave birth, and he ordered me to marry if I wished. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: It has been narrated that Ibn Abbas referred to the hadith of Subai'ah, meaning when he used it as evidence against him. He said: And this is authenticated from him, that his companions issued a fatwa based on the hadith of Subai'ah, as is the saying of all the scholars. Likewise, an exception is made from that for the wife if she is a slave woman, for her waiting period is half that of a free woman, two months and five nights according to the majority of scholars, because since she is half that of a free woman in the prescribed punishment, so too should she be half that of her in the waiting period. Some scholars, such as Muhammad ibn Sirin and some of the Zahiris, consider free wives and slave girls equal in this regard, based on the generality of the verse and because the waiting period is a matter of nature in which creation is equal. Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Abu al-Aaliyah and others have mentioned that the wisdom in making the waiting period for death four months and ten days is due to the possibility that the womb may contain a pregnancy. If one waits for this period, it will become apparent if it exists, as stated in the hadith of Ibn Masoud in the two Sahihs and others: “The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty days as a drop of sperm, then it becomes a clot for a similar period, then it becomes a lump of flesh for a similar period, then the angel is sent to him and he breathes the spirit into him.” So these are three forties with four months, and the precaution is to wait ten days after that because some months may be missing, then because movement appears after the spirit is breathed into him, and God knows best. Saeed ibn Abi Arouba said, on the authority of Qatadah: I asked Saeed ibn al-Musayyab: What is the matter with the ten? He said: The spirit is breathed into it. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: I said to Abu al-Aaliyah: Why are these ten days included with the four months? He said: Because the soul is breathed into her. Both were narrated by Ibn Jarir. From here Imam Ahmad went, in a narration from him, to the fact that the waiting period of the mother of a child is the same as the waiting period of a free woman here, because she has become a bed like free women. And for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Raja’ ibn Haywah, on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb, on the authority of Amr ibn al-‘As, who said: Do not confuse us with the Sunnah of our Prophet, the waiting period of the mother of a child, if her master dies, is four months and ten days. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Qubaysah, on the authority of Ghundar, and on the authority of Ibn al-Muthanna, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of al-Rabi’, all three of them on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Matar al-Warraq, on the authority of Raja’ ibn Haywah, on the authority of Qubaysah, on the authority of Amr ibn al-‘As, and he mentioned it. It was narrated from Imam Ahmad that he denied this hadith, and it was said that Qubaysah did not hear Omar, and a group of the Salaf adopted this hadith, including Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Abu Ayyad, Al-Zuhri, and Omar bin Abdul Aziz, and Yazid bin Abdul Malik bin Marwan, the Commander of the Faithful, used to command this, and Al-Awza’i, Ishaq bin Rahawayh, and Ahmad bin Hanbal said this in a narration from him, and Tawus and Qatadah said: The waiting period of a slave woman if her master dies is half the waiting period of a free woman, two months and five nights. Abu Hanifa and his companions, Al-Thawri, Al-Hasan bin Salih bin Hayy said: She waits for three menstrual periods, and this is the opinion of Ali, Ibn Masoud, Ata, and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad said in the well-known opinion from him: Her waiting period is one menstrual period, and Ibn Omar, Al-Sha’bi, Makhul, Al-Layth, Abu Ubaid, Abu Thawr, and the majority say this, and Al-Layth said: If he died while she was menstruating, it would suffice her. Malik said: If she was one of those who did not menstruate, then three months. Al-Shafi’i and the majority said: I prefer one or three months, and God knows best. And His saying: “And when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” From this we learn that it is obligatory for a woman whose husband has died to mourn for the duration of her waiting period, as it was proven in the two Sahihs through more than one chain of transmission on the authority of Umm Habibah and Zainab bint Jahsh, the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband, for whom she shall have four months and ten days. And in the two Sahihs also on the authority of Umm Salamah that a woman said: O Messenger of God, my daughter’s husband died and she has a sore eye, should we apply kohl to it? He said: No, all of that. He said: No, two or three times, then he said: It is only four months and ten days, and one of you in the pre-Islamic era would remain for a year. Zainab bint Umm Salamah said: When a woman’s husband died, she would enter a hut and wear her worst clothes, and she would not touch perfume or anything else until a year had passed, then she would go out and be given dung and throw it away, then she would be brought a donkey, sheep, or bird and she would be deflowered with it. It is rare for a woman to be deflowered without her dying. Hence, many scholars have said that this verse abrogates the verse that follows it, which is His statement: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall bequeath to their wives a year’s maintenance, without putting them out Al-Masdar Online, 2017, as Ibn Abbas and others said. There is a view on this, as will be explained later. The point is that mourning is an expression for not wearing adornments such as perfume and wearing clothes, jewelry, and other things that invite her to her husbands. It is obligatory in the waiting period of a woman who has died, according to one opinion, and it is not obligatory in the waiting period of a woman who has revocable divorce, according to one opinion. Is it obligatory in the waiting period of a woman who has irrevocably divorced, there are two opinions. Mourning is obligatory for all wives whose husbands have died, whether they are young, hopeless, free, slave women, Muslim women or non-Muslim women, due to the generality of the verse. Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah and his companions said: There is no mourning for a non-Muslim woman. Ashhab and Ibn Nafi’ from the companions of Malik said the same. The proof of the one who said this statement is the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband, for four months and ten days. They said: So he made it an act of worship. Abu Hanifah and his companions and al-Thawri included the young woman among them because of the lack of obligation. Abu Hanifah and his companions included the Muslim slave woman because of her deficiency. The place to establish all of this is in the books of rulings and branches, and God is the guide to what is right. And his saying, And when they have reached their term, meaning their waiting period has ended, was said by Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas. There is no blame upon you, Az-Zuhri said, meaning upon her guardians. For what they do, meaning the women whose waiting period has ended. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If a woman is divorced or her husband dies, then when her waiting period has ended, there is no blame upon her for adorning herself, making herself beautiful, and offering herself for marriage, for that is what is known. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid, There is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner, he said: lawful, good marriage. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Az-Zuhri, As-Suddi, and others like that.
2:235: God the Almighty says: And there is no blame upon you if you propose to women during their waiting period after the death of their husbands without stating it explicitly. Al-Thawri, Shu'bah, Jarir and others said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And there is no blame upon you for what you propose to women, he said: The insinuation is to say: I want to get married, and I love a woman for her sake and her affair - he proposes to her by speaking to her in a good manner - and in another narration: I wish that God had provided me with a wife, and the like of this, and he does not initiate the proposal, and in another narration: I do not want to marry anyone other than you, God willing, and I wish that I had found a righteous woman, and he does not initiate the proposal as long as she is in her waiting period. Al-Bukhari narrated it in a suspended manner and said: And Talq bin Ghannam said to me, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And there is no blame upon you for what you propose to women is to say: I want to get married, and women are among my needs, and I wish that a woman would be made easy for me Valid, and thus said Mujahid, Tawus, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Zuhri, Yazid bin Qusayt, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, and more than one of the predecessors and imams regarding insinuation: It is permissible for a woman whose husband has died to propose to her without explicitly stating the marriage proposal to her. And thus is the ruling on a woman who has been irrevocably divorced: it is permissible to insinuate it to her, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Fatimah bint Qays when her husband Abu Amr bin Hafs divorced her with the last of three divorces, so he ordered her to observe her waiting period in the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, and he said to her: When she becomes permissible, then inform me. So when she becomes permissible, Usamah bin Zaid, his freedman, proposed to her and married her to him. As for a divorced woman, there is no disagreement that it is not permissible for anyone other than her husband to explicitly propose to her or insinuate it to her, and God knows best. And His statement, Or did you conceal it within yourselves, meaning did you conceal within yourselves the matter of proposing to them? This is like the statement of God Almighty, And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare, and like His statement, And I know what you conceal and what you declare. For this reason He said, God knows that you will mention them, meaning within yourselves, so He removed the hardship from you in that. Then he said: But do not make secret promises to them. Abu Majlaz, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Jabir bin Zaid, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Sulayman At-Taymi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and As-Suddi said: He means adultery, which is the meaning of adultery, and it is the meaning of Al-Awfi’s narration from Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Ali bin Abi Talhah said from Ibn Abbas: But do not make secret promises to them. Do not say to her: I am in love, and promise me that you will not marry anyone other than me, and the like. This is also narrated from Sa’id bin Jubayr, Al-Sha’bi, Ikrimah, Abu Ad-Dahhak, Az-Zuhri, Mujahid, and Ath-Thawri, which is that he takes her covenant that she will not marry anyone other than him. On the authority of Mujahid: It is a man saying to a woman: Do not miss yourself from me, for I will marry you. Qatada said: It is that he takes a woman’s pledge while she is in her waiting period that she will not marry anyone else. God forbade that, and presented it and permitted engagement and speaking in a good manner. Ibn Zayd said: But do not make a secret promise to them means that he marries her secretly during her waiting period, then when she becomes permissible, he makes that public. It is possible that the verse is general in all of that, for this reason he said: Unless you speak a respectable word. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, As-Suddi, Ath-Thawri and Ibn Zayd said: He meant by it what was mentioned previously about permitting insinuations like saying: I am interested in you and the like. Muhammad bin Sirin said: I said to Ubaydah: What is the meaning of his statement: Unless you speak a respectable word? He said: He says to her guardian: Do not precede me with her, meaning do not marry her until you tell me. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And His statement, And do not determine to tie the marriage knot until the prescribed period has reached its term means do not tie the marriage knot until the waiting period has expired. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ash-Sha’bi, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Az-Zuhri, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, As-Suddi, Ath-Thawri and Ad-Dahhak said: Until the prescribed period has reached its term means do not tie the marriage contract until the waiting period has expired. The scholars have unanimously agreed that the marriage contract is not valid during the waiting period. They differed concerning a man who marries a woman during her waiting period and consummates the marriage with her. Should he separate them? Is she ever forbidden to him? There are two opinions: The majority say that she is not forbidden to him, but he may propose to her when her waiting period has ended. Imam Malik believed that she is forbidden to him forever, and he provided evidence for that with what he narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab and Sulayman ibn Yasar, that Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Any woman who marries during her waiting period, if her husband who married her did not consummate the marriage with her, they are separated, then she observes the remainder of her waiting period from her first husband, and he was a suitor among the suitors, and if he consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, then she observes the remainder of her waiting period from her first husband, then she observes the waiting period from the other, then he never marries her again. They said: The basis for this is that when the husband hastened what God had made permissible, he was punished with the opposite of his intention, so she is forbidden to him forever, like a murderer who is forbidden from inheriting. Al-Shafi’i narrated this trace from Malik. Al-Bayhaqi said: He went with it in the old and went back on it in the new, because of Ali’s saying that she is permissible for him. I said He said: Then it is disconnected from Umar. Al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, that Umar went back on that, and made her dowry and made them come together. And His saying: And know that God knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him, He threatened them for what occurs in their hearts regarding matters of women, and He guided them to harbor good and not evil, then He did not make them despair of His mercy, nor did He make them lose hope of His return, so He said: And know that God is Forgiving and Forbearing.
2:236: God the Almighty permitted divorcing a woman after the marriage contract was concluded, and before consummating the marriage. Ibn Abbas, Tawus, Ibrahim, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The touch of marriage, and it is even permissible to divorce her before consummating the marriage and the obligation is hers, if she was delegated, even if this would break her heart. For this reason, God the Almighty commanded that she be given a gift, which is to compensate her for what she missed with something given by her husband according to his situation, according to the ability of the wealthy, and according to the ability of the poor. Sufyan Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said, the highest of the gift of divorce is a servant, and below that is paper, and below that is clothing. Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If he is well-off, he gives her a gift of a servant or something similar, and if he is poor, he gives her three garments. Al-Sha'bi said: The middle of that is a shield, a veil, a sheet, and a jilbab. He said: Shuraih used to give her a gift of five hundred. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Ayoub bin Sirin, who said: He used to enjoy the servant, or the expenses, or the clothing. He said: Al-Hasan bin Ali enjoyed the wife with ten thousand, and it is narrated that the woman said: A small enjoyment from a separated lover. Abu Hanifa held that if the spouses disputed over the amount of the enjoyment, she is entitled to half the dowry of her peers. Al-Shafi’i said in Al-Jadid: The husband is not forced to pay a known amount except for the least amount that can be called enjoyment, and I prefer that, as I prefer thirty dirhams, as narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both. Scholars also differed: Is the pleasure due to every divorced woman or is the pleasure due to the one who has not been consummated with and has not been obligated to do so? There are several opinions: One of them is that the pleasure is due to every divorced woman, based on the generality of the Almighty’s statement: Divorced women shall have a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous. And based on the Almighty’s statement: “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release.” And they had been obligated to do so and had been consummated with. This is the opinion of Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and it is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, and some of them considered it the new and correct one, and God knows best. The second opinion is that it is obligatory for the divorced woman if she was divorced before touching them, even if it was obligatory for her, because God the Almighty said: “O you who believe! When you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period to count for them. So provide for them and release them with graciousness.” Shu’bah and others said, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: This verse in al-Ahzab abrogated the verse in al-Baqarah. Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d and Abu Usayd, that they said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) married Umaymah bint Shurahbil, and when she was brought to him, he stretched out his hand to her, and it was as if she disliked that, so he ordered Abu Usayd to prepare her and clothe her in two blue garments. The third opinion is that the enjoyment is only obligatory for the divorced woman if he did not consummate the marriage with her and did not assign anything to her. If he did consummate the marriage with her, she is obligated to receive a dowry similar to hers if she was married. If he did assign it to her and divorced her before consummation, she is obligated to receive half of it. If he consummated the marriage with her, then all of it is settled, and that is a compensation for her for the enjoyment. Rather, the one who was afflicted was not assigned anything to her and did not consummate the marriage with her. This is the opinion of Ibn Umar and Mujahid. Some scholars have recommended it for every divorced woman except the one who was delegated and separated before consummation. This is not objectionable. It is based on the verse of choice in Al-Ahzab. For this reason, God the Almighty said: The wealthy shall have his due, and the poor shall have his due, as provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good. “And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous.” Some scholars say that it is absolutely recommended. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Kathir ibn Shihab al-Qazwini told us, Muhammad ibn Saeed ibn Sabeq told us, Amr - meaning Ibn Abi Qais - told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: They mentioned to him temporary marriage, should one be imprisoned for it? So he recited: The wealthy man shall bear his due share, and the poor man shall bear his due share. Al-Sha’bi said: By God, I have not seen anyone imprisoned for it, and by God, if it were obligatory, the judges would have been imprisoned for it.
2:237: This noble verse is one of the things that indicates that the pleasure is specific to what the first verse indicated, since in this verse he only made obligatory half of the imposed dowry if the husband divorced before consummation. If there had been another obligation of pleasure, he would have made it clear, especially since he linked it to what preceded it regarding the specificity of pleasure to that verse, and God knows best. And dividing the dowry in this case is a matter agreed upon by the scholars, there is no disagreement among them about it, because if he had named a dowry for her and then separated from her before consummating the marriage, then she is entitled to half of the dowry he named, except that the three scholars say that the entire dowry is due if the husband is alone with her even if he has not consummated the marriage with her, and this is the old school of thought of al-Shafi’i, and the ruling of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs is this, but al-Shafi’i said: Muslim ibn Khalid informed us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said about a man who marries a woman and is alone with her without touching her, then divorces her: She is only entitled to half of the dowry, because God says: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry, then half of what you specified [al-Shafi’i said: This is what I say, and it is apparent in the Book. Al-Bayhaqi and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, even if it is not reliable, we have narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so it is his statement. And his saying: unless they forgive meaning the women, from what is due to her from her husband, so she is not obligated to do anything from him. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: unless they forgive he said: unless the previously married woman forgives and gives up her right. Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Shuraih, Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Sha’bi, al-Hasan, Nafi’, Qatadah, Jabir ibn Zayd, Ata’ al-Khurasani, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Ibn Sirin, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and al-Suddi. He said: Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi disagreed with them and said: unless they forgive meaning the men, and it is an odd statement that was not followed. End of his statement. And his saying: Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah that Amr ibn Shu’ayb told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The husband is the one who has the marriage contract. And this is how Ibn Mardawayh attributed it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah on his authority. And Ibn Jarir attributed it on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned it and did not say on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, so God knows best. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Habib told us, Abu Dawud told us, Jabir, meaning Ibn Abi Hazim, told us, on the authority of Isa, meaning Ibn Asim, he said: I heard Shuraih say: Ali bin Abi Talib asked me about the one who has the marriage contract in his hand, so I said to him: He is the woman’s guardian, so Ali said: No, rather he is the husband, then he said: And in one of the narrations on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Jubayr bin Mut’im, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Shuraih in one of his two opinions, and Saeed bin Jubayr, Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi, Ikrimah, Nafi’, Muhammad bin Sirin, Al-Dahhak, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, Jabir bin Zaid, Abu Majlaz, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Iyas bin Mu’awiyah, Makhul, and Muqatil bin Hayyan, that he is the husband I said: And this is the new opinion of Al-Shafi’i, and the school of Abu Hanifa and his companions, and Al-Thawri, Ibn Shubramah, and Al-Awza’i, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and the basis of this opinion is that the one who has the marriage contract in his hand is the true husband, for he has the power to conclude it, confirm it, annul it, and destroy it, and just as it is not permissible for the guardian, To give something from the money of the female guardian to someone else, and the same applies to the dowry. He said: The second view is that my father told us, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, Amr ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - regarding the one in whose hand is the marriage contract - he said: That is her father, her brother, or the one she cannot marry except with his permission. It was narrated on the authority of Alqamah, Al-Hasan, Ata’, Tawus, Al-Zuhri, Rabi’ah, Zaid ibn Aslam, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Ikrimah in one of his two opinions, and Muhammad ibn Sirin in one of his two opinions that it is the guardian. This is the school of Malik, and the old opinion of Al-Shafi’i, and its basis is that the guardian is the one who gave it to her, so he has the right to dispose of it, unlike the rest of her money. Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: God permitted forgiveness and commanded it, so any woman who is chaste, her forgiveness is permissible. If she is stingy and miserly, her guardian forgives, his forgiveness is permissible. This requires the validity of the guardian’s forgiveness even if she is sane. It was narrated on the authority of Shuraih, but Al-Sha’bi denounced him, so he changed his mind and became the husband, and he would perform a Mubahalah on him. And his saying: And that you pardon is closer to righteousness. Ibn Jarir said: Some of them said: It was addressed to men and women. Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, I heard Ibn Jurayj narrating on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And that you pardon is closer to righteousness. He said: The one closest to righteousness is the one who pardons. And this was narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and others. Mujahid, Al-Nakha’i, Ad-Dahhak, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas and Ath-Thawri said: The virtue here is that the woman forgives half of her dowry or the man completes her dowry. That is why He said, And do not forget graciousness between you, meaning kindness, as Sa’id said. Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, As-Suddi and Abu Wa’il Al-Ma’ruf said: It means do not neglect it, but rather use it between you. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim told us, Musa bin Ishaq told us, Uqbah bin Makram told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Abdullah bin Al-Waleed Ar-Rasafi told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A time will come upon the people when the believer will bite what is in his hands and forget graciousness. God the Most High said, “And do not forget graciousness between you,” Evil people who sell to every one who is forced. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade selling to one who is forced and selling with uncertainty. If you have something good, then give it to your brother and do not increase it.” From destruction to his destruction, for a Muslim is a brother to a Muslim. He does not grieve him or deprive him. Sufyan said: On the authority of Abu Harun, he said: I saw Awn bin Abdullah in the assembly of Al-Qurazi, and Awn was talking to us and his beard was dripping with tears, and he said: I kept company with the rich and I was the most worried of them when I saw them with the best clothes, the best smell, and the best mounts, and I sat with the poor and felt comfortable with them, and he said: And do not forget to be generous to one another if a beggar comes to him and he does not have anything, then let him pray for him, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do meaning nothing of your affairs and conditions is hidden from Him, and He will reward every worker according to his work.
2:238: And God commands us to maintain the prayers at their appointed times, to preserve their limits, and to perform them at their appointed times, as is proven in the two Sahihs: “On the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Which deed is best? He said: Prayer at its appointed time. I said: Then what? He said: Jihad in the way of God. I said: Then what? He said: Honoring one’s parents.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me about them, and if I had asked him for more, he would have given me more. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar bin Hafs bin `Aasim, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Ghannam, on the authority of his grandmother, the mother of his father, Al-Dunya, on the authority of his grandmother, Umm Farwah, who was one of those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention the deeds, and he said: The most beloved of deeds to God is to hasten to the prayer at its first time. And this is how Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it. He said: We do not know it except through the path of Al-`Umari, and it is not strong according to the people of Hadith. God, may God bless him and grant him peace, singled out from among them with more emphasis the middle prayer, and the predecessors and successors differed about it, which prayer is it? It was said: It is the morning prayer. Malik narrated it in Al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas. Hisham, Ibn Ulayyah, Ghandar, Ibn Abi Udayy, Abdul Wahhab, Sharik and others said on the authority of Awf Al-A’rabi on the authority of Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, and he said: I prayed the dawn prayer behind Ibn Abbas, and he made the qunut in it and raised his hands, then he said: This is the middle prayer in which we were commanded to stand devoutly. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and he also narrated it from the hadith of Awf on the authority of Khalas bin Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Awf told us on the authority of Abu Al-Munhal, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he prayed the morning prayer in the mosque of Basra, and he made the qunut before bowing, and he said: This is the middle prayer that God mentioned in His Book, and He said: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer and stand before God, devoutly obedient. He also said: Muhammad bin Isa Al-Damaghani told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas told us on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, who said: I prayed behind Abdullah bin Qais in Basra, the dawn prayer, so I said to a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was next to me: What is the middle prayer? He said: This prayer. It was narrated through another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Rabi’ on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, that he prayed the dawn prayer with the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when they finished, he said: I said to them: Which of them is the middle prayer? They said: The one I prayed before. He also said: Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Uthma told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The middle prayer is the dawn prayer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Omar, Abu Umamah, Anas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ubaid bin Umair, Ata, Mujahid, Jabir bin Zaid, Ikrimah, and Al-Rabi bin Anas. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad and Ibn Al-Had as well. It is what Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, stated, citing as evidence the words of God Almighty: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. Qunut, according to him, is in the dawn prayer. Some of them said: It is the middle prayer, considering that it is not shortened, and it is between two shortened four-unit prayers, and it is followed by the Maghrib prayer. It was said: Because it is between two loud prayers and two silent daytime prayers. It was said: It is the noon prayer. Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us, on the authority of Al-Zubayr, meaning Ibn Amr, on the authority of Zuhrah, meaning Ibn Ma’bad, who said: We were sitting with Zaid bin Thabit, so they sent. To Usamah, and they asked him about the middle prayer, and he said: It is the noon prayer. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray it in the middle of the day. Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, `Amr ibn Abi Hakim told me, I heard Az-Zubayr narrating from `Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer in the middle of the day, and he did not pray a prayer that was more difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than it. Then the verse was revealed: Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. He said: There are two prayers before it and two prayers after it. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan from the hadith of Shu`bah with it. Ahmad also said: Yazid told us, Ibn Abi Dhi`b told us, from Az-Zubayr, that a group of Quraish passed by Zayd ibn Thabit while they were gathered, so they sent two of their servants to ask him about the middle prayer. He said: It is the afternoon prayer. Two of their men stood up and asked him, and he said: It is the noon prayer. Then they turned to Usamah ibn Zaid and asked him. He said: It is the noon prayer. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer in the heat of the day, and there would be nothing behind him except one or two rows, and the people would be in their afternoon meal and doing their business. Then God revealed: Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let these men desist, or I will burn their houses. Az-Zubayr is the son of Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri. He did not meet any of the Companions. The correct version is what was mentioned above from his narration on the authority of Zuhrah ibn Ma’bad and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. Shu’bah and Hammam said on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit, who said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and others said, on the authority of Shu’bah: ‘Umar ibn Sulayman, from the descendants of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, told me: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abaan ibn ‘Uthman narrating on the authority of his father, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Zaydah on the authority of ‘Abd al-Samad on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of ‘Umar ibn Sulayman on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, in a hadith that traces it back to the Prophet, who said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer. Among those who narrated that it is the noon prayer are Ibn ‘Umar, Abu Sa’id and ‘A’ishah, with differences of opinion on their authority. It is the opinion of ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and ‘Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Haad, and a narration on the authority of Abu Hanifah, may God have mercy on them. It was said that it is the ‘Asr prayer. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Baghawi, may God have mercy on them, said: It is the opinion of most scholars among the Companions and others. Judge Al-Mawardi said: It is the opinion of the majority of the followers. Al-Hafiz Abu Omar bin Abdul-Barr said: It is the opinion of most of the people of the hadith. Abu Muhammad bin Atiyah said in his interpretation: It is the opinion of the majority of people. Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Abdul-Mumin bin Khalaf Al-Dimyati said in his book called Kashf Al-Mughta’a Claying for the Middle Prayer, in which he stated: It is the afternoon prayer. He narrated it from Omar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Abu Ayyub, Abdullah bin Amr, Samurah bin Jundub, Abu Hurairah, Abu Saeed, Hafsah, Umm Habibah, Umm Salamah, and from Ibn Abbas and Aisha according to the correct opinion from them. Ubaidah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Razin, Zur bin Hubaish, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ibn Sirin, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, Ubaid bin Maryam and others said the same. It is the school of thought of Ahmad bin Hanbal. Judge Al-Mawardi and Al-Shafi’i said: Ibn Al-Mundhir said: It is the correct opinion from Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, and it was chosen by Ibn Habib Al-Maliki, may God have mercy on them. The evidence for that was mentioned - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Shatir bin Shakl, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the Day of the Confederates, “They distracted us from the middle prayer, the ‘Asr prayer. May God fill their hearts and homes with fire.” Then he prayed it between the two evening prayers, Maghrib and ‘Isha. Muslim narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Abu Muawiyah Muhammad bin Hazim Al-Dareer, and Al-Nasa’i from the path of ‘Isa bin Yunus, both of them from Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim bin Subayh, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Shatir bin Shakl bin Hamid, on the authority of ‘Ali bin Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Muslim also narrated it from the path of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin ‘Utaybah, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, on the authority of ‘Ali bin Abi Talib, and it was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, and more than one of the authors of the Musnads, Sunans, and Sahihs, through paths that would take too long to mention, on the authority of ‘Ubaydah Al-Salmani, on the authority of ‘Ali, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the path of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, on the authority of ‘Ali, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is not known that he heard it from him, and he said: Ibn Abi Hatim: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, who said: I said to Ubaidah: Ask Ali about the middle prayer. So he asked him, and he said: We used to think it was the dawn or the morning prayer, until I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the Day of the Confederates: “They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May God fill their graves, their bellies, or their homes with fire.” Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Ibn Mahdi with it. The hadith on the Day of the Confederates, and the polytheists distracting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from performing the afternoon prayer on that day, is narrated on the authority of a group of the companions whose mention would take too long. Rather, what is meant is the narration of those among them who explicitly stated in their narration that the middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud and al-Bara` ibn `Azib, may God be pleased with them. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the Asr prayer. And Haz and Affan told us: Aban told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, and he named it for us as the Asr prayer. And Muhammad ibn Ja’far and Ruh told us: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the Asr prayer. Ibn Ja’far said: He was asked about the middle prayer. And Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, and he said: It is good and authentic. And he heard another Hadith from him. And Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Mani’ told us, Abdul-Wahhab ibn ‘Ata’ told us, on the authority of Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the Asr prayer.
