Another way, rather another hadith Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Jarshi al-Wasiti told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, he said: Sadaqah ibn Khalid told me, Khalid ibn Dahqan told me, on the authority of Khalid ibn Sublan, on the authority of Kuhayl ibn Harmalah, he said: Abu Hurayrah was asked about the middle prayer, and he said: We differed about it as you differed about it, and we were in the courtyard of the house of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among us was the righteous man Abu Hashim ibn Utbah ibn Rabi’ah ibn Abd Shams, so he said: I know that for you, so he stood up and asked permission to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he entered upon him and then he came out to us, and he said: He told us that it is the afternoon prayer, very strange from this aspect. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abd al-Salam told us on the authority of Muslim, the freed slave of Abu Jubayr, Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi told me: I was sitting with Abd al-Aziz ibn Marwan, and he said: O so-and-so, go to so-and-so and say to him: What did you hear from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the middle prayer? A man sitting there said: “Abu Bakr and Umar sent me, and I was a young boy, to ask him about the middle prayer. He took my little finger and said, ‘This is the dawn prayer.’ He held the one next to it and said, ‘This is the noon prayer.’ Then he held the thumb and said, ‘This is the sunset prayer.’ Then he held the one next to it and said, ‘This is the night prayer.’ Then he said, ‘Which of your fingers are left?’ I said, ‘The middle one.’ He said, ‘Which of the prayers are left?’ I said, ‘The afternoon prayer.’ He said, ‘It is the afternoon prayer.’” Also very strange. Another hadith Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Ta’i told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, my father told me, Abu Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shureih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. Its chain of transmission is sound. Another hadith Abu al-Hatim ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zuhair told us, al-Jarrah ibn Mukhallad told us, Amr ibn Asim told us, Hammam ibn Muwarriq al-Ajli told us, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Masraf from Zubayd al-Yami, from Murrah al-Hamadani, from Ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer, then he said: It is good and authentic. Muslim included it in his Sahih from the path of Muhammad ibn Talhah with it, and its wording is: They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, the hadith. These are texts on the issue that do not bear any meaning, and this is confirmed by the command to maintain it, and his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the authentic hadith narrated by al-Zuhri from Salim, from his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth. And in the Sahih also from the hadith of al-Awza`i, from Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, from Abi Qilabah, from Abi Katheer, from Abi al-Muhajir, from Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Pray early on a cloudy day, for whoever misses the afternoon prayer, his deeds will be in vain. And Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi`ah told us, from Abdullah ibn Hubayrah, from Abi Tamim narrated on the authority of Abu Nusrah al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the Asr prayer in one of their valleys, called al-Humays, and said: “This prayer was offered to those before you, but they neglected it. Beware, whoever prays it, his reward will be doubled for him. Beware, there is no prayer after it until you see the witness.” Then he said: He narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Ishaq on the authority of al-Layth on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nu’aym on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hubayrah on his authority. And Muslim and al-Nasa’i narrated it in this way, both of them on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Layth. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me, both of them on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nu’aym al-Hadrami, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hubayrah al-Saba’i on his authority. As for the hadith that Imam Ahmad also narrated, Ishaq told us, Malik told me, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Yunus, the freed slave of Aisha, who said: Aisha ordered me to write a copy of the Qur’an for her. She said: When you reach this verse, Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, then inform me. So when… When she reached it, she called her and dictated to me, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. He said: I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muslim narrated it in this way from Yahya ibn Yahya from Malik. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna al-Hajjaj told me, Hammad told us from Hisham ibn Urwah from his father, who said: In Aisha’s copy of the Qur’an was, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the afternoon prayer. This is how he narrated it from al-Hasan al-Basri that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it in this way. Imam Malik also narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Amr ibn Rafi’, who said: I was writing a copy of the Qur’an for Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: When you reach this verse, then call me, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer. When I reached it, I called her and she dictated to me, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. This is how Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar narrated it, saying: Abu Ja`far Muhammad bin Ali and Nafi`, the freed slave of Ibn `Umar, told me that `Umar bin Nafi` said something similar and added, as I memorized it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another way on the authority of Hafsa Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Azdi, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah, that Hafsa ordered someone to write a copy of the Qur’an for her, and she said: When you reach this verse, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, then let me know. So when he reached it, he let her know, and she said: Write, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the afternoon prayer. Another way Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna told me, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Ubayd God told us on the authority of Nafi’ that Hafsah ordered her slave to write a copy of the Qur’an for her, and she said: When you reach this verse, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, do not write it until I dictate it to you as you heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite it. So when he reached it, she ordered him to write it, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer and stand before God, devoutly obedient. Nafi’ said: So I read that copy of the Qur’an, and I found the letter waw in it. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ubayd ibn Umair that they both read it like this. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abda told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Abu Salamah told me on the authority of Amr ibn Rafi’, the freed slave of Umar, who said: In Hafsa’s copy of the Qur’an it was: Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. The report of the opposition is that he connected the afternoon prayer to the middle prayer with the conjunction waw, which requires difference, so that indicates that it is other than it. This was answered with aspects one of them that if this was narrated as a report, then the hadith of Ali is more correct and explicit than it. This may be that the waw is redundant, as in his saying: And thus do We explain the signs, that the way of the criminals may be made clear. “And thus did We show Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among those who are certain.” Or it may be for connecting attributes, not for connecting entities, as in his saying: But he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets. And as in his saying: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, Who created and proportioned, Who determined and guided, Who brought forth. Al-Mar’a and many similar examples. The poet said: To the venerable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place Abu Dawood Al-Ayadi said: Death and misfortune have prevailed over them, so they have their heads in the echo of the graves. Death is the end. Adi bin Zaid Al-Abbadi said: She presented the leather to Rahshiya, but he found her words to be lies and falsehoods. Lying is perjury. Sibawayh, the Sheikh of grammarians, stated that it is permissible for a speaker to say: I passed by your brother and your companion, and the companion is the brother himself, and God knows best. As for if it was narrated that it is the Qur’an, then it was not transmitted in succession and is not proven by a single report like the Qur’an. For this reason, the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, did not establish it in the Mushaf, nor did any of the reciters whose recitation establishes the proof, neither from the Seven nor from others, recite it like that. Then what indicates the abrogation of this recitation mentioned in this hadith was narrated. Muslim said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh told us, Yahya ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq, on the authority of Shaqiq ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, who said: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer was revealed, so we recited it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God willed, then God abrogated it and revealed: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer. A man who was with Shaqiq, Zahir, said to him: Is it the afternoon prayer? He said: I have told you how it was revealed, and how God the Almighty abrogated it. Muslim said: Al-Ashja’i narrated it on the authority of Al-Thawri, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Shaqiq. I said: Muslim did not narrate from Shaqiq except this one hadith, and God knows best. So based on this, this recitation, which is the recitation of Al-Jada, abrogates the wording of the narration of Aisha and Hafsa and its meaning, if the waw indicates difference, otherwise only its wording, and God knows best. It was said: The middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and there is a problem with its chain of transmission, as he narrated it on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu al-Jamahir on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Abu al-Khalil on the authority of his uncle on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Jarir narrated this statement on the authority of Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb, and he also narrated on the authority of Qatadah with a difference of opinion from him. Some of them based this statement on the fact that it is in the middle in number between the four-unit and the two-unit prayer, and that it is the odd number of obligatory prayers, and because of what has been reported about its virtue, and God knows best. It was said: It is the last supper, chosen by Ali bin Ahmed Al-Wahidi in his famous interpretation, and it was said: It is one of the five, not specifically, and it was made ambiguous in them, just as the Night of Decree was made ambiguous in the year, the month, or the ten, and this statement is narrated from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Shuraih Al-Qadi, Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Omar, and Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham, and it was also transmitted from Zaid bin Thabit and Imam Al-Haramayn Al-Juwayni chose it in his end. It was said: Rather, the middle prayer is the sum of the five prayers. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Umar, and its authenticity is also questionable. It is surprising that this statement was chosen by Sheikh Abu Amr bin Abdul Barr Al-Namri, the Imam of Transocean, and it is one of the major sins if he chose it with his knowledge and memorization of what was not supported by evidence from the Book, Sunnah, or Athar. It was said: It is the Isha prayer and the Fajr prayer. It was said: Rather, it is the congregational prayer. It was said: The Friday prayer. It was said: The fear prayer. It was said: Rather, it is the Eid Al-Fitr prayer. It was said: Rather, it is the Eid Al-Adha prayer. It was said: The Witr prayer. It was said: The Duha prayer. Others hesitated regarding it because the evidence conflicted with them, and they did not see any reason to prefer it, and there was no consensus on one statement, rather the dispute regarding it has continued to exist from the time of the Companions until now. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar and Ibn Muthanna told me: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: I heard Qatadah narrating on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab: The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) differed regarding the middle prayer like this, and he interlaced his fingers. All of these statements are weak in relation to the one before it. Rather, the crux and the arena of dispute are regarding the dawn and afternoon prayers. It has been established in the Sunnah that they are the afternoon prayers, so it is necessary to resort to them. Imam Abu Muhammad `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi may God have mercy on them both narrated in the book of al-Shafi`i may God have mercy on him: My father told us, I heard Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi say: al-Shafi`i said: Everything I have said was from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Contrary to what I say, which is correct, the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more appropriate, so do not imitate me. This is also what Al-Rabi’, Al-Za’farani, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i. Musa Abu Al-Walid ibn Abi Al-Jarud said on the authority of Al-Shafi’i: If the hadith is correct and I say something, then I retract my statement and say that. This is from his authority and trustworthiness. This is the same as his brothers among the imams, may God have mercy on them, that the middle prayer is the afternoon prayer, even though it has been stated in Al-Jadeed and other books that it is the dawn prayer due to the soundness of the hadiths that it is the afternoon prayer. A group of the hadith scholars of the Shafi’i school agreed with him on this method, and they insisted that it is the dawn prayer with one statement. Al-Marudi said: Some of them narrated two statements on the issue, and there is another place to establish the objections and answers other than this, and we have devoted it separately, praise and thanks be to God. And the Almighty’s saying: And stand before God, devoutly obedient, meaning humble, submissive, and submissive before Him. This matter necessitates abandoning speech during prayer because it contradicts it. For this reason, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused to respond to Ibn Masoud when he greeted him while he was praying, he apologized to him for that and said, Prayer is a distraction. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Muawiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami when he spoke during the prayer, “This prayer is not suitable for any of the speech of people. It is only glorification, magnification, and remembrance of God.” Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Yahya ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Ismail, al-Harith ibn Shabil told me, on the authority of Abu Amr al-Shaibani, on the authority of Zaid ibn Arqam, who said: A man would speak to his companion during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about a need during the prayer, until this verse was revealed, And stand before God, devoutly obedient, and he ordered us to be silent. It was narrated by all except Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ismail. This hadith was problematic for a group of scholars, as it was proven to them that the prohibition of speaking during the prayer was in Mecca before the migration to Medina and after the migration to the land of Abyssinia, as indicated by the hadith of Ibn Masoud in Sahih, who said: We used to greet the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, before we migrated to Abyssinia while he was praying, and he would respond to us. He said: When we arrived, I greeted him, but he did not respond to me, and I was overcome by what was near and far, and when he greeted him, he said, I did not… “I will reply to you, except that I was in prayer, and God does what He wills of His command, and among what He has done is that you should not speak during prayer.” Ibn Mas`ud was one of those who converted to Islam in the past and migrated to Abyssinia, then came from there to Mecca with those who came and migrated to Medina. This verse, And stand before God, devoutly obedient, is Medinan without dispute. Some said: Zayd ibn Arqam only meant by his statement, A man would speak to his brother about his need during prayer, to inform about the type of speech, and he used this verse as evidence for the prohibition of that according to what he understood from it, and God knows best. Others said: He only meant that that had occurred in Medina after the migration to it, and that it had been permitted twice and prohibited twice, as some of our companions and others chose, and the first is more apparent, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Bishr ibn al-Walid informed us, Ishaq ibn Yahya informed us on the authority of al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: We used to greet one another during prayer, so I passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, but he did not respond to me, so it occurred to me that it had been revealed about something. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished his prayer, he said, “And upon you be peace, O Muslim, and the mercy of God. God, the Almighty, does what He wills of His command. When you are in prayer, then pray qunut and do not speak.” And His statement, But if you fear, then on foot or riding; but when you are secure, then remember God as He has taught you that which you did not know, when God, the Almighty, commanded His servants to maintain the prayers and to perform their limits, and emphasized the matter by emphasizing it, He mentioned the situation in which a person is distracted from performing them in the most perfect manner, which is the situation of fighting and the outbreak of war. So He said, But if you fear, then on foot or riding, meaning pray in any situation, whether on foot or riding, meaning facing the qiblah or not, as Malik said on the authority of Nafi’ that Ibn Umar, when asked about the prayer of fear, described it, then said: If the fear was more severe than that, pray on foot or riding, facing the qiblah or not. Nafi’ said: I do not think that Ibn Umar mentioned that except on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Al-Bukhari narrated it. This is it. Muslim’s wording, and Al-Bukhari narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar or close to it. Muslim also narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: If the fear is more severe than that, then pray while riding or standing, gesturing. And in the hadith of Abdullah ibn Unais Al-Juhani, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Khalid ibn Sufyan Al-Hudhali to kill him, and he was towards Arafat or Arafat, and when he faced him, the time for the afternoon prayer came, he said: I feared that I would miss it, so I began to pray while gesturing. The hadith in its entirety was narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud with a good chain of transmission. This is from the concessions that God has granted to His servants and removed the burdens and shackles from them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Shabib ibn Bishr on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: In this verse, the one riding prays on his mount and the one walking on his feet. He said: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Makhul, Al-Suddi, Al-Hakam, Malik, Al-Awza’i, Al-Thawri, and Al-Hasan ibn Salih, something similar. That - and he added: And he nods his head wherever he is facing, then he said: My father told us, Ghassan told us, Dawud told us - meaning Ibn Ulayyah - on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Jabir Ibn Abdullah, he said: If there is a duel, then let him nod his head wherever his face is, so that is his saying on foot or riding, and it was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Saeed Ibn Jubayr, Ata’, Atiyyah, Al-Hakam, Hammad, and Qatadah something similar to that, and Imam Ahmad went in what he stated to the effect that the fear prayer is sometimes performed as one rak’ah if the two armies clash, and on that is based the hadith narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Abu Uwanah Al-Waddah Ibn Abdullah Al-Yashkari - Muslim, Al-Nasa’i, and Ayoub Ibn A’idh added - both of them on the authority of Bakir Ibn Al-Akhns Al-Kufi, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God imposed prayer on the tongue of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the city, four, and in travel, two, and in fear, one rak’ah, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, and others said the same. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Mahdi told us on the authority of Shu’bah, he said: I asked Al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatadah about the prayer of swordsmanship, and they said: It is one rak’ah. Al-Thawri narrated this same thing from them, and Ibn Jarir also said: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, Al-Mas’udi told us, Yazid Al-Faqir told us on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: The prayer of fear is one rak’ah. Ibn Jarir chose this statement, and Al-Bukhari said: Chapter on prayer when confronting fortresses and meeting the enemy. Al-Awza’i said: If the conquest is ready and they are not able to pray, they should pray by gesturing, each person for himself. If they are not able to gesture, they should delay the prayer until the fighting ends and they are safe, and they should pray two rak’ahs. If they are not able to, they should pray one rak’ah and two prostrations. If they are not able to, they should not say Takbir and they should delay it until they are safe. And Makhul said the same, and Anas bin Malik said: I was present at the battle of Tustar Fortress at dawn and the fighting was intense, so they were unable to pray, so we did not pray until after the sun had risen, so we prayed it while we were with Abu Musa, and he opened it for us. Anas said: I would not be pleased with that prayer for the world and everything in it. This is the wording of Al-Bukhari, then he cited as evidence for that the hadith of his delaying the afternoon prayer on the day of Al-Khandaq due to the excuse of fighting until the sun had set, and his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that to his companions when he prepared them for Banu Qurayzah, None of you should pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. Some of them were overtaken by the prayer on the road, so they prayed and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not want us to do anything except hasten our journey. Some of them were overtaken by the prayer but did not pray until the sun had set in Banu Qurayzah, so he did not rebuke either group. This is according to Al-Bukhari’s choice of this statement, and the majority are against it, and they rely on the fact that the prayer of fear in the manner in which it was mentioned in the Qur’an in Surat An-Nisa’, and the hadiths were mentioned about it, was not prescribed in the Battle of Al-Khandaq, but rather it was prescribed after that, and this was explicitly stated in the hadith of Abu Sa’id and others. As for Makhul, Al-Awza’i, and Al-Bukhari, they respond that the permissibility of the prayer of fear after that does not contradict the permissibility of that, because this is a rare and special case, in which the same is permissible. We said that the evidence for this is the actions of the Companions during the time of Omar in the conquest of Tustar, which became well-known and was not denied, and God knows best. And His statement, So when you are secure, remember God, meaning, establish your prayer as you have been commanded, so complete its bowing, prostration, standing, sitting, humility, and prostration, as He has taught you that which you did not know, meaning just as He has bestowed upon you, guided you, and taught you what will benefit you in this world and the Hereafter, so meet Him with gratitude and remembrance, like His statement after the fear prayer, “So when you are secure, establish prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.” And the hadiths that have been reported about the fear prayer and its descriptions will come in Surat An-Nisa’ when God Almighty says, And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, the verse.
2:239: And God commands us to maintain the prayers at their appointed times, to preserve their limits, and to perform them at their appointed times, as is proven in the two Sahihs: “On the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Which deed is best? He said: Prayer at its appointed time. I said: Then what? He said: Jihad in the way of God. I said: Then what? He said: Honoring one’s parents.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me about them, and if I had asked him for more, he would have given me more. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar bin Hafs bin `Aasim, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Ghannam, on the authority of his grandmother, the mother of his father, Al-Dunya, on the authority of his grandmother, Umm Farwah, who was one of those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention the deeds, and he said: The most beloved of deeds to God is to hasten to the prayer at its first time. And this is how Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it. He said: We do not know it except through the path of Al-`Umari, and it is not strong according to the people of Hadith. God, may God bless him and grant him peace, singled out from among them with more emphasis the middle prayer, and the predecessors and successors differed about it, which prayer is it? It was said: It is the morning prayer. Malik narrated it in Al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas. Hisham, Ibn Ulayyah, Ghandar, Ibn Abi Udayy, Abdul Wahhab, Sharik and others said on the authority of Awf Al-A’rabi on the authority of Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, and he said: I prayed the dawn prayer behind Ibn Abbas, and he made the qunut in it and raised his hands, then he said: This is the middle prayer in which we were commanded to stand devoutly. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and he also narrated it from the hadith of Awf on the authority of Khalas bin Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Awf told us on the authority of Abu Al-Munhal, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he prayed the morning prayer in the mosque of Basra, and he made the qunut before bowing, and he said: This is the middle prayer that God mentioned in His Book, and He said: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer and stand before God, devoutly obedient. He also said: Muhammad bin Isa Al-Damaghani told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas told us on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, who said: I prayed behind Abdullah bin Qais in Basra, the dawn prayer, so I said to a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was next to me: What is the middle prayer? He said: This prayer. It was narrated through another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Rabi’ on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, that he prayed the dawn prayer with the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when they finished, he said: I said to them: Which of them is the middle prayer? They said: The one I prayed before. He also said: Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Uthma told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The middle prayer is the dawn prayer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Omar, Abu Umamah, Anas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ubaid bin Umair, Ata, Mujahid, Jabir bin Zaid, Ikrimah, and Al-Rabi bin Anas. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad and Ibn Al-Had as well. It is what Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, stated, citing as evidence the words of God Almighty: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. Qunut, according to him, is in the dawn prayer. Some of them said: It is the middle prayer, considering that it is not shortened, and it is between two shortened four-unit prayers, and it is followed by the Maghrib prayer. It was said: Because it is between two loud prayers and two silent daytime prayers. It was said: It is the noon prayer. Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us, on the authority of Al-Zubayr, meaning Ibn Amr, on the authority of Zuhrah, meaning Ibn Ma’bad, who said: We were sitting with Zaid bin Thabit, so they sent. To Usamah, and they asked him about the middle prayer, and he said: It is the noon prayer. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray it in the middle of the day. Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, `Amr ibn Abi Hakim told me, I heard Az-Zubayr narrating from `Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer in the middle of the day, and he did not pray a prayer that was more difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than it. Then the verse was revealed: Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. He said: There are two prayers before it and two prayers after it. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan from the hadith of Shu`bah with it. Ahmad also said: Yazid told us, Ibn Abi Dhi`b told us, from Az-Zubayr, that a group of Quraish passed by Zayd ibn Thabit while they were gathered, so they sent two of their servants to ask him about the middle prayer. He said: It is the afternoon prayer. Two of their men stood up and asked him, and he said: It is the noon prayer. Then they turned to Usamah ibn Zaid and asked him. He said: It is the noon prayer. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer in the heat of the day, and there would be nothing behind him except one or two rows, and the people would be in their afternoon meal and doing their business. Then God revealed: Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let these men desist, or I will burn their houses. Az-Zubayr is the son of Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri. He did not meet any of the Companions. The correct version is what was mentioned above from his narration on the authority of Zuhrah ibn Ma’bad and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. Shu’bah and Hammam said on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit, who said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and others said, on the authority of Shu’bah: ‘Umar ibn Sulayman, from the descendants of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, told me: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abaan ibn ‘Uthman narrating on the authority of his father, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Zaydah on the authority of ‘Abd al-Samad on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of ‘Umar ibn Sulayman on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, in a hadith that traces it back to the Prophet, who said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer. Among those who narrated that it is the noon prayer are Ibn ‘Umar, Abu Sa’id and ‘A’ishah, with differences of opinion on their authority. It is the opinion of ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and ‘Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Haad, and a narration on the authority of Abu Hanifah, may God have mercy on them. It was said that it is the ‘Asr prayer. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Baghawi, may God have mercy on them, said: It is the opinion of most scholars among the Companions and others. Judge Al-Mawardi said: It is the opinion of the majority of the followers. Al-Hafiz Abu Omar bin Abdul-Barr said: It is the opinion of most of the people of the hadith. Abu Muhammad bin Atiyah said in his interpretation: It is the opinion of the majority of people. Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Abdul-Mumin bin Khalaf Al-Dimyati said in his book called Kashf Al-Mughta’a Claying for the Middle Prayer, in which he stated: It is the afternoon prayer. He narrated it from Omar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Abu Ayyub, Abdullah bin Amr, Samurah bin Jundub, Abu Hurairah, Abu Saeed, Hafsah, Umm Habibah, Umm Salamah, and from Ibn Abbas and Aisha according to the correct opinion from them. Ubaidah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Razin, Zur bin Hubaish, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ibn Sirin, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, Ubaid bin Maryam and others said the same. It is the school of thought of Ahmad bin Hanbal. Judge Al-Mawardi and Al-Shafi’i said: Ibn Al-Mundhir said: It is the correct opinion from Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, and it was chosen by Ibn Habib Al-Maliki, may God have mercy on them. The evidence for that was mentioned - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Shatir bin Shakl, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the Day of the Confederates, “They distracted us from the middle prayer, the ‘Asr prayer. May God fill their hearts and homes with fire.” Then he prayed it between the two evening prayers, Maghrib and ‘Isha. Muslim narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Abu Muawiyah Muhammad bin Hazim Al-Dareer, and Al-Nasa’i from the path of ‘Isa bin Yunus, both of them from Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim bin Subayh, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Shatir bin Shakl bin Hamid, on the authority of ‘Ali bin Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Muslim also narrated it from the path of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin ‘Utaybah, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, on the authority of ‘Ali bin Abi Talib, and it was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, and more than one of the authors of the Musnads, Sunans, and Sahihs, through paths that would take too long to mention, on the authority of ‘Ubaydah Al-Salmani, on the authority of ‘Ali, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the path of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, on the authority of ‘Ali, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is not known that he heard it from him, and he said: Ibn Abi Hatim: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, who said: I said to Ubaidah: Ask Ali about the middle prayer. So he asked him, and he said: We used to think it was the dawn or the morning prayer, until I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the Day of the Confederates: “They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May God fill their graves, their bellies, or their homes with fire.” Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Ibn Mahdi with it. The hadith on the Day of the Confederates, and the polytheists distracting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from performing the afternoon prayer on that day, is narrated on the authority of a group of the companions whose mention would take too long. Rather, what is meant is the narration of those among them who explicitly stated in their narration that the middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud and al-Bara` ibn `Azib, may God be pleased with them. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the Asr prayer. And Haz and Affan told us: Aban told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, and he named it for us as the Asr prayer. And Muhammad ibn Ja’far and Ruh told us: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the Asr prayer. Ibn Ja’far said: He was asked about the middle prayer. And Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, and he said: It is good and authentic. And he heard another Hadith from him. And Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Mani’ told us, Abdul-Wahhab ibn ‘Ata’ told us, on the authority of Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the Asr prayer. Another way, rather another hadith Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Jarshi al-Wasiti told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, he said: Sadaqah ibn Khalid told me, Khalid ibn Dahqan told me, on the authority of Khalid ibn Sublan, on the authority of Kuhayl ibn Harmalah, he said: Abu Hurayrah was asked about the middle prayer, and he said: We differed about it as you differed about it, and we were in the courtyard of the house of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among us was the righteous man Abu Hashim ibn Utbah ibn Rabi’ah ibn Abd Shams, so he said: I know that for you, so he stood up and asked permission to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he entered upon him and then he came out to us, and he said: He told us that it is the afternoon prayer, very strange from this aspect. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abd al-Salam told us on the authority of Muslim, the freed slave of Abu Jubayr, Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi told me: I was sitting with Abd al-Aziz ibn Marwan, and he said: O so-and-so, go to so-and-so and say to him: What did you hear from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the middle prayer? A man sitting there said: “Abu Bakr and Umar sent me, and I was a young boy, to ask him about the middle prayer. He took my little finger and said, ‘This is the dawn prayer.’ He held the one next to it and said, ‘This is the noon prayer.’ Then he held the thumb and said, ‘This is the sunset prayer.’ Then he held the one next to it and said, ‘This is the night prayer.’ Then he said, ‘Which of your fingers are left?’ I said, ‘The middle one.’ He said, ‘Which of the prayers are left?’ I said, ‘The afternoon prayer.’ He said, ‘It is the afternoon prayer.’” Also very strange. Another hadith Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Ta’i told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, my father told me, Abu Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shureih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. Its chain of transmission is sound. Another hadith Abu al-Hatim ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zuhair told us, al-Jarrah ibn Mukhallad told us, Amr ibn Asim told us, Hammam ibn Muwarriq al-Ajli told us, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Masraf from Zubayd al-Yami, from Murrah al-Hamadani, from Ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer, then he said: It is good and authentic. Muslim included it in his Sahih from the path of Muhammad ibn Talhah with it, and its wording is: They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, the hadith. These are texts on the issue that do not bear any meaning, and this is confirmed by the command to maintain it, and his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the authentic hadith narrated by al-Zuhri from Salim, from his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth. And in the Sahih also from the hadith of al-Awza`i, from Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, from Abi Qilabah, from Abi Katheer, from Abi al-Muhajir, from Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Pray early on a cloudy day, for whoever misses the afternoon prayer, his deeds will be in vain. And Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi`ah told us, from Abdullah ibn Hubayrah, from Abi Tamim narrated on the authority of Abu Nusrah al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the Asr prayer in one of their valleys, called al-Humays, and said: “This prayer was offered to those before you, but they neglected it. Beware, whoever prays it, his reward will be doubled for him. Beware, there is no prayer after it until you see the witness.” Then he said: He narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Ishaq on the authority of al-Layth on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nu’aym on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hubayrah on his authority. And Muslim and al-Nasa’i narrated it in this way, both of them on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Layth. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me, both of them on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nu’aym al-Hadrami, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hubayrah al-Saba’i on his authority. As for the hadith that Imam Ahmad also narrated, Ishaq told us, Malik told me, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Yunus, the freed slave of Aisha, who said: Aisha ordered me to write a copy of the Qur’an for her. She said: When you reach this verse, Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, then inform me. So when… When she reached it, she called her and dictated to me, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. He said: I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muslim narrated it in this way from Yahya ibn Yahya from Malik. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna al-Hajjaj told me, Hammad told us from Hisham ibn Urwah from his father, who said: In Aisha’s copy of the Qur’an was, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the afternoon prayer. This is how he narrated it from al-Hasan al-Basri that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it in this way. Imam Malik also narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Amr ibn Rafi’, who said: I was writing a copy of the Qur’an for Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: When you reach this verse, then call me, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer. When I reached it, I called her and she dictated to me, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. This is how Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar narrated it, saying: Abu Ja`far Muhammad bin Ali and Nafi`, the freed slave of Ibn `Umar, told me that `Umar bin Nafi` said something similar and added, as I memorized it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another way on the authority of Hafsa Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Azdi, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah, that Hafsa ordered someone to write a copy of the Qur’an for her, and she said: When you reach this verse, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, then let me know. So when he reached it, he let her know, and she said: Write, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the afternoon prayer. Another way Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna told me, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Ubayd God told us on the authority of Nafi’ that Hafsah ordered her slave to write a copy of the Qur’an for her, and she said: When you reach this verse, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, do not write it until I dictate it to you as you heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite it. So when he reached it, she ordered him to write it, Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer and stand before God, devoutly obedient. Nafi’ said: So I read that copy of the Qur’an, and I found the letter waw in it. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ubayd ibn Umair that they both read it like this. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abda told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Abu Salamah told me on the authority of Amr ibn Rafi’, the freed slave of Umar, who said: In Hafsa’s copy of the Qur’an it was: Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. The report of the opposition is that he connected the afternoon prayer to the middle prayer with the conjunction waw, which requires difference, so that indicates that it is other than it. This was answered with aspects one of them that if this was narrated as a report, then the hadith of Ali is more correct and explicit than it. This may be that the waw is redundant, as in his saying: And thus do We explain the signs, that the way of the criminals may be made clear. “And thus did We show Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among those who are certain.” Or it may be for connecting attributes, not for connecting entities, as in his saying: But he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets. And as in his saying: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, Who created and proportioned, Who determined and guided, Who brought forth. Al-Mar’a and many similar examples. The poet said: To the venerable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place Abu Dawood Al-Ayadi said: Death and misfortune have prevailed over them, so they have their heads in the echo of the graves. Death is the end. Adi bin Zaid Al-Abbadi said: She presented the leather to Rahshiya, but he found her words to be lies and falsehoods. Lying is perjury. Sibawayh, the Sheikh of grammarians, stated that it is permissible for a speaker to say: I passed by your brother and your companion, and the companion is the brother himself, and God knows best. As for if it was narrated that it is the Qur’an, then it was not transmitted in succession and is not proven by a single report like the Qur’an. For this reason, the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, did not establish it in the Mushaf, nor did any of the reciters whose recitation establishes the proof, neither from the Seven nor from others, recite it like that. Then what indicates the abrogation of this recitation mentioned in this hadith was narrated. Muslim said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh told us, Yahya ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq, on the authority of Shaqiq ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, who said: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer was revealed, so we recited it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God willed, then God abrogated it and revealed: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer. A man who was with Shaqiq, Zahir, said to him: Is it the afternoon prayer? He said: I have told you how it was revealed, and how God the Almighty abrogated it. Muslim said: Al-Ashja’i narrated it on the authority of Al-Thawri, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Shaqiq. I said: Muslim did not narrate from Shaqiq except this one hadith, and God knows best. So based on this, this recitation, which is the recitation of Al-Jada, abrogates the wording of the narration of Aisha and Hafsa and its meaning, if the waw indicates difference, otherwise only its wording, and God knows best. It was said: The middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and there is a problem with its chain of transmission, as he narrated it on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu al-Jamahir on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Abu al-Khalil on the authority of his uncle on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Jarir narrated this statement on the authority of Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb, and he also narrated on the authority of Qatadah with a difference of opinion from him. Some of them based this statement on the fact that it is in the middle in number between the four-unit and the two-unit prayer, and that it is the odd number of obligatory prayers, and because of what has been reported about its virtue, and God knows best. It was said: It is the last supper, chosen by Ali bin Ahmed Al-Wahidi in his famous interpretation, and it was said: It is one of the five, not specifically, and it was made ambiguous in them, just as the Night of Decree was made ambiguous in the year, the month, or the ten, and this statement is narrated from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Shuraih Al-Qadi, Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Omar, and Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham, and it was also transmitted from Zaid bin Thabit and Imam Al-Haramayn Al-Juwayni chose it in his end. It was said: Rather, the middle prayer is the sum of the five prayers. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Umar, and its authenticity is also questionable. It is surprising that this statement was chosen by Sheikh Abu Amr bin Abdul Barr Al-Namri, the Imam of Transocean, and it is one of the major sins if he chose it with his knowledge and memorization of what was not supported by evidence from the Book, Sunnah, or Athar. It was said: It is the Isha prayer and the Fajr prayer. It was said: Rather, it is the congregational prayer. It was said: The Friday prayer. It was said: The fear prayer. It was said: Rather, it is the Eid Al-Fitr prayer. It was said: Rather, it is the Eid Al-Adha prayer. It was said: The Witr prayer. It was said: The Duha prayer. Others hesitated regarding it because the evidence conflicted with them, and they did not see any reason to prefer it, and there was no consensus on one statement, rather the dispute regarding it has continued to exist from the time of the Companions until now. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar and Ibn Muthanna told me: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: I heard Qatadah narrating on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab: The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) differed regarding the middle prayer like this, and he interlaced his fingers. All of these statements are weak in relation to the one before it. Rather, the crux and the arena of dispute are regarding the dawn and afternoon prayers. It has been established in the Sunnah that they are the afternoon prayers, so it is necessary to resort to them. Imam Abu Muhammad `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi may God have mercy on them both narrated in the book of al-Shafi`i may God have mercy on him: My father told us, I heard Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi say: al-Shafi`i said: Everything I have said was from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Contrary to what I say, which is correct, the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more appropriate, so do not imitate me. This is also what Al-Rabi’, Al-Za’farani, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i. Musa Abu Al-Walid ibn Abi Al-Jarud said on the authority of Al-Shafi’i: If the hadith is correct and I say something, then I retract my statement and say that. This is from his authority and trustworthiness. This is the same as his brothers among the imams, may God have mercy on them, that the middle prayer is the afternoon prayer, even though it has been stated in Al-Jadeed and other books that it is the dawn prayer due to the soundness of the hadiths that it is the afternoon prayer. A group of the hadith scholars of the Shafi’i school agreed with him on this method, and they insisted that it is the dawn prayer with one statement. Al-Marudi said: Some of them narrated two statements on the issue, and there is another place to establish the objections and answers other than this, and we have devoted it separately, praise and thanks be to God. And the Almighty’s saying: And stand before God, devoutly obedient, meaning humble, submissive, and submissive before Him. This matter necessitates abandoning speech during prayer because it contradicts it. For this reason, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused to respond to Ibn Masoud when he greeted him while he was praying, he apologized to him for that and said, Prayer is a distraction. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Muawiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami when he spoke during the prayer, “This prayer is not suitable for any of the speech of people. It is only glorification, magnification, and remembrance of God.” Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Yahya ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Ismail, al-Harith ibn Shabil told me, on the authority of Abu Amr al-Shaibani, on the authority of Zaid ibn Arqam, who said: A man would speak to his companion during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about a need during the prayer, until this verse was revealed, And stand before God, devoutly obedient, and he ordered us to be silent. It was narrated by all except Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ismail. This hadith was problematic for a group of scholars, as it was proven to them that the prohibition of speaking during the prayer was in Mecca before the migration to Medina and after the migration to the land of Abyssinia, as indicated by the hadith of Ibn Masoud in Sahih, who said: We used to greet the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, before we migrated to Abyssinia while he was praying, and he would respond to us. He said: When we arrived, I greeted him, but he did not respond to me, and I was overcome by what was near and far, and when he greeted him, he said, I did not… “I will reply to you, except that I was in prayer, and God does what He wills of His command, and among what He has done is that you should not speak during prayer.” Ibn Mas`ud was one of those who converted to Islam in the past and migrated to Abyssinia, then came from there to Mecca with those who came and migrated to Medina. This verse, And stand before God, devoutly obedient, is Medinan without dispute. Some said: Zayd ibn Arqam only meant by his statement, A man would speak to his brother about his need during prayer, to inform about the type of speech, and he used this verse as evidence for the prohibition of that according to what he understood from it, and God knows best. Others said: He only meant that that had occurred in Medina after the migration to it, and that it had been permitted twice and prohibited twice, as some of our companions and others chose, and the first is more apparent, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Bishr ibn al-Walid informed us, Ishaq ibn Yahya informed us on the authority of al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: We used to greet one another during prayer, so I passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, but he did not respond to me, so it occurred to me that it had been revealed about something. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished his prayer, he said, “And upon you be peace, O Muslim, and the mercy of God. God, the Almighty, does what He wills of His command. When you are in prayer, then pray qunut and do not speak.” And His statement, But if you fear, then on foot or riding; but when you are secure, then remember God as He has taught you that which you did not know, when God, the Almighty, commanded His servants to maintain the prayers and to perform their limits, and emphasized the matter by emphasizing it, He mentioned the situation in which a person is distracted from performing them in the most perfect manner, which is the situation of fighting and the outbreak of war. So He said, But if you fear, then on foot or riding, meaning pray in any situation, whether on foot or riding, meaning facing the qiblah or not, as Malik said on the authority of Nafi’ that Ibn Umar, when asked about the prayer of fear, described it, then said: If the fear was more severe than that, pray on foot or riding, facing the qiblah or not. Nafi’ said: I do not think that Ibn Umar mentioned that except on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Al-Bukhari narrated it. This is it. Muslim’s wording, and Al-Bukhari narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar or close to it. Muslim also narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: If the fear is more severe than that, then pray while riding or standing, gesturing. And in the hadith of Abdullah ibn Unais Al-Juhani, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Khalid ibn Sufyan Al-Hudhali to kill him, and he was towards Arafat or Arafat, and when he faced him, the time for the afternoon prayer came, he said: I feared that I would miss it, so I began to pray while gesturing. The hadith in its entirety was narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud with a good chain of transmission. This is from the concessions that God has granted to His servants and removed the burdens and shackles from them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Shabib ibn Bishr on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: In this verse, the one riding prays on his mount and the one walking on his feet. He said: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Makhul, Al-Suddi, Al-Hakam, Malik, Al-Awza’i, Al-Thawri, and Al-Hasan ibn Salih, something similar. That - and he added: And he nods his head wherever he is facing, then he said: My father told us, Ghassan told us, Dawud told us - meaning Ibn Ulayyah - on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Jabir Ibn Abdullah, he said: If there is a duel, then let him nod his head wherever his face is, so that is his saying on foot or riding, and it was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Saeed Ibn Jubayr, Ata’, Atiyyah, Al-Hakam, Hammad, and Qatadah something similar to that, and Imam Ahmad went in what he stated to the effect that the fear prayer is sometimes performed as one rak’ah if the two armies clash, and on that is based the hadith narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Abu Uwanah Al-Waddah Ibn Abdullah Al-Yashkari - Muslim, Al-Nasa’i, and Ayoub Ibn A’idh added - both of them on the authority of Bakir Ibn Al-Akhns Al-Kufi, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God imposed prayer on the tongue of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the city, four, and in travel, two, and in fear, one rak’ah, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, and others said the same. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Mahdi told us on the authority of Shu’bah, he said: I asked Al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatadah about the prayer of swordsmanship, and they said: It is one rak’ah. Al-Thawri narrated this same thing from them, and Ibn Jarir also said: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, Al-Mas’udi told us, Yazid Al-Faqir told us on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: The prayer of fear is one rak’ah. Ibn Jarir chose this statement, and Al-Bukhari said: Chapter on prayer when confronting fortresses and meeting the enemy. Al-Awza’i said: If the conquest is ready and they are not able to pray, they should pray by gesturing, each person for himself. If they are not able to gesture, they should delay the prayer until the fighting ends and they are safe, and they should pray two rak’ahs. If they are not able to, they should pray one rak’ah and two prostrations. If they are not able to, they should not say Takbir and they should delay it until they are safe. And Makhul said the same, and Anas bin Malik said: I was present at the battle of Tustar Fortress at dawn and the fighting was intense, so they were unable to pray, so we did not pray until after the sun had risen, so we prayed it while we were with Abu Musa, and he opened it for us. Anas said: I would not be pleased with that prayer for the world and everything in it. This is the wording of Al-Bukhari, then he cited as evidence for that the hadith of his delaying the afternoon prayer on the day of Al-Khandaq due to the excuse of fighting until the sun had set, and his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that to his companions when he prepared them for Banu Qurayzah, None of you should pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. Some of them were overtaken by the prayer on the road, so they prayed and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not want us to do anything except hasten our journey. Some of them were overtaken by the prayer but did not pray until the sun had set in Banu Qurayzah, so he did not rebuke either group. This is according to Al-Bukhari’s choice of this statement, and the majority are against it, and they rely on the fact that the prayer of fear in the manner in which it was mentioned in the Qur’an in Surat An-Nisa’, and the hadiths were mentioned about it, was not prescribed in the Battle of Al-Khandaq, but rather it was prescribed after that, and this was explicitly stated in the hadith of Abu Sa’id and others. As for Makhul, Al-Awza’i, and Al-Bukhari, they respond that the permissibility of the prayer of fear after that does not contradict the permissibility of that, because this is a rare and special case, in which the same is permissible. We said that the evidence for this is the actions of the Companions during the time of Omar in the conquest of Tustar, which became well-known and was not denied, and God knows best. And His statement, So when you are secure, remember God, meaning, establish your prayer as you have been commanded, so complete its bowing, prostration, standing, sitting, humility, and prostration, as He has taught you that which you did not know, meaning just as He has bestowed upon you, guided you, and taught you what will benefit you in this world and the Hereafter, so meet Him with gratitude and remembrance, like His statement after the fear prayer, “So when you are secure, establish prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.” And the hadiths that have been reported about the fear prayer and its descriptions will come in Surat An-Nisa’ when God Almighty says, And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, the verse.
2:240: The majority said: This verse was abrogated by the one before it, which is His statement: They shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten. Al-Bukhari said: Umayyah told us, Yazid ibn Zari' told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Ibn Abi Mulaykah, Ibn al-Zubayr said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan: And those of you who die and leave wives behind was abrogated by the other verse, so you did not write it or leave it, he said: O son of my brother, I will not change any of it from its place. The meaning of this problem that Ibn al-Zubayr said to Uthman: If its ruling was abrogated by the four months, then what is the wisdom in keeping its form even though its ruling was removed, and keeping its form after the one that abrogated it gives the impression that its ruling remained? The Commander of the Faithful replied that this was a matter of revelation, and I found it confirmed in the Qur’an after that, so I confirmed it where I found it. Then he said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Ibrahim, Ata’, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas that it was abrogated. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If a man died and left his wife, she would observe a year of waiting in his house, and he would spend on her from his money. This is the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died, unless she is pregnant, in which case her waiting period is until she gives birth. But if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave.” So he explained the inheritance of a woman, leaving a will, and spending. But if they go out, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an honorable manner.” He said: God made the completion of the year seven months and twenty nights, a will. If she wishes, she may live in her will, and if she wishes, she may go out. This is the statement of God: “Without turning them out. But if they go out, there is no blame upon you.” So the waiting period is obligatory upon her as it is. This was claimed by Mujahid, may God have mercy on him. Ata’ said: If she wishes, she may observe the waiting period with her family and live in her will, and if she wishes, she may go out, based on the statement of God: There is no blame upon you for what they do. The majority, so that it would be abrogated by the four months and ten days, and it only indicated that it was from the category of the will for wives to be able to live in the houses of their husbands after their death for a full year if they chose that, and for this reason he said a will for their husbands meaning God commands you regarding them a will like his saying God commands you concerning your children the verse, and his saying: a will from God and it was said: it was only erected on the meaning of so make a will for them and others read it with the nominative as a will on the meaning of a will was written upon you and Ibn Jarir chose it, and they do not prevent him from that for his saying other than expulsion but if their waiting period ends with the four months and ten days, or by giving birth, and they choose to go out and move from that house, then they are not prevented from that for his saying but if they go out, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of good and this saying has a direction, and in the wording there is support for it, and a group of them chose it, including Imam Abu al-Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah and others rejected it, including Sheikh Abu Omar Ibn Abd al-Barr, and the saying of Ata and those who followed him, on the basis that This is abrogated by the verse on inheritance. If they meant what exceeded four months and ten days, then it is permissible. If they meant that the residence for four months and ten days is not obligatory in the estate of the deceased, then this is a matter of disagreement among the imams, and they are two opinions of al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. She said: So I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to return to my family in Banu Khadrah, because my husband did not leave me in a residence that he owned or provide for me. She said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. She said: So I turned away, and when I was in the room, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me or ordered me. She said: When Uthman ibn Affan came to power, he sent for me and asked me about that, so I told him and he followed it and ruled accordingly. Al-Nasa’i also narrated it with Ibn Majah through various chains of narration on the authority of Sa’d ibn Ishaq with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said when the words of God Almighty were revealed: A provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous, a man said: If you wish, you can do well, and if you wish, I will not do it. So God revealed this verse: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous. This verse was used as evidence by those scholars who believed that the provision of a divorced woman is obligatory, whether she was delegated, or had a duty imposed upon her, or was divorced before touching her, or was consummated with her. This is a statement from al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr and others from the Salaf went to it, and Ibn Jarir chose it. And whoever did not make it obligatory absolutely, specifies from this generality the meaning of God Almighty’s saying: “There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or appointed for them a dowry. And give them a provision, the wealthy according to his ability, and the poor according to his ability, a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous.” The first responded that this is from the category of mentioning some of the individuals of the generality, so there is no specification according to the well-known text, and God knows best. And His saying, Thus does God make clear to you His signs, meaning in what He has permitted and forbidden, His obligations and His limits, in what He has commanded you and forbidden you from. He has made it clear, explained and interpreted, and He has not left it ambiguous at a time when you need it. That you may understand, meaning that you may comprehend and reflect.

2:243: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they were four thousand, and on his authority they were eight thousand, and Abu Saleh said: nine thousand, and on the authority of Ibn Abbas forty thousand, and Wahb bin Munabbih and Abu Malik said: they were thirty-some thousand. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: They were the people of a village called Dawurdan. And Al-Suddi and Abu Saleh said the same, and he added: from before Wasit, and Saeed bin Abdul Aziz said: They were from the people of Adhraat, and Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ who said: This is a parable. And Ali bin Asim said: They were from the people of Dawurdan, a village one farsakh from before Wasit. And Wakee’ bin Al-Jarrah said in his interpretation: Sufyan told us on the authority of Maysarah bin Habib Al-Nahdi, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr Al-Asadi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes, and they were thousands, for fear of death? He said: They were four thousand who went forth fleeing from the plague. They said: We will come to a land where there is no death. Then when they were in such and such a place, God said to them, Die. So they died. Then a prophet from among the prophets passed by them and called upon his Lord to revive them, and He revived them. That is what God Almighty said, Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes, and they were thousands, for fear of death? The verse. More than one of the predecessors mentioned that these people were the people of a town in the time of the Children of Israel, and their land became unhealthy, and a severe epidemic struck them, so they fled to the wilderness to escape death, and they descended into a swampy valley, and they filled the space between its two sides, so God sent to them two angels, one from the bottom of the valley, and the other from the top, and they shouted at them with one shout, and they all died the death of one man, so they were herded into pens, and walls and graves were built over them, and they perished and were torn apart and dispersed, and after a long time, a prophet from the prophets of the Children of Israel, called Ezekiel, passed by them, and asked God to revive them through his hands, so He answered him to that, and He commanded him to say: O decayed bones, God commands you to come together, so the bones of every body came together, one to the other, then He commanded him to call: O bones, God commands you to be clothed with flesh, nerves and skin, and that was while he was watching, then He commanded him to call: O bones Spirits, God commands you to return every soul to the body it inhabited, so they rose alive, looking that God had revived them after their long sleep, and they said: Glory be to You, there is no god but You.
