There is no part of my body that does not have a wound, a stab or a blow, and here I am dying on my bed like a donkey dies. May the eyes of cowards never sleep. He means that he is in pain because he did not die killed in war, and he regrets that, and he is in pain that he will die on his bed. And His statement: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? God the Almighty urges His servants to spend in the way of God. God the Almighty has repeated this verse in His Noble Book in more than one place. In the hadith of revelation, God the Almighty says: Who would lend to one who is neither destitute nor unjust? Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Arfa told us, Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Hamid Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: When the verse Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him? was revealed, Abu Ad-Dahdah Al-Ansari said: O Messenger of God, does God the Almighty want a loan from us? He said: Yes, O Abu Ad-Dahdah. He said: Show me your hand, O Messenger of God. He said: So he gave him his hand, and said: I have loaned my garden to my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and he said: And his garden in which there were six hundred palm trees, and Umm Ad-Dahdah and her children were in it. He said: So Abu Ad-Dahdah came and called her: O Umm Ad-Dahdah. She said: At your service. He said: Come out, for I have loaned it to my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, with a similar chain of transmission. His saying: A good loan was narrated on the authority of Umar and others among the predecessors, meaning spending in the way of God. It was said: It means spending on children, and it was said: It means glorifying and sanctifying God. His saying: Then He will multiply it for him many times over is as God Almighty said: “The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain [of corn] which grows seven ears, in each ear is a hundred grains. And God multiplies for whom He wills” (al-Baqarah 2:174), and we will discuss it. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, who said: I came to Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, and I said to him: It has reached me that you say that a good deed is multiplied by a thousand thousand good deeds. He said: What is so strange about that? I heard it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: God multiplies a good deed by two thousand thousand good deeds. This is a strange hadith, and Ali bin Zaid bin Jud’an has some objectionable narrations, but Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another chain of transmission, and he said: Abu Khallad Sulayman bin Khallad Al-Mu’addab told us, Yunus bin Muhammad Al-Mu’addab told us, Muhammad bin Uqbah Al-Rafa’i told us, on the authority of Ziyad Al-Jassas, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, who said: No one sat with Abu Hurairah more than me, so he came before me on Hajj. He said: I came after him, and the people of Basra narrated from him that he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God multiplies a good deed by a thousand thousand good deeds. So I said: Woe to you, by God, no one sat with me more. To Abu Hurairah from me, so I did not hear this hadith, he said: I carried myself wanting to catch up with him but I found that he had set out on Hajj, so I set out on Hajj to tell him about this hadith, so I met him for this, and I said: O Abu Hurairah, what is the hadith that I heard the people of Basra narrating from you? He said: What is it? I said: They claim that you say: God multiplies the good deed a thousand thousand times over. He said: O Abu Uthman, what is that that astonishes you, when God says: Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And He says: But what is the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter but little? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God multiplies the good deed a thousand thousand times over. And in the meaning of this hadith is what was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and others on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar bin Al-Khattab, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever enters a market and says: ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things’, God will write for him a million good deeds and erase from him a million bad deeds.” The hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah Ismail bin Ibrahim bin Bassam told us, Abu Ismail Al-Mu’addab told us, on the authority of Isa bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: When the verse, The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a seed [of grain] which grows seven ears was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, My Lord, increase my Ummah, and the verse, Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over was revealed. He said, My Lord, increase my Ummah, and the verse, Only the patient will be given their reward in full, without account was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it. On the authority of Ka'b al-Ahbar: A man came to him and said: I heard a man say: Whoever recites Say, He is God, the One once, God will build for him ten thousand thousand rooms of pearls and rubies in Paradise. Do I believe that? He said: Yes. Or are you amazed by that? He said: Yes, and twenty thousand thousand and thirty thousand thousand, and none can count that except God. Then he recited: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? So the abundance from God is innumerable. And His statement: And God withholds and expands means spend and do not worry, for God is the Provider. He restricts the provision of whomever He wills of His servants, and expands it for others. He has the perfect wisdom in that. And to Him you will be returned meaning on the Day of Resurrection.
2:246: Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: This prophet is Joshua bin Nun. Ibn Jarir said: He means the son of Ephraim, the son of Joseph, the son of Jacob. This statement is far-fetched because this was a long time after Moses, and it was in the time of David, peace be upon him, as is stated in the story. There were more than a thousand years between David and Moses, and God knows best. Al-Suddi said: He is Simeon. Mujahid said: He is Samuel, peace be upon him. Muhammad bin Ishaq said the same on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih: He is Shimriel bin Bali bin Alqamah bin Tarkham bin Al-Yahed bin Bahrad bin Alqamah bin Majib bin Amusa bin Azariah bin Safiyya bin Alqamah bin Abi Yashf bin Qarun bin Yizhar bin Qahath bin Levi, Jacob bin Isaac bin Abraham, peace be upon him. Wahb ibn Munabbih and others said: The Children of Israel were on the path of righteousness for a period of time after Moses, peace be upon him, then they innovated, and some of them worshipped idols, and there were still among them prophets who commanded them to do good, forbade them from evil, and established them on the path of the Torah, until they did what they did. Then God sent their enemies against them, so they killed a great number of them, and took many people captive, and took many lands from them, and no one fought them except that they defeated him, and that was because they had the Torah, and the Ark that had been in ancient times, and that was inherited by their successors from their predecessors to Moses, peace be upon him, so they continued to persist in misguidance until some of the kings took it from them in some of the wars, and they took the Torah from their hands, and there remained among them those who preserved it except a few, and prophecy was cut off from their tribes, and there remained from the tribe of Levi, in which there were prophets, except a woman who was pregnant from her husband who had been killed, so they took her and imprisoned her in A house, and they kept it, perhaps God would grant her a boy who would be a prophet for them. The woman kept praying to God Almighty to grant her a boy, so God heard her and gave her a boy, so she named him Samuel, meaning God heard my prayer. Some of them say: Simeon, which is the same, so that boy grew up and was raised among them, and God made her grow well for them. When he reached the age of prophets, God inspired him and ordered him to call to Him and to declare His Oneness. So he called the Children of Israel, and they asked him to establish a king for them with whom they could fight their enemies. The king had also perished among them, so the Prophet said to them: Is it possible that if God establishes a king for you, you will not fight and fulfill what you pledged to fight with him? They said: Why should we not fight in the cause of God while we have been expelled from our homes and our children? That is, the country was taken from us and the children were taken captive. God Almighty said: “But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned back, except for a few of them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.” That is, they did not fulfill what they promised, but most of them refrained from fighting. And God knows them.
2:247: That is, when they asked their prophet to appoint a king from among them, he appointed Talut for them, and he was a man from their army, and he was not from the royal house among them, because the king was from the tribe of Judah, and this was not from that tribe, so they said: How can he be king over us? That is, how can he be king over us and we are more deserving of the kingship than he is and he has not been given an abundance of wealth That is, he is poor and has no wealth to support the kingship, and some of them mentioned that he was a water-carrier, and it was said: a tanner, and this is an objection from them to their prophet and stubbornness, and it would have been better for them to obey and speak well, then the prophet answered them saying: God chose him over you That is, He chose him for you from among you, and God knows him better than you, he says: I am not the one who appointed him of my own accord, rather God commanded me to do so when you asked me to do so, and He increased him abundantly in knowledge and body That is, he is, despite this, more knowledgeable than you, and more noble, and more complex than you, and stronger And patience in war and knowledge of it, meaning he is more perfect in knowledge and stature than you, and from here the king should have knowledge and good appearance and great strength in his body and soul, then he said, And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills, meaning He is the ruler who does whatever He wills, and is not questioned about what He does, and they are questioned because of His knowledge, wisdom, and compassion for His creation, and for this reason he said, And God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing, meaning He is All-Encompassing in grace, He chooses for His mercy whomever He wills, and He is All-Knowing of who deserves the kingdom and who does not deserve it.
2:248: Their prophet says to them: The sign of the blessing of the kingdom of Talut upon you is that God will return to you the Ark that was taken from you. In it is tranquility from your Lord. It was said that it means dignity and majesty. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah, In it is tranquility, meaning dignity. Al-Rabi' said: Mercy. This was also narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked Ata' about his statement, In it is tranquility from your Lord. He said: What you know of the signs of God and find peace in it. Al-Hasan al-Basri said the same. It was also said: Tranquility is a golden basin in which the hearts of the prophets were washed. God gave it to Moses, peace be upon him, and he placed the tablets in it. Al-Suddi narrated it on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ali, who said: Tranquility has a face like the face of a human being, and it is a delicate soul. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Dawud told us, Shu’bah, Hammad ibn Salamah and Abu Al-Ahwas told us, all on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid ibn Arara, on the authority of Ali, who said: Sakinah is a strong wind, and it has two heads. Mujahid said: It has two wings and a tail. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: Sakinah is the head of a dead cat. If it screams in the coffin with the scream of a cat, they will be certain of victory, and conquest will come to them. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Bakkar ibn Abdullah told us that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: Sakinah is a spirit from God that speaks. If they disagree about something, it speaks, and informs them of what they want. - And his saying, And what remains of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Muthanna told us, Abu al-Walid told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, And what remains of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, he said: His staff, and the fragments of the tablets. And this is what Qatada, al-Suddi, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Ikrimah said, and he added: And the Torah. Abu Salih said, And what remains of what the family of Moses left behind, meaning the staff of Moses, the staff of Aaron, two tablets of the Torah, and the manna. Atiyah ibn Sa’d said: The staff of Moses, the staff of Aaron, the clothes of Moses, the clothes of Aaron, and the fragments of the tablets. Abd al-Razzaq said: I asked al-Thawri about his saying, And what remains of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, and he said: Some of them say: A handful of manna, and the fragments of the tablets, and some of them say: The staff and the sandals. - And his saying, The angels carried it. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: The angels came carrying the Ark between the heaven and the earth until they placed it in front of Talut while the people were watching. Al-Suddi said: The Ark was in the house of Talut in the morning, so they believed in the prophethood of Simeon and obeyed Talut. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of some of his sheikhs, the angels brought it, driving it on a wheel on a cow, and it was said: on two cows. Another one mentioned: The Ark was in Jericho, and when the polytheists took it, they placed it in the house of their gods under their great idol, so the Ark was on top of the idol, so they lowered it and placed it under it, and it became like that, so they nailed it under it, and the idol became broken-legged, thrown far away, so they knew that this was a command from God that they could not handle, so they took the Ark out of their country, and placed it in some of the villages, and a disease struck its necks, so a slave girl from the captives of the Children of Israel ordered them to return it to the Children of Israel so that they could be freed from this disease, so they carried it on two cows and they traveled with it, and no one would approach it except that he would die, until they approached the country of the Children of Israel, so they broke the yokes and returned, and the Children of Israel came and took it, and it was said: David, peace be upon him, received it, and when he went to them, he was ashamed of his joy at that, and it was said: two young men from them, and God knows best. And it was said: The Ark was in a village of the villages of Palestine called Azdred. And His saying, Indeed in that is a sign for you, meaning, of my truthfulness in what I brought you of prophethood, and in what I commanded you to do of obeying Talut, if you are believers, meaning in God and the Last Day.
2:249: The Almighty says, informing about Talut, the king of the Children of Israel, when he went out with his soldiers, and those who obeyed him from the leaders of the Children of Israel, and his army at that time, according to what Al-Suddi mentioned, was eighty thousand, and God knows best, that he said, God will test you, meaning He will test you with a river, Ibn Abbas and others said: It is a river between Jordan and Palestine, meaning the famous Sharia River, So whoever drinks from it is not of me, meaning he will not accompany me today in this regard, And whoever does not taste it is of me, except for whoever scoops a handful with his hand, meaning there is no harm on him, God the Almighty said: So they drank from it, except for a few of them, Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Whoever scoops from it with his hand is satisfied, and whoever drinks from it is not satisfied. And this is how Al-Suddi narrated it from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, and this is how Qatada and Ibn Shawdhab said, and Al-Suddi said: The army was eighty thousand, and seventy-six thousand drank from it, and four thousand remained with it, this is what he said. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Isra'il, Sufyan Ath-Thawri and Mis'ar bin Kadam on the authority of Abu Ishaq As-Sabi'i on the authority of Al-Bara' bin Azib, who said: We used to say that the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were three hundred and a few on the day of Badr were the same number as the companions of Saul who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except believers. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Raja', on the authority of Isra'il bin Yunus, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-Bara', in a similar manner. For this reason, God Almighty said: But when he and those who believed with him crossed it, they said, 'We have no strength today against Goliath and his soldiers.' That is, they were too numerous to face their enemy because of their great number, so their scholars, who knew that God's promise was true, encouraged them, for victory from God is not due to great numbers or numbers. For this reason, they said, How often has a small company overcome a large one by God's permission? And God is with the patient.
2:250: That is, when the party of faith, who were few of the companions of Talut, faced their enemy, the companions of Goliath, who were many in number, they said, ‘Our Lord, pour out upon us patience’ that is, send down patience upon us from You and plant firmly our feet that is, in meeting the enemies, and spare us flight and helplessness and give us victory over the disbelieving people. God the Almighty said: And they defeated them by God’s permission meaning they overcame them and subdued them with God’s victory for them and David killed Goliath It was mentioned in the Israelite narrations that he killed him with a slingshot that was in his hand, he threw it at him and hit him and killed him, and Talut had promised him that if he killed Goliath he would marry him to his daughter, share his blessings with him, and make him a partner in his affairs, so he fulfilled his promise to him and then the kingdom passed to David, peace be upon him, along with what God had granted him of great prophecy. For this reason God the Almighty said: And God gave him the kingdom which was in Talut’s hand and wisdom meaning prophecy after Samuel and taught him whatever He willed meaning whatever God willed of the knowledge that was unique to him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God the Almighty said: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted meaning had God not repelled some people by means of others as He repelled the Children of Israel by fighting Talut and the bravery of David, they would have perished as God the Almighty said: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of God is much mentioned would have been pulled down the verse, and Ibn Jarir said: He told me Abu Hamid al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, Hafs ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suqah, on the authority of Wabra ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will repel calamity from a hundred of his neighbors through the righteous Muslim. Then Ibn Umar recited: And were it not that God checks some people by means of others, the earth would indeed be corrupted. This is a weak chain of transmission, for this Yahya ibn Saeed is Ibn al-Attar al-Himsi, and he is very weak. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Hamid al-Himsi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will reform through the righteousness of the Muslim man his children, his children’s children, the people of his household, and the households around him, and they will continue to be in the protection of God, the Almighty, as long as he is among them.” This is also strange and weak, based on what was mentioned above. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ali ibn Ismail ibn Hammad narrated to us. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Zaid ibn al-Habbab told us, Hammad ibn Zaid told me, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who traced the hadith back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There will remain among you seven, through whom you will be victorious, through whom you will receive rain, and through whom you will be provided for, until the command of God comes. Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad told us, Muhammad ibn Jarir ibn Yazid told us, Abu Muadh Nahar ibn Muadh ibn Uthman al-Laythi told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu al-Ash’ath al-San’ani, on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The substitutes in my nation are thirty, through whom you will receive rain, and through whom you will be victorious. Qatada said: I hope that al-Hasan will be among them. His saying, But God is full of bounty to the worlds, meaning He is full of grace and mercy towards them, and He protects them from one another, and He has the judgment, wisdom, and proof against His creation in all His actions and words. Then the Almighty said: These are the verses of God which We recite to you in truth, and indeed, you are among the messengers. That is, these are the verses of God which We have related to you regarding the matter of those whom We have mentioned in truth, that is, the reality of the matter that was in accordance with what is in the hands of the People of the Book of the truth that the scholars of the Children of Israel know. And indeed, you, O Muhammad, are among the messengers. This is an emphasis and introduction to the oath.

God the Almighty said: And they defeated them by God’s permission meaning they overcame them and subdued them with God’s victory for them and David killed Goliath It was mentioned in the Israelite narrations that he killed him with a slingshot that was in his hand, he threw it at him and hit him and killed him, and Talut had promised him that if he killed Goliath he would marry him to his daughter, share his blessings with him, and make him a partner in his affairs, so he fulfilled his promise to him and then the kingdom passed to David, peace be upon him, along with what God had granted him of great prophecy. For this reason God the Almighty said: And God gave him the kingdom which was in Talut’s hand and wisdom meaning prophecy after Samuel and taught him whatever He willed meaning whatever God willed of the knowledge that was unique to him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God the Almighty said: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted meaning had God not repelled some people by means of others as He repelled the Children of Israel by fighting Talut and the bravery of David, they would have perished as God the Almighty said: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of God is much mentioned would have been pulled down the verse, and Ibn Jarir said: He told me Abu Hamid al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, Hafs ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suqah, on the authority of Wabra ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will repel calamity from a hundred of his neighbors through the righteous Muslim. Then Ibn Umar recited: And were it not that God checks some people by means of others, the earth would indeed be corrupted. This is a weak chain of transmission, for this Yahya ibn Saeed is Ibn al-Attar al-Himsi, and he is very weak. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Hamid al-Himsi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will reform through the righteousness of the Muslim man his children, his children’s children, the people of his household, and the households around him, and they will continue to be in the protection of God, the Almighty, as long as he is among them.” This is also strange and weak, based on what was mentioned above. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ali ibn Ismail ibn Hammad narrated to us. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Zaid ibn al-Habbab told us, Hammad ibn Zaid told me, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who traced the hadith back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There will remain among you seven, through whom you will be victorious, through whom you will receive rain, and through whom you will be provided for, until the command of God comes. Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad told us, Muhammad ibn Jarir ibn Yazid told us, Abu Muadh Nahar ibn Muadh ibn Uthman al-Laythi told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu al-Ash’ath al-San’ani, on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The substitutes in my nation are thirty, through whom you will receive rain, and through whom you will be victorious. Qatada said: I hope that al-Hasan will be among them. His saying, But God is full of bounty to the worlds, meaning He is full of grace and mercy towards them, and He protects them from one another, and He has the judgment, wisdom, and proof against His creation in all His actions and words. Then the Almighty said: These are the verses of God which We recite to you in truth, and indeed, you are among the messengers. That is, these are the verses of God which We have related to you regarding the matter of those whom We have mentioned in truth, that is, the reality of the matter that was in accordance with what is in the hands of the People of the Book of the truth that the scholars of the Children of Israel know. And indeed, you, O Muhammad, are among the messengers. This is an emphasis and introduction to the oath.
2:253: God Almighty tells us that He preferred some messengers over others, as He Almighty said: And We have certainly preferred some prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms, and He said here "These are the messengers, some of them We preferred over others. Among them were those to whom God spoke," meaning Moses and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and likewise Adam, as mentioned in the hadith narrated in Sahih Ibn Hibban on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, And He raised some of them in degrees, as was proven in the hadith of the Night Journey when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the prophets in the heavens according to the differences in their status with God Almighty. If it is said, what is the connection between this verse and the hadith proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said that a Muslim man and a Jewish man quarreled, and the Jew said in an oath he was dividing: No, by Him who chose Moses over the worlds. So the Muslim raised his hand and slapped the Jew in the face, and he said: What wicked one? And over Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? The Jew came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and complained about the Muslim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not give me precedence over the prophets, for people will be struck dumb on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness. Then I will find Moses holding on to the legs of the Throne, and I will not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was rewarded with the thunderbolt of Mount Tur. So do not give me precedence over the prophets.” In another narration: Do not give precedence over the prophets. The answer has several aspects: One This was before he knew of the precedence, and there is a view on this. Second He said this out of modesty and humility. Third This is a prohibition against giving precedence in a situation like this, when you are arbitrated during a dispute or quarrel. Fourth Do not give precedence merely on the basis of opinions and fanaticism. Fifth The place of precedence is not up to you, but rather it is up to God Almighty, and you must submit and surrender to Him, and believe in Him. And His statement, And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs, meaning the conclusive arguments and evidence of the truth of what he brought to the Children of Israel, that he was the servant and messenger of God to them, and We supported him with the Holy Spirit, meaning that God supported him with Gabriel, peace be upon him. Then God Almighty said, “And if God had willed, those after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them, but they differed. And among them were those who believed and those who disbelieved. And if God had willed, they would not have fought one another,” meaning all of that is due to God’s decree and predestination, which is why they said, But God does what He wills.
2:254: God Almighty commands His servants to spend from what He has provided them in His way, the way of goodness, to save the reward for that with their Lord and King, and to hasten to do that in this worldly life, before there comes a Day meaning the Day of Resurrection in which there will be no selling, no friendship, no intercession meaning no one will be sold for himself, nor will he be ransomed for money even if he were to give it, even if he were to bring the earth full of gold, and no one’s friendship will benefit him, meaning his friendship, nor even his kinship, as He said, Then when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another nor intercession: meaning the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them. His saying, And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers, is a subject confined to its predicate, meaning, there is no wrongdoer more wrongdoing than the one who meets God on that Day as a disbeliever. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Dinar that he said: Praise be to God who said, And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers, and did not say, And the wrongdoers are the disbelievers.
2:255: This is the Throne Verse, and it has a great status. It has been authenticated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that it is the best verse in the Book of God. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Saeed Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Saleel, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rabah, on the authority of Abu - who is Ibn Ka'b - that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him, Which verse in the Book of God is the greatest? He said, God and His Messenger know best. He repeated it several times, then he said, The Throne Verse. He said, Congratulations to you, Abu Al-Mundhir, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it has a tongue and lips that sanctify the King at the foot of the Throne. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Abdul A'la bin Abdul A'la, on the authority of Al-Jariry, and he did not have the addition: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, etc. Another hadith on the authority of my father also on the merit of Ayat al-Kursi, Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi told us, Mubashar told us on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abdah bin Abi Lubabah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi bin Ka’b, that his father told him that he had a jar of dates. He said: My father used to look after it, but he found it decreasing. He said: So he guarded it one night, and behold, it was a beast resembling a young boy. He said: So I greeted it, and it returned the greeting. He said: So I said: Who are you? Are you a jinn or a human? He said: A jinn. He said: Give me your hand. He said: So he gave me his hand, and behold, it was the hand of a dog and the hair of a dog. I said: This is how the jinn were created. He said: I know that there is none among the jinn stronger than me. I said: So what made you do what you did? He said: I have heard that you are a man who loves charity, so we wanted to share in your food. He said: So my father said to him: What will protect us from you? He said: This verse, the Throne Verse. Then he went to the Prophet and told him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The wicked one has spoken the truth. And thus Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Harb bin Shaddad, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Al-Hadrami bin Lahiq, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Abi bin Kaab, on the authority of his grandfather, on his authority. And Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Another path Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, `Uthman ibn Ghiyath told us, he said: I heard Abu al-Salil say: A man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to talk to people until they became too many for him, so he would climb onto the roof of a house and talk to people. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which verse in the Qur’an is the greatest? A man said: God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Sustaining. He said: So he put his hand between my shoulders, and I felt its coolness between my breasts, or he said: So he put his hand between my breasts, and I felt its coolness between my shoulders, and he said: May knowledge be pleasant to you, O Abu al-Mundhir. Another hadith on the authority of Al-Asqa’ Al-Baqri. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Abu Zaid Al-Qurtisi told us, Ya’qub bin Abi Abbad Al-Makki told us, Muslim bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Umar bin Ata’ told me that the freed slave of Ibn Al-Asqa’ was a truthful man, he told him on the authority of Al-Asqa’ Al-Bakri, that he heard him say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them describing the emigrants, and a man asked him: Which verse in the Qur’an is the greatest? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Drowsiness does not overtake Him nor sleep,” until the verse was completed. Another hadith - On the authority of Anas - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Al-Harith told us, Salamah bin Wardan told me, that Anas bin Malik told him, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked a man from among his companions, saying, ‘O so-and-so, have you married? ’ He said, ‘No, and I do not have anything with which to marry. ’ He said, ‘Do you not have Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad? ’ He said, ‘Yes. ’ He said, ‘A quarter of the Qur’an. ’ He said, ‘Do you not have Qul Ya Alayhi Al-Kafirun? ’ He said, ‘Yes. ’ He said, ‘A quarter of the Qur’an. ’ He said, ‘Do you not have Idha Zalat? ’ He said, ‘Yes. ’ He said, ‘A quarter of the Qur’an. ’ He said, ‘Do you not have Idha Fazal God... Ayat Al-Kursi? ’ He said, ‘Yes. ’ He said, ‘A quarter of the Qur’an. ’ He said, ‘Do you not have Idha Wa Haram? ’ He said, ‘Yes. ’ He said, ‘A quarter of the Qur’an. ’ He said, ‘Do you not have Ayat Al-Kursi: God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. ’ He said, ‘Yes. ’ He said, ‘A quarter of the Qur’an. ’ He said, ‘Do you not have Idha Wa Haram Al-Kafirun? ’ He said, ‘Yes. ’ He said, ‘A quarter of the Qur’an. ’ He said, ‘Do you not have Idha Wa Har Another hadith on the authority of Abu Dharr Jundub bin Junada. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, al-Mas`udi narrated to us, Abu `Umar al-Dimashqi informed me, on the authority of `Ubayd al-Khashkhash, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the mosque and sat down. He said: “O Abu Dharr, have you prayed?” I said: No. He said: Get up and pray. So I got up and prayed, then sat down. He said: O Abu Dharr, seek refuge in God from the evil of the devils of mankind and jinn. I said: O Messenger of God, are there devils among mankind? He said: Yes. I said: O Messenger of God, prayer? He said: It is the best prescribed, whoever wishes, may do less, and whoever wishes, may do more. I said: O Messenger of God, what about fasting? He said: It is an obligatory duty and is rewarded, and with God is more. I said: O Messenger of God, what about charity? He said: It is multiplied many times over. I said: O Messenger of God, which of them is best? He said: The effort of one who is poor, or gives to a poor person. I said: O Messenger of God, which of the prophets was the first? He said: Adam. I said: O Messenger of God, was there a prophet? He said: Yes, a prophet who was spoken to. I said: O Messenger of God, how many were the messengers? He said: Three hundred and fifteen, a large crowd, and he said once, and fifteen. I said: O Messenger of God, which of what was revealed to you is the greatest? He said: The Throne Verse: God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Narrated by Al-Nasa’i. Another hadith on the authority of Abu Ayoub Khalid bin Zaid Al-Ansari, may God be pleased with him and satisfy him. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of his brother Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, “On the authority of Abu Ayyub, that he was in a clearing of his, and the ghoul used to come and take, so he complained about it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: When you see it, say: In the name of God, answer the Messenger of God. He said: So it came, so he said to it, so he took it, and it said: I will not return, so he released it, so he came and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What has happened to your prisoner? He said: I took it, and it said: I will not return, so I released it, so he said: It is returning, so I took it two or three times, and each time it said: I will not return, so he said: It is returning, so I took it, and it said: Send me, and I will teach you something to say so that nothing will come near you, the Throne Verse, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he told him, so he said: She has spoken the truth and she is a liar.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Fada’il al-Qur’an on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri with it, and he said: It is good and strange. The ghoul in the language of the Arabs is the jinn if It appears at night. Al-Bukhari mentioned this story on the authority of Abu Hurairah, so he said in the Book of the Virtues of the Qur’an, and in the Book of Agency, and in the Description of Satan in his Sahih, Uthman bin Al-Haitham Abu Amr said: Aouf told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entrusted me with guarding the zakat of Ramadan, and a man came to me and began to scoop up food. I took him and said: I will take you to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Leave me, for I am in need and have children and I have a great need. He said: So I left him and in the morning, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Hurairah, what did your prisoner do last night? He said: I said, O Messenger of God, he complained of a great need and children, so I took pity on him and let him go. He said: He lied to you and will return. I knew that he would return because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that he would return, so I lay in wait for him, and he came scooping up food, so I took him and said: I will take you to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Leave me, for I am in need and have children. Children, I will not return. So I took pity on him and let him go. In the morning, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to me, O Abu Hurairah, what did your prisoner do last night? I said, O Messenger of God, he complained of need and children, so I took pity on him and let him go. He said, He has lied to you and will return. So I watched him a third time, and he came scooping up food. I seized him and said, “I will take you to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and this is the last of the three times that you claim that you will not return and then return.” He said, Let me teach you some words by which God will benefit you. I said, What are they? He said, “When you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi: ‘God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining,’ until you finish the verse, for there will be a guardian from God over you, and no devil will come near you until morning.” So I let him go. In the morning, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to me, What did your prisoner do last night? I said, O Messenger of God, he claimed that he would teach me some words by which God would benefit me. So I let him go. He said, What are they? He said to me: When you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi from the beginning until you finish the verse: God - there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. And he said to me: There will remain upon you a guardian from God, and no devil will come near you until morning. And they were the most eager of all to do good. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Has he not told you the truth, even though he is a liar? Do you know whom you have been addressing for three nights, O Abu Hurairah? I said: No. He said, That is a devil. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in a definitive manner. Al-Nasa'i narrated it in Al-Yawm wa Al-Laylah on the authority of Ibrahim bin Ya'qub, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Haitham, and he mentioned it. It was narrated from another source on the authority of Abu Hurairah in another context similar to this. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said in his interpretation: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Amruwayh Al-Saffar narrated to us, Ahmad bin Zuhair bin Harb narrated to us, Muslim bin Ibrahim informed us, Ismail bin Muslim Al-Abdi informed us, Abu Al-Mutawakkil Al-Naji informed us that Abu Hurairah had the key to the house of charity, and there were dates in it. One day he went and opened the door, and found that a handful of dates had been taken from it. He entered another day and found that a handful of dates had been taken from it. Then he entered a third day and found that the same amount had been taken from it. Abu Hurairah complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, Do you want to take this companion of yours? He said, Yes. He said, So when you open the door, say, 'Glory be to Him who has subjected you, Muhammad. So he went and opened the door and said, Glory be to Him who has subjected you to Muhammad. He was standing before him. He said, O enemy of God, you are the one who did this. He said, "Yes, leave me alone, for I will not return. I only take it from a poor family of jinn." So he left him alone. Then he returned a second time, then a third time. I said, "Did you not promise me that you would not return? I will not leave you today until I take you to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace." He said, Do not do that, for if you leave me alone, I will teach you words that, if you say them, no jinn, young or old, male or female, will come near you. He said to him, You must do that? He said, Yes. He said, What are they? He said, God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. He recited the Throne Verse until he finished it, then he left it and went away and did not return. Abu Hurairah mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, Do you not know that it is like that? Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Shu’ayb ibn Harb, on the authority of Ismail ibn Muslim, on the authority of Abu al-Mutawakkil, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with it. A similar incident had also occurred to Abu ibn Ka’b, so these are three incidents. Another story Abu Ubaid said in the book of Al-Gharib: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: A man from among mankind went out, and a man from among the jinn met him and said: Will you wrestle with me? If you defeat me, I will teach you a verse that if you recite it when you enter your house, no devil will enter it. So he wrestled with him and defeated him, and he said: I see that you are small and thin, as if your arms are the arms of a dog. Is this how you are, O all of you jinn, or are you among them? He said: I am well-versed among them. So he came back to me and wrestled with him, and the human defeated him. Then he said: Recite the Throne Verse, for no one recites it when he enters his house except that the devil comes out, and he has a fart like the fart of a donkey. So it was said to Ibn Masoud: Is it Umar? He said: Who could he be but Umar? Abu Ubaid said: The small one is the one with a thin body, and the khaikh with the voiced kha, and it is said with the silent ha’ is the fart. Another hadith on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah said in his Mustadrak: Ali bin Hamshan told us, Sufyan told us, Bishr bin Musa told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Hakim bin Jubayr Al-Asadi told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Surat Al-Baqarah contains a verse that is the master of the verses of the Qur’an. If it is recited in a house in which there is a devil, he will leave it: Ayat Al-Kursi.” And he narrated it in the same way from another chain of transmission on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubayr. Then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, but they did not include it. This is what he said. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Za’idah, and its wording is: “Everything has a peak, and the peak of the Qur’an is Surat Al-Baqarah. In it is a verse that is the master of the verses of the Qur’an: Ayat Al-Kursi.” Then he said: It is strange. We do not know it except from the hadith of Hakim bin Jubayr. Shu’bah spoke about it and declared it weak. I said And Ahmad and Yahya bin Ma’in and more than one of the imams declared it weak, and Ibn Mahdi abandoned it and Al-Sa’di declared it a liar. Another hadith Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdul-Baqi bin Nafi’ told us, Isa bin Muhammad Al-Marwazi told us, Umar bin Muhammad Al-Bukhari told us, Isa bin Ghanjar told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Kaysan, Yahya told us, Ibn Aqil told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Ya’mar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab: That he went out one day to the people while they were gathering and said: Who among you will tell me the greatest verse in the Qur’an? Ibn Mas’ud said: I have fallen upon the expert, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The greatest verse in the Qur’an is ‘God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.’ Another hadith In its inclusion of the greatest name of God, Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Bakr told us, Abdullah bin Ziyad told us, Shahr bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Asma bint Yazid bin Al-Sakn, she said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about these two verses, God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and “Alif, Lam, Meem. God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining,” In them is the greatest name of God. And thus Abu Dawud narrated it, on the authority of Musaddad, and Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ali bin Khashram, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, all three of them on the authority of Isa bin Yunus, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abi Ziyad, with it, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Another hadith in the meaning of this, on the authority of Umamah, may God be pleased with him, Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Ismail told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Abdullah bin Al-Ala bin Zaid told us that he heard Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman narrating on the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, who said: “The greatest name of God, by which if He is called upon, He answers, is in three: Surat Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, and Ta-Ha.” Hisham, who is Ibn Ammar, the preacher of Damascus, said: As for Al-Baqarah and God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and in Al-Imran “Alif, Lam, Meem. God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining,” and in Ta-Ha And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Another hadith on the authority of Abu Umamah regarding the merit of reciting it after the obligatory prayer. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Muhriz ibn Musawwar al-Adami told us, Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan told us, al-Husayn ibn Bishr told us in Tarsus, Muhammad ibn Himyar told us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except death. And this is how al-Nasa’i narrated it in al-Yawm wa al-Laylah, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Bishr, and Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Himyar, who is al-Himsi, also one of the men of al-Bukhari, so its chain of transmission meets the criteria of al-Bukhari. Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi claimed that it is a fabricated hadith, and God knows best. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar to this hadith on the authority of Ali, al-Mughira ibn Shu’bah, and Jabir ibn Abdullah, but there is weakness in the chain of transmission of each of them. Ibn Mardawayh also said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Muqri told us, Yahya ibn Darastawayh al-Marwazi told us, Ziyad ibn Ibrahim told us, Abu Hamza al-Sakri told us, on the authority of al-Muthanna, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God revealed to Moses ibn Imran, peace be upon him, to recite Ayat al-Kursi after every prescribed prayer, for whoever recites it after every prescribed prayer, I will give him the heart of the grateful, the tongue of the rememberers, the reward of the prophets, and the deeds of the truthful. No one perseveres in this except a prophet, a truthful person, or a servant whose heart has been tested for faith, or who is intended to be killed in the way of God.” This is a very strange hadith. Another hadith that it protects whoever recites it at the beginning of the day and the beginning of the night. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Yahya bin Al-Mughira Abu Salamah Al-Makhzumi Al-Madani told us, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Al-Maliki, on the authority of Zurarah bin Mus`ab, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites ‘Ha Meem’ The Believer to ‘To Him is the destination’ and the Throne Verse in the morning, will be protected by them until the evening, and whoever recites them in the evening will be protected by them until the morning.” Then he said: This is a strange hadith, and some of the people of knowledge have spoken about Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr bin Abi Maleka Al-Maliki, regarding his memorization. There are other hadiths about its merits, which we have left out for the sake of brevity due to their lack of authenticity and the weakness of their chains of transmission, such as the hadith of Ali about reciting it during cupping, that it takes the place of two cuppings. And the hadith of Abu Hurairah about writing it on the left hand with saffron seven times, and licking it to memorize it and not forget, both of which were mentioned by Ibn Mardawayh, and others. This verse contains ten independent sentences. His saying, God, there is no god but He, is a statement that He is the One who is unique in divinity for all creation. The Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, meaning the Ever-Living in Himself who never dies, the Sustainer of all others. Omar used to recite the Qiyam, so all existence is in need of Him, and He is independent of them, they do not exist without His command, like His saying, And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command, and His saying, Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep, meaning He is not afflicted by deficiency, heedlessness, or neglect of His creation, rather He is in charge of every soul for what it has earned, Witness over all things, nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing is hidden from Him. And part of the perfection of Self-Sustaining is that He is not afflicted by drowsiness or sleep, so His saying, Neither overtakes Him, means drowsiness, which is sleepiness and drowsiness, does not overcome Him, and for this reason he said, nor sleep, because it is stronger than drowsiness. In Sahih, on the authority of Abu Musa, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us and said four words, and he said: “God does not sleep, and it is not befitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the balance and raises it. The deeds of the day are raised to Him before the deeds of the night, and the deeds of the night before the deeds of the day. His veil is light or fire. If He were to remove it, the radiance of His face would burn everything that His sight reaches of His creation.” And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us, al-Hakam ibn Abaan informed me, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep, that Moses, peace be upon him, asked the angels: Does God Almighty sleep? Then God Almighty inspired the angels and ordered them to keep him awake for three days, so that they would not let him sleep, so they did, then they gave him two bottles, so he held them, then they left him and warned him not to break them. He said: So he began to doze off while they were in his hand, and in each hand there was one. He said: So he began to doze off and wake up, and doze off and wake up, until he dozed off, then he struck one of them with the other and broke them. Muammar said: It is only an example that God Almighty made, saying: So the heavens and the earth are in His hand, and thus Ibn Jarir narrated it, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Yahya, on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, and he mentioned it, and it is from the report of the Children of Israel, and it is from what is known that Moses, peace be upon him, is not unaware of such a matter of God Almighty, and that He is far removed from it, and stranger than all of this is the hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir: Ishaq bin Abi Israel told us. Hisham bin Yusuf narrated to us, on the authority of Umayyah bin Shibl, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Aban, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abu Ikrimah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating about Moses, peace be upon him, on the pulpit. He said: “It occurred to Moses, ‘Does God sleep?’ So he sent an angel to him, who kept him awake for three days. Then he gave him two bottles, one in each hand, and ordered him to keep them. He said: ‘So he began to sleep, and his hands almost met, and he would wake up and hold one over the other, until he fell asleep, and his hands clapped together and the two bottles broke.’ He said: ‘God, the Almighty, the Majestic, set forth an example, that if God were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not hold together.’” This is a very strange hadith, and it is most likely that it is an Israelite hadith, not a hadith traceable back to the Prophet, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Al-Qasim bin Atiyah told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Dashtaki told us, my father told me on the authority of his father, Ash'ath bin Ishaq told us on the authority of Ja'far bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Children of Israel said: O Moses, does your Lord sleep? He said: Fear God. So his Lord, the Almighty, called to him: O Moses, they ask you, does your Lord sleep? Take two bottles in your hands and get up tonight. So Moses did, and when a third of the night had passed, he dozed off and fell on his knees, then he recovered and held them together. When it was the end of the night, he dozed off and the two bottles fell and broke. He said: O Moses, if I were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would fall and they would perish just as the two bottles in your hands perished. So God, the Almighty, revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Throne Verse. His saying, To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, is a statement that all are His servants and in His kingdom, and under His control and authority, like His saying, “There is none in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them exactly. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.” And His saying, Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? is like His saying, And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after God has given permission to whomever He wills and is pleased with. And like His saying, And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased. This is from His greatness, majesty, and pride, the Almighty and Majestic, that no one dares to intercede for anyone with Him except with His permission for him to intercede, as in the hadith of intercession: “I come beneath the Throne and prostrate, and He leaves me as long as God wills that He leaves me. Then it is said, ‘Raise your head and say, “You hear, and intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.” He said, Then He sets a limit for me and I admit them into Paradise. His statement: He knows what is before them and what is behind them is evidence of His comprehensive knowledge of all beings, their past, present, and future, like His statement, informing us about the angels: “And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that. And your Lord is not forgetful.” His statement: And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills means that no one has access to anything of God’s knowledge except what God Almighty has informed him of and made him aware of. It is possible that what is meant is that they do not have access to anything of the knowledge of His essence and attributes except what God has informed them of, like His statement: And they do not encompass Him in knowledge. And His statement: His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Mutraf bin Tarif, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth, he said: His knowledge. And Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Abdullah bin Idris and Hisham, both of them on the authority of Mutraf bin Tarif with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: And something similar was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, then Ibn Jarir said: And others said the Throne is the place of the feet, then he narrated it on the authority of Abu Musa, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak, and Muslim Al-Batin. And Shuja’ bin Mukhallad said in his interpretation: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ammar Al-Dhahabi, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God Almighty: His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth? He said: His Kursi is the place of His feet, and the Throne is not estimated except by God, the Almighty and Majestic. This is how this hadith was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh on the authority of Shuja’ bin Mukhallad Al-Fallas, so he mentioned it, and he made a mistake. It was narrated by Wakee’ in his Tafsir: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ammar Al-Dhahabi, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Kursi is the place of the feet, and no one can estimate the value of the Throne. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Muadh, on the authority of Abu Asim, on the authority of Sufyan, who is Al-Thawri, with his chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a similar chain of transmission, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, but they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Al-Hakim bin Dhahir Al-Ghazari Al-Kufi, and he is rejected, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but it is also not authentic. Al-Suddi said, on the authority of Abu Malik: The Kursi is under the Throne. Al-Suddi said: The heavens and the earth are inside the Kursi, and the Kursi is in front of the Throne. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If the seven heavens and the seven earths were spread out and then connected to each other, they would not be in comparison to the vastness of the Kursi except as a ring in a desert. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told me, Ibn Zayd said: My father told me, he said: The Messenger of God said: The seven heavens in comparison to the Kursi are like seven dirhams thrown into a shield. He said: Abu Dharr said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The Kursi in comparison to the Throne is like an iron ring thrown into a desert. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Sulayman bin Ahmad told us, Abdullah bin Wahib al-Muqri told us, Muhammad bin Abi al-Sarri al-Asqalani told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Tamimi told us, on the authority of al-Qasim bin Muhammad al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, that he asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the Throne, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the seven heavens and the seven earths are nothing compared to the Throne but a ring cast in a desert land, and the superiority of the Throne over the Throne is like the superiority of the desert land over that ring.” Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Zuhair narrated to us, Ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Khalifa, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, who said: A woman came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Ask God to admit me into Paradise. He said: So the Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, glorified Him and said: His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth, and it creaks like the creaking of a new saddle because of its weight. It was narrated by Al-Hafiz Al-Bazzar in his famous Musnad, and by Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir in their Tafsirs, and by Al-Tabarani and Ibn Abi Asim in their two books on the Sunnah, and by Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya in his book Al-Mukhtar from the hadith of Abu Ishaq Al-Sabi'i, on the authority of Abdullah bin Khalifa, and it is not that famous, and there is doubt about his hearing it from Umar. Then some of them narrate it from him on the authority of Umar as a mursal, and some of them narrate it from him as a mursal, and some of them add a strange addition to its text, and some of them delete it. Stranger than this is the hadith of Jubayr bin Mut'im on the description of the Throne, as narrated by Abu Dawud in his book on the Sunnah from his Sunan, and God knows best. Ibn Mardawayh and others narrated hadiths from Buraydah, Jabir and others about the placement of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection to separate judgments. It appears that this is not mentioned in this verse. Some Islamic astronomers have claimed that the Throne is, according to them, the eighth sphere, which is the sphere of fixed things, above which is the ninth sphere, which is the etheric sphere and is called the Atlas. Others have rejected this. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Juwaybir on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to say: The Throne is the Throne. What is correct is that the Throne is not the Throne, and the Throne is larger than it, as indicated by the traces and reports. Ibn Jarir relied on the hadith of Abdullah bin Khalifa on the authority of Umar on this, but I have a question about its authenticity. And God knows best. And His statement: And He is not burdened by their preservation means that He is not burdened or overwhelmed by the preservation of the heavens and the earth, and whoever is in them, and whoever is between them, rather it is easy for Him, simple for Him, and He is the One who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned, the Watcher over all things, so nothing is hidden from Him and nothing is absent from Him, and all things are insignificant in His hands, He who is not questioned about what He does, while they are questioned, and He is the Subduer of all things, the Accountant over all things, the Watcher, the Most High, the Magnificent, there is no god but Him, and no Lord but Him, so His statement: And He is the Most High, the Magnificent is like His statement: The Great, the Most High. These verses and what is similar to them from the authentic hadiths, the best in them is the method of the righteous predecessors, they left them as they came without specification or likening.
2:256: God Almighty says: There is no compulsion in religion meaning do not force anyone to enter the religion of Islam, for it is clear and evident, its evidence and proofs are obvious, and there is no need for anyone to be forced to enter it. Rather, whoever God guides to Islam, opens his heart, and enlightens his insight, enters it with clear evidence. And whoever God blinds his heart and seals his hearing and sight, then entering the religion under compulsion and coercion will not benefit him. They have mentioned that the reason for the revelation of this verse was about a group of the Ansar, even though its ruling is general. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A woman would be a free woman, and she would promise that if she had a child alive, she would convert to Judaism. When Banu Nadir were expelled, there were some of the sons of the Ansar among them, so they said: We will not abandon our sons. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “There is no compulsion in religion. Verily, the right course has become distinct from error.” Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i both narrated it on the authority of Bandar on his authority, and from other chains of transmission on the authority of Shu’bah on his authority, something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Shu’bah on his authority, and this is how Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha’bi, al-Hasan al-Basri and others mentioned that it was revealed regarding that. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad al-Harshi, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: There is no compulsion in religion. He said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar from Banu Salim ibn Awf, called al-Husayni, who had two Christian sons and he was a Muslim man. So he said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why don’t you compel them, for they have refused to accept anything but Christianity? So God revealed that about him. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Al-Suddi narrated something similar to that, and added: They had become Christians at the hands of merchants who came from Ash-Sham carrying oil. When they decided to go with them, their father wanted to force them, and he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to send after them, so this verse was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Amr ibn Awf told us, Sharik told us on the authority of Abu Hilal on the authority of Asq, who said: I was in their religion a Christian slave of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, so he used to offer me Islam, but I refused, so he would say, There is no compulsion in religion, and he would say, O Asq, if you had become Muslim, we would have sought your help in some of the affairs of the Muslims. A large group of scholars have said that this applies to the People of the Book, and whoever entered their religion before the abrogation and change if they paid the jizyah. Others said: Rather, it was abrogated by the verse on fighting, and that all nations must be called to enter the true religion, the religion of Islam. If one of them refused to enter it, and did not submit to it or pay the jizyah, he would be fought until he was killed. This is the meaning of Coercion, God Almighty said: “You will be called to a people of great strength. You will fight them or they will submit.” And God Almighty said: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And God Almighty said: “O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you and let them find in you harshness. And know that God is with the righteous.” And in the Sahih: Your Lord is amazed at a people who are led to Paradise in chains, meaning the prisoners who are brought to the lands of Islam in documents, shackles, chains and shackles, then after that they submit, and their deeds and inner selves are reformed, so they are among the people of Paradise. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Yahya told us on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man who had converted to Islam, he said: I find myself reluctant, he said: Even if you are reluctant, then it is a correct triliteral, but it is not of this type, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not force him to convert to Islam, rather he called him to it, and informed him that his soul was not receptive to it, rather it was reluctant, so he said to him: Convert to Islam even if you are reluctant, for God will grant you good intention and sincerity. And His statement: “So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in God has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And God is Hearing and Knowing.” That is, whoever rejects rivals and idols, and what Satan calls for of worshipping everything that is worshipped besides God, and believes in the Oneness of God and worships Him alone, and bears witness that there is no god but Him, has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. That is, he has been steadfast in his matter, and has adhered to the best path and the straight path. Abu Qasim al-Baghawi said: Abu Ruh al-Baldi told us, Abu al-Ahwas Salam bin Salim told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hassan, who is the son of Qaid al-Absi, who said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Magic is magic, and Taghut is Satan, and courage and cowardice are instincts that exist in men. The brave man fights for someone he does not know, and the coward flees from his mother, even if a man is noble in his religion, and his lineage is his character, even if he is Persian or Nabataean. Thus, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hassan bin Qaid al-Absi, on the authority of Umar, and he mentioned it. The meaning of his statement about the tyrant: he is the devil, is very strong, as it includes every evil that the people of ignorance were doing, from worshipping idols and resorting to them for judgment, and seeking their help. And his saying: He has grasped the firmest handhold that will never break means he has grasped the religion with the strongest reason, and he likened that to a strong handhold that will never break, it is in itself firm, solid and strong and its bond is strong and intense, and for this reason he said: He has grasped the firmest handhold that will never break verse. Mujahid said: The firmest handhold means faith. Al-Suddi said: It is Islam. Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Dahhak said: It means there is no god but God. Anas bin Malik said: The firmest handhold is the Qur’an. Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d said: It is love for the sake of God and hatred for the sake of God. All of these statements are correct and there is no contradiction between them. Muadh ibn Jabal said about his statement: Its continuity will not break without entering Paradise. Mujahid and Saeed ibn Jubayr said: He has grasped the firmest handhold that will never break. Then he recited: Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Yusuf told us, Ibn Awf told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Abbad, who said: I was in the mosque, and a man came with signs of humility on his face, so he prayed two rak’ahs in which he made them brief. The people said: This is a man from the people of Paradise. When he left, I followed him until he entered his house, and I entered with him and spoke to him. When he felt comfortable, I said to him: When the people entered the mosque, they said: So-and-so. He said: Glory be to God, it is not appropriate for anyone to say what he does not know. I will tell you why. I saw a vision during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I narrated it to him. I saw as if I was in a green garden. Ibn Awn said: He mentioned its greenery and spaciousness. In the middle of it was an iron column, the bottom of which was in the ground and the top of which was in the sky, at the top of a handle. I was told to climb up on it, but I said: I cannot. Then a middleman came to me - Ibn Awn said: He was the servant - and lifted my clothes from behind me and said: Climb up. So I climbed up until I took hold of the handle. He said: Hold on to the handle. I woke up and it was in my hand. I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him about it. He said: As for the garden, it is the garden of Islam. As for the pillar, it is the pillar of Islam. As for the handle, it is the firmest handle. You are upon Islam until you die. He said: He is Abdullah bin Salam. They included it in their two Sahihs on the authority of Abdullah bin Awn, so I went to him. Al-Bukhari included it from another chain of transmission, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin. Another way and another context Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa and Uthman informed us, they said: Hammad bin Salamah informed us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of Kharsha bin Al-Har, he said: I came to Madinah and sat with an elder in the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an old man came leaning on his stick, and the people said: Whoever is pleased to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this one. He stood behind a pillar and prayed two rak’ahs. I said to him: Some people said: Such and such. He said: Paradise belongs to God, and He admits whomever He wills. I saw a vision during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if a man came to me and said: Go. So I went with him and he took me along a great path. A path was shown to my left, and I wanted to take it. He said: You are not one of its people. Then a path was shown to my right, and I took it until I reached a slippery mountain. He took me by the hand and made me walk until I took hold of the handle. He said: Hold on. I said: Yes. He kicked the pillar with his foot, and I held on to the handle. I told the story to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: I have seen something good. As for the great path, it is the place of assembly.
