As for the path shown to your left, it is the path of the people of Hell, and you are not one of its people. As for the path shown to your right, it is the path of the people of Paradise. As for the slippery mountain, it is the abode of the martyrs. As for the handle that you held on to, it is the handle of Islam. So hold on to it until you die.” He said: I only hope to be among the people of Paradise. He said: “And if he is Abdullah bin Salam, then this is how it was narrated by Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Ahmad bin Sulayman on the authority of Affan, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Shaybah on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Musa Al-Ashib, both of them on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah with a similar chain of transmission. Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musah, on the authority of Kharsha bin Al-Har Al-Fazari with a similar chain of transmission.
2:257: The Almighty informs us that He guides those who follow His pleasure to the paths of peace, and He brings His believing servants out of the darkness of disbelief, doubt and suspicion into the light of the clear, evident, evident, easy and illuminating truth, and that the disbelievers are only supported by Satan, who makes their ignorance and misguidance seem attractive to them, and leads them out and deviates them from the path of truth into disbelief and slander. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. For this reason, the Almighty used the word light alone, and the word darkness in the plural, because the truth is one and disbelief is of many kinds, but they are false, as He said, “And this is My straight path, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path. This He has enjoined upon you that you may become righteous.” The Almighty also said, And He has made darkness and light. The Almighty also said, On the right and the left, and other verses whose wording indicates the uniqueness of the truth and the spread, uniqueness and branching of falsehood. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Maysarah told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abi Uthman told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid, who said: The people of desires will be resurrected, or he said: The people of trials will be resurrected. So whoever’s desire is faith, his trial will be white and luminous, and whoever’s desire is disbelief, his trial will be black and dark. Then he recited this verse: “God is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light. But as for those who disbelieve, their allies are false deities. They bring them out from the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.”
2:258: This one who argued with Abraham about his Lord is the King of Babylon, Nimrod bin Canaan bin Cush bin Sam bin Noah, and it is said Nimrod bin Falakh bin Ubar bin Shalih bin Arphaxad bin Sam bin Noah, and the first is the opinion of Mujahid and others. Mujahid said: The kings of the world, its easts and its wests, are four: two believers and two disbelievers. The two believers are Solomon bin David and Dhul-Qarnayn, and the two disbelievers are Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar, and God knows best. The meaning of his saying: Have you not seen that is, in your heart, O Muhammad, the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, that is, the existence of his Lord, and that is because he denied that there was a god other than Him, as Pharaoh said after him to his al-Nas 114:I do not know of any god for you other than me. What led him to this tyranny, severe disbelief, and intense obstinacy was his arrogance and the length of his reign. It is said that he remained in his kingdom for four hundred years, and for this reason he said: If God gave him the kingdom. He asked Abraham for evidence of the existence of the Lord to whom he called, so Abraham said: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. That is, the evidence of his existence is the occurrence of these things, the observation after their nonexistence, and their nonexistence after their existence. This is evidence of the existence of the doer of choice, necessarily, because they did not occur by themselves, so they must have a Creator who brought them into existence, and He is the Lord to whom I call to worship alone, with no partner. At that point, the disputer - who was Nimrod - said: I give life and cause death. Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Suddi, and others said: That is because two men were brought to me, and they deserved to be killed, so I ordered the killing of one of them - so he was killed, and I ordered the pardon of the other, so he was not killed. That is the meaning of giving life and causing death. And it appears - and God knows best - that he did not mean this because it is not an answer to what Abraham said, nor is it in its meaning because it does not prevent the existence of the Creator. Rather, he wanted to claim this position for himself out of stubbornness and obstinacy and to give the impression that he is the doer of that, and that he is the one who gives life and causes death, as Pharaoh followed in his saying: I do not know of any god for you other than me. That is why Abraham said to him, when he claimed this obstinacy: Then God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west. That is, if you are as you claim, that you give life and cause death, then the one who gives life and causes death is the one who controls existence in creating its essence and subjugating its planets and movements. So this sun appears every day from the east. If you are a god as you claim, who gives life and causes death, then bring it from the west? When he knew his weakness and his isolation and that he was not able to resist in this situation, he was dumbfounded, that is, he was mute, so he did not speak, and the proof was established against him. God Almighty said: And God does not guide the wrongdoing people, that is, He does not inspire them with an argument or proof, rather their argument is invalid with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment. This revelation in this sense is better than what many logicians have mentioned. Abraham’s deviation from the first situation to the second situation is a transition from evidence to a clearer one. Some of them may use the phrase a vision that destroys it, but it is not as they said. Rather, the first situation is like an introduction to the second, and it shows the invalidity of what Nimrod claimed in the first and second, and praise and thanks be to God. Al-Suddi mentioned that this debate was between Abraham and Nimrod after Abraham came out of the fire, and he had not met the king until that day, so this debate took place between them. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, that Nimrod had food and people used to come to him for provisions. So Ibrahim came with a group of others to bring provisions, and there was this debate between them. Ibrahim was not given as much food as he gave to the people, but rather he went out without any food with him. So when he approached his family, he went to a mound of dirt and filled his two buckets with it, and said: I will distract my family from me when I come to them. So when he came, he put down his baggage, came, leaned back, and slept. So his wife Sarah went to the buckets and found them full of good food, so she prepared food. So when Ibrahim woke up, he found what they had prepared, so he said: Where did you get this? She said: Who brought it? So he knew that it was provision from God Almighty. Zaid bin Aslam said: God sent an angel to that tyrannical king, ordering him to believe in God, but he refused. Then he called him a second time, but he refused, then a third time, but he refused. He said: Gather your forces and gather my forces. So Nimrod gathered his army and soldiers at sunrise, and God sent upon them a swarm of mosquitoes such that they could not see the sun. God set them on them, and they ate their flesh and blood, and left them exposed bones. One of them entered the king’s nostrils, and it remained in the king’s nostrils for four hundred years, and God tormented him with it. He would hit his head with the gates during this period, until God destroyed him with it.
2:259: The Almighty said: "Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord?" This is as strong as His saying: Have you seen the like of the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord? That is why He followed it with His saying: "Or like the one who passed by a town and it was desolate on its roofs?" They differed about who this passer-by was. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, on the authority of Issam bin Rawad, on the authority of Adam bin Abi Iyas, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Najiyah bin Kaab, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, that he said: He is Ezra. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Najiyah himself, and Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, and Sulayman bin Buraydah. This is the well-known statement. Wahb bin Munabbih and Abdullah bin Ubayd said: He is Jeremiah bin Hilqiya. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, that he said: He is the name of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: I heard Sulayman ibn Muhammad al-Yassari al-Jari from the people of al-Jari, the cousin of Mutraf, who said: I heard Salman say: A man from the people of Ash-Sham says: The one whom God caused to die for a hundred years and then resurrected him is called Ezekiel ibn Buwar. Mujahid ibn Jabr said: He is a man from the Children of Israel. As for the village, it is well-known that it is Jerusalem. He passed by it after Bukhtanasr destroyed it and killed its people. And it was empty, meaning that there was no one in it, from their saying, The house was empty, it was empty. - And his saying, on its thrones, meaning its roofs and walls had fallen onto its courtyards. So he stood thinking about what had become of it after the great construction, and he said, How can God revive this after its death? This is because he saw its destruction and its severe ruin and its distance from returning to what it was. God Almighty said, So God caused him to die for a hundred years, then He resurrected him. He said: And the country was inhabited after seventy years had passed since his death, and its inhabitants were complete, and the Children of Israel returned to it. So when God Almighty resurrected him after his death, the first thing that God revived in him was to see with them God’s work in him: how to revive his body. So when he became straight, God said to him, meaning through the angel: How long have you remained? He said, I have remained a day or part of a day. He said: This is because he died at the beginning of the day, then God resurrected him at the end of the day. So when he saw the sun remaining, he thought that it was the sun of that day, so he said, or part of a day. He said, “Rather, you have remained a hundred years. So look at your food and your drink. “And look at your donkey,” meaning how God the Almighty will revive it, and you will see. And We will make you a sign for the people, meaning a proof of the Resurrection. And look at the bones, how We raise them, meaning We raise them, so that some of them are mounted on others. Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Nafi’ ibn Abi Nu’aym from Ismail ibn Hakim, from Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit, from his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: How We raise it, with a zay, then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic. They did not narrate it. It was recited Nanshizha, meaning We revive it, as Mujahid said, Then We clothe it with flesh. Al-Suddi and others said: The bones of his donkey were scattered around him, right and left. He looked at them and they were shining white. Then God sent a wind that gathered them from every place in that neighborhood. Then He put each bone in its place until it became a standing donkey made of bones with no flesh on it. Then God covered it with flesh, nerves, veins, and skin. God sent an angel who blew into the donkey’s nostrils, and it brayed with the permission of God Almighty. All of this was in the sight of the Almighty. Then, when all of this became clear to him, He said, ‘I know that God has power over all things.’ That is, I know this, and I have seen it with my own eyes. So I am the most knowledgeable of the people of my time about this. Others read, He said, ‘I know,’ meaning that he was commanded to know.
2:260: They mentioned reasons for Abraham's question, including that when he said to Nimrod, My Lord is He who gives life and causes death, he wanted to ascend from the knowledge of certainty of that to the eye of certainty, and to see that with observation, so he said, My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said, Do you not believe? He said, Yes, but to reassure my heart. As for the hadith narrated by Al-Bukhari regarding this verse: Ahmad bin Salih told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Salamah, and Saeed on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We are more deserving of doubt than Abraham when he said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' He said, 'Do you not believe?' He said, 'Yes, but to reassure my heart.' Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Harmalah bin Yahya, on the authority of Wahb, so what is meant here by doubt is not what someone who has no knowledge might understand, without dispute, and this hadith has been answered with answers, one of which is: And his saying, He said, ‘Then take four birds and cut them to yourself.’ The commentators differed as to what these four were, although there is no point in specifying them, for if that were important, the Qur’an would have stated it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said they were the crane, the peacock, the rooster, and the pigeon. And it was also narrated on his authority that he took a goose, a young ostrich, a rooster, and a peacock. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: They were a dove, a rooster, a peacock, and a crow. And his saying, Then cut them to yourself, meaning: cut them. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, Abu al-Aswad al-Du’ali, Wahb ibn Munabbih, al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and others. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And he brought them to you means he bound them, and when he bound them he slaughtered them, then he placed a part of them on each mountain, and they mentioned that he took four birds, slaughtered them, then cut them up, plucked their feathers, tore them apart, and mixed some of them with others, then divided them into parts, and placed a part of them on each mountain, it was said four mountains, and it was said seven, Ibn Abbas said: And he took their heads in his hand, then God Almighty commanded him to call them, so he called them as God Almighty commanded him, and he began to look at the feathers flying to the feathers, and the blood to the blood, and the flesh to the flesh, and the parts of each bird, some of them connected to each other, until each bird stood separately, and they came to him walking, running, so that he would be more eloquent in the vision that he asked for, and each bird began to come to take its head that was in the hand of Abraham, peace be upon him, so if he presented to it something other than its head, it would reject it, and if he presented to it its head, it would ride with the rest of its body by the power and strength of God, and for this reason he said, And know that God is Exalted in Might and Wise, meaning Exalted in Might, He is not defeated. Nothing, and nothing is prevented from Him, and whatever He wills is without any obstacle, because He is the Subduer of all things, Wise in His words and deeds, His law and His decree. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Ayoub regarding His statement, but that my heart may be reassured, he said: Ibn Abbas said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that I have more hope for than it. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, I heard Zayd ibn Ali narrating on the authority of a man on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab who said: Abdullah ibn Abbas and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As agreed to meet. He said: And we were young men. So one of them said to the other: Which verse in the Book of God do you have the most hope for this nation? Abdullah bin Amr said: God’s statement: “Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins’” (al-Baqarah 2:170), and Ibn Abbas said: If you say this, then I say that what is more hopeful for this nation is the statement of Abraham: My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said: Do you not believe? He said: Yes, but so that my heart may be reassured. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Saleh, the scribe of al-Layth, told us, Muhammad bin Abi Salamah told me on the authority of Amr, Ibn al-Munkadir told me that Abdullah bin Abbas and Abdullah bin Amr bin al-As met, and Ibn Abbas said to Ibn Amr bin al-As: Which verse in the Qur’an do you hope for the most? Abdullah bin Amr said: God’s statement: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair’ (al-Baqarah 2:170), and Ibn Abbas said: But I say the statement of God, the Almighty: “And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.’ He said: “Do you not believe?” He said: Yes. So he was pleased with Abraham’s statement: Yes. He said: This is because It is objected to in the souls and the devil whispers it, and thus Al-Hakim narrated it in Al-Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ya’qub bin Al-Ahzam, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abdullah Al-Sa’di, on the authority of Bishr bin Omar Al-Zahrani, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Salamah with his chain of transmission similarly, then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it.
2:261: This is a parable that God the Almighty has given to multiply the reward for those who spend in His cause and seeking His pleasure, and that a good deed is multiplied tenfold to seven hundredfold, so He said, The parable of those who spend their wealth in the cause of God. Saeed bin Jubair said: It means in obedience to God. Makhul said: It means spending in jihad, such as tying horses, preparing weapons, and other things. Shabib bin Bishr said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The dirham in jihad and Hajj is multiplied to seven hundredfold, and for this reason God the Almighty said: Like a seed which grows seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains. This parable is more eloquent in the souls than mentioning the number seven hundred, for this indicates that God the Almighty increases righteous deeds for their doers, just as He increases the seed for those who sow it in good soil, and the Sunnah has mentioned multiplying the good deed to seven hundredfold. Imam Ahmad said: Ziyad bin Al-Rabi’ Abu Khidash narrated to us, Wasil, the freed slave of Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Bashar bin Abi Saif Al-Jarmi, on the authority of Ayyad bin Ghutayf, who said: We entered upon Abu Ubaidah to visit him for a complaint that had afflicted him in his side, and his wife Tahifa was sitting by his head. We said: How did Abu Ubaidah spend the night? She said: By God, he spent the night in reward. Abu Ubaidah said: I did not spend the night in reward. He was facing the wall, then he turned his face towards the people and said: Will you not ask me about what I said? They said: We were not pleased with what you said, so we asked you about it. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever spends a surplus amount in the way of God, it will be seven hundred. Whoever spends on himself and his family, or visits a sick person, or removes harm, the good deed will be rewarded tenfold. Fasting is a shield as long as it is not torn apart. Whoever God Almighty afflicts with a calamity in his body, it will be an expiation for him.” Al-Nasa’i narrated some of it in fasting from a hadith that he continued with, and from another chain of transmission that was interrupted. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Sulayman, I heard Abu `Amr al-Shaybani on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that a man gave away a bridled camel in charity for the sake of God, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You will come on the Day of Resurrection with nine hundred bridled camels. Muslim and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sulayman ibn Mihran on the authority of al-A`mash, and Muslim’s wording is: A man came with a bridled camel and said: O Messenger of God, this is for the sake of God, so he said: You will have seven hundred bridled camels on the Day of Resurrection. Another hadith - Ahmad said: Amr bin Majma Abu Al-Mundhir Al-Kindi told us, Ibrahim Al-Hijri told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has made the good deed of the son of Adam equal to ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, except for fasting. Fasting is for Me, and I will reward it. The fasting person has two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy on the Day of Resurrection. The bad breath of the fasting person is better to God than the scent of musk.” Another hadith - Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every deed of the son of Adam is multiplied, a good deed, ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, to whatever God wills. God says, except for fasting, for it is for Me, and I will reward it. He leaves his food and drink for My sake. And for the fasting person there are two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord. And the bad breath of the fasting person is better to God than the scent of musk. Fasting is a shield, fasting is a shield.” Muslim narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Saeed Al-Ashja, both on the authority of Wakee’ on his authority. Another hadith - Ahmad said: Hussein bin Ali told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Al-Rakim, on the authority of Yasir bin Umaila, on the authority of Khuraim bin Fatik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever spends money in the way of God, it will be multiplied seven hundredfold. Another hadith - Abu Dawud said: Muhammad bin Amr bin Al-Sarh informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, on the authority of Yahya bin Ayoub and Saeed bin Ayoub, on the authority of Zaban bin Faid, on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, prayer, fasting, and remembrance of God are multiplied seven hundred times over spending in the way of God. Another hadith - Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father informed us, Harun bin Abdullah bin Marwan told us, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, on the authority of Al-Khalil bin Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever sends money in the way of God and stays in his house, he will receive seven hundred dirhams on the Day of Resurrection for every dirham, and whoever fights in the way of God and spends in that direction, he will receive seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham, then he recited this verse: ‘And God multiplies for whom He wills.’” This is a strange hadith, and the hadith of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah about multiplying the reward of a good deed to two thousand thousand good deeds has already been presented, when he said: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? The verse. Another hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Ubaidullah bin Al-Askari Al-Bazzaz told us, Al-Hasan bin Ali bin Shabib told us, Mahmoud bin Khalid Al-Dimashqi told us, my father told us, on the authority of Isa bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: When this verse was revealed, The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, O Lord, increase my nation. He said, So God revealed, ‘Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan?’ He said, “O Lord, increase my nation. He said, So God revealed, ‘Only the patient will be given their reward without account.’ Abu Hatim and Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Hajib bin Arkin, on the authority of Abu Umar Hafs bin Umar bin Abdul Aziz Al-Muqri, on the authority of Abu Ismail Al-Mu’addib, on the authority of Isa bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and he mentioned it. And His saying here, And God multiplies for whom He wills, meaning according to his sincerity in his work, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing, meaning His grace is all-Encompassing and abundant, more than His creation, and He knows who deserves it and who does not deserve it. Glory be to Him and praise be to Him.
2:262: God Almighty praises those who spend in His cause, and then do not follow up what they have spent of good deeds and charity with a favour to the one who gave it to them, so they do not show it to anyone, nor do they show it with words or deeds. His statement, nor harm means that they will not do to those they have done good anything unpleasant that would nullify their previous good deeds. Then God Almighty promised them a great reward for that, saying, For them is their reward with their Lord, meaning their reward is from God, not from anyone else. And there is no fear concerning them, meaning regarding the horrors that they will face on the Day of Resurrection. Nor will they grieve, meaning regarding the children they left behind, nor what they missed of worldly life and its pleasures, nor will they regret it, because they have reached what is better for them than that. Then God Almighty said: A kind word meaning a kind word and a prayer for a Muslim and forgiveness meaning pardon and forgiveness for a verbal or physical injustice are better than charity followed by injury. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Fadil told us: I read on the authority of Muqal ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, who said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no charity more beloved to God than a good word. Have you not heard His saying: “A good word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. God is independent of His creation.” Forbearing means He is forbearing, forgives, pardons, and overlooks them. There are hadiths that prohibit boasting in charity. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musahhir, on the authority of Kharsha ibn Al-Har, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: the one who boasts of what he has given, the one who lets his garment trail, and the one who sells his goods by means of false oaths.” Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Yahya told us, Uthman ibn Muhammad Al-Duri told us, Hisham ibn Kharijah told us, Sulayman ibn Uqbah told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who boasts, nor one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who denies destiny will enter Paradise. Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated something similar from the hadith of Yunus ibn Maysarah. Then Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Yasar al-A’raj, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not look at on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:one who is disobedient to his parents, one who is addicted to alcohol, and one who boasts about what he has given.” Al-Nasa’i narrated from Malik ibn Sa’d, on the authority of his uncle Ruh ibn Ubadah, on the authority of Atab ibn Bashir, on the authority of Khasif al-Jazari, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who disobeys his parents, nor one who boasts about destiny will enter Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from al-Hasan ibn al-Munhal, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Asar al-Mawsili, on the authority of Atab, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abdul Karim bin Malik Al-Jazari, from Mujahid, his saying, and it was narrated from Mujahid, from Abu Saeed, and from Mujahid from Abu Hurairah, something similar to it. That is why God the Most High said: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury. So He informed that charity is invalidated by what follows it of reminders or injury, so the reward of charity is not fulfilled by the sin of reminders or injury. Then God the Most High said: Like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people. That is, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, just as the charity of one who shows off to people is invalidated, so he shows them that he wants the face of God, but his only intention is for people to praise him or for him to be known for his beautiful qualities so that he will be thanked among people, or it will be said that he is generous, and other worldly purposes, while he has lost sight of dealing with God the Most High and seeking His pleasure and abundant reward. That is why He said: And he does not believe in God and the Last Day. Then God the Most High gave an example of the hypocrite with his spending. Ad-Dahhak said: And the one who follows his spending with reminders or injury, so He said: Then his example is like that of a smooth rock. And it is a plural. Safwana, some of them say: Safwan is also used singularly, and it is the smooth rock, upon it was dust, and a downpour struck it meaning heavy rain, and left it hard meaning the downpour left that Safwan hard, meaning smooth and dry, meaning there was nothing of that dust on it, rather it was all gone, meaning likewise the deeds of the hypocrites go away and vanish before God even if their deeds appear to people to be like dust, and for this reason He said, They have no power over anything of what they have earned, and God does not guide the disbelieving people.
2:263: God Almighty praises those who spend in His cause, and then do not follow up what they have spent of good deeds and charity with a favour to the one who gave it to them, so they do not show it to anyone, nor do they show it with words or deeds. His statement, nor harm means that they will not do to those they have done good anything unpleasant that would nullify their previous good deeds. Then God Almighty promised them a great reward for that, saying, For them is their reward with their Lord, meaning their reward is from God, not from anyone else. And there is no fear concerning them, meaning regarding the horrors that they will face on the Day of Resurrection. Nor will they grieve, meaning regarding the children they left behind, nor what they missed of worldly life and its pleasures, nor will they regret it, because they have reached what is better for them than that. Then God Almighty said: A kind word meaning a kind word and a prayer for a Muslim and forgiveness meaning pardon and forgiveness for a verbal or physical injustice are better than charity followed by injury. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Fadil told us: I read on the authority of Muqal ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, who said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no charity more beloved to God than a good word. Have you not heard His saying: “A good word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. God is independent of His creation.” Forbearing means He is forbearing, forgives, pardons, and overlooks them. There are hadiths that prohibit boasting in charity. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musahhir, on the authority of Kharsha ibn Al-Har, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: the one who boasts of what he has given, the one who lets his garment trail, and the one who sells his goods by means of false oaths.” Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Yahya told us, Uthman ibn Muhammad Al-Duri told us, Hisham ibn Kharijah told us, Sulayman ibn Uqbah told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who boasts, nor one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who denies destiny will enter Paradise. Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated something similar from the hadith of Yunus ibn Maysarah. Then Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Yasar al-A’raj, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not look at on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:one who is disobedient to his parents, one who is addicted to alcohol, and one who boasts about what he has given.” Al-Nasa’i narrated from Malik ibn Sa’d, on the authority of his uncle Ruh ibn Ubadah, on the authority of Atab ibn Bashir, on the authority of Khasif al-Jazari, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who disobeys his parents, nor one who boasts about destiny will enter Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from al-Hasan ibn al-Munhal, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Asar al-Mawsili, on the authority of Atab, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abdul Karim bin Malik Al-Jazari, from Mujahid, his saying, and it was narrated from Mujahid, from Abu Saeed, and from Mujahid from Abu Hurairah, something similar to it. That is why God the Most High said: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury. So He informed that charity is invalidated by what follows it of reminders or injury, so the reward of charity is not fulfilled by the sin of reminders or injury. Then God the Most High said: Like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people. That is, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, just as the charity of one who shows off to people is invalidated, so he shows them that he wants the face of God, but his only intention is for people to praise him or for him to be known for his beautiful qualities so that he will be thanked among people, or it will be said that he is generous, and other worldly purposes, while he has lost sight of dealing with God the Most High and seeking His pleasure and abundant reward. That is why He said: And he does not believe in God and the Last Day. Then God the Most High gave an example of the hypocrite with his spending. Ad-Dahhak said: And the one who follows his spending with reminders or injury, so He said: Then his example is like that of a smooth rock. And it is a plural. Safwana, some of them say: Safwan is also used singularly, and it is the smooth rock, upon it was dust, and a downpour struck it meaning heavy rain, and left it hard meaning the downpour left that Safwan hard, meaning smooth and dry, meaning there was nothing of that dust on it, rather it was all gone, meaning likewise the deeds of the hypocrites go away and vanish before God even if their deeds appear to people to be like dust, and for this reason He said, They have no power over anything of what they have earned, and God does not guide the disbelieving people.
2:264: God Almighty praises those who spend in His cause, and then do not follow up what they have spent of good deeds and charity with a favour to the one who gave it to them, so they do not show it to anyone, nor do they show it with words or deeds. His statement, nor harm means that they will not do to those they have done good anything unpleasant that would nullify their previous good deeds. Then God Almighty promised them a great reward for that, saying, For them is their reward with their Lord, meaning their reward is from God, not from anyone else. And there is no fear concerning them, meaning regarding the horrors that they will face on the Day of Resurrection. Nor will they grieve, meaning regarding the children they left behind, nor what they missed of worldly life and its pleasures, nor will they regret it, because they have reached what is better for them than that. Then God Almighty said: A kind word meaning a kind word and a prayer for a Muslim and forgiveness meaning pardon and forgiveness for a verbal or physical injustice are better than charity followed by injury. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Fadil told us: I read on the authority of Muqal ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, who said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no charity more beloved to God than a good word. Have you not heard His saying: “A good word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. God is independent of His creation.” Forbearing means He is forbearing, forgives, pardons, and overlooks them. There are hadiths that prohibit boasting in charity. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musahhir, on the authority of Kharsha ibn Al-Har, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: the one who boasts of what he has given, the one who lets his garment trail, and the one who sells his goods by means of false oaths.” Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Yahya told us, Uthman ibn Muhammad Al-Duri told us, Hisham ibn Kharijah told us, Sulayman ibn Uqbah told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who boasts, nor one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who denies destiny will enter Paradise. Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated something similar from the hadith of Yunus ibn Maysarah. Then Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Yasar al-A’raj, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not look at on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:one who is disobedient to his parents, one who is addicted to alcohol, and one who boasts about what he has given.” Al-Nasa’i narrated from Malik ibn Sa’d, on the authority of his uncle Ruh ibn Ubadah, on the authority of Atab ibn Bashir, on the authority of Khasif al-Jazari, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who disobeys his parents, nor one who boasts about destiny will enter Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from al-Hasan ibn al-Munhal, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Asar al-Mawsili, on the authority of Atab, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abdul Karim bin Malik Al-Jazari, from Mujahid, his saying, and it was narrated from Mujahid, from Abu Saeed, and from Mujahid from Abu Hurairah, something similar to it. That is why God the Most High said: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury. So He informed that charity is invalidated by what follows it of reminders or injury, so the reward of charity is not fulfilled by the sin of reminders or injury. Then God the Most High said: Like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people. That is, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, just as the charity of one who shows off to people is invalidated, so he shows them that he wants the face of God, but his only intention is for people to praise him or for him to be known for his beautiful qualities so that he will be thanked among people, or it will be said that he is generous, and other worldly purposes, while he has lost sight of dealing with God the Most High and seeking His pleasure and abundant reward. That is why He said: And he does not believe in God and the Last Day. Then God the Most High gave an example of the hypocrite with his spending. Ad-Dahhak said: And the one who follows his spending with reminders or injury, so He said: Then his example is like that of a smooth rock. And it is a plural. Safwana, some of them say: Safwan is also used singularly, and it is the smooth rock, upon it was dust, and a downpour struck it meaning heavy rain, and left it hard meaning the downpour left that Safwan hard, meaning smooth and dry, meaning there was nothing of that dust on it, rather it was all gone, meaning likewise the deeds of the hypocrites go away and vanish before God even if their deeds appear to people to be like dust, and for this reason He said, They have no power over anything of what they have earned, and God does not guide the disbelieving people.
2:265: This is like the believers who spend their money seeking the pleasure of God in that, and to reassure themselves meaning they are certain and convinced that God will reward them for that with the greatest reward, and similar to this is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him, in the authentic hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon, Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and in the hope of reward meaning he believes that God has prescribed it and in the hope of reward from God, Al-Sha’bi said: and to reassure themselves meaning belief and certainty, and this is what Qatada, Abu Salih, and Ibn Zayd said, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: meaning they are certain where to put their charity. And his saying, Like a garden on a hill, which according to the majority is: a high place on the ground. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak added, and rivers flow on it. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: There are three languages for the hill: there are three readings: with a damma on the ra’, which is what most of the people of Madinah, Hijaz, and Iraq read, and with a fatha, which is the reading of some of the people of Ash-Sham and Kufa, and it is said that it is the language of Tamim, and with a kasra on the ra’, and it is mentioned that it is the reading of Ibn Abbas. And his saying, A downpour struck it, meaning heavy rain, as mentioned above, so it produced its fruit, meaning its fruit, twice, meaning in relation to other gardens. But if a downpour did not strike it, then a drizzle, Ad-Dahhak said: It is the drizzle, which is the softness of the rain. That is, this garden on this hill will never dry up, because if a downpour did not strike it, then a drizzle, and whatever it was, it was sufficient for it. Likewise, the work of the believer will never be lost, rather God accepts it and multiplies it and makes it grow, each worker according to his ability. For this reason, He said, And God is Seeing of what you do, meaning nothing of the deeds of His servants is hidden from Him.
2:266: Al-Bukhari said when interpreting this verse: Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham - he is Ibn Yusuf - told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, I heard Abdullah bin Abi Malekah narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and I heard his brother Abu Bakr bin Abi Malekah narrating on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, he said: Umar bin Al-Khattab said one day to the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: About whom do you think this verse was revealed? Would any of you like to have a garden of date palms and grapes? They said: God knows best. Umar became angry and said: Say: We know or we do not know. Ibn Abbas said: I have something in my mind about it, O Commander of the Faithful. Umar said: O son of my brother, say it and do not belittle yourself. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: You have given an example of a deed. Umar said: What deed? Ibn Abbas said: A rich man who works in obedience to God, then God sent Satan to him, so he committed sins until he drowned his deeds. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Za’farani, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Muhammad Al-A’war, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, so he mentioned it and it is one of the individuals of Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him. In this hadith is sufficient in explaining this verse, and clarifying what it contains of an example of the work of someone who did good deeds first, then after that his course was reversed and he exchanged good deeds for bad deeds, God forbid that, so he nullified with his second work what he had done previously of good, and he needed something from the first in the most difficult of circumstances, so nothing came of it and he was betrayed when he needed it most, and for this reason God the Almighty said: And old age overtook him, and he had weak offspring, and a whirlwind struck it meaning a strong wind with fire in it and it was burned meaning it burned its fruits and destroyed its trees, so what would be his state? Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God gave a good example, and all of His examples are good. He said, Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it, and for him therein all kinds of fruits? He said, And old age overtook him, and his children and descendants were weak at the end of his life, and a hurricane with fire came to him and burned his garden, so he did not have the strength to plant something like it, and his descendants did not have any good to return to him. And so will the disbeliever be on the Day of Resurrection when he is returned to God Almighty. He has no good to seek repentance for, just as this man does not have the strength to plant something like his garden, and he does not find that he has provided for himself any good to return to him, just as his children did not provide for him, and he was deprived of his reward when he was the poorest of those he had been to, just as this man was deprived of his garden when he was the poorest of those he had been to when he was old and his descendants were weak. Thus, Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say in his supplication, O God, make Your provision most abundant for me when I grow old and my life comes to an end. For this reason, God the Almighty said, Thus does God make clear to you the signs that you may give thought. That is, you may consider and understand the examples and meanings and apply them to their intended meaning. As God the Almighty said, And these examples We present to the people, but none grasps them except those of knowledge.
2:267: God Almighty commands His believing servants to spend, and what is meant by this here is charity. Ibn Abbas said: From the good things that He has provided them with from the money that they have earned. Mujahid said: He means trade by making it easy for them. Ali and Al-Suddi said: From the good things that you have earned means gold and silver, and from the fruits and crops that He has grown for them from the earth. Ibn Abbas said: He commanded them to spend from the best, finest and most precious money, and He forbade them from giving charity from the most vile and base money, which is its filth, for God is good and does not accept anything but good. For this reason He said: And do not aim for the bad meaning do not intend the bad from it, spending and you would not take it meaning if you were given it you would not take it, unless you overlook it, for God is richer than you, so do not make for God what you dislike. It was said that its meaning is And do not aim for the bad from it, spending meaning do not deviate from lawful money and aim for the unlawful, making your spending From him, and here he mentions the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Sabah bin Muhammad, on the authority of Marra Al-Hamdani, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has divided your morals among you as He has divided your provisions among you. God gives the world to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, and He does not give religion except to whom He loves. So whoever God gives religion to, He loves him. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a servant does not become Muslim until his heart and tongue become Muslim, and he does not become a believer until his neighbor is safe from his evils. They said: What are his evils, O Prophet of God? He said: His deception and oppression. A servant does not earn wealth from an unlawful source and spends from it and it is blessed for him, nor does he give charity and it is accepted from him, nor does he leave it behind him except that he will be in the Fire. God does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed, evil does not erase evil.” The correct statement is the first. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Al-Husayn bin Umar Al-Abqari told us, my father told me, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Al-Bara bin Azib. May God be pleased with him, in the words of God, “O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim towards the bad thereof, spending [something],” the verse, he said: It was revealed about the Ansar. When the days of the palm harvest came, the Ansar would bring out unripe dates from their walls and hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the poor immigrants would eat from it. One of them would take the husks and put them in with the bunches of unripe dates, thinking that this was permissible. So God revealed about the one who did that, And do not aim towards the bad thereof, spending [something], then Ibn Jarir, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it through Al-Suddi, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Al-Bara’, in a similar manner. Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, but they did not include it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Al-Bara’, may God be pleased with him, And do not aim towards the bad thereof, spending [something] while you are not believers. He said: It was revealed about us. We were palm tree owners, and a man would bring from his palm trees according to their abundance or scarcity, and he would bring a spear and hang it in the mosque. The people of the Suffah did not have food, so when one of them came, he would hit it with his stick and the ripe dates would fall from it, and he would eat. There were people who did not desire good, and they would bring a spear with husks and straw, and they would bring a spear that had broken and hang it, so it was revealed: And do not aim at the bad thereof, spending [in charity], and you would not take it [from yourselves] unless you close your eyes to it. He said: If one of you were given a gift like what he was given, he would not take it except out of closeness and shyness. After that, a man from among us would come with the best of what he had. And this is how it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi, on the authority of Ubaidullah, who is Ibn Musa Al-Absi, on the authority of Israel, on Al-Suddi, who is Ismail bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ghifari, whose name is Ghazwan, on the authority of Al-Baraa, and he mentioned something similar, then he said: This is a good and strange hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Katheer narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Haneef, on the authority of his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade two types of dates, al-Ja’rur and al-Habiq. People used to perform tayammum on the worst of their fruits, then give them out in charity. So the verse was revealed: And do not give away the bad ones, spending them in charity. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn on the authority of al-Zuhri, then he said: Abu al-Walid attributed it to Sulayman ibn Katheer on the authority of al-Zuhri, and its wording is: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade al-Ja’rur and the type of al-Habiq from being taken in charity. Al-Nasa’i narrated this hadith on the authority of Abd al-Jalil ibn Hamid al-Yahsabi, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Umamah, and he did not say on the authority of his father, so he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wahb narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Abd al-Jalil. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, regarding this verse: And do not give away the bad ones, spending them in charity. “You spend.” He said: The earnings of a Muslim should not be impure, but he should not believe in chaff, a counterfeit dirham, or anything that is not good. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Hammad, who is Ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “A lizard was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he did not eat it and did not forbid it. I said: O Messenger of God, should we feed it to the poor?” He said: Do not feed them what you do not eat. Then he narrated it on the authority of Affan on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on his authority. I said: O Messenger of God, should I not feed it to the poor? He said: Do not feed them what you do not eat. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, And you would not take it unless you close your eyes to it, meaning: If a man had a right over another man and he gave it to him, he would not take it unless he saw that he had reduced his right to it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ali bin Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And you would not take it unless you close your eyes to it, meaning: If you had a right over someone and he came to you with a right less than your right, you would not take it according to the good account until you reduced it. He said: That is what His statement, Unless you close your eyes to it, so how can you accept for me what you would not accept for yourselves, when my right over you is from the best of your wealth and your souls? Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and he added: And it is His statement, You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. Then it was narrated through Al-Awfi and others, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar to that, and more than one person mentioned it likewise. And His statement: And know that God is Rich and Praiseworthy means that if He commands you to give charity and to give good charity, He is Rich and Praiseworthy, and that is only to make the rich equal to the poor, like His statement: God does not need their meat or their blood, but He needs piety from you. He is Rich and does not need any of His creation, and all of His creation are poor towards Him. He is Vast in bounty, and what He has is never exhausted. So whoever gives charity from good earnings, let him know that God is Rich and Vast in giving, Generous and Bountiful, and He will reward him for it and multiply it for him many times over. He who lends is not destitute or unjust. He is Praiseworthy, meaning He is praised in all of His actions, words, laws, and decrees. There is no god but Him, and there is no lord but Him. And his saying: “The devil threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Hunad ibn al-Sari told us, Abu al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The devil has a touch with the son of Adam and the angel has a touch. As for the touch of the devil, it is a threat of evil and a denial of the truth. As for the touch of the angel, it is a threat of good and belief in the truth. So whoever finds that, let him know that it is from God, so let him praise God. And whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge from the devil.” Then he recited: The devil threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And thus it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i in their two books of interpretation from their Sunans, both of them, on the authority of Hunad ibn al-Sari. It was narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, on the authority of Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili, on the authority of Hunad, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good and rare hadith. It is the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas, meaning Salam ibn Salim. We do not know it to be traced back to the Prophet except through his hadith. This is what he said: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, with a similar chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. However, Mis`ar narrated it on the authority of `Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas `Auf ibn Malik ibn Nadlah, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, so he included it among his words, and God knows best. The meaning of the words of God the Almighty: Satan threatens you with poverty means he frightens you with poverty so that you hold on to what is in your hands and do not spend it in the way of God’s pleasure. And enjoins you to immorality means that in addition to forbidding you from spending for fear of poverty, he enjoins you to commit sins, transgressions, forbidden acts, and disobeying God’s Messenger. God the Almighty said: And God promises you forgiveness from Him meaning in return for what Satan enjoins you to commit. And in return that is, in return for what Satan has made you fear of poverty, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing. And his saying: He gives wisdom to whom He wills, Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means knowledge of the Qur’an, its abrogating and abrogated verses, its clear and ambiguous verses, its beginning and end, its lawful and unlawful verses, and its likes. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, Wisdom is the Qur’an, meaning its interpretation. Ibn Abbas said: For it has been recited by the righteous and the wicked. It was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid: He means by wisdom correctness in speech. Layth bin Abi Sulaym said, on the authority of Mujahid: He gives wisdom to whom He wills: It is not prophecy, but rather knowledge, jurisprudence, and the Qur’an. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Wisdom is the fear of God, for fear of God is the head of all wisdom. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Baqiyyah on the authority of Uthman bin Zafar Al-Juhani, on the authority of Abu Ammar Al-Asadi, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, The head of wisdom is the fear of God. Abu Al-Aaliyah said in a narration on his authority: Wisdom is the Book and understanding. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: Wisdom is understanding. Abu Malik said: Wisdom is the Sunnah. Ibn Wahb said, on the authority of Malik, that Zaid bin Aslam said: Wisdom is the mind. Malik said: It has occurred to me that wisdom is understanding the religion of God, and a matter that God instills in the hearts from His mercy and grace. What makes this clear is that you find a man who is wise in worldly matters when he looks into them, and you find another who is weak in worldly matters, knowledgeable in the matter of his religion and perceptive of it. God gives it to him and deprives him of this. So wisdom is understanding the religion of God. Al-Suddi said: Wisdom is prophethood. The correct view is that wisdom, as the majority said, is not specific to prophethood, but is more general than it, and the highest of it is prophethood, and the message is more specific. However, the followers of the prophets have a share of goodness by way of following, as came in the hadiths: Whoever memorizes the Qur’an, prophethood has been placed between his shoulders, except that revelation is not sent to him. It was narrated by Wakee’ bin Al-Jarrah in his interpretation, on the authority of Ismail bin Rafi’, on the authority of a man he did not name, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar. And his saying: And Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ and Yazid told us. Ibn Abbas said: From the good things that He has provided them with from the money that they have earned. Mujahid said: He means trade by making it easy for them. Ali and Al-Suddi said: From the good things that you have earned means gold and silver, and from the fruits and crops that He has grown for them from the earth. Ibn Abbas said: He commanded them to spend from the best, finest and most precious money, and He forbade them from giving charity from the most vile and base money, which is its filth, for God is good and does not accept anything but good. For this reason He said: And do not aim for the bad meaning do not intend the bad from it, spending and you would not take it meaning if you were given it you would not take it, unless you overlook it, for God is richer than you, so do not make for God what you dislike. It was said that its meaning is And do not aim for the bad from it, spending meaning do not deviate from lawful money and aim for the unlawful, making your spending From him, and here he mentions the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Sabah bin Muhammad, on the authority of Marra Al-Hamdani, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has divided your morals among you as He has divided your provisions among you. God gives the world to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, and He does not give religion except to whom He loves. So whoever God gives religion to, He loves him. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a servant does not become Muslim until his heart and tongue become Muslim, and he does not become a believer until his neighbor is safe from his evils. They said: What are his evils, O Prophet of God? He said: His deception and oppression. A servant does not earn wealth from an unlawful source and spends from it and it is blessed for him, nor does he give charity and it is accepted from him, nor does he leave it behind him except that he will be in the Fire. God does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed, evil does not erase evil.” The correct statement is the first. May God be pleased with him, in the words of God, “O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim towards the bad thereof, spending [something],” the verse, he said: It was revealed about the Ansar. When the days of the palm harvest came, the Ansar would bring out unripe dates from their walls and hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the poor immigrants would eat from it. One of them would take the husks and put them in with the bunches of unripe dates, thinking that this was permissible. So God revealed about the one who did that, And do not aim towards the bad thereof, spending [something], then Ibn Jarir, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it through Al-Suddi, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Al-Bara’, in a similar manner. Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, but they did not include it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Al-Bara’, may God be pleased with him, And do not aim towards the bad thereof, spending [something] while you are not believers. He said: It was revealed about us. We were palm tree owners, and a man would bring from his palm trees according to their abundance or scarcity, and he would bring a spear and hang it in the mosque. The people of the Suffah did not have food, so when one of them came, he would hit it with his stick and the ripe dates would fall from it, and he would eat. There were people who did not desire good, and they would bring a spear with husks and straw, and they would bring a spear that had broken and hang it, so it was revealed: And do not aim at the bad thereof, spending [in charity], and you would not take it [from yourselves] unless you close your eyes to it. He said: If one of you were given a gift like what he was given, he would not take it except out of closeness and shyness. After that, a man from among us would come with the best of what he had. And this is how it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi, on the authority of Ubaidullah, who is Ibn Musa Al-Absi, on the authority of Israel, on Al-Suddi, who is Ismail bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ghifari, whose name is Ghazwan, on the authority of Al-Baraa, and he mentioned something similar, then he said: This is a good and strange hadith. People used to perform tayammum on the worst of their fruits, then give them out in charity. So the verse was revealed: And do not give away the bad ones, spending them in charity. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn on the authority of al-Zuhri, then he said: Abu al-Walid attributed it to Sulayman ibn Katheer on the authority of al-Zuhri, and its wording is: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade al-Ja’rur and the type of al-Habiq from being taken in charity. Al-Nasa’i narrated this hadith on the authority of Abd al-Jalil ibn Hamid al-Yahsabi, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Umamah, and he did not say on the authority of his father, so he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wahb narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Abd al-Jalil. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Hammad, who is Ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “A lizard was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he did not eat it and did not forbid it. I said: O Messenger of God, should we feed it to the poor?” He said: Do not feed them what you do not eat. Then he narrated it on the authority of Affan on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on his authority. I said: O Messenger of God, should I not feed it to the poor? He said: Do not feed them what you do not eat. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, And you would not take it unless you close your eyes to it, meaning: If a man had a right over another man and he gave it to him, he would not take it unless he saw that he had reduced his right to it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ali bin Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And you would not take it unless you close your eyes to it, meaning: If you had a right over someone and he came to you with a right less than your right, you would not take it according to the good account until you reduced it. He said: That is what His statement, Unless you close your eyes to it, so how can you accept for me what you would not accept for yourselves, when my right over you is from the best of your wealth and your souls? Then it was narrated through Al-Awfi and others, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar to that, and more than one person mentioned it likewise. And His statement: And know that God is Rich and Praiseworthy means that if He commands you to give charity and to give good charity, He is Rich and Praiseworthy, and that is only to make the rich equal to the poor, like His statement: God does not need their meat or their blood, but He needs piety from you. He is Rich and does not need any of His creation, and all of His creation are poor towards Him. He is Vast in bounty, and what He has is never exhausted. So whoever gives charity from good earnings, let him know that God is Rich and Vast in giving, Generous and Bountiful, and He will reward him for it and multiply it for him many times over. He who lends is not destitute or unjust. He is Praiseworthy, meaning He is praised in all of His actions, words, laws, and decrees. There is no god but Him, and there is no lord but Him. And his saying: “The devil threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Hunad ibn al-Sari told us, Abu al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The devil has a touch with the son of Adam and the angel has a touch. As for the touch of the devil, it is a threat of evil and a denial of the truth. As for the touch of the angel, it is a threat of good and belief in the truth. So whoever finds that, let him know that it is from God, so let him praise God. And whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge from the devil.” Then he recited: The devil threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And thus it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i in their two books of interpretation from their Sunans, both of them, on the authority of Hunad ibn al-Sari. It was narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, on the authority of Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili, on the authority of Hunad, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good and rare hadith. It is the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas, meaning Salam ibn Salim. We do not know it to be traced back to the Prophet except through his hadith. This is what he said: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, with a similar chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. However, Mis`ar narrated it on the authority of `Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas `Auf ibn Malik ibn Nadlah, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, so he included it among his words, and God knows best. And enjoins you to immorality means that in addition to forbidding you from spending for fear of poverty, he enjoins you to commit sins, transgressions, forbidden acts, and disobeying God’s Messenger. God the Almighty said: And God promises you forgiveness from Him meaning in return for what Satan enjoins you to commit. And in return that is, in return for what Satan has made you fear of poverty, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing. And his saying: He gives wisdom to whom He wills, Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means knowledge of the Qur’an, its abrogating and abrogated verses, its clear and ambiguous verses, its beginning and end, its lawful and unlawful verses, and its likes. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, Wisdom is the Qur’an, meaning its interpretation. Ibn Abbas said: For it has been recited by the righteous and the wicked. It was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid: He means by wisdom correctness in speech. Layth bin Abi Sulaym said, on the authority of Mujahid: He gives wisdom to whom He wills: It is not prophecy, but rather knowledge, jurisprudence, and the Qur’an. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Baqiyyah on the authority of Uthman bin Zafar Al-Juhani, on the authority of Abu Ammar Al-Asadi, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, The head of wisdom is the fear of God. Abu Al-Aaliyah said in a narration on his authority: Wisdom is the Book and understanding. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: Wisdom is understanding. Abu Malik said: Wisdom is the Sunnah. Ibn Wahb said, on the authority of Malik, that Zaid bin Aslam said: Wisdom is the mind. Malik said: It has occurred to me that wisdom is understanding the religion of God, and a matter that God instills in the hearts from His mercy and grace. God gives it to him and deprives him of this. So wisdom is understanding the religion of God. Al-Suddi said: Wisdom is prophethood.
