The correct view is that wisdom, as the majority said, is not specific to prophethood, but is more general than it, and the highest of it is prophethood, and the message is more specific. However, the followers of the prophets have a share of goodness by way of following, as came in the hadiths: Whoever memorizes the Qur’an, prophethood has been placed between his shoulders, except that revelation is not sent to him. It was narrated by Wakee’ bin Al-Jarrah in his interpretation, on the authority of Ismail bin Rafi’, on the authority of a man he did not name, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar. And his saying: And Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ and Yazid told us. They said: Ismail, meaning Ibn Abi Khalid, told us on the authority of Qais, who is Ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, say: “There is no envy except in two cases: a man to whom God has given wealth and he spends it in the right way, and a man to whom God has given wisdom and he judges by it and teaches it.” And thus it was narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ismail Abu Khalid. His saying: None will remember except those of understanding, meaning that none will benefit from the admonition and reminder except those who have a mind and intellect, with which they understand the discourse and the meaning of the words.
2:270: God Almighty informs us that He knows all the good deeds of those who do good, including spending and vows, and this includes His reward for that with the most abundant reward for those who do that, seeking His face and hoping for His promise, and He threatens those who do not obey Him, but rather disobey His command, deny His report, and worship others besides Him, so He said, And the wrongdoers will have no helpers, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, to save them from God’s punishment and vengeance. His saying: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good. That is, if you disclose them, they are good things. And his saying: But if you conceal it and give it to the poor, it is better for you. This indicates that keeping charity secret is better than making it public, because it is further from showing off, unless making it public results in a greater benefit than people following his example, in which case it is better in this regard. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who recites the Qur’an publicly is like he who gives charity publicly, and reciting the Qur’an in secret is like he who gives charity in secret. The basic principle is that keeping it secret is better for this verse, and because it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Seven will be shaded by God in His shade on the day when there is no shade except His shade: a just ruler, a young man who grew up in the worship of God, two men who love each other for the sake of God, meeting and parting for that reason, a man whose heart is attached to the mosque when he leaves it until he returns to it, a man who remembers God in private and his eyes overflow with tears, a man who is invited by a woman of status and beauty and he says: I fear God, Lord of the worlds, and a man who gives charity and conceals it such that his left hand does not know what his right hand spends.” Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace: He said, “When God created the earth, it began to shake, so He created the mountains and threw them upon it, and it settled. The angels were amazed at God’s creation of the mountains, and they said, ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than mountains?’ He said, ‘Yes, iron.’ They said, ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than iron?’ He said, ‘Yes, fire.’ They said, ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than fire?’ He said, ‘Yes, water.’ They said, ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than water?’ He said, ‘Yes, wind.’ They said, ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than wind?’ He said: Yes, the son of Adam gives charity with his right hand and hides it from his left. We have mentioned in the merit of Ayat al-Kursi on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: I said, O Messenger of God, which charity is best? He said: “Secretly to a poor person or an effort from one who is poor.” Narrated by Ahmad and narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ali bin Yazid on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of Abu Dharr, so he mentioned it and added, then he began with this verse: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you. The verse, and in the narrated hadith: Secret charity extinguishes the wrath of the Lord Almighty. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, al-Husayn bin Ziyad al-Muharibi, the tutor of Muharib, told us, Musa bin Umair on the authority of Amer al-Sha’bi in his saying: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you. He said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. As for Umar, he brought half of his wealth until he gave it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “What He said: I left them half of my wealth. As for Abu Bakr, he came with all of his wealth, almost hiding it from himself, until he gave it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: What did you leave behind for your family, O Abu Bakr? He said: The provision of God and the provision of His Messenger. Omar, may God be pleased with him, wept and said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Abu Bakr. By God, we have never raced to a door of goodness without you being the first. This hadith was narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Omar, may God be pleased with him, but we have only included it here because of Al-Sha’bi’s statement: The verse was revealed regarding that. Then the verse is general in that concealing charity is better, whether it is obligatory or voluntary. However, Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his interpretation of this verse. He said: God made secret voluntary charity better than its public giving, so he said seventy times, and He made the obligatory charity, its public giving, better than its secret giving, so he said twenty-five times. And His statement: “And He will expiate for you some of your misdeeds” meaning instead of charity, especially if it is secret, you will obtain good in raising your ranks and He will expiate for you your misdeeds. And and He will expiate has been read in the subjunctive mood as an appositive to the place of the answer to the condition, which is His statement: Then it is good like His statement: So give charity and be and His statement: And God is Aware of what you do meaning nothing of that is hidden from Him and He will reward you for it.

2:272: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Salam ibn Abd al-Rahim informed us, al-Faryabi informed us, Sufyan informed us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They were reluctant to submit to their polytheist lineages, so they asked and he permitted them, so this verse was revealed: “You are not responsible for their guidance, but God guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend of good is for yourselves, and you do not spend except seeking the countenance of God. And whatever you spend of good will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.” And likewise Abu Hudhaiqah, Ibn al-Mubarak, Abu Ahmad al-Zubaidi, and Abu Dawud al-Hadrami narrated it on the authority of Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Atiyah informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman, meaning al-Dashtaki, informed us, my father informed me on the authority of his father, Ash’ath ibn Ishaq informed us on the authority of Ja’far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to command that charity should not be given except to the people of Islam, until this verse was revealed: You are not responsible for their guidance to the end of it, then he commanded charity after it to everyone who asked you from every religion, and it will come in the words of God Almighty: God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes the verse, the hadith of Asma’ bint al-Siddiq on that. His saying: And whatever you spend of good is for yourselves is like his saying: Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul and there are many similar examples in the Qur’an. And his saying, And you do not spend except seeking the face of God, Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The believer’s spending is for himself, and the believer does not spend when he spends except seeking the face of God. Ata Al-Khurasani said: It means if you give for the face of God, then you do not care what his work was. This is a good meaning and its gist is that if the one who gives charity for the sake of God, then his reward is upon God, and he is not responsible for the one who did good, or the wicked, or the deserving, or other, and he is rewarded for his intention. The basis for this is the complete verse: And whatever you spend in good will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged. The hadith narrated in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man said: I will give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and put it in the hand of an adulteress. The people were talking in the morning: He gave charity to an adulteress. So he said: O God, to You be praise for an adulteress. I will give charity tonight. So he put it in the hand of a rich man. They were talking in the morning: He gave charity tonight to a rich man. He said: O God, to You be praise for a rich man. I will give charity tonight. So he went out and put it in the hand of a thief. They were talking in the morning: He gave charity tonight to a thief. So he said: O God, to You be praise for an adulteress, a rich man, and a thief. So he was brought and it was said to him: As for your charity, it has been accepted, but as for the adulteress Perhaps she will abstain from fornication, perhaps the rich will take heed and spend from what God has given him, and perhaps the thief will abstain from stealing from her.” And His saying, for the poor who are restricted in the cause of God, means the emigrants who have devoted themselves to God and His Messenger and have settled in Medina, and they have no means to provide for themselves what would enrich them, and who are unable to travel throughout the land, means traveling to seek a livelihood, and traveling throughout the land is traveling. God the Most High said, And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, and God the Most High said, He knows that there will be among you sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God and others fighting in the cause of God, the verse. And his saying, The ignorant thinks them rich because of their self-restraint, meaning the ignorant of their situation and condition thinks them rich because of their self-restraint in their clothing, condition, and speech. In this meaning is the hadith agreed upon as authentic on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “The poor person is not the one who goes around and is satisfied with one or two dates, one or two mouthfuls, or one or two meals. Rather, the poor person is the one who does not find wealth that would make him independent, and no one notices him so that he can be given charity, and he does not ask people for anything.” Narrated by Ahmad from the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud as well. His saying, You will recognize them by their mark, meaning by what is apparent to those with understanding of their characteristics, as God Almighty said, Their mark is on their faces, and He said, And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech, and in the hadith in the Sunan, Beware of the intuition of the believer, for he sees with the light of God, then he recited, Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs. And his saying: They do not ask people insistently means they do not insist in asking and burden people with what they do not need. If he asks and he has enough to do without asking, then he has joined in asking. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Sharik ibn Abi Namir told us that `Ata’ ibn Yasar and `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi `Umrah al-Ansari said: We heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The poor person is not the one who is satisfied with a date or two, nor a morsel or two. Rather, the poor person is the one who is too modest.” Read if you wish, meaning his saying they do not ask people insistently. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ismail ibn Ja`far al-Madini, from Sharik ibn `Abdullah ibn Abi Namir, from `Ata’ ibn Yasar alone, from Abu Hurairah with it. Abu `Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa’i said: `Ali ibn Hajar told us, Ismail told us, Sharik told us, and he is the son of Abi Namir, from `Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurairah with it, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: “The poor person is not the one who is satisfied with one or two dates, or one or two mouthfuls, but the poor person is the one who is too modest. Read if you wish, ‘They do not ask people insistently.’” Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Abi Dhi’b informed me, on the authority of Abu al-Walid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The poor person is not the one who goes around to you and you feed him mouthful by mouthful, but the poor person is the one who is too modest and does not ask people insistently. Ibn Jarir said: Mu’tamir informed me, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Malik, on the authority of Salih ibn Suwayd, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The poor person is not the one who goes around and is satisfied with one or two mouthfuls, but the poor person is too modest in his house and does not ask people for anything when he is in need. Read if you wish, ‘They do not ask people insistently.’ Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi informed us, Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man from Muzaynah, that his mother said to him: Why don’t you go and ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the people ask him? So I went to ask him and found him standing and giving a sermon, and he was saying: “Whoever seeks chastity, God will make him chaste, and whoever seeks self-sufficiency, God will make him rich, and whoever asks people while he has the equivalent of five aqeeqahs, has indeed asked people persistently.” So I said to myself: A she-camel of mine is better than five aqeeqs, and his slave has another she-camel, which is better than five aqeeqs. So I went back and did not ask him. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal told us, on the authority of Ammarah ibn Ghaziyah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Saeed, on the authority of his father, who said: My mother sent me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask him, so I came to him and sat down. He said: He faced me and said: “Whoever seeks self-sufficiency, God will make him rich, and whoever seeks self-sufficiency, God will suffice him, and whoever asks while he has the equivalent of an aqeeqah has indeed been persistent.” So I said: My she-camel, the ruby, is better than an aqeeqah. So I went back and did not ask him. This is how Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah. Abu Dawud and Hisham ibn Ammar both added on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Men narrated with his chain of transmission similarly. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Jamahir told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Rijal told us, on the authority of Ammarah ibn Ghaziyah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Saeed, who said: Abu Saeed al-Khudri said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever asks while he has the value of an ounce is being persistent. An ounce is forty dirhams. Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of a man from Banu Asad, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever asks for an ounce or its equivalent has asked persistently. Imam Ahmad also said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hakim ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his request will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches or bruises on his face. They said: O Messenger of God, what is his sufficiency? He said: Fifty dirhams or its equivalent in gold. It was narrated by the four scholars of Sunan from the hadith of Hakim bin Jubayr al-Asadi al-Kufi, and Shu’bah bin al-Hajjaj left it out, and more than one of the imams declared it weak because of this hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Hadrami told us, Abu Husayn Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told us, my father told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, who said: Al-Harith heard from a man from Quraysh in Ash-Sham that Abu Dharr was in need, so he sent him three hundred dinars. He said: Abdullah did not find a man more insignificant to him than me. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever asks while he has forty has been persistent. Abu Dharr gave him forty dirhams, forty sheep, and two servants. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said: He meant two servants. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, Abdul-Jabbar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Sabur, on the authority of Amr bin Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Whoever asks and has forty dirhams is a beggar, and he is like a handful of sand. He meant sand. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Adam, on the authority of Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, with a chain of transmission similar to it, saying: And whatever you spend of good, God is Knowing of it. That is, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward him with the most abundant and complete reward on the Day of Resurrection when he will be most in need of it. And His statement, “Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord. And no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.” This is praise from the Almighty to those who spend in His cause and seeking His pleasure at all times, day and night, and in all circumstances, secretly and publicly, to the point that spending on one’s family is also included in that, as it was proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas when he visited him sick in the year of the conquest, and in another narration in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, And you will not spend anything seeking thereby the face of God except that you will increase in degree and elevation by it, even what you put in your wife’s mouth. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Bahz told us: Shu`bah told us on the authority of `Adi ibn Thabit, who said: I heard `Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Ansari narrating on the authority of Abu Mas`ud, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If a Muslim spends on his family something, expecting reward from God, it is considered charity for him. They both included it on the authority of Shu`bah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur`ah told us, Sulayman ibn `Abd al-Rahman told us, Muhammad ibn Shu`ayb told us, who said: I heard Sa`id ibn Yasar on the authority of Yazid ibn `Abdullah ibn `Urayb al-Maliki, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: This verse was revealed about the owners of horses: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord. Habash al-San’ani said on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, he said: They are those who feed horses in the way of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then he said: And it was also narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, Saeed bin al-Musayyab, and Makhul. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed al-Ashja told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab bin Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of his father, he said: Ali had four dirhams, so he spent one dirham at night, one dirham during the day, one dirham secretly, and one dirham openly, so the verse was revealed: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab bin Mujahid, and it is weak, but Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that it was revealed regarding Ali bin Abi Talib, and his statement: Then they will have their reward with their Lord means on the Day of Resurrection for what they did of spending in acts of obedience. And there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Its interpretation was presented above.
2:273: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Salam ibn Abd al-Rahim informed us, al-Faryabi informed us, Sufyan informed us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They were reluctant to submit to their polytheist lineages, so they asked and he permitted them, so this verse was revealed: “You are not responsible for their guidance, but God guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend of good is for yourselves, and you do not spend except seeking the countenance of God. And whatever you spend of good will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.” And likewise Abu Hudhaiqah, Ibn al-Mubarak, Abu Ahmad al-Zubaidi, and Abu Dawud al-Hadrami narrated it on the authority of Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, on his authority. So I went back and did not ask him. An ounce is forty dirhams. Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of a man from Banu Asad, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever asks for an ounce or its equivalent has asked persistently. Imam Ahmad also said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hakim ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his request will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches or bruises on his face. They said: O Messenger of God, what is his sufficiency? He said: Fifty dirhams or its equivalent in gold. Abu Dharr gave him forty dirhams, forty sheep, and two servants. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said: He meant two servants. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, Abdul-Jabbar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Sabur, on the authority of Amr bin Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Bahz told us: Shu`bah told us on the authority of `Adi ibn Thabit, who said: I heard `Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Ansari narrating on the authority of Abu Mas`ud, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If a Muslim spends on his family something, expecting reward from God, it is considered charity for him. They both included it on the authority of Shu`bah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur`ah told us, Sulayman ibn `Abd al-Rahman told us, Muhammad ibn Shu`ayb told us, who said: I heard Sa`id ibn Yasar on the authority of Yazid ibn `Abdullah ibn `Urayb al-Maliki, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: This verse was revealed about the owners of horses: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord. Habash al-San’ani said on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, he said: They are those who feed horses in the way of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then he said: And it was also narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, Saeed bin al-Musayyab, and Makhul. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed al-Ashja told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab bin Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of his father, he said: Ali had four dirhams, so he spent one dirham at night, one dirham during the day, one dirham secretly, and one dirham openly, so the verse was revealed: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab bin Mujahid, and it is weak, but Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that it was revealed regarding Ali bin Abi Talib, and his statement: Then they will have their reward with their Lord means on the Day of Resurrection for what they did of spending in acts of obedience. And there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Its interpretation was presented above.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed al-Ashja told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab bin Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of his father, he said: Ali had four dirhams, so he spent one dirham at night, one dirham during the day, one dirham secretly, and one dirham openly, so the verse was revealed: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab bin Mujahid, and it is weak, but Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that it was revealed regarding Ali bin Abi Talib, and his statement: Then they will have their reward with their Lord means on the Day of Resurrection for what they did of spending in acts of obedience. And there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Its interpretation was presented above.
2:276: God the Almighty informs us that He will destroy usury, that is, He will remove it either by removing it completely from the hand of its owner, or by depriving him of the blessing of his wealth so that he will not benefit from it, but rather He will destroy it in this world and punish him for it on the Day of Resurrection, as God the Almighty said: “Say, ‘Not equal are the bad and the good, even if the abundance of the bad pleases you. ’” And God the Almighty said: And He will put the bad one upon the other and pile them all up and put them in Hell. And He said: And whatever you give in interest so that it may increase within the wealth of the people, it will not increase with God. And Ibn Jarir said: In His statement, God destroys usury, this is similar to the report narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud that he said: Usury, even if it increases, its consequence will be little. This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, and he said: Hajjaj told us. Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Rakeen bin Al-Rabi’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Even if usury increases, its consequences lead to poverty. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Al-Abbas bin Ja’far, on the authority of Amr bin Awn, on the authority of Yahya bin Za’idah, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Al-Rakeen bin Al-Rabi’ bin Umaila Al-Fazari, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one commits usury more than that his consequences lead to poverty. This is a matter of dealing, the opposite of what is intended, as Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa’id, a client of Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Al-Haytham bin Nafih Al-Zahiri narrated to us, Abu Yahya, a man from the people of Mecca, narrated to me, on the authority of Farrukh, the client of Uthman, that Umar, who was at that time the Commander of the Faithful, came out of the mosque and saw food spread out, so he said: What is this food? They said: Food that was brought to us. He said: May God bless it and the one who brought it. It was said: O Commander of the Faithful, it has been hoarded. He said: Who hoarded it? They said: Farrukh is the freed slave of Uthman and so-and-so is the freed slave of Umar. So he sent for them and said: What made you hoard the food of the Muslims? They said: O Commander of the Faithful, we buy with our money and sell. Umar said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever hoards the food of the Muslims, God will strike him with bankruptcy or leprosy. At that, Farrukh said: I swear to God and I swear to you that I will never go back to eating food again. As for the freed slave of Umar, he said: We buy with our money and sell. Abu Yahya said: I saw the freed slave of Umar with leprosy. Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Al-Haytham bin Rafi’ with it, and its wording is: Whoever hoards the food of the Muslims, God will strike him with bankruptcy and leprosy. And his saying, And He increases the charity was read with a damma on the ya’ and with a light emphasis, from riba al-shay’ yarbu wa rabaha yarbihu, meaning he increased it and made it grow, and yarbi was read with a damma and with a shaddah from tarbiyah. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Katheer told us, Katheer told us, he heard Abu al-Nasr, Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Dinar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from good earnings – and God does not accept anything but good – then God accepts it with His right hand and then makes it grow for its owner as one of you makes his foal grow, until it becomes like a mountain.” This is how it was narrated in the Book of Zakat. He said in the Book of Monotheism: Khalid bin Mukhallad bin Sulayman bin Bilal said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission similarly. Muslim narrated it in Zakat, on the authority of Ahmad bin Uthman bin Hakim, on the authority of Khalid bin Mukhallad, and he mentioned it. Al-Bukhari said: Muslim bin Abi Maryam, Zaid bin Aslam, and Suhayl narrated it, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: As for the narration of Muslim bin Abi Maryam, Al-Bukhari was the only one to mention it. As for the path of Zaid bin Aslam, Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, on the authority of Abu Al-Tahir bin Al-Sarh, on the authority of Abu Wahb, on the authority of Hisham bin Saeed, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on his authority. As for the hadith of Suhayl, Muslim narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Ya’qub bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Suhayl, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari said: And Warqa’ said on the authority of Ibn Dinar, on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This hadith was attributed from this source by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi, on the authority of Al-Hakim and others, on the authority of Al-Asamm, on the authority of Al-Abbas Al-Marwazi, on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr, Hashim bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of Warqa’, who is Ibn Umar Al-Yashkuri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from lawful earnings – and nothing ascends to God except that which is lawful – then God accepts it with His right hand. And he raises it for its owner as one of you raises his foal, until it becomes like Uhud.” And thus this hadith was narrated by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i, all of them, on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Sa’d al-Maqburi. And al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id al-Ansari, and on the authority of Yahya al-Qattan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, all three of them on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yasar Abu al-Habbab al-Madani, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it. And it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah from another chain of transmission, so Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad told us: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty accepts charity, and takes it in His right hand and raises it for one of you as one of you raises his foal or foal, until a morsel becomes like Uhud. And the confirmation of that is in the Book of God: God destroys interest and increases charities. And Ahmad narrated it likewise, on the authority of Waki`, and it is in the interpretation of Waki`, and it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Waki`, and he said: It is good and authentic. And thus it was narrated by Al-Thawri, on the authority of `Ibad bin Mansur, on the authority of `Abbad bin Mansur, and Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Khalaf bin Al-Waleed, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of `Abd Al-Wahid bin Damrah and `Ibad bin Mansur, both of them on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Ibn Jarir, on the authority of Muhammad bin `Abd Al-Malik bin Ishaq, on the authority of `Abd Al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If a servant gives charity from something good, God accepts it from him, and takes it in His right hand and raises it as one of you raises his foal or his young camel. And a man gives charity with a morsel and it grows in the hand of God, or he said in the palm of God, until it becomes like Mount Uhud, so give charity.” And thus it was narrated by Ahmad, on the authority of `Abd Al-Razzaq, and this is a strange path with a sound chain of transmission, but its wording is strange, and what is preserved is what came before, and it was narrated on the authority of `Aishah, the Mother of the Believers, and Imam Ahmad said: `Abd Al-Razzaq told us. As-Samad narrated to us Hammad from Thabit, from Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, from Aisha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God nurtures a date or a morsel of food for one of you as one of you nurtures his foal or young camel, until it becomes like Mount Uhud. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source. Al-Bazzar said: Yahya bin Al-Mu’alla bin Mansour narrated to us, Ismail narrated to us, my father narrated to me from Yahya bin Saeed from Umrah from Aisha from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from Ad-Dahhak bin Uthman from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man gives charity from good earnings, and God accepts only good, and the Most Merciful receives it with His hand and nurtures it as one of you nurtures his foal or young camel, or he said his young camel. Then he said: We do not know of anyone who narrated it from Yahya bin Saeed from Umrah except Abu Uways. And His saying, And God does not love every ungrateful sinner, meaning He does not love the one who is ungrateful in heart and sinful in word and deed. There is a need for a connection in concluding this verse with this description, which is that the usurer is not satisfied with what God has apportioned for him from lawful earnings, nor is he satisfied with what He has prescribed for him from permissible earnings. He seeks to consume people’s money unjustly, through all kinds of wicked earnings. He is ungrateful for the blessing bestowed upon him, unjust and sinful in consuming people’s money unjustly. Then God the Almighty said, praising the believers in their Lord, who obey His command, who give thanks to Him, who do good to His creation in establishing prayer and giving zakat, informing them of the honor He has prepared for them, and that on the Day of Resurrection they will be safe from consequences, so He said, “Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and established prayer and given zakat will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.”

2:278: God Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to fear Him, forbidding them from what brings them closer to His wrath and distances them from His pleasure, so He said, O you who have believed, fear God, meaning fear Him and observe Him in what you do, and give up what remains of interest, meaning leave what you owe people from the increase in capital, after this warning, if you are believers, meaning in what God has prescribed for you of permitting trade and forbidding interest and other things. Zaid bin Aslam, Ibn Jurayj, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Al-Suddi mentioned that this context was revealed regarding Banu Amr bin Umair from Thaqeef, and Banu Al-Mughirah from Banu Makhzum, among whom there was interest in the pre-Islamic era. When Islam came and they entered it, Thaqeef asked to take it from them, so they consulted and Banu Al-Mughirah said, We do not pay interest in Islam by earning Islam. So Atab bin Asid, the governor of Mecca, wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, so this verse was revealed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to him about it. “O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of your usury, if you are believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger.” They said, We will repent to God, and they gave up what remained of their usury, so they all abandoned it. This is a clear threat and warning for those who persist in engaging in usury after being warned. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said, Then be informed of a war, meaning be certain of a war from God and His Messenger. It was mentioned in the narration of Rabi’ah ibn Kulthum, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to the usurer: Take your weapons for war. Then he recited, But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger. So whoever persists in usury and does not desist from it, it is the right of the leader of the Muslims to ask him to repent, and if he desists, otherwise his neck will be struck. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abdul A'la, Hisham bin Hassan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they said: By God, these money changers are usurers, and they have been declared a war by God and His Messenger. If there were a just leader over the people, he would call them to repentance. If they repent, well and good, fine. Qatada said: God has threatened them with death as they hear, and has made them a source of embarrassment wherever they go. So beware of mixing with these usurious transactions, for God has made what is permissible abundant and good, so do not let poverty force you to disobey Him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God has threatened the one who consumes usury with death. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Al-Suhayli said: That is why Aisha said to Umm Muhibbah, the freed slave of Zayd bin Arqam, in the matter of the ‘ayna: Tell him that his jihad with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been invalidated unless he repents. She singled out jihad because it is against His statement: So declare war from God and His Messenger. He said: This meaning has been mentioned by many. He said: But its chain of transmission to Aisha is weak. - Then the Almighty said: “And if you repent, you shall have your capital sums. You shall not be wronged,” meaning by taking the increase. Nor shall you be wronged, meaning by placing the capital sums as well. Rather, you shall have what you gave without increasing it or decreasing it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ashkab told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Shabib ibn Gharqadah al-Mubarqi, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Amr ibn al-Ahwas, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and said: “Behold, all usury that existed in the Age of Ignorance has been abolished from you in its entirety. You shall have your capital sums. You shall not wrong, nor shall you be wronged. The first usury to be abolished was the usury of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. It was all abolished.” And so did his grandfather Sulayman ibn al-Ahwas. Ibn Mardawayh said: Al-Shafi’i told us, Muadh ibn al-Muthanna told us, Musaddad told us, Abu al-Ahwas told us, Shabib ibn Gharqadah told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Amr, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Behold, all usury from Usury of the Age of Ignorance is abolished. You have your capital. You do not wrong, nor are you wronged.” And thus he narrated it from the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Hamza al-Raqashi, on the authority of Umar, who is Ibn Kharijah, and he mentioned it. And His statement, “But if he is in hardship, then grant him postponement until it is easy for him. And if you remit it by charity, that is better for you, if you only knew.” God Almighty commands patience with the one in hardship who cannot pay, so He said, But if he is in hardship, then grant him postponement until it is easy for him. This is not like the people of ignorance used to say to their debtor when the debt became due: Either pay it or increase it, then he would urge them to forgive it, and he promised goodness and great reward for that. He said, And if you remit it by charity, that is better for you, if you only knew. That is, that you leave the principal completely and forgive the debtor. Hadiths have been transmitted from multiple chains of transmission from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to that effect. The first hadith on the authority of Abu Umamah As`ad bin Zararah. Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Shu`ayb al-Rajani told us, Yahya bin Hakim al-Muqawwam told us, Muhammad bin Bakr al-Barsani told us, Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told us, Asim bin Ubaidullah told me, on the authority of Abu Umamah As`ad bin Zararah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever would like God to shade him on the Day when there is no shade but His shade, let him make it easy for one in difficulty or forgive him. Another hadith on the authority of Buraydah. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul-Warith told us, Muhammad bin Juhadah told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraydah, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity like that for every day. He said: Then I heard him say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity double that for every day. I said: I heard you, O Messenger of God, say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity like that for every day. Then I heard you say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity double that for every day. He said: “He will receive a charity like that for every day before the debt is due. When the debt is due, then grant him respite, and he will receive a charity double that for every day.” Another hadith On the authority of Abu Qatada Al-Harith bin Rib’i Al-Ansari. Ahmad said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Khatmi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, that Abu Qatada had a debt on a man, and he used to come to him to collect it, but he would hide from him. One day, a boy came out, so he asked him about him, and he said: Yes, he is in the house eating a pot of dates. So he called him and said: O so-and-so, come out, for I have been told that you are here. So he came out to him, and he said: What is keeping you away from me? He said: I am in financial difficulty and I do not have anything. He said: By God, are you in financial difficulty? He said: Yes. So Abu Qatada cried, then he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever relieves his debtor or erases his debt, will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection. Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih. Another hadith On the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said: Al-Akhnas Ahmad ibn Imran told us, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, Abu Malik al-Ashja`i told us, on the authority of Rib`i ibn Kharash, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will bring one of His servants on the Day of Resurrection and say: What did you do in this world? He will say: O Lord, I did not do for You even an atom’s weight in this world that I could hope for from You.” He said it three times. The servant will say at the end: O Lord, You gave me surplus wealth, and I was a man who used to trade with people, and it was my nature to be flexible, so I was easy on the wealthy and gave respite to the poor. He said: Then God, the Almighty, will say: I am the one most deserving of ease. Enter Paradise.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Rib’i ibn Harash, on the authority of Hudhayfah. Muslim, Uqbah ibn Amir and Abu Mas’ud al-Badri added something similar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari’s wording is: Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Yahya ibn Hamza told us, al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abdullah, that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There was a merchant who used to lend money to people. If he saw someone who was insolvent, he would say to his servants: ‘Forgive him, perhaps God will forgive us.’ So God forgave him.” Another hadith on the authority of Sahl ibn Hanif, Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ya`qub told us, Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Abu Al-Walid Hisham ibn Abd Al-Malik told us, Amr ibn Thabit told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn `Aqil told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sahl ibn Hanif, that Sahl told him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever helps a mujahid in the cause of God, or a warrior, or a debtor in his hardship, or a slave in his slave’s servitude, God will shade him in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His shade.” Then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Another hadith On the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Obaid told us, on the authority of Yusuf bin Suhaib, on the authority of Zaid Al-Ami, on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wants his supplication to be answered and his distress to be relieved, let him relieve the debtor. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Masoud Uqbah bin Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Abu Malik told us, on the authority of Rib’i bin Harash, on the authority of Hudhayfah, that a man was brought to God, the Almighty, and He said: What did you do in this world? The man said to him: I did not do an atom’s weight of good. He said it three times, and on the third time He said: I was given surplus wealth in this world, so I used to trade with people, so I was easier on the wealthy and gave respite to the poor. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: We are more deserving of that than you. Forgive My servant, so He forgave him. Abu Masoud said: This is how I heard it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is how Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Malik Sa’d bin Tariq. Another hadith on the authority of Imran bin Husayn. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has a right over a man and delays it, he will receive a charity for every day. Strange from this aspect, and something similar has been mentioned previously from Buraydah. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Al-Yusr Kaab bin Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Muawiyah bin Amr told us, Zaidah told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Rib’i, who said: Abu Al-Yusr told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty or forgives his debt, God will shade him in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His. Muslim included it in his Sahih and from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibad bin Al-Walid bin Ibadah bin As-Samit, who said: My father and I went out seeking knowledge in this neighborhood of the Ansar before they perished. The first one we met was Abu Al-Yusr, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He had with him a slave of his who had a bundle of scrolls. Abu Al-Yusr was wearing a cloak and a pair of gloves, and his slave was wearing a cloak and a pair of gloves. My father said to him: Uncle, I see a blaze of anger on your face. He said: Yes, I owed so-and-so bin so-and-so - the thief - money. I went to his family and greeted him. I said: Is he to blame? They said: No. So his son Jafar came out to me, so I said: Where is your father? He said: He heard your voice and entered my mother's couch, so I said: Come out to me, for I know where you are. So he came out, so I said: What made you hide from me? He said: By God, I will tell you and not lie to you. By God, I feared that I would tell you and lie to you or promise you something and then fail you. I was the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and by God, I was in financial difficulty. He said: I said: By God. He said: I said: By God? He said: God. Then he brought his scroll and erased it with his hand, then said: If you find a judgement, then judge me, otherwise you are absolved. So I bear witness with the sight of these two eyes of mine - and he put his fingers on his eyes - and these two ears of mine heard, and my heart retained it - and he pointed to the corners of his heart - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty or forgives his debt, God will shelter him in His shade. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Another hadith on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami al-Khurasani told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the mosque and he was saying with his hand: Like this, and Abd al-Rahman pointed with his hand to the ground: “Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty or forgives his debt, God will protect him from the heat of Hellfire. Beware, the deeds of Paradise are made difficult by a hill - three times - Beware, the deeds of Hellfire are made easy by a slip, and the happy one is the one who is protected from trials. There is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant swallows it for the sake of God except that God fills his heart with faith.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another path Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Burani, the judge of Al-Hudaibiyah from the lands of Rabi’ah, told us, Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us, Al-Hakam bin Al-Jarud told us, Ibn Abi Al-Muta’id, the maternal uncle of Ibn Uyaynah, told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever grants respite to a person in difficulty until he is able to pay, God will grant him respite for his sin until he repents. Then the Almighty said, admonishing His servants, and reminding them of the passing of this world, and the annihilation of what is in it of wealth and other things, and the coming of the Hereafter, and returning to Him, the Almighty, and His holding His creation to account for what they did, and His rewarding them for what they earned of good and evil, and warning them of His punishment, so He said: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.” It has been narrated that this verse was the last verse revealed from the Noble Qur’an, so Ibn Lahi’ah said: Ata’ bin Dinar told me, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, who said: The last verse revealed from the entire Qur’an was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived nine nights after the revelation of this verse, then he died on Monday, two nights before the end of Rabi’ al-Awwal, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of al-Mas’udi from Habib bin Abi Thabit, from Sa’id bin Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse revealed was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. God.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse to be revealed from the Qur’an was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.” Ad-Dahhak and Al-Awfi narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ath-Thawri narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse to be revealed was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. There were thirty-one days between its revelation and the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived nine nights after it, and he began on Saturday and died on Monday. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Atiyyah narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The last verse to be revealed was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.”
2:279: God Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to fear Him, forbidding them from what brings them closer to His wrath and distances them from His pleasure, so He said, O you who have believed, fear God, meaning fear Him and observe Him in what you do, and give up what remains of interest, meaning leave what you owe people from the increase in capital, after this warning, if you are believers, meaning in what God has prescribed for you of permitting trade and forbidding interest and other things. Zaid bin Aslam, Ibn Jurayj, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Al-Suddi mentioned that this context was revealed regarding Banu Amr bin Umair from Thaqeef, and Banu Al-Mughirah from Banu Makhzum, among whom there was interest in the pre-Islamic era. When Islam came and they entered it, Thaqeef asked to take it from them, so they consulted and Banu Al-Mughirah said, We do not pay interest in Islam by earning Islam. So Atab bin Asid, the governor of Mecca, wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, so this verse was revealed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to him about it. “O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of your usury, if you are believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger.” They said, We will repent to God, and they gave up what remained of their usury, so they all abandoned it. This is a clear threat and warning for those who persist in engaging in usury after being warned. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said, Then be informed of a war, meaning be certain of a war from God and His Messenger. It was mentioned in the narration of Rabi’ah ibn Kulthum, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to the usurer: Take your weapons for war. Then he recited, But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger. So whoever persists in usury and does not desist from it, it is the right of the leader of the Muslims to ask him to repent, and if he desists, otherwise his neck will be struck. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abdul A'la, Hisham bin Hassan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they said: By God, these money changers are usurers, and they have been declared a war by God and His Messenger. If there were a just leader over the people, he would call them to repentance. If they repent, well and good, fine. Qatada said: God has threatened them with death as they hear, and has made them a source of embarrassment wherever they go. So beware of mixing with these usurious transactions, for God has made what is permissible abundant and good, so do not let poverty force you to disobey Him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God has threatened the one who consumes usury with death. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Al-Suhayli said: That is why Aisha said to Umm Muhibbah, the freed slave of Zayd bin Arqam, in the matter of the ‘ayna: Tell him that his jihad with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been invalidated unless he repents. She singled out jihad because it is against His statement: So declare war from God and His Messenger. He said: This meaning has been mentioned by many. He said: But its chain of transmission to Aisha is weak. - Then the Almighty said: “And if you repent, you shall have your capital sums. You shall not be wronged,” meaning by taking the increase. Nor shall you be wronged, meaning by placing the capital sums as well. Rather, you shall have what you gave without increasing it or decreasing it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ashkab told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Shabib ibn Gharqadah al-Mubarqi, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Amr ibn al-Ahwas, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and said: “Behold, all usury that existed in the Age of Ignorance has been abolished from you in its entirety. You shall have your capital sums. You shall not wrong, nor shall you be wronged. The first usury to be abolished was the usury of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. It was all abolished.” And so did his grandfather Sulayman ibn al-Ahwas. Ibn Mardawayh said: Al-Shafi’i told us, Muadh ibn al-Muthanna told us, Musaddad told us, Abu al-Ahwas told us, Shabib ibn Gharqadah told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Amr, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Behold, all usury from Usury of the Age of Ignorance is abolished. You have your capital. You do not wrong, nor are you wronged.” And thus he narrated it from the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Hamza al-Raqashi, on the authority of Umar, who is Ibn Kharijah, and he mentioned it. And His statement, “But if he is in hardship, then grant him postponement until it is easy for him. And if you remit it by charity, that is better for you, if you only knew.” God Almighty commands patience with the one in hardship who cannot pay, so He said, But if he is in hardship, then grant him postponement until it is easy for him. This is not like the people of ignorance used to say to their debtor when the debt became due: Either pay it or increase it, then he would urge them to forgive it, and he promised goodness and great reward for that. He said, And if you remit it by charity, that is better for you, if you only knew. That is, that you leave the principal completely and forgive the debtor. God.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse to be revealed from the Qur’an was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived nine nights after it, and he began on Saturday and died on Monday. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Atiyyah narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The last verse to be revealed was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.”

Zaid bin Aslam, Ibn Jurayj, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Al-Suddi mentioned that this context was revealed regarding Banu Amr bin Umair from Thaqeef, and Banu Al-Mughirah from Banu Makhzum, among whom there was interest in the pre-Islamic era. When Islam came and they entered it, Thaqeef asked to take it from them, so they consulted and Banu Al-Mughirah said, We do not pay interest in Islam by earning Islam. So Atab bin Asid, the governor of Mecca, wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, so this verse was revealed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to him about it. “O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of your usury, if you are believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger.” They said, We will repent to God, and they gave up what remained of their usury, so they all abandoned it. This is a clear threat and warning for those who persist in engaging in usury after being warned. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said, Then be informed of a war, meaning be certain of a war from God and His Messenger. It was mentioned in the narration of Rabi’ah ibn Kulthum, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to the usurer: Take your weapons for war. Then he recited, But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger. So whoever persists in usury and does not desist from it, it is the right of the leader of the Muslims to ask him to repent, and if he desists, otherwise his neck will be struck. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abdul A'la, Hisham bin Hassan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they said: By God, these money changers are usurers, and they have been declared a war by God and His Messenger. If there were a just leader over the people, he would call them to repentance. If they repent, well and good, fine. Qatada said: God has threatened them with death as they hear, and has made them a source of embarrassment wherever they go. So beware of mixing with these usurious transactions, for God has made what is permissible abundant and good, so do not let poverty force you to disobey Him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God has threatened the one who consumes usury with death. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. He said: But its chain of transmission to Aisha is weak. - Then the Almighty said: “And if you repent, you shall have your capital sums. You shall not be wronged,” meaning by taking the increase. You shall have your capital sums. You shall not wrong, nor shall you be wronged. The first usury to be abolished was the usury of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. It was all abolished.” And so did his grandfather Sulayman ibn al-Ahwas. You have your capital. You do not wrong, nor are you wronged.” And thus he narrated it from the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Hamza al-Raqashi, on the authority of Umar, who is Ibn Kharijah, and he mentioned it. And His statement, “But if he is in hardship, then grant him postponement until it is easy for him. And if you remit it by charity, that is better for you, if you only knew.” God Almighty commands patience with the one in hardship who cannot pay, so He said, But if he is in hardship, then grant him postponement until it is easy for him. This is not like the people of ignorance used to say to their debtor when the debt became due: Either pay it or increase it, then he would urge them to forgive it, and he promised goodness and great reward for that. He said, And if you remit it by charity, that is better for you, if you only knew. That is, that you leave the principal completely and forgive the debtor. The first hadith on the authority of Abu Umamah As`ad bin Zararah. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul-Warith told us, Muhammad bin Juhadah told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraydah, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity like that for every day. He said: Then I heard him say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity double that for every day. I said: I heard you, O Messenger of God, say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity like that for every day. Then I heard you say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity double that for every day. He said: “He will receive a charity like that for every day before the debt is due. When the debt is due, then grant him respite, and he will receive a charity double that for every day.” Another hadith On the authority of Abu Qatada Al-Harith bin Rib’i Al-Ansari. Ahmad said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Khatmi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, that Abu Qatada had a debt on a man, and he used to come to him to collect it, but he would hide from him. One day, a boy came out, so he asked him about him, and he said: Yes, he is in the house eating a pot of dates. So he called him and said: O so-and-so, come out, for I have been told that you are here. So he came out to him, and he said: What is keeping you away from me? He said: I am in financial difficulty and I do not have anything. He said: By God, are you in financial difficulty? He said: Yes. So Abu Qatada cried, then he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever relieves his debtor or erases his debt, will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection. Another hadith On the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said: Al-Akhnas Ahmad ibn Imran told us, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, Abu Malik al-Ashja`i told us, on the authority of Rib`i ibn Kharash, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will bring one of His servants on the Day of Resurrection and say: What did you do in this world? The servant will say at the end: O Lord, You gave me surplus wealth, and I was a man who used to trade with people, and it was my nature to be flexible, so I was easy on the wealthy and gave respite to the poor. He said: Then God, the Almighty, will say: I am the one most deserving of ease. Muslim, Uqbah ibn Amir and Abu Mas’ud al-Badri added something similar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari’s wording is: Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Yahya ibn Hamza told us, al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abdullah, that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There was a merchant who used to lend money to people. Another hadith On the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Obaid told us, on the authority of Yusuf bin Suhaib, on the authority of Zaid Al-Ami, on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wants his supplication to be answered and his distress to be relieved, let him relieve the debtor. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Masoud Uqbah bin Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Abu Malik told us, on the authority of Rib’i bin Harash, on the authority of Hudhayfah, that a man was brought to God, the Almighty, and He said: What did you do in this world? The man said to him: I did not do an atom’s weight of good. He said it three times, and on the third time He said: I was given surplus wealth in this world, so I used to trade with people, so I was easier on the wealthy and gave respite to the poor. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: We are more deserving of that than you. Forgive My servant, so He forgave him. Abu Masoud said: This is how I heard it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is how Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Malik Sa’d bin Tariq. Another hadith on the authority of Imran bin Husayn. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has a right over a man and delays it, he will receive a charity for every day. Abu Al-Yusr was wearing a cloak and a pair of gloves, and his slave was wearing a cloak and a pair of gloves. My father said to him: Uncle, I see a blaze of anger on your face. He said: Yes, I owed so-and-so bin so-and-so - the thief - money. I went to his family and greeted him. I said: Is he to blame? By God, I feared that I would tell you and lie to you or promise you something and then fail you.
