Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Shu`ayb al-Rajani told us, Yahya bin Hakim al-Muqawwam told us, Muhammad bin Bakr al-Barsani told us, Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told us, Asim bin Ubaidullah told me, on the authority of Abu Umamah As`ad bin Zararah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever would like God to shade him on the Day when there is no shade but His shade, let him make it easy for one in difficulty or forgive him. Another hadith on the authority of Buraydah. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul-Warith told us, Muhammad bin Juhadah told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraydah, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity like that for every day. He said: Then I heard him say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity double that for every day. I said: I heard you, O Messenger of God, say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity like that for every day. Then I heard you say: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty will receive a charity double that for every day. He said: “He will receive a charity like that for every day before the debt is due. When the debt is due, then grant him respite, and he will receive a charity double that for every day.” Another hadith On the authority of Abu Qatada Al-Harith bin Rib’i Al-Ansari. Ahmad said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Khatmi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, that Abu Qatada had a debt on a man, and he used to come to him to collect it, but he would hide from him. One day, a boy came out, so he asked him about him, and he said: Yes, he is in the house eating a pot of dates. So he called him and said: O so-and-so, come out, for I have been told that you are here. So he came out to him, and he said: What is keeping you away from me? He said: I am in financial difficulty and I do not have anything. He said: By God, are you in financial difficulty? He said: Yes. So Abu Qatada cried, then he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever relieves his debtor or erases his debt, will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection. Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih. Another hadith On the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said: Al-Akhnas Ahmad ibn Imran told us, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, Abu Malik al-Ashja`i told us, on the authority of Rib`i ibn Kharash, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will bring one of His servants on the Day of Resurrection and say: What did you do in this world? He will say: O Lord, I did not do for You even an atom’s weight in this world that I could hope for from You.” He said it three times. The servant will say at the end: O Lord, You gave me surplus wealth, and I was a man who used to trade with people, and it was my nature to be flexible, so I was easy on the wealthy and gave respite to the poor. He said: Then God, the Almighty, will say: I am the one most deserving of ease. Enter Paradise.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Rib’i ibn Harash, on the authority of Hudhayfah. Muslim, Uqbah ibn Amir and Abu Mas’ud al-Badri added something similar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari’s wording is: Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Yahya ibn Hamza told us, al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abdullah, that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There was a merchant who used to lend money to people. If he saw someone who was insolvent, he would say to his servants: ‘Forgive him, perhaps God will forgive us.’ So God forgave him.” Another hadith on the authority of Sahl ibn Hanif, Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ya`qub told us, Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Abu Al-Walid Hisham ibn Abd Al-Malik told us, Amr ibn Thabit told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn `Aqil told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sahl ibn Hanif, that Sahl told him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever helps a mujahid in the cause of God, or a warrior, or a debtor in his hardship, or a slave in his slave’s servitude, God will shade him in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His shade.” Then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Another hadith On the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Obaid told us, on the authority of Yusuf bin Suhaib, on the authority of Zaid Al-Ami, on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wants his supplication to be answered and his distress to be relieved, let him relieve the debtor. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Masoud Uqbah bin Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Abu Malik told us, on the authority of Rib’i bin Harash, on the authority of Hudhayfah, that a man was brought to God, the Almighty, and He said: What did you do in this world? The man said to him: I did not do an atom’s weight of good. He said it three times, and on the third time He said: I was given surplus wealth in this world, so I used to trade with people, so I was easier on the wealthy and gave respite to the poor. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: We are more deserving of that than you. Forgive My servant, so He forgave him. Abu Masoud said: This is how I heard it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is how Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Malik Sa’d bin Tariq. Another hadith on the authority of Imran bin Husayn. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has a right over a man and delays it, he will receive a charity for every day. Strange from this aspect, and something similar has been mentioned previously from Buraydah. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Al-Yusr Kaab bin Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Muawiyah bin Amr told us, Zaidah told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Rib’i, who said: Abu Al-Yusr told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty or forgives his debt, God will shade him in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His. Muslim included it in his Sahih and from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibad bin Al-Walid bin Ibadah bin As-Samit, who said: My father and I went out seeking knowledge in this neighborhood of the Ansar before they perished. The first one we met was Abu Al-Yusr, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He had with him a slave of his who had a bundle of scrolls. Abu Al-Yusr was wearing a cloak and a pair of gloves, and his slave was wearing a cloak and a pair of gloves. My father said to him: Uncle, I see a blaze of anger on your face. He said: Yes, I owed so-and-so bin so-and-so - the thief - money. I went to his family and greeted him. I said: Is he to blame? They said: No. So his son Jafar came out to me, so I said: Where is your father? He said: He heard your voice and entered my mother's couch, so I said: Come out to me, for I know where you are. So he came out, so I said: What made you hide from me? He said: By God, I will tell you and not lie to you. By God, I feared that I would tell you and lie to you or promise you something and then fail you. I was the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and by God, I was in financial difficulty. He said: I said: By God. He said: I said: By God? He said: God. Then he brought his scroll and erased it with his hand, then said: If you find a judgement, then judge me, otherwise you are absolved. So I bear witness with the sight of these two eyes of mine - and he put his fingers on his eyes - and these two ears of mine heard, and my heart retained it - and he pointed to the corners of his heart - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Whoever grants respite to one in financial difficulty or forgives his debt, God will shelter him in His shade. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Another hadith On the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, al-Hasan ibn Asad ibn Salim al-Kufi told us, al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Ziyad al-Qurashi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhjan, the freed slave of Uthman, on the authority of Uthman, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God will shade an eye in His shade on a day when there is no shade but His shade, whoever grants respite to one in difficulty, or spares a debtor. Another hadith on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami al-Khurasani told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the mosque and he was saying with his hand: Like this, and Abd al-Rahman pointed with his hand to the ground: “Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty or forgives his debt, God will protect him from the heat of Hellfire. Beware, the deeds of Paradise are made difficult by a hill - three times - Beware, the deeds of Hellfire are made easy by a slip, and the happy one is the one who is protected from trials. There is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant swallows it for the sake of God except that God fills his heart with faith.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another path Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Burani, the judge of Al-Hudaibiyah from the lands of Rabi’ah, told us, Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us, Al-Hakam bin Al-Jarud told us, Ibn Abi Al-Muta’id, the maternal uncle of Ibn Uyaynah, told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever grants respite to a person in difficulty until he is able to pay, God will grant him respite for his sin until he repents. Then the Almighty said, admonishing His servants, and reminding them of the passing of this world, and the annihilation of what is in it of wealth and other things, and the coming of the Hereafter, and returning to Him, the Almighty, and His holding His creation to account for what they did, and His rewarding them for what they earned of good and evil, and warning them of His punishment, so He said: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.” It has been narrated that this verse was the last verse revealed from the Noble Qur’an, so Ibn Lahi’ah said: Ata’ bin Dinar told me, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, who said: The last verse revealed from the entire Qur’an was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived nine nights after the revelation of this verse, then he died on Monday, two nights before the end of Rabi’ al-Awwal, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of al-Mas’udi from Habib bin Abi Thabit, from Sa’id bin Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse revealed was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. God.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse to be revealed from the Qur’an was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.” Ad-Dahhak and Al-Awfi narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ath-Thawri narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse to be revealed was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. There were thirty-one days between its revelation and the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived nine nights after it, and he began on Saturday and died on Monday. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Atiyyah narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The last verse to be revealed was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.”
2:282: This noble verse is the longest verse in the Noble Qur’an. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me that he was informed that the most recent verse in the Qur’an about the Throne is the verse of debt. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mahran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said when the verse of debt was revealed: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first to deny was Adam, peace be upon him. When God created Adam, He wiped his back and brought forth from him what will remain until the Day of Resurrection. Then He began to show him his descendants and saw among them a man blossoming. He said: O Lord, who is this? He said: He is your son David. He said: O Lord, how old is he? He said: Sixty years. He said: O Lord, increase his lifespan. He said: No, unless I add from your lifespan. Adam’s lifespan was a thousand years, so He added forty years to it. He wrote a book for him and had the angels bear witness to it. When Adam was dying and the angels came to him, he said: Forty years of my life remain. It was said to him: You gave them to your son David. He said: You did not do that. So God brought out the book for him and had the angels bear witness to it.” Aswad bin Aamer told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, and he mentioned it and added to it, So God completed it for David as a hundred and completed it for Adam as a thousand years. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it likewise on the authority of Yusuf bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah: This is a very strange hadith, and Ali bin Zaid bin Jud’an is notorious in his hadiths. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak in a similar manner from the hadith of al-Harith bin Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Wathab from Saeed al-Maqburi from Abu Hurayrah, and from the narration of Abu Dawud bin Abi Hind from al-Sha’bi from Abu Hurayrah, and from the path of Muhammad bin Amr from Abu Salamah from Abu Hurayrah, and from the hadith of Tamam bin Saad from Zaid bin Aslam from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it in a similar manner. His statement: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. This is guidance from God the Almighty to His believing servants when they deal with deferred transactions to write them down, so that this will be more accurate in preserving their amount and timing and more precise for the witness in them. He pointed this out at the end of the verse where He said: That is more just in the sight of God and more suitable for testimony and more likely to prevent you from having doubts. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. He said: It was revealed regarding the Salam contract for an unknown term. Qatada said, on the authority of Abu Hassan al-A’raj, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I bear witness to the guaranteed advance payment for a specified term that God has permitted it and permitted it. Then he recited: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term. Narrated by al-Bukhari, and it is confirmed in the two Sahihs from the narration of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Kathir. On the authority of Abu al-Munhal, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and they were paying in advance for fruits for one, two, or three years. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever pays in advance should pay in advance for a known measure, a known weight, and a known term. His statement: Then write it down is a command from God Almighty to write it down for its documentation and preservation. If it is said: It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are an illiterate nation; we do not write nor do we calculate. So what is the connection between that and the command to write it down? The answer is that religion, as such, does not need writing at all, because God has made the Book of God easy for people to memorize, and the Sunnahs are also preserved from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. What God has commanded to be written are only partial things that occur among people, so they were commanded as a matter of guidance, not an obligation as some of them have gone to. Ibn Jurayj said: Whoever professes a religion should write, and whoever buys should bear witness. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that Abu Sulayman al-Mar’ashi was a man who accompanied Ka’b, so he said to his companions one day: Do you know of an oppressed person who called upon his Lord and He did not answer him? They said: How can that be? He said: A man sold something on credit but did not have witnesses or write it down. When his money became due, his friend denied it, so he called upon his Lord, but He did not answer him, because he had disobeyed his Lord. Abu Saeed, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Zayd, and others said: This was obligatory, then it was abrogated by His statement: But if one of you trusts another, then let the one who is trusted discharge his trust. The evidence for this is also the hadith that was narrated from the law of those before us and is established in our law, and it did not deny the lack of writing it down and having witnesses. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Laith told us, from Ja’far bin Rabi’ah, from Abd Al-Rahman bin Hormuz, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he mentioned that a man from the Children of Israel asked some of the Children of Israel to lend him a thousand dinars, so he said: Bring me witnesses so that I may have them as witnesses. He said: God is sufficient as a witness. He said: Bring me a guarantor. He said: God is sufficient as a guarantor. He said: You have spoken the truth. So he paid it for a specified period. He went out to sea and fulfilled his need. Then he looked for a ship to come on for the period he had set, but he did not find a ship. So he took a piece of wood and carved it, and put in it a thousand dinars and a document with it to its owner. Then he pushed it into place and brought it to the sea. Then he said: O God, You know that I borrowed so-and-so a thousand dinars. He asked me for a guarantor, so I said: God is sufficient as a guarantor. He agreed to that. He asked me for a witness, so I said: God is sufficient as a witness. I said: God is sufficient as a witness. He agreed to that. I have tried hard to find a ship to send it to him for what he gave me, but I did not find a ship. I have entrusted it to you. So he threw it into the sea until it entered it. Then he turned back while he was in that state looking for a ship to go to his country. Then the man who had loaned him came out looking for a ship that might bring him his money. Then he found the piece of wood with the money in it. He took it for his family as firewood. When he broke it, he found the money and the document. Then he said: The man who had borrowed from him came and brought him a thousand dinars and said: By God, I have been striving hard to find a boat to bring you your money, but I have not found a boat before the one I came in. He said: Did you send me something? He said: Didn’t I tell you that I had not found a boat before the one I came in? He said: Then God has fulfilled for you what you sent for in the wood, so go back with your thousand, guided. This is a sound chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari narrated it in seven places through sound chains of transmission, with a chain of transmission with a definitive form. He said: Al-Layth ibn Sa`id said, and he mentioned it. It is said that in some of them it is on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth on his authority. His saying: And let a scribe write between you in justice, meaning in fairness and truth, and he should not drag anyone in writing, and he should only write what they agreed upon, without adding or subtracting. And his saying, And let no scribe refuse to write as God has taught him, so let him write, meaning, one who knows how to write should not refuse if he is asked to write for people and there is no necessity for him to do so. So as God has taught him what he did not know, let him give charity to others who do not know how to write and let him write, as it came in the hadith, It is charity to help a craftsman or to make a craft for someone who is not good at writing, and in another hadith, Whoever conceals knowledge that he knows will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire. Mujahid and Ata’ said: It is obligatory for the writer to write. And his saying, And let the one upon whom the right is dictate and let him fear God his Lord, meaning, let the debtor dictate to the writer what he owes of the debt and let him fear God in that, and let him not withhold anything from it, meaning let him not conceal anything from it, and if the one upon whom the right is is a fool, who is prevented from spending and the like, or weak, meaning young, or insane, or is unable to dictate himself, either due to a defect or ignorance of where that is correct or his mistake, then let his guardian dictate with justice. And his saying: And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men is an order to have witnesses along with writing for greater authenticity. But if there are not two men, then a man and two women. This only applies to money, and what is meant by it is money. The two women were established in place of the man because of the deficiency of the woman’s intellect, as Muslim said in his Sahih: Qutaybah told us, Ismail bin Ja’far told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: O group of women, give charity and seek forgiveness frequently, for I have seen that you are the majority of the people of Hellfire. One of them said: Why, O Messenger of God, are you the majority of the people of Hellfire? He said: “You curse frequently and are ungrateful to your husbands. I have never seen anyone deficient in intellect and religion who can overcome a man of reason more than you.” She said: O Messenger of God, what is the deficiency of intellect and religion? He said: “As for the deficiency of her intellect, the testimony of two women is equal to the testimony of a man, so this is a deficiency of intellect. And she spends nights not praying and breaking her fast in Ramadan, so this is a deficiency of religion.” His statement: from among the witnesses whom you accept indicates that justice is a condition for witnesses. This is a restriction that Al-Shafi’i ruled on every general statement in the Qur’an that commands witnesses without any condition. He used this verse as evidence to reject the concealed, indicating that the witness must be just and acceptable. His statement: lest one of them should err means the two women if she forgets to testify. Then one of them reminds the other means that she will be reminded of what happened with the testimony. Others read this with emphasis from the word remember. Whoever says that her testimony with her makes it like the testimony of a man has gone too far. The first is correct, and God knows best. And his saying: And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon It was said: Its meaning is if they are called upon to bear witness, then they must answer, and this is the saying of Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and this is like his saying: And let not the scribe refuse to write as God has taught him, so let him write. From here it is understood that bearing witness is a communal obligation, and it was said that it is the doctrine of the majority, and what is meant by his saying: And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon is to perform, because of the reality of his saying witnesses, and the witness is in reality among those who bear witness, so if he is called upon to perform it, then he must answer if it is required, otherwise it is a communal obligation, and God knows best. And Mujahid, Abu Majlaz and more than one said: If you are called upon to bear witness, then you have the choice, and if you bear witness and are called upon, then answer, and it has been proven in Sahih Muslim and the Sunan through Malik, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm, on the authority of his father Abdullah bin Amr bin Uthman, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Zaid bin Khalid, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you about the best of the witnesses? The one who bears witness before he is asked. As for the other hadith in the two Sahihs, Shall I not tell you about the worst of martyrs? Those who testify before they are martyred. And likewise his saying, Then there will come a people whose oaths will precede their testimony, and their testimony will precede their oaths. And in another narration, Then there will come a people who will testify but will not be martyred. These are the false witnesses. It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan Al-Basri that it includes both situations: bearing witness and performing. And His saying: And do not be weary of writing it down, whether it is small or large, until its term This is from the completion of guidance, which is the command to write down the truth, whether it is small or large. So He said: And do not be weary, meaning do not tire of writing down the truth, regardless of its condition, whether it is small or large, until its term. And His saying: That is more just in the sight of God and more correct for testimony, and more likely that you will not have doubts, meaning that what We have commanded you to do, of writing down the truth if it is deferred, is more just in the sight of God, meaning more just and more correct for testimony, meaning it is more established for the witness if he writes his handwriting and then sees it, he will remember the testimony, because it is possible that if he did not write it down, he will forget it, as is often the case. And more likely that you will not have doubts, and closer to not having doubts. Rather, when there is a dispute, you will refer to the book that you wrote, and He will decide between you without doubt. His saying: Unless it is a present trade that you conduct among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down. That is, if the sale is for present trade, hand to hand, then there is no problem with not writing it down, because the objection to leaving it out is removed. As for witnessing the sale, God the Almighty said: And bring to witness when you make a transaction. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Bakr told me, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, Ata’ ibn Dinar told me, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And bring to witness when you make a transaction, meaning bring to witness your right whether it is due or not, so bring to witness your right in every case. He said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, Mujahid, Ata’ and Ad-Dahhak. Al-Sha’bi and Al-Hasan said: This command was abrogated by His statement: But if one of you trusts another, then let the one who is trusted discharge his trust. This command is understood by the majority of scholars as guidance and recommendation, not as obligation. The evidence for that is the hadith of Khuzaymah ibn Thabit Al-Ansari, which Imam Ahmad narrated: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu’ayb told us on the authority of Az-Zuhri, ‘Amara ibn Khuzaymah Al-Ansari told me that his uncle told him, and he was one of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, bought a horse from a Bedouin. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed him to pay him the price of his horse. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hurried and the Bedouin was slow. Some men began to intercept the Bedouin and bargain with him for the horse, not realizing that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had bought it, until some of them raised the price of the Bedouin over the price of the horse that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had bought. The Bedouin called out to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: If you are going to buy this horse, then buy it, otherwise sell it. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard the Bedouin’s call, he said: Did I not buy it from you? The Bedouin said: No, by God, I did not sell it to you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, I have bought it from you. The people began to seek refuge with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Bedouin, and they were both arguing. The Bedouin began to say: Bring a witness who will testify that I have given you allegiance. Whoever of the Muslims came would say to the Bedouin: Woe to you, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only said the truth. Until Khuzaymah came and listened to the argument of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the argument of the Bedouin, saying: Bring a witness who will testify that I have given you allegiance. Khuzaymah said: I testify that you have given him allegiance. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to Khuzaymah and said: What do you testify to? He said: By your belief, O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the testimony of Khuzaymah equal to the testimony of two men. This is how Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Shu`ayb and al-Nasa’i from the narration of Muhammad ibn al-Waleed al-Zubaidi, and both of them from al-Zuhri with something similar. However, caution is to guide to what the two imams, al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated from the narration of Mu`adh ibn Mu`adh al-`Anbari, from Firas, from al-Sha`bi, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Three call upon God and their supplications are not answered: a man who has a wife of bad character and does not divorce her, a man who gives the wealth of an orphan before he reaches puberty, and a man who lends money to a man and he does not testify.” Then al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs. He said: They did not include it because the companions of Shu`bah attributed this hadith to Abu Musa, but they agreed on the chain of transmission of Shu`bah’s hadith with this chain of transmission: Three will be given their reward twice. And the Almighty’s saying: And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed. It was said: Its meaning is that neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed, so that one writes something other than what he dictates, and another testifies something other than what he heard, or he conceals it completely, and this is the saying of Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. It was said: Its meaning is that he does not strike them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Asid bin Asim told us, Al-Hussein, meaning Ibn Hafs, told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyadah, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, And let no scribe or witness be harmed, he said: A man comes and calls them to write and testify, and they say: We have a need, so he says: You have been commanded to respond, so he does not have the right to harm them. He said: And it was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Mujahid, Tawus, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Atiyah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and As-Suddi, something similar to that. And His statement, And if you do, then it is a transgression upon you, meaning if you disobey what you are commanded to do or do what you are forbidden from, then it is a transgression that will be upon you, meaning it is inherent in you, you will not deviate from it or be separated from it. And His statement, And fear God, meaning fear Him, observe Him, follow His command, and abandon His warning. And God will teach you, is like His statement, O you who have believed, if you fear God. He will make for you a criterion.” And like His saying: “O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you will walk.” And His saying: And God is Knowing of all things. That is, He is All-Knowing of the truths of matters, their interests, and their consequences. Nothing is hidden from Him. Rather, His knowledge encompasses all beings.
2:283: God the Almighty says: And if you are on a journey meaning traveling and you have contracted a loan for a specified period and you cannot find a scribe to write for you, Ibn Abbas said: Or they find him and they cannot find paper or inkwell or pen, then let there be a pledge in possession, meaning let there be a pledge in possession instead of writing, meaning in the hand of the rightful owner. His statement: a pledge in possession has been used as evidence that the pledge is not binding except by possession, as is the view of Al-Shafi'i and the majority. Others have used it as evidence that the pledge must be in possession in the hand of the mortgagee, and this is a narration from Imam Ahmad, and a group has adopted it. Others from the Salaf have used this verse as evidence that the pledge is not permissible except when traveling, as Mujahid and others said. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and his armor was mortgaged to a Jew for thirty wasqs of barley, which he mortgaged as food for his family, and in another narration: from the Jews of Medina. In the narration of Al-Shafi’i, according to Abu Al-Shahm Al-Yahudi, and the report of these issues is in the great book of rulings, and praise and thanks be to God, and with Him is help sought. And his saying: If some of you trust others, then let him who is trusted discharge his trust. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with a good chain of narration on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that he said: This abrogated what came before it. Al-Sha’bi said: If some of you trust others, there is no problem if you do not write it down or bear witness. And his saying: And let him fear God, his Lord, means the one who is trusted, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The hand is responsible for what it has taken until it discharges it. His statement: And do not conceal testimony means do not hide it or conceal it, and do not reveal it. Ibn Abbas and others said: False testimony is one of the greatest major sins, and so is concealing it. That is why He said: And whoever conceals it, then his heart is sinful. Al-Suddi said: He means his heart is wicked. This is like the statement of God the Most High: And we do not conceal the testimony of God; indeed, if we did, we would be among the sinners. And God the Most High said: “O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether he is rich or poor, God is more worthy of both of them. So follow not [your] inclination, lest you be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or turn aside, then indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.” And likewise He said here: “And do not conceal testimony. And whoever conceals it, then his heart is sinful. And God, with what you do, is Knowing.”
2:284: God Almighty tells us that He owns the heavens and the earth and what is in them and what is between them, and that He is the All-Knower of what is in them. Nothing is hidden from Him, nor are the secrets or consciences, no matter how subtle or hidden they are. He informed us that He will hold His servants accountable for what they have done and what they have hidden in their hearts, as God Almighty said: “Say: Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, God knows it. He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and God is over all things competent.” And He said: He knows the secret and what is more hidden. The verses on this are very many, and He informed us in this with more than knowledge, which is accountability for that. For this reason, when this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the Companions, may God be pleased with them, and they feared it and God’s accountability for their great and small deeds, and this was due to the strength of their faith and conviction. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim told us, Abu Abd al-Rahman, meaning al-Ala’, told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. And God is over all things competent,” this was difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then they knelt down and said: O Messenger of God, we have been charged with actions that we are capable of, prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity, and this verse has been revealed to you, and we are not capable of it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Do you want to say as the People of the Book before you said: ‘We hear and we disobey’? Rather, say: ‘We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination.’” When the people acknowledged it and their tongues were humbled by it, God revealed after it: “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say, ‘We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination.’” When they did that, God abrogated it and revealed: “God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake.” And so on. Muslim narrated it alone from the hadith of Yazid ibn Zurai’, on the authority of Ruh ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and he mentioned something similar and the same wording. When they did that, God abrogated it and revealed: “God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has committed. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake.” He said: Yes. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. He said: Yes. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. He said: Yes. “And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” He said: Yes. Hadith of Ibn Abbas on that Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by Sufyan on the authority of Adam bin Sulayman, I heard Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When this verse was revealed, And if you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it, he said, something of it entered their hearts that had not entered their hearts before, he said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Say, ‘We hear, we obey, and we submit,’ so God cast faith into their hearts, and God revealed, “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers, and they say, ‘We hear and we obey. We seek Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination,’” until His saying, So give us victory over the disbelieving people. And Muslim narrated it thus on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq bin Ibrahim, all three of them on the authority of Wakee’, and he added, Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake, he said: I have done so, Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us, he said: I have done so. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. He said: I have done so. “And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” He said: I have done so. Another way On the authority of Ibn Abbas. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Humayd al-Araj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I entered upon Ibn Abbas and said: O Abu Abbas, I was with Ibn Omar when he recited this verse and wept. He said: Which verse? I said: And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it. Ibn Abbas said: When this verse was revealed, it greatly saddened the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and angered them greatly. They said: O Messenger of God, we are doomed if we are to be held accountable for what we say and what we do. As for our hearts, they are not in our hands. So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to them: Say, ‘We hear and obey.’ They said: We hear and obey. He said: This verse abrogated it: “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God.” to: “God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned.” So they were permitted to speak of their own souls and were held accountable for their actions. Another way from him. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Saeed bin Marjana, he heard him narrating: While he was sitting with Abdullah bin Omar, he recited this verse: “To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And if you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it and then forgive whom He wills.” The verse, so he said: By God, if God were to punish us for this, we would perish. Then Ibn Omar cried until he heard his sobs. Ibn Marjana said: So I got up and went to Ibn Abbas, and I mentioned to him what Ibn Omar had said and what he had done when he recited it, so Ibn Abbas said: May God forgive Abu Abd al-Rahman, by my life, the Muslims felt from it what Abdullah bin Omar felt when it was revealed, so God revealed after it: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity to the end of the surah. Ibn Abbas said: So this whispering was something that the Muslims could not bear, and the matter came to the point that God, the Almighty, decreed that the soul shall have what it has earned and shall bear what it has earned in word and deed. Another way Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, that his father recited, And if you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it, and his eyes filled with tears. When Ibn Abbas heard of his action, he said: May God have mercy on Abu Abd Al-Rahman, he did as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did when it was revealed, and the verse after it abrogated it, God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, so these are authentic ways on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it has been proven on the authority of Ibn Umar as it has been proven on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq told us, Ruh told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Marwan Al-Asghar, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, I think he was Ibn Umar, And if you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, he said: The verse after it abrogated it. And thus it was narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Ka’b Al-Ahbar, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, Ikrimah, Sa’id bin Jubayr, and Qatadah, that it was abrogated. With the one after it, and it has been proven by what the group narrated in their six books on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Zararah bin Abi Awfa, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forgiven my nation for what their souls have thought of, as long as they do not speak of it or act upon it. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God said: If My servant intends to do a bad deed, do not write it down against him. If he does it, write it down as a bad deed. If he intends to do a good deed but does not do it, write it down as a good deed. If he does it, write it down as ten good deeds.” The wording of Muslim is in his Ifrad, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ja’far, on the authority of al-Ala’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “God said: If My servant intends to do a good deed but does not do it, I write it down as a good deed for him. If he does it, I write it down as ten good deeds for him, up to seven hundred times. If he intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, I do not write it down against him. If he does it, I write it down as one bad deed.” Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us on the authority of Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God said: If My servant intends to do a good deed, I write it down for him as a good deed so long as he does not do it. If he does it, I write it down as ten times its like. If he intends to do a bad deed, I forgive him for it so long as he does not do it. If he does it, I write it down as one like it.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The angels said: ‘O Lord, Your servant intends to do a bad deed, and You are All-Knowing about him. So He said: ‘Watch him. If he does it, write it down for him as one like it. If he abandons it, write it down as one good deed. He only abandons it because of My sake.’” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If someone improves his Islam, then for every good deed he does, it is written down for him as ten times its like up to seven hundred times, and every bad deed is written down as one like it until he meets God, the Almighty.” Muslim alone transmitted it on the authority of Muhammad bin Rafi’ on the authority of Abdul Razzaq with this context and wording, and some of it is in Sahih al-Bukhari. Muslim also said: Abu Kuraib told us, Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed will be recorded for him. Whoever intends to do a good deed and does it, ten to seven hundred will be recorded for him. Whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, it will not be recorded for him, but if he does it, it will be recorded.” Muslim is the only one to narrate this, not any other author of the books. Muslim also said: Shaiban bin Farukh told us, Abdul Warith told us, on the authority of Al-Ja`d Abu Uthman, Abu Raja` Al-`Attardi told us, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he narrates on the authority of his Lord, the Most High, who said: “God has written down the good deeds and the bad deeds, then explained that. So whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, God writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed. And if he intends to do a good deed but does not do it, God writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed. And if he intends to do it and does it, God writes it down with Himself as ten good deeds to seven hundred times or many times more. And if he intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, God writes it down with Himself as a good deed. And if he intends to do it and does it, God writes it down with Himself as one bad deed.” Then Muslim narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya, on the authority of Ja`far bin Sulayman, on the authority of Al-Ja`d Abu Uthman, in this chain of transmission with the same meaning as the hadith of Abd Al-Razzaq. And he added, And God erased it, and none perishes on the authority of God except one who perishes. And in the hadith of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and asked him, saying: We find within ourselves that which one of us would be too ashamed to speak of. He said: And have you found it? They said: Yes. He said: That is the clear expression of faith. This is the wording of Muslim. It is also in Muslim, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with it. Muslim also narrated from the hadith of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about whispers, and he said: That is the clear expression of faith. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it, it was not abrogated, but when God gathers the creation on the Day of Resurrection, He will say: I will inform you of what you concealed in yourselves of which My angels have not seen. As for the believers, He will inform them and forgive them for what they told themselves, and this is His statement, God will bring you to account for it, meaning: He will inform you. As for the people of doubt and suspicion, He will inform them of what they concealed of denial, and this is His statement, Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and this is His statement, But He will take you to task for what your hearts have earned, meaning of doubt and hypocrisy. Al-Awfi and Al-Dahhak narrated something similar to this on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak something similar, and from Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he said: It is a decisive verse that has not been abrogated. Ibn Jarir chose that and provided evidence that accountability does not necessarily entail punishment, and that the Almighty may hold accountable and forgive, or hold accountable and punish, with the hadith that he narrated regarding this verse, saying: Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Abi Uday told us, from Saeed bin Hisham H and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ibn Hisham told us, they both said in their hadith on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Safwan bin Mahraz, he said: While we were circumambulating the House with Abdullah bin Umar and he was circumambulating, a man came to him and said: O Ibn Umar, what did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about the secret conversation? He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The believer draws near to his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, until He places His cloak over him and makes him confess his sins and says to him: Do you know such and such? He says: O Lord, I know, twice, until he has reached what God willed for him to reach, He says: Then I have concealed it from you in The world and I forgive you for it today, he said: Then he will be given his record of good deeds or his book in his right hand, and as for the disbelievers and hypocrites, it will be called out to them before all witnesses: “These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.” This hadith is narrated in the two Sahihs and others through various chains of transmission on the authority of Qatada with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of his father, he said: I asked Aisha about this verse: And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it. She said: No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, so she said: This is the slave’s pledge to God and what befalls him of fever and calamity, and the merchandise that he places in the hand of his sleeve and loses it, and is alarmed by it, then finds it in his buckle, until the believer emerges from his sins as red gold emerges. And likewise, at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir narrated it through the chain of Hammad ibn Salamah with it. At-Tirmidhi said: It is strange, we do not know it except from His hadith. I said His sheikh Ali bin Jadaan is weak and strange in his narrations, and he narrates this hadith on the authority of his father’s wife Umm Muhammad Umayyah bint Abdullah, on the authority of Aisha, and she has no other narration on her authority in the books.
2:285: Mentioning the hadiths reported on the merits of these two noble verses. May God benefit us with them. The first hadith - Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Katheer told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever recites the two verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him. The rest of the group narrated it on the authority of Sulayman bin Mihran al-A’mash with a similar chain of transmission, and it is in the two Sahihs on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on his authority, and it is also in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. Abd al-Rahman said: Then I met Abu Mas’ud and he narrated it to me. And this is how Ahmad bin Hanbal narrated it. Yahya bin Adam told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever recites the two verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him. The cow is enough for him at night. The second hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Hussain told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rab’i, on the authority of Kharsha bin Al-Har, on the authority of Al-Ma’rur bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was given the final verses of Surat Al-Baqarah from a treasure under the Throne, which no prophet before me was given. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Al-Ashja’i, on the authority of Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rab’i, on the authority of Zaid bin Dhibyan, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was given the final verses of Surat Al-Baqarah from a treasure under the Throne. The third hadith - Muslim said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Usamah told us, Malik bin Mughul told us H and Ibn Numayr and Zuhair bin Harb told us, all on the authority of Abdullah bin Numayr, and their wording is similar. Ibn Numayr said: My father told us, Malik bin Mughul told us on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Adi, on the authority of Talhah, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the seventh heaven. What ascends from the earth ends at it and is taken from it, and what descends from above it ends at it and is taken from it. He said, When that which covers the Lote Tree covers it, he said: A bed of gold. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given three things: He was given the five daily prayers, he was given the last verses of Surat Al-Baqarah, and forgiveness was given to those of his nation who did not associate anything with God for their sins. The fourth hadith Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Ibrahim al-Razi told us, Salamah bin al-Fadl told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told me, on the authority of Yazid Abu Habib, on the authority of Murthad bin Abdullah al-Yazni, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Recite the two verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah, for I have been given them from a treasure beneath the Throne. This is a good chain of transmission, and they did not include it in their books. The fifth hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Kamil told us, Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Harbi told us, Marwan told us, Ibn Awanah told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Rubai, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We have been given three things over the al-Nas 114:I have been given these verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah from a treasure house beneath the Throne. No one was given them before me, and no one will be given them after me.” Then he narrated it from the hadith of Na’im ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Rubai, on the authority of Hudhayfah, in a similar manner. It was mentioned earlier in the hadith that God said: Yes, and in another hadith: God said: I have done it. And His saying, You are our Master, meaning, You are our Guardian and Supporter, and upon You we rely, and upon You we seek help, and upon You we rely, and we have no power or strength except with You, So give us victory over the disbelieving people, meaning, those who denied Your religion, and rejected Your Oneness and the message of Your Prophet, and worshipped other than You and associated with You from Your servants, so give us victory over them, and make for us the best outcome over them in this world and the Hereafter. God said, Yes. And in the hadith narrated by Muslim on the authority of Ibn Abbas, God said, I have done so. And Ibn Jarir said: Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, Abu Nu’aym told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, that when Muadh may God be pleased with him finished this surah, So give us victory over the disbelieving people, he would say, Ameen. And Waki’ narrated it on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, that when he finished Surat Al-Baqarah, he would say, Ameen.
